Its values are continuous linear maps on the full joint coordinate space, so time and label derivatives remain available.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.deri.summary: Preserve phase periodicity when taking slab derivatives

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.deri.text: For `hT : 0 < T`, the underlying smooth profile of a periodic derivative is exactly the derivative of the underlying smooth profile. This definitional equality makes the restriction transparent to pointwise calculations. Periodicity changes the type of the output, while its derivative values remain unchanged.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.deri.summary: The periodic derivative is the original slab derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.exis.text: Packages already supplied smooth fields `B` and `q` satisfying the mean equation into phase-periodic profiles. Their values agree with the supplied fields throughout the closed slab and are independent of phase. This is a representation bridge, not an endpoint existence theorem and not a proof of spatial periodicity in the label variable.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.exis.summary: A given smooth mean becomes a periodic hierarchy output

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.exis.text: For smooth phase-independent strain and transported nonzero covector, turns a phase-periodic zero-average source into a periodic transverse output with zero initial velocity. The output satisfies the material-plus-phase-pressure equation. Nonvanishing is supplied at time zero and propagated by the covector equation; the theorem does not assert a quantitative weighted estimate.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.exis.summary: The transverse solve lies in the periodic profile space

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.ext.text: Two periodic profiles are equal if their values agree at every point of the slab. Their underlying smooth representatives are zero everywhere else, so no off-slab comparison is required. This extensionality result is used to prove identities of differential and averaging operators pointwise.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.ext.summary: Compare periodic profiles only on the time slab

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.fder.text: The derivative within the slab of a periodic profile is itself periodic under one phase translation. Translation preserves the domain and the function, so the translated derivative equals the original derivative. This equality also covers time endpoints and is stated without a positive-time hypothesis.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.fder.summary: The slab derivative has the same phase period

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.hasD.text: For a fixed time in the closed slab and any label, the one-variable phase slice has derivative given by the joint derivative within the slab applied to the unit phase direction. The whole phase line stays inside the domain, so this is an ordinary derivative even at a time endpoint.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.hasD.summary: A phase slice differentiates by the slab derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.map.text: A bounded linear map on the value space induces a linear map on periodic profiles. Pointwise postcomposition preserves the unit phase period, and the existing smooth-profile construction supplies smoothness. No phase averaging is involved, so every on-slab value is simply its original linear image.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.map.summary: Preserve the phase period under a linear image

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.map_.text: The underlying smooth profile of the periodic linear-image operation equals the smooth-profile linear-image operation on the input. This definitional equality transfers evaluation formulas across the periodic wrapper. It records that periodicity is additional certified structure, not a change to the function being transformed.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.map_.summary: The linear image keeps its pointwise meaning

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.ofPe.text: If every fixed time-label slice of a smooth profile has period one on the slab, this packages the profile as periodic. Slice periodicity is translated into joint-coordinate periodicity, and zero extension handles all other times. The construction does not alter any underlying function value.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.ofPe.summary: Package unit-periodic slices returned by a solver

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.ofPe.text: The periodic profile produced from slice-periodicity proofs has exactly the original smooth profile as its underlying value. This definitional equality lets solver outputs be used without rewriting their formulas. The constructor adds only a periodicity proof; smoothness and off-slab behavior remain those of the input.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.ofPe.summary: Packaging periodic slices leaves the profile unchanged

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.ofPh.text: A smooth profile whose phase slices are constant on the slab is placed in the periodic submodule. Its underlying representative is unchanged, since phase independence already supplies the required unit-period identity. This construction is used for coefficient fields such as the inverse deformation and transported covector.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.ofPh.summary: Regard a phase-independent coefficient as periodic

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.ofPh.text: For a phase-independent smooth profile, the underlying value of its periodic embedding is definitionally the same profile. The equality confirms that adding periodicity does not resample or average the coefficient. Its independence proof is only used to justify membership in the periodic submodule.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.ofPh.summary: The independent coefficient keeps its original profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.ofSm.text: Given a function smooth on the slab and globally periodic in the joint phase direction, this first forms its zero extension and then proves that extension periodic. On-slab values are unchanged. The input periodicity proof concerns the actual function; it is not generated by wrapping an arbitrary function modulo one.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.ofSm.summary: Turn a smooth periodic function into a profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.ofSm.text: At a point of the slab, the periodic profile created from a smooth periodic function has exactly the original value. The theorem only removes the representation wrappers. The zero-extension convention outside the slab is unaffected, and the periodicity proof contributes no change to the function.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.ofSm.summary: Evaluate a periodic profile before changing representation

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.peri.text: A periodic profile carries the identity that translating its representative by `hierarchyPhasePeriod` leaves the value unchanged. This theorem simply exposes that stored proof. Its two `.val` projections pass through the periodic submodule and the smooth profile to the ordinary function.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.peri.summary: Read the stored unit-period translation identity

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.peri.text: This record packages the actual material derivative, label and phase gradients, label and phase advection, and phase mean on periodic profiles. Each component is the corresponding concrete smooth-profile operation with its periodicity proved. The coefficient profiles `G`, `M`, and `κ` remain arbitrary periodic inputs.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.peri.summary: The physical profile operators on periodic functions

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.peri.text: The underlying smooth output of this component of `periodicHierarchyOperators` is exactly the actual unit-period phase average of the vector profile. The equality is definitional: restriction to periodic inputs adds closure proofs while retaining the original operation. It lets pointwise formulas from the smooth-profile layer apply directly.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.peri.summary: Read the actual phase mean through the wrapper

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.peri.text: The underlying smooth output of this component of `periodicHierarchyOperators` is exactly the derivative of the second velocity in the coframe direction selected by the first. The equality is definitional: restriction to periodic inputs adds closure proofs while retaining the original operation. It lets pointwise formulas from the smooth-profile layer apply directly.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.peri.summary: Read concrete label advection through the wrapper

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.peri.text: The underlying smooth output of this component of `periodicHierarchyOperators` is exactly the scalar pressure gradient formed from the coframe G. The equality is definitional: restriction to periodic inputs adds closure proofs while retaining the original operation. It lets pointwise formulas from the smooth-profile layer apply directly.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.peri.summary: Read the concrete label gradient through the wrapper

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.peri.text: The underlying smooth output of this component of `periodicHierarchyOperators` is exactly the time derivative within the slab plus multiplication by M. The equality is definitional: restriction to periodic inputs adds closure proofs while retaining the original operation. It lets pointwise formulas from the smooth-profile layer apply directly.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.peri.summary: Read the concrete material operator through the wrapper

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.peri.text: The underlying smooth output of this component of `periodicHierarchyOperators` is exactly the derivative of the second velocity in the phase direction selected by its first argument and κ. The equality is definitional: restriction to periodic inputs adds closure proofs while retaining the original operation. It lets pointwise formulas from the smooth-profile layer apply directly.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.peri.summary: Read concrete phase advection through the wrapper

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.peri.text: The underlying smooth output of this component of `periodicHierarchyOperators` is exactly the scalar phase derivative multiplied by κ. The equality is definitional: restriction to periodic inputs adds closure proofs while retaining the original operation. It lets pointwise formulas from the smooth-profile layer apply directly.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.peri.summary: Read the concrete fast gradient through the wrapper

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.peri.text: If a smooth profile is invariant under one phase translation at every slab point, its whole representative is periodic. Outside the slab both translated and untranslated values are zero, since phase translation preserves membership. This proves global representative periodicity without assuming global smoothness.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.peri.summary: Extend on-slab periodicity to the representative

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.phas.text: If the second input `g` is phase independent, concrete phase advection by any first input `f` vanishes. The direction may have a nonzero phase speed, but it acts on a constant phase slice. This is the compatibility needed for means appearing as the advected field.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.phas.summary: A phase-independent field cannot be differentiated in phase

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.phas.text: If `hf` says that the inner product of κ with the first input `f` is zero at every slab point, phase advection of any second input vanishes. The selected phase direction is then the zero vector. The conclusion depends on transversality of the advecting field, not phase independence.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.phas.summary: A transverse field cannot advect in the phase direction

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.phas.text: The phase average of the centered completion input is the zero smooth profile. The proof uses linearity and idempotence of phase averaging. This equality holds in the profile space, whose representatives are zero outside the time slab, and supplies the mean condition required for a periodic potential.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.phas.summary: Centering a profile removes its phase average

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.phas.text: For a profile independent of phase on the slab, the derivative within the slab applied to the unit phase direction is zero at every slab point. The proof compares the actual derivative of its constant phase slice with the derivative of a constant function. No time-independence conclusion is drawn.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.phas.summary: An independent profile has no phase derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.phas.text: The joint vector `(0,0,c)` equals `c • hierarchyPhasePeriod`. This elementary coordinate identity lets linearity of a Fréchet derivative factor the scalar phase speed out of a directional derivative. It is used for both phase-independence cancellation and transversality cancellation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.phas.summary: Every fast direction scales the unit phase direction

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.phas.text: If the scalar pressure profile is phase independent, its concrete fast gradient vanishes. Its scalar phase derivative is zero, so multiplying by the transported covector still gives zero. This supplies the pressure compatibility required of a mean output, for arbitrary periodic coefficient profiles.

If a periodic profile equals its phase average, its underlying smooth profile is independent of phase on the slab. The average is already known to ignore the output phase coordinate, and the equality transfers that fact. This turns the abstract mean-output condition into actual phase independence.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.phas.summary: A fixed point of averaging is phase independent

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.phas.text: For each time and label, the phase slice of a periodic profile has period one. This also holds for the stored representative outside the slab, where that representative is zero.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.phas.summary: A bundled profile has period one in phase

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.phas.text: At every time in $[0,T]$ and every label, subtracting the phase average from a periodic profile leaves a one-periodic phase function. The mean is constant in phase and therefore unchanged by a unit shift. This is the periodicity input for constructing the normalized potential of arbitrary periodic data.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.phas.summary: Centering preserves phase periodicity on every slab slice

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.prof.text: The actual phase-averaging operator restricts to periodic vector profiles because its output is phase independent. It is a linear map using the same unit-period integral as the smooth-profile operator. The construction changes neither the time domain nor the coefficient functions outside their existing representation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.prof.summary: Average within the space of periodic profiles

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.prof.text: When the underlying smooth profile is independent of phase on the slab, the periodic phase-averaging operator fixes it. The proof lifts the corresponding smooth-profile identity. This establishes one direction of the correspondence between actual phase independence and being fixed by the concrete averaging operator.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.prof.summary: The mean of an independent profile is itself

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.prof.text: The periodic phase-averaging operator is idempotent: averaging an already averaged profile returns the same result. The first average is phase independent, so the fixed-point lemma applies. This supplies the concrete projection law required by the abstract finite-hierarchy solvers.

Averaging any smooth vector profile produces a profile independent of the output phase coordinate. The proof evaluates the same phase integral at two output phases; their time and label coordinates agree. The input need not already be periodic for this phase-independence statement.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.prof.summary: The phase mean no longer depends on phase

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.prof.text: The underlying smooth profile of the periodic phase mean equals the smooth-profile phase mean of the input. This definitional equality transfers the integral evaluation formula to the periodic space. It confirms that the submodule restriction does not replace averaging with an unrelated linear projection.

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.rest.text: A linear map between smooth profile spaces restricts to their periodic submodules when `hL` proves its output periodic for every periodic input. The restriction changes the types, not the underlying operation. It therefore supplies closure of concrete differentiation and averaging operations without introducing a new formula.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.rest.summary: Restrict a linear operator to periodic profiles

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.rest.text: A bilinear operation on smooth profiles is restricted to periodic inputs and periodic outputs using the supplied closure proof `hL`. Linearity in each argument is retained. This packages concrete advection and operator-field multiplication on the periodic space while keeping their original action on functions.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.rest.summary: Restrict both arguments of a bilinear operator

TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.rest.text: After restricting a bilinear operator to periodic profiles, its underlying output equals `L f.val g.val`. The statement exposes the actual operation before restriction. Its proof is reflexivity because the periodicity certificate changes only the output type, rather than changing its values.

The underlying smooth profile of a restricted linear operator is the original map `L` applied to the input’s underlying profile. This is a definitional equality. The closure proof `hL` certifies periodicity while leaving the computed function untouched, enabling transfer of previously proved pointwise formulas.
TorusEuler.HierarchyPeriodicProfile.rest.summary: Read the original linear operator after restriction

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfilePoint.text:
The profile domain is the product of real time, three-dimensional labels and a real phase. Time restrictions and periodicity are imposed by separate slab and profile definitions.

Default-value audit (b5): This is a type abbreviation for the source type displayed here. It does not by itself assert a PDE, nonvanishing, smoothness or an existence theorem.

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfileReflectionPar.text:
The reflected profile has sign -1 for velocity and sign +1 for pressure and even label coefficients.

Default-value audit (b5): The sign is any real scalar in the definition. The intended even/odd cases are sign=1 and sign=−1; for other signs the condition may force additional degeneracy.
TorusEuler.HierarchyProfileReflectionPar.summary: Even and odd parity under joint reflection

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.text:
The profiles, divergence completions and two parts of the pressure at each level of the finite expansion.

Default-value audit (b5): The record contains five arbitrary sequences. It does not impose the hierarchy recurrence, support, parity or initial conditions; these enter through separate laws and the constructed expansion.
TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.summary: Oscillations, means and pressures at each level

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.AgreesBefor.text: Two profile families agree before $p$ when their velocities, completions, means, and oscillatory pressures agree at every index $i<p$. Mean pressures are deliberately absent: the preliminary source never reads them. This is the exact relation needed to replace a truncated recursion prefix by the completed family.

If two profile families satisfy `AgreesBefore` at $p$ and `hi : i < p`, their $Y_i$ blocks agree. The proof uses equality of `V i` and `C (i-1)`. Since natural subtraction gives $i-1\le i$, the completion is still among the earlier inputs.
TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.AgreesBefor.summary: Earlier oscillatory blocks agree with the prefix

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.AgreesBefor.text: Agreement of profile families before $p$ gives equality of the full block $Z_i$ for each `hi : i < p`. The earlier $Y_i$ identity supplies the oscillatory part, and the stored equality of `B i` supplies the mean. This lets quadratic source sums use the final family.
TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.AgreesBefor.summary: Earlier full blocks agree with the prefix

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.LevelMem.text: At one storage level, requires the oscillation, completion and mean to belong to the velocity submodule, and both scalar pressures to belong to the pressure submodule. The record is abstract and can express more than parity. Remember that the stored completion `C p` is the paper correction at level `p + 1`.
TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.LevelMem.summary: The velocity and pressure components have their prescribed symmetry

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.LevelMem.Y_.text: If both level `p` and level `p - 1` satisfy the membership record, their oscillation and preceding stored completion sum to a velocity-class element. Natural subtraction appears because Lean stores the completion of wave `p - 1` there. At index zero this is truncated subtraction, so applications use the construction’s zero conventions.
TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.LevelMem.Y_.summary: The oscillation and preceding completion keep velocity symmetry

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.LevelMem.Z_.text: Uses membership at the current and previous storage levels to place the full block `Z p` in the velocity submodule. First the oscillation and preceding completion form `Y p`; then the mean is added. Closure under addition supplies the result, with no equation or phase-independence conclusion implied.
TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.LevelMem.Z_.summary: Adding the mean preserves the block symmetry

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.Y.text:
The level-$p$ oscillatory block $Y_p=V_p+C_{p-1}$. This algebraic definition takes a family `u : HierarchyProfiles E F` and a natural-number level `p`. It introduces no equation or estimate. The separate construction sets $C_0=0$, so the first block is $V_1$, and the frequency estimates explain why the preceding divergence correction belongs at the next oscillatory level.

Default-value audit (b5): The predecessor p−1 is natural subtraction, so p=0 selects index zero. Uses at positive levels and the zero initial correction establish the paper interpretation; the definition alone is not a recurrence.
TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.Y.summary: Oscillation with the preceding divergence correction

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.Z.text: The full level-$p$ block is $Z_p=Y_p+B_p$. Here `u.Y p` contains `u.V p + u.C (p-1)`: the Lean completion `C (p-1)` corresponds to the paper’s $C_p$. This definition alone imposes neither phase independence on the mean nor transversality on the oscillation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.Z.summary: The oscillatory block with its mean correction

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.divergence_.text: The finite velocity has zero divergence when every completed oscillation `u.V i + u.C i` and every mean `u.B i` has zero image under the supplied linear map `divergence`. The theorem assumes these properties on retained indices only. It does not establish that the map is a differential divergence.
TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.divergence_.summary: Sum the divergence-free completed waves and means

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.pressure.text: The finite pressure is the sum of `u.p p + u.q p` over $1\le p\le P$. These fields represent the oscillatory pressure and the pressure from the mean equation. Neither zero phase mean nor the normalization $\bar q_1=0$ follows from the sum itself; later construction lemmas supply them.

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.pressure_me.text: Adds the oscillatory and mean pressure components over the retained finite depth, using submodule closure. Membership is assumed for every storage level. When the submodule is the even-reflection class this gives the pressure parity, but the generic statement itself is not restricted to any particular symmetry or differential equation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.pressure_me.summary: The total pressure inherits the pressure symmetry

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.velocity.text: For a nonnegative depth $P$, this is the finite sum of the oscillations $V_p$, their generated divergence corrections and the means $B_p$, for $1\le p\le P$. The formal indexing stores the correction generated by $V_p$ at index $p$; the paper denotes it by $C_{p+1}$. Consequently the sum in paper notation is $\sum_{p=1}^P(V_p+C_{p+1}+B_p)$. If $P=0$, it is zero. The definition applies to arbitrary families in an additive space; transversality, phase means, differential equations and estimates are not assumptions of this sum. Evaluation at the transported phase and addition of the parent produce the physical approximate velocity.
TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.velocity.summary: The sum includes the last divergence correction

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.velocity_eq.text: If `hP : 1 ≤ P`, `hC₀ : u.C 0 = 0`, and both `V` and `B` vanish at $P+1$, then the finite velocity equals the sum of `u.Z i` through $P+1$. The added block consists only of the final completion, stored as `u.C P`.
TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.velocity_eq.summary: Include the last divergence correction as one block

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.velocity_eq.text: Let $P\ge1$ and suppose the first correction in the paper's indexing is $C_1=0$. For arbitrary families of vectors in an additive group, the formal statement proves $\sum_{p=1}^P(V_p+C_{p+1}+B_p)=\sum_{p=1}^P Z_p+C_{P+1}$, where $Z_p=V_p+C_p+B_p$. The stored correction at index $p$ is generated by $V_p$, which accounts for the shift by one. Thus the completed final oscillation contributes $C_{P+1}$ even though there is no retained $V_{P+1}$. This is an equality of finite sums; no evolution equation, support property or norm estimate is used.
TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.velocity_eq.summary: Reindexing gives the expansion displayed in the introduction

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.velocity_me.text: If every storage level has the prescribed memberships, the finite sum defining the perturbation at depth `P` lies in the velocity submodule. Each summand includes the oscillation, its stored completion and the mean. The theorem is finite and algebraic; it makes no assertion about an infinite hierarchy or its convergence.
TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.velocity_me.summary: The finite perturbation inherits the velocity symmetry

TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.velocity_su.text: For a linear `average`, suppose every oscillation and completion averages to zero and every mean is fixed by averaging. Subtracting the average of the finite velocity then leaves exactly the sum of `V p + C p`. This algebraic identity applies to any depth, including the empty sum.
TorusEuler.HierarchyProfiles.velocity_su.summary: Subtracting the mean leaves the completed oscillations

TorusEuler.HierarchyRelayCoefficientJets.text:
A finite smooth coefficient budget shared by the normalized potential and pressure operators and the inverse-radius coframe rows.

Default-value audit (b5): Unlike a raw word bound, this predicate explicitly includes smoothness of the phase-independent coefficient lift. It records derivative estimates as assumptions rather than deriving them.
TorusEuler.HierarchyRelayCoefficientJets.summary: Derivative bounds for potential and pressure coefficients

TorusEuler.HierarchyRelayCoefficientJets.text: If order-`j` coefficient jets are bounded by $C_j A D^{qj}$ and $\ell D^q\le1$, their weighted finite-order budget is $(\sum_{j\le n}C_j)A$. The coefficient is globally smooth, and all scalar budgets and scales are nonnegative. Thus the derivative-order growth is absorbed by the label radius, while `A` retains the order-independent parent loss.
TorusEuler.HierarchyRelayCoefficientJets.summary: Rescaling absorbs the derivative-order growth of parent coefficients

TorusEuler.HierarchyRelayWordBound.text:
A uniform bound for the individual weighted derivatives in the finite sup norm. The order counts labels and phase together.

Default-value audit (b5): The predicate bounds totalized directional derivatives and includes the zeroth word. It alone does not assert smoothness; the analytic estimates separately require smooth inputs before interpreting higher words as classical derivatives.
TorusEuler.HierarchyRelayWordBound.summary: A uniform bound for every weighted derivative word

TorusEuler.HierarchyRelayWordBound.clm_a.text: Applying a bounded coefficient to a bounded profile costs the product of their word bounds with the finite Leibniz factor.
TorusEuler.HierarchyRelayWordBound.clm_a.summary: Leibniz bounds for applying a coefficient field

TorusEuler.HierarchyRelayWordBound.finit.text: A uniform bound `B` for every admissible weighted derivative word gives a finite word norm bounded by the number of words times `B`. The nonnegative component of `HierarchyRelayWordBound` also bounds the inserted zero value in each supremum set. This converts individual derivative bounds into the exact finite norm.
TorusEuler.HierarchyRelayWordBound.finit.summary: A bound on each derivative controls their finite sum

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.text:
This is the subtype of functions belonging to the smooth-profile submodule. The stored representative is zero off the time slab and smooth within it; global smoothness across the two time boundaries is not asserted by the type.

Default-value audit (b5): The abbreviation inherits the zero-off-slab convention and within-slab smoothness. It does not state smoothness as a function on all real times.

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.advect.text: A linear direction map `D` turns an advecting profile into a smooth direction field. The resulting bilinear operator differentiates the second profile along that field using the actual slab derivative. This separates the geometry of the direction from differentiation of the advected profile.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.advect.summary: Use one profile to choose another’s derivative direction

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.advect.text: At a slab point, advection of `f` by `a` is `fderivWithin` of `f` evaluated on the direction `(D a).val x`. The positive-time and membership hypotheses justify this pointwise formula. It shows explicitly that the derivative falls on the second argument.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.advect.summary: Read advection as an actual directional derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.applyF.text: This bilinear map evaluates an operator-valued smooth profile on a vector-valued smooth profile pointwise. The first argument provides a bounded linear operator at each point, while the second provides its input. Joint smoothness is preserved, and both additive and scalar linearity are proved in the profile spaces.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.applyF.summary: Multiply a smooth operator field by a profile

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.applyF.text: At an on-slab point, `applyField A f` equals the bounded linear operator `A.val x` applied to `f.val x`. This equality exposes the concrete multiplication hidden by the two linear-map wrappers. It supplies the evaluation rule used in coframe directions and material derivatives.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.applyF.summary: Read the operator applied to its local vector

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.consta.text: The constant profile has the specified value `a` throughout the closed slab and uses the standard zero representative outside it. It supplies coordinate directions and fixed vectors to profile operators. Despite the name, its representative need not be globally constant when `a` is nonzero.

For any point satisfying the slab membership hypothesis, the value of `constant a` is exactly `a`. The theorem distinguishes the mathematical constant on the slab from its zero extension outside. It is used when fixed time, label, or phase directions enter differential operators.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.consta.summary: Evaluate a constant profile within the slab

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.contDi.text: Two vector fields smooth on the hierarchy profile slab have a cross product smooth on that same slab. The proof expands the three coordinates into sums and products of scalar components. It does not require nonvanishing or transversality; those properties enter the normalized potential separately.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.contDi.summary: Taking a cross product preserves smoothness on the slab

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.contDi.text: Graph evaluation preserves the full joint smoothness within the slab.

For positive slab length, averaging a vector profile over its unit-period phase produces a jointly smooth function of time, label, and phase on the slab. The averaged expression ignores the output phase coordinate. The proof uses the parameter-dependent phase integral, together with convexity and unique differentiability of the parameter domain.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.contDi.summary: Phase averaging preserves smoothness on the slab

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.contDi.text: For positive slab length, smooth covector and velocity profiles yield a smooth wave potential provided the covector read at phase zero never vanishes on the slab. The definition freezes that covector in the phase variable before integrating. The conclusion is `ContDiffOn` on the slab, not global smoothness of the zero extension.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.contDi.summary: The normalized potential is smooth on the profile slab

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.contDi.text: Fixing any time in the closed slab gives a globally smooth function of label and phase. The conclusion includes boundary times because the profile stores smoothness within the slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.contDi.summary: A smooth slab profile has smooth spatial slices

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.contin.text: At a time belonging to $[0,T]$ and a fixed spatial label, a smooth hierarchy profile is continuous as a function of phase. This follows by restricting its smooth label-and-phase slice along a constant-label inclusion. No assertion is made about regularity across the slab’s time boundary.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.contin.summary: Every phase slice of a smooth profile is continuous

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.contin.text: At a time `ht : t ∈ Icc 0 T`, the phase slice of a smooth profile is continuous on the whole real phase line. The argument composes on-slab continuity with the slice inclusion. This continuity supplies integrability and linearity properties for the phase mean.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.contin.summary: Every fixed time-label phase slice is continuous

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.deriva.text: For `hT : 0 < T`, this linear map sends a smooth profile to its Fréchet derivative within the slab, represented again by zero extension. Positive slab length gives unique derivatives at the time endpoints. The result is a profile of continuous linear maps on the full time-label-phase space.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.deriva.summary: Differentiate within the closed time slab

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.deriva.text: For positive slab length, a direction profile `D` defines a linear differentiation operator on smooth profiles. It first takes the derivative within the slab and then evaluates that derivative on the direction at the same point. The direction may vary in time, label, and phase.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.deriva.summary: Differentiate along a smooth field of directions

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.deriva.text: The directional derivative profile evaluates to the Fréchet derivative within the slab applied to `D.val x`. The hypotheses require positive slab length and membership of the evaluation point. This is the explicit chain-rule form used to interpret label, phase, and time differentiation.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.deriva.summary: Read the directional derivative at a slab point

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.deriva.text: At an on-slab point, applying the profile derivative gives exactly `fderivWithin` of its stored function with respect to the closed slab. The parameter `hT` supplies positive slab length. No global differentiability of the zero extension is asserted or needed to read this equality.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.deriva.summary: Evaluate the actual derivative within the slab

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.diverg.text: A transverse profile plus its curl completion yields a divergence-free Eulerian field after graph evaluation. The covector is nonzero, the inverse-label chart is twice differentiable, and the coframe and covector must agree with its actual derivative at every graph label. This theorem transfers the already-established slow-fast cancellation to ordinary spatial divergence.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.diverg.summary: A completed transverse oscillation is physically divergence free

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.diverg.text: Given the inverse-label derivative and agreement of the coframe and covector at the graph point, ordinary Eulerian divergence equals the graph evaluation of total profile divergence. The profile is smooth on a positive-length slab and the chosen time lies in it. This also works at time endpoints because only spatial differentiation is used.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.diverg.summary: Graph evaluation turns profile divergence into Eulerian divergence

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.diverg.text: A zero profile divergence transports to zero Eulerian divergence.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.diverg.summary: Zero profile divergence gives an incompressible physical field

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.eq_zer.text: The field is smooth on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$; phase periodicity is unnecessary for this continuity argument. A smooth correction that vanishes before activation also vanishes at $t_0$, provided $0<t_0\le T$. This supplies the zero value at the beginning of the active interval in §5.4. When $t_0=0$, the same conclusion comes from the prescribed zero initial velocity, rather than from earlier vanishing.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.eq_zer.summary: Continuity carries inactivity to the activation time

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.eq_zer.text: Every smooth slab profile is stored as a function that vanishes outside `hierarchyProfileSlab T`. The hypothesis `hx` identifies such a point, and the theorem projects the stored zero-extension property. It says nothing about a smooth extension across the time endpoints; derivatives used later are derivatives within the slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.eq_zer.summary: Profiles are represented by zero outside the slab

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.euclid.text: For `i : Fin 3`, this is the Euclidean coordinate vector with component one at index $i$ and zero at the other two indices. The finite index type rules out invalid coordinates. The basis is used to reconstruct a vector gradient from its three scalar directional derivatives.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.euclid.summary: The coordinate vectors for the physical gradient

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.exists.text: Smooth label fields `B` and `q` satisfying the mean momentum equation on the slab are lifted to phase-independent profiles and packaged as a `HierarchyMeanOutput`. The conclusion preserves their actual values and proves the concrete material-plus-label-gradient equation. No endpoint conditions or existence of `B,q` are proved here; those belong to the endpoint mean solver.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.exists.summary: A supplied smooth mean equation gives the hierarchy mean output

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.exists.text: Smooth phase-independent strain and covector coefficients, nonzero initial covectors, their covector evolution, and a smooth periodic zero-mean source give a concrete transverse output. The velocity starts at zero, and both velocity and pressure are periodic in phase. The theorem invokes the smooth transverse ODE solver, then identifies its momentum equation with the hierarchy operators.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.exists.summary: The smooth zero-initial transverse solve supplies hierarchy data

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.exists.text: Given smooth velocity and pressure on the slab, zero velocity phase mean, pointwise transversality, and the prescribed momentum equation, this theorem packages them as a `HierarchyTransverseOutput`. The conclusion preserves both supplied functions on every slab slice. It assumes the analytic solution and does not prove its existence or impose an initial condition.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.exists.summary: A supplied transverse solution realizes the hierarchy equation

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.ext.text: Two smooth slab profiles agreeing on the slab are equal as stored functions, because both use the specified zero extension outside it. No global continuation argument is involved.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.ext.summary: Equality on the slab determines the stored profile

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.fderiv.text: For a positive slab and closed envelope `S`, proves that a profile vanishing before activation or outside `S` has zero full within-slab derivative there. Closedness makes the inactive condition relatively open. Local equality to zero and uniqueness of within derivatives justify the result; pointwise vanishing at an isolated point would not suffice.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.fderiv.summary: A derivative vanishes on the relatively open inactive region

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.fderiv.text: At a time in the slab, evaluates the spatial derivative of a fixed-phase profile slice by applying the full within-slab derivative to direction `(0,d,0)`. Smoothness is built into the profile. The slice insertion stays in the slab for all labels, so this chain-rule identity does not require an ambient time extension.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.fderiv.summary: A label derivative is a direction of the full slab derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.graphR.text:
Read the actual smooth profile on the transported graph.

Default-value audit (b5): The profile is only asserted smooth within its time slab. Its stored zero extension is used outside; graph evaluation alone does not prove global smoothness across the time endpoints.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.graphR.summary: Reading a profile on the transported graph

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.graph_.text: The sum of the three coordinate components times their Euclidean basis vectors equals the original vector. This finite-dimensional identity is unconditional. It converts the coordinate definition of the profile label gradient into the adjoint-coframe expression used by the physical pressure chain rule.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.graph_.summary: Coordinate components reconstruct the gradient vector

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.hasDer.text: The phase direction ranges over the entire real line at each fixed time and label.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.hasDer.summary: The phase derivative along a profile slice

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.hasDer.text: Restriction to a time line extracts the actual time derivative, including at the boundary of the closed slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.hasDer.summary: The time derivative along a profile slice

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.hierar.text:
The actual profile operators in (5.20) and (5.25) on a closed time slab.

Default-value audit (b5): Derivative values must be read with the regularity and slab hypotheses of the source construction; raw totalized derivatives alone do not establish classical differentiability.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.hierar.summary: Concrete differential operators on the time slab

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.hierar.text: Evaluation of the material operator is the within-slab time derivative of the profile plus multiplication by M. The operator has been expressed in parent labels, so no separate label transport term appears here.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.hierar.summary: The material operator is time derivative plus strain

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelA.text: If the coframe and both input profiles are phase independent, their label advection is phase independent as well. The derivative acts only on the label slice, whose values do not change with phase. This verifies the mean-product condition used to cancel the source’s inactive-region average.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelA.summary: Slow advection of means remains independent of phase

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelD.text: The operator profile `G` acts pointwise on a velocity profile, and its result is inserted into the label component of the joint direction. The resulting map is linear in the velocity. The definition uses the given coframe values but does not assert that they come from an inverse flow.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelD.summary: The coframe turns velocity into a label direction

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelD.text: At an on-slab point, the direction selected from `G` and `u` is exactly `(0, G.val x (u.val x), 0)`. Thus only the label coordinates vary. The theorem exposes the pointwise meaning of the composed profile maps without imposing extra geometry on `G`.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelD.summary: Read the coframe direction in coordinates

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelG.text:
The three scalar coframe derivatives form the Eulerian label gradient.

Default-value audit (b5): Derivative values must be read with the regularity and slab hypotheses of the source construction; raw totalized derivatives alone do not establish classical differentiability. Finite sums and index sets are defined at zero order or empty ranges as well. The paper use supplies the intended order and level restrictions.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelG.summary: The three slow derivatives of a scalar profile

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelG.text: The bundled slow gradient is the sum of within-slab directional derivatives in the three coframe directions, multiplied by their Eulerian basis vectors. This is an evaluation identity at a point of the slab, rather than an estimate.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelG.summary: The slow gradient written in coordinate directions

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelG.text: The coframe label gradient of a scalar profile is the coframe transpose applied to its ordinary label gradient.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelG.summary: Label pressure gradients use the transposed coframe

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelG.text: If the label component of a scalar profile’s derivative is represented by the vector `qa`, then its encoded label gradient at a slab point equals the coframe adjoint applied to `qa`. Positive slab length supplies the derivative operator. The statement identifies the representation rather than proving a pressure or flow equation.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelG.summary: The encoded label gradient is the adjoint coframe gradient

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.labelI.text: This bounded linear map embeds a vector of labels into the joint time-label-phase space, with zero time and phase components. It is a coordinate inclusion used when the coframe converts a physical direction into a label direction. No differential or flow property is asserted.

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.linear.text: For a smooth periodic parent flow and coefficient profiles equal to its actual inverse coframe, strain and transported covector, the physical graph of the material and pressure operators equals the linearized momentum expression. The time derivative is taken within the closed slab. The proof polarizes the nonlinear graph identity to remove quadratic self-advection of the perturbation.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.linear.summary: The profile mean equation becomes physical linearized momentum

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.localR.text: A smooth profile satisfying a given scalar reflection law on the slab satisfies that law globally as a representative function. Reflection preserves the time slab, and the profile is zero outside it. This is a support convention argument, not a claim that the representative is globally smooth across endpoint times.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.localR.summary: Reflection parity on the slab extends to its zero representative

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.map.text: A bounded linear map `Fmap : E →L[ℝ] F` acts on each value of a smooth slab profile, producing another smooth profile. The result is linear in the input profile. Boundedness gives continuous linear postcomposition and therefore preservation of the supplied smoothness on the slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.map.summary: Apply a bounded linear map to profile values

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.map_ap.text: At a point of the time slab, the profile obtained by `map Fmap f` has value `Fmap (f.val x)`. This is the pointwise interpretation of bounded linear postcomposition. The on-slab hypothesis removes the constructor’s zero-extension branch before applying the map.

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.moment.text: At a slab point, the residual of the parent plus a graph-read perturbation equals the graph-read concrete profile momentum plus the parent residual. The assumptions identify `G`, `M`, and `κ` with the actual inverse-label derivative, parent gradient, and transported covector. The inverse-label transport equation and differentiability hypotheses are supplied explicitly.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.moment.summary: Profile momentum evaluates to the physical residual identity

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.moment.text:
Let $U$ be smooth and periodic on $[0,T]	imes\mathbb R^3$, with smooth inverse flow $a=X_{t,0}(x)$, and let $W(t,a,s)$ and $q(t,a,s)$ be smooth profiles. Identify their coefficients with $(D_aX)^{-1}$, $M=
abla U\circ X$ and $\kappa=(D_aX)^{-T}k_*$. Then the momentum residual of $U+W^
atural,p+q^
atural$ equals $R_U$ plus the evaluation of $(\partial_t+M)W+(W\cdot\widetilde{\mathbf d})W+\widetilde{\mathbf d}q$, where $f^
atural(t,x)=f(t,a,k_*\cdot a)$. Spatial differentiability of $p$ is required at the evaluation point. The time derivative is taken within $[0,T]$. This is the coordinate identity used in Lemma 5.8, before applying the expansion equations.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.moment.summary: Transport the complete profile momentum into physical coordinates

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.ofSmoo.text: Given `hf : ContDiffOn ℝ ∞ f (hierarchyProfileSlab T)`, this returns the same function on the closed slab and zero everywhere else. The construction creates a representative suitable for pointwise linear algebra. It requires smoothness only within the slab and does not make the zero extension globally smooth.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.ofSmoo.summary: Represent a smooth slab function by its zero extension

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.ofSmoo.text: At a point satisfying `hx : x ∈ hierarchyProfileSlab T`, the representative constructed by `ofSmooth` evaluates to the original function `f x`. The membership condition is essential because the constructor replaces values outside the slab with zero. This lemma removes the representation wrapper in pointwise equations.

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.phaseD.text: If the fixed-time, fixed-label phase slice of a smooth profile is constant, its joint within-slab derivative in any pure phase direction `(0,0,c)` vanishes. The time must belong to the slab. This establishes the vanishing phase-advection and phase-gradient conditions required when a mean field is packaged into the hierarchy.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.phaseD.summary: Phase-independent profiles have zero phase derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.phaseD.text: The transported covector profile `κ` is converted to its inner-product functional and applied to an advecting velocity. The scalar result is inserted into the phase coordinate. This gives a linear map from velocity profiles to pure phase directions, including zero when the velocity is transverse.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.phaseD.summary: Contract velocity with the transported covector

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.phaseD.text: At a point of the slab, `phaseDirections κ u` is `(0, 0, ⟪κ,u⟫)`, with both fields evaluated at that point. Only the phase component changes. This identity makes the transversality condition visible as the vanishing of the entire fast direction.

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.phaseG.text:
The fast scalar derivative of the pressure multiplies the transported covector.

Default-value audit (b5): Derivative values must be read with the regularity and slab hypotheses of the source construction; raw totalized derivatives alone do not establish classical differentiability.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.phaseG.summary: The fast pressure gradient follows the transported covector

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.phaseG.text: At a slab point, the fast gradient is the directional derivative in the phase variable multiplied by the covector. The derivative is taken with time and label fixed.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.phaseG.summary: The fast gradient is covector times phase derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.phaseI.text: This bounded linear coordinate inclusion sends a scalar to a direction with only a phase component. It is used after contracting an advecting velocity with the transported covector. The definition concerns the joint coordinate space, without imposing periodicity or a nonzero phase speed.

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.pressu.text: This private linear map evaluates a smooth hierarchy profile on a specified physical phase graph at a fixed time and position. Linearity follows from pointwise addition and scalar multiplication of profiles. The definition accepts arbitrary `A`, `k`, time and position; geometric correctness and slab membership are hypotheses in subsequent uses.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.pressu.summary: Graph evaluation is linear in the profile

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: Let $T>0$ and let $V$, a matrix field $G$, and a covector field be smooth on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$. The formal definition first uses the covector at phase zero, assumed nonzero, to form $Q[V]=-\partial_s^{-1}(\kappa\times V/|\kappa|^2)$, and then takes the curl of $D_aQ[V]G$ at fixed phase. In the paper $G=(D_aX)^{-1}$ and $\kappa$ is independent of phase, giving $C[V]=\mathbf d\times Q[V]$. The formula alone assumes neither transversality nor periodicity. To conclude that $V+C[V]$ is divergence free, the covector and derivative directions must come from the same flow and $V$ must be transverse.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Take the curl of the phase potential at fixed phase

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: Fix $T>0$, an activation time $\tau$ and a closed label set $S$. Suppose the smooth profile $V(t,a,s)$ vanishes for every phase whenever $0\le t\le T$ and either $t<\tau$ or $a\notin S$. With smooth derivative matrix $G$ and nonzero covector, the formal statement proves the same vanishing for $C[V]$. Phase integration preserves the label set, and label differentiation is local on its open complement. This gives the support control used by the construction. The paper states the conclusion for the support at each fixed time; the formal hypothesis uses one common closed set throughout the interval.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The correction vanishes wherever the common support condition holds

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: At any slab time, including an endpoint, assume the entire label-phase slice of `V` vanishes. Its concrete divergence completion vanishes on that slice as well. The proof uses only label and phase operations, so no time neighborhood of zero values is needed. A nonzero covector on the slab is required by the completion construction.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Completion preserves an identically zero time slice

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: Fix $t\in[0,T]$, $T>0$, and a twice continuously differentiable coordinate map $A$. Suppose the derivative directions at label $A(x)$ equal $D_xA$, the nonzero covector there equals $(D_xA)^Tk_*$, and $\kappa\cdot V=0$ for all labels and phases. The formal statement proves $\partial_s(\kappa\cdot C[V])=-\mathbf d\cdot V$ at every $x,s$, with $\mathbf d=(D_xA)^T\nabla_a$. In the paper $A=X(t,\cdot)^{-1}$. No claim about an arbitrary unrelated matrix field is made. This is the derivative identity preceding (3.6); recovering $\kappa\cdot C[V]$ itself additionally uses its zero phase mean.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The correction cancels the slow divergence after phase differentiation

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: On $[0,T]$, let $V$ be smooth, period one in phase and of zero phase mean, with $V(t,-a,-s)=-V(t,a,s)$. Assume the smooth derivative matrix and covector are even under the same reflection and the covector at phase zero never vanishes. The formal statement proves $C[V](t,-a,-s)=-C[V](t,a,s)$. The normalized phase primitive changes the parity once, and the label curl changes it again. This is the correction part of the oddness argument in §3.1. Oddness of the physical velocity follows after evaluation along an odd inverse flow; that evaluation is not part of this conclusion.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Simultaneous reflection of label and phase changes the correction sign

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: For a nonzero covector and transverse input, the profile plus its curl completion has zero slow-plus-fast divergence. The hypotheses identify `G` with the derivative of a twice differentiable inverse chart `A` and `κ` with its adjoint applied to the launch covector. This proves the geometric claim at every phase, rather than merely along one evaluated graph.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The completed transverse profile is divergence free in the chart

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: At a time in the closed slab, applying the profile’s within-slab derivative to `(0,d,0)` equals the ordinary Fréchet derivative of its fixed-time, fixed-phase label slice applied to `d`. The label line remains entirely within the slab. This identifies the coordinate calculus used by the concrete hierarchy with familiar spatial derivatives.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The label component of the joint derivative is spatial differentiation

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: For a positive slab length, this linear operator takes the joint within-slab derivative of a smooth vector profile and restricts it to label directions. Its output is a smooth profile of continuous linear maps. The following evaluation theorem identifies it with the ordinary label derivative on the slab, including endpoint times.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The profile derivative with time and phase fixed

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: At any time in $[0,T]$, evaluating the profile label differential gives the ordinary Fréchet derivative of the label slice with time and phase fixed. Positive slab length ensures the joint derivative operator is valid. The spatial inclusion stays inside the slab, so no time-boundary extension is needed.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The encoded label differential is the ordinary spatial derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text:
The slow divergence contracts the label derivative with the inverse-flow differential in the Eulerian directions.

Default-value audit (b5): The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The slow divergence in parent coordinates

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: At fixed time and phase, the slow divergence is the trace of the label derivative composed with the inverse-flow differential. This identifies the coordinate definition with the invariant contraction used in the paper.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Slow divergence is a coframe trace contraction

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: This continuous linear inclusion sends a spatial label increment to the corresponding joint increment with zero time and phase components. It identifies exactly which directions are differentiated by the label differential. The map is constructed from the standard left and right product inclusions.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The label direction inside the joint profile space

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text:
Averaging the actual unit-period phase yields a smooth phase-independent profile.

Default-value audit (b5): The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Averaging a smooth profile over one phase period

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: At a point of the slab, evaluation of the averaged profile is the unit-period phase mean at the same time and label. The result explains the average operator used by the hierarchy.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The bundled phase average equals the unit-period integral

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: Let $T>0$, let $V$, $G$ and $\kappa$ be smooth profiles on the closed time slab, and assume $G$ is independent of phase and $\kappa(t,a,0)\ne0$. The formal statement proves $\int_0^1C[V](t,a,s)\,ds=0$. It uses the normalized potential, whose mean is zero, and commutes phase integration with the label derivative. No transversality or period-one hypothesis on $V$ is needed for this average identity. In the paper $G=(D_aX)^{-1}$, so its phase independence is automatic. This fixes the integration constant when the longitudinal derivative is integrated to obtain (3.6).
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Averaging commutes with the curl when its coefficients are phase independent

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: If `h` says that every on-slab phase slice is constant, its phase average equals the original profile. The proof identifies the integrand with a constant and uses the normalized average of a constant. Equality outside the slab follows from the common zero-extension representation.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Averaging leaves a phase-independent profile unchanged

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: If the coframe is independent of phase and the potential has zero phase average, its slow curl also has zero phase average. The proof commutes the label derivative through the phase integral and then applies the fixed linear curl map. The phase-independence hypothesis on `G` is essential to moving that coefficient outside the average.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The slow curl preserves zero phase average

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: For $T>0$, take smooth profiles $V$ and $\kappa$ with $\kappa(t,a,0)\ne0$ on $[0,T]$. The potential is formed at each fixed $(t,a)$ using that covector and the primitive whose average over $0\le s\le1$ is subtracted. The formal statement proves $\int_0^1Q[V](t,a,s)\,ds=0$. It does not require $V$ to be transverse, periodic or of zero phase mean. Those latter phase conditions ensure periodicity of the potential in the paper; subtraction of an additive mean by itself does not turn a primitive with nonzero drift into a periodic function.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Subtracting the primitive mean fixes its additive constant

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text:
The fast divergence contracts the phase derivative with the transported covector.

Default-value audit (b5): Derivative values must be read with the regularity and slab hypotheses of the source construction; raw totalized derivatives alone do not establish classical differentiability.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The phase derivative contribution to divergence

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: At a slab point, the fast divergence is the inner product of the covector with the phase derivative of the vector profile. The label coordinates are fixed in this derivative.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Fast divergence pairs the covector with the phase derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text:
The slow Eulerian curl of the potential in the label chart.

Default-value audit (b5): The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The slow curl in parent label coordinates

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: For smooth $Q(t,a,s)$ and matrix field $G(t,a,s)$ on $[0,T]$, $T>0$, the formal statement identifies the slow curl at any time in the interval with the ordinary curl components of the linear map $D_aQ\,G$. Time and phase are held fixed in this derivative. When $G=(D_aX)^{-1}$, the three columns give the Eulerian coordinate directions expressed in labels, and the expression is $\mathbf d\times Q$. The equality holds without assuming that $G$ arises from a flow. It displays the one label derivative in the correction; it is not a quantitative norm estimate.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The slow curl uses one label derivative of the potential

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: Let $T>0$, fix $t\in[0,T]$, and let $A:\mathbb R^3\to\mathbb R^3$ be $C^2$. Suppose the smooth matrix field $G$ satisfies $G(t,A(x),s)=D_xA$ for every $x,s$. For every smooth potential $Q$, the formal statement proves that the divergence at fixed phase of its slow curl vanishes at labels $A(x)$. Indeed, after composition with $A$ this is the usual divergence of the curl of $Q(t,A(x),s)$. In §3.1, $A$ is the inverse flow. The compatibility with a single coordinate map is essential; the result is not asserted for arbitrary derivative directions.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: A common coordinate map supplies the divergence cancellation

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: If the coframe and potential are each one-periodic in phase at a fixed time, their slow curl is one-periodic as well. Equality of phase-shifted potential slices gives equality of their label derivatives. The theorem does not need phase independence of the coframe, only the stated periodicity.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The slow curl preserves phase periodicity

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: If the coframe and potential are even under joint reflection of labels and phase, taking the slow curl makes the result odd. A label derivative reverses the potential’s reflection sign, while the coframe does not change it. The statement holds for smooth profile representatives on a positive-length slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The slow curl of an even potential is odd

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text:
The total divergence operator for a vector profile at arbitrary label and phase.

Default-value audit (b5): The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The sum of slow and fast profile divergence

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: On the slab, evaluating the total profile-divergence operator gives the sum of the coframe-weighted label trace and the covector paired with the phase derivative. This theorem unfolds both encoded operators into ordinary derivatives. It holds for any smooth input profile and does not require transversality or zero divergence.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Total profile divergence is the slow trace plus phase contraction

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: If each inverse chart is surjective and twice differentiable, and the coframe and covector agree with its derivative, the completed transverse profile has total divergence zero as a profile-space equality. Surjectivity matters: it extends the cancellation from labels reached by the chart to every label and every phase on the slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: Surjective inverse charts give divergence cancellation at every label

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: For a phase-independent mean profile, zero physical divergence of its graph evaluation implies zero total profile divergence, provided the differentiable inverse charts are surjective and the geometric coefficients match them. Phase independence transfers the physical graph’s conclusion to arbitrary phase values. The solenoidal physical mean is an explicit hypothesis.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: A solenoidal physical mean has zero profile divergence

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: This continuous linear map sends a three-dimensional derivative operator to the trace of its underlying linear map. Additivity and real homogeneity come from trace. Finite dimensionality makes the linear map continuous, allowing it to act on smooth profile fields when defining the slow divergence.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The matrix trace as a continuous linear map

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text:
The actual phase primitive defining `Q[V]`. The covector is read at phase zero because the geometric covector is phase independent.

Default-value audit (b5): The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The phase primitive defining the vector potential

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: On the slab, the profile potential evaluates to the normalized phase primitive of the cross product with the covector at phase zero. The construction requires a nonzero covector; reading it at phase zero matches its later phase-independent use.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: The bundled potential has the pointwise integral formula

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: At a fixed time and label, a one-periodic velocity profile with zero phase mean gives a one-periodic normalized wave potential. The covector is nonzero throughout the slab so the profile constructor is defined with its regularity proof. The statement does not require transversality because periodicity depends on the primitive’s mean, not on fast-curl inversion.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: A periodic zero-mean input has a periodic potential

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.text: With an even nonvanishing covector and an odd velocity under joint label-and-phase reflection, the normalized potential is even. The velocity must also have periodic zero-mean phase slices. Reversing phase changes the sign of integration, cancelling the input’s odd sign; the zero-mean normalization prevents an extra constant.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.profil.summary: An odd velocity has an even normalized potential

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.slabTi.text: This linear operator takes the derivative of a smooth slab profile in the direction $(1,0,0)$. Time changes while label and phase remain fixed. Its input `hT : 0 < T` makes the closed slab a domain with unique derivatives. After graph evaluation the same operation corresponds to a material derivative, so it must not be read as a fixed-position Eulerian derivative.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.slabTi.summary: Differentiate a profile at fixed label and phase

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.slabTi.text: At a point `z` belonging to the profile slab, `slabTimePartial` evaluates to the within-Fréchet derivative of the profile applied to $(1,0,0)$. The domain-membership hypothesis is essential because profile representatives are set to zero outside the slab. This gives the concrete meaning of the linear operator before its chain rule along the inverse flow.

Let $T>0$, let $U$ be a smooth periodic velocity on $[0,T]	imes\mathbb R^3$, and let $X$ be its two-time flow. Write $A(t,x)=X(t,0,x)$ for the inverse label map. For a smooth profile $f(t,a,s)$ and a fixed covector $k$, evaluate $f$ at $(t,A(t,x),k\cdot A(t,x))$ to obtain $f^
atural$. The formal statement proves $(\partial_t+U\cdot
abla)f^
atural=(\partial_t f)^
atural$ at every point of the closed slab. On the right, both label and phase are held fixed; endpoint time derivatives are taken from within $[0,T]$. This is the first-order identity behind the auxiliary note's formula for every order. Higher orders require repeated application; they are not the conclusion of this single declaration.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.slabTi.summary: Transporting a profile converts its time derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.smooth.text: A smooth profile carries smoothness within the closed time–label–phase slab. This projection of its membership condition is the regularity input for the concrete differential operators.
TorusEuler.HierarchySmoothProfile.smooth.summary: A bundled profile is smooth within its slab

TorusEuler.HierarchySourceTermBounds.text: This proposition bundles the exact mean decomposition, the zero-mean relay, three mean-product estimates, the parent residual estimate, and the relay, slow and fast transverse estimates. Derivative hypotheses are requested only when `n + 1 ≤ H`, and level hypotheses only from two through `P`. It is an input contract for assembly, not an existence theorem for those estimates.
TorusEuler.HierarchySourceTermBounds.summary: The individual source estimates needed by the recurrence

TorusEuler.HierarchySupportLaws.text:
Local operations preserve vanishing on the inactive region. Slow advection of two means is again fixed by the phase average.

Default-value audit (b5): These are preservation properties supplied for an operator family. The record does not prove locality or support preservation for arbitrary linear maps.
TorusEuler.HierarchySupportLaws.summary: Support properties of the hierarchy operations

TorusEuler.HierarchySupportLaws.construc.text: For depth at least one, propagates inactive-region membership through every oscillation, completion and oscillatory pressure, and through all retained transverse sources. It assumes support preservation of the selected transverse solver and completion. Means need only be fixed by averaging; neither their velocity nor their pressure is asserted to vanish on this region.
TorusEuler.HierarchySupportLaws.construc.summary: The selected recursion keeps oscillations in the inactive submodule

TorusEuler.HierarchySupportLaws.labelPro.text: If the two oscillatory blocks belong to the inactive submodule, the full label-advection product differs from the mean-mean product by an element of that submodule. Bilinearity expands the difference into terms with an inactive factor. No vanishing of the means is assumed, which is essential for the endpoint mean equation.
TorusEuler.HierarchySupportLaws.labelPro.summary: Removing the mean product leaves an inactive oscillatory term

TorusEuler.HierarchySupportLaws.partialS.text: Extracts the positive index bounds and exact sum relation from a filtered hierarchy interaction pair. These facts identify which lower levels appear in a source at level `p`. The natural subtraction in the level function is justified by the lower bound on the first index before arithmetic reasoning is applied.
TorusEuler.HierarchySupportLaws.partialS.summary: Source interactions use the prescribed level relation

TorusEuler.HierarchySupportLaws.remainde.text: Subtracts the retained tail sum of mean-mean label advections from the finite remainder and proves that the difference lies in the inactive submodule. All oscillations, completions and oscillatory pressures must be inactive. This identifies what remains; it does not assert that the full remainder vanishes outside the envelope.
TorusEuler.HierarchySupportLaws.remainde.summary: Only slow products of means survive outside the oscillations

TorusEuler.HierarchySupportLaws.transver.text: At level at least two, assumes older oscillations, completions and pressures vanish on the inactive region, while every mean is fixed by averaging. The preliminary source differs there from a sum of mean-mean products; subtracting its average removes that sum. The supplementary source also vanishes because its differentiated oscillatory factor is inactive.
TorusEuler.HierarchySupportLaws.transver.summary: Centering removes the surviving mean products outside the envelope

TorusEuler.HierarchyTransverseOutput.text:
Package an oscillatory velocity and pressure with zero phase mean and vanishing fast advection in every test direction. These are the algebraic constraints expected of a transverse hierarchy solve; the evolution equation is supplied by the solver separately.

Default-value audit (b5): The structure records velocity, pressure, zero phase mean, and zero fast self-advection constraints. It does not assert an ODE solve or nonzero amplitude, so the all-zero output is allowed.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTransverseOutput.summary: A transverse oscillation with its pressure

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.text:
This subtype imposes both period-one phase dependence and simultaneous label–phase lattice invariance on a smooth slab profile. These are exact function identities, not properties of a chosen Fourier approximation.

Default-value audit (b5): The underlying representative is zero outside the slab, with smoothness and twisted periodicity on its stored domain. The abbreviation adds no existence assertion for nonzero waves.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.summary: The space of twisted periodic slab profiles

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Label.text: This predicate asks that the phase-zero label slice be spatially periodic at every time of the slab. It does not by itself assert phase independence or periodicity at other phase values. Those additional facts are supplied when phase-independent coefficients or phase averages are sent to the torus mean solver.
