TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.text: Stores the deformation, inverse, material strain and time derivative on the label torus, with their evolution equations and exact profile values. Both inverse identities, finite coefficient bounds and the one-sided endpoint Hessian inequality are required. These are hypotheses for a real endpoint problem, not merely names for arbitrary bounded matrices.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.summary: The deformation data required by the endpoint mean solver

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.text: Requires the deformation, inverse and strain lifts to be even at every time in the closed slab. This property is used only when selecting the odd mean and even pressure from an endpoint solution. It does not assert oddness of the forcing or automatically establish parity of the solved fields.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.summary: The mean coefficients are even in their spatial labels

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.text: Uses the record’s `inverse_value` identity to show that the coframe profile has the same value at every phase. It is a lift of a torus coefficient depending only on time and label. This independence is needed for averaging and for slow advection of mean fields to remain a mean.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.summary: The inverse coframe profile is independent of phase

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.text: When the transverse covector agrees with the adjoint inverse deformation applied to the carrier, the mean geometry supplies smooth lift and pullback maps. They satisfy the time-evolution law, a left-inverse identity, and the transverse-projection identity. The theorem also proves the covector is nonzero on the active interval, using the geometric data rather than assuming an arbitrary projection.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.summary: The mean geometry supplies transverse coordinates and projection

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.text: Assume the central wave, coframe and strain bounds, compatibility of the covector, and the displayed small label-variation condition. Every fixed-plane homogeneous solution at a label within $2\ell$ of a lattice point has weighted growth at most $eD^3$. The theorem also supplies the positive central norm and its continuous within-interval derivative. The interval length is bounded by `T ≤ 1`.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.summary: The central wave controls forward growth on the envelope

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.text: At any time in the closed slab, the generator formed from the transverse strain, lift and pullback is spatially periodic in the label. This lets the forward stability estimate near the origin be transferred to every periodic copy of the envelope. The theorem states an exact periodicity property, not a bound on the generator.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.summary: The fixed-plane generator is periodic in the label

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.text:
The parent deformation lifts the fixed launch plane into the moving transverse plane.

Default-value audit (b5): The map is defined on the orthogonal complement of the launch covector. For k=0 that domain is the whole space; the actual launch assumptions exclude zero before treating it as a two-dimensional plane.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.summary: Lifting the launch plane into the transported plane

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.text:
The inverse parent deformation reads the coordinates of the transverse projection in the fixed launch plane.

Default-value audit (b5): The projected pullback is defined for arbitrary coefficient values. Its inverse relationship with the lift requires the coframe identities and a nonzero transported covector.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanC.summary: Reading fixed coordinates after transverse projection

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanR.text: Packages a mean output together with divergence-free label velocity, displacement vanishing at both endpoints, and the physical-component relation `B = F v`. It keeps the raw endpoint solution and states whether the output is unchanged or its odd part. Recovery and nonincreasing label-norm fields preserve quantitative information through that optional symmetry selection.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.MeanR.summary: One endpoint mean with its normalization and recovery data

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paper.text: Packages the qualitative approximation properties, oscillation and mean Hölder bounds, residual estimate, signed pressure-Hessian cap, central-gradient error and perturbed-flow deformation for one fixed `PhysicalApproximationData`. Every field concerns that same hierarchy and parent graph. The cutoff, `switchSize` and cost parameters are supplied freely; their identification with the paper quantities belongs to constructors. This proposition requires the listed facts rather than establishing them by its definition.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paper.summary: The physical estimates for one common approximation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text:
Exact coefficients with their physical values on the parent label slab.

Default-value audit (b5): The coefficient profiles are tied by value equalities to the specified U, X and k. The record also contains analytic mean and transverse data. These obligations must be constructed; they are not inferred from arbitrary profile fields.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: The physical coefficients carried by the parent geometry

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text: Builds the physical leading input from the explicit stationary-shear velocity and pressure profiles. The hypotheses require a nonzero carrier, a positive envelope fitting inside the centered cell, and phase width in $(0,1]$, as well as the exact parent and flow identifications. Both switch sources are zero because this first wave is already present at activation. Momentum, parity and transverse equations are included as proof fields.

For any set `S` containing the support of the periodized radial envelope, the constructed leading input satisfies `Inactive 0 S`. The proof uses vanishing of that envelope for both velocity and phase pressure; the two switch sources are identically zero. The conclusion is restricted to the hierarchy slab through the definition of `Inactive`, rather than an assertion about every real time.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: The first profiles vanish outside the envelope

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text: Under `hU` and `hX`, the parent velocity and two-time flow are exactly the stationary shear and its flow. The theorem identifies the general twisted hierarchy operators with the explicit first-wave operators by comparing the inverse deformation, material gradient and transported covector. It licenses reuse of the explicit wave equations for the actual parent geometry; it does not select that geometry.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: The stationary shear gives the same operators

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text: Proves surjectivity of the inverse parent chart and evaluates the coframe and covector on that chart. They become its Jacobian and the adjoint Jacobian applied to the carrier. The identities use the actual flow inverse relation, providing the chain-rule data needed when profiles are read as physical fields.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: The profile coframe becomes the actual inverse-chart derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text: Converts the parent-geometry reflection theorem into the `MeanCoefficients.Even` predicate for the exact selected coefficient record. The value identities tie the profile inverse and strain to their torus lifts. This lets the mean solver’s conditional symmetry clause apply to an odd forcing without selecting a new coefficient system.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: The selected mean coefficients have the required even symmetry

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text: For a divergence-free smooth periodic parent and a certified mean result, proves zero total profile divergence of the physical-component mean. Phase independence removes the fast derivative. The slow part follows from the volume-preserving parent deformation and divergence-free label velocity through the Piola identity, rather than from phase averaging alone.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: The physical mean is divergence free in profile coordinates

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text: Assume $0\le t_0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge1$, smooth periodic $U$, both deformations bounded by $\mathsf D$ and velocity derivatives bounded by $R_n\mathsf D^j$. Put $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$, $a\ge16$, and $\lambda=|\kappa(t_0,0)|>0$. For a positive continuous weight $\gamma$, zero-mean transverse profiles satisfy $\|C[V]\|_{[n],\gamma}\le K_n\lambda^{-1}\|V\|_{[n+1],\gamma}$, where $K_n=C_n\mathsf D^{2(15+a)}$. If $V_t+MV+\kappa\mathsf p_s=f$ with centered pressure, the same coefficient bounds $(\partial_t+M)C[V]+\mathbf d\mathsf p$ by the sum of the next-order norms of $V,f$. Centering of $V,f$ holds throughout $[0,T]$; transversality and the equation are needed only on $[t_0,T]$. These norms differentiate label and phase, not time, before dividing by $\gamma$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: Bound the correction and its material derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text: Let $0\le t_0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge1$ and $\lambda=|\kappa(t_0,0)|>0$. Assume a smooth periodic parent with both deformation bounds $\mathsf D$ and velocity derivative bounds $R_n\mathsf D^j$, and a localized seed whose leading velocity and pressure admit smooth compatible phase profiles. With $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$, $a\ge16$, and positive continuous $\gamma$, the formal statement supplies full-interval profiles agreeing with the unswitched $A_1,\mathsf p[A_1]$ on $[t_0,T]$. There they solve the homogeneous transverse equation. Both $C[A_1]$ and $(\partial_t+M)C[A_1]+\mathbf d\mathsf p[A_1]$ are bounded at order $n$ by $C_n\mathsf D^{2(15+a)}\lambda^{-1}\|A_1\|_{[n+1],\gamma}$. Nothing asserts vanishing of the unswitched wave before activation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: Estimate the leading wave throughout the active interval

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text: Specializes the mean-result divergence theorem to the exact output chosen by `physicalSolvers`. It requires the actual parent flow, smooth periodic divergence-free velocity, and `T ≤ 1` for the endpoint solver. This supplies a concrete zero-divergence certificate for the physical graph construction without changing the selected mean.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: The selected mean solve satisfies the graph divergence requirement

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text: For an actual odd smooth periodic parent flow, proves evenness of the inverse coframe, material strain, transported covector and deformation at labels. Oddness of the flow and evenness of the derivative of an odd map supply the sign relations. Profile parity outside the slab uses their zero representative convention.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: An odd parent gives even deformation, strain and covector

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text: The transverse covector of `ParentGeometry` equals the adjoint mean inverse applied to the fixed carrier at every slab point. This is the compatibility relation needed by the fixed transverse coordinate system. It identifies two representations of the same wave vector without introducing a new quantitative bound.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: The carrier is pulled back by the inverse coframe

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.text: At a slab time and label, `ParentGeometry` identifies its mean inverse with the derivative of the inverse flow evaluated along the forward flow, its strain with the physical velocity gradient there, and its covector with `labelWaveVector`. These are exact value identities connecting the stored coefficient profiles to the parent field.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Paren.summary: Read the transverse coefficients from the parent flow

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Phase.text: Records that the integral over one phase period vanishes for every time on $[0,T]$ and every label. The field is already a smooth twisted profile; this predicate adds its normalization. It is used when taking periodic phase primitives and when multiplying by coefficients independent of phase. It contains no estimate on the profile's size.

If `f` has zero phase mean and the operator-valued profile `c` is phase-independent on the slab, their pointwise application has zero phase mean. Completeness of the input and output spaces supports the phase integrals. At each time and label the fixed bounded linear map passes through the integral, so its application to the mean is zero.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Phase.summary: A phase independent coefficient preserves the zero mean

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Phase.text: If `hf` gives zero phase mean for a smooth profile, every time jet has zero phase mean on the same nondegenerate slab. The proof applies the earlier derivative-of-average theorem. This preserves the normalization needed to apply the phase primitive repeatedly while differentiating the auxiliary oscillatory hierarchy.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Phase.summary: Time differentiation preserves the zero phase mean

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Combines $T \le  1$, a physical leading input, and a phase-independent odd profile whose value on the slab equals the parent momentum residual pulled back by `X 0 t`. The pressure `p` and parent geometry are fixed parameters. The depth `P` indexes later constructions but is not constrained by the structure; existence does not establish the quantitative approximation estimates.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Parent residual and data for the finite expansion

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: This predicate requires a graph-evaluated profile time derivative of order $j$ to have spatial derivative bound $CB^m$ whenever $j\le q$ and $j+m\le N$. Time derivatives are taken on the profile before graph evaluation, so they are material derivatives after a flow readout. The total-order restriction is part of the predicate; it does not assert all pairs with $j\le q,m\le N$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Geometric spatial bounds for material profile time derivatives

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: This proposition records zero phase mean for the leading pressure and activation force, transversality of that force, and equality of `completionSwitch` with its selected completion. It does not store a new solution or numerical estimate. Together with the leading momentum equation already in the physical data, these fields justify the level-two relay cancellation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The leading wave normalization needed by the first correction

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: From `LeadingRelayData`, the stored completion switch has zero phase average. The proof rewrites it as completion of the activation force and uses the finite solver’s centering property with the supplied zero-force-mean field. This makes the switch suitable for both the averaged-source cancellation and the recurrence assembly.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The leading normalization centers the completion switch

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Defines the profile multiplying the activation derivative as the centered wrapped unswitched leading velocity plus its wrapped slow curl completion. It is a raw function of time, label, and phase. The definition itself does not claim time smoothness across activation; subsequent residual formulas only require its regularity on slices where the switch derivative is nonzero.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Unswitched leading velocity together with its completion

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: At a time on the parent slab, assumes two jets of the wrapped unswitched leading velocity, three jets of its actual wave potential, and two radius-weighted inverse-coframe jets. It bounds the activation primary by $\mathrm{BV} + \lVert \mathrm{curlOfDerivativeCLM}\rVert \cdot \ell^{-1}\cdot 4\cdot \mathrm{BP}\cdot \mathrm{BG}$. The identity uses the actual inverse deformation from parent geometry; the jet estimates are hypotheses, not consequences of the seed interface alone.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Two primary jets follow from the exact wrapped potential

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a hierarchy-regular active seed, assumes three scaled jets of the raw unswitched leading velocity, three scaled potential-coefficient jets, and two radius-weighted inverse-coframe jets. Centered wrapping and the normalized potential estimate then give two jets of the actual activation primary. The explicit budget is $\mathrm{BV} + \lVert \mathrm{curlOfDerivativeCLM}\rVert \cdot \ell^{-1}\cdot 4\cdot (16\cdot \mathrm{BK}\cdot \mathrm{BV})\cdot \mathrm{BG}$, exposing every finite derivative cost.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Three leading jets control two completed activation jets

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: At a slab time where the switch derivative is nonzero, the unswitched primary profile is smooth in label and phase. Its product with the switch derivative is already a smooth profile; division by this nonzero time-only scalar recovers the primary. The theorem intentionally makes no such inference on slices where that derivative vanishes.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Recover primary smoothness on an active switch slice

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: When `b.leading` is exactly the later-wave input built from the stated seed and parent, the sum of its two switch profiles at every slab slice equals the derivative of the time switch times `activationPrimary`. The identity uses the same coframe and transported covector as the hierarchy and applies to all labels and phases.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Both activation sources share one time factor

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: At depth $P\ge2$, the last retained velocity is a selected transverse correction with no activation switch. Its material completion plus label pressure gradient is bounded by the normalized relay estimate applied to its actual source. The right side uses measured oscillation and source sizes at order $n+1$, multiplied by one inverse frequency.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The last retained wave controls the linear tail

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Assuming $2 \le  P$, a smooth periodic odd divergence-free parent, smooth periodic even pressure, and the parent label flow, derives `PhysicalApproximationProperties b`. It discharges the previous theorem’s mean-divergence premise using the physical solver’s Piola identity. The conclusion remains qualitative: numerical size and pressure estimates are proved separately.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The selected hierarchy satisfies the qualitative approximation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For depth at least two, a smooth periodic odd divergence-free parent, even smooth periodic pressure, and its label flow, proves every `PhysicalApproximationProperties` field. The additional premise `hB` requires each selected mean solve to have zero total profile divergence. Reflection propagates through the hierarchy, curl completion handles transverse divergence, and graph identities give the exact residual.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Assemble the physical equations from mean incompressibility

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text:
For $P\ge2$, take the finite expansion built from the same smooth periodic parent $U,p$, its flow $X$, a leading profile with the prescribed reflection symmetry, and the actual residual $R_U=U_t+U\cdot
abla U+
abla p$. Assume $U$ is odd and divergence free. Then $V=U+W^
atural$ and $\Pi=p+\mathsf P^
atural$ are smooth and periodic on $[0,T]$, $V$ is odd and divergence free, and their momentum residual is the evaluated expansion remainder plus the two activation terms. Here $f^
atural(t,x)=f(t,X_{t,0}x,k_*\cdot X_{t,0}x)$. This proves the qualitative part of Lemma 5.8 for the selected construction; quantitative norm estimates are separate.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The constructed expansion supplies the qualitative physical assertions

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: At an index in levels two through `P`, the actual mean forcing is fixed by the hierarchy average. The averaged source is already phase independent, and the parent residual has the same property. This supplies the correct input condition for the selected mean solve and later label-only norm comparisons.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Every retained mean source is phase independent

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a level between two and `P`, the relay’s phase average vanishes if the leading pressure and completion switch are centered. The proof identifies the previous completion with the selected curl construction, obtains its zero mean, and combines this with the retained pressure normalization. This isolates the linear contribution from the mean source.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The selected linear relay has zero phase mean

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a retained level, the phase average of the actual source before the mean solve is a sum of oscillation advection, divergence–oscillation products, and mean–mean advection. The theorem uses the genuine inverse label flow, zero pressure mean, and centered switch. Its proof imports the geometric cancellation that replaces the fast averaged product by a slow derivative.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The selected mean source contains exactly three slow products

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For positive retained depth, a closed envelope set, and a leading input inactive before `t₀` or outside that set, the centered finite velocity profile is zero at every slab time strictly before activation. The proof expands it as the finite sum of oscillations and completions and applies their inherited inactivity. The phase-independent mean is removed before this conclusion is asserted.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The full centered profile vanishes before activation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For every correction field `v`, the velocity passed to `ChildFlow.childVelocity` equals the already defined physical approximate velocity plus `v`. The identity is definitional and ensures that the flow estimate and cutoff estimate refer to the same field. Smoothness, smallness, and divergence conditions on `v` are imposed only when applying those estimates.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The child flow uses the same approximate velocity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Given an order-`m` inverse-coframe bound and a profile seminorm bound $AD^q\mathrm{freq}^{\alpha}$, with nonnegative costs, $D\ge1$, and positive frequency, the scaled coframe-applied slice has order-`m` phase jets bounded by the coframe cost times $AD^{q+1}\mathrm{freq}^{\alpha}$. The proof combines the finite product estimate with the conversion from mixed-word norms to scaled Fréchet jets.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: A coframe consumes one parent power in the jet bound

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: This definition is six times the product of the numbers of admissible mixed words through orders $n$ and $n+1$, multiplied by $2^n2^{n+1}$. It collects the combinatorial factors in the completion estimate. Parent geometry, frequency, and input norms are deliberately kept outside this order-only quantity.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The explicit derivative-count factor in the curl estimate

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: At a point where both vector fields are differentiable, divergence of their sum is the sum of their divergences. The proof unfolds divergence into the trace expressed by a finite coordinate sum and uses additivity of the Fréchet derivative. The differentiability premises prevent relying on the total derivative convention at a nondifferentiable point.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Divergence distributes over two differentiable vector fields

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Fix bounds $\|D^jU\|\le W_n\mathsf D^j$ for $1\le j\le n$, a smooth periodic parent flow with both deformation norms at most $\mathsf D\ge2$, and a central seed satisfying the transverse stability and positive coupling conditions (5.5). If $0<T\le1$, $\lambda\ge1$, $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda$, and the envelope is sufficiently small, then the completed unswitched wave $A_1+C[A_1]$, in coordinates $(a/\ell_*,s/h)$ with $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, has derivatives of orders zero through two bounded by $\gamma(t)C\mathsf D^{a+27}\lambda^{-5/4}$ on $[t_0,T]$. Here $\ell_*^{-1}\le\mathsf D^a$ and $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|$. The constants are selected before the parent. This supplies a pointwise derivative bound, not the whole residual estimate (5.48).
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Bound the completed leading wave before activation is applied

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: If `0 < T ≤ 1`, `i ≤ q`, and the order-$q$ time seminorm is bounded by $M$, then the base seminorm of the order-$i$ profile derivative is at most $q!T^{-q}M$. The proof extracts the $i$th nonnegative term and enlarges its factorial and inverse-time power. No derivative of a time-dependent amplitude weight is taken.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The factorial norm bounds every individual time derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Assume a profile vanishes off a closed subset of the active interval, and its positive weight is bounded by $C_\gamma$ on that support. Weighted profile-derivative bounds, the stated readout-map coefficient controls, and `hWave` then give a graph bound with amplitude $C_\gamma\mathrm{freq}^{\alpha}$ and spatial rate $\mathrm{freq}^2$. Outside the support all time derivatives vanish. This retains the smaller amplitude available only on the switching interval.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Closed support preserves the small activation amplitude

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For positive depth, this converts the actual factorial norms of the mean, oscillation, remainder, and switch profiles into their four `GeometricGraphJet` bounds. It assumes inverse-flow coefficient bounds, the carrier-rate absorption `hWave`, inactivity before activation, and closed switch support. The mean retains rate $D^{a+1}$; the other terms use $\mathrm{freq}^2$. The switch amplitude keeps the support bound $\Gamma$, and every amplitude pays the extraction factor $q!T^{-q}$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The selected hierarchy supplies four distinct graph bounds

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a smooth periodic parent with its label flow, the inverse label map and the coframe $B(a)=D(X(t,0))(X(0,t,a))$ are smooth at every slab time. Evaluating `B` at the inverse label of an Eulerian point returns the inverse flow derivative at that point. The proof uses the actual flow inverse identity.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The graph coframe is the inverse flow derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: This real expression collects the graph differentiation cost, retained higher-level count, coefficient jet bounds and level-loss factors in the higher-pressure estimate. It contains no carrier-frequency decay itself; the theorem multiplies it by $\mathrm{freq}^{-5/12}$. Its purpose is to expose how constants depend on depth and parent coefficients.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The explicit coefficient in the higher-pressure Hessian estimate

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: This scalar field is the physical graph of the sum of selected transverse pressures at levels two through `P`. The leading pressure is excluded. This separation is needed because the higher terms are bounded in operator norm using the transverse equation, while the leading term is controlled by a one-sided Hessian estimate.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Read the higher selected oscillatory pressures together

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Let $0<T\le1$ and let the constructed finite approximation have depth $P\ge1$. Assume its leading velocity, pressure and both activation terms vanish for $t<\tau$ or outside one closed label set $S$. If $0\le t\le T$ and either $t<\tau$ or $X(t,\cdot)^{-1}(x)\notin S$, the formal statement gives zero for the whole oscillatory velocity. The residual there is precisely the retained remainder of interactions between the mean corrections, evaluated along the inverse flow. This proves the localized part of the assertion in §1.3. It does not give the same support to the means or assert that the entire approximate Euler residual vanishes outside the wave.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Outside the transported support only interactions between means remain

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The leading-pressure field is the inverse-label graph of the pressure component of the selected leading output. It refers to the same leading input used to construct the hierarchy. To apply the signed seed estimate, a later theorem explicitly identifies this output pressure with the regular seed’s twisted pressure.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Read the leading selected pressure in physical coordinates

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Assume the leading output pressure is exactly the twisted pressure of the supplied regular seed, and that seed has a primary budget at every slab time. For a smooth periodic parent flow, the actual `leadingPressure` then satisfies the explicit signed Hessian upper bound. The equality hypothesis `hSeed` prevents applying a seed estimate to an unrelated selected pressure.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Transfer the signed seed estimate to the selected leading pressure

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Reads `b.leading.output.V` on the same inverse-flow phase graph used for the complete approximation. It isolates the leading wave from the rest of the retained oscillation. This definition does not require $P \ge  1$; identifying it as the first term of the retained sum is a separate theorem with that depth hypothesis.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Eulerian readout of the prescribed leading wave

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: If `hL` identifies the approximation's leading input with the explicit first-wave input, evaluating its velocity on the physical phase graph recovers the localized transported profile. The equality holds for `t` in the closed slab. The inverse flow is the stationary shear at negative time, so the phase and label substitutions are the ones used in the explicit first-wave construction.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Reading the first profile gives its physical wave

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Reads the phase average of the retained profile velocity along the inverse parent flow. This produces the Eulerian mean correction, whose profile is independent of phase. It is separated from the oscillatory correction because its estimates and support differ: the mean may extend throughout the torus and before the wave activates.

For at least one retained level and a smooth periodic divergence-free parent flow, the actual physical mean correction has zero spatial divergence at all slab times. The proof uses the selected mean divergence equations and the physical graph identity. This supplies a necessary hypothesis when taking divergence of the summed physical momentum equation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The physical mean correction is divergence free

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For `1 ≤ P`, the physical mean correction equals the graph of the sum of selected mean profiles from level two through `P`. The first mean profile is zero by construction. This identity links the velocity field already used by the approximation to exactly the mean sum appearing in the pressure calculation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The mean velocity begins at the second level

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text:
For the finite hierarchy built from a parent flow and its leading wave, the phase average of the retained velocity profile, evaluated at $a=X_{t,0}(x)$ and $s=k_*\cdot a$, equals $(\sum_{p=1}^{P}B_p)^
atural$. The first mean is zero, so this is $ ar W^
atural=(\sum_{p=2}^{P}B_p)^
atural$ in §5.6. The equality uses the zero phase averages of each oscillatory profile and its curl correction. It is an exact identity for the selected expansion, not an estimate and not an assertion about arbitrary independently chosen mean fields.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Phase averaging recovers the selected mean corrections exactly

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Fix a finite order $q$ and a depth $P\ge1$. Suppose the selected expansion satisfies its level estimates through order $q+1$, with frequency $\lambda\ge1$, positive continuous weight on $[t_0,T]$, and inverse-flow coefficients obeying $\ell_*^j\|D^jB\|\le L\mathsf D$ for $j\le q+1$, where $B(X_{t,0}x)=D(X_{t,0})(x)$. Assume $\ell_*^{-1}\le\mathsf D^a$ and the hierarchy loss is at most $K\mathsf D^c$. If $b\ge a+1,6c$ and the chosen constant absorbs the displayed finite sum, then $\|\bar W^\natural(t)\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le C_{\rm mean}\mathsf D^{b(m+2)}\lambda^{-5/2}$ for every $m\le q$ and $t\in[0,T]$. Phase independence removes the fast phase derivative cost. The theorem assumes these quantitative inputs; it does not establish all of Lemma 5.8 from the parent alone.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The mean retains its frequency decay at every fixed order

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text:
Let $U$ be smooth and periodic on $[0,T]	imes\mathbb R^3$, let $X$ be its flow, and take a selected finite hierarchy of depth $P\ge1$. Write $ ar W^
atural$ for the evaluated phase mean, $ ar q^
atural$ for the sum of mean pressures, and $ ar f^
atural$ for their summed sources. Then $(\partial_t+U\cdot
abla) ar W^
atural+( ar W^
atural\cdot
abla)U+
abla ar q^
atural= ar f^
atural$ throughout $[0,T]$. Endpoint time derivatives are taken from within that interval. This is the linearized equation used in Lemma 5.9. The mean fields are those supplied by the hierarchy; the assertion is not an existence theorem for an arbitrary source.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Summing mean equations gives the linearized Euler equation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The physical mean forcing is the inverse-label graph of the sum of `meanForceAt i` over levels two through `P`. This sums the actual forcing records, including the single parent-residual contribution at level two. It is a concrete velocity-valued function whose momentum identity and estimates are established subsequently.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Sum the selected mean sources on the physical graph

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: This definition takes the negative phase average of the hierarchy source at index `i` and subtracts the parent residual exactly when `i = 2`. It is the actual mean forcing used by the selected construction. The function is defined at every natural index, but its equation and estimates are invoked on retained levels two through `P`.

The mean-pressure field is the graph of the finite sum of selected scalar pressures `q i` at levels two through `P`. This retains the actual pressure supplied by each mean solve. It does not replace those pressures with an independently chosen Poisson solution; the Poisson equation is derived from their summed linearized momentum equation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Sum the selected mean pressures on the physical graph

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text:
For a smooth periodic divergence-free parent $U$ and its flow on $[0,T]$, take the selected hierarchy of depth $P\ge1$. Its summed mean velocity $ ar W^
atural$ and source $ ar f^
atural$ satisfy $\Delta ar q^
atural=\operatorname{div} ar f^
atural-2\operatorname{tr}(
abla U\,
abla ar W^
atural)$ at every time and point, where $ ar q^
atural$ is the summed mean pressure. This is the Poisson equation in the proof of Lemma 5.9. The trace is the trace of the product of the two derivative matrices, not their scalar product. The equation follows from the linearized momentum equation and the zero divergence of both velocity fields.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Divergence determines the Hessian source for the mean pressure

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Assume the measured levels of the chosen physical approximation satisfy the order-two bounds. Then the unweighted seminorms of its summed means and actual mean sources are bounded by the same level-count factor times $C\,\mathrm{loss}^6\mathrm{freq}^{-5/2}$. This specializes the abstract finite-sum estimate to the exact sources stored in the physical construction.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The actual mean velocity and force share one finite bound

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: At an active time $t\in[t_0,T]$, suppose $0<\gamma\le1$, $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, $|k_*|\le\mathsf D\lambda$, $\ell_*^{-1}\le\mathsf D^a$, and the inverse-flow coefficient satisfies $\ell_*^j\|D^jB\|\le L\mathsf D$ for $j\le1$. If $\|W_{\rm osc}-V_1\|_{[1],\gamma}\le C_1\mathsf D^{e_1}\lambda^{-23/12}$ and $\|\bar W\|_{[1]}\le C_2\mathsf D^{e_2}\lambda^{-5/2}$, then the sum of their physical derivative norms at the origin is at most $(48LC_1\mathsf D^{\max(a,1)+1+e_1}+24LC_2\mathsf D^{a+1+e_2})\lambda^{-5/12}$. Here evaluation uses $a=X_{t,0}(x)$ and phase $k_*\cdot a$. The formal statement stops at this intermediate bound; obtaining $|E_c|\le\lambda^{-1/3}$ also requires the step smallness condition.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: One physical derivative preserves decay of the nonleading terms

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Assume inactive leading data on a closed support, positive envelope length, prescribed phase width, a positive weight bounded by one, controlled coefficient jets and actual level bounds at orders one and two. Then the higher oscillatory pressure Hessian is bounded on the entire slab by its explicit prefactor times $\mathrm{freq}^{-5/12}$. Support propagation supplies zero pressure before activation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The actual higher pressures obey the full-slab Hessian bound

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For the actual physical approximation, parent flow and incompressibility hypotheses establish the summed linearized equation and divergence constraint. Together with second-order bounds on the selected mean and forcing sums, controlled inverse coframe jets, and a parent-gradient Hölder bound, this gives the displayed Hessian norm estimate with frequency decay $\mathrm{freq}^{-5/2}$. The bound is for the actual selected mean pressure.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The selected mean pressure has the expected small Hessian

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Abbreviates `twistedHierarchyOperators` built from the inverse deformation, strain, and transported covector of `d`. The `_data` argument makes the operators accessible from approximation data, but its contents do not change the operator choice. These are the same parent operators used for the transverse, mean, and curl completion equations.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Operators determined by the parent geometry

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Subtracts the phase average from the full retained velocity and reads the result on the graph determined by the inverse parent flow `X t 0`. The result is the Eulerian oscillatory correction. Removing the average here is algebraic; the later graph-sum identity identifies it with the completed transverse levels.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Eulerian readout of the zero mean oscillation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For the selected depth-$P$ expansion, this is the physical evaluation of all curl corrections and the transverse velocities from level two onward. In the paper’s indexing it is $(\sum_{p=2}^{P}V_p+\sum_{p=2}^{P+1}C_p)^\natural$. Evaluation means $a=X_{t,0}(x)$ and $s=k_*\cdot a$. The stored curl correction at index $p$ corresponds to the paper’s $C_{p+1}$, which explains the different indices in the formula. For $P\ge1$ the hierarchy identities identify this field with $(W_{\rm osc}-V_1)^\natural$. Its definition supplies neither a smallness estimate nor the central-gradient bound.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Retain every curl correction after removing the leading oscillation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For `PhysicalApproximationData b` and `hP : 1 ≤ P`, the physical oscillation remainder equals the inverse-label graph of the total profile minus its phase average and first transverse profile. This is equality of velocity fields, with no estimate. The depth hypothesis identifies the selected first profile with the leading input. Later bounds differentiate this exact remainder at the origin.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Remove the leading wave from the centered expansion

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Assuming at least one retained level, the physical oscillation remainder is the graph of the full retained profile minus its phase average and its first transverse velocity. The construction identifies that first velocity with the given leading output. This equality connects the named physical remainder to the measured profile sum used in the central estimate.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The physical remainder is the leading-subtracted oscillation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: From order-one actual level bounds, a controlled inverse-flow coframe, admissible label and phase scales, and a loss bound $\mathrm{loss} \le  K \cdot  D^c$, bounds the physical remainder’s derivative on the active slab. Its frequency decay is $-5/12$, obtained from $-23/12$ after one carrier derivative costs $3/2$. The displayed constant retains depth cardinality, coframe, and loss dependence.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: One physical derivative leaves a decaying oscillatory remainder

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Under `IsLabelFlowOn`, smoothness of the parent on the closed slab, and spatial periodicity, the Eulerian higher oscillation remainder is jointly smooth on that slab. The argument combines smooth retained profiles with smooth inverse labels. This is qualitative regularity; it does not establish the small derivative bound used for the central error.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Smoothness of the higher oscillation on the graph

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Identifies the zero-mean part of the constructed velocity with the graph of the sum of $V_i+C_i$ over $1\le i\le P$. The Lean completion `C i` belongs to velocity `V i`; the paper denotes that completion by $C_{i+1}$. The equality comes from the solver construction and includes the empty-depth case.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The oscillation is the sum of completed levels

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Assuming `hP : 1 ≤ P`, splits the oscillation into the prescribed leading velocity and `oscillationRemainder`. The proof separates the first summand and uses that the constructed `V 1` is the given leading output. The remainder includes the leading curl completion as well as all transverse and completion terms from levels two onward.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Separate the leading wave from the oscillation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Assuming the leading transverse profile is zero on the initial slice, the physical oscillatory velocity is identically zero at time zero. The proof includes all retained transverse profiles and their completions, using completion’s preservation of a zero slice. No lower bound on retained depth is needed for this statement; an empty sum also vanishes.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The physical oscillation vanishes initially

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: With $P \ge  1$, a closed support set, $0 < \tau$, and inactive leading data, the Eulerian oscillation vanishes whenever $t \le  \tau$ or the inverse label lies outside that set. The non-strict time inequality includes the activation slice. The theorem concerns the oscillation only; mean corrections need not vanish there.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The oscillation vanishes through a positive activation time

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For positive retained depth, closed label support and nonnegative activation time, inactive leading data imply that the physical oscillation vanishes through activation and outside the transported support. When activation equals zero, `hLead` explicitly supplies the leading zero initial slice. This extra endpoint premise avoids inferring a boundary value from an empty interval of earlier slab times.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Include the activation endpoint in the vanishing statement

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Let $P\ge1$ and $\lambda\ge1$. Suppose the selected hierarchy has order-zero level bounds with constant $C\ge0$ and loss $L\ge1$, its oscillation vanishes before $t_0$, and its continuous weight satisfies $0<\gamma(t)\le1$ on $[t_0,T]$. If $C_{\rm step}\ge2PCL^2$, then $|W_{\rm osc}^\natural(t,x)|\le C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-5/4}$ for every $t\in[0,T]$ and $x\in\mathbb R^3$. Here the physical field is evaluated through the inverse parent labels and phase $k_*\cdot a$. This is the summation step behind (5.47). The level estimates and preactivation vanishing are assumptions of this helper result.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Sum weighted level bounds without paying a derivative cost

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: If the approximation’s leading data equal the constructed paper-cutoff input, the slice of its leading and completion switch terms equals the cutoff derivative times `activationPrimary` for that same seed and coframe. The identity holds at every slab time and label-phase point. It is an exact source formula before any norm estimate.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The full activation slice is the derivative times the primary wave

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D,\lambda\ge1$, and let a smooth periodic divergence-free parent have deformation norms at most $\mathsf D$. Assume its inverse-flow coefficient has derivatives $\|D^jB\|\le C_j\mathsf D^{7j+1}$. Require $0<\ell_*\le1$, $\ell_*\mathsf D^7\le1$, $\ell_*^{-1}\le\mathsf D^a$, $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$ and $|k_*|\le\mathsf D\lambda$. A selected depth-$P\ge2$ expansion must satisfy its qualitative physical properties, preactivation vanishing and level bounds through order two with loss $\mathsf D^r$ and continuous weight $0<\gamma\le1$. If $b\ge2\max(a,1)+6r+9$ and $C_{\rm step}=\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b$ dominates the explicit coefficient costs, then $C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$ implies that every smooth periodic divergence-free $v$ with each derivative through order two bounded by $\lambda^{-5/2}$ admits a flow $Y$ of $V+v$ satisfying $\|D Y_{0,t}\|,\|D Y_{t,0}\|\le C_{\rm step}\lambda^{1/4}$ on $[0,T]$. The weight here is arbitrary; quantitative hierarchy and coefficient estimates are premises.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Small scaled gradients control both directions of the perturbed flow

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text:
Fix the selected finite hierarchy over $U,p$ on $[0,T]$, and assume its assembled physical fields have already been proved smooth, with odd divergence-free velocity and the exact residual identity. The formal statement records those properties for $V=U+W^
atural$ and $\Pi=p+\mathsf P^
atural$, and rewrites their residual as $R_P^
atural+R_{\widetilde\chi}^
atural$. The latter is the sum of the leading activation term and its curl completion. Here $f^
atural(t,x)=f(t,X_{t,0}x,k_*\cdot X_{t,0}x)$. This declaration collects established properties; it does not independently derive them from the standing parent assumptions. That distinction matters when comparing this link with Lemma 5.8.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Collect the established physical properties and split the residual

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Fix $m\ge0$ and $P\ge1$. Suppose the selected hierarchy has level bounds through order $m+1$ with loss $\mathsf D^r$, vanishes before activation, and has $0<\gamma\le1$ afterward. Assume $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, $|k_*|\le\mathsf D\lambda$, $\ell_*^{-1}\le\mathsf D^a$, and scaled derivatives of the inverse-flow coefficient through order $m+1$ are at most $L\mathsf D$. For $b\ge\max(a,1)+1,2r$, the evaluated oscillation belongs to $C^{m,1/2}$ and obeys $\|W_{\rm osc}^\natural(t)\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le C_{m,P}\mathsf D^{b(m+2)}\lambda^{3(m+1)/2-5/4}$ on $[0,T]$. This is only the first estimate in (5.48). The extra derivative supplies Hölder control; the level and coefficient estimates are premises here.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: One extra profile derivative gives the half Hölder bound

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a fixed approximation of positive depth, assumes its qualitative properties, all-order actual level estimates, a positive amplitude weight bounded by one, inactivity before launch and coframe jet bounds. It derives the oscillatory and mean Hölder estimates with the explicit prefactors above. Scale assumptions and the `hGraph` and `hLoss` exponent inequalities remain inputs; the theorem does not establish the level recurrence itself.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Physical Hölder estimates from the measured levels

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text:
For a smooth periodic divergence-free parent and a selected depth-$P\ge1$ hierarchy on $[0,T]$, assume the level bounds through order two, $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, and $0<\gamma\le1$ on the active interval. Also assume the displayed bounds on the inverse deformation, strain and longitudinal projection, and $\|
abla U\|_{C^{0,1/2}}\le C_U\mathsf D^2$. Then the Hessian of $\sum_{p=2}^P\mathsf p_p^
atural$ is bounded in operator norm by a specified coefficient times $\lambda^{-5/12}$, while that of $\sum_{p=2}^P ar q_p^
atural$ is bounded by a specified coefficient times $\mathsf D^{6r+2a+2}\lambda^{-5/2}$. The coefficients depend on the input bounds and depth. These are conditional estimates for the actual hierarchy; neither bounds the leading pressure Hessian in absolute value.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The two nonleading pressures have different frequency decay

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Identifies the approximation’s leading velocity and pressure with a supplied regular seed, then combines its `PrimaryPressureBudget` with a smooth periodic odd parent flow. It proves a signed upper Hessian bound on the entire slab and the exact rank-one central gradient with the selected `waveSwitch`. The full approximation’s higher corrections and central error are outside this declaration.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Reading the seed pressure and central gradient

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text:
Let $V=U+W^
atural$, $\Pi=p+\mathsf P^
atural$ be an assembled approximation on $[0,T]$. Assume the leading pressure has upper Hessian bound $L\lambda^{-1/4}I$, the higher and mean pressures have Hessian norms at most $H\lambda^{-5/12}$ and $M\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $L+H+M\le C_{m step}$. Assume also the exact central identity $D V_1^
atural=\widetilde\chi\mathbf a\otimes\kappa$, first-order hierarchy and inverse-flow bounds, $0<\gamma\le1$, and that their central remainder cost is at most $C_{m step}$. If $\lambda\ge1$ and $C_{m step}\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, then $D^2(\Pi-p)\le C_{m step}\lambda^{-1/4}I$ on $[0,T]$, and $D V(t,0)=D U(t,0)+\widetilde\chi\mathbf a\otimes\kappa+E_c$ with $\|E_c\|\le\lambda^{-1/3}$ on $[t_0,T]$. This combines supplied estimates; it does not prove them separately.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Combine the signed pressure bound with the central remainder estimate

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a fixed constructed family on $[0,T]$, $H_p$ is its preliminary source and $R_U\circ X$ its phase-independent residual. The source for the level-$p$ mean equation is $-\langle H_p\rangle_s$, with the additional term $-R_U\circ X$ only at $p=2$. This is exactly the distinction in (5.27). The source belongs to the same selected expansion as its mean correction and is the quantity estimated in the unweighted norms of Theorem 5.6.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Cancel the phase average and the parent residual

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Assume $P\ge2$, a smooth periodic divergence-free parent and its flow, and a constructed family whose leading velocity, pressure and activation contribution vanish before $t_0$ and outside a closed label set $S$. For $W=\sum_{p=1}^P(V_p+C_{p+1}+B_p)$ and $\mathsf P=\sum_{p=1}^P(\mathsf p_p+\bar q_p)$, the formal theorem gives $\widetilde{\mathbf d}\cdot W=0$ and momentum residual $R_P+R_{\widetilde\chi}$. It also gives all phase-average, support and terminal conventions, and identifies $R_P$ with the final linear terms and quadratic interactions above depth $P$. Outside $S$, the remainder is phase independent. Every profile is smooth on $[0,T]$ and satisfies the phase period and coupled label translations. The construction is an input here, not an existence conclusion.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Identify the sums, residual, support, and smoothness

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Assume $\lambda\ge1$, $L\ge1$, a positive continuous weight on $[t_0,T]$, and every level bound through depth $P$, at the order under consideration. Summing the retained level estimates yields (5.37): the oscillatory correction has scale $\lambda^{-5/4}$, while both the mean sum and its source sum have scale $\lambda^{-5/2}$. The formal bounds concern the constructed profiles and retain the parent residual in the first mean source. The finite number of levels enters the constants.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Sum the actual level estimates through the chosen depth

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The strain profile stored in the physical approximation data is phase independent. This is read from its physical value as a pulled-back parent gradient and is used in averaging and cancellation identities.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The parent strain has no phase dependence

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: If each profile in the retained higher-level range is fixed by the hierarchy average, their finite sum is phase independent. The theorem first uses linearity of the average and then its concrete independence property. The empty range is allowed and gives the zero profile, which also has no phase dependence.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: A finite sum of means remains independent of phase

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: At a slab time, pulling the finite velocity profile back by the inverse parent coframe sends its phase average to the average part and its centered profile to the oscillatory part. The proof moves the phase-independent linear map through the period integral. The word `zero` refers to the additional Eulerian correction being zero; the phase mean need not vanish.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The uncut pullback preserves the phase decomposition

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The preceding pointwise average and oscillation identities are promoted to equalities of functions of label and phase at a fixed slab time. The proof uses function extensionality twice and contains no new averaging argument. These equalities permit rewriting the functions inside scaled phase-jet bounds for the same finite velocity profile.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The pullback identities hold as full label–phase functions

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: A jointly smooth field on the closed physical slab restricts to a smooth spatial function at each slab time. The proof composes with the constant-time map. This provides the spatial smoothness used in graph readout and Hölder estimates, without asserting smoothness for times outside the slab.

Assume a smooth periodic parent flow, parent mixed derivative bounds, and `GeometricGraphJet` bounds for the actual mean, oscillation, tail, and switch profiles. Then Eulerian time derivatives of the mean and full velocity have spatial half Hölder bounds when $i+m+1\le N$; the residual has order-one half Hölder bounds when $i+2\le N$. The mean keeps its smaller spatial rate, while the oscillatory terms use the larger carrier rate.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Four graph bounds give the physical time estimates

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For nonnegative rate and $t < t_0$, the switch derivative is zero because the switch agrees with the constant zero function on a neighborhood of `t`. This version uses eventual equality and the strict inequality directly. The endpoint-inclusive version appears in the leading-input module.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The activation derivative is zero strictly before the start

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: If the inverse label map and the profile’s joint label-phase slice are smooth at a fixed time, their transported phase-graph readout is a smooth spatial field. The phase coordinate is the continuous linear functional given by the carrier dot product composed with inverse labels. No time derivative or time-smoothness conclusion is involved.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Smooth profile slices stay smooth on the phase graph

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Turns the approximate pressure at time `t` into an `EndpointSmoothPotential` using smoothness and periodicity from `PhysicalApproximationProperties`. On the slab its lift is the actual approximate pressure. Off the slab the definition deliberately chooses the zero potential, making a total family available to the Fourier-cutoff interface.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: A periodic pressure potential on each slab slice

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: At a time $t \in  [0,T]$, the lift of `b.potential h t` is exactly `b.pressure t`. The proof selects the in-slab branch of the definition. This identity is used to rewrite the cutoff interface’s pressure gradient back to the pressure in the physical momentum equation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The slice potential equals the approximate pressure

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The component signed and norm bounds, a sum of constants at most `Cstep`, and the actual physical approximation properties give the parent Hessian plus $C_{\rm step}\mathrm{freq}^{-1/4}$ as an upper quadratic bound for the pressure potential. This is the form needed for the next endpoint coercivity argument. It remains a one-sided inequality.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The pressure potential retains the parent plus step upper bound

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Assume the physical approximation properties, twice differentiable parent pressure and a signed Hessian bound for the pressure increment. The lifted torus pressure potential then has Hessian bounded above by the parent Hessian plus that increment bound. The argument uses equality of the selected lift with the physical pressure on the slab, so no extra pressure term is introduced.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Pass the correction bound to the torus pressure representative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Given a parent pressure $p$, parent transition family $X$, and the selected depth-$P$ hierarchy, define $\Pi(t,x)=p(t,x)+\mathsf P(t,a,k_*\cdot a)$ with $a=X_{t,0}(x)$. The profile $\mathsf P$ is the sum of the hierarchy’s oscillatory and mean pressures. This is the pressure in the approximate momentum equation of §5.6. The definition alone neither imposes zero spatial mean on $\Pi$ nor asserts the Poisson equation of an exact Euler solution. In particular, the later pressure paired with $S_\Lambda V$ is defined separately by its zero-mean Poisson problem and compared with this $\Pi$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Evaluate the same finite pressure expansion as the velocity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Given a signed leading Hessian upper bound and norm bounds for the higher and mean Hessians, the total pressure increment has a signed upper bound with the sum of the three constants at scale $\mathrm{freq}^{-1/4}$. Frequency at least one permits the faster-decaying terms to be enlarged. The component estimates are hypotheses here, not derived in this assembly theorem.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Add the three exact pressure contributions at the step scale

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a retained hierarchy containing its first level, the pressure minus parent pressure equals the three named physical fields: leading pressure, higher oscillatory pressure and mean pressure. This is equality of scalar functions at every time. It is the decomposition used to combine the component Hessian bounds without introducing an untracked remainder.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The pressure increment is exactly leading plus higher plus mean

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For at least one retained level, the pressure increment is exactly the leading selected pressure graph plus the higher transverse-pressure graphs and the mean-pressure graphs at levels two through `P`. This equality is valid as a function at every time. It uses the construction’s zero first mean pressure and selected first transverse pressure.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Separate the selected pressure into three profile sums

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Evaluates the retained profile velocity at an independent time, label, and phase. The expression `(b.profiles.velocity P).val.val.val` unwraps the twisted, periodic, and smooth-profile subtypes. This field still lives in label and phase coordinates; composing with the inverse flow and setting the phase to the carrier dot product happens in the Eulerian definitions.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Retained velocity before reading the phase graph

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The retained velocity is one-periodic in its phase variable for every time and label. This is a defining property of the intermediate `HierarchyPeriodicProfile` subtype. No restriction $t \in  [0,T]$ is needed, since the wrapped profile remains periodic and is zero away from its time slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: One phase period leaves the retained velocity unchanged

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For any integer lattice vector, translating the label and translating the phase by its dot product with `k` leaves the retained profile unchanged. This is skew periodicity, not separate periodicity of the label variable at fixed phase. It permits arbitrary real carrier vectors while producing periodic Eulerian fields on the transported phase graph.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Lattice shifts carry the matching phase shift

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For $t \in  [0,T]$, the map `(a,s) ↦ b.profileVelocity t a s` is smooth on the full label and phase space. This follows from the smooth-profile subtype rather than an estimate on its derivatives. The statement fixes time; it does not assert that the zero extension is smooth across the endpoints of the slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Smoothness in label and phase at fixed time

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a fixed depth, smooth profiles are periodic in phase and satisfy $F(t,a+n,s+k_*\cdot n)=F(t,a,s)$ for $n\in\mathbb Z^3$. The finite hierarchy is obtained by successively applying the endpoint mean solve, transverse solve, and curl correction, starting from the chosen leading wave. The parent residual and activation terms are fixed inputs. These are the actual profiles used in Proposition 5.4; their estimates are subsequent conclusions of Theorem 5.6.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Build the finite hierarchy from the physical inputs

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Given parent coefficient caps, nonnegative costs, depth at least two, $1\le\mathrm{freq}\le\mathrm{next}$, leading inactivity, and $0<\gamma\le1$ on the active slab, measured-level bounds through order two and the certified cutoff’s tail estimate give its corrected pullback-jet record. The oscillatory jets have order two and frequency decay $-5/4$; the mean jets have order one and decay $-5/2$. The parent exponent is $6r+8$, with `r = lossPower`. Inactivity and the weight bound permit unweighting; frequency ordering absorbs the next-frequency tail, which contributes only to the mean.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Measured levels and the actual tail supply corrected pullback jets

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Reads the hierarchy remainder at depth `P` together with the leading and completion switches on the Eulerian graph. This is the candidate physical residual produced by the finite expansion. Its equality to the momentum residual of the defined velocity and pressure is a theorem under parent smoothness, incompressibility, flow, and depth assumptions.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Retained tail plus both activation contributions

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For the exact later-wave leading input and every slab time, the residual is the retained tail read on the inverse-flow graph plus the switch derivative times the transported `activationPrimary`. The `hLeading` identity ties this formula to the selected seed, so the activation field is not an unrelated auxiliary source.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The later residual is the tail plus the switched primary

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text:
Let $U$ be a smooth odd periodic parent with flow $X$, and let the leading profile of a selected finite expansion come from an even localized seed and a smooth cutoff $\widetilde\chi$ vanishing before $t_0$. Then its defined physical residual equals $R_P^
atural+\widetilde\chi\,{}^{\prime}(A_1+C[A_1])^
atural$ throughout $[0,T]$. Evaluation is through $a=X_{t,0}(x)$ and $s=k_*\cdot a$. The cutoff and seed must be the ones used to form that expansion. This identifies the two activation contributions with the completed unswitched leading wave. The equality is a decomposition of the constructed residual; identifying it with $V_t+V\cdot
abla V+
abla\Pi$ uses the separate physical momentum identity.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Separate expansion depth from the derivative of the time cutoff

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For every time, the defined physical residual splits into the graph of the retained hierarchy remainder and the graph of the sum of the two switch profiles. This is a definitional additive identity and does not require a depth bound. Equality with the actual Euler momentum equation is supplied separately by approximation properties.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Separate the retained residual from the activation source

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: If both stored switch profiles are zero, the defined residual is exactly the graph of the hierarchy remainder at every time. This is the no-switch situation used for the first wave. The theorem only simplifies the decomposition; it does not assert that the retained tail or the momentum residual itself is zero.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: With no activation source only the retained tail remains

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Specializes the general tail-plus-primary readout estimate to the actual seed, switch derivative, and hierarchy leading input. The supplied measured tail, primary jet bounds, coframe estimates, and coefficient caps give first-order half-Hölder residual control. The theorem derives the residual identity and needed primary slice smoothness from the exact `hLeading` compatibility.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Bound the residual of the selected later-wave graph

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: From an unweighted order-two bound on the actual retained tail, a weighted order-two primary bound, graph coframe estimates, and $|\sigma|\\gamma \le  S$, obtains first-order half-Hölder residual control by $\mathrm{Cstep} \cdot  \mathrm{freq}^2 \cdot  (\mathrm{freq}^{-2\cdot \mathrm{depth}/3} + S)$. The residual decomposition and scalar caps are explicit hypotheses. Primary smoothness is needed only where $\sigma \ne  0$; inactive or zero-switch slices are treated separately.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Read the tail and activation bounds into physical space

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a selected expansion over a smooth odd periodic parent, use the same even localized seed and smooth cutoff $\widetilde\chi$ to form its leading wave. Assume $\lambda\ge1$, $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, $|k_*|\le\mathsf D\lambda$, controlled inverse-flow derivatives through order two, an order-two remainder bound at scale $\lambda^{-2P/3-5/4}$, and scaled derivatives through order two of $A_1+C[A_1]$ bounded by $\gamma(t)C\mathsf D^p\lambda^{-5/4}$. The weight is continuous and nonnegative on $[t_0,T]$. If $C_{\rm step}$ dominates the two explicit coefficient costs, then $\|R_V(t)\|_{C^{1,1/2}}\le C_{\rm step}\lambda^2(\lambda^{-2P/3}+\sup_{[t_0,T]}|\widetilde\chi\,{}^{\prime}|\gamma)$ for all $t\in[0,T]$, with Hölder regularity included. This supplies the residual clause of (5.48), conditional on the stated profile bounds.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Keep the actual weighted activation derivative in the residual estimate

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Combines the actual later-graph estimate with the scheduled depth and switch-smallness hypotheses. At every slab time it concludes both first-order half-Hölder regularity and a norm at most the next frequency’s power $-7/2$. The weighted primary and unweighted retained-tail bounds remain explicit inputs, as do the scalar caps and $\mathrm{Cstep} \cdot  \mu$ budget.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The selected later-wave residual meets the scheduled decay

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For frequency at least two and depth six times the next frequency exponent, converts the supplied residual-rate estimate into the next frequency’s power $-7/2$. The hypotheses include $\mu \ge  1$, nonnegative `Cstep`, and $\mathrm{Cstep} \cdot  \mu \le  \mathrm{freq}^{1/16}$. The proof identifies both depth and switch errors with the next-frequency scale $-4$ before absorbing prefactors.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The chosen depth makes the residual small for the next wave

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For approximation data with both switch profiles zero, derives first-order half-Hölder residual regularity and the next-frequency power $-7/2$ bound from the measured retained tail. The proof applies the general readout theorem with zero primary and zero switch. It still requires graph coefficient control, the scheduled depth, and the scalar absorption budget.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The first-wave residual meets the same scheduled decay

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Given `LeadingRelayData` and one active-interval coefficient budget, this theorem returns two inequalities: completion of any centered input loses one derivative and gains inverse frequency, and each selected relay is bounded by the preceding measured oscillation plus source. The supplied cap inequalities place both explicit order constants under `L`; the theorem does not choose those caps.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The selected completion and relay obey a common bound

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a selected physical approximation with its leading compatibility data, actual parent flow, and smooth periodic parent velocity, one relay coefficient budget gives both completion and relay estimates. The assumptions include a positive frequency and amplitude weight and a cap on the explicit coefficient cost. Relays are covered through level `P+1`; the measured mean force uses `q-1` while oscillatory profiles use `q`.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: One coefficient budget controls completion and every selected relay

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The theorem derives the recurrence for the actual finite hierarchy from support, cancellation, and linear estimates, after receiving coefficient caps and primitive bounds at the required finite orders. Residual, leading-wave, mean-solver, and transverse-solver bounds remain explicit final premises. The conclusion is `HierarchyNormRecurrence`; obtaining the depth-decay theorem requires the separate numerical induction.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The selected physical profiles satisfy the norm recurrence

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: On the actual selected profiles, assume the parent flow and regularity laws, inactive support, positive scales and amplitude weight, the six primitive linear bounds, and source coefficient caps. With `P ≥ 2`, `n+3*P ≤ H`, `K,L ≥ 1`, and the frequency smallness condition, obtain the mixed norm recurrence, all retained level bounds, oscillation and mean sums, and the final remainder estimate. Mean forcing uses time order `q-1`, with natural subtraction at `q=0`.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Run the finite hierarchy recurrence in mixed time norms

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The source for correction level `i` is the negative phase-mean-free part of `sourceBeforeMean`, minus the specified mean-phase advection term. It is computed from the actual finite hierarchy, its depth, and its activation completion. The abbreviation neither solves the transverse equation nor asserts mean zero; these properties are supplied by the selected solver theorem at valid correction levels.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The exact source of a selected transverse correction

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: At a retained correction level `i ∈ Icc 2 P`, the selected velocity and carrier-normalized pressure satisfy a factorial time-norm bound in terms of the exact selected force. Besides positive frequency and amplitude weight, the theorem assumes an undifferentiated inverse estimate `hbase` and four coefficient time budgets. It uses equalities with the actual transverse solver output, so the estimate remains attached to the retained profiles.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Time bounds for the exact retained transverse solution

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: This variant of the selected transverse time estimate accepts the ordinary measured oscillatory row, which includes velocity plus normalized pressure, as its zeroth-order input. At a level in `2,…,P`, discarding the nonnegative pressure term supplies the velocity bound required by the previous theorem. The same positive-frequency, weight, and four coefficient-budget assumptions are retained.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Use the measured spatial row to start transverse time estimates

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: If the prescribed level-one pressure has zero phase mean, then every retained pressure does. The proof separates level one from higher levels, where the pressure is produced by the selected transverse solver and inherits its normalization. No statement is made about unretained indices, and no mean-pressure normalization is inferred from this oscillatory result.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Every retained oscillatory pressure is centered

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: A jointly smooth vector field on the closed time slab has a smooth spatial slice at any time belonging to that slab. The proof composes with the map sending `x` to `(t,x)` and then uses smoothness on the whole spatial space. No differentiability in time outside the slab is asserted.

Returns the canonical finite-hierarchy solvers from `physicalSolvers`, using the parent geometry together with `b.time_le_one`. These solvers provide the endpoint mean inverse, transverse equation, and curl completion used in all retained levels. The abbreviation supplies selected solution operators; the estimates for their outputs are proved in later modules.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Selected mean transverse and completion solutions

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: If the parent frequency `μ` is at least one, the schedule exponent parameter is positive, and `Cstep` is at most the new frequency’s power $1/32$, then $\mathrm{Cstep} \cdot  \mu$ is at most its power $1/16$. The large scheduled exponent bounds the parent frequency by another $1/32$ power; no nonnegative assumption on `Cstep` is needed.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Absorb the parent frequency into the step budget

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The material operator applied to the sum of selected means, plus label and phase gradients of the summed mean pressures, equals the sum of the actual mean sources. This is an exact identity of profiles. It follows by adding each selected mean equation and includes an empty retained range without requiring a lower bound on `P`.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The selected mean equations add without an extra error
