TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Defines the scalar $q!T^{-q}$ used to extract any derivative through order $q$ from the factorially weighted time seminorm. It bounds the individual extraction costs when $0<T\le1$. The definition itself permits arbitrary $T$; the following extraction theorem supplies the positivity and upper bound that give this expression its intended meaning.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The common factorial time extraction cost

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For positive hierarchy depth and a closed spatial support set, the supplied `Inactive` data imply that the selected oscillatory profile vanishes at every label and phase whenever the slab time is strictly before $t_0$. The proof expands the oscillation as the finite sum of oscillatory velocities and completions and applies their inherited inactive-region support.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The selected oscillation is zero before activation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Under the smooth periodic parent and flow hypotheses, each time derivative of the actual approximation residual equals the sum of derivatives of the graph-read hierarchy remainder and the combined switch profile. Both the leading and completion switch forces remain in that combined term. This exact identity is used before applying separate amplitude and support bounds.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Residual time derivatives split into tail and activation terms

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a smooth periodic parent with its label flow, each Eulerian time derivative of the selected approximation splits into the parent derivative, oscillatory correction derivative, and mean correction derivative. The theorem uses the exact velocity decomposition and smoothness of the inverse-flow graph evaluations. It is a function equality at a time in the positive-length slab, without estimating any term.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Velocity time derivatives split into parent and two corrections

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: If a profile is zero at every label and phase outside a closed time set, each of its time derivatives is also zero there at slab times. Closedness makes the complement a neighborhood on which the time curve is zero. The proof uses local congruence of within-time derivatives, so it covers slab endpoints without imposing new boundary conditions.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: All profile time derivatives vanish outside closed support

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a depth-$P\ge1$ selected expansion, assume level estimates through order two with loss $\mathsf D^r$, bounds on all scaled inverse-deformation coefficients, preactivation vanishing, and $0<\gamma\le1$ on $[t_0,T]$. Set the added perturbation $v$ to zero and pull the correction into parent labels: $c=(D_aX)^{-1}W$. In coordinates $(a/\ell_*,s/h)$, its oscillation has derivatives through order two bounded by $A_{\rm osc}\mathsf D^{2r+1}\lambda^{-5/4}$; its phase mean has derivatives through order one bounded by $A_{\rm mean}\mathsf D^{6r+1}\lambda^{-5/2}$. Both hold on $[0,T]$. This does not state the second-order mean estimate displayed in the paper’s proof of Lemma 5.10, or handle a nonzero perturbation. The weaker intermediate estimate suffices for the subsequent flow proof.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Only one mean derivative is required for the flow argument

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For $P\ge2$, the actual selected remainder is bounded on the full slab by an explicit finite-pair constant times $\mathrm{freq}^{-5/4-2P/3}$. Premises include level bounds through order $n+1$, inactivity, coefficient and relay caps, and $L^6\mathrm{freq}^{-1/12}\le1$. The activation switch is excluded from this remainder and must be estimated separately.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The actual residual tail has the claimed frequency decay

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a parent velocity $U$, its transition family $X$, and the selected depth-$P$ hierarchy, define $V(t,x)=U(t,x)+W(t,a,k_*\cdot a)$, where $a=X_{t,0}(x)$ and $W$ is the retained velocity profile. This is $V=U+W^\natural$ at the start of §5.6. The profile contains transverse oscillations, their curl corrections and the mean terms from the same finite recursion. The definition alone does not say that $V$ is incompressible or solves Euler; the construction separately proves zero divergence and identifies its nonzero momentum residual. Its smoothness assertions concern the closed interval $[0,T]$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Add the evaluated finite correction to the parent velocity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For $P \ge  1$, sums the actual level estimates to bound the oscillatory profile, its leading-subtracted remainder, and its phase average. Their frequency rates are respectively $-5/4$, $-23/12$, and $-5/2$, with explicit depth-cardinality and loss factors. The oscillatory bounds use the positive amplitude weight; the mean uses an unweighted seminorm. No Eulerian graph derivative is taken yet.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Sum the measured oscillation remainder and mean bounds

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a hierarchy of depth at least one and the explicit first leading input, the physical velocity equals stationary shear plus the leading wave, higher oscillatory remainder and mean correction. The time belongs to the closed parent slab. This identity keeps the selected correction fields themselves, so subsequent estimates apply to the actual approximation rather than to unrelated witnesses.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The first velocity separates its four terms

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For the finite approximation on $[0,T]$ at depth $P\ge1$, the formal statement is the exact equality $V=U+V_1^\natural+W_{\mathrm{osc}}+B$, where $U$ is the parent, $V_1$ the activated leading profile, $W_{\mathrm{osc}}$ contains the remaining oscillations and divergence corrections, and $B$ is the sum of the phase-independent means. Evaluation uses the inverse parent flow and the phase $k_*\cdot a$. The components are those of the already constructed finite family. This equality explains the decomposition in §1.3; it does not itself bound the residual or establish the smallness of any summand.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The approximate velocity separates parent, leading wave, oscillations and mean

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: The approximate velocity equals the parent plus the zero-mean oscillation plus the mean correction. This is an identity for any `PhysicalApproximationData`, obtained by inserting and subtracting the profile average at each graph point. It needs no lower bound on depth and does not provide estimates for any of the three summands.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Split the velocity into parent oscillation and mean

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: If the selected leading velocity vanishes at time zero, every retained transverse velocity profile has zero initial values and zero phase average. The proof separates the leading level from later levels selected by the zero-initial-data transverse solver. It says nothing about the mean profiles, whose endpoint problem may produce nonzero initial velocity.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Every retained transverse profile has zero initial data

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Combines measured levels through order $P+1$, graph coframe control, a positive weight at most one, inactivity before activation, and parent jet bounds to bound the order-`P` physical velocity norm. The result is $1+\mathrm{norm}\le3\,\mathrm{freq}^{2(P+1)}$ for the scheduled new frequency. Explicit graph-cost inequalities and prefactor caps absorb all dependence on order and depth.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The retained physical velocity satisfies the full-depth budget

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a hierarchy-regular seed at an active time, a scaled jet bound for the unwrapped unswitched leading wave transfers unchanged to its centered skew-periodization. The wrapped profile is jointly smooth in label and phase, one-periodic, and has zero phase mean. Envelope support inside the centered cell supplies boundary smoothness; phase translation preserves the mean, and the centered-cell jet theorem transfers the budget.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Centered wrapping preserves the unswitched leading jet budget

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Collects joint slab smoothness, spatial periodicity, velocity-type oddness, even pressure, Eulerian divergence freedom, the full profile divergence identity, and exact equality between momentum and `b.residual`. The fields are already fixed by `b`; the structure records propositions about them. It deliberately contains no residual smallness, pressure Hessian, or growth estimate.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Qualitative equations and symmetries of the approximate fields

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a supplied cutoff stage with cutoff bounds and the full-depth velocity estimate, proves that the difference between cutoff and untruncated velocities is smooth, periodic and divergence free. On the slab its order-two half-Hölder norm is at most the child frequency to power $-5/2$. This is the small correction required by the next deformation estimate.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The cutoff tail is small enough for the child flow

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Given the step numerical budget and a full-depth Hölder bound for the actual approximation, bounds the weighted truncation error by the fifth inverse power of the following frequency. The cutoff is taken at the fifth power of the child frequency. This theorem performs the numerical absorption; the approximation-size estimate remains an explicit hypothesis `hSize`.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The scheduled Fourier tail decays at the next frequency

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For each time in the slab, rewrites the exact residual equation using the lift of the smooth periodic slice potential. The time derivative is `derivWithin` on $[0,T]$, so the statement includes both time endpoints. It identifies the equation used by the cutoff stage without asserting that this residual vanishes.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Write the momentum equation with the slice potential

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Given qualitative physical approximation properties and an even multiplier `ψ`, produces a truncated-child stage whose input velocity and residual are exactly `b.velocity` and `b.residual`. Its pressure input is the slice potential already constructed from `b`. The radius `Λ` is arbitrary here; numerical cutoff bounds and admissibility are additional later requirements.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Truncate the same physical velocity and residual

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Packages a transverse output, two switch profiles, the leading momentum identity, and the odd velocity and even pressure parities. The parent geometry `d` fixes the actual hierarchy operators. The identity includes `leadingSwitch`, while `completionSwitch` is retained separately for the finite expansion. This structure does not itself require nonzero amplitude, normalization, or quantitative bounds.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Leading profiles and the two activation sources

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Requires the leading velocity, phase pressure, leading switch, and completion switch to vanish on `hierarchyInactiveRegion T τ S`. That region lies on the time slab and consists of times before `τ` or labels outside `S`. The four conditions concern the supplied leading input only; later support propagation is a separate theorem.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: A common region where leading inputs vanish

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: If an even-reflection profile agrees on the slab with a label-only function `f`, then `f t` is even for every slab time. Setting the phase to zero converts simultaneous label-phase reflection into ordinary label reflection. This extracts parity of the physical strain and transported covector from the parent-geometry profiles.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Even phase independent profiles give even label fields

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Constructs `PhysicalLeadingInput g` using a seed over the same parent’s material gradient and transported covector. It requires seed regularity, the smooth periodic odd parent flow, and even seed amplitude. The output, momentum identity, and two activation sources are those already proved for the wrapped seed; parent reflection supplies the needed coframe and coefficient parities.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Build the physical leading input from the selected seed

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a closed `S` containing the support of the periodized radial envelope, the later-wave physical input is inactive before `t₀` and outside `S`. It packages the four established vanishing statements for velocity, pressure, and the two switch sources. The construction hypotheses match `ofLaterWave`, so support belongs to that exact selected input.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The physical leading input inherits its envelope support

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Builds `PhysicalLeadingInput` for a smooth periodic odd parent flow and a regular seed with even label amplitude. It constructs the leading transverse pair, the leading activation source, its curl completion, the momentum identity and their required parity. The cutoff is supplied rather than chosen, and no quantitative seed or pressure estimates are part of this constructor.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Constructing the physical leading input from the paper cutoff

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Let $0\le t_0<T$, and take the constructed smooth seed, its radial envelope inside the label cell, $0<h\le1$, and the transported nonzero covector. Assume a smooth periodic odd parent and an even seed on $[t_0,T]$. For any smooth $0\le\widetilde\chi\le1$ on $[0,T]$ vanishing before $t_0$, the formal statement gives $C[\widetilde\chi A_1]=\widetilde\chi C[A_1]$ and identifies the corresponding activation term as $\widetilde\chi'C[A_1]$. Both equalities hold for every label and phase after the prescribed extension from the centered cell. The statement verifies (3.7) for this selected wave family; the paper formulates the identity for arbitrary suitable leading data.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The cutoff multiplies the correction and its activation term

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For a seed launched at time zero with the constant first cutoff, the constructed physical leading input has both `leadingSwitch = 0` and `completionSwitch = 0`. Smoothness, periodicity, parent oddness and amplitude evenness are retained hypotheses. The velocity itself is not zero: only the sources generated by differentiating its constant time cutoff vanish.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The first wave has no completion activation source

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: For the leading input built from the paper cutoff, all four relevant profiles vanish before activation and outside a closed label set containing the envelope support. The conclusion is the bundled `Inactive` property. The support inclusion and closedness of `S` are explicit, because curl completion must also vanish in the same region.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The leading input vanishes in its inactive region

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: If an approximation’s leading data equal the `ofPaperCutoff` construction for the given parent and seed, the approximation has `LeadingRelayData`. The theorem derives this interface from the explicit leading equation and completion, rather than assuming it as an unrelated field. It does not provide the quantitative relay-coefficient estimates needed later in the recurrence.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: The constructed leading input supplies the relay identity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.text: Take the selected smooth localized seed with $0<h\le1$, a radial envelope contained in the label cell, and a smooth periodic odd parent whose transported covector is nonzero. Assume the seed is even on its active interval $[t_0,T]$. For any smooth cutoff $\widetilde\chi$ on $[0,T]$ valued in $[0,1]$ and zero before $t_0$, the sum of the leading and correction activation terms equals $\widetilde\chi'(A_1+C[A_1])$ at every label and phase. This is (3.8) for the selected periodically extended wave. It is an exact identity; a small residual also requires a bound on $\widetilde\chi'$ and the wave during activation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Physi.summary: Differentiating the cutoff multiplies the entire completed leading wave

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.text:
Smooth phase-independent coefficients of the actual affine-wave equation on the label torus.

Default-value audit (b5): The initial covector is required nonzero, and its evolution equation and joint smoothness are fields of the record. Later-time nonvanishing is proved from these conditions, rather than assumed from a totalized norm expression.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.summary: The coefficients of the transverse affine-wave equation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.text: Shows that changing only phase leaves the covector profile unchanged on the time slab. Both profile values equal the same actual covector at that time and label. This is needed when averaging fast advection and constructing the divergence completion; it follows from the record’s value identity, not just its periodicity.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.summary: The covector profile does not depend on phase

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.text: Propagates the initial nonzero covector along its linear transport equation at a fixed label. Continuity of the strain gives uniqueness, so a nonzero initial solution cannot become zero. The conclusion concerns the represented covector at phase zero on the closed slab; phase independence transfers it to other phases.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.summary: The transported covector stays nonzero on the slab

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.text: Derives spatial periodicity of the represented covector on each certified time slice. Phase independence turns the lattice-phase twist into ordinary label periodicity. The proof concerns the coefficient’s representation and does not itself establish the covector transport equation or its nonvanishing, which are separate fields of the coefficient record.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.summary: The transported covector is periodic in its labels

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.text: Derives label periodicity of the actual strain field on the closed time slab. Its values equal those of a twisted profile independently of phase, so the twist’s compensating phase shift has no effect. This extracts a property of the physical coefficients from their equality with the stored profile representation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.summary: The represented strain is periodic in its labels

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.text: Given `hfreq : freq ≠ 0` and `TransverseCoefficients d`, this constructs all four `TransverseTimeCoefficients` from their actual formulas. The scalar frequency and the covector are distinct: covector nonvanishing is inherited from `d`. Joint smoothness and periodicity allow the coefficients to be bundled as phase-independent profiles. The returned equalities identify the coefficients of this same transverse equation; no inverse estimate is part of the constructor.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.summary: Construct the coefficients for the selected transverse solve

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.text: The fields are smooth on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, one-periodic in phase, and invariant under $(a,s)\mapsto(a+n,s+k_*\cdot n)$. The transverse solution consists of a velocity $V$ and pressure $\mathsf p$ satisfying (5.15), with $V(0)=0$ and zero phase mean for the pressure. Its pressure is the normalized primitive specified by (5.16). The formulation also records the support and reflection properties used in §5.5: vanishing of the source before activation or outside a label set passes to both fields.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.summary: The forced equation includes its normalized pressure

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.text:
Let a transverse profile $V$ and its normalized pressure $q$ solve the transverse equation with source $F$ on $[0,T]$. For a differentiable inverse-label map $A$, assume its derivative is the inverse coefficient $G$ and $\kappa=G^Tk_*$. Then $
abla q^
atural=(\mathbf d q+P_\kappa(F-2MV))^
atural$, where $q^
atural(t,x)=q(t,A(t,x),k_*\cdot A(t,x))$ and $P_\kappa=\kappa\otimes\kappa/|\kappa|^2$. In Lemma 5.9 the source is $f_p+f_p^S$. This equation replaces one fast phase derivative by forcing and velocity terms. It is an identity, not yet the Hessian bound; one further derivative and quantitative profile bounds are still required.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.summary: Use the equation before taking another physical derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.text: For an actual `TransverseResult`, assume zero-mean forcing, inactivity outside a closed label support and before `t₀`, a positive differentiable weight, compatible lift and pullback, homogeneous weighted forward stability, and the displayed coefficient bounds. Then the velocity seminorm plus carrier-weighted pressure seminorm is bounded by `transverseSolveNormConstant` times the source seminorm. The active interval must satisfy `t₀ < T`.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.summary: The transverse solution obeys a weighted finite-order estimate

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.text: For `freq > 0`, the phase derivative of the normalized pressure profile equals the pressure-velocity coefficient acting on the selected velocity plus the pressure-source coefficient acting on `F`. This promotes the ordinary phase-slope equation to profile equality. It is an identity for the chosen pressure, whose zero phase mean is used separately to recover its norm.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.summary: The normalized pressure equation holds as a profile identity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.text: For positive carrier `freq`, the phase derivative of `freq • r.output.p` is the sum of the normalized pressure-velocity coefficient acting on `r.output.V` and the pressure-source coefficient acting on `F`. This is an ordinary phase derivative, not a time derivative. It preserves the pressure of the same selected transverse result and supplies its inverse-carrier scaling.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.summary: The normalized pressure has the selected phase slope

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.text: The pointwise projected velocity equation for `TransverseResult r` is promoted to an equality of twisted profiles: its time derivative is the sum of coefficient application to velocity and to source. Positive slab duration supplies unique within-derivatives. The same output profile `r.output.V` occurs on both sides, which is needed when its successive time norms are estimated.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.summary: The selected velocity equation holds as a profile identity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.text: For the selected result `r`, use a positive slab, $0\le t_0\le T$, and a continuous positive amplitude on the active slab. Assume `freq > 0`, nonnegative `C₀,C`, the undifferentiated estimate `hBase`, and coefficient bounds `hA`, `hB`, `hP`, `hQ`. The weighted time norm through order `q` of velocity plus `freq` times that of pressure is at most `transverseTimeCost` times the source norm through the same order. Zero phase mean recovers pressure from its slope and preserves the inverse-frequency gain.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.summary: Bound time jets of the same transverse velocity and pressure

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.text: For the existing `TransverseResult r`, its time derivative equals the stored velocity coefficient applied to its own velocity plus the source coefficient applied to `F`. The result is a `HasDerivWithinAt` statement at each slab time and label-phase point. It eliminates pressure using `r.pressure_slope`, retaining the same solution and force rather than invoking a fresh inverse.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.summary: Eliminate pressure in the selected transverse velocity equation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.text: This structure stores the velocity generator, source projection, and two normalized pressure coefficients as smooth twisted profiles, together with their exact slab values. Only the pressure coefficients use the normalized covector `freq⁻¹ • κ`. The fields certify identification with the supplied `TransverseCoefficients d`; they do not include numerical bounds, solve an equation, or assert positivity of `freq`.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.Trans.summary: The four coefficients of the transverse velocity and pressure

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text:
The parent coefficient budgets for the normalized potential, pressure, and the three coframe contractions in the linear relay.

Default-value audit (b5): This proposition requires genuine smooth coefficient fields and finite mixed-word bounds. It is a supplied budget, not a theorem that arbitrary parent data have those bounds.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: Parent coefficient bounds used by the linear relay

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: If $D\ge1$, $L\ge0$, and $|\ell^{-1}|\le D^q$, the budget $L(1+|\ell^{-1}|)D^{15}$ is bounded by $2LD^{15+q}$. The theorem enlarges a supplied budget accordingly. It does not choose the width; the crucial bound `hℓInv` must come from that earlier parameter choice.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The chosen width becomes a fixed parent power

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: Every field of a relay coefficient budget with value `A` remains true under a larger value `B`. The theorem applies the assembly rule with both parts enlarged by `hAB`. The derivative orders and coefficient functions stay fixed, so this step changes only the numerical allowance, not the underlying relay.

Given four potential or pressure coefficient bounds at order $n+1$ and three families of geometric row bounds at order $n$, this theorem builds one `WaveRelayCoefficientBudget`. The common value `K` must dominate both `Kp` and `Kg`. All analytic estimates are inputs here; the proof only enlarges and packages them.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: Combining potential and geometric coefficient allowances

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: This proposition records all-order label-jet bounds for the inverse coframe, strain, normalized covector, and inverse squared covector norm. Their slopes are seven, six, seven, and sixteen, with fixed residual powers. It also records slice smoothness and nonvanishing of the covector. The type `X` indexes times or any chosen subset without requiring time derivatives.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The parent derivatives needed for the linear relay

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: This proposition requires a common bound `K` for the coefficient time norms of a specified `WaveRelayTimeCoefficients` bundle. The four inner primitive coefficients are measured through spatial order `n+1`; curl, material, and gradient rows use order `n`. Every row uses the same time order `q`. The extra inner order is spent by the label derivative outside the primitive.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: One bound for all normalized relay coefficients

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: Packages four primitive coefficient profiles and three families of coordinate rows for a given inverse deformation `G`, material gradient `M`, covector `κ`, radius `ell`, and carrier `freq`. Each field carries its canonical equality at every slab time, label, and output phase, with `G`, `M`, and `κ` read at phase zero. These equalities fix the actual coefficients; they do not assert bounds, a flow equation, or nonvanishing of `κ`.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The normalized coefficients of completion and relay

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: This record requires mixed bounds through time order `q` with common spatial slope `p`. The four inner coefficient families use `Ainner` and `Cinner`, while curl, material, and gradient rows use `Aouter` and `Couter`. Separating them keeps the inverse label radius in the outer amplitude. These are required inequalities on supplied coefficients, not a theorem establishing them.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: Separate mixed bounds inside and outside the phase primitive

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: This proposition collects joint time-label smoothness for four inner potential or pressure coefficients and three coordinate-indexed outer geometric coefficients. It refers to the exact formulas built from `G`, `M`, `κ`, `ell`, and `freq`. It does not assert any mixed-jet size, and a constructor for the record must provide each regularity proof.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: Smoothness of the seven label coefficient families

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: Given the exact coefficient profiles `R` and their mixed label bounds, the theorem produces the factorial time-seminorm budget used for completion and relay estimates. It assumes $0<T\le1$, nonnegative amplitudes and costs, and `ell * D^p ≤ 1`. Inner coefficients are measured at spatial order `n+1`; outer rows at `n`. Their two resulting costs are added into one budget.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: Convert label coefficient jets to the relay budget

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: Defines the completion profile as the sum of three differentiated potential primitives, each acted on by its curl row, multiplied by `freq⁻¹`. The input `v` must have zero phase mean and the slab has positive length. This coordinate expression is built from the canonical coefficient bundle; its equality to the selected curl completion is proved separately under the necessary nondegeneracy assumptions.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: Completion as three normalized coordinate terms

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: Identifies `completionProfile` with the selected `complete` operator when the input's phase average is zero, `G` and `κ` are phase-independent, the covector never vanishes on the slab, the radius is nonzero, and the carrier is positive. The proof restores the carrier scale in the potential and the label scale in the curl. This equality connects the separately estimated expression to the actual hierarchy operator.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The normalized coordinate completion is the actual curl completion

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: Unfolds the completion profile at a slab time as the carrier inverse times three curl rows applied to scaled label derivatives of the normalized relay potential. The input is centered, and the canonical coefficient equalities replace the bundled rows and potential. This intermediate identity does not need nonzero carrier or radius; those assumptions enter the following comparison with the physical completion.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: Evaluate the completion through its canonical potential

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: For positive `freq`, a nonnegative cap `K`, and a `WaveRelayTimeCoefficientBudget`, bounds the weighted time norm of completion at order `n` by the common order constant times $K^2\mathrm{freq}^{-1}$ and the input norm at `n+1`. The input is centered. This theorem estimates the coordinate completion; identifying it with the selected physical completion additionally uses `completionProfile_eq_complete`.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: Completion keeps one inverse carrier factor after time differentiation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: For coordinate index `i`, this field is the curl row obtained from the phase-zero inverse coframe `G`, scaled by `ell⁻¹`. It converts one scaled label derivative into its contribution to the physical curl. The covector and new frequency do not occur in this outer geometric row; its explicit width cost is tracked separately.

From a nonnegative input cost array `C` and time order `q`, choose nonnegative arrays `Kinner` and `Kouter` before the slab, parent coefficients, frequency, or amplitude are supplied. Smooth phase-independent input profiles, a nowhere-zero normalized covector, four mixed bounds, and `ell * D^16 ≤ 1` then produce the exact relay profiles. Their common budget is $K_{\mathrm{inner}}(n)A^6+K_{\mathrm{outer}}(n)\|\ell^{-1}\|A^2$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: Choose relay coefficient costs before the parent data

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: At each time and label, the phase-zero inverse coframe determines a map from a scalar derivative to the vector pressure-gradient contribution in coordinate direction `i`. The factor `ell⁻¹` compensates for the scaled label derivative. This outer row has no inverse wave-vector factor and does not itself define the pressure.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: A label row for the pulled-back pressure gradient

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: This abbreviation evaluates a twisted profile at `(t,a,0)` and views the result as a function of time and label. By itself it does not assert that other phase values agree or that the label slice is spatially periodic. Those properties are supplied separately when the coefficient is converted back into a phase-independent profile.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: Read a coefficient at independent phase zero

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: This row combines the inverse coframe and strain as `M.comp (curlRow G) - curlRow (G.comp M)`, with the same inverse label-width factor. It is the geometric contribution to the material derivative of a completion. The formula is algebraic; identifying it with the evolving coframe requires the separate equation $G_t=-GM$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: A label row for the material derivative of the completion

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: Assuming phase independence of `G`, `M`, and `κ` and the `LabelRegularity` record, this constructor places each of the seven coefficient formulas into the smooth twisted profile space. Their periodicity follows from the phase-zero slices. Equality fields retain their exact values throughout the slab, so later norm estimates concern these coefficients rather than arbitrary fields with similar bounds.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: Build periodic profiles from the exact label coefficients

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: For two continuous functions in a complete normed space, the normalized phase primitive of their sum is the sum of their normalized primitives. The statement does not assume either function has zero phase mean. It proves the additive identity through derivative recovery and vanishing of the normalization constants, and is used to separate the relay's pressure and potential terms.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The normalized phase primitive is additive

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: At each time and label, normalize the phase-zero covector by `freq⁻¹` and apply the potential coefficient $v\mapsto-\|k\|^{-2}(k\times v)$. This is the inner coefficient used before a phase primitive in the completion and relay formulas. The abbreviation supplies exact values; smoothness, nonvanishing, and bounds are separate obligations.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The normalized potential coefficient on label space

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: This label field evaluates the strain `M` and normalized covector at phase zero, then applies the algebraic coefficient appearing in the time derivative of the wave potential. It is linear in the profile amplitude but depends nonlinearly on the normalized covector. Its name does not assert a differential identity; the covector and coframe evolution laws justify that interpretation later.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The time coefficient of the normalized potential

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: The `potentialTime` coefficient does not depend on the independent phase on the slab, because its stored formula uses only the material gradient and normalized covector at phase zero. This conclusion follows from the value equality, not from a time-derivative computation. It permits multiplying a centered velocity profile before taking the normalized primitive.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The differentiated potential coefficient is independent of phase

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: The potential coefficient in the supplied bundle is phase-independent on the time slab. Its defining equality evaluates a canonical function of the normalized covector at phase zero, so changing the output phase does not change the value. This property is needed to preserve the zero phase mean before taking the potential primitive.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The potential coefficient is independent of phase

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: This abbreviation gives the scalar row $v\mapsto-2\langle k,Mv\rangle/\|k\|^2$ at each label point, with `k` equal to `freq⁻¹` times the covector slice. It is the velocity contribution to the normalized oscillatory pressure. The source contribution is a different row, so this object alone is not the full pressure or its time derivative.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The normalized pressure coefficient multiplying velocity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: Shows that the row multiplying the velocity in the normalized oscillatory pressure is phase-independent on the slab. The bundle fixes it as a canonical function of `M` and the normalized covector at phase zero. This allows that row to pass through phase averaging when proving the pressure primitive remains normalized.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The pressure amplitude coefficient is independent of phase

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: Defines the corresponding two-product constant for a vector-to-scalar pressure coefficient followed by a scalar-to-vector gradient row. The inner operation is measured at order `n+1`, and the outer at `n`; the factor two again accounts for the normalized phase primitive. Its target spaces distinguish it from the vector primitive cost.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The order constant for pressure primitive terms

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: This scalar row maps a source vector to $\langle k,f\rangle/\|k\|^2$, using the phase-zero normalized covector. Together with the strain-dependent pressure-amplitude row it expresses the normalized pressure in the relay. The abbreviation merely identifies the coefficient function, leaving smoothness, valid normalization, and mixed bounds to later statements.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The normalized pressure coefficient multiplying the source

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: Shows that the row multiplying the forcing profile in the normalized pressure depends only on time and label. Its stored value formula reads the normalized covector at phase zero, so every independent phase gives the same row. Consequently it can preserve a forcing profile's zero phase mean before the pressure primitive is taken.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The pressure source coefficient is independent of phase

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: Packages evaluation at a point as a linear map for a profile with any normed real target space. It preserves finite sums and scalar multiples by their pointwise definitions. The private helper is used to unfold completion and relay formulas under evaluation, allowing the coordinate sums to be compared with their physical expressions.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: Evaluate a profile before comparing coordinate formulas

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: Defines the relay by summing five primitive terms in each of the three label directions and multiplying by `freq⁻¹`. They contain the time-potential coefficient on `v`, the potential coefficient on `f`, the material row on the potential of `v`, and the two pressure primitives. Both `v` and `f` are centered. The formula records the coordinate expression; equality with `waveRelayAt` is a later theorem.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: Relay as five normalized terms in each coordinate

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: For centered `v` and `f`, nonzero radius, positive carrier, and a time in the slab, evaluates the coordinate relay and identifies it with `waveRelayAt G M κ v f`. The proof restores the carrier scale, expands normalized potential and pressure primitives, and uses the three-coordinate formula. This is an algebraic identity of the canonical expressions; it does not assume that `v` solves the transverse evolution equation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The measured relay equals the canonical physical expression

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: Under positive carrier, `K ≥ 0`, and the common coefficient budget, bounds the coordinate relay time norm by the order constant times $K^2\mathrm{freq}^{-1}$ and the sum of the time norms of `v` and `f` at spatial order `n+1`. Both inputs are centered, and any bounded time weight is allowed. The time order stays `q`; its dependence is contained in the coefficient cap.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: Relay keeps one derivative loss and one inverse carrier factor

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: Restricts a smooth profile to any time on its slab and obtains an unrestricted smooth function of label and phase. The proof composes with the fixed-time coordinate inclusion. This private helper provides the Fréchet differentiability needed to expand the potential and pressure sums in the exact relay identification.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: A profile is smooth in label and phase at fixed time

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: Combines the vector and pressure primitive costs as nine times their sum. The factor accommodates the three coordinate directions and the groups of terms in the relay. This single spatial-order constant is used for both completion and relay; the time-order dependence and parent scale remain in the separately supplied coefficient bound `K`.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: One order constant covers completion and relay

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: Proves nonnegativity of the common completion and relay constant at every spatial order. Unfolding leaves operator norms, finite cardinalities, natural powers, and positive numerical factors. The result is used when multiplying coefficient and source inequalities in the mixed-time completion and relay bounds.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The common relay order constant is nonnegative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: Specializes the relay primitive estimate when the inner coefficient at order `n+1` and the outer row at order `n` are both bounded by `K ≥ 0`. Their product becomes $K^2$. The input remains centered, the inner coefficient phase-independent, and the output retains the input's bounded time weight. The spatial order on the input is still `n+1`.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: Two coefficient bounds give a square of their common cap

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: For any seminorm `N` and three profiles whose seminorms are each at most `C`, bounds the seminorm of their sum by `3 * C`. It uses the seminorm triangle inequality and the cardinality of `Fin 3`. No smoothness or frequency hypothesis is added to the profile type.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: Three bounded coordinate terms have at most triple the bound

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.text: Defines twice the product of the vector-operator evaluation constants at spatial orders `n` and `n+1`. The factor two comes from the normalized phase primitive; the order shift records its following label derivative. This constant depends only on spatial order and the fixed finite-dimensional evaluation map, not on frequency or time order.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.WaveR.summary: The order constant for vector primitive terms

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.activ.text: For the actual parent geometry, a regular seed and representatives agreeing with its unswitched velocity and pressure on the active interval, proves transversality and zero leading material-plus-phase-pressure momentum on that interval. The proof first works on the centered cell, uses within-interval time derivatives, then transfers by twisted periodicity. It does not extend the homogeneous equation to earlier times where the representatives were freely extended.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.activ.summary: The actual unswitched wave satisfies homogeneous active momentum

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.text: This measures a profile family and its exact algebraic source expressions using full-slab supremum seminorms for means and active amplitude-weighted supremum seminorms for oscillations and pressure. The `holder` flag is fixed to `False`. It supplies actual nonnegative measurements, while the analytic recurrence inequalities and hierarchy equations are still separate requirements.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.summary: Insert genuine spatial measurements into the hierarchy recurrence

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.text: The omitted completion–oscillation and mean–oscillation phase interactions are bounded by the supplied fast coefficient cap. Inactivity transfers `u.C (i-1)` and `u.Y j` to active amplitude norms, while the mean stays unweighted on the full slab. The resulting products use the completion or mean at order $n$ and the oscillation at order $n+1$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.summary: The two omitted fast interactions have measured bounds

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.text: The theorem bounds three terms separately: the averaged oscillation advection, the averaged divergence product, and advection between means. Their bounds use `actualMeasuredLevels` at order $n+1$. Inactivity converts full-slab oscillation norms to active weighted norms, while `hf : 0 ≤ freq` permits discarding the pressure part of the measured oscillation size.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.summary: The three slow contributions to a mean source

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.text: Replacing the positive amplitude weight by a positive constant multiple divides both the measured oscillatory level and its measured source by that constant. This uses the exact seminorm scaling for velocity, pressure and source. The result is restricted to these two quantities; it does not state a similar change for the unweighted mean levels.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.summary: Velocity and source sizes change by the same factor

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.text: The actual measurements satisfy the reconstruction inequality for `Y p = V p + C (p-1)` and the identity `s.Z = s.Y + s.mean`. The pressure contribution is nonnegative and can enlarge the oscillation bound. Here `s.Z` is a sum of two measurements, rather than the norm of the combined profile `u.Z p`.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.summary: Reconstruct the oscillatory and mean budgets from the profiles

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.text: Under a common scaled-row cap and inactivity of all `Y` profiles, the full-slab norm of a tail label product is at most $KL$ times the two measured `Z` sizes at order $n+1$. The first factor is enlarged to that order by monotonicity. The theorem requires $\ell\ne0$ and the supplied numerical coframe inequality.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.summary: A slow tail product costs one more mixed derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.text: Given coframe and fast-covector caps, phase independence of `G`, and inactivity of all oscillations and corrections, this theorem fills `HierarchySourceTermBounds` for the measured profiles. It still takes the exact averaged-source identity, centered-relay identity, residual bound, and relay bound as inputs. Thus it assembles the quadratic estimates; it does not independently derive those four premises.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.summary: Putting the actual sources into the norm recurrence

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.text: If `u.V (P+1)` and `u.B (P+1)` vanish, the measured `Y` and `Z` sizes at that index both equal the size of `u.C P`, and its mean size is zero. Lean indexes a completion by the velocity that produced it. This is the paper’s convention $Y_{P+1}=Z_{P+1}=C_{P+1}$ expressed in that indexing.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.summary: At the last index only the completion remains

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.text: When the oscillatory part `u.Y i` vanishes before activation and $\gamma\le1$, the full-slab unweighted norm of `u.Z i` is bounded by the measured amplitude norm of its oscillation plus the unweighted mean. The proof applies the triangle inequality to $Z_i=Y_i+B_i$ and changes norms only on the inactive oscillation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.summary: The full velocity is bounded by its measured pieces

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.text: Builds `HierarchySourceTermBounds` for the actual twisted operators, measuring mean forcing with `q-1` time jets and oscillatory forcing with `q`. It requires nonzero scales, a positive active weight bounded by one, inactivity of oscillations and completions, and coefficient caps. Exact mean-source identities, centered relay identities, the lower-order residual bound, and the relay estimate are supplied hypotheses. Natural subtraction gives `q-1 = 0` when `q = 0`; a strict order reduction is used only in positive-order applications.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.summary: The actual sources use one fewer time derivative for means

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.text: Bounds the three kinds of omitted products: slow label products, fast completion products, and fast mean products. All conclusions use the full time order `q`, while the measured-level record still stores mean forcing at `q-1`. The theorem assumes nonzero scales, coefficient caps, a positive active weight at most one, and inactivity of oscillations and completions. The resulting estimates are supplied to the finite-depth residual theorem; no residual sum is bounded here.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.summary: The omitted nonlinear terms obey the full time order bounds

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.text: This constructs the finite mixed-word seminorm of a twisted profile after restricting time to `A` and multiplying by the time-only weight `τ`. The explicit boundedness proof covers every profile and admissible word. The Boolean-like proposition `holder` controls whether half-Hölder difference quotients are included with the pointwise measurements.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.summary: Measure actual scaled derivatives on a chosen time set

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.text: The actual seminorm evaluates to the finite-word norm of `weightedSlices A τ f`. The equality is definitional and exposes that weighting occurs at fixed time before label and phase differentiation. The separate boundedness proof certifies the suprema while leaving their exact measurement formula unchanged.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.actua.summary: Read the finite norm of the weighted time slices

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.affin.text: The affine-wave amplitude operator equals minus the strain plus twice the strain followed by projection in the covector direction, written with the rank-one operator and $(\|\kappa\|^2)^{-1}$. This algebraic identity holds even at zero covector because both sides use totalized inversion. Nonzero covectors are required separately when this expression is interpreted as the transverse geometric projection.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.affin.summary: Separate the strain and projected strain terms

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.all_o.text: If a property of time, label and phase is preserved by the specified twisted lattice shifts and holds on the centered cell at every slab time, then it holds throughout the profile slab. The property is arbitrary. The proof moves each label to its centered representative and transports the assertion by the corresponding phase shift.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.all_o.summary: A centered-cell property extends by lattice shifts

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text:
The Appendix D seminorm with the reciprocal seed amplitude on the closed interval `[t₀,T]`, where the seed is strictly positive.

Default-value audit (b5): The definition requires 0 ≤ t₀ ≤ T, T > 0, continuity of γ and strict positivity at every active time. The compact-interval reciprocal bound is proved before selecting a numerical bound. Division by a vanishing amplitude is therefore excluded at the intended times.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: The finite norm divided by the seed amplitude

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: The amplitude seminorm is exactly the finite-word norm of the profile divided by `γ` on `Icc t₀ T`. Continuity and strict positivity of `γ` on that compact interval justify bounded inverse weight, including both endpoints. Only label and phase derivatives are measured; the weight is constant on each spatial slice.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: The amplitude-weighted norm uses the closed active interval

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: For a continuous strictly positive amplitude `γ` on $[t₀,T]$, averaging a profile does not increase its amplitude-weighted order-$n$ norm. Compactness gives a bound for $\gamma^{-1}$, allowing the bounded-weight theorem to apply. No assumption that $\gamma\le1$ or that the profile vanishes before activation is needed for this contraction.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: Phase averaging preserves the amplitude bound

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: If the mean–mean label product is fixed by phase averaging, subtracting the average leaves only terms with an oscillatory factor. Assuming `u.Y j` vanishes before activation and $\gamma\le1$, the centered norm is bounded by twice the slow cost times the weighted-plus-mean factor norms. The second factor consumes order $n+1$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: Centering removes the product of two means

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: This enlarges the first factor’s order in the centered slow-product estimate from $n$ to $n+1$, leaving the second already at $n+1$. Monotonicity of weighted and unweighted seminorms proves the bound. The same mean-invariance, inactivity, and $\gamma\le1$ hypotheses are retained for use in the recurrence.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: Both centered-product factors may use the next order

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: For $0<\gamma\le1$, a completion profile `C` that vanishes before activation has its full-slab norm controlled by its amplitude norm. Fast advection of `Y` by `C`, minus its phase average, is then bounded by twice the product estimate. The covector remains unweighted, and the derivative falls on `Y` at order $n+1$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: Centering a fast product costs a factor two

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: If a typed profile and a raw field agree on the active interval, their weighted finite mixed derivative norms agree at every order. The interval lies in the parent slab, and its amplitude weight is continuous and strictly positive. The proof rewrites equal time slices before differentiating in labels and phase; it does not need the two fields to agree outside the active interval.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: The typed amplitude norm equals the raw active norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: On the active interval with continuous positive `γ`, label advection is controlled by the amplitude norm of `z` and the full-slab unweighted norm of `g`, with one extra derivative on `g`. The inverse amplitude is a bounded time multiplier. No derivative of `γ` enters this estimate.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: The advector can carry the amplitude weight

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: With the same positive continuous amplitude, the weight may instead be placed on the differentiated profile `g`. The advector `z` is measured without weight on the full slab, while `g` uses order $n+1$ on the active interval. The coframe cost and nonzero label width remain hypotheses.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: The differentiated profile can carry the amplitude weight

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: If every time slice has scaled jets bounded by `γ t * B`, its amplitude-weighted seminorm is bounded by the number of admissible words times `B`. The theorem assumes nonzero scales, $B\ge0$, a nonempty slab, and continuous strictly positive `γ`. Positivity justifies cancelling the inverse weight after spatial and phase differentiation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: Scaled jets control the amplitude-weighted finite norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: Bound the exact sum of derivative seminorms by a common word bound.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: Word bounds control the exact weighted norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: For a mean-zero twisted profile and a continuous positive time weight on $[t_0,T]$, the oscillatory amplitude seminorm is at most twice the corresponding seminorm of its phase derivative. The interval starts at `t₀ ≥ 0` and is nonempty. The proof recovers the field as the periodic primitive of its derivative; no extra label or phase order is charged.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: The phase derivative controls a mean-zero profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: Increasing the derivative order from `n` to `m` with `n ≤ m` cannot decrease the amplitude seminorm. The active interval, scales, and positive amplitude function are unchanged. The proof adds nonnegative word measurements, so it does not require a comparison between distinct seed amplitudes.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: Higher spatial orders enlarge the same amplitude-weighted norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: For a continuous positive weight on the active closed interval and a positive constant `c`, replacing the weight by `c * γ` divides the amplitude seminorm by `c`. The statement works with either value of the Hölder flag. Positivity prevents the inverse factor from degenerating and preserves the seminorm interpretation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: Multiplying the weight divides the amplitude seminorm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: Let the profiles be smooth and compatible with the label lattice on $[0,T]$, let $h\ne0$, and let $\gamma$ be continuous and strictly positive on $[t_0,T]$. The weighted norm of $(Z\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY$ is controlled by the unweighted norm of $Z$, the next weighted norm of $Y$, and the coefficient $h^{-1}\kappa$. This gives the second estimate of (5.39) after applying the parent bounds. With $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, the resulting frequency cost is $\lambda^{3/2}$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: A fast derivative costs the scaled wave vector

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: For the product $(\mathbf d\cdot V)Y$, this version assigns the reciprocal amplitude to `V`, which is measured at order $n+1$. The second factor uses the full-slab unweighted order-$n$ norm. The theorem allows the declared Hölder flag and obtains the same $3Q_n^2L$ coframe cost.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: Weighting the factor inside the divergence

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.text: Here the amplitude weight is assigned to `Y`, while the differentiated factor `V` is measured in the unweighted order-$(n+1)$ norm. The estimate applies on the active interval with positive continuous `γ`, nonzero label width, and the supplied scaled-row bound. This placement is needed for mixed mean–oscillation interactions.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ampli.summary: Weighting the factor outside the divergence

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.apply.text: An operator-valued twisted profile acts pointwise on a vector-valued profile with the same carrier. Each factor repeats under the same joint shift, so the result does too. This bilinear operation retains smoothness and phase periodicity and supports the concrete hierarchy’s coefficient multiplications.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.apply.summary: Apply compatible operator and vector profiles pointwise

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.apply.text: At a point `x` of the profile slab, `applyField A f` evaluates to the continuous linear map `A x` applied to `f x`. This exposes the ordinary pointwise meaning of the bundled bilinear operation. The lemma is used to turn equalities of profile values into the Leibniz identities needed for the time norm.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.apply.summary: Evaluate an operator profile on a vector profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.apply.text: For two bundled profiles `L` and `f`, evaluation of `applyField L f` at a slab point is ordinary application of $L(x)$ to $f(x)$. The result is valid for arbitrary real normed spaces of the declared types. It is an encoding identity used to expose scalar contractions inside divergence estimates.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.apply.summary: Applying a profile of linear maps pointwise

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.apply.text: The underlying periodic output of pointwise application in the twisted space is the corresponding periodic application of the two underlying inputs. This definitional equality exposes the original operation. It lets the proof of a concrete equation ignore the additional lattice-symmetry wrapper without losing that certified property.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.apply.summary: The twisted product retains ordinary operator application

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: The coefficient-independent twisted phase average is the actual unit-period integral.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: The twisted average is the unit-period integral

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: The lattice-compatible correction has zero phase average. This supplies the completion law of the finite solver.

For the constructed hierarchy, the phase average of the source equals the three slow-product sums. The hypotheses identify the selected completion with the concrete curl completion, impose phase-independent geometric coefficients and zero-mean selected pressures, and require a surjective label map with the correct coframe. The result establishes the cancellations that the abstract assembly lemma previously assumed.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: The selected twisted hierarchy has the exact averaged source

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: For positive slab length, a phase-independent twisted profile is fixed by the concrete average operator. This converts a value-level independence statement into the algebraic identity required by hierarchy construction. The period has length one, so averaging a constant phase slice returns that same slice.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: A phase-independent profile equals its average

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: If `C` has zero operator average and `D` agrees on the slab with a scalar time multiple of `C`, then `D` also has zero average. The theorem uses pointwise equality `hD` and does not demand differentiability of the scalar function. This handles the activation multiplier in the leading completion relay.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: A time multiplier preserves zero phase average

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: The abstract averaging operator evaluates to the ordinary one-period phase mean of the profile at fixed time and label. It identifies the algebraic hierarchy source split with the paper's averaging convention.
The concrete phase-average operator is idempotent. Taking a second full-period average therefore leaves the first average unchanged.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: Averaging a mean profile leaves it unchanged

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: A hierarchy average is a phase-independent, label-periodic mean profile.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: Averaging produces a periodic mean profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: All fields are smooth on $[0,T]$, periodic in phase and compatible with label translations; $\mathbf d=(D_aX)^{-T}\nabla_a$. If $Y$ has zero phase average and $B$ is independent of phase, then $\langle(Y\cdot\mathbf d)B\rangle_s=0$. The parent deformation coefficients are also phase independent. This removes one kind of mixed product when averaging $H_p$ in the proof of Theorem 5.6, leaving only interactions between two oscillations or two means.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: The mixed label interaction has zero phase average

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: Here the deformation coefficients in $\mathbf d=(D_aX)^{-T}\nabla_a$ are phase independent and all profiles are smooth and phase periodic on $[0,T]$. For a phase-independent $B$ and a zero-mean oscillation $Y$, the average of $(B\cdot\mathbf d)Y$ vanishes. Smoothness allows label differentiation to commute with phase averaging. Together with the reversed interaction, this supplies the mixed-product cancellation used after (5.42) to express the mean source using only the three displayed sums.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: The other mixed label interaction also averages to zero

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: The product of two phase-independent means under slow advection is phase independent.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: Slow advection of means is phase independent

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: Assume `G` is independent of phase and the scalar pressure profile has zero phase mean at every time and label. Then its label-gradient profile has zero average under the twisted operators. The derivative-of-average identity and coefficient independence are both needed; zero mean of pressure alone would not remove a phase-dependent coefficient.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: A phase-independent coframe preserves the pressure cancellation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: The phase average of a twisted vector profile is genuinely periodic in the labels at phase zero. A label translation changes the phase by the carrier pairing, but averaging over a full period removes that shift. This supplies an ordinary torus field for the mean solver, rather than merely a twisted field.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: Averaging removes the phase twist from the labels

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: The label-coordinate material relay preserves the unit-period phase mean zero.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: Material evolution preserves zero phase mean

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: The profiles are smooth on $[0,T]$, with phase period one; $\langle\cdot\rangle_s$ denotes integration over one phase period. The phase average of $(B\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY$ is zero whenever $B$ and $\kappa$ are phase independent and $Y$ is periodic. No zero-mean condition on $Y$ is needed for this identity. Applying it to each term of (5.28) proves that the supplementary source is admissible for the transverse equation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: The supplementary forcing has zero phase average

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: The inverse label map is assumed twice continuously differentiable and surjective, with the stated deformation and transported covector, and $\kappa\ne0$. Periodic integration by parts and the divergence correction identity give $\langle(C[V]\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY\rangle_s=\langle(\mathbf d\cdot V)Y\rangle_s$. The profile $V$ must be transverse and have zero phase average, with coefficients supplied by the parent flow. This is the cancellation in (5.42) that avoids the fast derivative cost when estimating the mean source.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: Phase integration turns the correction into a label divergence

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: The full-period phase average preserves reflection parity.

Let the deformation and strain coefficients be phase independent, and let the preceding correction, pressure and subtracted activation term each have zero phase average. The preceding curl correction and oscillatory pressure have zero phase average, so their linear contribution to $H_p$ averages to zero. The activation term removed at level two also has zero average. This leaves the quadratic terms, together with the separately added parent residual at level two, as the forcing of the mean equation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: Linear corrections do not contribute to the mean source

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.text: For $p\le P$, assume smooth phase-periodic profiles, phase-independent means, transverse zero-mean velocities and actual curl corrections, with $\kappa\ne0$ and coefficients induced by a twice differentiable surjective inverse label map. Averaging $H_p$ leaves label advection between oscillations, the label-divergence products obtained from (5.42), and label advection between means. The identity uses the actual transported coefficients and curl corrections, as well as the zero-mean and transversality constraints. It gives the three sums after (5.42); the source at level two additionally includes $R_U\circ X$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.avera.summary: Only slow quadratic interactions survive phase averaging

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text:
On a twisted profile every mixed jet is bounded on the slab, so any bounded time multiplier gives a genuine real-valued finite seminorm.

Default-value audit (b5): The interval is nondegenerate by hT and the chosen time set lies within it. The proof hτ bounds the weight, while profile smoothness and periodicity bound the sampled jets. An empty time set is allowed and gives a harmless zero seminorm.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: The finite seminorm with a bounded time weight

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: The bundled seminorm evaluates to the exact finite mixed-word norm of the weighted slices. Its construction includes a bound on the time weight and requires the indexing times to lie inside the closed slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: The weighted seminorm equals the finite derivative norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: Phase averaging is contractive for the supremum-based finite mixed seminorm with any bounded time-only weight on `A`. Each constant derivative word commutes with averaging, and the norm of its phase integral is bounded by the corresponding supremum. The flag `False` specifies this theorem’s supremum norm; no Hölder contraction is claimed here.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: Phase averaging decreases each weighted finite norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: A pointwise bilinear product is bounded by the product of the factor seminorms when `τfg = τf * τg` on the time set and all three multipliers are bounded. The explicit constant is the admissible-word count times $2^n$ times twice the bilinear-map norm. The result covers both supremum and optional half-Hölder measurements.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: Place a product’s time weight on its two factors

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: For a centered profile, phase-independent coframe and covector, and nonzero covector, the weighted completion norm costs one extra mixed derivative and one inverse positive frequency. The theorem assumes the geometric curl-row and normalized-potential coefficient budgets. Its explicit constant contains admissible-word counts, powers of two, and $K^2$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: The completion gains one inverse frequency

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: Let $\ell_*\ne0$ and suppose every order-$n$ scaled inverse-deformation row is bounded by $L$. Both time multipliers are bounded on a subset of $[0,T]$. The norm of $(Z\cdot\mathbf d)Z^{\prime}$ is bounded by the current-order norm of $Z$, the next-order norm of $Z^{\prime}$, and the scaled inverse deformation bound. This is part of (5.39). The formal estimate allows separate bounded time weights on the two factors, so the amplitude weight can be placed on either one.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: Control a product with one extra label derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: The actual fixed-weight seminorm is monotone in derivative order.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: Weighted seminorms increase with derivative order

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: If `A ⊆ B ⊆ Icc 0 T`, the seminorm on `A` is at most the seminorm on `B` with the same multiplier and derivative order. Boundedness of the multiplier is assumed on the larger set. The comparison restricts available samples and does not compare different weights.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: A smaller time set has no larger weighted norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: Assuming `hh : h ≠ 0`, the order-$n$ norm of fast advection is bounded by two product constants, the unweighted scaled-covector norm, the order-$n$ advector norm, and the weighted order-$(n+1)$ norm of $Y$. The bounded time weight `τ` lives on `A`; only the differentiated profile carries it.

For a centered smooth profile, bounds the weighted finite-word seminorm of its phase primitive by twice that of the profile, at the same spatial and phase order. The time set `A` is any subset of the slab, and `τ` is any weight with the supplied bound `hτ`. The theorem uses the non-Hölder seminorm (`False`); it does not differentiate the weight.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: The normalized primitive costs at most a factor of two

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: The order-$n$ seminorm of one scaled label derivative is bounded by the order-$(n+1)$ seminorm of the original profile, with the same bounded time weight. The statement allows either value of `holder`. Constant directions commute, so the extra derivative belongs to the enlarged finite family without differentiating the time weight.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: A scaled label derivative consumes one order

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: The weighted seminorm through order `n` of one scaled profile derivative is bounded by the original profile's seminorm through order `n+1`. The assertion permits either value of the Hölder flag `holder`, any subset of the time slab, and any bounded time weight. The derivative acts only on label and phase variables, leaving that weight untouched.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: A scaled derivative spends one spatial order

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: Assume $\ell_*\ne0$, smooth profiles, bounded time weights whose product is the output weight, and order-$n$ bounds for the scaled rows of the inverse deformation. The product $(\mathbf d\cdot V)Y$ is bounded using one extra derivative of $V$, the current-order norm of $Y$, and the scaled inverse deformation coefficients. This supplies the other slow product in (5.39). The formal statement also permits Hölder norms and distributes a bounded time weight between the two factors.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: Control the other slow quadratic interaction

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: If every full-slab scaled coframe-row norm is at most `L` and $\ell\ne0$, the weighted order-$n$ divergence norm is bounded by $3Q_nL$ times the weighted order-$(n+1)$ norm of `V`. Here $Q_n$ is the finite product constant. The factor three counts spatial coordinates; the weight stays entirely on `V`.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: The three coframe rows bound slow divergence

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.text: If `R` evaluates to the raw relay of centered profiles `V` and `F`, a common normalized coefficient budget bounds its weighted order-$n$ norm by the explicit order constant times $K^2\,\mathrm{freq}^{-1}$ and their order-$(n+1)$ norms. The weight is only bounded in time; `freq > 0` and $\ell\ne0$ are explicit.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.bound.summary: The linear relay gains one inverse frequency

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.text:
The same periodic curl completion, restricted to the lattice-compatible profiles of the finite hierarchy.

Default-value audit (b5): The constructor requires T>0, phase independence of the covector and its nonvanishing on the slab. The returned twisted profile is built from a proved completion, not a default branch on failed hypotheses.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.summary: The curl correction within the twisted profile space

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.compl.text: For a zero-phase-mean velocity and phase-independent `G` and `κ`, the bundled completion evaluates to the pulled-back curl of its relay potential. Covector nonvanishing is required to form the smooth potential. The result identifies the actual completion profile with the concrete curl expression used in finite-order estimates.
