This is the table needed to turn a mean-profile derivative bound into an order-`m` physical Hölder estimate, which spends one additional spatial derivative. The definition imposes no sign restrictions on the table.

Combines the phase-independent graph cost through order `m+1`, the retained-level count and the cumulative order table into the mean correction’s Hölder prefactor. Unlike the oscillatory case, the graph readout contributes no phase-frequency loss. The parent and frequency powers are specified by the applying estimate, not by this coefficient alone.

Combines the order-`m+1` oscillatory graph cost, the number of retained levels and their common coefficient into the prefactor for the order-`m` Hölder estimate. The factor $3(m+1)$ accounts for passing from derivative bounds to the chosen spatial norm. This definition contains no frequency or parent-scale powers; those appear separately in the theorem.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: Fast advection is the phase derivative times the covector pairing.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: Fast advection is the covector pairing times phase derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: For `hT : 0 < T` and a time in the closed slab, fast advection equals $\langle\kappa,Z\rangle$ times the derivative of the fixed-time slice of $Y$ in direction $(0,1)$. The proof restricts the slab derivative to label and phase variables; it differentiates neither time nor the advecting factor.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: Fast advection differentiates the phase slice

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: Expresses fast advection as a product of the scaled covector applied to the advector and the scaled independent-phase derivative of the target field. The only scale cancellation required is `h ≠ 0`; `ℓ` is arbitrary. The identity exposes the existing reciprocal phase width in the coefficient instead of treating time differentiation as a new frequency loss.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: Fast advection retains the covector and phase derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: If the advected profile is phase independent, its phase derivative vanishes and so does fast advection by any vector profile. This does not require the advecting profile to be transverse.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: A phase-independent input has no fast advection

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: If the advecting profile is perpendicular to the covector at every slab point, its pairing in the fast-advection operator is zero. The advected profile may depend on phase.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: A transverse advecting field has no fast advection

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: Fast phase advection has sign minus the product of the profile signs.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: Fast advection multiplies signs and reverses parity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: For positive slab length, the concrete phase-advection operator preserves every carrier-dependent lattice shift when its inputs lie in the common twisted space. The proof checks that the phase derivative of the second field and the contraction of κ with the first repeat under the same shift. This is a closure result, rather than an evolution or cancellation equation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: Phase advection respects the carrier translation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: Defines the linear phase-derivative operator on a bundled twisted profile using the direction $(0,0,1)$. The time and label coordinates are held fixed. Its argument `hT : 0 < T` supports within-slab differentiation in the bundled smooth-profile construction, while the phase coordinate itself ranges over all real numbers.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: Differentiate a profile in its independent phase

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: At `t ∈ Icc 0 T`, evaluation of `phaseDerivative hT f` equals the ordinary derivative of $s\mapsto f(t,a,s)$. The bundled profile supplies smoothness, and `hT` gives a positive time interval. This identifies the internal directional-derivative construction with the independent phase derivative used in the hierarchy formulas.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: The profile phase operator is the ordinary phase derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: For a smooth function `hf` and any constant direction `d` in label–phase space, differentiating its averaged phase translates equals averaging that directional derivative. The proof differentiates under the interval integral and then commutes evaluation of a continuous linear map with integration. The direction may include both label and phase components.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: A constant derivative commutes with phase averaging

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: For a twisted pressure profile independent of phase on the slab, the fast gradient in `twistedHierarchyOperators` is zero. The proof lifts the periodic-space result through the twisted wrapper. It requires actual phase independence of the pressure and does not infer that property merely from lattice compatibility.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: A twisted mean pressure has no fast gradient

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: Evaluate the abstract fast pressure-gradient operator as the phase derivative of the scalar profile times the wave vector. This is the concrete phase part of the hierarchy gradient.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: The phase pressure gradient on a twisted profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: The fast pressure gradient reverses the reflection sign with an even transported wave vector.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: The fast pressure gradient reverses parity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: For positive slab length, the concrete phase gradient preserves every carrier-dependent lattice shift when its inputs lie in the common twisted space. The proof checks that the phase derivative of the pressure and the covector κ repeat under the same shift. This is a closure result, rather than an evolution or cancellation equation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: The fast gradient respects the carrier translation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: Assume a smooth everywhere nonzero covector and positive carrier frequency. Jet bounds for the normalized covector and the reciprocal squared norm yield a jet bound for the pressure-source coefficient, with product factor $2^N$. The theorem also proves smoothness. Nonvanishing is required for the reciprocal coefficient, rather than supplied by the bound itself.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: Bound the normalized pressure source coefficient

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: A smooth comparison profile `f` agreeing with a twisted profile on the entire centered cell transfers its scaled jet bound to that profile everywhere. The time lies in $[0,T]$, and both label and phase scales are nonzero. Twisted lattice translations transport derivatives to the cell; unique differentiability handles points on its boundary.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: Cellwise agreement transfers the scaled derivative estimate

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: If `profilePhaseAverage hT v = 0`, then the scalar phase mean of every slab-time and label slice of `v` vanishes. The proof evaluates the bundled equality at phase zero and unfolds the averaging operator. Although the docstring says “exactly when,” this declaration proves only this implication; its use here needs no converse.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: A zero profile average gives zero instantaneous phase means

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: Subtracting the twisted profile’s phase average makes every phase slice have zero mean at every time in the slab. Idempotence of the underlying periodic averaging operator supplies the equality. The lattice twist remains in the surrounding profile type; the assertion itself is a fixed-label integral identity.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: A centered twisted profile has zero phase average

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: For a twisted profile whose operator average is zero, the unit-period integral of its values vanishes at each label and each time in the positive slab. The coefficient fields `G`, `M` and `κ` parameterize the operators but do not change this integral. The conclusion translates the algebraic average into the analytic phase mean.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: The abstract zero average is the actual phase integral

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: Assume every label slice of the fixed-time profile has zero phase mean. The mean of the operator-valued label derivative then vanishes. Smoothness and completeness justify differentiation of the phase integral. This is stronger than checking a single label direction and supports cancellation after applying phase-independent matrices.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: The label derivative of an oscillation averages to zero

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: For a unit-periodic vector function, replacing the phase by its negative leaves the phase mean unchanged. Reversing the integration interval and then shifting it by one period gives the same integral. The result supports propagation of joint label-phase reflection symmetry through the averaging operator.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: A complete phase average is invariant under reversal

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: If `hmean` says the profile has zero phase average at every time and label, then every bundled time derivative has the same zero average. The complete target space and `0 < T` permit differentiation of the integral. Induction compares that derivative with the derivative of the identically zero curve, including at both ends of the interval.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: All time derivatives preserve zero phase mean

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: If the phase mean vanishes at every time and label on a positive closed slab, the mean of the within-slab time derivative also vanishes there. The proof differentiates the parameter integral using the profile regularity. Positive slab length supplies the unique within-derivative behavior at both temporal endpoints.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: Time differentiation preserves a vanishing phase average

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: For a unit-periodic vector function, translating the phase argument by any real `b` leaves its phase mean unchanged. The proof translates the interval integral and uses equality of integrals over intervals of length one. This is the step that removes carrier-induced phase offsets from averaged profiles.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: A complete phase average ignores the starting phase

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: Any finite word in constant directions commutes with averaging phase translates of a smooth function. The proof inducts over the word and applies the single-derivative identity to the already differentiated smooth field. There is no sorting or derivative-order bound in this identity; those restrictions arise only when constructing a finite norm.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: Every constant derivative word commutes with averaging

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: For a transverse velocity satisfying the bundled momentum equation on all of $[0,T]$, the pressure equals `oscillatoryPhasePressure` whenever its phase mean is zero. The proof specializes the active-interval result to time zero. The evolution and nonvanishing of the covector are necessary premises, not consequences of the momentum identity alone.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: The full-slab pressure is the normalized primitive

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: On a nondegenerate active interval, covector evolution and $\kappa\cdot V=0$ imply the pressure-slope formula from the momentum equation. The zero phase mean then identifies `p` with its normalized phase primitive. Nonvanishing `κ` justifies division by its squared norm; `hstart` permits unique within-interval differentiation at the endpoints.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: Transversality determines the zero-mean pressure

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: Constructs a smooth twisted profile from the normalized phase primitive of `f`, given `hT : 0 < T` and `hf : PhaseMeanZero f`. The construction proves periodicity using the zero phase mean and proves the original lattice twist using translation of the normalized primitive. It preserves the same time slab and carrier vector; it does not choose an arbitrary antiderivative.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: The centered profile has a normalized periodic primitive

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: Evaluating `phasePrimitiveProfile` at a slab time, label, and phase gives the scalar-phase primitive of the corresponding slice of `f`. Both `hT` and the zero-mean proof are retained from the constructor. This exact value formula is restricted to `t ∈ Icc 0 T`; it does not identify any auxiliary off-slab extension chosen by the bundle.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: Read the periodic primitive at a point on the slab

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.text: Shows that integrating a smooth twisted profile in the phase variable and subtracting the primitive's phase mean preserves joint smoothness in time, label, and phase on the slab. The only additional parameter is `hT : 0 < T`. This helper concerns smoothness, while periodicity and lattice-twist compatibility are proved separately for the bundled primitive.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.phase.summary: The phase primitive remains jointly smooth

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.physi.text: For a retained level at least two, the concrete hierarchy with inactive leading data satisfies the measured transverse-solve inequality. The hypotheses supply weighted forward stability, coefficient-word bounds and a numerical majorant for `transverseSolveNormConstant`. Support propagation supplies the corresponding inactivity of the actual source. Thus the estimate applies to the selected construction rather than an unrelated solution.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.physi.summary: The selected hierarchy inherits the transverse solve bound

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.physi.text: Instantiates the abstract support theorem with the physical mean, transverse and curl solvers. The coefficient records supply the necessary phase independence, nonvanishing and support-preservation properties. Positive activation extends vanishing to the launch slice; depth at least one and `0 < T ≤ 1` remain required. The tail consists of slow mean products on that region.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.physi.summary: The physical solvers preserve support through positive activation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.physi.text: Assume $0<T\le1$, depth $P\ge1$, a closed support set, valid mean and transverse solution operators, and leading velocity, pressure and activation error vanishing on the indicated region. Before activation or outside the envelope, all transverse velocities, curl corrections, oscillatory pressures, and transverse sources vanish. There the remainder equals a sum of products $(B_i\cdot\mathbf d)B_j$. This proves the final support assertion of Proposition 5.4. The means may persist on that region because the endpoint problem selects their initial values globally in time.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.physi.summary: Only interactions between means remain outside the wave

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.physi.text: Combines the selected endpoint mean, the selected zero-start transverse solve and the concrete curl completion into `FiniteHierarchySolvers`. The coefficients provide phase independence and nonvanishing needed for averaging and completion identities. This creates the operators used by the ordered recursion; it does not itself choose a depth or build a finished perturbation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.physi.summary: The finite expansion uses actual mean and transverse solves

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.physi.text: For a zero-mean forcing and a positive slab of duration at most one, the output of the physical transverse solver is the output of a `TransverseResult`. The proof names the concrete selected result. This compatibility witness is needed because higher-pressure estimates use the pressure-slope identity carried by that result, not only an abstract output record.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.physi.summary: The physical solver returns its actual transverse solution

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.point.text: This bundles pointwise application of a continuous bilinear map `B` as a bilinear map between twisted profile spaces. It first maps the first profile into a profile of linear maps, then uses `applyField` on the second profile. Smoothness and the twist law follow from the existing profile operations; no estimate or inverse equation is supplied.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.point.summary: Apply a fixed bilinear map to two profiles

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.point.text: At any point in the profile slab, the bundled `pointwiseBilinear B f g` has value `B (f x) (g x)`. The statement only unwraps the profile construction. This evaluation identity is used to match a general continuous bilinear map to the concrete products and spatial norm estimates appearing in the hierarchy.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.primi.text: For a continuous one-periodic function `f` with zero phase mean, translating its argument by `b` commutes with taking the normalized phase primitive. The zero-mean assumption makes the primitive periodic and fixes the otherwise possible additive constant. This identity is used to preserve the lattice twist when a primitive is bundled as a profile.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.primi.summary: The normalized primitive respects phase translation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.produ.text: If the fixed bilinear map `B` has operator norm at most one, its time-product cost is bounded by the common quadratic constant at order `n`. Both constants count the same admissible derivative words. This comparison removes map-specific constants for scalar multiplication and row evaluation in the auxiliary advection estimates.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.produ.summary: Unit norm bilinear maps share the quadratic constant

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.profi.text:
The concrete phase average closes the twisted space.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.profi.summary: Phase averaging within the twisted profile space

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.profi.text: The underlying periodic profile of the phase average in the twisted space equals the periodic phase average of the underlying input. This definitional equality keeps the actual integral formula available. The extra lattice compatibility is proved using translation invariance of a full-period phase integral.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.profi.summary: Read the same phase mean after adding the twist

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.profi.text: If a smooth profile agrees on the slab with a phase-independent field having a stated label-reflection sign, the stored profile has simultaneous reflection parity everywhere. On the slab this uses the value identity; off the slab both representative values are zero. The theorem does not claim a smooth time extension across the slab boundary.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.profi.summary: Slab parity extends to the stored zero representative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.profi.text: The concrete twisted completion gives the solenoidal input required by `construct_divergence_eq_zero`. The transverse-output equation alone supplies pointwise transversality via the skew-periodic probe.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.profi.summary: The completed transverse output has zero profile divergence

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.profi.text: This is the full-slab version of the potential-time identity, taking activation time zero. The hypotheses require the nonvanishing covector, its adjoint evolution, and the velocity’s momentum equation at every time in $[0,T]$. The result is a within-slab derivative at any chosen time, including either endpoint.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.profi.summary: The potential-time formula on the whole slab

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.profi.text: On $[t₀,T]$, a velocity satisfying the supplied transverse momentum equation has potential-time derivative given by `relayPotentialTimeProfile`. The covector must be nonzero and solve its adjoint evolution on the full slab. The pressure term disappears because its cross product with the covector vanishes. This theorem states a within-interval derivative, not an extension beyond the endpoints.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.profi.summary: The transverse equation differentiates the potential on the active interval

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.profi.text: Fixes a label `a` in a smooth twisted profile and obtains joint continuity in time and independent phase on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R$. This follows by composing the bundled smooth function with the coordinate inclusion. It supplies the continuity hypothesis for differentiating a phase integral; no derivative interchange is asserted yet.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.profi.summary: A fixed label leaves a continuous time and phase slice

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.profi.text: For `T > 0`, identifies the derivative of the time slice at a fixed label and phase with the evaluated bundled `timeDerivative`. The time lies in the closed slab, so the conclusion is `HasDerivWithinAt`, including its endpoints. Smoothness comes from the profile bundle and gives an actual derivative witness, not only a totalized derivative expression.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.profi.summary: A fixed label and phase give the genuine time derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.quadr.text: Proves nonnegativity of the finite-word product constant for four label and phase directions at every spatial order. It unfolds the cardinality and positive numerical factors. This private sign lemma permits later inequalities to be multiplied by the common quadratic constant without changing their direction.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.quadr.summary: The common quadratic product constant is nonnegative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ratio.text: A constant rescaling of the amplitude weight preserves forward stability.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.ratio.summary: Constant amplitude rescaling preserves forward stability

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.rawMe.text: For the actual `MeanResult`, the unweighted profile norm of its $q$th time derivative is at most the finite label norm of the $q$th Eulerian time derivative of `rawMean`. The selected output is either that raw mean or its odd part. Phase independence removes phase words, and parity projection does not increase the label norm.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.rawMe.summary: The selected mean inherits each raw time derivative bound

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.refle.text:
Reflection is an actual linear self-map on the twisted profile space.

Default-value audit (b5): The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.

A reflection identity verified on `hierarchyProfileSlab T` gives `HierarchyProfileReflectionParity` on the whole profile domain. The proof splits on membership in the slab. Outside it, both reflected and original profile values are zero by the smooth-profile representation, because reflection changes label and phase but preserves time.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.refle.summary: Reflection extends from the slab to the profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.refle.text: Defines the real submodule of twisted profiles satisfying a specified sign under simultaneous label and phase reflection. Sign minus one describes odd velocity profiles, while sign one describes even pressures. The definition accepts any real sign, but the concrete Euler parity arguments use only these two values.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.refle.summary: Profiles with a fixed simultaneous reflection sign

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.refle.text: The equation reflection f = sign • f is equivalent to the pointwise reflection-parity predicate. The scalar sign is arbitrary here; odd and even applications use −1 and 1 respectively.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.refle.summary: Operator equality characterizes the reflection sign

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.refle.text: Evaluation of the reflection operator equals evaluation of the original profile at the point with label and phase negated. This is the value identity used in parity calculations.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.refle.summary: Reflected profiles evaluate at the reflected point

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.refle.text: The linear reflection map is an involution on twisted profiles. This is an algebraic property of the simultaneous label and phase reversal.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.refle.summary: Reflecting twice recovers the original profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.relay.text: An existing `HierarchyRelayCoefficientJets` proof with bound `A` remains valid with any `B ≥ A`. Smoothness is unchanged, and both the allowance’s nonnegativity and each word estimate are enlarged by the same inequality. This lemma combines separately obtained potential and geometric bounds into one shared budget.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.relay.summary: A larger coefficient allowance preserves every derivative bound

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.relay.text: If `f` is differentiable at `(a,s)`, its relay label jet is exactly the derivative of $b\mapsto f(b,s)$ at `a`. The proof decomposes the derivative on the product space into its label and phase parts. It translates between the mixed-coordinate potential and the ordinary derivative used in a pulled-back curl.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.relay.summary: The label jet is the fixed-phase derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.relay.text: Constructs the normalized phase primitive of `applyField c f`, given a centered input `f` and a phase-independent coefficient `c`. The coefficient may vary in time and label. Its phase independence preserves the input's zero mean, so the output is again a smooth twisted profile on the same positive-length slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.relay.summary: Apply a coefficient before taking the normalized phase primitive

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.relay.text: At any slab time and label, evaluates the bundled relay primitive as the normalized primitive of the coefficient at phase zero applied to the phase slice of `f`. The hypothesis `hc` makes that zero-phase coefficient equal to the coefficient at every phase. This is a value identity, with the centered input and positive slab required by the constructor.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.relay.summary: Read the relay primitive using the coefficient at phase zero

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.relay.text: Forms a relay term by first applying the phase-independent coefficient `c` to a centered profile, taking its normalized phase primitive, differentiating in one scaled label direction, and applying `row`. The row is a smooth operator-valued profile and need not itself be phase-independent here. The result retains the same slab and lattice twist.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.relay.summary: One coefficient row after a differentiated phase primitive

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.relay.text: Evaluates the relay term as the row applied to a scaled label derivative of the normalized primitive, with the inner coefficient read at phase zero. The identity holds at every time on the slab and every label-phase point. It exposes exactly which derivative acts on the primitive and its inner coefficient, before time or spatial norm estimates are applied.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.relay.summary: Read one relay term as a weighted coordinate derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.remai.text: Assumes the finite remainder and completion-switch term are odd and uses the leading momentum equation to identify the leading switch term. Even material and covector coefficients turn the odd leading velocity and even pressure into another odd term. Adding them preserves reflection parity of the complete profile residual.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.remai.summary: The switch error preserves the odd residual

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.restr.text: A linear operation on periodic profiles restricts to twisted profiles when `hL` proves that every twisted input produces all required lattice translation identities. The operation’s underlying values do not change. This separates a concrete operator formula from the extra proof that it respects the carrier geometry.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.restr.summary: Restrict an operator to the carrier-compatible space

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.restr.text: This restricts a bilinear map on periodic profiles to inputs and outputs with the same carrier-dependent lattice symmetry. The proof `hL` establishes closure jointly for both arguments. Linearity in each argument is retained, allowing concrete advection and pointwise operator multiplication in the twisted hierarchy.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.restr.summary: Preserve the common twist in a bilinear operation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.restr.text: The underlying periodic profile of the restricted bilinear output is `L f.val g.val`. This is a definitional equality, confirming that both arguments and the result are merely being regarded in a smaller certified space. It transfers concrete bilinear evaluation formulas without additional analytic assumptions.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.restr.summary: Read the bilinear operation before the twisted wrapper

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.restr.text: The underlying periodic output of a restricted linear map is exactly `L` applied to the underlying periodic input. This definitional identity removes the twisted wrapper in computations. The accompanying closure proof changes the certified function space but does not change any value of the operation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.restr.summary: The carrier restriction leaves the linear operation unchanged

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.restr.text: Restricting a full-slab norm to $[t₀,T]$ with weight one cannot increase it, provided `ht₀ : 0 ≤ t₀`. The assertion works with either Hölder flag. Its role is to replace unweighted factors on the active interval by quantities already measured on the whole parent slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.restr.summary: The active interval has a smaller unweighted norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.rowAp.text: Bounds the bilinear operator that evaluates a continuous linear functional on a vector by one in operator norm. The statement is purely about `Vec3` and its continuous linear dual. It supplies the map norm hypothesis used to give row evaluation the common quadratic product constant.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.rowAp.summary: Applying a row has bilinear norm at most one

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.text: This definition turns the $i$th row of the inverse coframe `G` into a scalar-valued linear-map profile and multiplies it by $\ell^{-1}$. Pairing it with an $\ell$-scaled label derivative recovers an unscaled physical derivative. The definition preserves the twisted-profile structure through a fixed continuous linear map.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.summary: An inverse-coframe row divided by the label width

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.text: At a point `hx` in the closed time slab, the bundled coefficient applied to a vector `v` is $\ell^{-1}(Gv)_i$. Unfolding the fixed linear map proves the identity. Neither invertibility of `G` nor nonzero $\ell$ is needed for this evaluation formula; those conditions belong to later estimates.

An exact phase-independent profile representation of a smooth coframe field transfers its mixed bound to each scaled coframe row. The output factorial time norm at spatial order `n` is at most the label-time conversion cost times `ell⁻¹*A`. The hypotheses include $0<T\le1$, nonnegative scales and costs, and `ell * D^p ≤ 1`; no derivative order is spent on a time derivative.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.summary: A scaled coframe row costs one inverse label width

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.text: The fixed-time derivative of `V` is evaluated in the $i$th label direction scaled by $\ell$, giving another twisted profile. The phase-width parameter `h` is present in the common mixed-direction notation, but this coordinate uses the label branch. `hT : 0 < T` supports the slab derivative construction.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.summary: One label derivative with its width included

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.text: For `ht : t ∈ Icc 0 T`, the value of the scaled derivative profile is the directional derivative of $V(t,\cdot)$ in the corresponding mixed label direction. The theorem unfolds the profile derivative and fixed evaluation map. It justifies applying ordinary fixed-time product estimates to the bundled hierarchy operation.

Identifies the earlier `scaledLabelDerivativeProfile` with the corresponding `scaledProfileDerivative` direction. The statement assumes only a positive slab length and fixed real scales. The proof evaluates both definitions on the slab. This compatibility allows the earlier slow-divergence identity to reuse the new time-commuting directional operator.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.summary: Two label derivative constructions agree as profiles

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.text: Assume derivatives through order `n` are bounded by $C D^{pj+q}$, with nonnegative `C`, `D ≥ 1`, and $\ell D^p\le1$. The label-rescaled function then has a jet bound $CD^q$ at all those orders. The estimate separates the derivative-dependent power, removed by scaling, from the fixed parent loss.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.summary: A small label scale absorbs derivative-dependent parent powers

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.text: This profile sends a vector to its inner product with $\kappa/h$. The map is applied to the bundled smooth twisted profile, so its periodicity and slab interpretation are retained. It isolates the coefficient measured separately from the advector and differentiated profile in the fast-advection estimate.

At a time `ht` in $[0,T]$, evaluation of the bundled scaled coefficient is exactly $h^{-1}\langle\kappa(t,a,s),\cdot\rangle$. The equality unfolds the successive smooth and periodic profile wrappers. It imposes no nonzero-width assumption, so it remains an evaluation identity when $h=0$.

From raw mixed bounds for `freq⁻¹ • f`, bounds the time norm of the scaled phase coefficient $h^{-1}\langle\kappa,\cdot\rangle$. It assumes `freq > 0`, `h = freq^(-1/2)`, `0 < T ≤ 1`, and `ℓ D^p ≤ 1`, together with the coefficient value identity and sign conditions. Restoring the carrier and phase inverse lengths contributes exactly $\mathrm{freq}^{3/2}$; the remaining constant is the same label time-seminorm cost.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.summary: The fast coefficient retains its explicit frequency loss

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.text: For a phase-independent twisted profile, the unweighted seminorm at any phase scale controls the scaled jets of its phase-zero label field with phase scale one. The equality follows because changing the phase has no effect on values. The time must lie in a positive-length slab; no extra carrier-frequency factor is introduced.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.summary: A mean profile uses unit phase scale without changing its budget

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.text: At any time in a positive-length slab, the actual unweighted mixed-word seminorm bounds scaled slice jets with factor $4^n$. No separate bounded-supremum hypothesis is needed: smoothness, twisted periodicity, and the compact time slab provide it. The `False` argument selects the finite supremum norm without Hölder quotients.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.summary: The actual unweighted seminorm controls every scaled slice jet

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.text: On an active interval $[t_0,T]$ inside the slab, a continuous strictly positive amplitude weight gives slice jets bounded by $\gamma(t)4^n$ times the amplitude seminorm. Compactness bounds the reciprocal weight, ensuring the real suprema are meaningful. Only label and phase derivatives are taken, so no time derivatives of the weight enter.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.summary: The actual amplitude seminorm recovers the weight on each slice

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.text: Selects one of four constant directions in the profile variables: three label directions scaled by `ell`, or the independent phase direction scaled by `h`. The time component is zero. With `hT : 0 < T`, this is a linear operator on smooth twisted profiles, preserving their slab and lattice twist. It is not a time derivative or a derivative along the flow.

Evaluating the bundled scaled derivative at `t` gives the ordinary directional derivative of the label-phase slice along `hierarchyMixedDirection ell h i`. The time belongs to the slab and `T > 0`. This identifies a within-slab derivative of the full profile with an unrestricted spatial derivative of its smooth fixed-time slice.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.summary: Read a scaled derivative on a fixed time slice

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.text: For a coordinate `i : Fin 3`, evaluating the corresponding scaled profile derivative gives `ℓ` times the spatial label derivative in that coordinate direction. The phase and time are held fixed, and the time lies on a nondegenerate slab. This exact identity exposes the factor that cancels the reciprocal radius in a scaled coframe row.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.summary: The label derivative carries its radius scale

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.text: At an active time with positive continuous weight and `γ t ≤ 1`, the scaled fixed-time profile has an order-`n` jet bound given by $4^n$ times its amplitude seminorm. This converts the hierarchy derivative-word norm into ordinary Fréchet derivative bounds. The weight cap is required to pass from the weighted estimate to the unweighted slice.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.scale.summary: Convert the weighted profile norm into a slice jet bound

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.selec.text: For $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge1$ and $\ell_*>0$, consider the selected mean $B=D_aXv$ with a phase-independent source. Assume its endpoint inverse estimates, spatial coefficient bounds through order $n$, and half-Hölder bounds for time derivatives of $K,\Omega,D_aX$ through order $q$. The source and $(D_aX)^T$ are needed only through order $\max(q-1,0)$. The formal statement bounds the unweighted $\mathcal J_q(B)$ by an explicit nonnegative expression in those bounds, $\mathsf D$, the inverse exponent, $n$ and $q$, linear in the source bound. Thus, for $q\ge1$, the source is differentiated once less than the mean. At $q=0$ the source order is zero, not minus one. Some endpoint-inverse data and the spatial seminorm are defined in omitted files, so their exact hypotheses cannot all be recovered from this packet.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.selec.summary: The selected mean gains one source derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.selec.text: If `T ≤ 1` and every raw mean time derivative through order $q$ has the same nonnegative label-norm bound $C$, the factorially weighted time norm of the hierarchy’s selected mean is at most $(q+1)C$. The label scale is nonnegative. Each weight $T^i/i!$ is at most one, and the preceding selection estimate controls each term.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.selec.summary: Raw mean bounds control its factorial time norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slice.text: This function reads the actual values of a twisted hierarchy profile at time `t`, retaining label and phase as free arguments. It only removes subtype wrappers and fixes time. Smoothness of the resulting slice is proved when `t` belongs to the slab; outside it the underlying profile convention gives zero values.

If the uncurried field is smooth on `[0,T] × Vec3`, then its slice at any $t \in  [0,T]$ is smooth on all of `Vec3`. The proof composes with the smooth inclusion $x \mapsto  (t,x)$. No smoothness outside the time slab is inferred from this restriction argument.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowA.text: For arbitrary smooth twisted coefficients and profiles, the abstract label-advection operator equals the sum of its three coordinate contributions. The proof expands the label vector `G z` in the Euclidean basis and uses linearity of the slice derivative. The identity uses `hT > 0` to identify slab and fixed-time derivatives.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowA.summary: Summing coordinate contributions gives slow advection

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowA.text: This helper multiplies the $i$th component of `G z` by the $i$th label derivative of `g`. Both operations are built from bundled continuous linear maps and `applyField`. Summing the three coordinates recovers label advection; the definition itself makes no claim about a numerical bound or amplitude weight.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowA.summary: A single coordinate contribution to slow advection

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowA.text: At a slab time, the helper is $(Gz)_i$ times the derivative of the fixed-time slice of `g` in direction $(e_i,0)$. The statement unfolds the bundled derivative and application operations. It fixes exactly which profile is differentiated, preventing the coefficient or advector from being mistaken for the derivative’s target.

For nonzero label width, one coordinate of slow advection has its order-$n$ weighted norm bounded by two product constants, the scaled-row norm, the order-$n$ norm of the advector, and the order-$(n+1)$ norm of the differentiated profile. Separate bounded time weights `r` and `q` multiply to the output weight.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowC.text: A common upper bound `L` for the three scaled-row seminorms must be nonnegative, because any one of those seminorms is nonnegative. Hence $3Q_n^2L$ is nonnegative. This elementary fact legitimizes multiplying inequalities by the slow-interaction cost; it derives the sign from `hG` instead of assuming it separately.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowL.text: This definition forms the slow divergence of `V` using the coframe `G`, then equips it with phase periodicity and lattice-twisted periodicity. The derivative acts in label variables only. The construction preserves the actual divergence values on the slab and is used inside the averaged completion source.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowL.summary: The label divergence as a twisted scalar profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowL.text:
The slow divergence times a second vector profile in the averaged completion source.

Default-value audit (b5): The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowL.summary: Slow divergence multiplied by a second vector profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowL.text: The bundled product evaluates to the slow label divergence of V multiplied by Y. It is the term obtained when phase integration by parts removes a fast derivative from the averaged source.

Rewrites the slow divergence product of `V` and `Y` as the scalar sum of three coframe rows applied to scaled label derivatives of `V`, multiplied by `Y`. The radius `ℓ` must be nonzero to undo the scaling. The identity makes explicit that the additional label derivative falls on the first input rather than on the second.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowL.summary: Slow divergence differentiates the first factor

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowL.text: The product of the slow divergence of the zero profile with any second profile is zero. The conclusion is equality of twisted vector profiles, so all representation layers are included. It removes the artificial zero level when reindexing the completion contribution in the hierarchy average.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowL.summary: A zero first profile contributes no divergence product

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowL.text: At a slab point, slow label divergence is the sum of the three coordinate components of the derivative of `V`, evaluated along `G` applied to each standard basis vector. This is the coordinate contraction representing the divergence in label coordinates. The theorem identifies values; no bound on the coframe is assumed.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowL.summary: Evaluate divergence in the three coframe directions

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowL.text: The equivalent trace contraction by rows puts the label derivative in a fixed coordinate direction before applying the coframe.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowL.summary: Slow divergence written as coordinate row contractions

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowL.text: When `hℓ : ℓ ≠ 0`, slow label divergence equals the sum of the three scaled coframe rows applied to the corresponding scaled label derivatives. Each factor of $\ell$ cancels its inverse. The proof rewrites the trace coordinate by coordinate and uses the derivative of the fixed-time label–phase slice.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowL.summary: Slow divergence is a sum of three contractions

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowL.text: The underlying smooth profile of `slowLabelDivergence hT G V` is exactly the concrete `slowDiv` construction. The theorem is a definitional equality after forgetting the two periodicity wrappers. It lets derivative and averaging lemmas use the actual divergence rather than reason through the extra subtype fields.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.slowL.summary: Forgetting periodic structure recovers the slow divergence

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.smoot.text: A smooth spatial slice of the label map `A` turns a twisted profile into a smooth Eulerian graph readout at a time in $[0,T]$. Time membership is explicit because the profile’s regularity is bundled only on that slab. The conclusion is spatial smoothness at the chosen time, not a new jointly smooth flow.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.solve.text: Chooses one inhabitant of `MeanResult` supplied by `exists_meanResult`, for the same coefficients and mean source. The return type includes the endpoint, normalization, recovery and conditional symmetry certificates. Subsequent estimates refer to this exact selected result, rather than to another mean solution that happens to satisfy the equation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.solve.summary: Select a certified physical endpoint mean

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.solve.text: Assume smooth phase-independent strain and nonzero covector with $\kappa_t=-M^T\kappa$, and smooth source profiles on $[0,T]$ compatible with phase and label translations. This is the solution of (5.15) used at each level of the expansion: its velocity starts from zero and its pressure has zero phase mean. It is selected from the proved existence result for a smooth source with zero phase mean. Its equations and support properties therefore accompany the selected fields.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.solve.summary: Each forcing is assigned its transverse solution

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.spati.text: For a phase-independent profile, smooth inverse-label map and controlled coframe jets through order two, its physical graph has first-order half-Hölder norm at most $13824Q^2$ times the second-order unweighted profile seminorm. The scale condition `ell⁻¹ * C ≤ Q` accounts for physical derivatives. No carrier-frequency loss appears because the profile has no phase dependence.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.spati.summary: Convert a label mean bound into a physical Hölder bound

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.spati.text: For a jointly smooth periodic parent with label flow, every fixed-position time jet of a twisted profile evaluated on the inverse-flow graph is spatially periodic on the closed slab. The proof first uses the twisted periodicity law to obtain periodicity of the graph and then differentiates equal time slices. It does not require separate periodicity assumptions on each jet.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.spati.summary: Eulerian time derivatives of the graph stay periodic

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.spati.text: If the label map commutes with integer translations by the same translation, evaluating a twisted profile on its phase graph gives a spatially periodic field. The statement uses the twist relation to cancel the phase shift.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.spati.summary: Twisted periodicity gives periodic graph values

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.spati.text: Actual inverse parent labels supply the affine lattice shift.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.spati.summary: Inverse parent labels give the required lattice shift

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.spati.text: At a slab time `t`, evaluating a twisted coefficient at independent phase zero gives a spatially periodic label field, provided the profile is phase independent. The twist shifts phase under a lattice translation; phase independence removes that shift. The result concerns this fixed-time slice and supplies no derivative estimate.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.spati.summary: A phase-independent twisted coefficient is spatially periodic

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.sum_c.text: Expresses any vector in `Vec3` as the sum of its three coordinates times the corresponding coordinate direction. This finite-dimensional identity has no time, scale, or regularity assumptions. It is used to expand the coframe-transformed advector into the three slow label derivatives in the auxiliary source calculation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.sum_c.summary: Recover a vector from its three coordinate directions

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.text: The cost multiplies the number of admissible derivative words by $2^n$ and twice the operator norm of continuous linear evaluation. It depends on spatial order `n` and the source and target spaces. This explicit constant is carried unchanged into the factorial time product estimate; it is not a uniform bound over all spatial orders.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.summary: The spatial cost of coefficient application

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.text: For every natural spatial order and any normed source and target spaces, `terminalApplyFieldCost` is nonnegative. The proof uses the sign of its finite cardinality, power of two, and operator norm. This is the sign needed when replacing coefficient norms by larger bounds in the transverse time recurrence.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.summary: The coefficient application cost is nonnegative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.text: For any continuous bilinear map `B`, combining two jointly smooth coefficient fields on the same set yields another jointly smooth field there. The set need not be a nondegenerate slab, since this statement only preserves already supplied regularity. The helper proves smoothness before mixed derivative estimates are applied to coefficient products.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.summary: Bilinear combinations of smooth coefficients stay smooth

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.text: Let $\lambda>0$, let $K$ and $P$ be nonnegative integers with $P=6K$, and put $\lambda_+=\lambda^K$. The formal statement rewrites the expansion's remainder factor as $\lambda^{-5/4}\lambda_+^{-4}$; its exponent before rewriting is $-5/4-2P/3$. This is precisely the arithmetic used in auxiliary equation (2.5) to obtain the next-frequency decay. No bound for a residual or profile is assumed or proved here. Such an analytic bound must already contain the stated remainder factor. All fractional and negative exponents in this identity are real powers of positive numbers.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.summary: The chosen depth yields the next-frequency power

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.text: If the parent derivative cap satisfies $D\le C\mu^A$, with $\mu\ge1$, nonnegative $C,D$, and $i\le q$, the conversion factor $(1+2^{N+q}D)^i$ is at most $(1+2^{N+q}C)^q\mu^{Aq}$. This scalar inequality makes its parent-frequency exponent independent of spatial order $N$, although the finite coefficient still depends on $N$ and $q$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.summary: Eulerian time conversion costs a fixed parent power

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.text: Defines the product constant as the number of admissible derivative words through order `n`, times $2^n$ and $2\|B\|$. The bilinear map `B` is fixed. No time order occurs in the formula because factorial time weights absorb the time-binomial convolution in the product estimate that follows.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.summary: The spatial product constant in the time norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.text: A constant coefficient field has `TerminalMixedJetBound` with amplitude one and cost sequence constantly equal to its norm, whenever `D ≥ 1`. Every positive-order derivative vanishes, so the only nonzero case is time and spatial order zero. This includes the identity coefficient in the transverse projection without assuming a positive time duration in the statement.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.summary: Constant coefficients satisfy the mixed derivative bound

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.text: Packages value evaluation at a fixed profile point `x` as a linear map from vector profiles to `Vec3`. Addition and scalar multiplication are pointwise, so their preservation is definitional. This private map lets the source proof move evaluation through finite sums when reconstructing advection from its three coordinate terms.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.summary: Evaluate a vector profile as a linear map

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.text: Given the profile equation `heq` and coefficient time norms at most nonnegative `C`, the velocity time norm through `q` is bounded by $(1+T K_n C)^q$ times the sum of its undifferentiated weighted norm and the source time norm. The undifferentiated velocity norm remains an input. Thus this theorem extends a base estimate; it does not prove the inverse estimate from the differential equation alone.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.summary: Inductively control time derivatives of the projected velocity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.text: This continuous bilinear map turns two vectors into a rank-one endomorphism by combining the inner-product functional with scalar multiplication. Its diagonal gives the operator used in the projection along the covector. Bundling it as a bilinear map lets the mixed derivative product theorem estimate that projection without inventing a new calculus rule.

Applying `terminalRankOne` twice to the same vector is exactly `InnerProductSpace.rankOne ℝ v v`. The equality is definitional and holds also at zero. It connects the continuous bilinear representation used in the estimates to the geometric rank-one projection expression used in the transverse amplitude equation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.summary: The diagonal bilinear map is the rank-one operator

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.text: Any real seminorm of a finite sum is at most the sum of the seminorms of its terms. The private helper works in an arbitrary real module and requires no profile or smoothness structure. It is the algebraic triangle inequality used before estimating each binomial term in the time-differentiated product.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.summary: A seminorm bounds a finite sum term by term

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.text: For positive `T`, the next factorial weight is at most `T` times its predecessor. The exact relation includes division by `i + 1`, which can only reduce the nonnegative value. This inequality converts the positive-order terms of a time seminorm into a shorter seminorm of the first time derivative.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.summary: The next time weight costs one slab factor

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.text: Let $\lambda>0$, let $a$ be a nonnegative integer, and assume $\mathsf D^{\max(a,1)+1}\le\lambda^{1/2}$. Then the formal statement proves $\mathsf D^{\max(a,1)+1}\lambda^{3/2}\le\lambda^2$. It is a numerical implication, valid without constructing a profile. In the auxiliary argument, $\lambda^{3/2}$ is the cost of a phase derivative after physical evaluation, and the factor involving $\mathsf D$ comes from the label derivatives. The frequency schedule is needed separately to establish the hypothesis at sufficiently late stages. The declaration gives no estimate for a phase-independent mean or for the derivatives of the parent velocity.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.summary: A parent-scale bound absorbs the phase cost

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.text: With `0 ≤ t₀ ≤ T`, positive `T`, and a positive continuous amplitude `γ` on the active interval, the weighted norm of `A f` is bounded by the spatial application cost times the unweighted coefficient norm and weighted field norm. The reciprocal amplitude belongs only to the operand side. The proof bounds it on the compact active interval before using the product estimate.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.summary: A coefficient acts on an amplitude-weighted profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.text: The factorial time norm of `A f` satisfies the same application estimate as its spatial norm. Coefficient jets use an unweighted norm on the full slab, and field jets retain the reciprocal-amplitude norm on the active interval. Positivity and continuity of `γ` are inherited hypotheses. No time derivative falls on that amplitude weight.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.termi.summary: The weighted coefficient product keeps its spatial cost

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeD.text: For $T>0$ and a smooth profile $f(t,a,s)$ on $0\le t\le T$, the formal object is differentiation in the direction $(1,0,0)$ of the variables $(t,a,s)$. Thus it represents $\partial_t f$ with both the Lagrangian label $a$ and the independent phase $s$ fixed. At the two time endpoints the derivative is taken within the closed interval. It preserves the class of smooth profiles used by the construction. After evaluation along the inverse parent flow this derivative becomes the material derivative $\partial_t+U\cdot\nabla_x$. It is therefore not the derivative at a fixed physical point used in auxiliary Lemmas 1.2 and 1.3.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeD.summary: The label and independent phase remain fixed

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeD.text: For `t ∈ Icc 0 T`, the time derivative of a twisted profile equals the one-variable `derivWithin` of its value with `x : Vec3 × ℝ` fixed. The pair `x` contains the label and independent phase. Positive `T` permits the within chain rule at both endpoints. This derivative becomes a material derivative only after evaluation on the transported phase graph.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeD.summary: Time differentiation fixes label and independent phase

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeD.text: For smooth slab profiles `A` and `f`, the time derivative at fixed label and phase obeys the two-term product rule. Unlike commutation with a fixed linear map, the coefficient profile is differentiated as well. The result is an equality of bundled profiles, derived by specializing directional differentiation to $(1,0,0)$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeD.summary: Differentiate both factors in a time-dependent coefficient product

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: The operator `timeJet hT i` is the `i`th power of the linear time derivative on smooth twisted profiles. Powers mean composition, with the zeroth power equal to the identity. The bundled output keeps the original periodicity and twist laws, allowing subsequent label and phase operations to act on the actual differentiated profile.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Iterate time differentiation while retaining the profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Given $T>0$, a nonnegative integer $q$, and any spatial seminorm $N$ on the smooth profiles, the formal object is $\mathcal J_q(f)=\sum_{i=0}^q T^iN(\partial_t^i f)/i!$. The derivatives hold label and independent phase fixed on $[0,T]$. This is a seminorm: it need not distinguish all nonzero profiles. If $N$ includes division by the positive central amplitude $\gamma$, that division occurs after differentiating $f$; no derivative of $\gamma$ is introduced. The definition supplies the time weights in the auxiliary note, but does not itself specify the spatial norm, its derivative weights, or its domain of suprema; those depend on the chosen $N$.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Time derivatives are measured before being summed

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: In the active amplitude-weighted time norm, subtracting a profile's phase average costs at most twice the original norm. The amplitude is continuous and strictly positive on the active interval, and `T > 0`. The estimate combines the triangle inequality with contraction of phase averaging, which commutes with all the time derivatives.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Centering in phase costs at most a factor of two

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: For a completion `C` that vanishes before activation, and an active weight with $0<\gamma\le1$, bounds the centered fast advection of `Y` by `C` using amplitude norms on both fields. The phase scale must be nonzero. The scaled covector remains unweighted, and the target uses order `n+1`. The factor two comes from centering; inactivity permits replacing the completion's full-slab norm by its amplitude norm.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: The centered fast completion uses two amplitude measurements

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: For positive continuous `γ` on the active interval, places its reciprocal measurement weight on the advector `z`, while the differentiated target `g` uses the full-slab unweighted norm. With nonzero radius and row cap `L`, the slow-advection bound is $3Q_n^2L$ times these norms at orders `n` and `n+1`. No assumption `γ ≤ 1` is needed for this split alone.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Put the amplitude weight on the slow advector

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: For positive continuous `γ`, places the active reciprocal-amplitude weight on the differentiated field `g`; the advector `z` uses the unweighted full-slab norm. It assumes nonzero radius and the scaled coframe row cap. The factor is $3Q_n^2L$, and the extra spatial order is spent on the weighted target. This complements the version with the weight on the advector.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: With a continuous positive amplitude on the active interval, increasing spatial order from `m` to `n ≥ m` can only increase the amplitude-weighted factorial time seminorm. The same `q` time derivatives and the same active interval are used on both sides. The proof is the monotonicity of the underlying spatial seminorm.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: The fast-advection estimate puts the reciprocal-amplitude weight on the target profile at spatial order `n+1`. The advector and scaled covector use unweighted full-slab time norms at order `n`. It assumes a positive continuous active weight and `h ≠ 0`; no inactivity or upper bound on `γ` is used here. These additional hypotheses enter when another factor is replaced by its amplitude norm.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: This unfolds `timeJetSeminorm` into the sum of $T^i/i!$ times the spatial seminorm of the `i`th profile time jet, for $0\le i\le q$. The positive-duration proof is carried by the constructor. Spatial amplitude weights, if present in `N`, are applied after differentiation rather than differentiated together with the profile.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Read the time norm as a finite weighted sum

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Given a spatial estimate for `applyField` with nonnegative constant `C`, the time norm of an operator profile acting on a vector profile is bounded by `C` times their respective time norms. The hypothesis applies to every pair of input profiles. The proof combines the actual binomial application formula with the general factorial convolution inequality.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Apply the time product bound to operator profiles

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Specializes the time product bound to a profile of bounded linear maps `B` applied pointwise to a vector profile `f`. The coefficient is measured without the time weight, and the field carries the bounded weight on `A`. Both are differentiated through time order `q`. The product constant is for operator evaluation, so derivatives of a time-dependent coefficient are included.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: A time dependent coefficient acts with its measured norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Bounds row-profile evaluation in the factorial time norm by the common quadratic constant times the unweighted row norm and weighted vector norm. The time weight is bounded on a subset of the positive-length slab. All time jets through `q` and spatial words through `n` are included; the row's own time derivatives are part of its measured norm.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: A coefficient row acts with one quadratic product cost

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: For the actual averaging operator in `twistedHierarchyOperators`, the factorial time seminorm of the phase average is at most that of the original vector profile. It uses the non-Hölder spatial seminorm, any bounded time weight, and any subset of the slab. The flow coefficient arguments do not enter the averaging action; time derivatives commute with the average.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Phase averaging does not increase the time norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Assume `hJet` supplies a binomial identity for every target jet through `q`, and `hBound` estimates each product term with nonnegative cost `C`. Then the target factorial time norm is at most `C` times the product of the two input time norms. The operation `B` is an arbitrary function here; its needed properties are carried by those explicit hypotheses.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Combine a Leibniz identity with spatial product estimates

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Given nonnegative `C` and a binomial-convolution bound for every target jet through `q`, the target time seminorm is at most `C` times the product of the two input time seminorms. The factorial weights cancel the binomial coefficients, and positivity bounds the remaining triangular convolution by a product. The lemma assumes the jetwise estimate instead of deriving a Leibniz identity.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Lift a jetwise bilinear bound to the time norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: On a set `S ⊆ Icc 0 T`, assume bounded weights satisfy `τfg = τf * τg`. The time norm of the bilinear product is bounded by the original finite-word spatial product cost times the two weighted time norms. Weights are applied to each differentiated slice; no derivative of `τf`, `τg`, or `τfg` is taken or assumed.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Multiply weighted profiles after taking their time jets

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Assumes `hmean` says the mean–mean slow advection is unchanged by phase averaging. It also requires `γ ≤ 1`, inactivity of `u.Y j` before launch, nonzero radius, and the row cap `L`. The centered label product is bounded by $2(3Q_n^2L)$ times two sums of amplitude-measured oscillations and unweighted means, each at spatial order `n+1`. The cancellation is an explicit hypothesis here, supplied from mean independence in the source assembly.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: The centered slow source loses its mean–mean term

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Assumes each of the three scaled coframe rows has time norm at most `L` at order `n`, and that the output weight factors as the two input weights. With `ℓ ≠ 0`, slow advection is bounded by $3Q_n^2L$ times the advector norm at `n` and the target norm at `n+1`. Here $Q_n$ is the finite-word quadratic constant, and every factor uses the same time order `q`.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Slow advection preserves the chosen split of time weights

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Assumes `f` vanishes before `t₀`, while its continuous active weight satisfies $0<\gamma\le1$ on $[t_0,T]$. The full-slab unweighted time seminorm is then bounded by the active-interval seminorm of each derivative divided by `γ`, summed with factorial weights. Inactivity passes to every time jet, and `γ ≤ 1` controls the active portion. The statement does not differentiate `γ`.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: If a smooth raw field agrees with a twisted profile on the centered cell during $[t_0,T]$, bounds for its scaled active time derivatives transfer to the profile’s weighted time norm. The label and phase scales must be nonzero, the active interval must have positive length, and $\gamma$ must be continuous and positive. The final constant is the sum of factorial time weights times the number of admissible words.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: If `h` bounds the target seminorm of each time jet of `g` by `C` times the source seminorm of the corresponding jet of `f`, the same factor `C` bounds the complete time norm through `q`. The hypothesis is jetwise and must be supplied. No linear operator or commutation property is inferred merely from this summation lemma.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Sum a linear estimate over all time orders

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: If `p ≤ q`, the time seminorm through `p` is bounded by the time seminorm through `q` for the same spatial seminorm and profile. The proof includes a shorter finite sum in a longer one. All new terms are nonnegative because `hT` is positive and `N` is a seminorm; no bound on individual derivatives is assumed.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: A pointwise comparison `hNM : N ≤ M` between spatial seminorms carries to their factorial time seminorms at every fixed time order `q`. The proof applies the comparison to each time jet and multiplies by its positive weight. The derivative order and underlying profile remain unchanged, so this is an order comparison of norms rather than a regularity result.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: A larger spatial seminorm gives a larger time norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: With `h ≠ 0`, bounds fast advection using the measured scaled covector, an advector at spatial order `n`, and the differentiated profile at `n+1`. The output time weight splits exactly as `τZ * τY`. The multiplicative constant is $Q_n^2$; the carrier and reciprocal phase-width losses remain in `scaledPhaseCoefficientProfile h κ`, rather than being hidden in this numerical constant.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: For a centered profile in a complete normed space, bounds the factorial time norm of its normalized phase primitive by twice the original norm. Time order `q` and spatial order `n` are unchanged. The weight is any bounded function on a subset of the slab. Commutation of primitive and time jets lets the same spatial inverse estimate apply term by term.
