TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: If a fixed continuous bilinear map satisfies the spatial seminorm bound `h` with nonnegative constant `C` for all pairs of profiles, its factorial time seminorm obeys the same product estimate with the same `C`. The theorem proves the required Leibniz identity for this map and sums it. There is no additional factor depending on time order in the spatial product cost.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Spatial bilinear estimates keep their cost in time norms

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Bounds the time seminorm of `pointwiseBilinear B f g` by the spatial product constant times the unweighted norm of `f` and the weighted norm of `g`. The weight is bounded on `A ⊆ [0,T]`, and the same spatial order and Hölder flag are used throughout. Factorial time weights absorb Leibniz coefficients; derivatives are taken before the weight is applied.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: The factorial time product keeps the spatial constant

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Bounds one relay primitive term in a weighted factorial time norm. The outer row uses the unweighted norm at spatial order `n`; the inner coefficient and input use order `n+1`. The constant is twice the product of their two multiplication constants, reflecting the normalized primitive. The input is centered, the inner coefficient is phase-independent, and the weight is bounded on a subset of the slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: The relay term spends one label order and two coefficient norms

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: The factorial time seminorm measured on any subset `A` of the slab with constant weight one is at most the full-slab unweighted seminorm. The time jets themselves are still defined on the original positive-length slab. This statement restricts the measurement set; it does not replace the within-derivative domain by `A`.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Restricting measured times can only decrease the unweighted norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: For a coefficient row `R`, advector `z`, and target `y`, estimates the product of `R z` with one scaled derivative of `y`. The output weight is the product of the two input weights. The bound has the square of the quadratic constant, the unweighted row norm at order `n`, the advector at `n`, and the target at `n+1`. The time order remains `q`.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: One advection term costs two products and one derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: After summing time jets through `q` with factorial weights, one scaled spatial derivative still costs exactly one extra spatial order. The same bounded weight and time subset occur on both sides, and the Hölder flag is unchanged. The proof commutes the time jet with the constant direction, then applies the spatial derivative estimate to each term.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: The time norm retains the same spatial derivative cost

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: For nonzero radius and a common time-norm cap `L` on the scaled coframe rows, estimates the slow divergence product with exact splitting of the two time weights. The first field `V` is measured at spatial order `n+1`, while `Y` is measured at `n`. The factor is $3Q_n^2L$. This distinction matters when inserting the divergence term into the mean-source recurrence.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: The divergence product spends its extra order on the first field

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: For a scalar and vector profile, assumes three bounded weights satisfy `τP = τZ * τY` on the measured time set. Their pointwise scalar multiple has time norm at most the common quadratic constant times the two corresponding weighted norms. The identity between weights is pointwise; no derivative of a weight is taken or required.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Product weights split between the two differentiated factors

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: The time seminorm through `q + 1` is bounded by the undifferentiated spatial seminorm plus `T` times the time seminorm through `q` of the first profile time derivative. This holds for any spatial seminorm on a positive-length slab. The recurrence loses no spatial order and is the summation step used in the transverse time induction.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: The next time norm uses one differentiated profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Specializes the split-weight slow-advection estimate to constant weight one on the whole slab. The radius is nonzero, and each scaled coframe row has time norm at most `L`. The bound is $3Q_n^2L$ times the advector at spatial order `n` and the target at `n+1`, all through time order `q`.

For `m ≤ n`, the unweighted factorial time seminorm through spatial order `m` is at most the one through `n`. The time order `q`, slab, scales, and profile are unchanged. This follows from inclusion of the admissible spatial derivative words, applied to every time jet.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: The unweighted time norm grows with spatial order

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: For a vector profile and `n ≤ m`, compares the full-slab unweighted factorial time seminorm at spatial order `n` with that at `m`. The time order remains `q`. This local order-inclusion lemma is used in source assembly to give all measured factors the spatial order required by the hierarchy recurrence.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Use a higher spatial order in a source estimate

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Sets every weight to one in the fast-advection time estimate. With `h ≠ 0`, the bound is $Q_n^2$ times the unweighted scaled-covector norm, the advector norm at order `n`, and the target norm at `n+1`. The coefficient norm contains the carrier and phase-width scaling; there is no additional frequency assumption in this theorem.

Uses constant time weights in the slow-divergence product bound. Given nonzero `ℓ` and the coframe row cap `L`, the first vector field is measured through spatial order `n+1` and the second through `n`, with time order `q` for both. The factor $3Q_n^2L$ is inherited from the three coordinate rows and two products.

Suppose `r` agrees on the slab with the wave-relay formula built from mean-zero profiles `v` and `f`. A coefficient budget at order `n`, positive frequency, nonzero label width, and a bounded time weight then yield the factorial time estimate for `r`. The right side costs the explicit relay constant times `K^2/freq` and the order-`n+1` norms of `v` and `f`.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Estimate the actual relay from its exact phase representation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: For a positive-length slab, `timeJetSeminorm hT 0 N f` equals `N f`. The finite sum has only the undifferentiated profile, with weight one. This connects the higher-time estimates to the undifferentiated mean and transverse estimates already available in the main construction; no new inverse estimate is proved here.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: The order-zero time norm is the spatial norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Evaluating `timeJet hT i f` at `(t,x)` with `t ∈ Icc 0 T` gives `iteratedDerivWithin i` of the scalar-time slice with label and phase fixed. The proof iterates the first-derivative evaluation identity. It includes the endpoints of the positive slab and does not replace within derivatives by derivatives of an arbitrary outside extension.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Profile time jets are genuine closed-slab derivatives

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: For every natural order `n`, the time jet of `applyField A f` is the sum over `0 ≤ i ≤ n` of $\binom ni$ times the `i`th coefficient jet acting on the complementary field jet. Positive `T` supports the closed-slab calculus. Induction uses the first-order product rule and Pascal’s identity, without spending label derivatives.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: The binomial rule for time-dependent coefficient profiles

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Every iterated time jet commutes with one derivative along a fixed vector `v`. The statement applies equally to a label direction, the independent phase direction, or another time direction. Induction on the time order reduces the result to symmetry of two constant-direction derivatives, preserving the same profile rather than selecting a new representative.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Time jets commute with label and phase derivatives

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: If a bundled profile equals `f t a` throughout the slab, its `i`th time jet evaluates to `slabTimeJet 0 T i f t a`. The hypothesis `hVal` identifies values for every phase, and `hT` gives a nondegenerate time slab. This is a fixed-label identity; it makes no claim that a moving Eulerian observation point has the same ordinary time derivative.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: A label field keeps its time derivative after bundling

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: The order-`i` profile time jet of `map L f` equals `map L` of the time jet of `f`, assuming `hT : 0 < T`. The proof iterates the directional commutation rule in the time direction. This removes fixed linear contractions from repeated differentiation without changing spatial derivative orders or introducing coefficient derivatives.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: All profile time jets commute with fixed linear maps

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: For a bundled smooth twisted profile on a positive closed slab, the jth time jet commutes with every fixed weighted label-and-phase derivative word. Both ℓ and h remain constant during differentiation. Induction on the word reduces the claim to commutation of time and constant directional derivatives. No estimate or growth bound for either side is included.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Time derivatives commute with fixed spatial words

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: If `f` is phase independent, each of its profile time jets is also phase independent. The hypothesis `hT : 0 < T` provides the legitimate within-time derivative, while `hmean` supplies equality of slices at all phases. The proof differentiates these equal functions on the same interval, retaining the special mean-field class during Eulerian conversion.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Time derivatives preserve independence of phase

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Taking a time jet of the normalized primitive gives the normalized primitive of the time jet, as equality of twisted profiles. The input has zero phase mean, and its time jet receives the corresponding proof from `PhaseMeanZero.timeJet`. The theorem uses the pointwise phase-integral interchange and `T > 0`, so the identity includes endpoint times.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: The bundled primitive commutes with time differentiation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: The $n$th profile time derivative of a fixed bilinear product is the sum of $\binom ni B(\partial_t^if,\partial_t^{n-i}g)$ over `i ≤ n`. The only time-domain requirement is positive slab length, since the profile types supply smoothness. The proof derives this from operator application and commutation with the fixed map `B`.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Time jets satisfy the bilinear binomial formula

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: States equality of bundled vector profiles obtained by averaging in phase before or after any time jet. The hypothesis `hT` ensures a nondegenerate closed time interval. The proof evaluates profiles, rewrites the phase average as its integral from zero to one, and uses the fixed-interval derivative interchange. No additional source or amplitude hypothesis is needed.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Phase averaging commutes with every time derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: For a smooth twisted profile on a positive-length slab, an arbitrary time jet commutes with one scaled label or independent-phase derivative. The scales `ell` and `h` are fixed real parameters, and the selected direction is constant. The statement is equality of profiles and has no derivative-loss estimate or differentiation of a time-dependent scale.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Time and scaled spatial derivatives commute

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: The jet of order `i + 1` is obtained by applying one profile time derivative to `timeJet hT i f`. The identity holds as an equality of bundled profiles, including their fixed zero representative outside the slab. It is the recurrence used when the proof estimates a new time order from the preceding one.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: The jet of order `i + 1` also equals `timeJet hT i` applied to the first time derivative of `f`. Both sides are powers of the same linear operator, so no additional smoothness or commutator assumption is needed. This orientation is useful when a differential equation already supplies the first derivative.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Take the first time derivative before the remaining jets

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: For any smooth twisted profile and positive slab duration, `timeJet hT 0 f` equals `f`. This follows from the zeroth power of the linear operator. It provides the base case for induction on time order, where the auxiliary estimates must recover the existing spatial estimates without changing the field.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: The zeroth time jet is the original profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.text: Assumes a smooth profile is zero at every slab time strictly earlier than `t₀`. At any such time, every bundled time jet is also zero at every label and phase. The conclusion still requires `t < t₀`; it does not assert the value at the activation time itself. The argument uses local equality to zero within the closed slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeJ.summary: Every time derivative vanishes before activation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.timeS.text: The time slice at fixed label and phase has a derivative within the closed interval, given by the full profile derivative in direction $(1,0,0)$. This formulation includes both endpoints without imposing an extension beyond them. It is the time-derivative identity used when differentiating a zero phase mean.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.time_.text: Given nonnegative `c`, `x`, and `y`, together with upper bounds `c ≤ d`, `x ≤ a`, and `y ≤ b`, concludes $cxy\le d(ab)$. The hypotheses also ensure the necessary upper factors are nonnegative. This private real-inequality helper collects coefficient and profile estimates into the standard source-bound format.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.trans.text: For nonnegative reference coefficient bounds and `D ≥ 1`, the explicit solve coefficient with duration `r ≤ 1` is bounded by a reference constant times $D^{20}$. The reference constant is nonnegative and depends on derivative order, while the parent exponent twenty does not. The statement is a numerical comparison of the defined coefficients.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.trans.text: This explicit expression combines the repeated velocity-equation factor, the undifferentiated inverse constant `C₀`, and the normalized pressure application cost. It depends on `T`, spatial order `n`, time order `q`, and coefficient bound `C`. The formula records how the velocity and pressure estimates are added after the zero-mean phase estimate.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.trans.text: Assume $0\le T\le1$, `D ≥ 1`, and nonnegative inverse and coefficient costs bounded respectively by `A₀*D^a` and `A*D^b`. The transverse time constant is at most its unit-time version with coefficients `A₀,A`, multiplied by $D^{a+b(q+1)}$. The spatial order may affect the fixed constant, but it does not enter this exponent.

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.trans.text: If the slab parameter `T` and both input constants `C₀,C` are nonnegative, the combined transverse time cost is nonnegative for every `n,q`. The proof uses nonnegativity of the scalar and vector application costs. This lemma concerns the numerical formula only; it does not establish coefficient bounds or the undifferentiated inverse estimate.

This real expression collects the product-rule factor, lift and pullback bounds, homogeneous forward bound, interval duration, and the derivative-word factor for the transverse ODE. It is the coefficient multiplying the source seminorm before summing over words. Its arguments are unrestricted real numbers; positivity is imposed when using it as an estimate.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.trans.summary: The coefficient for a differentiated transverse velocity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.trans.text: Bounds the explicit transverse-velocity coefficient with duration factor `r ≤ 1` by the unit-duration coefficient times `B+H`. The listed coefficient caps and `H` are nonnegative. The binder `B` is unrestricted, since its contribution is unchanged on both sides. This algebraic simplification does not supply the inverse or source estimates that use the coefficient.

The proof constructs a sine probe whose phase derivative is nonzero at the chosen point. The universal quantifier over test profiles is essential; a single test would not suffice.

This is a definitional equality. The lattice-compatibility proof is retained in the outer wrapper, while the concrete value calculation is exactly the one already established in the periodic space.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.summary: Read the material operator before the twisted restriction

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.text: The underlying periodic output of this twisted hierarchy component equals the corresponding periodic operation: the phase derivative of the second field selected by the first field and κ. This is a definitional equality. The lattice-compatibility proof is retained in the outer wrapper, while the concrete value calculation is exactly the one already established in the periodic space.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.summary: Read phase advection before the twisted restriction

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.text: The underlying periodic output of this twisted hierarchy component equals the corresponding periodic operation: the phase derivative multiplied by κ. This is a definitional equality. The lattice-compatibility proof is retained in the outer wrapper, while the concrete value calculation is exactly the one already established in the periodic space.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.summary: Read the fast gradient before the twisted restriction

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.text: For every integer lattice vector, a twisted profile’s representative is periodic under the corresponding joint label-phase shift. This theorem exposes the proof stored in the twisted submodule. The three value projections pass through the twisted, periodic, and smooth wrappers to the actual function.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.summary: Read the stored carrier-compatible translation identity

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.text: The periodic completion of twisted data is invariant under every prescribed joint lattice-and-phase shift. The covector must be phase independent and nonzero on the slab. Translation covariance of the normalized potential gives equality of label derivatives; outside the slab, both sides vanish by the profile convention.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.summary: Curl completion preserves the joint lattice and phase shift

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.text: A twisted profile is invariant under label translation by an integer vector together with the matching phase shift. This identity is what makes graph evaluation periodic in physical space.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.summary: Values agree after the simultaneous lattice shift

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.text: If a periodic profile satisfies every carrier-dependent lattice translation identity on the slab, its whole representative satisfies those identities. Outside the slab both sides vanish, since the shifts leave time fixed. This supports packaging solver outputs whose geometric properties are proved only on the time domain.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.twist.summary: Extend the twisted identity beyond the slab

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.uniqu.text: Proves `UniqueDiffOn` for the closed centered label cell by its convex geometry and nonempty interior. This supplies uniqueness of derivatives even at the cell faces. It is the necessary justification for differentiating an equality known on the closed cell when computing the curl completion of a wrapped profile.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.uniqu.summary: The closed centered cell has unique differentiation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.text:
The unweighted norm measures the entire time slab.

Default-value audit (b5): The positive-time hypothesis and the constant unit weight make the sampled derivatives bounded on the whole closed slab. This is a seminorm on bundled profiles, so it does not infer regularity from a bare numeric bound.

With weight one and all times in $[0,T]$, the phase average has no larger order-$n$ mixed seminorm than the original profile. This is the unweighted specialization of the bounded-weight contraction. It is used before estimating averaged quadratic terms, preserving the derivative order already assigned to their factors.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.summary: Phase averaging decreases the full-slab norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.text: A whole-slab bilinear product is bounded using the first factor’s full unweighted norm and the second factor’s active amplitude norm. The second factor must vanish before activation, and the positive amplitude must be at most one. The proof combines the product inequality with the inactive-profile comparison, retaining an explicit word-count constant.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.summary: Control a whole-slab product using its inactive oscillatory factor

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.text: If the twisted average fixes a profile, its unweighted mixed seminorm equals the label-word norm of the phase-zero slice. The proof first deduces phase independence from the averaging identity. This version matches the certificate returned by the mean solver and avoids requiring a separate pointwise independence premise.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.summary: A profile fixed by averaging has the label-only norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.text: For a phase-independent twisted profile on a positive slab, the unweighted mixed seminorm with Hölder flag `False` equals the label-word norm of the phase-zero slice. The phase scale is arbitrary because words involving phase derivatives vanish. This is an exact equality, with no additional constant or derivative loss.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.summary: The unweighted mean norm is exactly the label norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.text: On the full slab, label advection of `g` by `z` costs $3Q_n^2L$ times their order-$n$ and order-$(n+1)$ norms, respectively. The row bound `hG` and nonzero label width are explicit. Setting both time weights to one in the general product estimate gives this unweighted form.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.summary: Slow advection costs one label derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.text: If the profile is zero before activation and the active amplitude satisfies `0 < γ ≤ 1`, its full-slab unweighted seminorm is at most its active amplitude seminorm. Before activation every spatial derivative is zero; afterward dividing by `γ` enlarges every measurement. The conclusion is not valid for a general mean profile lacking the inactivity assumption.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.summary: The active weighted norm controls the whole inactive-prefix profile

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.text: If a twisted profile equals a phase-independent label coefficient on the slab and the coefficient has word bound `B`, its unweighted finite seminorm is at most the number of admissible words times `B`. The equality premise `hval` connects the abstract coefficient to the profile being measured. This avoids replacing the actual norm by an unrelated allowance.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.summary: A coefficient word bound controls its exact seminorm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.text: For n ≤ m, the order-n unweighted seminorm is at most the order-m seminorm. The scales, Hölder flag and profile are unchanged.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.summary: Unweighted seminorms increase with derivative order

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.text: This specializes the bounded-weight fast-advection estimate to weight one on all of $[0,T]$. The differentiated profile still costs one extra mixed derivative, while the covector and advector use order $n$. The hypothesis `hh : h ≠ 0` is retained; the theorem does not itself estimate the scaled covector by a frequency power.

Assume `G` is phase independent, its label derivatives satisfy `hjets`, and $\ell D^q\le1$ with nonnegative scales and constants. The scaled-row norm is bounded by the number of admissible words times the sum of derivative constants times $|\ell^{-1}|LD^p$. The residual inverse width stays explicit; the order-dependent factor $D^{qj}$ is absorbed.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.summary: Label scaling absorbs derivative-dependent parent powers

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.text: For a phase-independent covector with normalized label-jet bounds, $h=\mathrm{freq}^{-1/2}$ and $\ell D^7\le1$ imply the exact scaled-covector seminorm is bounded by an order constant times $D^2\mathrm{freq}^{3/2}$. Positive frequency justifies the normalization. The proof separates $h^{-1}\mathrm{freq}$ from the width-scaled label derivatives.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.summary: The scaled phase covector costs frequency to the three halves

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.text: The norm of $(\mathbf d\cdot V)Y$ is bounded by $3Q_n^2L$ times the order-$(n+1)$ norm of `V` and order-$n$ norm of `Y`. The theorem retains the `holder` flag, the common scaled-row bound, and $\ell\ne0$. It follows by taking all time weights equal to one.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.summary: A divergence product differentiates its first factor

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.text: Converts `hRaw`, a mixed bound with amplitude `A` and slope `p`, into an unweighted profile seminorm bound for any time jet `i ≤ q`. It assumes nonnegative `ℓ`, `D`, `A`, and `C`, and `hScale : ℓ * D^p ≤ 1`. The profile is phase-independent by `hVal`, so the phase length is unrestricted. The surviving amplitude is `A`, multiplied only by a finite sum and derivative-word count.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.summary: The label length absorbs the spatial derivative rate

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.text: Under the raw mixed bound and the same label-length condition, sums all time jets through `q` into `timeJetSeminorm`. The extra hypothesis `T ≤ 1` makes each factorial weight $T^i/i!$ at most one. The result is `terminalLabelTimeSeminormCost C q n * A`. Smoothness is supplied by the bundled profile and the value identity, not inferred from the bound alone.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.unwei.summary: Sum coefficient jets without changing their amplitude

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.veloc.text: Given a decomposition $V = U + O + M$, half-Hölder regularity at order `P`, and scheduled bounds for the parent, oscillation, and mean, proves $1 + \lVert V\rVert  \le  3 \cdot  \mathrm{freq}^{2\cdot (P+1)}$. It requires $\mu \ge  2$, a positive exponent parameter, and each prefactor at most `μ`. The estimate is an arithmetic aggregation of supplied component bounds.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.veloc.summary: Combine parent oscillation and mean at the full depth

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.veloc.text: An equality of twisted profiles `ops.material V + ops.phaseGrad p = F` yields the within-slab scalar-time equation at every label and phase. The proof evaluates the profile equality and applies the pointwise lemma. Phase independence of the strain and covector remains explicit; transverse and mean-zero constraints are separate facts.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.veloc.summary: The bundled momentum equation gives every slice equation

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.veloc.text: At one slab point, a twisted momentum equality determines the within-slab time derivative of `V` as forcing minus strain and phase-pressure terms. Phase independence of `M` and `κ` allows their values to be read at phase zero. Smoothness is already part of the profile type, so the result includes endpoint derivatives.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.veloc.summary: A pointwise momentum identity gives the time derivative

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.waveP.text: Multiplying the phase velocity by a real scalar multiplies its normalized wave potential by the same scalar. The covector and phase point are fixed. The proof uses linearity of the phase primitive and cross product; no nonzero covector hypothesis is needed for this algebraic identity of totalized expressions.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.waveP.summary: A scalar passes through the phase potential

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.waveR.text:
The fixed-time formula for the four slow relay terms, with the actual transported covector and the genuine phase profiles.

Default-value audit (b5): Reading coefficients at phase zero is appropriate once the coefficient profiles are phase independent. The raw expression does not itself impose that property or the momentum equation.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.waveR.summary: The slow relay in the actual parent chart

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.waveR.text:
The explicit order constant in the normalized linear relay estimate.

Default-value audit (b5): The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.waveR.summary: The explicit derivative-order constant for the relay

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.waveR.text: At relay level `p`, this definition uses the preceding transverse forcing, built from `sourceBeforeMean` after subtracting its average and the mean-phase advection. At level two it is set to zero because the activation completion is subtracted separately in the relay. The definition is total in `p`; later identities restrict to levels `2,…,P+1`.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.waveR.summary: The preceding force after removing the activation completion

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.weigh.text:
Evaluate the profile at times in `A`, with a scalar multiplier depending only on time. Using inverse amplitude here leaves label and phase orders intact.

Default-value audit (b5): The time index set A and scalar weight are arbitrary here; A may be empty and the weight may vanish. Smoothness and norm applications separately require slab membership and the appropriate weight bounds.

On a chosen time subset of the slab, the weighted slice of the bundled phase average equals the average of weighted phase translates of the original slice. Period one makes the integral independent of the starting phase. Since `τ` depends only on time, it factors through the phase integral without requiring a time derivative.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.weigh.summary: Weighted phase averages as translated integrals

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.weigh.text: A scalar time weight may be applied to the velocity slices before taking their normalized potential and slow curl.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.weigh.summary: Time weights pass through the normalized curl correction

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.weigh.text: A pointwise representation of an actual twisted source as the raw relay also represents its weighted slices using the weighted input slices.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.weigh.summary: The relay formula passes to amplitude-weighted slices

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.weigh.text: Restricting the scaled coframe-row profile to a time set `A` and weighting by one gives exactly the raw coefficient function used in the mixed-word estimate. The hypothesis `hA` ensures every evaluation lies in the slab. This identifies two encodings of the same row, without adding a coefficient bound.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.weigh.summary: The bundled row equals the coefficient in the norm

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.weigh.text: For a time in the slab, multiplying a smooth profile slice by an arbitrary scalar time weight leaves its label and phase dependence smooth. The weight needs no time differentiability for this fixed-time statement.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.weigh.summary: Weighted slices are smooth in label and phase

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.wordB.text: The actual measured source controls every normalized derivative word.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.wordB.summary: The amplitude seminorm controls every normalized word

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.wrapO.text: Wraps a raw phase-periodic field by centered twisted periodization and then regards it as a twisted profile on the closed time slab. Smoothness of the periodized field is supplied as `hf`; it is not deduced for arbitrary raw input. The resulting profile has exact phase and lattice compatibility, with the library’s zero extension outside the slab.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.wrapO.summary: Wrapping a smooth profile on the parent cell

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.wrapO.text: At a time in $[0,T]$, the wrapped profile evaluates to the centered twisted periodization of its raw input. The theorem explicitly unwraps the nested profile structures. It says nothing about evaluation outside the slab, where `ofSmooth` uses zero; nor does it remove the spatial periodization on an arbitrary label.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.wrapO.summary: Evaluating the wrapped profile inside the slab

TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.wrapp.text: For a function vanishing whenever the label norm is at least $2\ell$, its twisted periodization agrees with the original function on the centered cell, provided $2\ell<1/2$. The theorem needs only a zero value in the target type. The support gap provides a collar near every cell face where changing representatives cannot change the value.
TorusEuler.HierarchyTwistedProfile.wrapp.summary: Periodization leaves the supported central cell values unchanged

TorusEuler.HolderLabels.text: Abbreviates the unit three-torus used when comparing bundled quotient half-Hölder fields with periodic Euclidean lifts. The quotient carries the coordinate product metric, while `Vec3` carries its Euclidean norm. The later comparison constants account for this difference; the abbreviation itself asserts no equivalence of norms.

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerBase.text: Packages a zero-index stage, the first child stage and the wave linking them, all at activation zero. It fixes the first coupling to $2\pi$. The field called stationary is not itself required to be time independent. The explicit stationary-shear realization supplies that additional property when constructing the base.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerBase.summary: The initial stage and its first completed wave

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerBase.ofFirstWav.text: Builds the induction base from the stationary shear parent and the actual first cutoff child. The first wave uses the constant-one cutoff and activation time zero. Required inputs include the prescribed tilt, support, oscillation and correction estimates, a central split, a bound on remainder derivatives, cutoff-tail control, and lifetime conditions; the proof imports the explicit first-wave central calculation.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerBase.ofFirstWav.summary: Assemble the first cutoff wave over the stationary shear

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerBase.tip.text: Turns a certified base pair into the index-zero tip, using the lifetime bound to fit the first endpoint inside the stationary slab. All stored velocities and wave data are reused directly. The construction changes their packaging, rather than choosing replacement stages with only equal numerical bounds.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerBase.tip.summary: The initial pair forms a valid induction tip

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.text: Adds central wave vectors, amplitudes, cutoffs, gradient errors and physical crossings to an existing stage family `s`. Equalities identify the preceding and current pairs with those of each crossing. Bounds on strength, coupling and comparison errors are explicit fields. These identities prevent the terminal argument from combining estimates for unrelated wave or velocity sequences.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.summary: Central waves belonging to the same stages

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.ac.text: Proves monotonicity including the artificially stored index zero and the two equal initial activations. For successor indices it uses the nonnegative activation increments in `s`, rather than needing a fresh crossing argument. The distinction between monotonicity here and strict increase after the initial pair matters when forming the terminal-time sequence.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.ac.summary: The entire activation sequence is nondecreasing

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.ac.text: Shows that activation `j + 3` occurs strictly after activation `j + 2`. The stored crossing occurs after the switching time, and the positive physical growth rate makes that delay positive. This is compatible with the separately imposed equality of the first two wave activations at zero.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.ac.summary: Successive later activations are strictly separated

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.cl.text: Maps the normalized interval from zero to `w.window j` into the actual physical interval for wave `j + 2`. The rate is positive, and `physical_window` identifies the right endpoint. This verifies the domain hypothesis needed before applying normalized wave-comparison estimates to the stored physical crossing.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.cl.summary: The normalized clock stays inside its physical slab

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.cu.text: Defines the leading curl coefficient as $e^{-1}C^{-1}/(6A^2)$, where $C$ is the common strength constant and $A$ the comparison-window coefficient. The factor $e^{-1}$ records retained preceding-wave strength. Its strict positivity is proved separately, allowing the positive frequency power to dominate the error terms.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.cu.summary: The positive leading coefficient in the curl estimate

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.cu.text: Proves strict positivity of the explicit leading curl coefficient. Positivity of the exponential, inverse strength constant and squared window coefficient supplies the result. This is the nondegeneracy condition used when the eventual power lower bound is converted into divergence of the central vorticity.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.cu.summary: The leading curl contribution has positive coefficient

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.cu.text: Abbreviates three times the operator norm of the continuous linear map taking a velocity derivative to its curl. This constant controls the accumulated error terms in the central vorticity lower bound. It does not depend on the stage family or the index, and no positivity stronger than the needed norm properties is built into its name.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.cu.summary: A common coefficient for converting gradient errors to curl

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.ev.text: For all sufficiently large `j`, gives a central-curl lower bound on the half-open interval between activations `j + 2` and `j + 3`: a positive multiple of frequency `j + 1` to power $1/8$, minus an error of power $1/32$ and a constant. Hypotheses include common-slab containment, half-length bounds and uniform first-derivative convergence on every earlier compact time interval.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.ev.summary: The limit retains a growing curl on activation intervals

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.fi.text: Expresses the physical first coupling as the indicated frame entry of the central derivative of stage `j`. The preceding pair determines the frame, and `older_gradient` identifies the background matrix at activation. This is the bridge from the physical comparison notation to the coupling inequalities carried by the stage family.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.fi.summary: The first coupling uses the actual older gradient

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.in.text: Identifies the physical comparison initial strength with the product of the recorded preceding wave-vector and amplitude norms at activation `j + 2`. The equality uses both `preceding_vector` and `preceding_amplitude`. It is a compatibility fact, ensuring that the stored strength bounds concern the same pair used in the comparison.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.in.summary: The comparison strength uses the recorded preceding wave

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.no.text: Under the base-frequency lower bound, every stage frequency is at least two and therefore nonzero. This elementary consequence is stated separately because the scaled wave coordinates divide by the carrier frequency. It prevents those formulas from relying on Lean’s totalized value for division by zero.

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.or.text: Shows that the order at every positive stage index is at least one. At the first stage this is the initial-order equality; later it is part of the maximal admissible-order condition. The result licenses order-one correction estimates throughout the central curl argument, even before using eventual growth of the orders.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.or.summary: The construction always retains first derivatives

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.ph.text: Rewrites the physical active interval as the closed interval from activation `j + 2` to slab `j + 2`. The only substantive identification is the stored clock endpoint equality. This lets estimates stated on the stage interval satisfy hypotheses phrased using the physical amplification object.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.ph.summary: The comparison interval equals the recorded stage slab

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.ph.text: Assuming the base frequency is at least two, bounds `w.window j` by the common window coefficient times $(4\log\lambda_{j+4})^4$. The proof uses the actual clock endpoint, strength and coupling bounds, and the scheduled physical half-length. The conclusion concerns normalized time, not the duration of the physical interval itself.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.ph.summary: Each comparison window has a logarithmic upper bound

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.wi.text: Defines the positive coefficient $2\sqrt{8C\pi}$ from the common strength constant `w.strengthConstant`. It is independent of the stage index. The following estimates use it to bound normalized window lengths by fourth powers of logarithmic gains, with positivity proved separately from the record’s lower bound on $C$.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.wi.summary: A fixed coefficient for comparison-window bounds

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.wi.text: Uses the common strength lower bound and positivity of pi to show that `w.windowConstant` is positive. This justifies later divisions by its square in the vorticity coefficient. The theorem concerns one explicit constant and supplies no bound on the physical window until the separate comparison estimate is invoked.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerCentralWaves.wi.summary: The window coefficient is strictly positive

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.text: Stores lifetime bounds, one certified base and a successor function for every compatible finite prefix. Unlike the mere existence formulation `InductiveEulerSuccessor`, the function returns a particular step. Iterating this one function defines all later fields coherently; it is not a separate independent choice of a finished tower at each length.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.summary: A base pair and a chosen extension operation

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ac.text: Defines the activation sequence with an explicit zero at index zero and the activation of tip `n` at index `n + 1`. The first two positive indices therefore both evaluate to zero. Subsequent lemmas identify later activations with the crossings selected by actual successor steps.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ac.summary: The activation times read from the generated tips

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ac.text: Identifies activation `n + 3` with the crossing time of `selectedStep n`. The index shift accounts for the two initial waves already present at activation zero. This equality is what connects strict crossing delays and terminal interval estimates to the activation sequence used by the limit theorem.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ac.summary: Later activations are the selected physical crossings

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ac.text: Identifies activation `n + 2` with the next activation stored in generated tip `n`. This is a definitional consistency lemma between the global sequence and the local wave record. It allows local increment bounds to become bounds on consecutive entries of the single global activation sequence.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ac.summary: The next activation comes from the current completed wave

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ac.text: Computes activation at positive index one as zero using the activation stored by the base tip. This is the first completed wave supplied by the base pair. Subsequent physical crossing choices do not change that initial activation, and strict growth is only asserted after the two initial waves.

Computes activation at positive index two as zero from the base tip’s zero nextActivation, carried into its first successor tip. The crossing selected by that successor is activation three. Keeping these indices separate avoids confusing the second launch with the first strictly later crossing.

Computes activation at index zero as zero directly from the first branch of the global activation definition. This extra index belongs to the initial parent bookkeeping. The equality makes no claim about later crossing times or strict growth of the physical wave activation sequence.

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ce.text: Exports the central data and physical crossings from the same recursive construction into `InductiveEulerCentralWaves c.stages`. Stored equalities identify older gradients and preceding and current pairs. The crossing-time equality uses the global activation indexing. This shared origin is essential when later lower bounds are applied to the limit of those exact velocities.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ce.summary: The same choices supply the terminal central waves

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ol.text: Identifies the activation attached to the older member of generated tip `n` with the global activation at index `n`. The proof separates the zero-index case from successor indices. This equality supplies the dependent-type transport needed to compare the older stage object with the globally retained stage.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ol.summary: The older stage uses its original activation

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ol.text: After transporting across the equality of activation indices, proves that the older stage in tip `n` is exactly `c.stage n`. The symbol `▸` performs that type transport. This is an identity of certified stage objects, stronger than a statement that their velocities merely satisfy the same bounds.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ol.summary: The older tip member is exactly the retained earlier stage

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ol.text: Extracts the practical velocity equality from the generated tip and retained-stage definitions. It is used when exporting correction and gradient-splitting fields, whose formulas initially refer to the local older stage. The equality identifies actual functions and therefore allows the same derivative and residual expressions to be reused.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ol.summary: The older and retained velocities are the same function

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.se.text: Applies the stored successor function to the exact tip and history produced by `c.trace n`. This names the same step used by the next recursion branch. Later equalities identify its crossing and child with the activation and stage sequences, so compatibility is carried through to the terminal estimates.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.se.summary: The successor chosen at the generated prefix

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.sl.text: Defines the global slab sequence by applying the fixed parameter endpoint formula to each stage index and its generated activation. It introduces no independent sequence of endpoints. Subsequent strict-decrease and lifetime results therefore refer to the same intervals on which the retained stage certificates were constructed.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.sl.summary: The endpoint of each retained physical stage

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.sl.text: Proves strict decrease from each retained endpoint to the next. At the initial step, the one-quarter half-length bound leaves the first endpoint below one; at later steps, the current tip’s nesting theorem applies. This gives genuine time-domain containment for all members of the exported family.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.sl.summary: The retained stage endpoints strictly decrease

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.st.text: Returns the stored zero-index base at index zero and the parent of generated tip `n` at index `n + 1`. Its dependent return type records the corresponding value of `c.activation`. Thus the exported sequence uses the same stage objects that were passed from one local construction to the next.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.st.summary: The retained physical stage at each activation

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.st.text: Proves nonnegativity of the global activation sequence, including its extra zero index. At positive indices the generated tip carries the necessary certificate. This is used to place active intervals inside the closed time slabs where the corresponding velocities, pressures and flows have their stated regularity.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.st.summary: Every retained stage begins at a nonnegative time

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.st.text: Exports the generated velocities, residuals, activation times, slabs and oscillatory increments into `InductiveEulerStages`. Every estimate is taken from the retained stage or its actual linking wave. The older-velocity equality reconciles local and global formulas, while the physical-to-projected residual identity is used in the required orientation.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.st.summary: The compatible construction becomes one limit-input family

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ti.text: Projects the current tip from the recursively generated dependent pair `c.trace n`. The returned tip retains its index `n`, hence the types of its older and parent stages. This abbreviation changes only notation and does not perform an additional selection of stage or wave data.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.ti.summary: The final pair of stages in the generated history

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.tr.text: Builds the dependent pair of tip and prefix by natural-number recursion. At zero it uses the fixed base. At a successor it applies `c.successor` to the exact previously generated pair and appends that step. This is the construction that ensures all finite prefixes belong to one common sequence.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.tr.summary: One recursively chosen compatible history at every length

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.tr.text: For `k ≤ n`, restricting the generated length-`n` history to index `k` yields exactly `c.trace k`. The proof combines the recursive trace equation with preservation of earlier lookup under append. This supplies the common-prefix property required for a single infinite sequence of approximate solutions.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.tr.summary: Every generated history restricts to the same earlier history

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.tr.text: Unfolds one recursion step of `trace`, identifying the next tip and history with those obtained by appending `selectedStep n`. The equality is definitional. It exposes the exact compatibility needed in later lookup proofs rather than merely matching the lengths of the two histories.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerConstruction.tr.summary: The next generated history appends the selected step

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.text: The data are an integer $b\ge1$, a threshold $\mathcal B$, integer orders $q_j$, real frequencies $\lambda_j$, and two comparison constants. They must satisfy $q_1=1$, $\mathcal B(1)\le\lambda_0$, $\lambda_j=\lambda_{j-1}^{320b(q_j+1)}$, and the maximum rule in (1.14). At positive indices, $\mathcal B$ is positive and $\log\mathcal B(s)\ge4[320b(s+2)]^3$. The strength constant is at least $2$ and the integer comparison constant at least $240$. Threshold monotonicity and domination of analytic costs are not included here. Index zero is permitted, but the maximum rule begins with $q_2$; the powers separating successive frequencies are nonnegative integer powers. These conditions do not by themselves construct any velocity fields.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.summary: The frequency recurrence and order selection are imposed

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.Life.text: Collects a one-quarter upper bound for the first half-length, positivity of every half-length, the negative frequency-power upper bound, and contraction by a factor of at least four. These are arithmetic hypotheses on the chosen schedule. Together with activation increments they place each child endpoint strictly inside its parent interval.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.Life.summary: The numerical bounds that nest the time slabs

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.Step.text: The finite index type has one constructor for each analytic family label and three additional constructors for cutoff-tail, step, and mean costs. This lets a single threshold mechanism see all four families. Even if the analytic label type is empty, the three numerical cost rows remain present and must still be dominated.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.Step.summary: One finite index includes every kind of cost

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.Step.text: This structure records analytic costs with two natural indices and a finite family label, a cutoff-tail cost, a step constant, and mean costs. It is data supplied before the common schedule is chosen. No field asserts that these numbers bound an actual profile; the numerical selection theorem later makes the schedule dominate the supplied table.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.Step.summary: The four families of costs required by a step

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.Step.text: An analytic row at indices `m,p` sums absolute costs from derivative order zero through $m+3p$. The other three rows return the cutoff-tail, step, or mean cost at their indicated indices. This reserve is what later yields analytic control through $4P+1$ when the threshold is sampled at `m = P+1` and `p = P`.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.Step.summary: Analytic rows reserve three extra depth orders

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.Step.text: The formal object enlarges the list of fixed constants used to choose $\mathcal B$. For each additional family of constants $c(q,n,P)$ and each requested spatial order $m$, it inserts $\sum_{q=0}^m\sum_{n=0}^{m+r(q,P)}|c(q,n,P)|$, where the nonnegative integer $r(q,P)$ reserves extra spatial derivatives. The original analytic constants are retained, and the cutoff, step and mean constants are unchanged. This is a definition of the enlarged list, not an existence theorem for the velocity. It makes the auxiliary note's extra time-order requirements explicit and permits them to be fixed before the initial frequency is chosen.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.Step.summary: The original estimates share an enlarged majorant

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.Step.text: This proposition packages the required parent, child, next-frequency, depth, radius, and phase-width inequalities at one index. It includes domination of analytic costs through $4P+1$, step and recurrence smallness, mean and full-wave rates, cutoff-tail decay, and the final residual exponent. These are numerical hypotheses for later analytic assembly, not statements about any selected velocity or Fourier cutoff.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.Step.summary: All numerical inequalities for one scheduled physical step

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.Step.text: A `StepNumericalBudget` for the cost table enlarged by auxiliary time estimates implies the original step budget with exactly the same parameters. The proof takes each original analytic cost from the `inl` branch of the enlarged table; cutoff, step, and mean fields are retained. This ensures adding terminal requirements does not discard the hypotheses used by the physical construction.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.Step.summary: The enlarged schedule keeps the original step budgets

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.abs_.text: Fix finite families of the original and additional constants, a nonnegative integer exponent parameter $b$, and a reserve $r(q,P)$. Set $K(s)=320b(s+1)$. If the time order and depth satisfy $q,P\le7K(s)$ and the spatial order satisfies $m\le7K(s)+r(q,P)$, the formal statement bounds $|c(q,m,P)|$ by the enlarged threshold at $s$. Each absolute value occurs in one of its finite nonnegative sums. The statement is uniform over the admitted indices and does not depend on a constructed velocity. It proves a bound for the threshold obtained from this particular enlargement, not for an arbitrary function merely denoted by $\mathcal B$.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.abs_.summary: The enlarged majorant bounds every admitted entry

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.even.text: For arbitrary fixed real `C` and `A` and positive `ε`, eventually $C\lambda_i^A\le\lambda_{i+1}^{\varepsilon}$. Neither `C` nor `A` must be positive. The proof first makes the parent frequency dominate `C`, then makes the adjacent exponent large enough for $(1+A)/\varepsilon$. Positivity of the scheduled frequency justifies the real-power identities.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.even.summary: A fixed parent polynomial fits any positive child power

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.even.text: For a frequency sequence satisfying the construction's schedule, fix real numbers $C,A$ and $\varepsilon>0$. The formal statement gives an index after which $C\lambda_{j-1}^{A}\lambda_j^{-\varepsilon}\le1$. The index may depend on $C,A,\varepsilon$ and the chosen schedule; it is not uniform over increasing derivative orders or exponents. The frequencies are positive and $\lambda_j=\lambda_{j-1}^{K_j}$ with $K_j$ tending to infinity. This is the numerical absorption used with $\varepsilon=1/12$ in the auxiliary recurrence. The conclusion is an eventual inequality, not an estimate on any prescribed initial stage.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.even.summary: Frequency separation makes every fixed loss small

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.even.text: Fix spatial and time orders `m` and `q`. Eventually, with `K` evaluated at `P.order (i+2)`, both orders are at most `7*K`, and `P.stepDepth i + q + 2 ≤ 7*K`. Since the depth is `6*K`, the remaining growing margin accommodates the fixed extra time derivatives. The starting index may depend on both fixed orders.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.even.summary: Every fixed derivative order eventually fits the reserve

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.exis.text: Produces one threshold `N` such that every admissible parameter record with initial frequency at least `N` satisfies `LifetimeBounds`. The proof combines the schedule estimate with the explicit floor $4^{16}$. The threshold precedes the universally quantified parameter record, so it is not chosen separately at each induction step.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.exis.summary: A single frequency threshold supplies all lifetime bounds

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.exis.text: Given a finite family of signed order-dependent costs, an exponent at least one, comparison constant at least 240, and strength constant at least two, every sufficiently large initial frequency admits one schedule with lifetime bounds. At every stage it dominates the absolute values of all tabulated costs through the stated sevenfold exponent cutoff in both indices. The chosen threshold and all prescribed constants remain exactly fixed.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.exis.summary: One schedule absorbs all prescribed fixed-order costs

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.exis.text: Fixing the cost functions and a sufficient absolute exponent first, the theorem chooses a lower bound so every larger initial frequency admits parameters with the prescribed constants, lifetime bounds, and `StepNumericalBudget` at every index. The floor also includes the requested initial constraint, $e^4$, and the cutoff constant. The assumption that step costs are at least one remains explicit.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.exis.summary: A single initial threshold supplies all numerical step budgets

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.exis.text: Fix the main and auxiliary constant families, an extra derivative reserve, and the main numerical parameters. Assume that $b$ meets the main step's stated exponent lower bound, the comparison constant is at least $240$, the strength constant is at least $2$, and each step constant is at least $1$. The formal statement fixes the enlarged threshold and then finds $N_1$ such that every $N\ge N_1$ admits the required frequency schedule with $\lambda_0=N$. It preserves the main lifetime and step estimates. An auxiliary constant of orders $q,m,P$ is at most $\lambda_i$ when $q,P\le7K(q_{i+2})$ and $m\le7K(q_{i+2})+r(q,P)$. This selects numerical parameters; it does not by itself construct the Euler fields.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.exis.summary: The threshold precedes the initial frequency choice

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.firs.text: Sets the stationary shear's tilt to the coupling ratio associated with gain $4\log(\lambda_3)$. The input is a certified parameter record: its threshold floor and frequency recurrence already force positive large frequencies. The first-wave selection later exposes the gain and small-tilt inequalities in the form needed by the stationary geometry constructors.

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.pare.text: If the initial frequency is at least $e$ and the activation time t₀ is nonnegative, the child endpoint time P.slab (n+1) t₀ is at least $\lambda_n^{-1/8}$. The proof bounds the logarithmic factor in the scheduled half-length from below. Here slab is the final time of the interval starting at zero, not the duration measured from activation.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.pare.summary: The endpoint time bounds the parent scale

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.slab.text: Defines the stage endpoint from its index and activation time. Index zero has the fixed endpoint one; at index `n + 1` it is the activation plus twice the scheduled half-length at index `n`. The definition fixes the time bookkeeping before any stage field is selected.

Under the same initial-frequency and nonnegative-activation hypotheses, the inverse endpoint time to any natural power q is at most $\lambda_n^{q/8}$. Positivity follows from the parent-frequency lower bound before taking reciprocals. The estimate makes extraction of a fixed time derivative polynomial in the parent frequency, including the case $q=0$.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.slab.summary: Inverse time powers cost parent frequency

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.slab.text: Unfolds the positive-index endpoint into the activation time plus twice the preceding-index half-length. This keeps the indexing of stages and physical half-lengths explicit in later inequalities. Strictly later endpoints require positivity of the half-length, supplied by the lifetime certificate rather than this equality.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.slab.summary: Each later endpoint follows its activation

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.slab.text: Computes the zero-stage endpoint as one, regardless of the activation argument. This is the stationary parent convention used to start the recursion. The equality follows directly from pattern matching and does not by itself assert existence of a stationary Euler field on that interval.

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.step.text: For the frequency schedule, let $b\ge1$ be an integer and $K(s)=320b(s+1)$. At the internal step numbered $i\ge0$, which constructs the paper's wave $j=i+1$, the formal definition sets the depth equal to $6K(q_{i+2})=6K_{j+1}$. This is exactly (7.2) after accounting for the index shift. The depth and derivative orders are nonnegative integers. The definition chooses how many profiles enter the finite expansion; it does not itself prove the expansion estimates or smallness of its remainder.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.step.summary: Fixes the depth using the next derivative order

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.step.text: The floor is the maximum of one, the prescribed absolute exponent, the flow loss $\max(a,1)+(\max(a,1)+p)+1$, and six times the recurrence exponent. It is chosen before the frequency schedule. Requiring the schedule exponent to dominate this floor supplies all four exponent comparisons used by the step budget.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.step.summary: One exponent absorbs radius, flow, and recurrence losses

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.step.text: When the parameter threshold is exactly the table’s fixed-order threshold, the exponent dominates the stated floor, the initial frequency meets the cutoff floor, and every step cost is at least one, all stages satisfy `StepNumericalBudget`. The proof uses schedule growth and cost domination, including the analytic derivative reserve. It does not establish that the supplied costs bound the actual hierarchy.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.step.summary: The selected threshold supplies every step inequality

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.step.text: If the frequency is at least one and `C` is at most its $1/32$ power, then $C$ times the frequency to power $-1/12$ is at most one. The proof compares with the combined exponent $-5/96$. Nonnegativity of `C` is unnecessary because the multiplying real power is nonnegative.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.step.summary: The step rate beats the negative twelfth power

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.sum_.text: For $D\ge1$, nonnegative coefficients on a finite set, exponents bounded by `b`, and coefficient sum at most `Γ`, the sum of coefficient-weighted powers of $D$ is at most $\Gamma D^b$. The argument compares every power with $D^b$ before summing. An empty index set is allowed and leaves the explicit coefficient-sum hypothesis.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.sum_.summary: A finite sum shares its largest parent exponent

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.term.text: The exponent `frequencyExponent P.exponentParameter (P.order (i+1))` tends to infinity with `i`. The proof compares it from below with the already diverging order sequence. This is the quantitative separation behind the ability to absorb any fixed parent-frequency polynomial into a positive power of the next frequency.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.term.summary: Adjacent frequency exponents tend to infinity

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.term.text: For any admissible parameter record, the frequency sequence is monotone. The recurrence raises the preceding frequency to the scheduled positive exponent, and the initial frequency is already greater than one. This supplies comparisons between parent, child, and later frequencies without changing the chosen sequence.

The frequencies of an admissible parameter record tend to `atTop` as the stage index tends to `atTop`. This is stronger than a sequence of occasional large values: every fixed real lower bound is eventually exceeded. The proof uses the schedule recurrence and the initial frequency strictly above one.

Every `InductiveEulerParameters` record has `P.frequency 0 > 1`. The proof uses the positive exponent parameter, the logarithmic lower floor on the threshold at order one, and the initial-frequency threshold condition. No auxiliary estimate is assumed. This excludes degenerate bases when real powers and growth comparisons are used later.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.term.summary: The initial scheduled frequency exceeds one

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.term.text: The order sequence `P.order` tends to infinity. The proof combines frequency growth with the maximal admissible-order rule and the fixed threshold function. Thus every fixed derivative order eventually fits the schedule; the theorem does not assert one stage works simultaneously for all unbounded orders.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.term.summary: The scheduled derivative orders tend to infinity

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.term.text: Let the frequency schedule be fixed, assume $\lambda_0\ge e$, and let the activation time of a child interval be nonnegative. If $T$ is that interval's scheduled right endpoint and $\mu$ is the parent frequency, the formal statement proves $T^{-1}\le\mu^{1/8}$. The schedule gives $T>0$, so this reciprocal is the ordinary reciprocal. Consequently a derivative extraction cost $i!T^{-i}$ is at most $i!\mu^{i/8}$ for fixed $i$. The result establishes the time-scale part of the auxiliary note's polynomial bounds; it says nothing by itself about the reciprocal label radius or other powers of $\mathsf D$.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerParameters.term.summary: Time extraction costs a fixed parent power

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.text: Defines finite compatible histories by two constructors: an initial certified base, and appending an actual successor of the current tip. The type is indexed by both length and tip. This records compatibility in the type itself, which later allows a single infinite construction to retain every earlier stage without reselecting it.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.summary: A finite history indexed by its exact last stages

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.activeSl.text: Combines monotonicity of retrieved activation times with reverse monotonicity of their endpoints. The current closed active interval is therefore contained in each earlier retrieved active interval. The result is a domain inclusion for one compatible prefix, not a universal comparison of independently chosen stage intervals.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.activeSl.summary: The current interval lies inside every earlier active interval

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.exists_l.text: For `k + 1 ≤ n`, extracts a genuine successor step linking the two consecutive retrieved tips. The equality also identifies the later history as the earlier one with that step appended. This is the key bridge from compatibility encoded by prefixes to quantitative relations between successive physical crossings.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.exists_l.summary: Consecutive historical tips share an actual recorded successor

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.initial_.text: Retrieves the initial tip of any compatible prefix and proves its exit coupling equals $2\pi$. The base constructor supplies the equality, and appended steps preserve the initial lookup. This fixes the normalization for the finite coupling recurrence without assuming that every later coupling is unchanged.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.initial_.summary: Every compatible history starts with coupling two pi

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.later_wa.text: For an existing prefix and a selected later wave, proves the first coupling lies between $\pi$ and $4\pi$ and the coupling ratio equals the next scheduled value. The gradient is explicitly that of the actual parent. The base-frequency floor $e^4$ and compatible prefix are required before the child stage is constructed.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.later_wa.summary: The selected exit has the correct physical couplings

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.lookup.text: Given `k ≤ n`, recursively retrieves the tip and compatible history at index `k` from a prefix of length `n`. The dependent pair returns both objects together. At the current endpoint it returns the whole prefix; otherwise it descends into the previously recorded prefix, never choosing a different earlier construction.

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.lookup_a.text: Proves that the activation stored in any earlier retrieved tip is at most the current tip’s activation. The index restriction `k ≤ n` is essential. Induction over actual appended steps uses their nonnegative activation increments, rather than imposing monotonicity as an unrelated property of a separate time sequence.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.lookup_a.summary: Earlier waves activate no later than the current wave

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.lookup_a.text: If `k ≤ n`, looking up index `k` after appending a successor gives the same dependent pair as looking it up before the append. The two bound proofs may differ, but no earlier data change. This is the finite compatibility invariant used when extracting a common sequence.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.lookup_a.summary: Appending a stage preserves every earlier prefix

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.lookup_l.text: For indices `k ≤ l ≤ n`, first retrieving the prefix at `l` and then retrieving `k` gives the same dependent pair as retrieving `k` directly. The proof follows the prefix constructors. This guarantees coherence of historical stage data across nested uses of the lookup operation.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.lookup_l.summary: Repeated restriction agrees with direct restriction

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.lookup_s.text: Computes lookup at the prefix’s own index, returning exactly its current tip and history as a dependent pair. The result is stronger than equality of projected velocities. It supports later identity arguments where the stored successor must be attached to precisely the prefix that generated it.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.lookup_s.summary: Looking up the current stage returns the whole prefix

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.next_act.text: Places the next physical comparison interval inside every earlier active interval recorded by the prefix. It first fits inside the current interval using `LifetimeBounds`, then uses the prefix containment theorem. This lets the next construction safely consult old wave equations throughout its own complete comparison window.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.next_act.summary: The next comparison remains inside all recorded wave intervals

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.next_cou.text: Assuming the base frequency is at least $e^4$, bounds the first coupling at a newly selected crossing between $\pi$ and $4\pi$. The candidate crossing must start from the current exit coupling and scheduled ratio, and target the next scheduled ratio. Only the existing prefix and this comparison are required; the new child stage need not already exist.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.next_cou.summary: The next coupling is controlled before building its child

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.schedule.text: For a consecutive pair of historical indices inside the prefix, obtains the scheduled crossing relation between their exit couplings. It extracts the recorded successor through `exists_lookup_step` and applies that step’s crossing theorem. Thus the recurrence uses real recorded crossings throughout the finite history.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.schedule.summary: Every adjacent pair inherits its actual physical crossing

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.slab_le_.text: Shows that the current parent endpoint is no larger than the endpoint of any earlier retrieved parent. The proof composes containment supplied by the actual appended tips. This transports older smoothness and wave estimates to the smaller current interval while preserving which earlier stage they describe.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.slab_le_.summary: The current endpoint fits inside every earlier slab

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.tip_pare.text: For a certified finite prefix `prior`, the parent endpoint time at its tip is at most one. The initial case uses the lifetime bound on the first slab, and an appended step uses the strict decrease of the next endpoint. This ensures that all subsequent parent estimates apply on a duration no longer than one.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerPrefix.tip_pare.summary: Every parent slab stays inside the unit interval

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.text: Stores a continuous torus velocity, a normalized periodic pressure and a two-time flow for one specified stage and activation. Smoothness, oddness, divergence, Fourier support, deformation and a one-sided pressure-Hessian bound are certified. The residual is the physical momentum expression for these same fields, and `projected_eq` identifies it with projected momentum on the closed slab.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.summary: One actual truncated parent with its pressure and flow

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.text: This record contains a smaller positive time slab inside the stage domain, its actual hierarchy geometry, matching momentum residuals, and periodic Fourier-band residual data. It also stores a half-unit residual derivative bound and an odd phase-independent residual profile with the correct pulled-back values. These are certificate fields for an already given stage, not conclusions available from arbitrary geometry.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.summary: The inductive parent restricted to the next endpoint interval

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ac.text: For any physical approximation over the given parent geometry and pressure, proves that its stored parent residual equals the slab's residual profile. Both have the same pointwise momentum-residual value on the slab, so profile extensionality identifies them. This prevents the recurrence from using estimates for a different residual witness.
