TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ac.summary: The hierarchy residual equals the actual parent residual

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ce.text: Assume the launch relation identifies the fixed carrier with the forward-flow adjoint applied to `κ t₀`, and assume `κ` solves the central adjoint equation. Then `κ` equals the flow-transported label wave vector on the active interval. The origin-fixing property and uniqueness of the covector equation connect the two constructions.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ce.summary: The chosen central covector is the transported carrier

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ce.text: Given the launch identity and a `CenterWaveOn` for the central velocity gradient, this theorem rewrites the central wave using the actual `labelWaveVector` and strain along the parent trajectory. Since the flow fixes the origin, the strain is unchanged. All central-wave inequalities are transported with the same constant `D`.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ce.summary: Use the transported carrier in the central wave data

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.de.text: Given an `OnSlab` record, the stage flow remains a `ChildFlow.DeformationOn` on the smaller interval with parent frequency as its bound. The proof restricts the flow, lattice-equivariance and deformation estimates using the record’s subset field. It does not reconstruct the flow or enlarge the original stage interval.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.de.summary: The restricted parent retains its deformation bounds

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ex.text: Chooses absolute exponent floors and then a monotone order budget for any nonnegative seed costs. Under the actual central-wave, inactivity, positive-weight and leading-profile assumptions, plus $L^6\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, it proves the measured recurrence, all retained-level bounds and an order-two remainder estimate. The reserve is $H=\max(m,3)+3P$ and $L=\mathsf D^{2a+b_0}$. These estimates precede selection of the final frequency schedule.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ex.summary: One order budget controls the actual finite hierarchy

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ex.text: The stage transverse bound remains valid when the weight is $\mathrm{freq}^{3/4}\lVert b(t)\rVert$ instead of the central amplitude norm. The positive carrier frequency makes this a positive constant rescaling, and both source and solution sizes change by the same factor. The same envelope exponent and parent loss are retained.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ex.summary: Normalize the weight without changing the solve constant

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ex.text: Chooses a radius floor `A ≥ 30` and nonnegative spatial constants before the stage. For a selected slab with parent frequency at least two, $0<\ell\le(D^A)^{-1}$, a positive normalized carrier, a center wave, and an inactive leading profile, assumes common time-norm caps $C(m)D^e$ for the four transverse coefficients. Every retained correction level $2\le i\le N$ then satisfies an oscillatory velocity-and-pressure bound by its source, with factor `transverseTimeCost 1 m q (Krec m) (C m)` times $D^{20+e(q+1)}$. The coefficient estimates are inputs; the theorem supplies their selected-solver consequence.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ex.summary: The selected transverse solve has a uniform time recurrence bound

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ex.text: One envelope exponent and nonnegative order table work for all restricted inductive parents. With frequency at least two, compatible launch data, a central wave and inactive leading hierarchy input, the actual levels satisfy the transverse-solve bound with loss $(\mathrm{frequency}^9)^{20}$. The weight here is the unnormalized central amplitude norm; normalization is handled in the next module.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ex.summary: The inductive stage supplies the transverse recurrence

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ex.text: There is a nonnegative table `V N` such that every restricted stage with frequency at least two has order-`j` velocity derivatives bounded by $V_N(\mathrm{frequency}^9)^j$ whenever $1\le j\le N$. The table is chosen before the stage. Order zero is deliberately absent: only derivatives of the velocity are needed here.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ex.summary: One derivative table controls all inductive parents

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ex.text: Chooses order-dependent nonnegative constants for the unweighted finite derivative seminorm of the actual pulled-back parent residual. It assumes initial frequency at least one, slab duration at most one, nonnegative label scale and $\ell\mathsf D^6\le1$. For every order the bound is $C_m\lambda_{n+1}^{-5/2}$; phase width is unrestricted because this residual is independent of phase.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ex.summary: The actual parent residual has the level-two size

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ex.text: For a nonnegative input cost array and time order `q`, choose coefficient cost arrays before the stage data. A parent admissible on a positive slab of length at most one, frequency at least two, normalized nonzero launch covector, and the supplied velocity mixed bound yield jets of the forward coframe, inverse coframe, strain, normalized covector, and reciprocal squared length. All share spatial slope sixteen; reciprocal time growth uses its separate explicit amplitude.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ex.summary: Derive all flow coefficient jets on the selected parent slab

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ex.text: For the actual admissible parent, velocity and residual mixed bounds through `q` imply a mixed bound for the residual composed with the parent flow. The residual amplitude keeps $\lambda_{n+1}^{-5/2}$ and is multiplied by $(1+DA)^q$, with `D = λ_n^9` and spatial slope six. Costs are chosen before stage data, and the statement does not request an extra residual time derivative.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ex.summary: Pull back the residual while retaining its small frequency power

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.fl.text: The flow of an inductive parent fixes the origin at every time in the restricted slab. The proof uses the odd stage velocity and uniqueness of trajectories. This permits central strain and covector identities to be evaluated at the spatial origin instead of along a potentially moving central trajectory.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.fl.summary: Oddness keeps the parent flow at the origin

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.or.text: If the parent scale is at least one, increasing both a nonnegative coefficient and its natural exponent increases their product. This small inequality is used repeatedly when several analytic losses are placed under one chosen parent power. It is independent of any Euler equation, profile construction or frequency schedule.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.or.summary: Increasing a nonnegative coefficient and parent exponent preserves bounds

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ph.text: Given a restricted stage, duration at most one, a leading input, and depth, this definition builds the physical approximation data. Its residual is exactly `d.residualProfile`, with the stage’s momentum identity proving the required value equation. This ensures that later residual estimates apply to the same field that enters the selected hierarchy.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ph.summary: Building the approximation with the parent’s actual residual

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ph.text: The leading input of the newly assembled physical approximation is definitionally `L`. This equality records that the wrapper preserves the chosen wave, rather than selecting a second seed. It is valid at every natural depth and is used when transporting inactivity, pressure normalization, and switch identities into the approximation data.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ph.summary: The assembled approximation keeps the supplied leading wave

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ph.text: The physical approximation’s parent residual is exactly the residual profile already stored in the restricted parent. This definitional equality is important for quantitative estimates: no residual with merely similar bounds has been substituted. The theorem supplies identity of the fields, while the residual’s momentum interpretation is proved in the constructor.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ph.summary: The assembled approximation keeps the supplied parent residual

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ph.text: At depth at least two, a leading input over the restricted inductive parent gives the full `PhysicalApproximationProperties` package. The proof applies the general assembly theorem using the parent’s actual flow, smooth velocity and pressure, periodicity, oddness, and divergence freedom. The result provides qualitative premises for the later Fourier cutoff, not a numerical residual bound.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ph.summary: The restricted parent supplies all qualitative approximation properties

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ph.text: If the label envelope has radius at most $D^{-3}$, the parent frequency is at least two, and its deformation scale is at most `D`, every nonzero Eulerian oscillation lies within the inverse parent frequency of a lattice point. Inactivity first locates the inverse-flow label in the periodic envelope; the actual parent flow converts that to spatial distance.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ph.summary: The Eulerian oscillation stays near a lattice point

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ph.text: For positive activation time `τ ≤ T`, an inactive leading input and retained depth at least one imply that the actual Eulerian oscillation vanishes at every time in $[0,τ]$. The support envelope is the closed support of the periodized radial cutoff. This theorem concerns the oscillatory correction, not the generally nonzero mean correction.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ph.summary: The oscillation is zero through positive activation

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ra.text: For a restricted stage with frequency at least two, the forward flow derivative and the inverse flow derivative along the forward flow are each bounded by the ninth power of that frequency. The record originally supplies the smaller deformation bound. Enlarging it puts both operators on the common parent scale used in the transverse estimates.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ra.summary: Put both flow derivatives on the common parent scale

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ra.text: For an `OnSlab` record, the physical parent velocity gradient is bounded by the ninth power of the stage frequency at every point of the restricted slab. The proof reads the actual strain from the stored geometry. Unlike the coframe enlargement lemma, this statement needs no extra lower bound on the frequency.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.ra.summary: The parent strain obeys the common ninth-power bound

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.re.text: For `d : s.OnSlab hT k`, transfers a supplied mixed bound on $R_s(t,X_s(0,t,x))$ to `d.residualProfile`. It uses the exact residual-profile value identity. Under `T ≤ 1`, nonnegative data, and `ℓ D^p ≤ 1`, the time norm is bounded by the finite label cost times `A`. The theorem does not itself establish the parent residual's small amplitude.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.re.summary: The actual residual profile inherits its mixed time bound

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.re.text: Proves the same full-slab residual bound for the later-wave input. Besides the tail and numerical budget, it requires the exact leading-input identity, even seed, activation-primary two-jet estimate and a bound for $|\widetilde\chi'|\gamma$. The conclusion uses the selected seed and completion structure, rather than treating the switch forcing as an independent arbitrary residual.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.re.summary: The later residual includes its actual activation forcing

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.re.text: Assuming the numerical budget, coefficient caps, tail estimate and both switch sources equal to zero, proves an order-one half-Hölder residual bound of $\lambda_{i+2}^{-7/2}$ on the full slab. This is the first-wave case of the common residual estimate. It uses the actual hierarchy remainder; the bound is not inferred merely from zero activation.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.re.summary: The first residual is controlled by the expansion tail

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.sc.text: Derives all four velocity readout estimates from a numerical step budget, coefficient caps, parent Bernstein bounds and measured-level estimates through `depth + 1`. Inactivity controls the oscillation before activation, while the positive weight is used only on the active interval. The full-depth graph estimate and central derivative estimate refer to the same approximation and the same cost table.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.sc.summary: The measured hierarchy yields the scheduled velocity bounds

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.sm.text: The stage pressure is jointly smooth on the restricted closed slab recorded by `OnSlab`. Smoothness is inherited by restriction from the original stage domain. This allows the endpoint mean problem to use the same pressure while temporal derivatives and momentum residuals are interpreted on the smaller interval.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.sm.summary: The parent pressure stays smooth on the smaller slab

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.sm.text: For an `OnSlab` record, the actual stage residual is jointly smooth on its smaller closed slab. The proof uses the stage’s smooth momentum residual and the equality recorded on that interval. This gives regularity of the concrete forcing supplied to the mean equation, rather than merely of an independently chosen residual profile.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.sm.summary: The restricted momentum residual is smooth

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.sm.text: An `OnSlab` record restricts the stage’s joint smoothness assertion for velocity to the selected endpoint slab. The proof uses inclusion of the time intervals and leaves the whole spatial domain unchanged. This is a transport of an existing regularity theorem, not a new regularity estimate for truncated data.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.OnSlab.sm.summary: The parent velocity stays smooth on the smaller slab

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.StageCoef.text: This proposition packages positive widths, the inverse-radius identity, carrier and deformation bounds, chart smoothness, and raw and scaled coframe jets for one restricted stage. Its final fields bound the slow rows by an order constant times $D^{a+1}$ and the fast covector by that constant times $D^2\mathrm{freq}^{3/2}$. Each field refers to the same supplied stage geometry.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.StageCoef.summary: The actual parent chart with all coefficient bounds

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.StageCoef.text: For $D\ge1$ and $C_1\ge0$, the maximum of $D$ and $D^2+C_1D^8$ is bounded by $(1+C_1)D^8$. Although a `StageCoefficientCaps` proof is passed, its fields are unused in this numerical inequality. The result only consolidates already supplied coframe and first-derivative allowances for the cutoff tail.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.StageCoef.summary: The first coframe derivative fits one parent power

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.StageCoef.text: Given actual stage coefficient caps, $D\ge1$, nonnegative frequency, and $b\ge a+1$ with $a\ge7$, any `K` dominating the source-order cost covers both centered advection coefficients. The slow cap is at most $KD^b$; the fast cap is at most $KD^b\mathrm{freq}^{3/2}$. The parent exponent does not depend on the derivative order.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.StageCoef.summary: A fixed parent power covers slow and fast sources

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.StagePres.text: Collects the carrier bound, scaled inverse-deformation derivatives, adjoint, strain and longitudinal-projection derivatives, and the parent's half-Hölder gradient estimate. The constants `K` and `Kparent` are fixed-order scalar costs, while parent powers are explicit. This proposition is the geometric input to the higher and mean pressure bounds for one actual parent slab.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.StagePres.summary: The pressure uses fixed first and second derivative bounds

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.contDiff_.text: For a field smooth on the closed time slab, each fixed-time spatial slice is smooth on all of $\mathbb R^3$, provided the chosen time belongs to the slab. Composing with $x\mapsto(t,x)$ proves the result. No extension in time is constructed; only spatial variables are varied.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.contDiff_.summary: A smooth closed-slab field has smooth spatial slices

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_on.text: Chooses a parent exponent, radius floor and order constants before the parent slab or forcing. For sufficiently small radius, parent frequency at least two, duration at most one and a phase-independent force `hforce`, the selected mean solver's velocity at order $n$ is bounded by its force at order $n+1$ times an explicit parent power. This estimate concerns the actual solver used by the hierarchy.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_on.summary: The actual endpoint mean inverse loses one derivative

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_on.text: There exists a threshold at least four such that any inductive parameter sequence starting above it admits an `OnSlab` record for each stage, every positive smaller endpoint interval and every nonzero carrier. The theorem constructs the required residual and geometry certificates. The nonzero carrier and interval inclusion are explicit and cannot be dropped.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_on.summary: A single frequency threshold builds every restricted parent

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_re.text: Let $R_j$ be the residual of a smooth periodic stage on $[0,S_j]$, with $S_j>0$ and $\lambda_j\ge0$. For every nonnegative integer $q$, the formal statement represents $\partial_t^qR_j(t)$ by a continuous field on $\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$ whose Fourier coefficients vanish above $4\lambda_j^5$, for all $0\le t\le S_j$. Time differentiation fixes the physical point and is one-sided at the endpoints. The representation agrees with the periodic lift throughout that interval; values assigned outside it are irrelevant to this conclusion. This supplies the residual half of the Fourier-support sentence following auxiliary Lemma 1.3. The velocity band is a separate result.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_re.summary: Time differentiation does not enlarge spatial support

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_sl.text: There are constants $C_m\ge0$, chosen before the stage and time order, with the following property. On a positive stage interval, let $\lambda_j>0$. If $|\partial_t^qU_j|\le A$ everywhere, with $A\ge0$, then $\|D_x^m\partial_t^qU_j\|\le C_mA\lambda_j^{5m}$. The same implication holds for $R_j$ with any nonnegative bound $B$ in place of $A$. Both estimates include the time endpoints and use the operator norm of the full $m$th spatial derivative on the periodic lift. The paper sums coordinate partial derivatives; passing between these conventions changes only constants depending on $m$. Neither bound chooses the eventual exponent or stage in auxiliary Lemma 1.3.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_sl.summary: One spatial constant works for all time derivatives

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_sl.text: For fixed $q,A$, this selects an exponent $A\prime\ge A$ before the stage. If the stage frequency is at least two, its slab has positive length, velocity derivatives through $q$ are bounded by $\mu^A$, and the single order-$q$ residual derivative is bounded by one, then velocity derivatives through $q+1$ are bounded by $\mu^{A\prime}$. Bernstein and Hölder-Leray estimates control the differentiated advection.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_sl.summary: One more velocity time derivative costs a parent power

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_st.text: The theorem selects a nonnegative sequence `C` uniformly before the stage and order. For a restricted stage of duration at most one, parent frequency at least one, and a positive centrally normalized child frequency, it supplies `StageCoefficientCaps` with $D=\mu^9$, $\ell=D^{-a}$, and $h=\mathrm{freq}^{-1/2}$ whenever $a\ge7$.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_st.summary: One sequence bounds coefficients of every inductive stage

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_st.text: Selects `K ≥ 1` and `Kparent ≥ 0` before the stage, carrier, frequency or radius exponent. On a slab of duration at most one, with parent frequency at least one and a positive carrier normalized at a slab time, every exponent `a ≥ 7` gives the required pressure-geometry caps. Only fixed derivative orders one and two enter the selection.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_st.summary: One fixed pair of constants controls every stage pressure geometry

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_st.text: A single nonnegative sequence `L` bounds relay coefficients for all restricted inductive stages and every time subset of the slab. With $a\ge16$, $D=\mu^9$, and the selected widths, the allowance is $2L_mD^{15+a}$. The proof obtains transported coefficient jets and absorbs the inverse label width using its exact power definition.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_st.summary: Every restricted stage has a fixed-power relay allowance

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_te.text: Fix nonnegative integers $q,A$. The formal statement chooses an integer $A'\ge A$ and constants $C_m\ge0$ before the stage. Assume $S_j>0$, $\lambda_j\ge2$, and, for every $i\le q$, the pointwise bounds $|\partial_t^iU_j|\le\lambda_j^A$ and $|\partial_t^iR_j|\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-5/2}$ on the whole stage. It then bounds velocity through time order $q+1$ by $\lambda_j^{A'}$, and its $m$th spatial derivative by $C_m\lambda_j^{A'+5m}$. Residual derivatives are bounded by $C_m\lambda_j^{5m}\lambda_{j+1}^{-5/2}$ only through time order $q$. Spatial derivatives use multilinear operator norms. Thus the velocity gains one time order without assuming the corresponding new residual derivative.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_te.summary: The momentum equation advances velocity regularity

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_ve.text: Produces nonnegative constants depending only on derivative order, bounding the order-`k` derivative of any certified stage by $K_k\lambda^{5k+1}$. The frequency must be at least one and time must lie in its closed slab. The estimate combines velocity size $\lambda$ with Fourier support of size $2\lambda^5$, uniformly in the stage and spatial point.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_ve.summary: Fourier support bounds every spatial derivative

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_ve.text: There exists a nonnegative sequence $C(N)$, chosen before any induction parameters or stage, such that every stage with frequency at least one satisfies a jet bound through order $N+1$. The bound is $C(N)\,\mathrm{frequency}^{5(N+1)+1}$. Summing individual Bernstein constants makes the same constant cover all lower derivative orders without depending on the chosen stage.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_ve.summary: One Bernstein constant covers every lower spatial derivative

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_ve.text: Chooses one threshold above which the actual stage gradient is bounded by the ninth power of its frequency throughout its closed slab. The Bernstein constant at order one is absorbed into one extra frequency power. The threshold concerns the frequency of the specified stage, not necessarily the global initial frequency.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_ve.summary: A uniform threshold absorbs the gradient constant

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_ve.text: For every budget `m`, selects a uniform constant controlling all derivative orders `1 ≤ k ≤ m` at coframe scale $D=\lambda^9$. The proof sums the Bernstein constants and uses $5k+1\le9k$. The exclusion of `k = 0` is essential to that power comparison; the separate velocity bound handles order zero.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_ve.summary: The parent scale controls all positive derivative orders

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_ve.text: Let $U_j$ be a smooth periodic stage on $[0,S_j]$, with $S_j>0$. For every nonnegative integer $q$, the formal statement represents $\partial_t^qU_j(t)$ as a continuous field on $\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$ with Fourier support at most $2\lambda_j^5$, for every $0\le t\le S_j$. Its periodic lift agrees pointwise with the time derivative at fixed physical position. Endpoint derivatives are taken within the stage interval, and no agreement is asserted outside it. This proves the velocity part of the Fourier-support claim after auxiliary Lemma 1.3. It does not supply the residual's larger band or a bound on the size of either field.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.exists_ve.summary: Every time derivative retains the stage cutoff

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.graphCofr.text: Takes the coframe order constant at `depth + 1`. That extra spatial derivative is needed when the finite hierarchy is evaluated on the physical graph and then placed in a Hölder norm at the cutoff depth. The definition does not itself prove any coframe estimate; the corresponding stage coefficient certificate supplies it.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.graphCofr.summary: The inverse-flow coefficient is read at one extra order

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.graphLeve.text: Multiplies the common level bound by the number of retained levels in `Finset.Icc 1 depth`. This scalar estimates finite sums when individual profile bounds are converted into a bound for the assembled field. At zero depth the interval is empty; physical stage estimates later require a nonempty hierarchy of depth at least two.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.graphLeve.summary: The retained levels contribute their number times one bound

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.norm_mean.text: Takes a supplied order-zero half-Hölder estimate for a pressure Hessian and derives a pointwise operator-norm bound with parent exponent $6r+2(a+1)+2$ and decay $\lambda^{-5/2}$. Positivity assumptions control all scalar enlargements. The proof explicitly extracts boundedness from the Hölder predicate before using its supremum, avoiding reliance on an unchecked total supremum.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.norm_mean.summary: The mean Hessian norm follows from its closed-slab Hölder bound

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.norm_stag.text: Assuming geometry caps, measured level bounds at orders one and two, a positive bounded active weight and inactivity outside the selected support, bounds the Hessian norm of the actual higher oscillatory pressure by a fixed parent power times $\lambda^{-5/12}$. The conclusion holds on the full slab, with inactivity supplying control before activation.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.norm_stag.summary: The actual higher pressure has decay of order five twelfths

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.norm_stag.text: From pressure-geometry caps and order-two measured bounds at levels $2$ through `H`, proves a global-in-space Hessian norm bound for the actual mean pressure. It sums the mean equations, uses phase independence to control physical graph norms, and applies the periodic Poisson multiplier estimate. The result has decay $\lambda^{-5/2}$ with an explicit fixed parent power.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.norm_stag.summary: The actual mean pressure has the required Hessian norm

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.ofTruncat.text: Builds the stage at index `n` from an actual truncated child and supplied scheduled bounds. Equalities `hSlab` and `hRadius` identify its time slab and cutoff radius with the induction parameters. Velocity size, flow deformation, residual size at the next frequency, and the cumulative upper pressure-Hessian bound are hypotheses. Smoothness, parity, spectrum, and the Poisson equation come from the child.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.ofTruncat.summary: Use the actual cutoff child as an inductive stage

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.ofTruncat.text: The pressure of the stage built from a truncated child is exactly the child’s Poisson pressure, under the constructor’s full hypotheses. Substituting the slab and cutoff-radius equalities makes this definitional. The theorem preserves the pressure used in the child equation; it does not derive the separately supplied pressure-Hessian estimate.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.ofTruncat.summary: The stage retains the cutoff child pressure

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.ofTruncat.text: Under the same slab, radius, and scheduled-bound inputs as the stage constructor, its velocity is exactly the velocity of the truncated child. The proof substitutes the index equalities and reduces definitions. This guards against accidentally proving induction estimates for a field different from the one produced by Fourier truncation.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.ofTruncat.summary: The stage retains the cutoff child velocity

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.periodic_.text: Proves spatial periodicity of the Euclidean lift at every real time. Integer translations have the same image in the unit torus, so the result follows directly from the quotient representation. No smoothness, endpoint nesting, or equation of motion is needed for this representation fact.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.periodic_.summary: The lifted stage respects all lattice translations

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.potential.text: Combines a supplied one-sided leading-pressure estimate with operator-norm bounds for higher and mean pressures of the same approximation. If the cost and exponent budgets dominate all three contributions, the Hessian of the canonical potential is bounded above by the parent's Hessian plus the scheduled $\lambda^{-1/4}$ term. The leading contribution remains a signed quadratic-form estimate throughout.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.potential.summary: The actual pressure increment has a common upper Hessian bound

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.residual.text: Defines the physical momentum residual using the actual stage velocity and pressure, with the time derivative taken within its closed slab. This ties the error estimate to a concrete Euler expression. The associated stage field `projected_eq` is what permits rewriting it as the Leray-projected momentum residual.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.residual.summary: The momentum error for the stored pressure

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.text: Given the scalar cost inequality and an exponent dominating the common residual exponent, bounds the tail graph factor and activation graph factor separately by $\Gamma\mathsf D^b$. Nonnegative costs justify dropping the other summand from the total, and $\mathsf D\ge1$ permits enlargement of powers. No residual field is estimated by this arithmetic lemma alone.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.summary: Each residual contribution fits the common step bound

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.text: Defines the common parent exponent as $2(\max(a,1)+1)+p$, where `p` is the primary activation loss. The first term accounts for the two graph derivatives needed by the residual Hölder estimate. The natural maximum ensures the formula remains defined at small radius exponents, though the selected construction uses much larger ones.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.summary: Two graph derivatives add to the activation parent loss

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.text: When the radius exponent is at least one, substituting the actual activation loss `a + 27` gives the common residual exponent $3a+29$. The proof simplifies the natural maximum and then uses arithmetic. It records precisely how the two derivative losses are added to the primary activation estimate.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.summary: The chosen activation loss gives exponent three a plus twenty-nine

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.text: Combines the order-two graph factor with both the measured depth-tail cost and the leading activation cost. This produces a scalar large enough for the two residual contributions once their signs are established. The remaining parent exponent and child-frequency decay are kept separate for absorption by the common numerical schedule.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.summary: The remainder and activation share one graph cost

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.text: Nonnegative hierarchy costs and nonnegative primary activation cost imply a nonnegative residual step cost. The coframe expression appears squared, so no positivity assumption on the coefficient function is needed for this sign theorem. Analytic uses of that coefficient still require their own bounds in the subsequent residual estimates.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.summary: The total residual prefactor is nonnegative

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.text: Reads `K` at $(P+1)+3P$, combines it with the hierarchy-level constant and counts the omitted quadratic pairs. The resulting prefactor bounds the order-two expansion remainder at the selected depth. Its definition preserves the actual combinatorial tail count, which is later identified with the cost produced by the profile recurrence theorem.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.summary: The tail cost uses the same derivative reserve

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.text: For depth at least two, the profile theorem's reserve $\max(P+1,3)+3P$ equals $(P+1)+3P$. Substituting this identity shows its order-two remainder prefactor is exactly `scheduledResidualTailCost`. This avoids choosing a second order table for the residual and keeps the velocity and residual estimates on the same schedule.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.summary: The velocity reserve already covers the order-two tail

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.text: If the hierarchy cost function `K` is pointwise nonnegative, the selected tail prefactor is nonnegative at every depth. The squared level factor and finite pair counts introduce no negative terms. This sign is needed when multiplying the tail estimate by graph constants and comparing it with the total step budget.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.summary: The residual tail prefactor is nonnegative

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.text: Adds the scalar factors for the first derivative at the origin of the higher oscillatory remainder and the mean correction. The constants $96$ and $24$ retain the two distinct derivative estimates. This prefactor is then placed inside the common step budget used to bound the central-gradient error.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.summary: The two central corrections have a common scalar cost

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.text: Under pointwise nonnegativity of the coefficient and hierarchy cost functions, proves nonnegativity of the common velocity step cost and every mean cost. The argument uses the lower bounds for the coframe and hierarchy-level constants. These sign facts allow an individual contribution to be bounded by the larger combined step sum.

Evaluates the hierarchy-level constant at derivative reserve $(P+1)+3P$ and depth $P$. This reserves enough derivative orders to read the velocity at the cutoff depth. The definition merely selects the scalar expression from an order-cost function `K`; its useful nonnegativity follows later from assumptions on that function.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.summary: The cutoff uses the reserved hierarchy-level constant

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.text: Defines the prefactor for the mean correction's order-`m` physical Hölder estimate at a fixed depth. The coframe and retained-level bounds enter together with the chain-rule factors for `m + 1` derivatives. The parent power and frequency decay are accounted for elsewhere, so this scalar is selected before the schedule absorbs them.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.summary: The mean correction has an explicit order cost

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.text: Combines the coframe constant, retained-level count and chain-rule factors into the oscillatory velocity prefactor at the selected depth. Frequency and parent powers are kept outside this scalar. It is subsequently included in the common step cost, allowing the schedule to dominate all fixed-depth constants before any inductive stage is chosen.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.summary: The oscillatory graph has an explicit cutoff-depth cost

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.text: Multiplies the parent Bernstein constant at the chosen depth by $3(P+1)$. This is the fixed-order factor needed to bound the parent's Hölder norm from its uniform jets. The numerical schedule later ensures that this factor is small relative to the parent frequency; the definition alone gives no such absorption.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.summary: The parent Bernstein estimate has a fixed-depth prefactor

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.text: Adds four scalar contributions: the full-depth oscillatory cost, the full-depth mean cost, the supremum profile-sum cost and the central derivative cost. Each term is bounded by this sum once nonnegativity has been established. The resulting scalar becomes one part of the schedule's total step entry, alongside residual, pressure and flow costs.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.summary: One step cost covers the required velocity estimates

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.text: Assume `f ≥ 1`, nonnegative `K`, `2 * K ≤ f`, and `f² ≤ g`. Then $Kf^5g^{-3}\le1/2$. This converts the Fourier differentiation factor and next-frequency residual decay into the derivative budget used by `OnSlab`. Positivity of the denominators follows from the hypotheses; it is not supplied by total division.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.scheduled.summary: The residual derivative fits the half-unit budget

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.slabTimeJ.text: For a positive-length stage slab, the first fixed-point time derivative of the velocity equals its residual minus the periodic Leray projection of its advection. The proof uses the stage’s divergence-free condition to identify the tensor-divergence nonlinearity, then obtains an actual within-time derivative from projected momentum. The equality holds at both slab endpoints.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.slabTimeJ.summary: The first stage time derivative obeys the Leray equation

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.slabTimeJ.text: The order-$q+1$ velocity time derivative equals the order-$q$ residual derivative minus the Leray projection of the order-$q$ advection derivative. The stage slab must have positive length, and evaluation stays in it. The proof commutes time differentiation with the actual periodic projection. Expanding the advection into its binomial products is a separate theorem.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.slabTimeJ.summary: The next velocity derivative uses one lower residual derivative

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.slabTimeJ.text: For a smooth periodic stage on a positive interval $[0,S_j]$ and an integer $q\ge0$, the formal statement proves $\partial_t^{q+1}U_j=\partial_t^qR_j-\mathbb P\sum_{i=0}^q\binom qi((\partial_t^iU_j)\cdot\nabla)\partial_t^{q-i}U_j$. The identity holds at every spatial point and every time, with endpoint derivatives taken from within the slab. The stage equations already give incompressibility, so the advection sum is the divergence of the tensor sum in the paper. The auxiliary display is this formula with its positive time order written as $q+1$. No time derivative of the residual of order $q+1$ is required.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.slabTimeJ.summary: The next velocity derivative uses the preceding residual

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.slabTimeJ.text: At time order zero, the velocity is bounded by its stage frequency and the residual by the next frequency to the power $-5/2$, provided the stage frequency is at least one. The stage already carries a stronger residual bound with exponent $-3$; monotonicity for the next frequency, also at least one, gives the displayed weakening.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.slabTimeJ.summary: The undifferentiated stage already satisfies the base bounds

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.smooth_st.text: For an inductive Euler stage with a positive slab endpoint, its residual is jointly smooth on the closed slab. The theorem applies the closed-slab momentum-residual regularity result to the stage’s bundled velocity and pressure smoothness. It verifies the regularity of the actual residual definition before time derivatives and Fourier estimates are applied.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.smooth_st.summary: The actual stage residual is jointly smooth

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageCoef.text: This order-only quantity multiplies the number of admissible mixed derivative words by the sum of `C j` through order `m`. It converts bounds on individual parent derivatives into a bound on the exact finite seminorm. Parent powers, radius factors, and frequency are excluded from the definition and remain visible in the estimates.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageCoef.summary: A finite allowance for every coefficient word

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageCoef.text: If every parent coefficient constant `C j` is nonnegative, the finite coefficient-order allowance is nonnegative. The proof uses the nonnegative cardinality of admissible words and a sum of nonnegative constants. This sign fact is required when multiplying the allowance by parent powers or by a seminorm.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageCoef.summary: Nonnegative parent constants give a nonnegative allowance

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageCofr.text: The definition takes one plus the sum of `C j` through order `m`. It provides a single allowance for all coframe jets up to that order when reading a profile on the Eulerian graph. The added one ensures a lower bound of one once the supplied derivative constants are nonnegative.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageCofr.summary: A common coframe allowance through the requested order

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageCofr.text: Under nonnegativity of the sequence `C`, adding its finite partial sum to one gives a value at least one. The proof is the direct sum inequality. This supplies a convenient positive lower bound for later coframe and flow constants without claiming that any individual derivative is nonzero.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageCofr.summary: The common coframe allowance is at least one

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageHigh.text: Defines the scalar prefactor for the Hessian norm of the summed higher oscillatory pressure. It depends on the number of retained higher levels, their common bound and the fixed geometry constant. The separate parent exponent and frequency decay are supplied by the later analytic theorem, not by this definition.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageHigh.summary: The higher oscillatory pressure has a fixed-order scalar cost

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageMean.text: Defines the scalar prefactor for the mean pressure Hessian from the norm of the pressure-Hessian multiplier, the squared coframe constant, the number of mean levels, their common bound and the parent gradient constant. The multiplier norm is retained explicitly. Parent-scale powers and the $\lambda^{-5/2}$ decay are not part of this scalar.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageMean.summary: The mean pressure cost includes the Poisson multiplier norm

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageMean.text: Rearranges the squared coframe factor and mean-profile bound into a scalar prefactor times one parent power and the frequency decay. The equality holds for arbitrary real scalar inputs. Its purpose is to keep the order-two geometric constant outside the exponent, preserving the required independence of the schedule's parent-loss exponent.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageMean.summary: The mean graph constant stays outside the parent power

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stagePare.text: For a smooth velocity with first and second derivatives bounded by $R\mathsf D^j$, where $R\ge0$ and $\mathsf D\ge1$, proves the gradient has order-zero half-Hölder norm at most $3R\mathsf D^2$. The first jet bounds the supremum and the second supplies variation. This is a Euclidean estimate and does not require converting the field to a torus Fourier representation.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stagePare.summary: Two velocity jets control the gradient Hölder norm

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stagePres.text: Adds the leading signed-Hessian coefficient to the higher oscillatory and mean-Hessian coefficients at the selected depth. Both higher costs use the number of levels from two to the depth, so they vanish for an empty higher sum. With sign assumptions, each contribution is dominated by the combined cost used in the schedule.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stagePres.summary: The leading higher and mean pressure costs are added

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stagePres.text: Nonnegative geometry, parent, level and leading coefficients imply a nonnegative total pressure cost at every natural depth. The operator norm in the mean cost and the finite level count are already nonnegative. This supports the later comparison of the sum of three parent-scaled contributions with one common step bound.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stagePres.summary: The combined pressure cost is nonnegative

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stagePres.text: Takes the maximum of the leading-pressure exponent, the higher oscillatory exponent and the mean-pressure exponent. The latter two are explicit functions of the radius exponent and recurrence loss. This number allows all three pressure contributions to be enlarged to a common parent power once the parent scale is at least one.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stagePres.summary: One parent exponent covers all three pressure terms

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stagePres.text: If `a ≥ 24`, `r ≥ 9` and the leading-pressure exponent is no larger than $6r+2(a+1)+2$, the maximum defining the total pressure exponent equals that mean exponent. The proof compares natural-number expressions. It documents when the explicit maximum can be simplified, rather than assuming the leading term is automatically smaller.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stagePres.summary: The mean exponent dominates once the parameters are large enough

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stagePres.text: Restricts a jointly smooth field on a closed time slab to a fixed time belonging to that slab. Since the spatial domain is all of Euclidean space, the result is globally smooth in the spatial variable. This supplies ordinary spatial derivatives in the pressure estimates, including at the temporal endpoints.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stagePres.summary: A smooth slab field has smooth spatial slices

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stagePres.text: If each field at a retained mean level is fixed by the hierarchy's averaging operator, then their finite sum is phase independent. Linearity of the average first shows that the sum is also fixed; the phase-independence theorem then applies. The statement remains valid for an empty level set, where the sum is zero.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stagePres.summary: A finite sum of mean fields stays phase independent

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageSour.text: The source cost is $6Q_m^2$ times the coefficient-order constant. The factor covers the three spatial rows and the extra factor two from subtracting a phase average. The definition collects only order-dependent constants; the next theorem supplies the fixed parent power and the fast frequency factor.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageSour.summary: One order constant covers both advection estimates

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stageSour.text: When the derivative-constant sequence is nonnegative, the combined slow and fast source cost is nonnegative. The proof multiplies the nonnegative squared product constant by the already nonnegative coefficient allowance. It supplies the sign required when increasing the common order cost in the recurrence.

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stage_fre.text: If the initial stage frequency is at least four, every later frequency is at least that initial value. Each next frequency is at least twice its predecessor and at least its square. These inequalities follow from `InductiveEulerParameters` and make the fixed numerical residual and coercivity budgets valid at every stage.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.stage_fre.summary: The stage frequencies dominate their predecessors and squares

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.velocity.text: Lifts this particular stage’s continuous torus velocity through `toUnitTorus`. Its dependence on the stage parameters remains in the source record, while its resulting type is the common `Velocity` function type. Differential operators later act on this lift, with regularity inherited only on the certified closed time slab.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStage.velocity.summary: The Euclidean representative of one torus velocity

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.text: Packages a single frequency schedule, activation times, torus velocities, residuals and oscillatory increments. Its fields certify smoothness, oddness, divergence, Fourier support and the actual projected momentum equation. The correction bounds hold only through `order (n + 1)`. This record supplies the limit argument; it does not itself construct a family or include the matching central waves.

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.HasTermi.text: For the sequence of periodic stages, this condition requires that, for every pair of nonnegative integers $(m,q)$, all sufficiently large $j$ satisfy $\|\partial_t^q(U_j-U_{j-1}-O_j)(t)\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le\lambda_j^{-1}$ for every $t\in[0,S_j]$. The derivative fixes the spatial point and uses the closed child interval. Its starting stage may depend on both orders. The condition also requires finiteness of the formal spatial Hölder measurement, whose defining formula is not included in the packet. Unlike the full auxiliary Lemma 1.2, this condition alone contains no continuity of the time curve in that spatial norm. It records an assumption on a sequence rather than proving that the sequence satisfies it.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.HasTermi.summary: Each fixed pair of orders has a starting stage

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.StageMix.text: On the child slab, take the fixed-spatial-point time derivative of `velocity (n+1) - velocity n - oscillation (n+1)`. This predicate requires spatial half-Hölder membership at order `m` and norm at most the inverse child frequency at every time. The variables `q,m,n` specify one order pair and stage; eventual quantifiers occur in later auxiliary statements.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.StageMix.summary: The exact mixed increment of two consecutive stages

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.StageTim.text: At a specified stage $j$, for nonnegative integers $q$ and $\psi$, the formal condition requires $|\partial_t^iU_j(t,x)|\le\lambda_j^\psi$ and $|\partial_t^iR_j(t,x)|\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-5/2}$ for all $i\le q$, $t\in[0,S_j]$ and $x\in\mathbb R^3$. Fields are the periodic lifts, and time derivatives are taken at fixed $x$ within the closed interval. These are uniform pointwise inequalities. The condition does not choose $\psi$, assert validity at later stages, or require continuity in the spatial supremum norm. Those additional conclusions belong to auxiliary Lemma 1.3. The exponent $\psi$ is a nonnegative integer.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.StageTim.summary: Velocity and residual share one prescribed time order

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.Terminal.text: For a fixed sequence, this condition asks for two implications at sufficiently large stages. First, bounds $|\partial_t^iU_j|\le\lambda_j^\psi$ and $|\partial_t^iR_j|\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-5/2}$ for $i\le q$ must imply the corresponding child bounds through order $q+1$, with a new integer exponent depending on $q,\psi$. Second, for every fixed $m$, those parent bounds must imply $\|\partial_t^{q+1}(U_{j+1}-U_j-O_{j+1})\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-1}$ on the child interval. Both starting indices may depend on the indicated orders. This packages the analytic induction hypotheses; it does not prove them or explicitly state a formula for the child's residual.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.Terminal.summary: Advancing time order requires two separate estimates

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.correcti.text: Extracts a pointwise bound for the order `m` iterated Fréchet derivative of the nonoscillatory correction. The hypothesis `hm` restricts `m` to the scheduled order, and `ht` restricts time to the child slab. The proof uses the accompanying half-Hölder regularity certificate to justify reading the finite norm as a derivative bound.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.correcti.summary: The correction controls each spatial derivative

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.eventual.text: For all sufficiently large stages, bounds the derivative of the lifted velocity at the origin by the ninth power of that stage frequency, throughout its closed slab. Bernstein bounds use the stored Fourier support and velocity norm. The conclusion is eventual in the stage index, not an assertion that every stage satisfies this bound under `hinit` alone.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.eventual.summary: The older central gradient has a polynomial bound

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.eventual.text: Assume that the inverse stage frequencies tend to zero and that, for every fixed $(m,q)$, the correction after removing $O_j$ eventually has formal $C^{m,1/2}$ bound $\lambda_j^{-1}$ on $[0,S_j]$. For each $c\in\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3$, the formal statement gives one radius $r>0$ such that $D_x^m\partial_t^q(U_j-U_{j-1})$ has operator norm at most $\lambda_j^{-1}$ on $\overline B(c,r)\times[0,S_j]$ for all sufficiently large $j$. The starting index may depend on $(m,q)$, but the ball does not. The lattice is removed because it represents the single torus origin. This is a local derivative estimate for full increments, not the compact-set support statement itself.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.eventual.summary: One spatial neighborhood works for every derivative order

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.frequenc.text: Under `hinit`, proves that the next frequency is at least the current frequency raised to the natural power 288. The scheduled exponent is at least 320, so this deliberately weaker exponent follows by monotonicity of powers above one. It later absorbs the older gradient into a much smaller power of the next scale.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.frequenc.summary: Successive frequencies dominate a fixed large power

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.frequenc.text: Bounds four times the logarithm of frequency `i + 3` by the square of the logarithm at index `i`. The record supplies the threshold floor and maximal-order rule used by the schedule lemma. This is an algebraic scheduling estimate; it does not require adding a new base-frequency hypothesis to this declaration.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.frequenc.summary: Three later frequencies obey the logarithmic bound

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.frequenc.text: Carries the lower bound two from the initial frequency to arbitrary index `n`. The proof combines `hinit` with frequency monotonicity. This small fact supplies positivity for inverses, real powers and logarithms; it should not be read as a separate analytic estimate on a stage velocity.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.frequenc.summary: Every frequency exceeds the initial floor

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.frequenc.text: With `hinit : 2 ≤ s.frequency 0`, the power recurrence makes the full frequency sequence monotone. The exponent parameter already has a positive lower bound in the record. This is a schedule consequence, independent of the velocity fields, and is repeatedly used to transfer a base-frequency threshold to every later stage.

For inductive stage data whose initial frequency is at least two, every next frequency is at least the square of the current one. The proof uses monotonicity and the stored power recurrence, whose exponent is at least two. This is the growth estimate supplied to the terminal convergence construction; it does not itself prove convergence or divergence of a physical norm.

Weakens the power-288 growth estimate to the square-gap inequality needed by the abstract summability lemmas. The base-frequency hypothesis guarantees that powers are monotone in their exponent. This theorem connects the actual schedule to the generic convergence machinery without using any properties of the constructed fields.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.frequenc.summary: The frequencies grow at least quadratically

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.frequenc.text: Shows convergence of `s.frequency` to positive infinity in the `atTop` filter, assuming the initial frequency is at least two. The result follows from the prescribed power recurrence. It supports eventual absorption of fixed constants and shrinking localization radii, rather than asserting any finite numerical cutoff index.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.frequenc.summary: The frequency sequence escapes every bound

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.order_te.text: Proves that the scheduled orders tend to infinity, using the maximal admissible-order rule and divergence of the frequencies. A fixed threshold can eventually be met, so no derivative order is permanently excluded. The theorem needs `hinit`; it is the schedule fact that turns finitely many estimates at each stage into all-order convergence.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.order_te.summary: Every finite derivative order is eventually available

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.paper_pr.text: Assume a compatible inductive sequence with its stated regularity, residual and increment bounds, initial frequency $\lambda_0\ge2$, and activation times tending to $T>0$. Every stage must be defined at least through $T$. The formal theorem supplies a smooth odd periodic Euler solution on $[0,T)$, convergence of the initial data and uniform convergence in spatial $C^{m,1/2}$ on each $[0,S]$ with $S<T$. It also gives uniform velocity convergence on $[0,T]$ and a continuous terminal velocity. Any maximal solution from the same initial datum has lifespan at least $T$ and agrees before $T$. Equality with the maximal lifespan is not asserted here. The spatial Hölder norm sums the supremum and one-half Hölder seminorm of derivatives through order $m$.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.paper_pr.summary: Stage estimates imply smooth convergence before accumulation

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.periodic.text: Proves invariance of the lifted stage velocity under every integer lattice translation, for any stage and any real time. This uses the quotient map rather than the stage smoothness assumptions. It lets later estimates on a fundamental cell be transported to the whole Euclidean lift of the torus.

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.stageMix.text: Let $U_j$ and $O_j$ belong to the common stage sequence, and suppose $m\le q_j$, where $q_j$ is its retained spatial order. The formal statement gives finiteness of the spatial Hölder measurement and $\|U_j-U_{j-1}-O_j\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le\lambda_j^{-1}$ at every time in $[0,S_j]$. This is auxiliary Lemma 1.2 at time order zero, obtained directly from the existing correction estimate. The formal indexing uses the child of stage $j-1$. Time continuity in the spatial norm is not part of this particular conclusion. The defining formula of that spatial norm is absent from the packet; its stated interpretation is $C^{m,1/2}$.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.stageMix.summary: The main induction already supplies the base case

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.stageTim.text: Suppose that at stage $j$ every time derivative through order $q$ satisfies $|\partial_t^iU_j(t,x)|\le\lambda_j^\psi$ and $|\partial_t^iR_j(t,x)|\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-5/2}$ throughout $[0,S_j]\times\mathbb R^3$. For each $i\le q$ and each time in that interval, the formal statement proves the same two bounds after taking the supremum over $x$. The derivatives are at fixed physical position and include the one-sided endpoint values. The pointwise upper bounds make these suprema finite. This supplies the spatial norm inequalities in auxiliary equation (1.3); it does not supply time continuity, choose the exponent, or prove eventual validity along the sequence.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.stageTim.summary: Taking the spatial supremum preserves both inequalities

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.stageTim.text: Assume every frequency of the common stage sequence is at least one. Then, at every stage $j$, the formal statement proves $|U_j(t,x)|\le\lambda_j$ and $|R_j(t,x)|\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-5/2}$ on $[0,S_j]\times\mathbb R^3$. The first inequality is the stage velocity bound. The second follows from the stronger existing residual bound $\lambda_{j+1}^{-3}$ because $\lambda_{j+1}\ge1$. Thus the pointwise part of auxiliary Lemma 1.3 starts with $\psi_0=1$. The paper also includes continuity in the spatial supremum norm; that assertion is supplied separately and is not proved by these two inequalities alone.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.stageTim.summary: The initial exponent can be chosen as one

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.terminal.text: Fix a common stage sequence with $\lambda_j\ge1$ and $q_j\to\infty$. Assume that, eventually at every fixed time order, the parent velocity-residual bounds imply both the next child time bounds and the mixed correction bound. Then the formal statement proves: for each $q$ there is an integer $\psi_q$ such that $|\partial_t^iU_j|\le\lambda_j^{\psi_q}$ and $|\partial_t^iR_j|\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-5/2}$ for all $i\le q$ and all sufficiently large $j$; and for every fixed $(m,q)$ the correction after removing $O_j$ eventually has spatial Hölder bound $\lambda_j^{-1}$. All bounds hold throughout the appropriate closed stage intervals. The analytic implications are hypotheses, and time continuity in the stated norms remains separate.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.terminal.summary: Two induction hypotheses give both eventual bounds

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.terminal.text: Let $T>0$ and let the stage intervals be nested with $S_j\ge T$. Assume $\lambda_0\ge2$, $\lambda_{j+1}\ge\lambda_j^2$, and the eventual mixed correction bound of size $\lambda_j^{-1}$ at every fixed pair of orders. Suppose also that $U_j$ converges uniformly to $u$ on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$. The formal statement proves joint smoothness of $u$ on $[0,T]\times(\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3)$, interpreted with derivatives up to the time boundary. Periodic lattice translates of the origin are all removed. The result concerns this given uniform limit and does not independently construct it. It concludes smoothness; uniform convergence of its derivatives is stated in the separate local result.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.terminal.summary: Summable mixed increments yield joint boundary regularity

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.terminal.text: Assume $T>0$, nested stage intervals containing $[0,T]$, $\lambda_0\ge2$, $\lambda_{j+1}\ge\lambda_j^2$, and eventual mixed correction bounds $\lambda_j^{-1}$ at every fixed pair of orders. Let $U_j\to u$ uniformly on the closed common slab. For every $c\notin\mathbb Z^3$, the formal statement finds $r>0$ such that $u$ is jointly smooth on $[0,T]\times\overline B(c,r)$ and every joint space-time derivative of $U_j$ converges uniformly there to the corresponding derivative of $u$. Derivatives on this closed cylinder are taken within it, including at $T$. The same radius works for all orders. This supplies the local derivative convergence required before extending the velocity through the terminal time.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.terminal.summary: The same local cylinder works at every order

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.terminal.text: Assume `hLimit` gives uniform convergence of the stage velocities on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$, every stage slab contains $[0,T]$, and the slabs decrease. If `hJoint` bounds each joint derivative of consecutive increments by an order-dependent summable `weight`, then $u$ is jointly smooth on $[0,T]\times\overline B(c,r)$ and its derivatives are uniform limits there. Both `T` and `r` must be positive.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.terminal.summary: Stage increments give all derivatives on a terminal cylinder

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStages.velocity.text: Reads stage `n` on Euclidean space by composing its continuous torus velocity with `toUnitTorus`. This is the function used by the differential operators in the limit construction. The definition is meaningful at every real time, although smoothness and quantitative estimates are only supplied on the recorded stage slab.

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStep.text: Describes a successor of one exact tip. It stores the physical comparison, chosen crossing, new child and linking wave, with equalities identifying preceding and current wave pairs. The clock endpoint, gain ratio and comparison smallness bounds are also fields. These links are required before the step can be appended to a compatible prefix.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStep.summary: A new stage tied to its selected physical crossing

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStep.ofLaterWav.text: Builds a successor record from a later physical window, a selected crossing, a certified child and a wave linking the parent to that child. The hypotheses `hk` and `ha` identify the selected pair with the linking wave. The constructor assembles existing data; it does not manufacture the child estimates from a comparison alone.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStep.ofLaterWav.summary: Attach a selected comparison to its actual child

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStep.ofPhysical.text: Given a certified preceding prefix, later-wave selection, and an actual cutoff child, builds `InductiveEulerStep`. It derives crossing strength from the scheduled gain and exit coupling from the prefix, then combines them with the supplied oscillation, support, correction, central-error, and cutoff estimates. The new step therefore uses the same selected wave and physical child throughout.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStep.ofPhysical.summary: Close the later step with the same selected wave

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStep.parent_gra.text: On the next active slab, identifies the physical amplification gradient with the central derivative of the current parent velocity. The previous wave is fully switched on there. Rewriting its stored gradient splitting and the preceding pair and error equalities gives the identity, which is needed to interpret the next coupling physically.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStep.parent_gra.summary: The comparison gradient is the actual parent gradient

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStep.scheduledP.text: Packages the completed step as an `IsScheduledPhysicalCrossing` between the exit couplings of two exact tips, with their scheduled ratios. The proof uses `parent_gradient` at the crossing time. This prevents the coupling recurrence from being applied to a comparison matrix unrelated to the retained Euler stage.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStep.scheduledP.summary: The stored successor transports the scheduled couplings

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStep.tip.text: Forms the next tip from a completed successor step. The current parent becomes the older stage, the newly constructed child becomes the parent, and the crossing supplies the next activation. Nonnegativity and slab containment come from the previous tip and lifetime estimates, retaining the exact physical objects already constructed.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerStep.tip.summary: Appending a step advances the exact pair of stages

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerSuccessor.text: Abbreviates the local extension requirement: every index, exact tip and certified prefix ending there admits a successor step. The result is `Nonempty`, so this statement supplies existence rather than a preselected function. Requiring a compatible prefix is weaker and more appropriate than demanding a successor for arbitrary isolated tip data.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerSuccessor.summary: A local successor for every compatible finite history

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.text: Holds the older stage at index `n`, its child at index `n + 1`, and the completed wave that connects them. It also records the next activation selected by that wave. Nonnegative current activation and containment of the current endpoint in the older slab are explicit fields, preparing the next local construction.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.summary: Two consecutive stages and their next activation

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.LaterSelect.text: For a compatible window `w`, this abbreviation fixes the later-wave selection to the parent velocity, the schedule’s comparison constant and half-length, the next frequency, the following logarithmic gain, and parent scale. It keeps all those parameters tied to one tip. It does not by itself assert that such a crossing has been selected.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.LaterSelect.summary: The crossing problem with the next scheduled frequency

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.LaterWindow.text: This abbreviation fixes `LaterPhysicalWindow` to the older and parent velocities, the preceding wave vector and amplitude, its error, and the next scheduled time interval at tip `p`. It is a type of compatible comparison data, not a selected window. The actual window is supplied in `SelectedLaterInput`.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.LaterWindow.summary: The comparison window over the actual two preceding stages

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: This structure ties together a positive endpoint at most one, a sufficiently large parent frequency, a physical comparison window and crossing, a nonzero transported carrier, a restricted parent chart, and a local seed with regularity and even amplitude. Its fields ensure every subsequent physical profile uses the same wave and parent. No quantitative hierarchy bound is contained here.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: One selected wave and its compatible parent geometry

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: Defines the selected activation interval from `tip.nextActivation` to the smaller of the stage endpoint and one switching time later. This clipping makes the support set lie in the actual active slab. The positive rate is stored in `d.window.physical`, and the selected regularity gives an active interval of positive length.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The activation ramp clipped to the stage interval

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: The ramp attached to the selected later input is a closed subset of the real line because it is a closed interval. This topological fact is used when differentiating a field known to vanish outside the ramp: its complement is open, so the field remains zero in a neighborhood of every off-ramp time.

Every time in `activationRamp` belongs to the interval from the next activation time to the child-stage endpoint. The lower endpoints agree, and the ramp’s upper endpoint is a minimum bounded by that stage endpoint. This inclusion permits weighted estimates proved only on the active slab to be applied on the switch support.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The clipped ramp stays in the active slab

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: At a time `t` on the selected physical slab but outside $[t_0,t_0+1/r]$, the sum of `leadingSwitch` and `completionSwitch` is zero at every label and independent phase. The selected wave supplies $r>0$. The proof uses the exact activation-source formula and vanishing of the scalar switch derivative. This declaration states a value identity, not vanishing of every higher time derivative.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The activation source vanishes outside its switch interval

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: Within the actual child slab, the sum of the leading switch profile and its completion switch profile is zero outside the selected activation ramp. The proof evaluates the exact wrapped profiles and shows their shared scalar factor, the derivative of the wave switch, is zero. This is a support statement for the selected activation residual, not a norm estimate.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The combined activation residual vanishes off the ramp

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: This definition builds the physical approximation using the selected leading input, the actual parent pressure and residual, the stored duration bound, and the scheduled depth. It does not select alternative coefficients or a second wave. The subsequent properties theorem applies the general qualitative assembly to this precise approximation.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The selected hierarchy over the same restricted parent

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: This accessor returns the carrier formed from the selected crossing and parent launch deformation. Its mathematical guarantees come from the `carrier_nonzero`, `carrier_transport`, and `carrier_bound` fields of the same `SelectedLaterInput`. Keeping this accessor avoids accidentally using a carrier from a different selection when constructing twisted profiles.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The constant label covector of the selected wave

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: The selected carrier equals the adjoint of the parent flow derivative at the origin and activation, applied to the selected crossing’s wave vector there. The equality is definitional: the selected input was built with this carrier. It identifies the frequency in the label phase with the same physical wave used in the center equations.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The carrier is the pulled-back activation covector

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: The selected crossing’s wave vector and amplitude satisfy `CenterWaveOn` for the parent gradient at the origin, on the active slab and with the ninth-power parent scale. The proof is the stored `selection.center` field. This declaration exposes existing selected data; it does not solve another differential equation or select a different pair.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The selected pair already satisfies the central wave equations

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: The same center wave satisfies the center equations written along the parent trajectory of the zero label, with its wave vector replaced by the transported carrier. The parent-flow transport theorem uses launch membership and the carrier’s adjoint formula. The amplitude and active interval remain exactly those of the original selected crossing.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The central equations use the transported label covector

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: The weight at time `t` is the norm of the selected crossing amplitude multiplied by the child frequency to power $3/4$. It is defined for every real time, while its positivity, regularity, and upper bound are proved on the active slab. This is the same center weight used in the measured hierarchy and the switching estimate.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The central amplitude determines the hierarchy weight

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: This theorem extracts continuity of `centerWeight` on the active slab from `centerWeight_properties`. It supplies the exact continuity proof required when defining amplitude-weighted seminorms of the selected hierarchy. The conclusion concerns this restricted interval; it does not assert global continuity of an arbitrarily extended crossing amplitude.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The active weight has continuous time dependence

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: The selected normalized weight is at most one at every active time, directly by the packaged weight properties. This allows amplitude bounds to control ordinary profile sizes when the oscillatory profile is inactive before launch. The theorem does not provide the stronger exponentially small bound needed during the initial switching interval.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: Peak normalization bounds the active weight by one

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: At every time in the selected active interval, `centerWeight` is strictly positive. The proof projects the positivity component of `centerWeight_properties`; no new nonvanishing argument is carried out here. This prevents division by zero in the amplitude-weighted norms used for the selected hierarchy and leading-seed estimate.

On the active slab the selected weight is continuous, strictly positive, at most one, and has a continuous within-derivative. The proof obtains continuity of the parent gradient from its joint smoothness and applies the normalized-weight theorem for the selected center solution. The derivative assertion is restricted to the closed active interval, including its endpoints.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The active weight is positive, bounded, and differentiable

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: At each time in the active slab, the selected crossing amplitude has norm at most the child frequency to power $-3/4$. The proof identifies the physical crossing’s active interval with the scheduled slab and applies its attained-peak property. This is the actual normalized crossing, rather than an independently postulated amplitude bound.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The selected peak bounds every active amplitude

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: The central error is defined as the sum of the derivative at the origin of the higher oscillatory remainder and the derivative of the mean correction. It excludes both the parent gradient and the leading rank-one wave. The following splitting theorem identifies this exact quantity inside the gradient of the untruncated approximation.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The central derivative contributed by the corrections

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: The selected child frequency is at least one because the schedule makes it a natural power of the parent frequency, already at least two. This local consequence permits monotonic comparison of its real powers. It neither changes the schedule nor supplies the stronger initial-frequency thresholds used for activation and cutoff estimates.

The stored completion switch is definitionally the finite hierarchy solver’s completion of the leading switch force. This exact equality prevents a mismatch between the activation correction and the curl operator used at later levels. It is the cancellation premise that lets the level-two relay reduce to a homogeneous relay.
TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.summary: The activation completion uses the hierarchy’s curl operator

TorusEuler.InductiveEulerTip.SelectedLat.text: For a certified prefix and initial frequency at least $e^4$, the parent gradient in the selected wave’s frame has its first coupling between $\pi$ and $4\pi$.
