TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.labelWordNorm.text: For ℓ≥0 and smooth c, this groups the weighted label-word norm by word length. It is ∑_{m≤n}ℓ^m times the sum of the unit-direction suprema at order m. The same algebraic identity handles ordinary and half-Hölder values. No boundedness is assumed, so the identity remains an identity of the total real-valued expressions even when a constituent supremum is a default; actual norm estimates still require finiteness predicates.
TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.labelWordNorm.summary: The weighted word sum grouped by derivative order

TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.phaseAverage.text:
At each time and label this returns ∫₀¹ f(t,a,s) ds, viewed as a profile constant in s. It is the paper’s 〈f〉. The operation uses a Bochner interval integral and is defined for all functions and real normed target spaces; its analytic interpretation therefore requires integrability and, for nontrivial vector integration, completeness.

Default-value audit (b4): A Bochner integral can return zero if the integrand is not integrable, and in Mathlib it also uses a zero convention without a complete target. The definition itself assumes neither integrability nor CompleteSpace. In the (D.5) clause of Statement.lemma_D_1, CompleteSpace E is explicit and FieldNormFinite with γ>0 gives smooth, hence continuous, phase slices on every compact interval; these rule out the defaults. Phase periodicity is separately required there. No ENNReal.toReal occurs.

TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.phaseInverse.text:
This first forms s↦∫₀ˢ f(t,a,σ)dσ and then subtracts its average over one phase period. For continuous 1-periodic f with zero phase mean, it is the zero-mean periodic primitive denoted ∂_s^{−1}f. It is not an algebraic inverse on arbitrary functions; zero mean and periodicity are hypotheses of the analytic primitive clause, not of this definition.

Default-value audit (b4): Both the inner primitive and the outer mean are Bochner interval integrals, so nonintegrability or an incomplete target can collapse them to zero. Statement.lemma_D_1 assumes CompleteSpace, smooth finite-norm slices, periodicity and zero mean for the inverse bound. These make the integrals genuine and give the intended periodic primitive. Without zero mean the defined primitive need not be periodic, even when all integrals exist. There is no division by the mean.

TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.phasePartial.text:
This applies the derivative of f(t,a,s) in the fourth coordinate, the unit s direction. The label and time are held fixed. It is the ∂_s operation appearing in the finite norm and Lemma D.1; the definition itself does not impose periodicity or smoothness.

Default-value audit (b4): As for labelPartial, the underlying fderiv is total and may be zero for a nonsmooth function. The analytic clauses use FieldNormFinite, including smoothness in (a,s), and positive γ when weighted. Periodicity is separately needed for the phase-average/primitive clauses, not for taking this derivative.

TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.weighted.text:
This is f/γ, implemented as scalar multiplication of each spatial/phase slice by (γ(t))⁻¹. The weight depends only on time, so label and phase derivatives do not differentiate it. The arbitrary time type permits restriction to any desired slab without changing the definition.

Default-value audit (b4): At γ(t)=0 the inverse is zero, so the whole slice is sent to zero and its weighted norm can vanish for a nonzero field. Positivity of γ at every time is an explicit hypothesis of Lemma D.1 and is inherited from the positive seed weight in the applications. The definition alone imposes no guard. No square root or supremum is evaluated here.
TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.weighted.summary: Division by the time dependent amplitude weight

TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.weightedField.text: For a field $f(t,a,s)$ and a time-dependent scalar $\gamma(t)$, this expression is the mixed finite norm of $f(t,a,s)/\gamma(t)$: it sums $\ell_*^{|\beta|}h^j\sup|\partial_a^\beta\partial_s^j(f/\gamma)|$ over $|\beta|+j\le n$. All suprema include the chosen time set, labels and phases; only labels and phases are differentiated. The paper assumes $\gamma(t)>0$ on $[t_0,T]$, and the numbered estimates impose that assumption. The definition alone allows zero weights: at a time with $\gamma(t)=0$, the normalized field is assigned zero. Thus the expression alone cannot certify the paper's positive-amplitude normalization or the finiteness of its derivative bounds.
TorusEuler.Paper.AppendixD.weightedField.summary: Divides the field by its time-dependent amplitude

TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.MixedIncrementBound.text: Fix a stage $j$ and nonnegative integers $m,q$. Set $w(t,x)=\partial_t^q(U_j-U_{j-1}-O_j)(t,x)$, differentiating at fixed $x$ within $[0,S_j]$. The formal condition requires finiteness of the spatial Hölder measurement, its bound $\|w(t)\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le\lambda_j^{-1}$ for every $t$, and continuity of $t\mapsto w(t)$ in that norm. Thus it includes the meaning of the time-space norm in auxiliary equation (1.2), not merely a pointwise estimate. The spatial norm's defining formula is absent; accompanying comments describe operator norms of spatial derivatives. At $j=0$, the predecessor index is also zero because natural-number subtraction stops at zero. The auxiliary lemma uses this condition only eventually.
TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.MixedIncrementBound.summary: The estimate includes continuity in the spatial norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.Proof.theorem_1_1_o.text: Assume Theorem 7.1, Propositions 8.1, 8.2 and 8.4, Corollary 8.3, and the generalized mixed estimate for every qualifying construction. For each cutoff symbol and integer $a_0$, the conclusion chooses integers $b\ge1$, $a\ge a_0$ and majorants $F,G$. Thresholds satisfying the main conditions for $F$ and $G(7K(s))\le\mathcal B(s)$, with $K(s)=320b(s+1)$, exist; every such threshold yields a solution for all sufficiently large initial frequencies. The solution has bounded velocity, the main vorticity blow-up and integral conclusions, uniqueness among maximal solutions of finite lifespan with the same initial data, and a smooth periodic velocity extension through its terminal time off $\mathbb Z^3$. Euler is imposed only before that time. This is a proved implication. The supplied files explicitly leave its generalized mixed estimate unproved; a separate selected construction proves the existence conclusion.
TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.Proof.theorem_1_1_o.summary: The generalized extension follows from stronger hypotheses

TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.Statement.lemma_1_2.text: For each cutoff symbol, the formal statement asks for $a_0$ such that each integer $a\ge a_0$ has a majorant $G$, chosen before the construction. Every sequence satisfying the specified Section 7 step data, strength $18e^3$, and $G(7K(s))\le\mathcal B(s)$ must then satisfy $\|\partial_t^q(U_j-U_{j-1}-O_j)\|_{C([0,S_j];C^{m,1/2})}\le\lambda_j^{-1}$ eventually for every fixed $(m,q)$. Time derivatives fix the physical point; continuity in the spatial norm is included. The majorant also covers the main fixed-order constants used by this argument. This quantifies over every qualifying construction, whereas the paper discusses its selected one. The supplied file explicitly retains this assertion without a proof; the separately proved selected-construction result has narrower quantifiers.
TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.Statement.lemma_1_2.summary: This assertion is broader than the selected construction

TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.Statement.lemma_1_3.text: For each cutoff symbol and every sufficiently large integer envelope exponent $a$, the formal statement asks for a majorant $G$ chosen before the construction. For every sequence with the specified Section 7 data, strength $18e^3$, and threshold dominating $G(7K(s))$, it then asks that each $q$ admit integers $\psi_q,j_q$ such that, for $j\ge j_q$ and $i\le q$, $\|\partial_t^iU_j\|_{C_tL^\infty}\le\lambda_j^{\psi_q}$ and $\|\partial_t^iR_j\|_{C_tL^\infty}\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-5/2}$. Both time curves must be continuous in the supremum norm on $[0,S_j]$. The exponents and starting indices come after the construction. This universal formulation is explicitly unproved in the supplied files; the selected-construction theorem proves the auxiliary estimate with narrower quantifiers.
TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.Statement.lemma_1_3.summary: The exponent follows the construction and time order

TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.Statement.theorem_1.text: For every cutoff symbol and every lower bound on the integer envelope exponent, this formal statement asks for exponents $b,a$ and majorants $F,G$. Suitable thresholds $\mathcal B$ must exist, and every threshold satisfying both majorants must produce, for every sufficiently large initial frequency, a common sequence and a finite-time singular Euler solution. The solution retains bounded velocity, central vorticity divergence, divergent gradient and vorticity integrals, spatial limits off the origin, and uniqueness among maximal solutions of finite lifespan with the same initial data. Its periodic velocity must extend smoothly through the terminal time off $\mathbb Z^3$; Euler is imposed only before it. The supplied files explicitly leave this generalized assertion unproved. Their selected-construction existence theorem and the proved main Remark 1.2 establish the required existence of a strengthened solution.
TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.Statement.theorem_1.summary: Every qualifying threshold must yield the strengthened solution

TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.TimeBounds.text: For a specified stage $j$ and nonnegative integers $q,\psi_q$, the condition requires, for every $i\le q$, $|\partial_t^iU_j(t,x)|\le\lambda_j^{\psi_q}$ and $|\partial_t^iR_j(t,x)|\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-5/2}$ on $[0,S_j]\times\mathbb R^3$. It also requires continuity of both time curves in the spatial supremum norm. The fields are periodic lifts, so this is the intended $C([0,S_j];L^\infty)$ meaning of auxiliary equation (1.3). Derivatives fix $x$ and are one-sided at the endpoints. The exponent is an integer, not the cutoff symbol. This condition concerns one stage; it neither selects the exponent nor asserts that the estimates hold eventually.
TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.TimeBounds.summary: The two estimates include supremum-norm continuity

TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.TimeDerivativeThres.text: For a nonnegative integer $b$ and functions $G,\mathcal B$ on the nonnegative integers, the formal condition is $G(7K(s))\le\mathcal B(s)$ for every $s\ge1$, with $K(s)=320b(s+1)$. The argument of $G$ is therefore the largest derivative order and depth admitted by the auxiliary estimate. This condition alone does not require either function to be monotone or positive, and does not assert the main logarithmic lower bound for $\mathcal B$. Those properties enter through separate schedule or admissibility assumptions. The generalized auxiliary statements choose $G$ before the construction; its existence as a suitable analytic majorant is not supplied by this inequality itself.
TorusEuler.Paper.Aux.TimeDerivativeThres.summary: One majorant covers the additional derivative constants

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.CutoffSymbol.eve.text: A radial Fourier symbol is even. The norm is computed before phase substitution. Bounds for weighted profiles require a bounded inverse time weight on the active interval; continuous positivity supplies that bound for the actual central seed.

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.IsExpansion.eq_c.text: Every expansion is the library construction over `solvers d hM hO` (level by level), for the parent residual, activation term and leading pair of the expansion, given `MeanUnique d`. At level p the mean is solved before the transverse correction, because the new mean transports the leading wave. The finite recursion uses the prescribed mean pressure normalization and a zero-start transverse solution.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.IsExpansion.eq_c.summary: Identify an arbitrary expansion with the chosen recursion

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.IsExpansion.uniq.text: Uniqueness of the expansion: two families satisfying the defining recursions (`S5.IsExpansion`) for the same parent, cutoff, seed and depth have the same `R`, `S` and the same levels, given the uniqueness of the normalized mean solves (`MeanUnique`). The transverse levels are unique by `TransverseSolution.unique` (`V_p(0) = 0`, zero phase mean of `𝗉_p`), the leading level by its cell values, and the recursion propagates the agreement level by level. At level p the mean is solved before the transverse correction, because the new mean transports the leading wave. The finite recursion uses the prescribed mean pressure normalization and a zero-start transverse solution.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.IsExpansion.uniq.summary: The recursive expansion is unique at every retained level

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.IsSeed.eqOn.text: Uniqueness of the seed: two solutions of (3.2) with the initial data (5.4) agree on `[t₀,T] × ℝ³` (linear ODE uniqueness at each label). The seed is the solution of the projected initial-value problem on the active interval. Near-origin quantitative bounds are separate data in SeedNear and are proved later from smallness of the envelope; they are not part of the paper seed predicate itself.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.IsSeed.eqOn.summary: The projected initial amplitude determines the seed uniquely

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.IsSeed.eqOn_ampl.text: Every `S5.IsSeed` agrees on `[t₀,T] × ℝ³` with the amplitude of any library seed over the parent coefficients, with no regularity assumption on the library amplitude (linear ODE uniqueness at each label uses only the equation and the initial data). This identifies the seed with the `SeedOn` of `exists_seedOn_of_coframe_bounds`, which records no smoothness, in the proof of Lemma 5.3. The seed is the solution of the projected initial-value problem on the active interval. Near-origin quantitative bounds are separate data in SeedNear and are proved later from smallness of the envelope; they are not part of the paper seed predicate itself.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.IsSeed.eqOn_ampl.summary: Identify seed amplitudes using their equation and initial data

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.IsSeed.eqOn_seed.text: Every `S5.IsSeed` agrees on `[t₀,T] × ℝ³` with the amplitude of any library seed over the parent coefficients whose amplitude is smooth. The seed is the solution of the projected initial-value problem on the active interval. Near-origin quantitative bounds are separate data in SeedNear and are proved later from smallness of the envelope; they are not part of the paper seed predicate itself.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.IsSeed.eqOn_seed.summary: Identify a paper seed with a smooth library seed

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.IsTruncation.pre.text: Under the explicitly supplied periodic Poisson-pressure uniqueness assertion, two pressure representatives for the same truncation velocity agree on the slab. The gradient equation alone would leave a time-dependent constant; zero cell mean removes it. The ledger classifies the uniqueness helper as glue, so this note does not repeat the source comment's exclusive attribution to Proposition 5.11.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.IsTruncation.pre.summary: Pressure uniqueness needs the normalized Poisson problem

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.IsTruncation.pre.text: Under the supplied pressure-uniqueness hypothesis, the pressure of a paper truncation equals that of the corresponding child stage on the time slab. This is a normalization-sensitive comparison, rather than a new pressure estimate or a consequence of velocity equality alone.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.IsTruncation.pre.summary: Identify the normalized pressure of a child stage

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.IsTruncation.vel.text: The velocity of a truncation is the velocity of any child stage of the same field on `[0,T]`. The statement compares the paper truncation predicate with an existing child-stage construction on the same closed time interval. Pressure equality additionally uses the supplied uniqueness assertion and the chosen zero-mean normalization.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.IsTruncation.vel.summary: Identify a truncation with the constructed velocity

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.IsTruncation.vel.text: Two truncations of the same field have the same velocity on `[0,T]`, provided the field has a continuous torus lift at each time (every child stage provides one). The statement compares the paper truncation predicate with an existing child-stage construction on the same closed time interval. Pressure equality additionally uses the supplied uniqueness assertion and the chosen zero-mean normalization.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.IsTruncation.vel.summary: A Fourier truncation determines its velocity uniquely

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.Launch.active_su.text: The active interval lies inside the full interval. The parent is smooth, periodic, odd and divergence free on the closed time interval, with the deformation and velocity-gradient bounds of Section 5. The bridge extracts only the stated consequence of those hypotheses.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.Launch.active_su.summary: The active interval lies inside the full interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.Launch.carrier_e.text: The launch covector recovered from the central covector at `t₀`, `(D_aX(t₀,0))^T κ(t₀,0)`, is `k_*` (as in the library seed constructions). The parent is smooth, periodic, odd and divergence free on the closed time interval, with the deformation and velocity-gradient bounds of Section 5. The bridge extracts only the stated consequence of those hypotheses.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.Launch.carrier_e.summary: The launch covector recovers the constant carrier

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.Launch.end_pos.text: The final time is strictly positive. The parent is smooth, periodic, odd and divergence free on the closed time interval, with the deformation and velocity-gradient bounds of Section 5. The bridge extracts only the stated consequence of those hypotheses.

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.Launch.start_mem.text: Activation lies inside the full time interval. The parent is smooth, periodic, odd and divergence free on the closed time interval, with the deformation and velocity-gradient bounds of Section 5. The bridge extracts only the stated consequence of those hypotheses.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.Launch.start_mem.summary: Activation lies inside the full time interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.MeanSolvable.text:
Every phase-independent source admits a smooth mean velocity and pressure solving the two-endpoint mean equation, with the pressure normalized to zero cell mean. This is an input predicate for the finite recursion; meanSolvable_of_theorem42 proves it from the cited Theorem 4.2. The source comment saying that the endpoint bridge is not yet written is stale.

Default-value audit (b5): This is an existence predicate over every phase-independent source. It includes pressure normalization rather than relying on a default representative. It has no fallback zero solution, and the actual existence proof is supplied by meanSolvable_of_theorem42.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.MeanSolvable.summary: Existence of normalized solutions of the mean equation

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.MeanUnique.text:
Two mean solutions for the same source agree as velocity-pressure pairs when both pressures have zero cell mean. The endpoint condition fixes the velocity and the normalization fixes the pressure constant. meanUnique_of_theorem42 now supplies this predicate, contrary to the stale unfinished-bridge source comment.

Default-value audit (b5): The predicate compares two pairs only when both satisfy the mean equation and zero cell pressure mean. Dropping normalization would allow a time-dependent pressure constant, so the stored hypotheses are material. It is a conditional uniqueness predicate rather than an asserted instance.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.MeanUnique.summary: Uniqueness of normalized solutions of the mean equation

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.Origin.centerWav.text: The central data of `S5.Origin` in the form used by the library seed lemmas: `CenterWaveOn` at the parent gradient `∇U(t,0)`. The parent is smooth, periodic, odd and divergence free on the closed time interval, with the deformation and velocity-gradient bounds of Section 5. The bridge extracts only the stated consequence of those hypotheses.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.Origin.centerWav.summary: Recover the library central wave assumptions

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.Origin.exists_in.text: The inverse weight `γ⁻¹` is bounded on `[t₀,T]`, as needed for the seminorm properties of `S5.wNorm` (`wNorm_nonneg`, `wNorm_add_le`, ...). The parent is smooth, periodic, odd and divergence free on the closed time interval, with the deformation and velocity-gradient bounds of Section 5. The bridge extracts only the stated consequence of those hypotheses.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.Origin.exists_in.summary: The positive weight has a bounded inverse

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.Origin.weight_co.text: The weight `γ(t) = λ^{3/4}|𝐚(t,0)|` is continuous on `[t₀,T]`. The parent is smooth, periodic, odd and divergence free on the closed time interval, with the deformation and velocity-gradient bounds of Section 5. The bridge extracts only the stated consequence of those hypotheses.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.Origin.weight_co.summary: The central amplitude gives a continuous weight

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.Origin.weight_le.text: The weight `γ ≤ 1` on `[t₀,T]` (the normalization of §5.1). The parent is smooth, periodic, odd and divergence free on the closed time interval, with the deformation and velocity-gradient bounds of Section 5. The bridge extracts only the stated consequence of those hypotheses.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.Origin.weight_le.summary: The chosen amplitude normalization bounds the weight by one

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.Origin.weight_po.text: The weight `γ(t) = λ^{3/4}|𝐚(t,0)|` is positive on `[t₀,T]`. The parent is smooth, periodic, odd and divergence free on the closed time interval, with the deformation and velocity-gradient bounds of Section 5. The bridge extracts only the stated consequence of those hypotheses.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.Origin.weight_po.summary: The central amplitude gives a positive weight

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.Parent.exists_li.text: The velocity is Lipschitz in space, uniformly on `[0,T]`. The parent is smooth, periodic, odd and divergence free on the closed time interval, with the deformation and velocity-gradient bounds of Section 5. The bridge extracts only the stated consequence of those hypotheses.

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.SeedNear.text: This is a condition on $\mathbf a(t,a)$, a specified central amplitude, $M$, $\kappa$, and parameters on $[t_0,T]\times\{|a|\le2\ell_*\}$. The near-origin estimates include relative error proportional to $\lVert a\rVert$, upper and lower amplitude bounds, and a quantitative positive lower bound for the normalized coupling. They therefore contain more information than the two displayed inequalities (5.19). These properties describe the output of the seed comparison argument, rather than additional assumptions on every solution of the seed equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.SeedNear.summary: The nearby seed obeys amplitude and coupling comparisons

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.TransverseSoluti.text: The fields are smooth phase-periodic profiles on $[0,T]$, compatible with the same label translations and with the same transported nonzero covector. Two transverse solutions with the same source, zero initial velocity and zero-mean pressure agree. The homogeneous ordinary differential equation eliminates their velocity difference; pressure normalization then removes the remaining phase-constant difference. This proves the uniqueness asserted in §5.4 and transfers bounds for the chosen solution to every solution covered by Lemma 5.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.TransverseSoluti.summary: The source and normalization determine both unknown fields

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.TransverseSolvab.text:
Every source of zero phase mean has a solution of (5.15) from `V(0) = 0` with pressure of zero phase mean (the library ODE solve `exists_transverseResult`). The operators use the same parent inverse deformation, strain and transported covector as the paper. The selected transverse solution is determined by zero initial velocity and zero phase mean of its pressure.

Default-value audit (b5): The predicate is quantified only over sources with zero phase average and asks for an actual transverse-solution witness. It provides no solution for an inadmissible source and contains no default fallback. Zero start and pressure normalization are part of the solution predicate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.TransverseSolvab.summary: Existence of a transverse solution for every admissible source

TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.activationProfil.text:

Default-value audit (b5): The constructors require a positive envelope radius fitting strictly inside the label cell, positive phase width at most one, and the stated seed/launch regularity. For time factors the vanishing-before-activation hypothesis allows smooth extension across activation. They bundle a twisted profile; equality with a raw localized expression is asserted only on the proved slab and cell domains.
TorusEuler.Paper.Bridge.activationProfil.summary: The forcing introduced by switching on the wave

At level p the mean is solved before the transverse correction, because the new mean transports the leading wave. The finite recursion uses the prescribed mean pressure normalization and a zero-start transverse solution.

TorusEuler.Paper.Corollary83Conclusions.text: For prescribed $T,u,p$, these are the requirements of Corollary 8.3, not an existence proof. The velocity and mean-zero pressure solve smooth periodic Euler on $[0,T)$, where $0<T<\infty$, and have no smooth Euler continuation agreeing with the velocity there. Every maximal solution of finite lifespan from $u(0)$ must have the same terminal time $T$. Both $\int_0^T\|\operatorname{curl}u(t)\|_\infty\,dt$ and $\int_0^T\|\nabla u(t)\|_\infty\,dt$ are infinite. The formalization uses nonnegative Lebesgue integrals and essential suprema on $[-1/2,1/2]^3$; the gradient has its operator norm. No equation is imposed at $t=T$, and no value at that time contributes to either integral.
TorusEuler.Paper.Corollary83Conclusions.summary: Specify maximality, its time, and the two infinite integrals

TorusEuler.Paper.EndpointSystemSolution.text: On $[0,T]\times\mathbb T^3$, the unknowns satisfy $Kv-J(\Omega v)+L=c+G$, $z_t=v$, and $z(0)=z(T)=0$, where $J$ integrates from zero. The fields $z,v,c$ are spatially divergence free in the weak sense; $v$ and $G$ are continuous in time in $C^{0,1/2}$, and $G=\nabla_a\phi$ for a periodic scalar potential at each time. The spatial norm is the maximum of the supremum norm and the half-Hölder seminorm. Derivatives at time endpoints are one-sided. This is (4.9), with functions represented by periodic lifts to $\mathbb R^3$. The potential has no normalization or prescribed time regularity; uniqueness concerns its gradient.
TorusEuler.Paper.EndpointSystemSolution.summary: Specify displacement, velocity, constant field and pressure gradient

TorusEuler.Paper.FiniteSmallness.text:
For the preceding wave, set $\sigma=|k_p(t_0)||\mathbf a_p(t_0)|$, $
u=B_{12}(t_0)>0$, $\eta=B_{32}(t_0)>0$, $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$ and $\varepsilon=\eta/
u$. On a compact physical set $I$, let $\delta=\|B_{12}/
u-1\|_\infty+\|B_{32}/\eta-1\|_\infty+\|B\|_\infty/r+\|E_c\|_\infty/
u$, using Euclidean matrix operator norms. The formal condition is exactly $C_0\varepsilon\le1$ and $C_0T^{C_0}\delta\le\varepsilon$. Here $C_0$ is a nonnegative integer; the condition alone permits $C_0=0$ and does not require $T\ge2$. The lemmas separately impose a sufficiently large absolute lower bound on $C_0$ and $T\ge2$. If $I$ exceeds the physical interval corresponding to $[0,T]$, its larger suprema are used.
TorusEuler.Paper.FiniteSmallness.summary: Two inequalities quantify the required small coupling ratio and gradient error

TorusEuler.Paper.FreezingConclusion.text: Let $\mathcal R$ be a bounded projection on $C^{0,1/2}(\mathbb T^3;H)$ and $B$ a bounded operator-valued half-Hölder coefficient. The asserted conclusion is that $v\mapsto\mathcal R(Bv)$ is an isomorphism on the range of $\mathcal R$, with inverse bound $C(2+\mu^{-1}+\|B\|_\infty+L)^p$. Here $p$ is a nonnegative integer and $L$ is the supplied Lipschitz bound. If $B\in C^{k,1/2}$, $k\ge1$, the map and inverse preserve that class and have finite bounds there. This defines the conclusion used in Lemma A.2; it does not prove it or impose coercivity. Higher norms sum supremum and half-Hölder bounds on Fréchet derivatives through order $k$.
TorusEuler.Paper.FreezingConclusion.summary: State the base inverse and its higher regularity

TorusEuler.Paper.Lemma61Conclusions.text: For a first central wave over $B_\rho=2\pi(e_1+\rho e_3)\otimes e_2$, write $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a|$ and $\nu=(\kappa/|\kappa|)\cdot B_\rho(\mathbf a/|\mathbf a|)$. This formal condition requires, for every $\mathsf D\ge2$, $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for every transverse amplitude solution and every $0\le t'\le t\le T$, together with $\nu(t)\ge\mathsf D^{-1}$ on $[0,T]$. It also requires $\lambda^{1/4}/2\le|\mathbf a(0)||\kappa(0)|\le\lambda^{1/4}$. These are the mathematical conclusions of Lemma 6.1. This declaration describes the three required estimates; it does not assert that an arbitrary first wave satisfies them. The short-interval and parameter hypotheses enter in the theorem proving this condition.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lemma61Conclusions.summary: Specifies weighted propagation, positive coupling and initial strength

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.CommonIncrement.text: This proposition records the increment half of the joint auxiliary induction, uniformly over the cutoff and eligible construction choices in the statement layer. Given parent time bounds at order q, it demands eventual mixed increment bounds at order q + 1 for every spatial order m. The corresponding wrapper consumes this proposition as h. The definition itself does not discharge the analytic step.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.CommonIncrement.summary: The common increment induction step remains an input

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.CommonTime.text: This proposition states the general time-estimate step for constructions admitted by the auxiliary statement. After a cutoff symbol, envelope-exponent floor, and majorant are chosen, it quantifies over eligible parameter records and constructions. Bounds through order q at one stage must imply bounds through order q + 1 at the next, eventually. The file explicitly leaves this proposition open; defining it supplies no witness or proof.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.CommonTime.summary: The common time induction step remains an input

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.exists_offOrigi.text: With positive T, decreasing stage slabs containing T, initial frequency at least two, and terminal mixed increment bounds, there exists a field w smooth on the punctured closed slab. At each point of that slab the stages tend to w. The proof uses limUnder only after local summation supplies a genuine limit; no value or smoothness at a lattice point, or outside the stated slab, is concluded.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.exists_offOrigi.summary: Assemble a smooth limit on the punctured closed slab

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.exists_threshol.text: Given any nonnegative integer $b$ and real functions $F,G$ on the nonnegative integers, the formal statement constructs a common threshold. One choice in the proof is $\mathcal B(s)=\exp(4K(s+1)^3)+\sum_{t=0}^s(|F(t)|+|G(7K(t))|)$, where $K(s)=320b(s+1)$. It is positive and nondecreasing, dominates the main majorant and $G(7K(s))$, and satisfies the required logarithmic lower bound. No monotonicity or positivity of $F,G$ is assumed. This proves that the two numerical threshold requirements can be met simultaneously. It does not establish that the prescribed majorants bound the analytic constants of a particular construction.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.exists_threshol.summary: A single function dominates both prescribed majorants

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.joint_jets_of_i.text: Assume the stages converge uniformly to u on a closed time–ball cylinder, their slabs contain that cylinder and decrease, and every order of joint derivative increment has a summable eventual bound. For positive terminal time and ball radius, u is smooth within the cylinder. The hypothesis hLocal is local; no uniform convergence or terminal regularity at the singular origin is inferred.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.joint_jets_of_i.summary: Summable joint derivatives give a smooth local limit

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.lemma13_order.text: The input h1_3 is Lemma 1.3 of the main paper, not the auxiliary lemma with the same number. Applying it to the schedule recorded by P yields Tendsto P.order atTop atTop. The proof supplies the threshold, frequency recursion, and order-maximum conditions from P. This is the eventual-order fact needed for the zero-time-order mixed increment estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.lemma13_order.summary: The scheduled orders eventually exceed every fixed order

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.lemma_1_2_of_co.text: Assume the main order-growth lemma, the generalized auxiliary time bounds, and a uniform implication that advances the parent time bounds to the child's mixed correction bound. The formal statement deduces the generalized auxiliary Lemma 1.2: for each fixed $(m,q)$, the correction eventually has size at most $\lambda_j^{-1}$ in $C([0,S_j];C^{m,1/2})$, for every construction covered by the chosen threshold and step conditions. The threshold may be enlarged to satisfy all assumptions before choosing the construction. The analytic correction implication is an explicit hypothesis, as is the generalized time lemma. This declaration organizes those assumptions; it does not independently prove them or transfer the selected-construction theorem to all constructions.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.lemma_1_2_of_co.summary: The generalized estimate requires the common correction step

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.lemma_1_3_of_co.text: Assume a uniform implication that, for every qualifying construction and all sufficiently late stages, turns the parent bounds through order $q$ into child velocity and residual bounds through order $q+1$. The formal statement then obtains the generalized auxiliary Lemma 1.3, including time continuity in the spatial supremum norm. For each fixed $q$ and construction, one integer exponent and one starting stage work for all $i\le q$. The common implication is a mathematical hypothesis of this result, not a conclusion. The supplied files do not establish it for every construction quantified over by the generalized lemma; the separate selected-construction argument has more specific hypotheses.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.lemma_1_3_of_co.summary: A uniform induction step gives the generalized bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.local_limit_of_.text: For stages with decreasing slabs containing the positive time T, initial frequency at least two, and terminal mixed increment bounds, every point c in offOrigin has a positive-radius neighborhood with a uniform smooth limit on the closed time cylinder. The proof sums the increments there and bounds joint derivatives by summable reciprocal frequencies. offOrigin excludes every lattice translate of zero in the periodic lift.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.local_limit_of_.summary: Construct the terminal limit near a nonsingular point

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.mixedIncrementB.text: For a positive stage index j, the library StageMixedIncrementBound at j − 1 yields the auxiliary bound for step j. The hypotheses h71 and hSteps supply smoothness and the identification of the actual oscillation with its graph readout. They justify continuity in the spatial Hölder norm. The condition hj makes natural-number predecessor notation agree with the intended preceding stage.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.mixedIncrementB.summary: Restore continuity and indexing to the mixed increment bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.mixedIncrement_.text: The theorem assumes divergence of the scheduled orders, the common increment step hinc, and the eventual auxiliary time bounds h13, as well as the stage conclusions and step data. It derives the mixed increment estimate for every spatial and time order eventually. For time order zero it uses the construction correction bound; higher orders use hinc after increasing the starting index beyond both required thresholds.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.mixedIncrement_.summary: Combine the time estimates with the mixed increment step

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.one_le_frequenc.text: Every frequency in an InductiveEulerParameters record is at least one. The base case follows from the positive logarithmic threshold floor and the initial-threshold inequality; the induction uses the frequency power law. This is an arithmetic consequence of the parameter record, without an extra construction or convergence hypothesis. It justifies comparisons between natural and real powers in the auxiliary time bounds.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.one_le_frequenc.summary: Every scheduled frequency is at least one

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.smoothTerminalE.text: An existing HasSmoothOffOriginExtension witness gives the paper-facing SmoothTerminalExtension predicate by choosing the neighborhood to be all times times offOrigin. Periodicity and agreement with u are copied from the witness, while smoothness is restricted to the required union. No Euler equation is imposed on the extended field after T, and no regularity at lattice points is asserted.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.smoothTerminalE.summary: Read a periodic extension as a terminal neighborhood

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.smoothTerminalE.text: Assume a common sequence with the lifetime, support and estimates of Theorem 7.1, and an Euler solution $u,p$ with the convergence and initial-data conclusions of Proposition 8.1. Suppose every fixed mixed derivative of $U_j-U_{j-1}-O_j$ eventually has size at most $\lambda_j^{-1}$ in its spatial Hölder norm, with time continuity on $[0,S_j]$. The formal statement proves that this same velocity $u$ has a periodic smooth extension through $T_\infty$ away from $\mathbb Z^3$. The proof first obtains a smooth limit on the closed punctured slab and identifies it with $u$ for $t<T_\infty$ by convergence. It assumes the mixed estimates; it imposes no Euler equation on the extension after the terminal time.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.smoothTerminalE.summary: Mixed correction bounds preserve the preterminal solution

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.stageTimeBounds.text: An auxiliary TimeBounds hypothesis contains both numerical derivative bounds and continuity in the spatial supremum norm. This theorem projects the numerical bounds into StageTimeBounds for the same construction, orders, and stage. It performs no induction and proves no new estimate; it lets the common induction step consume the bounds already supplied by auxiliary Lemma 1.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.stageTimeBounds.summary: Discard continuity from the auxiliary time estimate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.stage_smooth.text: Theorem71Conclusions supplies a positive lifetime, stage smoothness, and periodic velocity. Together with the stage pressure data, the theorem proves positive slab length and joint smoothness and periodicity for both velocity and residual on that slab. The residual is the actual momentum residual of the stage velocity and pressure. These facts provide continuity in the spatial norms used by the auxiliary estimates.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.stage_smooth.summary: Velocity and residual are smooth on every stage slab

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.timeBounds_of_s.text: Given Theorem71Conclusions and StageTimeBounds, this theorem obtains the full auxiliary TimeBounds predicate. The numerical estimates are inherited unchanged. Joint smoothness and periodicity of velocity and residual give continuity of each fixed-spatial-point time derivative in the supremum norm. Thus the conclusion includes the membership in the continuous-in-time function space written in auxiliary display (1.3).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.timeBounds_of_s.summary: Restore continuity to the auxiliary time estimate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.timeBounds_of_s.text: Assume htime provides the eventual implication from order q bounds at stage n to order q + 1 bounds at stage n + 1. Together with Theorem71Conclusions, induction yields the exponent and starting index required by auxiliary (1.3), including continuity. The zero-order estimates come from the stage record. The analytic induction step is an explicit hypothesis here, not a conclusion established by this framing theorem.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.timeBounds_of_s.summary: Iterate a supplied step to all time orders

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.witness_of_sect.text: The inputs h81, h82, h83, and h84 are the four Section 8 conclusion predicates for the same construction, time, velocity, and pressure. Their fields assemble an EulerSingularityWitness with initial data u 0, together with uniqueness of the maximal velocity and its lifetime. This is a conjunction assembly: smoothness, blow-up, divergent integrals, and terminal limits are supplied by those inputs.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Aux.witness_of_sect.summary: Assemble the singularity witness from Section Eight

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Rem12.maximal_uniqu.text: Assume hu and hv are maximal Euler solutions with identical initial velocities. Periodic Euler uniqueness gives agreement on their common interval. If either lifetime were shorter, the other solution would be a forbidden extension, so both lifetimes coincide and the velocities agree throughout the half-open interval. The theorem claims velocity uniqueness; it does not compare the pressure fields as a separate conclusion.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Rem12.maximal_uniqu.summary: Maximal solutions from the same data have equal lifetimes

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Rem12.smoothTermina.text: The library extension predicate provides a periodic field smooth on all times away from the lattice and agreeing with u before T. Choosing that whole punctured space–time domain as the open neighborhood yields SmoothTerminalExtension. This is the conversion used by the active Remark 1.2 proof. Smooth extension of a field does not assert continuation of the Euler solution beyond its maximal time.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.Rem12.smoothTermina.summary: Convert the library extension for the active remark

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.abs_sub_le_of_h.text: On a nonnegative interval, a uniform absolute derivative bound gives variation from the initial value at most the bound times elapsed time. The statement uses within-interval derivatives, including the endpoints.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.coefficientBox.text:
Define the four-dimensional box used to compare finite-shear coefficients with the limit: bounded first and second coordinates, third coordinate between one half and three halves, and inverse shear squared between zero and one.

Default-value audit (b5): A negative radius can make the first two coordinate intervals empty. All compactness statements remain valid for that empty set; the application chooses a positive radius containing both the actual and reference coordinates. This set definition has no inverse or choice fallback.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.coefficientBox.summary: A compact region for coefficient comparison

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.continuousOn_sh.text: The rational coefficient map is continuous on the coefficient box because the third coordinate and the quadratic norm denominator stay strictly positive there. It does not assert continuity at singular inputs outside that box.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.continuousOn_sh.summary: Continuity of the reduced amplitude coefficients

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.cos_referenceAn.text: For any real $\varepsilon,\tau$, put $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)$. The formal identity is $\cos\varphi=(1+(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)^2)^{-1/2}$. The square root is positive because its argument is at least one; this formula therefore introduces no zero denominator. It identifies the cosine in (2.4) with the expression used in the reference estimates. No wave equation or sign condition on $\varepsilon$ is required. Restricting $\varepsilon\ge0$ additionally gives the paper’s angle range $0\le\varphi<\pi/2$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.cos_referenceAn.summary: The trigonometric cosine equals the explicit positive algebraic expression

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.driving_referen.text: For $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)$, the formal statement identifies $\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon\tan\varphi)$ with $(1-\varepsilon^2\tau^2/2)/(1+(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)^2)$. This holds for every real $\varepsilon,\tau$, since the denominator is strictly positive. It is the coefficient driving the first amplitude equation in (2.5), and the constant term in the Riccati equation (2.12). The identity changes notation only; it neither supplies a solution of either equation nor proves the amplitude gain. The sign change occurs when $\varepsilon\tan\varphi=1$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.driving_referen.summary: The trigonometric driving term equals its rational expression in time

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.entry_smul.text: Scalar multiplication of a linear map scales every frame entry by the same scalar. The identity does not require the frame to be orthonormal.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.eta_div_rate.text:
At activation, let $\sigma=|k_p||\mathbf a_p|>0$, $
u=B_{12}>0$, $\eta=B_{32}>0$, and define $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$, $S=\sigma/r$, $\varepsilon=\eta/
u$. The formal identity is $\eta/r=\varepsilon/(2S)$. Multiplying by $S$ gives $\eta S/r=\varepsilon/2$, one of the scalar conversions in the proof of Lemma 2.3. The quantities are frozen at $t_0$; the statement does not assert that the time-dependent coupling is constant. Positivity supplied by the amplification assumptions makes every displayed denominator nonzero.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.eta_div_rate.summary: The second coupling becomes the ratio divided by twice the shear scale

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.exists_coeffici.text: Compactness of the coefficient box turns continuity into a single input tolerance controlling all four output coefficients. The tolerance is fixed after epsilon and the box radius are fixed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.exists_coeffici.summary: A uniform modulus for the amplitude coefficients

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.gronwallBound_e.text: Identify the general Gronwall expression for this linear system with the explicitly defined scalar factor. This is an algebraic conversion, not an additional stability theorem.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.gronwallBound_e.summary: Evaluating the wave vector Gronwall factor

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.modelEntries_ap.text: Compute all three coordinates of the model matrix applied to a vector. The only nonzero output coordinates are the first and third multiples of the second input coordinate.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.model_case_equa.text:
Assume the frame identities of Lemma 2.2. Let a preceding nonzero transverse wave evolve over continuous trace-free $B$, with positive activation couplings $
u,\eta$ and strength $\sigma$. On the physical interval corresponding to $0\le	au\le T$, require $B_{12}=
u$, $B_{32}=\eta$, all other frame entries zero, and $E_c=0$. Launch $k=\lambda E_3$ with $\lambda>0$, and set $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$, $S=\sigma/r$, $\varepsilon=\eta/
u$. The formal statement proves $\sigma_p=\sigma$ and $\zeta_1'=-(1+1/(2S^2))\zeta_2$, $\zeta_2'=-\varepsilon\zeta_3$, $\zeta_3'=\varepsilon\zeta_2/(2S^2)$. For every transverse amplitude it also gives $\alpha_1'=-\alpha_2+\zeta_1\Pi$ and $\alpha_2'=-(1-1/(2S^2))\alpha_1+\varepsilon(\zeta_1\alpha_1+\zeta_2\alpha_2)/(2S^2\zeta_3)+\zeta_2\Pi/S^2$, where $\Pi=(2\zeta_2\alpha_1+(\zeta_1+\varepsilon\zeta_3)\alpha_2)/(\zeta_1^2+\zeta_2^2/S^2+\zeta_3^2)$ and $\zeta_3
e0$. Unlike the full lemma, this conditional calculation needs no $T\ge2$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.model_case_equa.summary: The two-entry background gives constant strength and exact finite-shear equations

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.norm_le_abs_add.text: Bound the Euclidean norm of a three-vector by the sum of the absolute values of its three coordinates. This converts scalar error estimates into the norm used in the uniform limit.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.norm_le_abs_add.summary: Euclidean norm bounded by coordinate magnitudes

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.nu_div_rate.text:
Let the activation strength $\sigma$ and first coupling $
u$ be positive, and set $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$ and $S=\sigma/r$. For the amplification data the formal statement proves $
u/r=1/(2S)$, equivalently $
u S/r=1/2$. This is the conversion used when the physical amplitude and wave-vector equations are written in normalized time in Lemma 2.3. It follows from $r^2=2\sigma
u$ and the nonzero denominators. It is an identity of the frozen activation values, with no claim that $B_{12}(t)$ remains constant.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.nu_div_rate.summary: The first coupling is the reciprocal of twice the shear scale

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.rate_sq.text:
For the preceding wave at activation, $\sigma=|k_p(t_0)||\mathbf a_p(t_0)|>0$ and $
u=E_1(t_0)\cdot B(t_0)E_2(t_0)>0$. The rate is defined by $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$. The formal statement proves $r^2=2\sigma
u$, the scalar identity used to rescale the model equations of Lemma 2.3. Positivity is part of the supplied amplification data, so the square root is the positive one. This assertion concerns the normalization only and does not construct a new wave or assert its growth rate equals $r$ at finite shear.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.rate_sq.summary: Squaring the positive growth rate recovers twice the strength times the coupling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.referenceSlope_.text: For any real $\varepsilon$ and function $Y$, the formal statement equates two conditions on $[0,\infty)$: $Y(0)=1$ and $Y'=\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon\tan\varphi)-\varepsilon\tau\sin2\varphi\,Y-Y^2$, with $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)$, or the same equation after these trigonometric coefficients are written as rational functions of $\varepsilon\tau^2/2$. The time derivative at zero is the right derivative. The function, initial value and domain are unchanged; no existence or uniqueness assertion is included. This is the precise change of notation connecting (2.12) to the algebraic reference estimates.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.referenceSlope_.summary: The trigonometric and algebraic initial value problems are equivalent

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.referenceSystem.text: Put $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)$ and $\zeta_0=(\varepsilon\tau^2/2,-\varepsilon\tau,1)$. The formal identity evaluates the four finite-shear coefficient formulas at $(\zeta,S^{-2})=(\zeta_0,0)$ and obtains the entries $-\varepsilon\tau\sin2\varphi$, $-\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon\tan\varphi)$, $-1$, $0$ of (2.5). It is an algebraic evaluation for arbitrary real parameters, not a convergence theorem. The evaluated denominator is $1+(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)^2>0$ and the third coordinate is one. Uniform convergence of actual coefficients additionally uses the model-wave estimates and continuity near these values.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.referenceSystem.summary: Evaluating the coefficient formulas at infinite shear gives the reference matrix

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.shearCoefficien.text:
Define the four rational entries of the finite-shear amplitude matrix as functions of the wave coordinates and inverse shear squared. The formula is separated from ODE solvability so that compact uniform continuity can prove coefficient convergence.

Default-value audit (b5): Division is total: a zero third coordinate or zero quadratic denominator gives Lean-defined values, not a valid reduced amplitude equation. Continuity and convergence are asserted only on a box with third coordinate at least one half and nonnegative inverse shear squared, which makes the denominators positive.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.shear_pos.text: The physical amplification parameters imply that the shear scale is strictly positive, allowing cancellation and division by that scale in the model equations.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.sin_referenceAn.text: Express the reference sine as the algebraic tangent parameter times its cosine factor. It translates trigonometric formulas into the rational quantities used in the scalar ODE library.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.sin_two_referen.text: Rewrite epsilon times time times sine of twice the reference angle as the library damping function. No positivity hypothesis is needed for this algebraic identity.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.smul_modelEntri.text: Scaling the model matrix scales its two nonzero entries. This identifies the physical and normalized model coefficients before the ODE calculation.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.strain_modelEnt.text: An orthonormal frame and the specified matrix entries determine the strain as the sum of the two model rank-one maps. Orthonormality is essential to reconstruct the operator from its entries.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.strongShearMatr.text: Identify the finite-shear reduced matrix with the four-entry rational coefficient map evaluated at the actual wave coordinates and inverse shear squared. The identity prepares the common continuity argument.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.strongShearMatr.summary: Finite shear coefficients in the common formula

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.strongShear_lim.text:
Assume the frame theorem of Lemma 2.2. Let a nonzero transverse preceding wave solve the wave equations over continuous trace-free $B$, with frame $E_1=k_p/|k_p|$, $E_2=\mathbf a_p/|\mathbf a_p|$, $E_3=E_1	imes E_2$. At activation $t_0$, take positive $\sigma=|k_p(t_0)||\mathbf a_p(t_0)|,
u,\eta$; put $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$, $S=\sigma/r$, $\varepsilon=\eta/
u$, $	au=r(t-t_0)$. On $[0,T]$, $T\ge2$, suppose only $B_{12}=
u,B_{32}=\eta$ are nonzero and $E_c=0$. Launch $\dot k=-M^Tk$, $M=B+\mathbf a_p\otimes k_p$, from $k(t_0)=\lambda E_3(t_0)$, $\lambda>0$. Write $k=\lambda(\zeta_1E_1+\zeta_2E_2/S+\zeta_3E_3)$ and $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)=(S\mathbf a\cdot E_1,\mathbf a\cdot E_2)$. For every $e>0$, one threshold $S_0(\varepsilon,T,e)$, chosen before the wave, makes $S\ge S_0$ imply the Euclidean bound $|\zeta-(\varepsilon	au^2/2,-\varepsilon	au,1)|\le e$ and $\zeta_3
e0$ throughout $[0,T]$. Each reduced amplitude coefficient differs by at most $e$ from $- igl( egin{smallmatrix}\varepsilon	au\sin2\varphi&\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon	an\varphi)\1&0\end{smallmatrix} igr)$, $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon	au^2/2)$. The physical interval lies in a supplied compact observation set. No polynomial dependence of $S_0$ on $T$ is asserted.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.strongShear_lim.summary: A single shear threshold controls all model waves throughout the fixed interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.tan_referenceAn.text: Rewrite the tangent of the arctangent angle as epsilon times time squared divided by two. This is a notation bridge and carries no ODE or growth estimate.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.zetaBound.text:
Define the scalar Gronwall factor for the wave-vector error with epsilon and interval length fixed. Multiplication by the small parameter one over twice shear squared gives the coordinate error bound used in the strong-shear limit.

Default-value audit (b5): The formula is total for all real epsilon and T. At epsilon = -2 the inverse denominator is Lean zero, so it is not a meaningful Gronwall estimate there; the nonnegativity and error lemmas assume epsilon and T nonnegative. No ODE solution is selected by this definition.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.zetaBound_nonne.text: For nonnegative epsilon and interval length, the Gronwall factor is nonnegative. These sign hypotheses ensure both the denominator and the exponential increment have the required signs.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.zeta_bounds.text: Let $0\le\mu\le1$, $\varepsilon\ge0$, and let $z$ solve $z_1'=-(1+\mu)z_2$, $z_2'=-\varepsilon z_3$, $z_3'=\varepsilon\mu z_2$ on $[0,T]$, with $z(0)=(0,0,1)$. The formal statement bounds each coordinate of $z-(\varepsilon\tau^2/2,-\varepsilon\tau,1)$ in absolute value by $\mu K$, where $K=\varepsilon T(1+\varepsilon)(e^{(2+\varepsilon)T}-1)/(2+\varepsilon)$. Thus for $\mu=1/(2S^2)$ it gives uniform convergence in Lemma 2.3, with Euclidean error at most $3\mu K$. No assumption $T\ge2$ is needed. The estimate grows exponentially in $T$ and is used with $T$ fixed; it is not the polynomial comparison of Lemma 2.4.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2a.zeta_bounds.summary: Gronwall’s inequality bounds every coordinate error by the inverse squared shear

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.abs_apply_le_no.text: The absolute value of an individual coordinate of a three-vector is at most its Euclidean norm. This transfers a vector error bound to each denominator-sensitive coordinate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.abs_apply_le_no.summary: Each coordinate is bounded by the vector norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.abs_div_le_self.text: Dividing a real quantity by a scale at least one does not increase its absolute value. This removes harmless inverse shear factors from residual estimates.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.abs_le_of_deriv.text: For a scalar function initially zero, a uniform derivative bound on the interval gives an absolute bound proportional to elapsed time. The result is used on the logarithm of the preceding strength ratio.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.abs_le_of_deriv.summary: A zero initial value and a bounded derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.abs_threeProduc.text: If three coefficients have a common absolute bound, their products with three coordinates have sum bounded by that coefficient bound times the sum of coordinate magnitudes.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.absorb.text: Increase the universal finite-smallness threshold enough to make a specified polynomial in the horizon times delta at most one half. The constants and exponent must be fixed before choosing that threshold.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.actual_coupling.text: Turn a polynomial-in-time additive coupling error into the epsilon-scaled error required by the preceding comparison, using the finite-smallness hypothesis. The early sign of the reference slope remains an explicit input.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.actual_coupling.summary: Absorbing polynomial errors in the coupling bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.actual_coupling.text:
Let $0<\varepsilon\le1/16$, $T\ge2$, and $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon	au^2/2)$. Suppose $Y=(1+e)\cos\varphi-\varepsilon	au\sin(2\varphi)/4$, $0\le e\le\varepsilon/8$ for $	au\ge0$, and $Y>0$ on $[0,\sqrt2/\varepsilon]$. If two scalar functions $n,h$ differ from the reference values of $
u_+/
u,\eta_+/
u$ by at most $\varepsilon/(8T^2)$ on $[0,T]$, then $n\ge\varepsilon/2$ there. For $	au\ge\sqrt2/\varepsilon$ it also gives $|n-1|\le\varepsilon$ and $|(h/n)/\cos\varphi-1|\le1/2$. The extra early positivity assumption is explicit in this version; the companion result derives the required lower bound without it.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.actual_coupling.summary: Reference comparison gives positivity and late-time ratios

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.alpha_one.text: The paper's second scaled amplitude coordinate agrees with the library coordinate V. No sign change or additional scale is needed.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.alpha_system_of.text: At normalized time $\tau$, write $U=-\alpha_1$ and $V=\alpha_2$ for the scaled components of the physical amplitude. Suppose this pair satisfies the reference equations with an added linear error $R$. The formal statement converts them to the paper’s pair $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)$, with reference matrix from (2.5) and error $PRP$, where $P=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1)$. Derivatives may be restricted to any prescribed time set. This is an exact sign change, valid pointwise under the two derivative assumptions; it does not estimate $R$ or prove that the wave follows the reference solution.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.alpha_system_of.summary: Conjugation returns the internal equations to the paper notation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.alpha_zero.text: The paper's first scaled amplitude coordinate is the negative of the library coordinate U. This sign change is why the error matrix is conjugated by a diagonal reflection.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.alpha_zero.summary: The sign convention for the first amplitude coordinate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.amplificationPh.text: Restricting to a nonempty compact subinterval cannot increase the physical error bound, under the continuity hypotheses needed for the suprema.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.amplificationPh.summary: Physical error decreases on a smaller interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.amplitude_late_.text: Let $0<\varepsilon\le1$, $2/\varepsilon\le\tau_m\le3/\varepsilon$, and $\tau_m\le\tau\le T$. Write $x=\varepsilon\tau^2/2$. Assume the reference representation with continuous $Y$ and $0\le e\le\varepsilon/8$, its amplitude-ratio formula, and its maximum at $\tau_m$. Suppose $ca_{\rm ref}\le A\le Ca_{\rm ref}$ on $[0,T]$, with $c,C>0$, and $M=\max_{[0,T]}A$. If $0\le k_{\min},k_{\max}$ and $k_{\min}x\le k\le k_{\max}x$, then $k_{\min}(c/C)\sqrt{x/\varepsilon}\le kA(\tau)/M\le3\exp(2)k_{\max}(C/c)\sqrt{x/\varepsilon}$. Here $k$ represents $|k(\tau)|/\lambda$. The maximum and comparison formulas are hypotheses; the result does not construct a wave or establish those inputs.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.amplitude_late_.summary: Comparison constants give an explicit late-time strength estimate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.basis_continuou.text: Extract continuity of the preceding frame from the wave and amplitude hypotheses. The proof needs only their regularity and nonvanishing, so no invocation of Lemma 2.2 is hidden here.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.basis_orthonorm.text: Normalize the nonzero perpendicular preceding wave and amplitude vectors and complete them by the cross product to obtain an orthonormal basis.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.basis_orthonorm.summary: Orthonormality of the preceding wave frame

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.clock_continuou.text: The affine map from normalized time to physical time is continuous. Its range lies in the required time window only under the separate interval hypothesis.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.clock_mem_slab.text: A normalized time in the allowed interval maps into the physical slab between activation and the terminal clock value. Positive rate gives the order preservation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.clock_mem_slab.summary: The normalized clock stays in its physical slab

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.conjError.text:
Define the error matrix by conjugating the library error through the first-coordinate reflection. This changes coordinate convention and does not introduce a new error source.

Default-value audit (b5): This is ordinary composition with a fixed reflection for every time and operator, including a zero error operator. No inverse or off-domain default is introduced; continuity and size estimates remain separate hypotheses or conclusions.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.conjError.summary: The error matrix in the paper coordinates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_co.text: Compose a continuous physical-time function with the normalized clock, assuming the clock maps the normalized interval into its domain.
A continuous error-operator curve remains continuous after composition with the fixed reflection on either side.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_co.summary: Continuity of the conjugated error matrix

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_cr.text: Two continuous three-vector fields have a continuous cross product. This supplies continuity of the third moving-frame vector.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_de.text: A continuous reference slope gives a continuous deviation after the algebraic change of variables, because the reference cosine factor never vanishes. No deviation ODE is assumed here.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_de.summary: Continuous deviation from a continuous reference slope

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_de.text: Recover the deviation as a quotient of the continuous slope plus damping by the positive cosine factor. Thus the deviation envelope is continuous on nonnegative times without appealing to an additional existence theorem.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_de.summary: Continuity of the bounded reference deviation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_fr.text: For continuous nonzero wave and amplitude vectors, all three normalized-frame vectors are continuous on the interval. This is a continuity fact; perpendicularity and orthonormality are handled separately.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_fr.summary: Continuity of the moving orthonormal frame

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_no.text: A continuous vector field that never vanishes on a set has a continuous normalized direction there. The nonvanishing assumption is necessary because normalization is totalized at zero in Lean.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_ph.text: Let $I$ be the compact physical observation set for a continuous gradient $M=B+\mathbf a_p\otimes k_p+E_c$, and assume $t_0+\tau/r\in I$ for $0\le\tau\le T$. If $k$ and $\mathbf a$ are continuous on $I$ and nonzero at those physical times, then $\widehat k\cdot M\widehat a$ and $(\widehat k\times\widehat a)\cdot M\widehat a$ are continuous functions of $\tau\in[0,T]$. These are the two couplings used in Proposition 2.8. This result proves continuity of each coupling, not of their quotient; continuity of $\eta_+/\nu_+$ additionally uses the positive lower bound for $\nu_+$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuousOn_ph.summary: Nonvanishing wave data make both frame entries continuous

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.continuous_damp.text: The quarter-damping term in the reference-slope representation is continuous. This supplies a continuous envelope when reconstructing the deviation from the paper's formula.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.coordinates_clo.text: Convert the vector comparison with the reference wave into three scalar error bounds for the moving-frame coordinates.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.coordinates_clo.summary: Coordinate errors from wave vector comparison

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.cos_referenceAn.text: Translate the paper's reference-angle cosine into the algebraic factor used in the scalar ODE library. The identity is unrestricted in epsilon and time.
Rewrite the squared reference cosine as the reciprocal of one plus the squared tangent parameter. This identifies the denominator in the relative wave-length estimate.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.coupling_budget.text: Choose a common polynomial error budget that dominates the wave-coordinate and slope errors and is at most one half. This puts the rational coupling comparison in a single admissible parameter range.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.coupling_budget.summary: One small error for all coupling estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.coupling_conclu.text: Absorb the concrete error 256 times the eighth power of the horizon times the common budget, plus twice delta, and apply the coupling comparison. This packages the final numerical step of Lemma 2.7 without recreating any numbered input.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.coupling_conclu.summary: Coupling conclusions from a common error budget

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.crossing_streng.text: Assume $0<\varepsilon\le1/2$, $0<\varepsilon_+\le\varepsilon/32$, $H=2/\sqrt{\varepsilon\varepsilon_+}\le T$, and $\lambda>0$. Let $Y$ have the representation (2.13), $0\le e\le\varepsilon/8$, the amplitude formula (2.14), $Y\le1$, and a reference maximum at $\tau_m\in[2/\varepsilon,3/\varepsilon]$ with logarithmic gain at least $\varepsilon^{-1/2}-1$. Suppose continuous nonzero $\mathbf a$ satisfies $|\log(|\mathbf a|/a_{\rm ref})|\le\varepsilon$, and $||k|^2\cos^2\varphi/\lambda^2-1|\le1/2$ for $\tau\ge2/\varepsilon$. If continuous $\rho$ lies between $\cos\varphi/2$ and $3\cos\varphi/2$ for $\tau\ge\sqrt2/\varepsilon$, then a crossing lies in $(\tau_m,H)$. For $M=\max_{[0,T]}|\mathbf a|$, every crossing in $[\tau_m,H]$ has $\exp(-1)/(4\sqrt{\varepsilon\varepsilon_+})\le|\mathbf a||k|/(\lambda M)\le18\exp(3)/\sqrt{\varepsilon\varepsilon_+}$, and $|\mathbf a|\le \exp(3-\varepsilon^{-1/2})M$ on $[0,1]$. The wave equations are replaced here by these explicit comparison assumptions.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.crossing_streng.summary: A comparison argument supplies crossings, strength and early suppression

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.damping_eq.text: Identify epsilon times time times sine of twice the angle with the library damping coefficient. This allows the same derivative equation to be read in both notations.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.deviation_eq_of.text: Given the paper's ansatz for the reference slope, solve algebraically for the library deviation. Strict positivity of the cosine factor justifies the division.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.deviation_eq_of.summary: Recovering the deviation from the slope formula

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.driving_eq.text: Identify the cosine-squared driving term of the paper's scalar equation with the algebraic coefficient used by the Riccati library.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.elapsed_mem_Icc.text: A physical time in the active slab has elapsed normalized time in the prescribed interval. This is the inverse interval calculation used to restrict arbitrary propagated amplitudes.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.elapsed_mem_Icc.summary: The physical slab maps to normalized time

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.errorSize_restr.text: The error size of the active-slab restriction is bounded by the original error size. The scalar inverse-shear contribution is unchanged and the physical supremum can only decrease.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.errorSize_restr.summary: The restricted amplification error is no larger

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.finiteSmallness.text: Transfer the finite-smallness hypothesis to the active slab using the preceding error monotonicity.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.flipCLM.text:
Define the bounded linear map sending a two-coordinate state to the negative of its first coordinate and the unchanged second coordinate. It reconciles the U,V convention with the paper's alpha coordinates.

Default-value audit (b5): This is a globally defined bounded linear reflection on a two-dimensional real space. It involves no division, choice of representative, interval restriction, or exceptional default.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.flipCLM.summary: Reflection of the first amplitude coordinate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.flipCLM_apply.text: Compute the reflection map as the pair consisting of minus the first coordinate and the second coordinate.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.geometry_of_clo.text: Coordinate closeness to the reference vector gives bounds on the first two scaled coordinates used in amplitude estimates. The hypotheses include the interval and epsilon bounds needed to absorb the reference polynomial terms.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.geometry_of_clo.summary: Geometry from nearby scaled wave coordinates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.gradient_contin.text: Combine the older gradient, preceding shear, and correction to obtain continuity of the full gradient on the physical time window. This is used for amplitude ODE solvability.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.gradient_contin.summary: Continuity of the full background gradient

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.growingFactor_r.text: A uniform logarithmic amplitude comparison, positivity, and twice epsilon at most one bound the reference-amplitude ratio by exp one times the actual amplitude ratio. This closes the physical propagator estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.growingFactor_r.summary: Replacing the reference ratio by the actual amplitude ratio

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.hasDerivWithinA.text: Apply the first coordinate projection to a within-interval derivative of a two-coordinate curve. This is ordinary bounded-linear-map differentiation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.hasDerivWithinA.summary: The derivative of the first state coordinate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.hasDerivWithinA.text: Apply the second coordinate projection to a within-interval derivative of a two-coordinate curve.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.hasDerivWithinA.summary: The derivative of the second state coordinate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.mapsTo_restrict.text: The normalized clock lands in the active slab by construction. This supplies the domain hypothesis for the copied amplification data.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.mapsTo_restrict.summary: The clock maps into the restricted interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.nbasis.text:
Abbreviate the preceding moving frame composed with the normalized clock. The expression is defined at every time, while orthonormality and ODE conclusions are asserted only on the admissible interval.

Default-value audit (b5): The original frame is evaluated at every real clock value, including outside its hypothesis window. Its constituent normalizations use total real inverses, so a zero vector has a formal value; orthonormality is used only where the amplification data give nonzero perpendicular vectors.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.ne_zero_of_zeta.text: If the third scaled wave coordinate is nonzero, then the underlying wave vector is nonzero. This supports later normalization of the new wave direction.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.ne_zero_of_zeta.summary: A nonzero third coordinate excludes a zero wave

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.newWaveVector_r.text: Restrict the new wave-vector data and its initial condition to the active slab. No new wave-vector solution is constructed.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.normFactor_cos_.text: Let $T\ge2$, $S^{-2}\le2\delta$, $0\le x\le T^2/4$, $|X-x|\le e_0\le1/2$, $|Q|\le T$, and $|Z-1|\le e_0$. Then $|(X^2+Q^2/S^2+Z^2)/(1+x^2)-1|\le2T^2e_0+2T^2\delta$. For the wave, $(X,Q,Z)=\zeta$, $x=\tan\varphi$ and $|k|^2=\lambda^2(X^2+Q^2/S^2+Z^2)$, so this is the estimate for $|k|^2\cos^2\varphi/\lambda^2$ used in Lemma 2.4. It is an algebraic implication of the coordinate bounds and proves no wave evolution. The displayed real-number formula also has a defined value at $S=0$; its physical application has $S>0$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.normFactor_cos_.summary: Coordinate errors control the cosine-weighted squared norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.norm_bounds_of_.text: At one time let the frame be orthonormal, $\lambda\ne0$, $S>0$, and $k\cdot\mathbf a=0$. Write $k=\lambda(\zeta_1E_1+\zeta_2E_2/S+\zeta_3E_3)$ and $\mathbf a=\alpha_1E_1/S+\alpha_2E_2+\alpha_3E_3/S$. Assume $T\ge1$, $|\zeta_1|\le T^2$, $|\zeta_2|\le T$, $\zeta_3\ge1/2$, $|Y|\le1$, and $\max\{|h-1|,|l|\}\le d\le1/2$, where $h=\alpha_2/a_{\rm ref}$ and $l=-(\alpha_1+Y\alpha_2)/(a_{\rm ref}\cos\varphi)$. Then $\alpha_2\le|\mathbf a|\le(1+40T^4S^{-2})\alpha_2$. This pointwise result supplies the norm comparison in (2.17); it assumes the normalized closeness rather than obtaining it from the differential equations.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.norm_bounds_of_.summary: Closeness to the growing state controls the physical norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.norm_conjError_.text: The norm of the conjugated error is at most the original error norm, using the norm-one bounds for the reflection on both sides.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.norm_flipCLM_le.text: Bound the operator norm of the diagonal reflection by one. The inequality is enough to transfer the error-operator estimate through conjugation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.norm_flipCLM_le.summary: The amplitude reflection does not increase norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.norm_movingAmpl.text: On $[0,T]$, let $Y$ solve the reference Riccati equation with nonnegative deviation $e$. Let the transverse amplitude satisfy the two perturbed reference equations in $(U,V)=(-\beta_1,\beta_2)$, with continuous error $R$ bounded by a continuous function $\eta$. For $0\le a\le t\le T$, assume an orthonormal frame, $\lambda\ne0$, $S\ge1$, $|\zeta_1|,|\zeta_2|\le S$, $1/2\le\zeta_3\le3/2$, $|Y|\le1$, and $|\zeta_1-\tan\varphi|\le1/2$ throughout $[a,t]$. Put $D=\int_a^t(1+|Y|)^2\eta/\cos\varphi$. The formal statement gives $|\mathbf b(t)|\le126S\exp(2D)a_{\rm ref}(t)|\mathbf b(a)|/a_{\rm ref}(a)$. The operator norm of $R$ uses the maximum norm on pairs. This is a conditional amplitude estimate, before the smallness condition bounds $D$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.norm_movingAmpl.summary: The normalized error integral controls arbitrary transverse amplitudes

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.norm_zeta_le.text: Let $T\ge2$. In the preceding wave’s orthonormal frame, write the new wave vector at physical time $t_0+\tau/r$ as $k=\lambda(\zeta_1E_1+\zeta_2E_2/S+\zeta_3E_3)$. If $|\zeta_1|\le T^2$, $|\zeta_2|\le T$, and $1/2\le\zeta_3\le3/2$, then the Euclidean norm of the scaled vector satisfies $|\zeta|\le3T^2$. The formal statement uses the scaled coordinates defined by the displayed pairings, even for arbitrary real $\lambda$; the physical wave assumes $\lambda>0$. This result only combines the three coordinate hypotheses and does not derive them from the wave equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.norm_zeta_le.summary: Three coordinate bounds give a Euclidean norm bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.norm_zeta_sub_l.text: Bound the norm of the wave-vector difference by the sum of its three scalar coordinate errors. This converts the quantitative nilpotent estimate to the statement of Lemma 2.4.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.norm_zeta_sub_l.summary: A vector error from scalar coordinate errors

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.normalizedCoupl.text: Under the moving-frame and nonvanishing assumptions, identify the algebraic normalized first and second couplings with the physical couplings divided by the preceding first coupling.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.normalizedCoupl.summary: Converting normalized couplings to physical rates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.normalizedState.text: Let $Y$ solve the reference Riccati equation on $[0,T]$ and have nonnegative deviation $e=(Y+\varepsilon\tau\sin(2\varphi)/4)/\cos\varphi-1$. Suppose $(U,V)$ satisfies the reference linear system with continuous added operator $R$, and $\|R\|\le\eta$ for continuous $\eta$. For $0\le a\le t\le T$, set $h=V/a_{\rm ref}$, $l=(U-YV)/(a_{\rm ref}\cos\varphi)$ and $D=\int_a^t(1+|Y|)^2\eta/\cos\varphi$. The formal statement gives $\|(h,l)(t)\|_\infty\le2\exp(2D)\|(h,l)(a)\|_\infty$. It does not state the paper’s numerical bound $4$ by itself: a further smallness estimate for $D$ is required. Here $U=-\alpha_1$, $V=\alpha_2$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.normalizedState.summary: An integral error bound controls the normalized solution

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.normalizedStrai.text: Identify the normalized strain, including preceding shear and correction, with the full physical gradient divided by the amplification rate.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.normalized_clos.text: On $[0,T]$, let $Y$ solve the reference Riccati equation with $Y(0)=1$ and nonnegative deviation $e$. Suppose the perturbed reference system for $(U,V)$ has $U(0)=V(0)=1$, continuous error $R$, and $\|R\|\le\eta$ for continuous $\eta$. Write $a_{\rm ref}=\exp\int_0^\tau Y$, $h=V/a_{\rm ref}$, $l=(U-YV)/(a_{\rm ref}\cos\varphi)$ and $D(t)=\int_0^t(1+|Y|)^2\eta/\cos\varphi$. Then $\max\{|h(t)-1|,|l(t)|\}\le4\exp(2D(t))D(t)$ for $0\le t\le T$. In paper notation the initial amplitude components are $(-1,1)$ because $U=-\alpha_1$. This quantitative bound precedes the separate argument that makes its right side at most $1/2$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.normalized_clos.summary: The normalized solution stays near its initial constant state

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S2b.normalized_fact.text:
For nonzero perpendicular preceding wave data with continuous trace-free $B$ and continuous $E_c$ on compact $I
i t_0$, put $\sigma=|k_p(t_0)||\mathbf a_p(t_0)|$, $
u=B_{12}(t_0)>0$, $\eta=B_{32}(t_0)>0$, $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$, $S=\sigma/r$, $\varepsilon=\eta/
u$. Let $\delta$ be the sum of the two relative coupling suprema, $\sup_I\|B\|/r$, and $\sup_I\|E_c\|/
