TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.contDiff_cofram.summary: Restriction to the transverse plane preserves smoothness

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.contDiff_slabSl.text: Joint smoothness on a time slab times all spatial parameters gives smoothness in the parameters at each allowed time. No extension of the time variable beyond the slab is asserted.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.contDiff_slabSl.summary: A smooth time slab has smooth spatial slices

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.d2Scale.text:
The power of the base scale: the chain scale `D` dominates `D₀ ^ d2Scale`. The bridge converts between coordinate word norms in Appendix D and Fréchet derivative bounds used by the fixed-plane construction. The conversion changes constants depending on the order, not the absolute parent exponent.

Default-value audit (b5): This is the fixed natural number 64. There is no choice, denominator or degenerate branch; it deliberately provides slack between a base parent scale and the scale of the copied chain.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.d2Scale.summary: The fixed exponent separating the two parent scales

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.derivWithin_add.text: The derivative within the closed interval of a sum equals the sum of the two derivatives when both summands are differentiable there. The nonempty interval supplies the local uniqueness of the derivative at its endpoints.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.derivWithin_add.summary: Time differentiation distributes over addition on the interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.derivWithin_smu.text: Constant scalar multiplication commutes with the time derivative within the interval for a differentiable function. This proves linearity of the time operator in the solution-family space.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.derivWithin_smu.summary: Time differentiation respects constant scaling on the interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.evA.text:
Evaluation of a coefficient at the empty word and the time `t`. The seminorms measure the empty word on the closed interval. They become norms of higher derivatives only after applying the commuting shifts; positivity of the weight and explicit boundedness justify the suprema.

They ignore higher-word entries and make no assertion about that time lying in the slab. The seminorm definitions index their time argument by the slab to enforce the intended domain.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.evA.summary: Evaluate the undifferentiated coefficient at one time

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.evE.summary: Evaluate the undifferentiated solution at one time

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.evF.summary: Evaluate the undifferentiated forcing at one time

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.exists_const_ge.text: A constant bounding the finitely many rescaling constants `R m`, `m ≤ N`. Here the lift is the deformation restricted to the fixed carrier plane, and the pullback is the inverse deformation followed by the transverse projection and orthogonal projection onto that plane. This avoids a separate Gram-matrix inverse estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.exists_const_ge.summary: Bound finitely many derivative constants at once

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.exists_leading_.text: The initial velocity and frequency-scaled pressure in (5.22) follow from the scaled envelope-amplitude and pressure operator jets on a time slice. The leading profile is built from a seed, a compact label envelope and the one-dimensional phase wave. All derivative orders use the same sufficiently small envelope radius; the estimates are on the active time interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.exists_leading_.summary: Slow derivatives control the leading velocity and pressure

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.exists_leading_.text: A switch of magnitude at most one leaves the common polynomial budget for the initial velocity and frequency-normalized pressure unchanged. The leading profile is built from a seed, a compact label envelope and the one-dimensional phase wave. All derivative orders use the same sufficiently small envelope radius; the estimates are on the active time interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.exists_leading_.summary: A bounded switch preserves the leading polynomial estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.exists_parent_c.text: The actual first parent coframe jets supply the label Lipschitz estimates for the flow Jacobians, material gradient and transverse projection. The transported wave-vector comparison is relative to the reference label. This is a finite derivative estimate for the localized leading profile. The phase width is positive and at most one, and the spatial envelope is kept separate from the central amplitude weight.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.exists_parent_c.summary: First derivatives control variation across the envelope

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.exists_scaled_d.text: The scaled derivatives of the wave profile are bounded by `C h` (Lemma 3.1 through `waveProfile_bounds`, replacing the original constants `1/2` and the library bounds). This is a finite derivative estimate for the localized leading profile. The phase width is positive and at most one, and the spatial envelope is kept separate from the central amplitude weight.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.exists_scaled_d.summary: Weighted profile derivatives have size proportional to the width

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.exists_scaled_w.text: Scaling the phase variable by the profile width gives uniform finite derivative bounds for the wave and its pressure primitive. This is a finite derivative estimate for the localized leading profile. The phase width is positive and at most one, and the spatial envelope is kept separate from the central amplitude weight.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.exists_scaled_w.summary: Rescaled wave profiles and primitives have bounded derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.exists_switched.text: The finite-order leading profile and pressure bounds follow from the corresponding slow-factor bounds. The pressure slow factor includes the frequency normalization in (5.22). This is a finite derivative estimate for the localized leading profile. The phase width is positive and at most one, and the spatial envelope is kept separate from the central amplitude weight.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.exists_switched.summary: Slow amplitude estimates control the leading profiles

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.fixedTransverse.text: The fixed transverse generator is the compression `π (-2 (G Q)(M F)) ι`. Here the lift is the deformation restricted to the fixed carrier plane, and the pullback is the inverse deformation followed by the transverse projection and orthogonal projection onto that plane. This avoids a separate Gram-matrix inverse estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.fixedTransverse.summary: Express the transverse generator in ambient coordinates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.g_l_pos.text: The time weight is positive at the left endpoint because the slab has ordered endpoints and positivity throughout its closed interval. This legitimizes the initial-data division in pF.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.hasDerivWithinA.text: A time translation carries a derivative within a translated interval to the corresponding derivative in the original time coordinate. It lets the zero-start ODE estimate be used with activation time as the left endpoint.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.hasDerivWithinA.summary: Translate the initial time in an ordinary differential equation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.hierarchyRelayW.text: The phase primitive of a linear combination of two zero-mean profiles costs no additional word length (shadow of `hierarchyRelayWordBound_linearPrimitive`, by (D.5) of Lemma D.1 through `Lib.S5a.relayWordBound_linearPrimitive_of_D1`; the positivity of `ℓ` and `h` is needed by (D.1)). This module passes supplied proofs of Lemmas 3.1, D.1 and D.2, and a derivative recurrence obtained from D.3, into the copied transverse argument. The local class is a bundle of hypotheses, not an additional axiom.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.hierarchyRelayW.summary: The phase primitive preserves the derivative order

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.inv_g_nonneg.text: The inverse time weight is nonnegative. The seminorms measure the empty word on the closed interval. They become norms of higher derivatives only after applying the commuting shifts; positivity of the weight and explicit boundedness justify the suprema.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.isSymm_cons.text: Prepending one direction to a permutation-invariant word family preserves permutation invariance of the remaining letters. This proves that the shift maps preserve their ambient linear spaces.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.isSymm_cons.summary: A further derivative preserves permutation invariance

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.iteratedFDeriv_.text: Replacing the finite index type of an iterated Fréchet derivative by an equal-length finite type leaves its evaluation unchanged after the corresponding vector reindexing. This is a type-level identification, not a further analytic estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.iteratedFDeriv_.summary: Changing the derivative index type preserves evaluation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.jetD3.text: Lemma D.3 (through `hD3`) applied to the jet spaces: the constant `Cn` depends only on the index type, the order `n` and the bound `q` of (D.7). Lemma D.3 is applied to families of derivative words of a finite-dimensional linear ODE. The forcing norm includes the initial datum, and the coefficient budget is the zero-order stability constant times the interval length times a positive-order derivative bound.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.jetD3.summary: Apply derivative lifting to the linear equation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.jetPower_of_coe.text: Coefficient power bounds control pointwise derivatives. The bridge converts between coordinate word norms in Appendix D and Fréchet derivative bounds used by the fixed-plane construction. The conversion changes constants depending on the order, not the absolute parent exponent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.jetPower_of_coe.summary: Coefficient power bounds control pointwise derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.labelDirection_.text: With unit label scale, an Appendix D label direction is exactly the corresponding Euclidean coordinate vector. The adjacent sum_coordinate' theorem proves reconstruction by a coordinate sum; the source comment above this theorem describes that different identity.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.labelDirection_.summary: Unit label directions are the coordinate vectors

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.le_supSem.text: Each member of a pointwise bounded family of seminorms is bounded by its supremum seminorm. Boundedness is supplied explicitly, so the supremum is not being treated as finite without a proof.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.le_supSem.summary: Each member lies below the supremum seminorm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.leafBounds_mono.text: The leaf jets at the scale `D` hold at every larger scale. The bridge converts between coordinate word norms in Appendix D and Fréchet derivative bounds used by the fixed-plane construction. The conversion changes constants depending on the order, not the absolute parent exponent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.leafBounds_mono.summary: Coefficient bounds persist when the parent scale increases

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.leavesOf.text:
The class `Leaves` from `h3_1`, `hD_1` and the weighted derivative recurrence. This module passes supplied proofs of Lemmas 3.1, D.1 and D.2, and a derivative recurrence obtained from D.3, into the copied transverse argument. The local class is a bundle of hypotheses, not an additional axiom.

Default-value audit (b5): Classical choice selects Φ from the existence proof supplied as hode, with its certified properties. No fallback instance is fabricated when hode is absent. The resulting class carries the actual h31, hD1 and hD2 proofs supplied by the caller.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.leavesOf.summary: Assemble the cited estimates as explicit inputs

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.lemma_5_3_of_le.text: Assume Proposition 5.1, Lemmas 3.1, D.1, D.2 and the weighted derivative estimate for linear ordinary differential equations supplied by Lemma D.3. The formal implication then proves Lemma 5.3. The parent on $0<T\le1$ is smooth, odd, periodic and divergence free, with $\mathsf D\ge2$, Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$ for $U,R_U$, gradient and deformation bounds $\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p-\nabla R_U\le I$. Require $0\le t_0<T$, $\lambda=|\kappa(t_0,0)|\ge1$, central transverse stability and coupling as in (5.5), and $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$. A sufficiently small $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$ gives $\|V\|_{[n],\gamma}\le C_n\mathsf D^C(\gamma(t_0)^{-1}\|V(t_0)\|_{[n]}+\|f\|_{[n],\gamma})$ for supported transverse solutions, the zero-initial velocity-pressure estimate, the leading-wave bound and $|\mathbf a(t,a)|\le2|\mathbf a(t,0)|$, $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a>0$ on $|a|\le2\ell_*$. The first estimate requires profiles smooth on all of $[0,T]$; the leading bound uses a separate homogeneous estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.lemma_5_3_of_le.summary: One radius makes all conclusions of Lemma 5.3 hold

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.linearODEWordFa.text:
The amplification factor of the word recurrence (shadow of `linearODEWordFactor`, whose explicit recursion is replaced by the factor of Lemma D.3). This module passes supplied proofs of Lemmas 3.1, D.1 and D.2, and a derivative recurrence obtained from D.3, into the copied transverse argument. The local class is a bundle of hypotheses, not an additional axiom.

Default-value audit (b5): This reads the factor stored in the current Leaves instance. It is a total real-valued function, but the nonnegativity and monotonicity lemmas apply only to a nonnegative coefficient budget. There is no asserted explicit recurrence or growth bound for the chosen factor.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.linearODEWordFa.summary: The chosen factor in the derivative recurrence

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.linearODEWordFa.text: The amplification factor `linearODEWordFactor` is monotone. TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.linearODEWordFa.summary: The derivative amplification factor increases with the coefficient bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.linearODEWordFa.summary: The derivative amplification factor is nonnegative

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.linearODE_weigh.text: The weighted derivative estimate applies to localized initial data and forcing on the active interval. Stability and positive-order coefficient estimates are used on their common closed support. The argument works on a nonempty closed active interval and with a positive time weight. Spatial derivatives act on the label and independent phase, while the time weight is divided out only after those derivatives.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.linearODE_weigh.summary: Bound weighted derivatives with supported initial data

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.lsum.text:
The sum over Leibniz distributions of derivatives. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.

Default-value audit (b5): The recursion is finite in the word length; the empty word contributes F([],[]) once. Repeated letters are counted through their different distributions, producing the required Leibniz multiplicities. There is no infinite sum, derivative assumption or division.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.lsum.summary: The sum over Leibniz distributions of derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.lsum_add.text: The Leibniz sum distributes over addition. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.lsum_add.summary: The Leibniz sum distributes over addition

It does not prove that derivative maps commute, despite the source comment. The actual commuting-shift results are DE_comm, DF_comm and DA_comm.

Only derivatives through the fixed order and times in the closed interval are retained; time differentiation is taken within that interval.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.lsum_eq_splits.text: The sum over splits is the list sum over `hierarchyLeibnizSplits`. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.lsum_neg.text: The Leibniz sum respects negation. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.lsum_perm.summary: Permuting derivative directions preserves the product expansion

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.mul_of_D2.text: Lemma D.2(a) in the pointwise form: products of jets with a power bound keep a power bound, with the exponent `2 max(a, b)`; the constants depend only on the value spaces, the input constants and the exponents. The bridge converts between coordinate word norms in Appendix D and Fréchet derivative bounds used by the fixed-plane construction. The conversion changes constants depending on the order, not the absolute parent exponent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.mul_of_D2.summary: Use the supplied coefficient product estimate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.norm_iteratedFD.text: A fixed contraction decreases derivative norms. Here the lift is the deformation restricted to the fixed carrier plane, and the pullback is the inverse deformation followed by the transverse projection and orthogonal projection onto that plane. This avoids a separate Gram-matrix inverse estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.norm_iteratedFD.summary: A fixed contraction decreases derivative norms

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.norm_iteratedFD.text: The lift `F ↦ F ι` to the transverse plane does not increase the jets. Here the lift is the deformation restricted to the fixed carrier plane, and the pullback is the inverse deformation followed by the transverse projection and orthogonal projection onto that plane. This avoids a separate Gram-matrix inverse estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.norm_iteratedFD.summary: Restriction to the transverse plane decreases derivative norms

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.norm_iteratedFD.text: The compression `π E ι` of a smooth field does not increase the jets. Here the lift is the deformation restricted to the fixed carrier plane, and the pullback is the inverse deformation followed by the transverse projection and orthogonal projection onto that plane. This avoids a separate Gram-matrix inverse estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.norm_iteratedFD.summary: Compression to the transverse plane decreases derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.norm_iteratedFD.text: The pointwise jet of a coefficient is at most `3 ^ m` times the order-`m` size `|c|_m`. The bridge converts between coordinate word norms in Appendix D and Fréchet derivative bounds used by the fixed-plane construction. The conversion changes constants depending on the order, not the absolute parent exponent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.norm_iteratedFD.summary: Coordinate derivative sums bound the Fréchet norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.norm_iteratedFD.text: The projection onto the transverse plane applied on the left does not increase the jets of a field with values in `S →L Vec3`. Here the lift is the deformation restricted to the fixed carrier plane, and the pullback is the inverse deformation followed by the transverse projection and orthogonal projection onto that plane. This avoids a separate Gram-matrix inverse estimate.

The projection onto the transverse plane applied on the left does not increase the jets of a field with values in `Vec3 →L Vec3`. Here the lift is the deformation restricted to the fixed carrier plane, and the pullback is the inverse deformation followed by the transverse projection and orthogonal projection onto that plane. This avoids a separate Gram-matrix inverse estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.norm_iteratedFD.summary: Orthogonal projection decreases ambient coefficient derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.norm_label_diff.text: A uniform bound on the first Fréchet derivative gives a Lipschitz difference bound between two labels. This elementary mean-value estimate turns the parent coefficient jets into a perturbation bound across the small envelope.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.norm_label_diff.summary: The first derivative bounds differences between labels

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.norm_listMapSum.text: The norm of a finite list sum, divided by a positive weight, is at most the sum of given termwise weighted bounds. This controls the differentiated Leibniz expansion after the time weight is applied.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.norm_word_inv_s.text: At a fixed time, multiplication by the inverse time weight factors through every parameter derivative word. The spatial derivative does not differentiate the weight; the norm acquires its scalar absolute value.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.norm_word_inv_s.summary: The time weight factors out of spatial derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.odeIdx.text: The weighted word recurrence at a fixed point for a finite ordered set of directions, from Lemma D.3 (`hD3`): the constant `Cn` only depends on the index type, the order `n` and the bound `q` of the product `K (r - l) C · #words`. Lemma D.3 is applied to families of derivative words of a finite-dimensional linear ODE. The forcing norm includes the initial datum, and the coefficient budget is the zero-order stability constant times the interval length times a positive-order derivative bound.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.odeIdx.summary: Lift the estimate for finitely many derivative directions

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.odeWordBound_of.text: Assume Lemma D.3. Let $x_t=A(t,p)x+f(t,p)$ be smooth on $[l,r]\times P$, where $l<r$ and $P,E$ are finite-dimensional real normed spaces. Let $g>0$ be continuously differentiable. Fix constant differentiation directions and $S\subset P$. Suppose every homogeneous solution satisfies $\|y(v)\|/g(v)\le K\|y(u)\|/g(u)$ for $p\in S$ and $l\le u\le v\le r$. For every ordered derivative of length at most $N$, assume the initial value divided by $g(l)$ is bounded by $B$, the forcing divided by $g(t)$ by $H$, and every positive-order coefficient derivative by $C$, uniformly on $S$. Here $K,B,H,C\ge0$. Then on $[l,r]\times S$ each solution derivative satisfies $\|\partial^w x(t,p)\|/g(t)\le\Phi_N(K(r-l)C)K(B+(r-l)H)$. The universal factor is nonnegative and nondecreasing in its argument. No smallness of $C$ is assumed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.odeWordBound_of.summary: A weighted propagation bound extends to higher derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.opNorm_le_bound.text: If a continuous multilinear map is bounded by a constant on tuples of unit vectors, its operator norm has the same bound. This converts directional derivative estimates into Fréchet derivative estimates.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.opNorm_le_bound.summary: Unit vectors determine the multilinear operator norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.opNorm_le_coord.text: The operator norm of a multilinear map on `ℝ³` is at most the sum of its values on coordinate vectors. The bridge converts between coordinate word norms in Appendix D and Fréchet derivative bounds used by the fixed-plane construction. The conversion changes constants depending on the order, not the absolute parent exponent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.opNorm_le_coord.summary: Coordinate evaluations bound a multilinear operator

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.oscillatoryPhas.text: The actual normalized pressure has one inverse factor of the carrier at every order, with the remaining constants given by the normalized covector and strain coefficient bounds. The argument works on a nonempty closed active interval and with a positive time weight. Spatial derivatives act on the label and independent phase, while the time weight is divided out only after those derivatives.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.oscillatoryPhas.summary: Pressure gains one inverse carrier frequency

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.oscillatoryVelo.text: Zero-start version of the weighted estimate for the transverse velocity. The argument works on a nonempty closed active interval and with a positive time weight. Spatial derivatives act on the label and independent phase, while the time weight is divided out only after those derivatives.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.oscillatoryVelo.summary: Bound transverse velocity with zero initial data

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.oscillatoryVelo.text: The finite weighted norm of the physical transverse velocity follows from the fixed-plane forward estimate and the word bounds of the two coframes. The force is measured in physical coordinates. The argument works on a nonempty closed active interval and with a positive time weight. Spatial derivatives act on the label and independent phase, while the time weight is divided out only after those derivatives.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.oscillatoryVelo.summary: Transfer the coordinate estimate to transverse velocity

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.pA.text:
The uniform coefficient seminorm on the time interval. The seminorms measure the empty word on the closed interval. They become norms of higher derivatives only after applying the commuting shifts; positivity of the weight and explicit boundedness justify the suprema.

Default-value audit (b5): The suprema are justified by the explicit boundedness lemmas and the slab is nonempty. The positive time weight legitimizes both the timewise division and pF's initial-value division. Only the empty word is measured before derivative shifts, so these are seminorms on whole families, not separating norms there.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.pA.summary: The uniform coefficient seminorm on the time interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.phaseJetBound_b.text: A continuous bilinear map applied to two smooth fields with finite derivative bounds again has such a bound. The output constant contains the bilinear operator norm and a Leibniz factor depending on the order.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.phaseJetBound_b.summary: Bilinear products preserve finite derivative bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.phaseJetBound_c.text: A field of continuous linear maps can be applied to a vector field while retaining finite derivative bounds. It is the bilinear product estimate specialized to operator evaluation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.phaseJetBound_c.summary: Apply an operator field with controlled derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.phaseJetBound_c.text: Composing a smooth field with a fixed linear contraction preserves its finite derivative bound. This is used to restrict or project ambient coefficients onto the transverse plane.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.phaseJetBound_c.summary: A fixed contraction preserves derivative bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.phaseJetBound_c.text: A constant scalar multiplies every derivative bound by its absolute value. No derivative of the scalar appears, since the scalar is independent of label and phase.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.phaseJetBound_n.text: The frequency-normalized pressure amplitude operator is the product of the normalized covector, the strain and the reciprocal squared covector norm. The leading profile is built from a seed, a compact label envelope and the one-dimensional phase wave. All derivative orders use the same sufficiently small envelope radius; the estimates are on the active time interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.phaseJetBound_n.summary: Bound the frequency normalized pressure amplitude

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.phaseJetBound_n.text: The carrier-normalized pressure operator costs a fixed power (D^7) through every fixed order of radius-normalized label derivatives. The rescaled jets of the coefficients `M`, `κ/λ` and `λ²/|κ|²` are bounded by Lemma D.2(c) (`rescale_of_D2`) at the base scale `D₀ ≤ D^{1/64}`. The leading profile is built from a seed, a compact label envelope and the one-dimensional phase wave. All derivative orders use the same sufficiently small envelope radius; the estimates are on the active time interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.phaseJetBound_n.summary: The pressure amplitude has uniform polynomial cost

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.phaseJetBound_s.text: A scalar phase function with bounded derivatives through order N gives the corresponding mixed Fréchet derivative bound for the field depending only on the scaled phase. Label directions contribute no derivatives, and the scaling contributes the appropriate powers of the width.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.phaseJetBound_s.summary: A phase function gives a mixed derivative bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.phaseJetBound_s.text: Finite derivative bounds for a localized vector amplitude and a scalar phase factor yield a bound for their product. The Leibniz factor depends on the retained order; the support remains in the amplitude factor.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.phaseJetBound_s.summary: Multiply localized amplitudes by phase profiles

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.phaseOperatorWo.text: For smooth summands the derivative word of their sum is the sum of the two derivative words. This permits the coefficient-times-solution and forcing contributions to the differentiated ODE to be estimated separately.
If two smooth fields agree on a neighborhood of the evaluation point, every fixed derivative word has the same value there. This justifies zero derivatives outside a closed support.

The parameter words of a linear solve on `[l, r]` satisfy the differentiated equation in time. Smooth parameter derivatives of the actual solution supply the abstract families used for D.3. Only derivatives through the fixed order and times in the closed interval are retained; time differentiation is taken within that interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.phaseOperatorWo.summary: Commute parameter derivatives with the linear time equation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.phaseOperatorWo.text: Mapping the letters of a derivative word through an index map is the same as changing the family of directions by that map. This reduces an arbitrary finite word to a finite index type before applying D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.phaseOperatorWo.summary: Reindex the directions of a derivative word

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.phaseOperatorWo.text: Every derivative word applied to the zero field is zero, including the empty word. This handles vanishing forcing and zero extensions in the weighted ODE estimate.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.phasePrimitive_.text: Multiplication by a constant scalar or fixed vector factor commutes with the zero-mean phase primitive under the stated integrability hypotheses. This separates the time weight and slow coefficients from phase integration.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.phasePrimitive_.summary: Constant scaling commutes with the phase primitive

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.qA.text:
The coefficient size at one time. The seminorms measure the empty word on the closed interval. They become norms of higher derivatives only after applying the commuting shifts; positivity of the weight and explicit boundedness justify the suprema.

Default-value audit (b5): The time argument is a member of the nonempty slab, so the weight divisions in qE and qF have positive denominators. The interval length is positive. These seminorms inspect only the empty word and may have nontrivial kernels; qA uses no weight division.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.qA_apply.text: Evaluate the pointwise coefficient seminorm. The seminorms measure the empty word on the closed interval. They become norms of higher derivatives only after applying the commuting shifts; positivity of the weight and explicit boundedness justify the suprema.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.rescale_of_D2.text: Lemma D.2(c) in the pointwise form: under `ℓ ≤ D^{-a}`, the rescaled jets `y ↦ f (ℓ y)` of a coefficient with the power bound are at most `C' D^a` at every order, and at most `C' ℓ D^{2a}` at every positive order. The bridge converts between coordinate word norms in Appendix D and Fréchet derivative bounds used by the fixed-plane construction. The conversion changes constants depending on the order, not the absolute parent exponent.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.rescaled_cofram.text: The rescaled jets of the lift `J`, the pullback `R` and the generator `A` of the transverse coframe, by Lemma D.2(c) (`rescale_of_D2`) applied to the ambient coefficients `F`, `G Q` and `-2 (G Q)(M F)` at the base scale `D₀` with `D₀ ^ d2Scale ≤ D`, and the fixed contractions. Here the lift is the deformation restricted to the fixed carrier plane, and the pullback is the inverse deformation followed by the transverse projection and orthogonal projection onto that plane. This avoids a separate Gram-matrix inverse estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.rescaled_cofram.summary: Small labels give uniform coframe derivative bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.rescaled_pressu.text: Fix $N\in\mathbb N$ and nonnegative constants $W_j$. Assume Lemmas 3.1, D.1, D.2 and the weighted derivative recurrence supplied by Lemma D.3. Let $\mathsf D,\mathsf D_0\ge1$, $\mathsf D_0^{64}\le\mathsf D$, $\ell_*>0$ and $\ell_*\mathsf D^{16}\le1$. Each coefficient $c=M,\kappa/\lambda,\lambda^2/|\kappa|^2$ must be smooth on $\mathbb R^3$ and satisfy $\|D^jc(a)\|\le W_j\mathsf D_0^{16(j+1)}$ for every $j,a$. There is $C\ge1$, fixed before these coefficients and scales, such that every derivative of order $0\le j\le N$ of the three rescaled coefficients $c(\ell_*a)$ is bounded respectively by $C\mathsf D$, $C\mathsf D^2$ and $C\mathsf D^4$. These are operator-norm bounds, uniform in $a$. The statement assumes neither $\lambda\ne0$ nor $\kappa\ne0$; division by zero is zero. Source and velocity estimates are still needed for (5.24).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.rescaled_pressu.summary: Small labels absorb derivative costs in pressure coefficients

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.rg_nonneg.text: The interval length divided by the weight is nonnegative. The seminorms measure the empty word on the closed interval. They become norms of higher derivatives only after applying the commuting shifts; positivity of the weight and explicit boundedness justify the suprema.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.rg_nonneg.summary: The interval length divided by the weight is nonnegative

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.sSup_word_nonne.text: Every word supremum in a `CoefficientPower` is nonnegative. TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.sSup_word_nonne.summary: The supremum of derivative sizes is nonnegative

Default-value audit (b5): Nonnegativity of the scalar is an explicit argument, so the formula c‖f(u)‖ satisfies the seminorm axioms even at c=0. It can vanish on a nontrivial kernel, and no separating norm is claimed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.scaledNormSem.summary: A nonnegative multiple of a linear image norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.scaledNormSem_a.summary: Evaluate the scaled linear image seminorm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.seedNear_mono.text: If the parent scale is positive and is increased, the same near-origin amplitude comparison remains valid and the reciprocal coupling lower bounds weaken. This is a monotonicity statement about already proved bounds, not a construction of the seed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.seedNear_mono.summary: Enlarging the parent bound weakens the seed estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.shiftLM.text:
Add one direction to a derivative family. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.

Default-value audit (b5): Prepending a letter is a total linear reindexing of any word family. It becomes a derivative operator only on families already known to represent derivatives. The map has no hidden continuity or bounded-operator claim.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.shiftLM_apply.text: Evaluate a family after adding a direction. These linear spaces encode the hypotheses of D.3 for an ODE with an initial datum. Permutation symmetry makes the derivative shifts commute; the equation uses the negative Leibniz expansion of coefficient multiplication.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.shiftLM_apply.summary: Evaluate a family after adding a direction

The bridge converts between coordinate word norms in Appendix D and Fréchet derivative bounds used by the fixed-plane construction. The conversion changes constants depending on the order, not the absolute parent exponent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.sum_coordinate'.summary: Coordinate vectors reconstruct every spatial vector

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.supSem.text:
The supremum of a pointwise bounded family of seminorms. The seminorms measure the empty word on the closed interval. They become norms of higher derivatives only after applying the commuting shifts; positivity of the weight and explicit boundedness justify the suprema.

Default-value audit (b5): The family must be pointwise bounded above; this hypothesis prevents treating an unbounded real supremum as a meaningful finite estimate. The resulting object is a seminorm, possibly with a nontrivial kernel. In slab applications the index type is nonempty, though the general definition does not impose that.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.supSem_apply.text: Evaluate the supremum seminorm pointwise. The seminorms measure the empty word on the closed interval. They become norms of higher derivatives only after applying the commuting shifts; positivity of the weight and explicit boundedness justify the suprema.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.supSem_le.text: Upper bound for a supremum seminorm from a pointwise bound. The seminorms measure the empty word on the closed interval. They become norms of higher derivatives only after applying the commuting shifts; positivity of the weight and explicit boundedness justify the suprema.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.supSem_le.summary: A common bound controls the supremum seminorm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.transverseCofra.text: Assume Lemmas 3.1, D.1, D.2 and the weighted derivative recurrence supplied by Lemma D.3. Let $\mathsf D\ge1$, $W_j\ge0$, $\kappa(a)=G(a)^Tk$ and $P_\kappa=\kappa\otimes\kappa/|\kappa|^2$. Suppose $F,G,M,P_\kappa$ are smooth matrix fields on $\mathbb R^3$, each satisfying $\|D^jc(a)\|\le W_j\mathsf D^{16(j+1)}$. Then $G(I-P_\kappa)$ and $-2G(I-P_\kappa)MF$ satisfy the respective bounds $C_j\mathsf D^{32(j+1)}$ and $C'_j\mathsf D^{64(j+1)}$ for every derivative order, with constants fixed before $k,\mathsf D,F,G,M$. The product estimate of Lemma D.2 proves these bounds. No inverse relation between $F,G$ is required. For the parent deformation they encode the projected inverse and the right-hand-side coefficient in (5.18). At $\kappa=0$, division by zero makes $P_\kappa=0$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.transverseCofra.summary: Product estimates control the projected inverse and generator

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.waveProfile_bou.text: The profile bounds of Lemma 3.1 in the form consumed by the chain: constants `C`, `C_j` independent of `h`, from `L.t31`. This module passes supplied proofs of Lemmas 3.1, D.1 and D.2, and a derivative recurrence obtained from D.3, into the copied transverse argument. The local class is a bundle of hypotheses, not an additional axiom.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.wbdd_of_continu.text: A continuous function on the compact slab is bounded relative to its positive continuous weight. Compactness and positivity bound the reciprocal weight; no lower bound uniform over all possible slabs is asserted.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.wbdd_of_continu.summary: Continuity gives a bound relative to the positive weight

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.weighted_homoge.text: The weighted homogeneous ODE estimate holds in the full Fréchet operator norm, by applying the word recurrence to arbitrary unit directions. The leading profile is built from a seed, a compact label envelope and the one-dimensional phase wave. All derivative orders use the same sufficiently small envelope radius; the estimates are on the active time interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.weighted_homoge.summary: Bound all derivatives of a homogeneous linear solution

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.wordA.text: Iterating the coefficient shift maps reads the coefficient family at the corresponding derivative word. The empty-word coefficient seminorm then measures exactly the required differentiated coefficient.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.wordA.summary: Read a coefficient derivative from its shifted family

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.wordE.text: Iterating the solution shift maps reads the solution family at the concatenated derivative word. The identity connects the abstract finite norm in D.3 with the concrete parameter-word derivatives.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.wordE.summary: Read a solution derivative from its shifted family

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.wordF_fst.text: Iterating the forcing-data shifts reads the forcing component at the corresponding word. This is the forcing half of the combined source-and-initial-data norm used in D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.wordF_fst.summary: Read a forcing derivative from its shifted family

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.wordF_snd.text: Iterating the forcing-data shifts reads the initial-value component at the corresponding word. This keeps differentiated initial data in the lifted estimate rather than treating them as zero.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.wordF_snd.summary: Read an initial derivative from its shifted family

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.word_eq_coordin.text: The word `List.ofFn β` of coordinate derivatives is the multilinear map on the coordinate vectors. The bridge converts between coordinate word norms in Appendix D and Fréchet derivative bounds used by the fixed-plane construction. The conversion changes constants depending on the order, not the absolute parent exponent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S53.word_eq_coordin.summary: Coordinate words evaluate the Fréchet derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5Bridge.contDiffOn.text: A smooth multiplier vanishing before `t₀` times a field that is smooth on the active slab `[t₀,T]` is smooth on the whole slab (copy of the private library lemma `contDiffOn_slab_multiplier`, `PaperGenericWaveSwitch.lean:167`). A smooth compactly supported label profile is extended with the twisted lattice rule and period one in phase. The envelope fitting strictly inside the centered cell is what permits equality with the original profile there.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5Bridge.contDiffOn.summary: A smooth cutoff extends active data across activation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5Bridge.eq_of_cent.text: A twisted profile is determined by its values on `[0,T] × [-1/2,1/2]³ × ℝ`. A smooth compactly supported label profile is extended with the twisted lattice rule and period one in phase. The envelope fitting strictly inside the centered cell is what permits equality with the original profile there.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5Bridge.eq_of_cent.summary: Cell values determine a twisted periodic profile

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5Bridge.forall_of_.text: A property of slab points that is invariant under the twisted lattice translations holds on the slab once it holds on the label cell (copy of the private library lemma `all_on_centeredCell`). A smooth compactly supported label profile is extended with the twisted lattice rule and period one in phase. The envelope fitting strictly inside the centered cell is what permits equality with the original profile there.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5Bridge.forall_of_.summary: A translation invariant property extends from the cell

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5Bridge.leadingBar.text: `F_h(s) 𝐚(t,a)` is jointly smooth on the active slab `[t₀,T] × ℝ³ × ℝ` (copy of the private library lemma `SeedOn.leadingBare_smooth`, `PaperGenericWaveSwitch.lean:128`, for any amplitude `amp`, with the regularity fields used by its proof as hypotheses). A smooth compactly supported label profile is extended with the twisted lattice rule and period one in phase. The envelope fitting strictly inside the centered cell is what permits equality with the original profile there.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5Bridge.leadingBar.summary: The seed times its phase profile is jointly smooth

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5Bridge.phaseMean_.text: The twisted extension of a field with zero phase mean at every label has zero phase mean (copy of the private library lemma `phaseMean_wrapped_shift`). A smooth compactly supported label profile is extended with the twisted lattice rule and period one in phase. The envelope fitting strictly inside the centered cell is what permits equality with the original profile there.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5Bridge.phaseMean_.summary: Twisted extension preserves a zero phase mean

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5Bridge.pressureBa.text: The leading pressure without its envelope, `-(2⟨κ, M𝐚⟩/|κ|²) P_h(s)`, is jointly smooth on the active slab (copy of the private library lemma `SeedOn.barePressure_smooth`, `PaperGenericWaveSwitch.lean:146`, for any coefficients `M`, `κ` and amplitude `amp`, with the private `barePressure` unfolded and the regularity fields used by its proof as hypotheses). A smooth compactly supported label profile is extended with the twisted lattice rule and period one in phase. The envelope fitting strictly inside the centered cell is what permits equality with the original profile there.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5Bridge.pressureBa.summary: The unswitched pressure is smooth for nonzero covectors

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5Bridge.wrapProfil.text:
The twisted profile of a field `f(t,a,s)` periodic in the phase, extended from the label cell by the twisted lattice translations (copy of the private library definition `wrapOnSlab`, `PaperGenericWaveSwitch.lean:75`). A smooth compactly supported label profile is extended with the twisted lattice rule and period one in phase. The envelope fitting strictly inside the centered cell is what permits equality with the original profile there.

Default-value audit (b5): Smoothness of the already periodized expression and period-one phase behavior are explicit inputs. The constructor proves the twisted lattice law and packages that field; it does not silently assume compact support or equality with the raw input on a cell. Those are separate geometric hypotheses in the later cell-equality lemmas.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5Bridge.wrapProfil.summary: Extend cell data by twisted lattice translations

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5Bridge.wrapProfil.text: Read the value of the twisted extension. A smooth compactly supported label profile is extended with the twisted lattice rule and period one in phase. The envelope fitting strictly inside the centered cell is what permits equality with the original profile there.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5Bridge.wrapped_eq.text: On the label cell the twisted extension of a field vanishing for `|a| ≥ 2ℓ` (`2ℓ < 1/2`) is the field itself (copy of the private library lemma `wrapped_eq_on_cell_of_radial_zero`). A smooth compactly supported label profile is extended with the twisted lattice rule and period one in phase. The envelope fitting strictly inside the centered cell is what permits equality with the original profile there.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5Bridge.wrapped_eq.summary: Localization makes the twisted extension agree on the cell

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.CoefficientPowe.text: The power bound (D.6) is monotone in the exponent, since `𝖣 ≥ 1`. This transfers the supplied coefficient estimates to the derivative conventions used by the seed construction. Increasing constants or the parent scale changes no field and imposes no new equation on the parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.CoefficientPowe.summary: Increase the exponent in a coefficient power estimate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.IsExpansion.ina.text: The profiles are smooth on $[0,T]$ and obey the phase period and coupled label translations; $0<2\ell_*<1/2$ keeps the envelope inside each cell. For any expansion satisfying the recurrence, $V_p$, $\mathsf p_p$, the curl corrections through $C_{P+1}$, and the transverse sources vanish before $t_0$ and outside the envelope. The envelope must fit strictly inside the label cell. These are the support conclusions of Proposition 5.4; the mean fields are not required to vanish before activation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.IsExpansion.ina.summary: The full expansion inherits the leading inactive region

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.IsExpansion.lea.text: The leading level of an expansion is the leading velocity profile of the bridge (`V₁ = χ̃A₁` on the label cell determines the profile). This is an exact finite algebraic identity. The final curl completion C_{P+1} is retained while the top velocity and mean profiles are set to zero; no assertion about convergence of an infinite expansion is involved.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.IsExpansion.lea.summary: The first level is the activated leading profile

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.LeafBounds.text:
The jets of the seven coefficient fields in the form in which the library chain consumes them (the conclusion of `exists_parent_coefficientJetBounds`), for the data `U, X, k`, the scale `D` and the frequency `Λ`, with constants `B`. This transfers the supplied coefficient estimates to the derivative conventions used by the seed construction. Increasing constants or the parent scale changes no field and imposes no new equation on the parent.

Default-value audit (b5): This predicate is a list of explicit pointwise derivative inequalities for all orders and allowed times. It does not itself demand a positive frequency or D≥1, so inverse-frequency expressions are totalized at other inputs. The actual parent/launch and scale hypotheses supply positivity and nonvanishing before these bounds are used analytically.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.LeafBounds.summary: Derivative bounds for the seven seed coefficients

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.MonoW.text:
Smooth fields whose weighted mixed derivatives of order at most `m` are bounded by `Ω^a Θ^i`: `Ω ≥ 1` absorbs the fixed constants (products, linear maps, numbers) and `Θ ≥ 1` the powers of `𝖣` (basic coefficients and `ℓ_*⁻¹`). The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numeric parameters Ω and Θ in MonoW are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient Ω of the mean equation.

Default-value audit (b5): The predicate includes smoothness and a word bound Ω^aΘ^i. It is defined for arbitrary real Ω and Θ, but monotonicity and product-budget theorems require the stated lower bounds (typically at least one). The symbols are numeric bounds, not the matrix coefficient Ω of the mean equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.MonoW.summary: Separate fixed constants from powers of the parent scale

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.MonoW.add.text: Add two coefficient bounds. The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numeric parameters Ω and Θ in MonoW are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient Ω of the mean equation.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.MonoW.bilinear.text: Bilinear products satisfy the monotone-weight bound (product estimate (D.4)). The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numeric parameters Ω and Θ in MonoW are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient Ω of the mean equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.MonoW.bilinear.summary: Multiply coefficient bounds using the cited product rule

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.MonoW.congr.text: Pointwise equal families satisfy the same monotone-weight bound. The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numeric parameters Ω and Θ in MonoW are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient Ω of the mean equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.MonoW.congr.summary: Equal fields satisfy the same two parameter bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.MonoW.const.text: A constant of norm at most `Ω` satisfies the monotone-weight bound. The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numeric parameters Ω and Θ in MonoW are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient Ω of the mean equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.MonoW.const.summary: A bounded constant satisfies the coefficient estimate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.MonoW.of_wb.text: A weighted bound of the product type gives the monotone-weight bound. The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numeric parameters Ω and Θ in MonoW are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient Ω of the mean equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.MonoW.of_wb.summary: Convert a derivative bound to separated coefficient costs

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.MonoW.raise.text: The monotone-weight bound persists when the parameters are raised. The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numeric parameters Ω and Θ in MonoW are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient Ω of the mean equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.MonoW.raise.summary: Increasing the exponents preserves the coefficient bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.MonoW.smul.text: Scale a coefficient by a controlled constant. The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numeric parameters Ω and Θ in MonoW are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient Ω of the mean equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.MonoW.smul.summary: Scale a coefficient by a controlled constant

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.MonoW.smulΘ.text: Multiplying by a scalar of size at most `Θ` (such as `ℓ_*⁻¹`) raises the power of `Θ`. The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numeric parameters Ω and Θ in MonoW are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient Ω of the mean equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.MonoW.smulΘ.summary: A parent scale factor raises the parent exponent

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.MonoW.sub.text: Subtract two fields with coefficient bounds. The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numeric parameters Ω and Θ in MonoW are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient Ω of the mean equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.MonoW.sub.summary: Subtract two fields with coefficient bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Cn_of.text:
The constant of Lemma D.3 for the index type `Fin 3`, the order `n` and the constants `C_m`. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default-value audit (b5): Classical choice reads an existing D.3 constant for the specified order and list of commutator bounds. The supplied D.3 proof certifies the chosen constant and later theorem records nonnegativity. No explicit formula or bound on its growth with n is asserted.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Cn_of.summary: The constant supplied by derivative lifting at this order

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Esp.text:
Towers of solenoidal velocities `u_w` with `∫_0^T u_w = 0`. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default-value audit (b5): The values lie in the solenoidal half-Hölder subspace, and every word has zero integral over [0,T]. The definition is constructed with T≥0; T=0 gives a trivial endpoint integral condition, while the endpoint inverse later assumes T>0. It does not impose zero initial velocity.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Esp.summary: Solenoidal derivative families with zero integrated displacement

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Esp_le_to.text: Forgetting the zero-integral condition embeds the constrained solenoidal family space into the symmetric continuous family space. No equation or estimate is added by this inclusion.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Esp_le_to.summary: Constrained solution families are continuous derivative families

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.IsDer.text:
A family related by actual spatial derivatives. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default-value audit (b5): The predicate asserts each spatial derivative relation only for times in [0,T]. If the interval were empty it would be vacuous; uses for the mean inverse have T>0. It does not by itself require time continuity or permutation symmetry, which the surrounding family structures provide.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.IsDer.summary: A family related by actual spatial derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.N_Tk_le.text: Operator bound for `Tk`: `Kv` enters directly, so the norm is at most `b_K = 4‖P‖` times that of `K`. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.N_Tk_le.summary: The kinetic action has a fixed operator bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.N_Tom_le.text: Operator bound for `Tom`: `Ωv` enters through time integration, so the norm is at most `b_Ω = 2‖P‖T` times that of `Ω`. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.N_Tom_le.summary: Time integration supplies the vorticity action bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.N_coe_eq.text: If a solenoidal time family and an ambient time family agree after inclusion on the closed interval, their closed-time norms are equal. The values outside that interval are irrelevant.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.N_coe_eq.summary: Passing to the ambient space preserves the time supremum

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Pr_coe.text: Applying the spatial projection to an already solenoidal field returns that same field. This removes redundant projections when comparing endpoint solutions.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Pr_coe.summary: Leray projection fixes every solenoidal field

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Sym.text:
Derivative families invariant under coordinate permutations. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default-value audit (b5): Only invariance under permutation of word indices is asserted. This does not imply the entries are spatial derivatives, continuous in time or solutions of any equation. The empty-word case is automatic.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Sym.summary: Derivative families invariant under coordinate permutations

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.SymTower.text:
Symmetric derivative towers of a smooth periodic field. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default-value audit (b5): The record includes symmetry, smooth time dependence, actual spatial-derivative relations and equality of lifted entries with the derivatives of the given field. Those assertions are restricted to the time slab. It is stronger than an arbitrary symmetric continuous family; its existence is separately proved from smooth periodic input.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.SymTower.summary: A smooth periodic field with its symmetric derivative family

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk.text:
Project the kinetic product and subtract its initial value. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default-value audit (b5): The expression subtracts its projected product at time zero, retaining the constant term of the integrated equation. It is total for arbitrary word families and does not require their being derivatives. The relevant continuity and norm bounds are separate hypotheses and results.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk.summary: Project the kinetic product and subtract its initial value

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.TkB.text:
The `K`-action as a bilinear map on the spaces of towers. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default-value audit (b5): These bilinear maps are bundled only after proving that the explicit kinetic and integrated vorticity actions preserve the required family spaces. The time interval is positive in their setup. They are algebraic maps with later seminorm bounds, not a claim that every input solves the mean equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.TkB.summary: The kinetic action on admissible derivative families

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.TkB_val.text: Forgetting the subspace proofs in the bilinear kinetic action gives the explicit expression P(au)(t)−P(au)(0) at every word. The term at time zero is retained because the integrated equation has an unknown constant.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.TkB_val.summary: Read the kinetic action on the underlying families

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_add_le.text: The projected kinetic product with its initial value subtracted respects addition in its coefficient argument, with the other input fixed. This supplies the corresponding linearity required for the bilinear operator in D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_add_le.summary: The kinetic action is additive in the coefficient

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_add_ri.text: The projected kinetic product with its initial value subtracted respects addition in its solution argument, with the other input fixed. This supplies the corresponding linearity required for the bilinear operator in D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_add_ri.summary: The kinetic action is additive in the velocity

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_contin.text: Continuous entries of the coefficient and solution families make each projected kinetic-product difference continuous in time. This validates its membership in the forcing-family space.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_contin.summary: The kinetic action preserves continuity in time

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_der.text: `Tk a v` of a derivative tower is a derivative tower (Leibniz rule; TeX 46-48). The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_der.summary: The kinetic action preserves spatial derivative relations

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_leibni.text: A coordinate shift of the projected kinetic product and its initial value is the sum of the terms with the shift assigned to the coefficient and to the solution. This is the unweighted word-family Leibniz rule; the weighted version is used in D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_leibni.summary: The kinetic action obeys the derivative product rule

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_mem.text: Permutation symmetry and continuity of the two inputs imply that the kinetic action belongs to the symmetric continuous forcing-family space. This is a well-definedness result for the operator, not the mean equation itself.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_mem.summary: The kinetic action gives an admissible forcing family

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_perm.text: Symmetric coefficient and solution families give a symmetric kinetic action after projection and subtraction of the time-zero value. No differentiation in time is involved.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_perm.summary: The kinetic action preserves permutation invariance

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_smul_l.text: The projected kinetic product with its initial value subtracted respects constant scalar multiplication in its coefficient argument, with the other input fixed. This supplies the corresponding linearity required for the bilinear operator in D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_smul_l.summary: The kinetic action respects coefficient scaling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_smul_r.text: The projected kinetic product with its initial value subtracted respects constant scalar multiplication in its solution argument, with the other input fixed. This supplies the corresponding linearity required for the bilinear operator in D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tk_smul_r.summary: The kinetic action respects velocity scaling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom.text:
Integrate and project the negative vorticity product. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default-value audit (b5): This expression is the negative projected clamped primitive of the finite Leibniz product. Its analytic interpretation uses T>0 and continuous inputs; arbitrary totalized integral values outside that setting are not used for estimates. The sign agrees with the integrated mean equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom.summary: Integrate and project the negative vorticity product

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.TomB.text:
The `Ω`-action as a bilinear map on the spaces of towers. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default-value audit (b5): These bilinear maps are bundled only after proving that the explicit kinetic and integrated vorticity actions preserve the required family spaces. The time interval is positive in their setup. They are algebraic maps with later seminorm bounds, not a claim that every input solves the mean equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.TomB.summary: The integrated vorticity action on admissible derivative families

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.TomB_val.text: Forgetting the subspace proofs in the bilinear vorticity action gives minus the projected time primitive of the Leibniz product. This is the coefficient term whose operator norm carries a factor T.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.TomB_val.summary: Read the vorticity action on the underlying families

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom_add_l.text: The negative projected time primitive of the product respects addition in its coefficient argument, with the other input fixed. Continuity on a nonnegative time interval supplies integrability for the additive identity. This supplies the corresponding linearity required for the bilinear operator in D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom_add_l.summary: The integrated vorticity action is additive in the coefficient

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom_add_r.text: The negative projected time primitive of the product respects addition in its solution argument, with the other input fixed. Continuity on a nonnegative time interval supplies integrability for the additive identity. This supplies the corresponding linearity required for the bilinear operator in D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom_add_r.summary: The integrated vorticity action is additive in the velocity

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom_conti.text: On a positive interval, continuity of both families makes each projected time-primitive product continuous. This validates the integrated term in the forcing-family space.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom_conti.summary: The integrated vorticity action preserves continuity in time

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom_leibn.text: A coordinate shift of the projected time integral of the product is the sum of the terms with the shift assigned to the coefficient and to the solution. This is the unweighted word-family Leibniz rule; the weighted version is used in D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom_leibn.summary: The integrated vorticity action obeys the derivative product rule

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom_mem.text: On a positive interval, the integrated vorticity action of two continuous symmetric families is again such a family. The proof combines symmetry with continuity of the primitive.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom_mem.summary: The integrated vorticity action gives an admissible forcing family

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom_perm.text: Symmetric coefficient and solution families give a symmetric integrated vorticity action. The word permutation affects neither the fixed time integral nor the projection.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom_perm.summary: The vorticity action preserves permutation invariance

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom_smul_.text: The negative projected time primitive of the product respects constant scalar multiplication in its coefficient argument, with the other input fixed. This supplies the corresponding linearity required for the bilinear operator in D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom_smul_.summary: The integrated vorticity action respects coefficient scaling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom_smul_.text: The negative projected time primitive of the product respects constant scalar multiplication in its solution argument, with the other input fixed. This supplies the corresponding linearity required for the bilinear operator in D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tom_smul_.summary: The integrated vorticity action respects velocity scaling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw.text:
Expand every derivative of coefficient times velocity. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default-value audit (b5): The finite recursion distributes each derivative letter between coefficient and solution. At the empty word it is the pointwise half-Hölder product. It is defined for arbitrary families; only IsDer and symmetry hypotheses make it the derivative family of an actual product.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw.summary: Expand every derivative of coefficient times velocity

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw0_bound.text: The zero-order coefficient product at an allowed time is bounded by twice the product of the two closed-time norms. The factor two is the half-Hölder multiplication bound used in this implementation.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw_add_le.text: The finite Leibniz product respects addition in its coefficient argument, with the other input fixed. This supplies the corresponding linearity required for the bilinear operator in D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw_add_le.summary: The Leibniz expansion is additive in the coefficient

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw_add_ri.text: The finite Leibniz product respects addition in its solution argument, with the other input fixed. This supplies the corresponding linearity required for the bilinear operator in D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw_add_ri.summary: The Leibniz expansion is additive in the velocity

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw_bound.text: The empty-word product has half-Hölder norm at most twice the product of the two input norms at the same time. This local multiplication bound becomes the operator bounds for the kinetic and integrated actions.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw_contin.text: Continuous coefficient and solution entries make every finite Leibniz product entry continuous in time on the closed interval. This gives integrability for the vorticity action.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw_contin.summary: Continuous coefficient and velocity families give continuous products

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw_der.text: The Leibniz expansion of two symmetric derivative towers is a derivative tower (product rule). The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw_der.summary: The Leibniz product of derivative families is differentiated correctly

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw_perm.text: The Leibniz product family is permutation invariant when both input families are. The induction accounts for every distribution of derivative letters between the two factors.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw_perm.summary: The Leibniz expansion is invariant under coordinate permutations

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw_smul_l.text: The finite Leibniz product respects constant scalar multiplication in its coefficient argument, with the other input fixed. This supplies the corresponding linearity required for the bilinear operator in D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw_smul_l.summary: The Leibniz expansion respects coefficient scaling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw_smul_r.text: The finite Leibniz product respects constant scalar multiplication in its solution argument, with the other input fixed. This supplies the corresponding linearity required for the bilinear operator in D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Tw_smul_r.summary: The Leibniz expansion respects velocity scaling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.Wd.text:
Words of the three label directions. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default-value audit (b5): This is the list type on the three coordinate directions. The empty word represents order zero. No ordering, smoothness, derivative relation or commutation property is built into the abbreviation.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.cl.text:
Time clamped to `[0,T]`, so that primitives only see the values on `[0,T]`. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default-value audit (b5): The formula max(0,min(t,T)) is total for all real T,t. Its interval-membership lemma requires T≥0; for T<0 the formula is zero rather than a point of the empty interval. On [0,T] it is the identity. No smoothness of this clamp across the endpoints is claimed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.cl.summary: Clamp the time to the closed parent interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.cl_eq.text: At a time already in [0,T], clamping returns the same time. This permits the totalized primitive to be replaced by the ordinary time primitive on the physical interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.cl_eq.summary: Clamping leaves times inside the interval unchanged

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.cl_mem.text: If T is nonnegative, the clamped time max(0,min(t,T)) lies in [0,T] for every real t. The sign hypothesis matters; the definition alone is total for all T.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.cm_add.text: Coefficient multiplication is additive in the matrix coefficient. This supplies the left linearity of the product used in the integrated mean equation.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.cm_smul.text: A scalar multiplying the matrix coefficient can be pulled out of coefficient multiplication. This supplies scalar linearity of the coefficient action.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.dA.text:
The weighted derivations `ℓ ∂_i` on the three spaces of towers. The mean argument represents spatial derivatives by symmetric families indexed by words. Solenoidal values and zero total time integral encode divergence freedom and the two displacement endpoints; additional derivative relations identify a family with derivatives of an actual field.

Default-value audit (b5): The weighted derivations are ℓ times restricted word shifts and are total even for negative or zero ℓ. The norm-identification and lifting results require ℓ≥0; the actual envelope radius is positive. They preserve the explicit subspace constraints by construction.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.dA.summary: The radius weighted derivative on coefficient families

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.dA_val.text: On underlying families, the coefficient derivation is exactly ℓ times the coordinate shift. This is the evaluation identity used in the weighted Leibniz rules.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.dA_val.summary: Read the radius weighted coefficient shift

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.dE.text:
The solution derivation is the coordinate shift multiplied by the label radius ℓ, restricted to solenoidal families with zero total time integral. It therefore encodes the derivative weight without losing the endpoint constraints.

Default-value audit (b5): The weighted derivations are ℓ times restricted word shifts and are total even for negative or zero ℓ. The norm-identification and lifting results require ℓ≥0; the actual envelope radius is positive. They preserve the explicit subspace constraints by construction.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.dE.summary: The radius weighted derivative on endpoint solution families

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.dE_val.text: On underlying constrained families, the solution derivation is exactly ℓ times the coordinate shift. The subtype carries the already-proved endpoint and solenoidal constraints.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.dF.text:
The forcing derivation is the coordinate shift multiplied by the label radius ℓ. It acts on the symmetric continuous families used for the projected forcing equation.

Default-value audit (b5): The weighted derivations are ℓ times restricted word shifts and are total even for negative or zero ℓ. The norm-identification and lifting results require ℓ≥0; the actual envelope radius is positive. They preserve the explicit subspace constraints by construction.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.dF.summary: The radius weighted derivative on forcing families

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.dF_val.text: On underlying forcing families, the forcing derivation is exactly ℓ times the coordinate shift. This relates the abstract derivation to the weighted word norm.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.Tower.endpointC.text: Time families equal on the closed interval have equal closed-time norms. The equality does not require their arbitrary values outside that interval to coincide.
