TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.toSpanL.summary: Turn a vector into scalar multiplication by that vector

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.toSpanL_apply.text: The map obtained from a vector sends a scalar r to r times that vector. This identifies scalar multiplication as a fixed bilinear map for the product bound.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.toSpanL_apply.summary: Evaluate the vector to scalar multiplication map

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.totalDivergence.text: Here $\kappa=(D_aX)^{-T}k_*\ne0$, the parent is smooth, periodic and volume preserving, and all constraints hold throughout $[0,T]$. A zero-mean transverse profile satisfies $\widetilde{\mathbf d}\cdot(V+C[V])=0$. The proof uses the identity $V+C[V]=\widetilde{\mathbf d}\times Q[V]$ in the transported parent geometry. Proposition 5.4 sums these completed oscillations and the separately divergence-free means to obtain the divergence constraint for the entire finite correction.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.totalDivergence.summary: The curl correction restores the full divergence constraint

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.totalDivergence.text: The parent is smooth and volume preserving on $[0,T]$, and the smooth periodic displacement satisfies $z(0)=z(T)=0$. The endpoint mean solution has $B=D_aXz_t$ with divergence-free label velocity $z_t$. Volume preservation and the Piola identity give $\mathbf d\cdot B=0$, and phase independence makes this the full divergence constraint as well. This supplies the mean terms in the divergence calculation for $W$ in Proposition 5.4.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.totalDivergence.summary: Transfer the divergence constraint through the parent flow

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.transverseSolut.text: A solution of (5.15) from `V(0) = 0` whose source has zero phase mean and vanishes on the inactive region vanishes there, together with its pressure: it is the library ODE solve (`exists_transverseResult`), by uniqueness (`Bridge.TransverseSolution.unique`), and that solve keeps the inactive region (its field `inactive`). The inactive set consists of times before activation or labels outside the periodized envelope support. The induction concerns oscillatory profiles and their sources; the means may already be nonzero before activation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.transverseSolut.summary: The transverse solve preserves the inactive region

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.transverseSourc.text: The transverse source `f_p + f_p^S` of level `p ≥ 2` vanishes on the inactive region when the lower levels do: `Y_j = V_j + C_j` for `1 ≤ j < p`, `C_p`, `𝗉_{p-1}` and (at `p = 2`) the activation correction `C[χ̃'A₁]` vanish there, and the means `B_j`, `1 ≤ j < p`, are phase independent (the statement holds for every `p`; it is used for `2 ≤ p ≤ P`). On the inactive region `H_p` reduces to the slow products of means, which the centring removes, and every term of `f_p^S` has an inactive second factor. The inactive set consists of times before activation or labels outside the periodized envelope support. The induction concerns oscillatory profiles and their sources; the means may already be nonzero before activation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.transverseSourc.summary: The next transverse source preserves the inactive region

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.truncProfiles.text:
The profiles of an expansion of depth `P` with the levels outside `1 ≤ p ≤ P` and the library corrections `u.C q` outside `q ≤ P` (that is, `C_{q+1}` outside `1 ≤ q + 1 ≤ P + 1`) set to zero. Only these levels enter `W`, `𝖯`, `R_P` and the sources of Proposition 5.4. This is an exact finite algebraic identity. The final curl completion C_{P+1} is retained while the top velocity and mean profiles are set to zero; no assertion about convergence of an infinite expansion is involved.

Default-value audit (b5): Levels outside the specified ranges are intentionally set to zero. The stored completion C is indexed with an offset: retaining C through P retains the physical completion C_{P+1}. The preservation theorems state exactly which V,B,p,q and derived C,Y,Z entries agree; no all-level equality with the original family is claimed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.truncProfiles.summary: Retain precisely the levels of a finite expansion

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.two_le_relayOme.text: The common product constant is at least two. The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numeric parameters Ω and Θ in MonoW are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient Ω of the mean equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.two_le_relayOme.summary: The common product constant is at least two

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.wNorm_zero.text: The zero profile has zero weighted norm. The completion and relay gain one inverse carrier frequency and cost one spatial derivative. The pressure and vector-potential formulas eliminate the dangerous fast derivative without differentiating the mean or the forcing in time.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.waveCompletion_.text: Positive spatial and phase scales, nonzero frequency and the specified coefficient word bounds imply an estimate for the curl completion. The result gains one inverse frequency and uses one additional derivative of the zero-mean input, with the primitive bound supplied by D.1.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.waveCompletion_.summary: The divergence correction gains one inverse frequency

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.waveLinearRelay.text: For smooth periodic zero-mean velocity and forcing, the specified potential, pressure and curl coefficient bounds control the four terms of the linear relay. The estimate gains one inverse frequency and costs one derivative. The source is used through its spatial words, never through a time derivative.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.waveLinearRelay.summary: Bound the four terms after differentiating the vector potential

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.wb_bilinear_of_.text: The product rule (D.4) of Lemma D.1 on word bounds: if every weighted mixed derivative of order at most `m` of `f` is at most `A` and of `g` at most `C`, those of `B(f, g)` are at most `productConstant m · ‖B‖ A C`. The norm of the product and its finiteness are the (D.4) clause of `hD` (weight `γ ≡ 1`). The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numeric parameters Ω and Θ in MonoW are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient Ω of the mean equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.wb_bilinear_of_.summary: The cited product rule bounds each derivative word

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.wb_congr.text: Equal fields satisfy the same derivative bound. The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numeric parameters Ω and Θ in MonoW are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient Ω of the mean equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.wb_congr.summary: Equal fields satisfy the same derivative bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.wb_const.text: Constant fields have uniform derivative bounds. The coefficient bookkeeping separates constants depending on the derivative order from powers of the parent bound. The numeric parameters Ω and Θ in MonoW are bounds, not the vorticity coefficient Ω of the mean equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.wb_const.summary: Constant fields have uniform derivative bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.weighted_one.text: Dividing by the unit weight changes nothing. The primitive estimate is taken from the supplied Lemma D.1. Its use, together with coefficient word bounds, yields the inverse-frequency gain in the curl correction and relay without a time derivative of the source.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.weighted_one.summary: Dividing by the unit weight changes nothing

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.wrapped_eq_on_c.text: On the centered label cell, the twisted periodization agrees with a field supported in the ball of radius 2ℓ when 2ℓ<1/2. The support and strict fitting condition are what prevent an additional translated copy from contributing.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5a.wrapped_eq_on_c.summary: The localized extension agrees with its cell data

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.CoefficientPowe.text: The power bound (D.6) is monotone in the exponent, since `𝖣 ≥ 1`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.CoefficientPowe.summary: Increasing the parent exponent preserves coefficient bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.coefficientPowe.text: Operator-norm jet bounds `‖D^m c(t,x)‖ ≤ K_m 𝖣^{a(m+1)}` of a field smooth in the label give the power bound (D.6) in the form of Appendix D, with constants `#{words of order m} · K_m`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.coefficientPowe.summary: Full coefficient jets imply the required power bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.exists_monotone.text: A nondecreasing coordinate word of length `m` is the word of a monotone map `Fin m → Fin 3`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.exists_monotone.summary: Sorted derivative words have monotone index maps

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.exists_sortedWo.text: Symmetry of the derivatives of a smooth function: every coordinate component `D^m f(x)(e_{β 0}, …, e_{β (m-1)})` is the value of one nondecreasing coordinate word of length `m` (the sorted word of the letters of `β`).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.exists_sortedWo.summary: Symmetry permits sorting the derivative directions

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.labelDirection_.text: The unit label directions of Appendix D are the coordinate directions.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.labelDirection_.summary: Unit label directions are coordinate directions

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.labelWord_eq_it.text: The value of a coordinate word is the iterated derivative on the coordinate directions of its letters.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.labelWord_eq_it.summary: Ordered label words evaluate Fréchet derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.mFourierCoeff_c.text: A continuous complex linear map commutes with Fourier coefficients of a continuous torus field. Here the map takes a complex Euclidean vector to a scalar, permitting coordinate projections of a vector frequency-support bound.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.mFourierCoeff_c.summary: Linear maps commute with Fourier coefficients

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.norm_iteratedFD.text: `‖D^m c(t,x)‖ ≤ 3^m |c|_m`: the operator norm of the `m`-th label derivative is bounded by the coefficient size `|c|_m = ∑_{|β|=m} sup |∂^β c|` of Appendix D.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.norm_iteratedFD.summary: Coefficient norms control full label derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.norm_iteratedFD.text: The power bound (D.6) in the form of Appendix D gives operator-norm jet bounds with the same exponent: `‖D^m c(t,x)‖ ≤ 3^m C_m 𝖣^{a(m+1)}`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.norm_iteratedFD.summary: Power bounds control full coefficient jets

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.norm_linearMap_.text: If a linear map on ℝ³ has norm at most M on each coordinate vector, then its operator norm is at most 3M. The codomain is an arbitrary real normed space; the proof expands an input in its three coordinates.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.norm_linearMap_.summary: Three coordinate bounds control a linear map

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.ofFnWord_eq_ite.text: The word of the letters `β 0, …, β (m-1)` is the iterated derivative on `e_{β 0}, …, e_{β (m-1)}`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.ofFnWord_eq_ite.summary: Indexed coordinate words evaluate Fréchet derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.opNorm_le_coord.text: The operator norm of a multilinear map on ℝ³ is bounded by the sum of the norms of its values on coordinate directions. The target may be any normed space, so this applies to coefficient operators as well as scalar fields.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.opNorm_le_coord.summary: Bounding multilinear norms by coordinate values

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.realNormedTorus.text: A continuous real vector field on the torus whose complexified Fourier coefficients vanish at the frequencies `|k| > R` is supported on frequencies at most `R` in the sense of the statement of Lemma B.1: every real linear measurement of it has vanishing Fourier coefficients at those frequencies.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.realNormedTorus.summary: Vector Fourier support bounds scalar projections

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.sum_coordinateD.text: A vector of `ℝ³` is the sum of its coordinates times the coordinate directions.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5b.sum_coordinateD.summary: Expanding vectors in the three coordinate directions

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.CentralReturnCl.text:
Packages the error estimate for the velocity gradient at the origin after subtracting the parent gradient and the switched rank one seed contribution. The eventual smallness assumption absorbs the D power and the λ^(−5/12) intermediate error into the stated λ^(−1/3) error.

Default-value audit (b5): This is a quantified estimate for valid expansion data, not an independently chosen pressure or velocity. It may be vacuous without admissible data; the subsequent proof supplies it under the cited hypotheses and Proposition 5.4 supplies expansion existence. Natural finite sums use the stated retained level range.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.CutBand.text:

The application obtains it from Lemma B.1 or (5.59), with an admissible cutoff, nonnegative constants and Λ ≥ 1. Empty or degenerate intervals do not replace the explicit strict time-length hypothesis where it is needed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.CutBand.summary: The Fourier cutoff confines the frequency support

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.EulerMean.text:
The Eulerian form of a solution `(B, q̄)` of (5.11) with source `f̄`: `b = B∘X⁻¹`, `q = q̄∘X⁻¹`, `f = f̄∘X⁻¹` are smooth and periodic, `div b = 0`, and the linearized Euler equation (4.12) holds, with the material derivative `∂_{(1,U)}` taken on the closed slab.

Default-value audit (b5): This is a conjunction recording smoothness, periodicity, divergence freeness and an Eulerian equation on the closed slab. It is not a chosen solution. The within-slab material derivative is interpreted through the supplied smoothness and positive time interval.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.HigherHessianCl.text: Fix sufficiently small $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$, $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, and a finite expansion of depth $P\ge2$ over a smooth odd divergence-free periodic parent on $0<T\le1$. The hypotheses include Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$ for $U,R_U$, deformation and gradient bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $D^2p-\nabla R_U\le I$. The central pair has activation frequency $\lambda\ge1$, positive transverse stability as in (5.5), and $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$. Under $\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, the assertion is $\|D_x^2\sum_{p=2}^{P}\mathsf p_p^\natural\|_\infty\le K_P\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/12}$ on $[0,T]$. The exponent and constants precede the parent and expansion. This declaration states the intermediate claim; the accompanying theorem proves it. No zero-mean Poisson requirement is imposed on the parent pressure.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.HigherHessianCl.summary: State the decay of the sum of higher oscillatory pressures

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.Icc_subset_Icc_.summary: The active interval lies within the full time slab

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.IsExpansion.ina.text: Supports of the expansion, given the support of the sources. If the sources `f_p + f_p^S` (`2 ≤ p ≤ P`) lie in the inactive submodule, then so do `V_p`, `𝗉_p` (`1 ≤ p ≤ P`) and `C_p` (`1 ≤ p ≤ P + 1`). The leading pair and the activation term vanish there by their cell values (3.7), (3.8); for `p ≥ 2` the transverse equation (5.15) with the zero initial datum is solved by the library ODE solve, which keeps the inactive region, and `C_{p+1} = C[V_p]`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.IsExpansion.ina.summary: Inactive sources force every oscillatory level to vanish

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.IsExpansion.lea.text: The leading pressure vanishes on the inactive region (no use of Proposition 5.4): on the label cell `𝗉₁ = χ̃ · (-c_𝐚) 𝗉_h` (`hu.leading_pressure`), `χ̃ = 0` for `t < t₀` (the cutoff) and `c_𝐚 = 0` off `supp g` (the radial envelope), as in.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.IsExpansion.lea.summary: The first pressure vanishes in the inactive region

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.LeadingHessianC.text:
Packages the leading pressure estimate as a quadratic-form upper bound for every vector v, with size C D^C λ^(−1/4)‖v‖². It deliberately does not bound the absolute value or operator norm of the leading Hessian; the large signed phase tensor is controlled only on its unfavorable side.

Default-value audit (b5): This is a quantified estimate for valid expansion data, not an independently chosen pressure or velocity. It may be vacuous without admissible data; the subsequent proof supplies it under the cited hypotheses and Proposition 5.4 supplies expansion existence. Natural finite sums use the stated retained level range.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.LeadingHessianC.summary: The signed leading pressure Hessian bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.MeanHessianClai.text: For a finite expansion of depth $P\ge2$, take a smooth odd divergence-free periodic parent on $0<T\le1$, with deformation and gradient bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, velocity and residual Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p-\nabla R_U\le I$. Require a nonzero transverse central seed of activation frequency $\lambda\ge1$, the stability and coupling conditions (5.5), and $0<\gamma\le1$. With sufficiently small $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$ and $\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, the assertion is $\|D_x^2\sum_{p=2}^{P}\bar q_p^\natural\|_\infty\le K_P\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/2}$ throughout $[0,T]$. It concerns the mean pressures belonging to that expansion. Constants are chosen before the parent and profiles. This declaration formulates the claim; it does not itself supply its proof.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.MeanHessianClai.summary: State the decay of the pressure attached to the mean corrections

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.ProductBound.text:
The product inequality (5.59) with the constants `Cm` (the statement `Paper.Statement.Text.eq_5_59` with its constants chosen).

Default-value audit (b5): This is a proposition stating one analytic property with chosen constants or cutoff parameters; the definition alone does not prove it. The application obtains it from Lemma B.1 or (5.59), with an admissible cutoff, nonnegative constants and Λ ≥ 1. Empty or degenerate intervals do not replace the explicit strict time-length hypothesis where it is needed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.ProductBound.summary: Chosen constants for the physical Hölder product estimate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.adjL.text:
The transpose `A ↦ Aᵀ` as a continuous linear map (copy of `Lib.S5a.adjL`).

Default-value audit (b5): This is a total algebraic or continuous-linear construction with no division or noncanonical choice. Zero inputs have their literal algebraic values. Any geometric identification or differentiability property is supplied separately by the consuming theorem.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.adjL.summary: Transposition as a continuous linear operator

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.adjL_apply.text: The transpose of `A` is `adjL A` (simp form of `adjL`).

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.average_transve.text: The transverse source `f_p + f_p^S` of (5.27), (5.28) has zero phase mean when the means `B_i`, `2 ≤ i ≤ p`, are phase independent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.average_transve.summary: The full transverse source has zero phase average

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.centralReturnCl.text: Assume the phase-profile normalization, existence and uniqueness of the finite expansion, its level estimates, and the physical derivative bounds of Lemma 5.7. For a depth-$P\ge2$ expansion over a smooth periodic odd divergence-free parent satisfying the deformation, residual and coercivity bounds of §5.1, take a nonzero stable transverse seed with $0<\gamma\le1$ and $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda\ge1$. Once the envelope is sufficiently small and $C_{\rm step}=\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b$ satisfies $C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, the conclusion is $\|D V(t,0)-D U(t,0)-\widetilde\chi(t)\mathbf a(t,0)\otimes\kappa(t,0)\|\le\lambda^{-1/3}$ for $t\in[t_0,T]$. The proof first bounds the higher-gradient error by $K_P\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/12}$ and then absorbs $\lambda^{-1/12}$. Constants precede the parent and expansion; the theorem is conditional on the listed earlier mathematical results.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.centralReturnCl.summary: Prove the central error bound from profile and evaluation estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.centralReturn_e.text: The central error. For an expansion of depth `P ≥ 1` over a parent, `V = U + W^♮` and `t ∈ [t₀,T]`, the difference `∇V(t,0) - ∇U(t,0) - χ̃(t) 𝐚(t,0) ⊗ κ(t,0)` equals `D_x(W_osc - V_1)^♮(t,0) + D_xW̄^♮(t,0)`. The profile facts `F_h(0) = 0`, `F_h'(0) = 1` enter through `leading_graph_hasFDerivAt_origin`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.centralReturn_e.summary: The central gradient equals the prescribed rank one part

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.closedSlabLeray.text: applying the real cutoff and the periodic Leray projection to the approximate momentum equation gives (5.58). The commutation of `S_Λ` with the time and space derivatives and the preservation of divergence freeness are the hypotheses `htime`, `hspace`, `hdivc` (Lemma B.1).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.closedSlabLeray.summary: Deriving the projected residual identity on the slab

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.coefC.text:
The number of words of length at most one in the three label directions.

Default-value audit (b5): The definition uses finite word counts and total real arithmetic. Maxima or absolute values, where present, ensure the chosen majorants remain nonnegative; the formula itself is not a proof that an arbitrary input constant bounds a field. The analytic estimates provide the corresponding coefficient or level bounds.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.coefC.summary: Counting the label words through order one

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.coefC_nonneg.text: The constant `coefC` of (D.6) at order one is nonnegative.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.coefC_nonneg.summary: Nonnegative counts of label derivative words

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.coefK.text:
The constant `κ₀ = #W_1 · max(K₁(1), 0)` bounding the order-one norms of the coefficients `(D_aX)⁻¹`, `M`, `P_κ` by `κ₀ 𝖣^{C₁}` ((D.6), (5.8) of Proposition 5.1).

Default-value audit (b5): The definition uses finite word counts and total real arithmetic. Maxima or absolute values, where present, ensure the chosen majorants remain nonnegative; the formula itself is not a proof that an arbitrary input constant bounds a field. The analytic estimates provide the corresponding coefficient or level bounds.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.coefK.summary: The coefficient constant from the parent geometry bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.coefNorm.text: The norm of a phase-independent coefficient `L(c(t,a))` on a time domain mapped into `[0,T]`, from the bounds (D.6) (`hD6`, finiteness of the jets) and (5.8) (`h58`) of Proposition 5.1: finite, and at most `#W_n ‖L‖ B`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.coefNorm.summary: Finite coefficient norms from the parent estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.coef_bounds.text: Norms of a phase-independent coefficient (copy of the S5b glue `coef_bounds`, with a vector-valued `L`). For a smooth `G` with uniformly bounded jets and `ℓ^m |∇^m G(t,a)| ≤ B` for `m ≤ n`, the field `(t,a,s) ↦ L(G(t,a))` has a finite norm (D.1) of order `n`, at most `#W_n ‖L‖ B`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.coef_bounds.summary: Profile norms of phase independent coefficients

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.contDiff_slice.text: A jointly smooth field on a closed time slab has a smooth spatial slice at each time belonging to that slab. The proof composes with the constant-time inclusion, so the slab endpoints cause no spatial differentiability problem.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.contDiff_slice.summary: Spatial smoothness of a closed slab field

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.contDiff_slice_.text: A jointly smooth field on [a,b] × ℝ³ has a smooth spatial slice for every t in [a,b], including both endpoints. This supplies the cutoff argument with spatial regularity without extending time derivatives beyond the slab.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.curlCorrection_.text: The divergence correction `C[V] = 𝐝 × Q[V]` of a profile vanishing on the inactive region vanishes there (it centres its input and acts pointwise in time and label).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.curlCorrection_.summary: The divergence correction preserves the inactive region

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.cutoffPressureT.summary: The quadratic velocity tail in the pressure estimate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.cutoffVelocityD.summary: The velocity change under Fourier truncation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.divergence_add_.text: The divergence is additive on differentiable fields.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.divergence_add_.summary: Divergence distributes over differentiable vector fields

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.envelopeSupport.text: The support `supp g` of the periodized envelope is invariant under lattice translations.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.envelopeSupport.summary: The envelope support is invariant under lattice shifts

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.exists_closedSl.text: Continuous spatially periodic slices on a closed time interval descend to continuous functions on the unit torus. The selected family agrees with the original velocity at every time in the interval; no agreement outside that interval is claimed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.exists_closedSl.summary: Representing every periodic time slice on the torus

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.exists_cutoffBo.text: Let $V,R_V$ be jointly smooth periodic fields on $[0,T]$, with $V$ divergence free, and let $\Pi(t,\cdot)$ be smooth and periodic at each time. Assume $V_t+V\cdot\nabla V+\nabla\Pi=R_V$. For $P\ge2$, $\Lambda\ge1$ and a smooth radial cutoff $0\le\psi\le1$, equal to one on the unit ball and zero outside radius two, take an already constructed stage $u=S_\Lambda V,p$. Given the real and complex Fourier tail estimates and Hölder product bound, constants independent of $T,\Lambda,V$ give $\|u(t)-V(t)\|_{C^{2,1/2}}\le K_P\varepsilon_\Lambda$. Separately, each of $\|R_u(t)\|_{C^{1,1/2}}$ and $\|D^2(p-\Pi)(t)\|_{C^{0,1/2}}$ is at most $C\|R_V(t)\|_{C^{1,1/2}}+K_P\varepsilon_\Lambda$, where $\varepsilon_\Lambda=\Lambda^{2-P}(1+\|V\|_{C_tC^{P,1/2}})^2$. These are pointwise-in-time estimates; the summed bound in (5.56) follows after enlarging constants. No time regularity of $\Pi$ is assumed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.exists_cutoffBo.summary: Control the velocity tail, residual, and pressure difference together

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.exists_mean_eul.text: The mean equation (5.11) is solvable, with the Eulerian form (4.12) (copy of `Lib.S5a.meanSolvable_of_theorem42`,, keeping the conjunct of the smooth-force item of Theorem 4.2 that the copy discarded): for a phase-independent source `f̄` there is a normalized solution `(B, q̄)` of (5.11) for which `b = B∘X⁻¹`, `q = q̄∘X⁻¹` and `f = f̄∘X⁻¹` satisfy `div b = 0` and the linearized Euler equation (4.12), the latter two being the conclusions of `h4_2` for the solution of (4.9) that gives `(B, q̄)`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.exists_mean_eul.summary: Solving the mean equation through linearized Euler evolution

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.exists_realFour.text: the zero-mean Poisson pressure of the cutoff velocity, whose residual is (5.58). The band and divergence properties of the cutoff are the hypotheses `hband`, `hdivc` (Lemma B.1).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.exists_realFour.summary: Constructing the zero mean pressure of the cutoff velocity

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.exists_torusVec.text: For a continuous torus vector field whose lift is C¹, its ith coordinate derivative is itself the lift of a continuous torus vector field. This supplies the input needed by the spatial derivative commutation clause of Lemma B.1.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.exists_torusVec.summary: A periodic coordinate derivative descends to the torus

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.expansionPressu.summary: Splitting the pressure into three contributions

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.expansion_eq_sp.text: `W = V_1 + (W_osc - V_1) + W̄`, with `W_osc - V_1 = ∑_{p=2}^P V_p + ∑_{p=1}^P C_{p+1}` and `W̄ = ∑_{p=2}^P B_p`, for profiles with `B_1 = 0`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.expansion_eq_sp.summary: Splitting the velocity into leading and remainder terms

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fderivWithin_sl.text: The material derivative of (4.12) on the closed slab: for `b` smooth on `[0,T] × ℝ³`, `∂_{(1,u)} b(t,x) = ∂_t b(t,x) + (Db)(t,x) u` (time derivative within `[0,T]`).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fderivWithin_sl.summary: Splitting the material derivative on a closed slab

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fderiv_graphFie.text: The chain rule for the readout `y ↦ G(Y y, k·Y y)` of a vector-valued label-phase field.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fderiv_graphFie.summary: Differentiating a vector field on the physical graph

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fderiv_inverseF.summary: The inverse deformation along the inverse flow

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fderiv_left_com.text: At a point where f is differentiable, applying a fixed continuous linear map L commutes with taking the Fréchet derivative: the derivative is L composed with Df. It is used to move tensor-column projections through derivatives.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fderiv_tensorCo.text: For a differentiable momentum-tensor field, differentiating its ith column in the ith coordinate direction equals taking the ith column of the tensor derivative in that direction. This permits the cutoff commutation argument to act column by column.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fderiv_tensorCo.summary: Differentiation commutes with selecting a tensor column

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fieldNormFinite.text: Finite norms (D.1) are closed under addition.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fieldNormFinite.summary: Finite derivative norms persist under addition

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fieldNormFinite.text: Finite norms (D.1) are closed under finite sums.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fieldNormFinite.summary: Finite sums retain finite derivative norms

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fieldNormFinite.text: The zero field has finite norms.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fieldNormFinite.summary: The zero profile has finite derivative norms

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fieldNorm_add_l.text: The norm (D.1) is subadditive on fields with finite norms.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fieldNorm_add_l.summary: The triangle inequality for profile norms

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fieldNorm_sum_l.text: The norm (D.1) of a finite sum of fields with finite norms is at most the sum of the norms.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fieldNorm_sum_l.summary: Bounding the derivative norm of a finite sum

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fieldNorm_zero.text: The zero field has norm zero.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.fieldNorm_zero.summary: The zero profile has zero derivative norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.gradient_graphR.text: The chain rule (3.1) for the gradient of the readout of a scalar profile: `∇_x f^♮ = (𝐝 f + κ ∂_s f)^♮`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.gradient_graphR.summary: The pressure gradient along the physical graph

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.graphRead_slice.text: The Eulerian readout `f^♮(t) = graphRead (X(t → 0)) f t` of a twisted profile is smooth on `ℝ³` at each time of the slab.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.graphRead_slice.summary: Smoothness of a physical graph evaluation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.hessianSub.text: For two C² scalar pressures p and q, the Hessian of p−q is the difference of their Hessians. This algebraic identity separates the cutoff pressure error from the approximate pressure before the one-sided comparison is added.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.hessianSub.summary: Taking the Hessian of a pressure difference

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.higherHessianCl.text: Assume the parent coefficient estimates, existence of the finite expansion, the hierarchy bounds, the physical derivative estimates and the finite-norm product estimates. For $P\ge2$, $0<T\le1$ and a smooth periodic parent satisfying the deformation, Fourier, residual and coercivity assumptions of §5.1, the formal statement proves $\|D_x^2\sum_{p=2}^{P}\mathsf p_p^\natural\|_\infty\le K_P\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/12}$ on $[0,T]$, under the central stability and coupling hypotheses, $0<\gamma\le1$ and $\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$. Constants precede the parent and expansion. The proof uses $\kappa\partial_s\mathsf p_p=P_\kappa(f_p+f_p^S-2MV_p)$ before taking one more physical derivative. Taking two unrestricted physical derivatives would instead leave $\lambda^{1/12}$. This proves the intermediate assertion (5.52), conditional on the stated earlier estimates.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.higherHessianCl.summary: Replace one phase derivative using the transverse pressure equation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.idB.text:
The identity of `𝓛(ℝ³)`, as the bilinear map `(A, v) ↦ A v`.

Default-value audit (b5): This is a total algebraic or continuous-linear construction with no division or noncanonical choice. Zero inputs have their literal algebraic values. Any geometric identification or differentiability property is supplied separately by the consuming theorem.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.idB.summary: Applying a coefficient operator to a vector

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.inactiveVP.text:
The inactive region `{t < t₀} ∪ {a ∉ supp g}` of the slab, as a submodule of profiles.

Default-value audit (b5): The vanishing submodule is defined by pointwise equalities before activation or outside the periodized envelope support. It imposes no condition on active points inside the support. Derivative closure uses the open complementary region and profile smoothness.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.inactiveVP.summary: Profiles vanishing before activation or outside the envelope

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.inactive_of_pro.text: Proposition 5.4 gives support of the sources and completed oscillatory sum, rather than all separate pressures. This lemma recovers the vanishing of V_p, p_p and C_p individually by starting with the leading pair and applying uniqueness of the zero-initial transverse solve at each level. The inactive region combines t < t₀ with labels outside the periodized envelope support.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.inactive_of_pro.summary: Recovering individual supports from the hierarchy support theorem

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.inner_carrier_f.text: The phase gradient is the transported wave vector: `k_*·D_xY v = κ(t, Y(x))·v`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.inner_carrier_f.summary: The carrier pulls back to the transported wave vector

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.inverseDeformat.text: The inverse deformation `G(t,·) = (D_aX(t,·))⁻¹` is smooth in the label.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.inverseDeformat.summary: Smoothness of the inverse deformation field

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.inverseFlow_lat.text: The inverse label flow is lattice equivariant.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.inverseFlow_lat.summary: The inverse flow respects lattice translations

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.inverseFlow_ori.text: The inverse label flow fixes the origin.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.inverseFlow_ori.summary: Oddness fixes the origin under the inverse flow

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.inverseFlow_rig.text: `X(t, Y(x)) = x` for the inverse flow `Y = X t 0`.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.inverseFlow_smo.text: The inverse label flow `Y(t) = X(t → 0)` of a parent is jointly smooth on the slab.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.jet_one_le.text: The first derivative of `Q` on `(α,σ)` from the scaled jets.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.jet_one_le.summary: Bounding a directional derivative from scaled jets

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.labelB.text:
`labelB j (A, r) = r Aᵀe_j`.

Default-value audit (b5): This is a total algebraic or continuous-linear construction with no division or noncanonical choice. Zero inputs have their literal algebraic values. Any geometric identification or differentiability property is supplied separately by the consuming theorem.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.labelB.summary: A scalar coefficient times a transposed coframe column

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.labelB_apply.text: Evaluation formula for the bilinear label map `labelB j`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.labelB_apply.summary: Evaluating the label gradient bilinear map

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.labelFlow_eq.text: Two label flows of a field that is uniformly Lipschitz in space on `[0,T]` agree on `[0,T]`.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.labelGrad_mem_i.text: The label gradient `𝐝q` of a profile vanishing on the inactive region vanishes there.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.labelGrad_mem_i.summary: Label gradients preserve vanishing in the inactive region

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.labelPaths_eqOn.text: Two particle paths with the same initial value and the same uniformly spatially Lipschitz velocity agree on the specified closed interval. The proof uses uniqueness for the time-dependent ODE, then extends equality from the initial point across the interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.labelPaths_eqOn.summary: Uniqueness of uniformly Lipschitz particle paths

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.labelPhaseUnsca.text:
The inverse of the label-phase scaling `(x,s) ↦ (ℓx, hs)`.

Default-value audit (b5): This linear map uses the total reciprocals ℓ⁻¹ and h⁻¹; if either scale is zero its corresponding component collapses. The cancellation theorem explicitly assumes nonzero scales, and the analytic applications use positive ℓ and h.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.le_abs_rpow_of_.text: `K 𝖣^C λ^{e₁} λ^{e₂} ≤ |K| 𝖣^C λ^e` for `λ ≥ 1` and `e₁ + e₂ ≤ e`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.le_abs_rpow_of_.summary: Absorbing smaller frequency powers into a common bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.leadingHessianC.text: Assume the phase-profile bounds, parent coefficient estimates, localized seed bounds, hierarchy estimates and finite-norm product estimates. For a finite expansion over a smooth periodic parent satisfying §5.1, with $\lambda\ge1$, $0<\gamma\le1$, sufficiently small envelope and $\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, the leading pressure satisfies $D_x^2\mathsf p_1^\natural\le K\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1/4}I$ on $[0,T]$. The coefficient $c_{\mathbf a}=2\widetilde\chi g(\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a)/|\kappa|^2$ is nonnegative, and the lower bound on $F_h\,{}^{\prime}$ controls $-c_{\mathbf a}F_h\,{}^{\prime}\kappa\otimes\kappa$ from above. The remaining tensors are bounded in norm. The formal proof obtains the leading pressure norm from the hierarchy estimate at level one; the paper cites (5.22). This difference concerns the argument, not the signed conclusion.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.leadingHessianC.summary: Positive coupling controls the only large pressure tensor by sign

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.leading_graph_h.text: The chain rule (3.1) at the origin for the leading oscillation: if `V_1` has the cell values `χ̃A₁ = χ̃ g 𝐚 F_h` of (3.7), then, for `t ∈ [t₀,T]`, `D_xV_1^♮(t,0) = χ̃(t) 𝐚(t,0) ⊗ κ(t,0)`. The inputs are `g(0) = 1` (`0 < ℓ_*`), `F_h(0) = 0` and `F_h'(0) = 1` (Lemma 3.1, here hypotheses), the fixed origin of the inverse flow, and `κ(t,0) = (D_xX(t → 0)(0))ᵀ k_*`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.leading_graph_h.summary: The leading wave gives the exact central rank one derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.leading_hess_po.text: The Hessian (5.51) at one point. For the vector fields `G₁ = 𝐝q`, `G₂ = κ∂_sq` of the label and phase gradient, read on the graph `Φ(y) = (Y y, k·Y y)`, the quadratic form of the derivative of `y ↦ G₁(Φ y) + G₂(Φ y)` is the phase term `c σ²` of `G₂` (`∂_sG₂ = c • κ`, `σ = κ·v = k·D_xY v`: the first tensor of (5.51)) plus the terms bounded by the scaled jets of order one of `G₁` (all components) and of `G₂` (label components only): the remaining tensors of (5.51).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.leading_hess_po.summary: Separating the signed leading pressure Hessian tensor

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.lemma59_of_clai.text: Lemma 5.9 from its four parts. (5.49) is the sum of the three Hessian bounds (`:252-255`); (5.50) is `CentralReturnClaim`. The constants are `a₀ = max` of the four, `b₀ = max (C₁ + C₂ + C₃) b₀(5.50)` and `Γ₀ P = max (1 + |K₁| + |K₂ P| + |K₃ P|) (Γ₀(5.50) P)`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.lemma59_of_clai.summary: Combining the three pressure bounds and central return

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.levelK.text:
The level constant of (5.52): `3c₁κ₀|K₆(2,p)| + (c₁κ₀ + c₁c₄κ₀²)|K₆(1,p)|`.

Default-value audit (b5): The definition uses finite word counts and total real arithmetic. Maxima or absolute values, where present, ensure the chosen majorants remain nonnegative; the formula itself is not a proof that an arbitrary input constant bounds a field. The analytic estimates provide the corresponding coefficient or level bounds.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.levelK.summary: The constant in one higher pressure estimate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.levelK_nonneg.text: The level constant `levelK K1 K6 p` of (5.52) is nonnegative.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.levelK_nonneg.summary: Nonnegative constants for the higher pressure levels

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.level_estimate.text: Real arithmetic for one level: with `B_c ℓ_*⁻¹ ≤ κ₀ Z`, `B_c ≤ κ₀ Z`, `B_c² ≤ κ₀² Z`, the level term of `wNorm_gradProfile_le` is at most `(3c_Lκ₀|K₂| + (c_Pκ₀ + c_Pc_Mκ₀²)|K₁|) Z X`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.level_estimate.summary: The frequency powers of one higher pressure level

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.meanHessianClai.text:
Assume the endpoint theorem, the hierarchy bounds, the physical evaluation estimates and the Fourier cutoff estimates. For a depth-$P\ge2$ expansion over the smooth periodic parent of §5.1, with its stable positively coupled nonzero seed, $0<\gamma\le1$ and $\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, the formal statement proves $\|D_x^2\sum_{p=2}^{P} ar q_p^
atural\|_\infty\le K_P\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/2}$ throughout $[0,T]$. The exponent and constants precede the parent and expansion. The mean equations give $\Delta ar q^
atural=\operatorname{div} ar f^
atural-2\operatorname{tr}(
abla U
abla ar W^
atural)$; phase-independent estimates bound its right-hand side and the bounded periodic operator $D^2\Delta^{-1}$ gives the Hessian bound. This is an absolute bound for the mean pressure, unlike the one-sided bound needed for the leading pressure.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.meanHessianClai.summary: Use the summed mean equation and the periodic Poisson estimate

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.meanSolution_ad.text: Sums of two solutions of (5.11) are solutions with the summed source.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.meanSolution_so.text: The source of a solution of (5.11) is independent of the phase.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.meanSolution_so.summary: A mean solution has a phase independent source

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.meanSolution_su.text: Finite sums of solutions of (5.11) are solutions with the summed source.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.meanSolution_su.summary: Summing the mean equations over all retained levels

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.mem_inactive_of.text: A twisted profile vanishes on the inactive region as soon as it vanishes at its inactive points over the label cell (the lattice twist and the periodicity of `supp g`).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.mem_inactive_of.summary: Vanishing on one cell implies vanishing everywhere

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.mixedDirection_.text: The weighted directions of (D.1) are constant, hence smooth.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.mixedDirection_.summary: The scaled coordinate directions are smooth

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.momentum_realFo.text: Copy of `momentum_realFourierCutoff_eq_residual_input` (the unprojected momentum identity behind (5.58)), with the commutation hypothesis `hspace` of Lemma B.1.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.momentum_realFo.summary: The momentum identity before the Leray projection

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.negB.text:
`negB (A, v) = -(A v + A v) = -2 A v`.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.negB.summary: Twice the negative strain action on a vector

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.nonempty_trunca.text: the truncation of §5.7 exists as a library child stage. The slice cutoff (`exists_truncatedParent_T1`) is inlined; oddness, divergence freeness and the band `2Λ` of the cutoff velocity come from the hypotheses `hpar`, `hdivc`, `hband` (Lemma B.1), and the Poisson pressure from the copy `exists_realFourierCutoffPoissonPressure`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.nonempty_trunca.summary: Constructing the smooth truncated child stage

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_adjL_le.text: The adjoint-type map `adjL` has operator norm at most one.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_adjL_le.summary: Transposition has operator norm at most one

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_carrier_le.summary: The carrier size is controlled by the parent deformation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_fderiv2_in.text: `|D_x²Y| ≤ 𝖣 B` when the label derivative of `G = (D_aX)⁻¹` is bounded by `B`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_fderiv2_in.summary: Bounding the second derivative of the inverse flow

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_fderiv_gra.text: (5.44) at `m = 1`, left side: the operator norm of `D_xf^♮(t,0)` is at most the sum of the suprema of the first coordinate derivatives of `f^♮(t)`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_fderiv_gra.summary: Profile words bound the derivative on the graph

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_fderiv_inv.summary: The parent bound controls the inverse deformation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_fderiv_le_.text: For a field with a bounded first derivative, the operator norm of the derivative at a point is at most the sum, over the coordinate words of length one, of the suprema in (5.44) at `m = 1`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_fderiv_le_.summary: First coordinate words control the derivative norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_idB_le.text: The identity bilinear map `idB` has norm at most one.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_idB_le.summary: Operator evaluation has bilinear norm at most one

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_iteratedFD.text: The iterated derivatives of `Q` from those of its scaled form.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_iteratedFD.summary: Unscaled derivatives from scaled jet bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_labelB_le.text: The bilinear label map `labelB j` has norm at most one.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_labelB_le.summary: The label gradient bilinear map is contractive

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_labelPhase.text: Norm bound for the unscaling of the label-phase jet.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_labelPhase.summary: Bounding the inverse label and phase scaling

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_labelWord_.text: A weighted label word of a smooth phase-independent field is at most `r^{|w|}` times the Fréchet jet of the same order.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_labelWord_.summary: Scaled label words are bounded by Fréchet jets

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_negB_le.text: The bilinear map `negB` has norm at most two.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_negB_le.summary: Twice the strain action has norm at most two

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.norm_waveVector.summary: The transported wave vector obeys the parent bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.odd_lift_of_cut.text: The parity clause of Lemma B.1 makes the cutoff of an odd lifted field odd (this replaces `odd_lift_realVectorFourierCutoff`).

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.opNorm_le_sum_c.text: The operator norm of a derivative is at most the sum of its values on the coordinate vectors.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.opNorm_le_sum_c.summary: Coordinate values control the derivative operator norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.parentGradient_.text: `‖∇U‖_{C^{0,1/2}} ≤ C𝖣²` for a smooth field with frequencies at most `4𝖣` and `‖∇U‖_∞ ≤ 𝖣`, from Bernstein's inequality (B.1) (`hB_1`), as in (copy of `exists_parentGradient_halfHolder_bound` with the Bernstein step from `hB_1`).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.parentGradient_.summary: Bernstein controls the parent gradient Hölder norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.periodic_sliceT.text: If every time slice of a velocity is spatially periodic on a closed interval, then its time derivative taken within that interval is spatially periodic at every time in the interval. The statement accommodates the endpoint derivative used by the cutoff momentum equation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.periodic_sliceT.summary: Closed slab time differentiation preserves spatial periodicity

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.phaseGrad_mem_i.text: The phase gradient `κ∂_s q` of a profile vanishing on the inactive region vanishes there (the inactive region does not depend on the phase).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.phaseGrad_mem_i.summary: Phase gradients preserve vanishing in the inactive region

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.phaseGrad_phase.text: On a phase line `q(a,s) = c P(s)` with `P' = F`, the phase derivative of the gradient field `G₂ = κ∂_sq` is `(c F'(s)) κ` (the first tensor `c_𝐚F_h'κ⊗κ` of (5.51)).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.phaseGrad_phase.summary: The phase derivative of the leading pressure gradient

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.phaseGrad_trans.text: The transverse equation (5.16): `κ∂_s𝗉 = P_κ(F - 2MV)` for a solution `(V, 𝗉)` of (5.15) with source `F` of zero phase mean, with `P_κ = |κ|⁻²κ⊗κ`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.phaseGrad_trans.summary: Eliminating a pressure derivative with the transverse equation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.phaseMean_eq_av.text: The phase mean of a profile is its average `⟨W⟩`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.phaseMean_eq_av.summary: Identifying the pulled back mean velocity

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.phaseOscillatio.text: The oscillatory part of the pulled-back field `c = (D_aX)^{-1}(W + v∘X)` is `(D_aX)^{-1}(W - ⟨W⟩)`: the perturbation `v∘X` and the coefficient are independent of the phase (`phaseOscillation_pullbackField_eq_uncut`), and the phase mean of the profile is the average `⟨W⟩` of the operators of the parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.phaseOscillatio.summary: Identifying the pulled back oscillatory velocity

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.prodC1.text:
The constant `#W_1 · 2 · 2` of (D.4) at order one for a bilinear map of norm at most one (the factor `2‖B‖ ≤ 2`).

Default-value audit (b5): The definition uses finite word counts and total real arithmetic. Maxima or absolute values, where present, ensure the chosen majorants remain nonnegative; the formula itself is not a proof that an arbitrary input constant bounds a field. The analytic estimates provide the corresponding coefficient or level bounds.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.prodC1.summary: The order one product constant for contractions

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.prodC1_nonneg.text: The constant `prodC1` of (D.4) at order one is nonnegative.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.prodC4.text:
The constant `#W_1 · 2 · 4` of (D.4) at order one for `‖B‖ ≤ 2`.

Default-value audit (b5): The definition uses finite word counts and total real arithmetic. Maxima or absolute values, where present, ensure the chosen majorants remain nonnegative; the formula itself is not a proof that an arbitrary input constant bounds a field. The analytic estimates provide the corresponding coefficient or level bounds.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.prodC4.summary: The order one product constant for twice an evaluation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.prodC4_nonneg.text: The constant `prodC4` of (D.4) at order one is nonnegative.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.prodC4_nonneg.summary: Nonnegative product constants for doubled evaluation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.profileDivergen.text: The vanishing of the total divergence `𝐝̃·W` of a profile, read along the parent flow: `div_y W(t, X(t,0)y, s) + ((D_aX)^{-T} k_*)·∂_s W = 0` at `y = X(0,t)a`. This is the computation of `HierarchyPhysicalApproximation.lean:370-401` for an arbitrary twisted profile.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.profileDivergen.summary: The profile divergence identity along the parent flow

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.profile_slice_s.text: A slice of a twisted profile is smooth in label and phase.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.profile_slice_s.summary: Smoothness of every label and phase slice

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.profile_sum_app.text: Evaluation of a finite sum of profiles.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.profile_sum_app.summary: Evaluating finite sums of hierarchy profiles

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.profile_sum_eva.text: Evaluation of a finite sum of twisted profiles.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.projectedMoment.text: Copy of `projectedMomentum_realFourierCutoff_eq_residual` with the commutation hypothesis `hspace` of Lemma B.1.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.projectedMoment.summary: The projected momentum identity after truncation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.quarter_pow.summary: The fourth root representation of the frequency

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.quarter_pow_neg.summary: Inverse frequency powers through the fourth root

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.radialEnvelope_.text: On the label cell, the envelope vanishes outside `supp g` (`2ℓ_* < 1/2`).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.radialEnvelope_.summary: The radial envelope vanishes outside its support

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.realTensorCutof.text: the tail of the real tensor cutoff `R ∘ S_Λ ∘ J` from the complex (B.2) (hypothesis `htc`, Lemma B.1) by contraction.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.realTensorCutof.summary: Transferring the complex cutoff tail to real tensors

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.realVectorFouri.text: the cutoff commutes with the tensor divergence of (5.58). The commutation of the real cutoff with the coordinate derivatives is the hypothesis `hspace` (Lemma B.1).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.realVectorFouri.summary: The cutoff commutes with tensor divergence

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.remainder_bound.text: Real arithmetic for the remaining tensors of (5.51): with `D, r ≥ 1`, `ℓ⁻¹ = D^a`, `h⁻¹ = r²`, `λ = r⁴` and the coefficient norms `B_c = c_c k_B D^{C₁}`, `B_κ = c_c D r⁴ k_B D^{C₁}`, the sum of the two terms is at most `28 c₁ c_c k_B D^N r⁶ W ‖v‖²` for `C₁ + 2a + 2 ≤ N`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.remainder_bound.summary: Estimating the two remaining leading Hessian tensors

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.scaledJets_appl.text: Scaled jets of `G(a) F(a,s)`: Leibniz' rule for the evaluation of a label-dependent operator `G` on a profile `F`, with `|ℓ| ≤ 1`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.scaledJets_appl.summary: Leibniz bounds for the inverse deformation times a profile

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.scaledJets_of_u.text: The scaled jets of a twisted profile at a time `t ∈ [0,T]` are bounded by its unweighted norm (D.1).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.scaledJets_of_u.summary: Unweighted profile norms bound the scaled jets

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.scaledJets_of_w.text: The scaled jets of a twisted profile at a time `t ∈ [t₀,T]` are bounded by its weighted norm (D.1), for a weight `0 < γ ≤ 1`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.scaledJets_of_w.summary: Weighted profile norms bound the scaled jets

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.scaled_unscale.text: Scaling then unscaling a jet is the identity.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.slice_smooth_c.text: A jointly smooth field on the slab is smooth at each time.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.slice_smooth_c.summary: Spatial smoothness of a coefficient slice

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.slices_labelGra.text: `𝐝q = ∑_j (∂_{a_j} q) Gᵀe_j` on a time set `A ⊆ [0,T]`, with `G = (D_aX)⁻¹`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.slices_labelGra.summary: Expanding the label gradient into coefficient products

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.slices_phaseGra.text: `κ∂_s𝗉 = P_κ(F - 2MV)` for a transverse solution, as the product `idB (P_κ, F + negB (M, V))` on a time set `A ⊆ [0,T]`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.slices_phaseGra.summary: The phase pressure gradient from the transverse equation

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.spatialHolderHa.text: For a field with finite C^(m,1/2) norm, sums the nonnegative derivative-level contributions. The finiteness hypothesis is retained because the norm uses real-valued suprema.
The second spatial derivative of a smooth periodic pressure is in `C^{0,1/2}`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.spatialHolderHa.summary: A smooth periodic pressure has a Hölder Hessian

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.spatialHolderHa.text: If n ≤ m and f has C^(m,1/2) regularity with finite norm, then f also has C^(n,1/2) regularity and its lower-order norm is at most the original one. The result uses nonnegative summands in the derivative-order sum.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.spatialHolderHa.summary: Lower derivative orders inherit Hölder regularity

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.spatialHolderHa.text: Negating a C^(m,1/2) field preserves the regularity predicate and leaves its norm unchanged. This is used when expressing cutoff differences with either sign.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.spatialHolderHa.summary: Negation preserves Hölder regularity and its norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.spatialHolderHa.text: the real cutoff is bounded on `C^{m,1/2}`, from (B.2) at `s = M = m` (hypothesis `hvt`, Lemma B.1).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.spatialHolderHa.summary: The real cutoff is bounded in Hölder norms

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.spatialLevel_no.text: For a C^(m,1/2) field and j ≤ m, both the supremum norm and the half Hölder seminorm of its jth derivative are finite and nonnegative. Their sum is the nonnegative contribution of that derivative order to the physical norm.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.spatialLevel_no.summary: Nonnegative derivative contributions to the Hölder norm

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.spatiallyPeriod.text: Any function on the unit torus becomes spatially periodic when composed with the quotient map from ℝ³. No regularity assumption is required for this equality.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.spatiallyPeriod.summary: Lifting a torus field gives spatial periodicity

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.tensorComplexif.text:
The complexification of the columns of a momentum tensor (the library's private `momentumTensorComplexify`, `TruncatedParentResidual.lean:631`).

Default-value audit (b5): This is a total algebraic or continuous-linear construction with no division or noncanonical choice. Zero inputs have their literal algebraic values. Any geometric identification or differentiability property is supplied separately by the consuming theorem.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.tensorComplexif.summary: Embedding a real momentum tensor into complex columns

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.tensorRealPart.text:
The real part of the columns (the library's private `momentumTensorRealPart`).

Default-value audit (b5): This is a total algebraic or continuous-linear construction with no division or noncanonical choice. Zero inputs have their literal algebraic values. Any geometric identification or differentiability property is supplied separately by the consuming theorem.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.tensorRealPart.summary: Taking real parts of momentum tensor columns

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.tensorRealPart_.text: Taking the real part of each column after embedding a real momentum tensor into the complex Euclidean space recovers the tensor. This is the algebraic identity needed to transfer the complex Fourier tail estimate to real tensor fields.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.tensorRealPart_.summary: Recovering a real tensor after complexification

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.toUnitTorus_neg.text: The quotient map from ℝ³ to the unit torus commutes with negation. It transfers the reflection identity for a torus cutoff to the lifted physical field.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.transverseSolut.text: A solution of (5.15) from `V(0) = 0` whose source has zero phase mean and vanishes on the inactive region vanishes there, together with its pressure: it is the library ODE solve (`exists_transverseResult`), by uniqueness (`Bridge.TransverseSolution.unique`), and that solve keeps the inactive region (its field `inactive`).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.transverseSolut.summary: Uniqueness propagates inactive sources to velocity and pressure

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.truncatedEulerP.text: Copy of `truncatedEulerProjectedResidual_holder_bound` (the velocity tail and (5.58) in physical Hölder norms), from the copy `truncatedParentProjectedResidual_holder_bound` with the momentum tensor; the B.1 tails and (5.59) are hypotheses.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.truncatedEulerP.summary: Bounding the velocity tail and projected Euler residual

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.truncatedParent.text: Let $P\ge2$, $\Lambda\ge1$, and let the periodic fields satisfy $V\in C^{P,1/2}$ and $R_V\in C^{1,1/2}$. Assume the real and complex Fourier tail estimates, a Hölder product estimate, a bounded linear projection on $C^{1,1/2}$, and the specified bounded bilinear product and contraction. Put $u=S_\Lambda V$ and $\varepsilon_\Lambda=\Lambda^{2-P}(1+\|V\|_{C^{P,1/2}})^2$. Then $u-V\in C^{2,1/2}$ and the projected expression in (5.58) belongs to $C^{1,1/2}$, with bounds $K_P\varepsilon_\Lambda$ and $C\|R_V\|_{C^{1,1/2}}+K_P\varepsilon_\Lambda$. The constant may depend on those operators, but not on the fields or cutoff frequency. This is a spatial estimate for an algebraically defined expression; its identification with the physical residual uses a separate momentum identity.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.truncatedParent.summary: Estimate the differentiated quadratic cutoff error in Hölder norms

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.wNorm_gradProfi.text: The norm of the gradient profile of a sum of levels. For `q_p` with transverse solutions `(V_p, 𝗉_p = q_p)` of (5.15) with sources `F_p`, `p ∈ s`, the profile `𝐝̃ ∑ q_p = 𝐝 ∑ q_p + κ∂_s ∑ q_p` has `‖·‖_{[1],γ}` at most the sum over `p` of the label part (`wNorm_labelGrad_le`) and the phase part (`wNorm_phaseGrad_le`).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.wNorm_gradProfi.summary: Bounding the summed higher pressure gradient profile

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.wNorm_labelGrad.text: `‖𝐝q‖_{[1],γ} ≤ C ‖G‖_{[1]} ℓ_*⁻¹ ‖q‖_{[2],γ}` ("The label derivative costs a power of `𝖣`"), by (D.4) for the products `(∂_{a_j} q) Gᵀe_j` and (D.3) for `∑_j ‖∂_{a_j} q‖_{[1],γ} ≤ 3 ℓ_*⁻¹ ‖q‖_{[2],γ}` (both from `hD_1`).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.wNorm_labelGrad.summary: Label pressure derivatives cost only a parent power

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.wNorm_phaseGrad.text: `‖κ∂_sq‖_{[1],γ} ≤ C ‖κ‖_{[1]} h⁻¹ ‖q‖_{[2],γ}`, by (D.4) for the product of the wave vector `κ` (phase independent) with `∂_sq` and (D.3) for `∂_s` (both from `hD_1`).
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.wNorm_phaseGrad.summary: A weighted bound for the scalar phase pressure gradient

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.wNorm_phaseGrad.text: `‖κ∂_s𝗉‖_{[1],γ} ≤ C ‖P_κ‖_{[1]} (‖f‖_{[1],γ} + C ‖M‖_{[1]} ‖V‖_{[1],γ})` for a transverse solution `(V, 𝗉)` of (5.15) with source `f` ("the phase term is bounded by the source and velocity"): `κ∂_s𝗉 = P_κ(f - 2MV)` is a product of the coefficient `P_κ` with `f + (-2)MV`, itself the sum of `f` and a product of the coefficient `M` with `V`; (D.4) of `hD_1` is used twice.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.wNorm_phaseGrad.summary: The source and velocity bound the phase pressure gradient

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.weighted_add.text: The time weight distributes over sums of fields.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.weighted_sum.text: The time weight distributes over finite sums of fields.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.word_add.text: Derivative words are additive on smooth functions.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.word_zero.text: Derivative words vanish on the zero function.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S5c.word_zero.summary: Derivative words annihilate the zero field

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.ApproxClause.text: Defines the portion of Lemma 5.8 needed for one local step: joint smoothness, periodicity, oddness and zero divergence of the graph-read velocity, periodic smooth pressure, and the momentum-residual identity on the closed slab. The residual is computed from those fields; it is not an independently assigned error variable.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.ApproxClause.summary: The approximate solution and its actual residual

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.Body510.text: Names Lemma 5.10 at fixed constants. A smooth periodic divergence-free correction `v`, with spatial derivatives through order two bounded by the prescribed small scale, is added to the approximate velocity. The conclusion provides a flow with deformation bounds and bounds every compatible label flow under the same hypotheses.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.Body510.summary: Flow deformation after a small correction

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.Body511.text: Bundles Proposition 5.11 after choosing `ψ`, the exponents and constants. It retains expansion and smallness hypotheses, then supplies a truncation and its regularity, Fourier support, velocity error, residual and pressure bounds. The residual is `momentumResidual` of the chosen velocity and pressure; the Fourier-tail parameter uses the slab Hölder norm.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.Body511.summary: Truncation estimates at a fixed Fourier symbol

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.Body54.text: Packages Proposition 5.4 after the radius exponent `a` has been fixed. Under the parent, launch and origin hypotheses it includes seed and expansion existence, finite-order uniqueness, divergence and residual identities, support, and vanishing before activation. The declaration names an assumed proposition; it proves none of those conclusions.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.Body54.summary: Expansion identities at a chosen radius exponent

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.Body58.text: Names the body of Lemma 5.8 with `a`, `b`, `Γ` and the order-dependent constants `K` fixed. The expansion, parent and smallness hypotheses remain explicit. Its conclusions cover smoothness, the exact momentum residual, oscillation and mean bounds, and the residual bound containing the derivative of the time cutoff.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.Body58.summary: Approximate solution estimates at fixed constants

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.Body59.text: Records Lemma 5.9 at specified constants while retaining the parent, seed, expansion and smallness assumptions. It bounds the quadratic form of the natural pressure Hessian and the error in the central rank-one gradient contribution. The latter assertion is restricted to the active interval from `t₀` through `T`.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.Body59.summary: Pressure and central gradient at fixed constants

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.CutoffChild.text: Stores a torus representative of an approximate velocity, its actual Fourier cutoff, and a smooth mean-zero pressure satisfying the Poisson and projected-momentum equations. Velocity regularity, oddness, zero divergence and Fourier support are fields. Unlike `TruncatedChildStage`, this record omits the approximate-residual representation and its cutoff identity.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.CutoffChild.summary: The Fourier cutoff and its Poisson pressure

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.CutoffChild.p.text: The cutoff child’s Euclidean velocity is spatially periodic for every real time. The proof uses equality in the unit torus after translation by an integer lattice vector. It needs no slab-membership premise because periodicity comes from the global torus representation, independently of the slab regularity fields.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.CutoffChild.r.text: Defines the residual from the cutoff child’s velocity and selected pressure using `momentumResidual` on the closed slab. The time derivative is therefore taken within that slab. No residual estimate is asserted here; those estimates must be supplied when the child becomes an inductive stage.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.CutoffChild.r.summary: Compute the momentum residual of the cutoff

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.CutoffChild.v.text: Defines the velocity by composing the stored continuous torus field with `toUnitTorus`. Thus the Euclidean field is periodic at every time by construction. Its smoothness and equation properties on the closed slab come from the record; this definition does not extend those properties to other times.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.CutoffChild.v.summary: Lift the cutoff velocity to Euclidean space

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.CutoffChild.v.text: Expresses the child velocity as the real vector Fourier cutoff of its stored approximate torus field, lifted back to Euclidean space. This equality holds at every time by the record’s `cutoff` field. Agreement of that representative with the original approximate velocity is separately restricted to the slab.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.CutoffChild.v.summary: Identify the lifted velocity with the Fourier cutoff

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.InductiveEule.text: Constructs an `InductiveEulerStage` from a cutoff child and explicit velocity, flow, residual and pressure bounds. Equalities `hSlab` and `hRadius` identify its time interval and Fourier radius with the schedule. The stored velocity and pressure are preserved; the residual bound is rewritten into the stage’s inverse-cube notation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.InductiveEule.summary: Turn the cutoff child into an inductive stage

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.InductiveEule.text: The stage assembled from a cutoff child has the same pressure function as that child. All bounds needed to construct the stage remain hypotheses; this theorem adds no pressure estimate. Its purpose is to transport the actual Poisson pressure and its Hessian bounds through the record constructor.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.InductiveEule.summary: The assembled stage preserves its pressure

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.InductiveEule.text: Under exactly the hypotheses of `InductiveEulerStage.ofCutoffChild`, its velocity equals the cutoff child’s lifted velocity. Substituting the slab and Fourier-radius equalities makes the result reflexive. This identity allows estimates proved for the child field to be used for the new indexed stage.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.InductiveEule.summary: The assembled stage preserves its velocity

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.InductiveEule.text: Builds a complete later step from a certified prefix, an actual later-wave selection and its cutoff child. The prefix supplies the accumulated first-coupling estimate; the crossing supplies strength and ratio information. The step uses the same child and wave throughout, preserving their quantitative and geometric identities.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.InductiveEule.summary: Extend the certified prefix with the constructed child

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.InductiveEule.text: For a growing crossing and a child decomposed as approximate velocity plus tail, adds the tail’s first spatial derivative to the central error. The assumed second-order tail bound and scheduled frequency relations improve the combined estimate to the inverse quarter power of the child frequency. The cutoff-weighted rank-one contribution is preserved.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.InductiveEule.summary: Add the Fourier tail to the central gradient error

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.InductiveEule.text: Constructs an `InductiveEulerWave` using the supplied crossing, cutoff child and quantitative hypotheses. It stores the actual amplitude, wave vector, smooth switch and corrected central error, then proves the crossing ratio and completed-cutoff clauses. The hypotheses tie the child velocity to the same cutoff field used in every error estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.InductiveEule.summary: Attach the actual crossing to the cutoff child

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.LocalStep.text: Asserts existence of the parent geometry, seed, cutoff and finite expansion that connect a specified parent stage, child stage and wave. The clauses include actual graph-read oscillation, truncation and approximate-residual identities. This is local data for already supplied stages; it does not by itself choose an infinite construction.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.LocalStep.summary: Record the parent and expansion for one step

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.StepApproxBou.text: Collects four properties of the supplied approximate fields: full-depth velocity size, residual size, oscillation size and low-order mean bounds. It is a proposition about existing velocities, not their construction. In particular, it contains no pressure-Hessian field; the child pressure is controlled later using Proposition 5.11.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.StepApproxBou.summary: The approximation estimates needed by one step

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.StepNumbers.text: Records the numerical conditions needed to apply the Section 5 statements at parent index `i`: flow smallness, residual decay, tail constants, parent jets, oscillation constants and mean bounds. The full-depth order is determined by `P.order (i + 2)`. This proposition concerns constants and frequencies, not existence of any velocity field.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.StepNumbers.summary: The numerical inequalities consumed by one step

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.TailBounds.text: Defines a uniform family of tail estimates for every `CutoffChild`: if the approximate velocity has Hölder regularity at order `M`, then its difference from the cutoff child has each lower order `m ≤ M`, with the usual factor $\Lambda^{m-M}$. The constants `Ct` are supplied, not constructed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.TailBounds.summary: All lower order errors of a Fourier cutoff

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.abs_le_orderM.text: For an order satisfying `hP : P ≤ 7 * frequencyExponent b s`, bounds its absolute constant by the finite majorant. The proof uses nonnegativity of every summand. It supplies the elementary domination needed when the construction chooses one threshold for many expansion orders.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.abs_log_le_of.text: If $|u-1|\le\varepsilon\le1/2$, then $|\log u|\le2\varepsilon$. The assumptions imply `u ≥ 1/2`, so the logarithm is controlled away from zero. This turns a relative estimate for the new first coupling into the logarithmic increment that is summed over successive crossings.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.abs_log_le_of.summary: Convert a small relative change to a logarithmic bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.activation_lt.text: Assuming `Theorem71Conclusions`, proves that every activation time is strictly below the limit `T`. Monotonicity and convergence first give a weak upper bound; comparison with a later strictly larger activation makes it strict. The low indices require a separate comparison with the third activation.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.activation_lt.summary: Every activation precedes the accumulation time

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.activation_mo.text: Extracts monotonicity of the whole activation sequence from `h71 : Theorem71Conclusions c C T`. The first two physical activation times coincide at zero, and the unused index zero is also zero. Strict growth is only supplied from index two onward, so the global conclusion is monotonicity.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.affineWave_ex.text: Given a continuous matrix field and nonzero perpendicular initial wave vector and amplitude, constructs solutions of the wave ODEs on the closed interval and preserves both nonvanishing and orthogonality. No Euler condition on the matrix field is assumed. This permits an approximate parent gradient, for which the affine Euler hypotheses need not hold.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.affineWave_ex.summary: Solve the wave equations over a continuous gradient

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.average_expan.text: For an expansion satisfying `S5.IsExpansion`, and assuming its first velocity level has zero phase average, proves that the whole expansion averages to the sum of mean terms from level two through `P`. Higher transverse profiles and curl corrections have zero mean, while the mean profiles are phase independent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.average_expan.summary: The phase average is exactly the mean correction

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.average_first.text: Proves zero phase average of the first velocity level from the actual expansion and seed data. The launch hypothesis, positive radius and phase width, and fit of the envelope inside the fundamental cell are retained. The proof identifies this level with the leading velocity profile, whose phase factor has mean zero.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.average_first.summary: The leading oscillation has zero phase average

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.band_mono.text: A continuous torus field supported at frequencies at most `D` also satisfies the support predicate for any larger cutoff `D′`. The proof simply restricts the vanishing requirement to fewer Fourier modes. No smoothness or positivity hypothesis is needed for this monotonicity statement.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.base_gradient.text: Adds the first spatial derivative of the actual cutoff tail to the approximate central error when the first cutoff is identically one. Differentiability, second-order tail control and the approximate gradient estimate are explicit premises. Large current frequency and a nondecreasing next frequency bound the new error by the inverse quarter power.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.base_gradient.summary: The first child has the required central gradient splitting

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.bernstein_all.text: From the assumed Lemma B.1, obtains nonnegative constants `K m` bounding the full $m$th derivative of a smooth periodic lift with frequencies at most $4D$. The conclusion is $K_m A D^m$ when the torus sup norm is at most `A`. The factor $3^m$ converts coordinate estimates to operator norms.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.bernstein_all.summary: Bernstein bounds for the full spatial derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.centerWaveOn_.text: From the assumed Lemma 2.6 and a growing crossing, proves `CenterWaveOn` whenever `D` dominates the transverse transfer constant and inverse coupling lower bound. The proof uses the transfer operator on every transverse solution and cancels the positive seed scaling. The crossing record supplies nonvanishing, orthogonality and the coupling estimate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.centerWaveOn_.summary: Transfer comparison bounds to the central seed hypotheses

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.centerWaveOn_.text: Converts `Lemma61Conclusions` for an existing first wave into `CenterWaveOn` for the stationary shear gradient, for positive frequency and any `D ≥ 2`. The propagation estimate’s normalization factor is canceled using nonvanishing amplitude, and the normalized coupling estimate becomes the required unnormalized inner-product lower bound.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.centerWaveOn_.summary: The first wave satisfies the central seed requirements

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.clock_mem_act.text: For any normalized time in `[0,T]`, its physical clock value belongs to the active slab. Strict monotonicity of the clock supplies both endpoints. This is the converse domain conversion needed when applying the comparison results and when transferring peak-amplitude statements to physical time.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.clock_mem_act.summary: Return normalized time to the active interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.complete_eq_z.text: If a twisted vector profile vanishes on an entire time slice, its divergence-correcting completion also vanishes on that slice. The covector is phase independent and nonzero, and the time lies in a positive slab. The proof first removes the zero phase average, then applies the completion’s slice identity.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.complete_eq_z.summary: A vanishing profile has a vanishing completion

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.conclusions_o.text: From an actual construction, the prescribed stationary base and cutoff formulas, and the initial-frequency floor, obtains the full `Theorem71Conclusions` bundle for some accumulation time. Most clauses come from stage and wave fields. The additional eventual-comparison clause uses the supplied Lemmas 1.3, 2.2 and B.1; it is not merely a projection.
TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.conclusions_o.summary: Export the quantitative conclusions and common lifetime

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.contDiff_slic.text: A function jointly smooth on a closed time slab is smooth in space at each time belonging to the slab. The target can be any real normed space. The proof composes with the smooth map sending a spatial point to the fixed-time pair, so no time-interior assumption is needed.

TorusEuler.Paper.Lib.S678a.continuousOn_.text: The cross product of two continuous three-dimensional vector functions is continuous on the same time set. The proof expands its three coordinates into products and differences. Combined with normalized wave directions, this proves continuity of the third coupling used to locate the next activation.

For a physical amplification window on a closed interval, its gradient is continuous there.
