u_+=\widehat k\cdot M\widehat a$, $\eta_+=(\widehat k	imes\widehat a)\cdot M\widehat a$, and $	au_m$ is the reference peak.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_2_8_o.summary: The reference and comparison lemmas imply the crossing conclusions

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_11_.text: Assume Lemmas 5.8 and 5.9, the Fourier cutoff estimates and the Hölder product inequality. For a depth-$P\ge2$ approximation $V,\Pi,R_V$ on $[0,T]$ satisfying those lemmas, take a smooth radial symbol $0\le\psi\le1$, equal to one on $|\xi|\le1$ and zero on $|\xi|>2$. For $\Lambda\ge1$, set $u=S_\Lambda V$ and choose the periodic zero-mean $p$ solving $\Delta p=-\operatorname{tr}((\nabla u)^2)$. This proves Proposition 5.11: $u,R_u$ are odd and divergence free with Fourier radii $2\Lambda,4\Lambda$, and $\|u-V\|_{C_tC^{2,1/2}}\le K_P\varepsilon_\Lambda$. The sum of residual and pressure-Hessian errors is at most $e=C\|R_V\|_{C_tC^{1,1/2}}+K_P\varepsilon_\Lambda$, where $\varepsilon_\Lambda=\Lambda^{2-P}(1+\|V\|_{C_tC^{P,1/2}})^2$. Moreover $D^2(p-p_U)\le(C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-1/4}+e)I$, with $C_{\rm step}=\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b$ from the approximation. Existence and uniqueness of the normalized Poisson pressure identify the constructed pressure.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_11_.summary: Transfer the approximation estimates to a Fourier truncated parent

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_1_o.text: Assuming Bernstein’s inequality and Lemma D.2, the formal implication proves Proposition 5.1. For a smooth periodic truncated parent on $[0,T]$, with both flow deformations and velocity gradient bounded by $\mathsf D$, and $\lambda=|\kappa(t_0,0)|>0$, it bounds $DX,DX^{-1},M,\kappa/\lambda,\lambda^2/|\kappa|^2,P_\kappa$ by $C_m\mathsf D^{C(m+1)}$ at order $m$. Fields satisfying $\|D^mf\|\le C_m^{\prime}A_f\mathsf D^m$ retain polynomial derivative bounds after composition with $X$. Sufficiently small $\ell_*$ absorbs the derivative-dependent powers in the scaled sums. The flow argument uses $\|D_a^nX\|\le C_n\mathsf D^{5n-4}$ for $n\ge1$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_1_o.summary: Bernstein and flow estimates control the six coefficient families

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_2_o.text: Assuming Proposition 5.1, Lemma D.1, (D.2) and (5.14), the formal implication proves $\|B\|_{[n]}\le C_n\mathsf D^C\|\bar f\|_{[n+1]}$ for every smooth periodic mean solution. The mean has $B=DXz_t$, $\operatorname{div}_az_t=0$ and $z(0)=z(T)=0$ on the whole interval $[0,T]$; the parent satisfies the band, deformation, residual and coercivity bounds. The radius is fixed sufficiently small and the exponent is independent of $n$. The proof first bounds $g=DX^T\bar f$ in the order-$(n+1)$ supremum norm, then uses the half-Hölder comparison; the final loss is exactly one source derivative.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_2_o.summary: Hölder comparison costs exactly one source derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_4_o.text: Assuming Theorem 4.2, the formal implication constructs the finite expansion at every depth $P\ge2$ for a smooth periodic solenoidal parent with the band, deformation, residual and coercivity bounds and a nonzero stable central seed with positive coupling. It supplies the localized seed, unique retained profile velocities and normalized pressures, and the identities $\widetilde{\mathbf d}\cdot W=0$ and momentum residual $R_P+R_{\widetilde\chi}$. Oscillations and their sources vanish before activation and outside the envelope; the mean may persist there. The radius is small enough that $2\ell_*<1/2$, allowing smooth continuation across label-cell faces.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_5_4_o.summary: The endpoint theorem supplies the mean solves and uniqueness

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_8_1_o.text: Assume the frequency conclusions of Lemma 1.3 and the product estimate (5.59). For any common construction satisfying Theorem 7.1, the formal statement produces smooth periodic $u,p$ solving incompressible Euler on $[0,T_\infty)$, with mean-zero pressure and odd velocity. The data $U_j(0)$ converge to the smooth odd divergence-free $u(0)$ in every $C^{m,1/2}$, and $U_j\to u$ uniformly in that spatial norm on each $[0,S]$, $S<T_\infty$. Every maximal solution of finite lifespan from $u(0)$ lasts at least to $T_\infty$ and agrees with $u$ before it. General maximal-solution existence is not a conclusion here. The exact numerical normalization of the spatial Hölder norm is imported from a file absent from this packet.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_8_1_o.summary: Construct a smooth limit and compare finite maximal lifespans

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_8_2_o.text: Assume the schedule, moving-frame, amplification and cutoff conclusions of Lemmas 1.3, 2.2, 2.4 and B.1. For a common construction satisfying Theorem 7.1 and its smooth Euler limit from Proposition 8.1, the formal statement proves uniformly bounded velocity and $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$ as $t\uparrow T_\infty$. It also supplies fixed $c>0,C$ with $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\ge c\lambda_{j-1}^{1/8}-C\lambda_{j-1}^{1/32}-C$ for every sufficiently late $[t_j,t_{j+1})$. These are period-one fields on $\mathbb R^3$ representing the torus. The quantitative estimate is an additional conclusion beyond the printed statement of Proposition 8.2 and applies to the limit $u$, rather than only to an approximation $U_j$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_8_2_o.summary: The wave estimates yield both terminal conclusions and a lower bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_8_4_o.text: Assume Lemma 1.3, a common construction satisfying Theorem 7.1, and its smooth periodic Euler limit from Proposition 8.1. For every compact $K\subset\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3$ and every integer $m\ge0$, both $u(t)$ and $\partial_tu(t)$ converge as $t\uparrow T_\infty$, uniformly on $K$ with all spatial derivatives through order $m$. Each limit extends to a $C^m$ field on an open neighbourhood of $K$. Removing the integer lattice represents removal of the torus origin. The time derivative is taken within $[0,T_\infty)$, including the right derivative at zero. Shrinking oscillation supports give the velocity limits; a separated pressure kernel handles the time derivative. The conclusion is not a smooth Euler continuation through the terminal time.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.proposition_8_4_o.summary: Velocity and its time derivative have local spatial derivative limits

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.remark_1_2.text: The formal proof chooses smooth odd divergence-free periodic data and a maximal Euler solution on $[0,T_*)$, where $0<T_*<\infty$. Velocity is bounded, central vorticity tends to infinity, both gradient and vorticity time integrals diverge, and velocity and its time derivative have all spatial limits away from the origin. In addition, the velocity has a smooth periodic extension through $T_*$ away from that point. Every other maximal solution from the chosen data has the same lifespan and velocity. The proof uses an auxiliary existence theorem with selected parameters. It does not establish the auxiliary note’s broader assertion for every admissible threshold, and imposes no Euler equation after $T_*$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.remark_1_2.summary: An existential auxiliary result supplies Remark 1.2

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.remark_1_2_of.text: Assuming hAux_1_1 proves the generalized auxiliary theorem, this wrapper chooses a cutoff symbol, takes the envelope floor to be zero, obtains an admissible threshold and a sufficiently large frequency, and projects a singularity witness with its smooth extension. This route is retained but unused after decision D28. The active spine proves the remark from auxiliaryTerminalSmoothness instead; hAux_1_1 is not discharged here.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.remark_1_2_of.summary: Obtain the remark from the generalized auxiliary theorem

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_1_1_of.text: This is a conditional theorem. Its assumptions are the existence of the common sequence fixed in §8, Proposition 8.1 on its smooth Euler limit, Proposition 8.2 on bounded velocity and central vorticity, Corollary 8.3 on maximal time and divergent integrals, and Proposition 8.4 on off-origin limits. From these it proves existence of smooth odd divergence-free periodic data whose maximal Euler solution satisfies every conclusion of Theorem 1.1. It also proves that any maximal solution from those data has the same lifespan and velocity. The inputs are mathematical assertions, not additional properties proved inside this assembly. The numbered theorem supplies them separately.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_1_1_of.summary: Five earlier assertions imply all of Theorem 1.1

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_4_2_of.text: Assuming Lemma 4.1, Theorem A.1 and Lemma A.2, the formal statement derives Theorem 4.2 for a smooth periodic divergence-free parent on $[0,T]$, $0<T\le1$, with $H^\#\le I$. It solves $Kv-J(\Omega v)+L=c+\nabla\phi$, $z_t=v$, $z(0)=z(T)=0$, uniquely for each continuous half-Hölder source, with weakly divergence-free $z,c$, a polynomial velocity bound, and a uniformly bounded fixed-time inverse. For smooth force sources it also gives a smooth correction solving the linearized Euler equations. Time is rescaled to $[0,1]$. The bound uses coefficient and first derivative suprema; the smooth pressure is reconstructed, rather than identified with the derivative of an arbitrary initial potential. Here $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_4_2_of.summary: Combine coercivity with both Hölder inverse results

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_5_6_of.text: Assuming Propositions 5.1, 5.2, 5.4, Lemmas 5.3, 5.5, D.1 and Bernstein’s inequality, the formal implication proves Theorem 5.6 for each depth-$P$ expansion. Under the smooth parent bounds, central transverse stability and $\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, level-$p$ oscillations decay as $\lambda^{-5/4-2(p-1)/3}$, means as $\lambda^{-5/2-2(p-2)/3}$ and $C_{p+1}$ as $\lambda^{-9/4-2(p-1)/3}$, up to $C_{n,p}\mathsf D^C$. The remainder is bounded by $C_{m,P}\lambda^{-5/4-2P/3}$. All derivative orders apply to the same profiles; the parent exponent is independent of order, level and depth.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_5_6_of.summary: Close the level induction with one fixed parent exponent

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_7_1_of.text: Assuming Lemmas 1.3, 2.2, 2.5–2.7, 5.8–5.10, 6.1 and B.1 and Propositions 2.8, 5.4 and 5.11, the formal theorem derives Theorem 7.1. For each admissible radial cutoff and integer floor $a_0$, it chooses integers $b\ge1$, $a\ge a_0$ and a majorant of the fixed-order constants. Every admissible threshold $\mathcal B$ above that majorant then permits the construction for all sufficiently large initial frequencies $N$. The resulting smooth odd periodic velocities have the residual, flow, pressure, central-wave and increment bounds of (T1)–(T4), with positive common time and $C=18e^3$. It also supplies the actual expansion and truncation of each step. The central covector is still not identified with the localized step's transported covector; the first-wave direction and attained normalization are not part of this exported conclusion.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_7_1_of.summary: Assembles one sequence after fixing the cutoff and parameter majorants

TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_A_1_of.text: Assume Lemma A.2. On $[0,1]\times\mathbb T^3$, suppose $K$ is symmetric, $\Omega$ skew-symmetric, both are time-continuous in $C^{0,1/2}$ with bounded first spatial derivatives, and the positive ellipticity and $H^1_0$ energy bounds (A.1)–(A.2) hold. The formal statement proves that every continuous half-Hölder source has a unique zero endpoint displacement, constant solenoidal field and periodic pressure gradient satisfying $Kv-J(\Omega v)+L=c+\nabla\phi$, $z_t=v$ and $z(0)=z(1)=0$. It includes a polynomial velocity estimate and smoothness for smooth data. The proof first inverts the equation on $L^2$ time paths, then recovers a continuous velocity using the inverse at each fixed time. Here $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proof.theorem_A_1_of.summary: Recover the endpoint solution from the freezing lemma

TorusEuler.Paper.Proposition81Conclusion.text: For a prescribed common construction and $T,u,p$, the formal statement requires the data $U_j(0)$ to converge to smooth odd divergence-free $u(0)$ in every $C^{m,1/2}$. It requires smooth periodic Euler evolution on $[0,T)$ with $T>0$, mean-zero pressure, odd velocity, and convergence $U_j\to u$ uniformly in the same spatial norm on every earlier $[0,S]$, $S<T$. Every maximal solution of finite lifespan with initial velocity $u(0)$ must last at least to $T$ and agree with $u$ on $[0,T)$. This is a list of required properties, not a theorem that such a solution exists. It does not quantify over an infinite maximal lifespan. The file defining the numerical Hölder norm is absent from the packet.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proposition81Conclusion.summary: Record convergence, smooth Euler evolution, and conditional maximal agreement

TorusEuler.Paper.Proposition82Conclusion.text: For prescribed $T,u$ and a frequency and activation schedule, the formal statement records three conditions: a single finite bound for $\|u(t)\|_\infty$ on $0\le t<T$; $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$ as $t\uparrow T$ within that interval; and fixed real $c>0,C$ such that $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\ge c\lambda_{j-1}^{1/8}-C\lambda_{j-1}^{1/32}-C$ on every sufficiently late $[t_j,t_{j+1})$. The last condition is stronger than the printed statement of Proposition 8.2. Positivity of $T$, the Euler equations and identification of $T$ with $T_\infty$ are supplied separately. The velocity norm is an essential supremum over the unit cell. Since only sufficiently large indices occur, subtraction in the index $j-1$ has its usual meaning.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proposition82Conclusion.summary: Require bounded velocity, full blow-up, and uniform interval lower bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.Proposition84Conclusion.text: Given $T$ and a field $u$, the formal statement requires the following for each of $u$ and its time derivative. For every compact $K\subset\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3$ and integer $m\ge0$, there is a $C^m$ field on an open neighbourhood of $K$ whose spatial derivatives through order $m$ are the uniform limits on $K$ as $t\uparrow T$ within $[0,T)$. This is the meaning of the two $C^m(K)$ limits in Proposition 8.4. The local limiting field may depend on $K$ and $m$. The time derivative is taken within the half-open lifespan. The condition itself neither proves existence of $u$ nor supplies a single jointly smooth extension in space and time.
TorusEuler.Paper.Proposition84Conclusion.summary: Require local limits for velocity and its first time derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.ReferenceSlope.text: For a real parameter $\varepsilon$, the formal condition says $Y(0)=1$ and $Y'=\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon\tan\varphi)-\varepsilon\tau\sin2\varphi\,Y-Y^2$ for every $\tau\ge0$, where $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)$. This is (2.12). At zero the derivative is taken from the right. Although $Y$ is a function on all real numbers, its values at negative times are unrestricted. The condition places no sign restriction on $\varepsilon$ and proves no existence, uniqueness or growth bound. Lemma 2.5 obtains those conclusions under $0<\varepsilon\le1$.
TorusEuler.Paper.ReferenceSlope.summary: The condition specifies the scalar initial value problem on the forward half-line

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Cd.text: The correction attached to $V_p$ is stored alongside that oscillation, but the paper denotes it by $C_{p+1}$. This definition recovers the paper's $C_q$ by reading the stored correction at index $q-1$. Indices are nonnegative integers: subtraction at $q=0$ gives zero rather than a negative index. Consequently $C_0$ and $C_1$ refer to the same stored entry, although only the paper's levels $q\ge1$ are used in the expansion. The condition $C_1=0$ must still be imposed or proved; it does not follow from this change of indexing.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Cd.summary: The correction of an oscillation carries the next paper index

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.CutoffSymbol.text:
This is the fixed symbol ψ from Appendix B. It is smooth on ℝ³, depends only on ‖ξ‖, lies between zero and one, equals one on the unit ball, and vanishes when ‖ξ‖>2. Smoothness makes the support inclusion agree with the compact-support formulation in the paper. The zero symbol cannot satisfy the unit-ball condition.

Default-value audit (b4): This predicate contains no numerical derivative, integral, quotient, supremum, ENNReal.toReal conversion or square root. ContDiff is a regularity assertion, not the value of a derivative. The condition ψ=1 on a nonempty ball excludes a trivial zero cutoff. The boundary ‖ξ‖=2 is handled by smoothness/continuity together with vanishing outside the closed ball.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.CutoffSymbol.summary: Smooth radial Fourier cutoff equal to one near zero

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsExpansion.text: On $[0,T]$, take a parent flow, cutoff $\widetilde\chi$, radial envelope, narrow profile and seed, and a depth $P$. An expansion must start with $V_1=\widetilde\chi A_1$, its corresponding phase pressure and $C_1=B_1=0$. It must satisfy $C_{p+1}=C[V_p]$ through level $P$. At levels $2\le p\le P$, the means solve the endpoint problem with forcing $-\langle H_p\rangle_s-\mathbf1_{p=2}R_U\circ X$, and the transverse velocities solve the zero-initial equation with oscillatory and supplementary forcing. Mean pressures have zero spatial mean; phase pressures have zero phase mean. Finally $V_{P+1}=B_{P+1}=0$. All profiles have phase period one and the label translation law needed for periodic physical evaluation. This defines the requirements; it does not prove existence or estimates.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsExpansion.summary: The definition specifies every equation through the retained depth

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsSeed.text: Let $M(t,a)=\nabla U(t,X_{0,t}(a))$ and $\kappa(t,a)=D(X_{t,0})(X_{0,t}(a))^Tk_*$. A seed is a smooth field $\mathbf a$ on $[t_0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$ which agrees with the central seed at $a=0$, starts from $(I-P_{\kappa(t_0,a)})\mathbf a(t_0,0)$, and solves $\partial_t\mathbf a=-M\mathbf a+2\kappa(\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a)/|\kappa|^2$ while satisfying $\kappa\cdot\mathbf a=0$. The differential equation uses derivatives within $[t_0,T]$ at its endpoints. This records the seed equation and (5.4), not the amplitude and coupling estimates on nearby labels. Those are later conclusions. Nonvanishing of $\kappa$ comes from the parent flow and nonzero carrier, not from this declaration alone.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsSeed.summary: Specify smooth transverse evolution from projected initial data

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsTruncation.text: This condition identifies $u$ with $S_\Lambda V$ on $[0,T]$ by requiring the cutoff formula for every continuous function on $\mathbb T^3=\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$ representing $V$. At each time, $p$ must be smooth, periodic, have zero integral over the centered unit cell, and solve $\Delta p=-\operatorname{tr}((\nabla u)^2)$. Existence of a continuous periodic representative of $V$ is not included in this condition: without one, its cutoff clause alone imposes no restriction. Proposition 5.11 supplies such a representative by proving $V$ smooth and periodic. The condition specifies the pressure spatially at each time; joint time smoothness is proved for the constructed truncation.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.IsTruncation.summary: Specify a Fourier cutoff and its normalized periodic Poisson pressure

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Launch.text: The conditions are $0\le t_0<T$, $k_*\ne0$, and $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda$, with $\kappa(t,a)=D(X_{t,0})(X_{0,t}(a))^Tk_*$. They specify the activation time and the frequency convention in §5.1. Thus $\lambda$ is the length of the transported vector at the origin when the wave is activated, not automatically $|k_*|$. These conditions do not themselves assert that $X$ is a differentiable flow or that $\lambda\ge1$; those requirements are supplied by the parent hypotheses. Together with the bounds for the forward and inverse deformation, they give (5.3).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Launch.summary: Measure frequency after transport at the activation point

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.MeanSolution.text: On $[0,T]$, let $X$ be the parent flow, $M=DU\circ X$ and $\mathbf d=(D_aX)^{-T}\nabla_a$. The formal condition on smooth phase-independent $B,\bar q$ is $B_t+MB+\mathbf d\bar q=\bar f$, with smooth periodic fields $z,v$ satisfying $z_t=v$, $\operatorname{div}_a v=0$, $z(0)=z(T)=0$ and $B=D_aXv$. Volume preservation converts this to $\mathbf d\cdot B=0$, as in (5.11). The pressure’s spatial mean is not fixed here. The conditions select $B(0)$ through both displacement endpoints; they do not require zero initial velocity or vanishing before activation.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.MeanSolution.summary: Zero displacement at both ends selects the mean velocity

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Origin.text: On $[t_0,T]$, the central seed $\mathbf a(t,0)$ and $\kappa(t,0)$ are nonzero and perpendicular, solve their coupled linear transport equations, and satisfy both conditions (5.5): every transverse solution grows relative to the seed by at most $\mathsf D$, and $\kappa\cdot M\mathbf a\ge\mathsf D^{-1}|\kappa||\mathbf a|$. The formal normalization is only $\gamma(t)=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$. With $\lambda\ge1$ from the parent, $\gamma$ is positive on the active interval. The paper fixes $\max\gamma=1$; this condition allows any smaller nonzero seed. The vector transport equation and nonvanishing are recorded explicitly, although they follow for a transported nonzero carrier. Frequency normalization is separate.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Origin.summary: Allow a smaller peak while retaining the central growth conditions

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Parent.text:
The domain is represented by periodic fields on $\mathbb R^3$. Require $T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\lambda\ge1$, smooth odd divergence-free $U$ with flow $X$, and Fourier support $|\xi|\le2\mathsf D$. Operator norms of $
abla U$, $D_aX$ and its inverse are at most $\mathsf D$. The pressure $p$ is smooth and periodic; $R_U=U_t+U\cdot
abla U+
abla p$ is odd, supported in $|\xi|\le4\mathsf D$, and has supremum norm at most $\lambda^{-5/2}$. Finally $D^2p-
abla R_U\le I$ as quadratic forms. The time derivative is within $[0,T]$. Unlike §5.1, this condition imposes neither $\int p=0$ nor $\Delta p=-\operatorname{tr}((
abla U)^2)$, and it does not assume $\operatorname{div}R_U=0$. The numbered results separately add $T>0$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Parent.summary: Record the parent bounds without imposing the Poisson normalization

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.TransverseSolution.text: Given the parent flow, its gradient $M$, transported covector $\kappa$ and forcing profile $f$, a transverse solution on $[0,T]$ satisfies $V_t+MV+\kappa\partial_s\pi=f$, $\kappa\cdot V=0$, $\langle V\rangle_s=0$ and $V(0,a,s)=0$. The phase pressure is also normalized by $\langle\pi\rangle_s=0$. These are smooth profiles with phase period one and the simultaneous label-phase translation law giving a periodic physical field. Time derivatives hold the label fixed. This is the problem used for (1.12) after its specified forcing is inserted. The definition describes a solution; it does not assert existence, uniqueness or a bound.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.TransverseSolution.summary: The correction starts from zero and remains perpendicular to the covector

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Yd.text: The paper’s $C_p$ is stored at index $p-1$; the physical expansion sets $C_1=0$. The field $Y_p=V_p+C_p$ groups the new transverse velocity with the divergence correction produced by $V_{p-1}$. This is the convention at the start of §5.5, reflecting the extra frequency gain of the correction. The sum itself imposes no equation; its size and constraints follow from the expansion equations and Theorem 5.6.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Yd.summary: Group the velocity with the preceding divergence correction

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Zd.text: For an indexed family of profiles, the formal definition gives $Z_p=V_p+C_p+B_p$ in the paper's notation. Here $C_p$ is generated by the preceding oscillation $V_{p-1}$: the stored correction index is one smaller than the paper index. The formula defines the level field used in the quadratic interactions of §1.3 and §5.5. It does not impose that $B_p$ is phase independent or that $V_p$ is transverse; these belong to the expansion equations. At index zero, subtraction is truncated to zero, so the intended mathematical use is at levels $p\ge1$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.Zd.summary: Each level combines its oscillation, inherited correction and mean

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.curlCorrection.text: Profiles are smooth on $[0,T]$, with phase period one and $F(t,a+n,s+k_*\cdot n)=F(t,a,s)$. Nonvanishing of the transported covector is supplied by the parent geometry. The correction is $C[V]=\mathbf d\times Q[V]$, with $Q[V]=-\partial_s^{-1}((\kappa\times V)/|\kappa|^2)$. For zero-mean transverse profiles it gives $V+C[V]=\widetilde{\mathbf d}\times Q[V]$, as used in §5.5. The formal operation acts on the oscillatory part of a general profile; the divergence identity requires the zero-mean and transversality assumptions.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.curlCorrection.summary: Take the label curl of the vector potential

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.envelopeSupport.text:
This takes the topological support of the envelope after periodic extension from the centered cell. The raw envelope is g(a)=χ(‖a‖/ℓ), using the fixed smooth cutoff in ActivationProfiles. periodizeCentered selects a representative in the half-open centered label cell, so this support is repeated across all lattice translates. Outside this set the oscillatory profiles and their sources vanish. It is not just one Euclidean ball when viewed on ℝ³.

Default-value audit (b4): radialEnvelope divides by ℓ. At ℓ=0 the quotient is zero everywhere, so the envelope is identically one and its support is all space, not a localized ball. radius with D≥2 gives ℓ>0. A sufficiently large exponent additionally keeps the support away from the cell boundary, making periodic extension smooth. tsupport is a topological closure, not a numerical supremum; no unbounded-sSup fallback is involved. No integral or ENNReal.toReal occurs.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.envelopeSupport.summary: Spatial support repeated over the label lattice

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.expansion.text: For depth $P\ge0$, the formal definition is $W=\sum_{p=1}^P(V_p+C_{p+1}+B_p)$, using the paper's indices. Thus the correction of $V_P$ remains even though the next oscillation is absent. When $C_1=0$ and $P\ge1$, regrouping gives $W=\sum_{p=1}^PZ_p+C_{P+1}$; when $P=0$, the sum is empty and equals zero. The definition accepts arbitrary additive families. To obtain the approximate velocity, one evaluates the profiles at $s=k_*\cdot a$, passes to physical coordinates and adds the parent. Differential equations, divergence cancellation and size estimates are additional facts.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.expansion.summary: Every oscillation is kept together with its own curl correction

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.expansionPressure.text: The depth $P$ is a nonnegative integer; an empty sum is zero, while Proposition 5.4 uses $P\ge2$. The profile pressure is $\mathsf P=\sum_{p=1}^{P}(\mathsf p_p+\bar q_p)$, as in Proposition 5.4. In an admissible expansion the oscillatory pressures have zero phase mean, the mean pressures are phase independent, and $\bar q_1=0$. Those equations and normalizations belong to the construction; this expression simply adds the selected pressure components.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.expansionPressure.summary: Sum the mean and oscillatory pressures through the depth

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.fieldNorm.text: For a field $f(t,a,s)$ and time set $I$, this expression sums the suprema of $\ell_*^{|\alpha|}h^j\partial_a^\alpha\partial_s^j(\tau(t)f)$ over $t\in I$, $a\in\mathbb R^3$ and $s\in\mathbb R$, for $|\alpha|+j\le n$. Each multi-index occurs once. Only label and phase are differentiated, so the time multiplier is applied after differentiation. For $\tau=\gamma^{-1}$ this is the weighted norm of Appendix D. The definition itself supplies neither boundedness nor positivity of $\gamma$; the analytic statements supply these conditions before using it as a norm.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.fieldNorm.summary: Label and phase derivatives carry their natural scales

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.launchNorm.text:
This is the finite norm of f(t₀,a,s) with time restricted to the singleton {t₀}. It supplies the initial-data term in (5.20). The singleton restricts only which slice is sampled; the differentiated variables remain a and s, so this is not a derivative within a singleton time set.

Default-value audit (b4): A time outside [0,T] reads the smooth profile’s stipulated zero extension, giving a zero slice irrespective of the interior data. Launch puts t₀ inside [0,T]; smoothness and the compact periodic quotient then bound all sampled jets. Real sSup must still be read with these guards, and zero ℓ or h suppresses the corresponding derivatives. There is no reciprocal weight, integration, ENNReal.toReal conversion or square root here.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.leading.text: For a seed field $\mathbf a(t,a)$, define $A_1(t,a,s)=g(a)\mathbf a(t,a)F_h(s)$ with $g(a)=\chi(|a|/\ell_*)$. The formalization selects a particular smooth radial cutoff $\chi$ and the periodic phase profile $F_h$ constructed earlier. This is the unswitched leading wave in §5.1; the time cutoff is introduced later as $V_1=\widetilde\chi A_1$. The formula itself assumes no differential equation for the seed and no positive radius or width. Its intended smooth localized interpretation uses $\ell_*>0$, $0<h\le1$, and the seed regularity on $[t_0,T]$ supplied in the application.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.leading.summary: Multiply the seed by the spatial envelope and phase profile

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.leadingPressure.text:
This is −2g(a)(κ·M𝐚)/‖κ‖² times P_h(s), where P_h is the zero-mean periodic primitive of F_h. The minus sign is part of the pressure formula. U and X provide the actual strain and transported covector; amp is the proposed seed. It is the unswitched pressure paired with A₁, not the parent pressure pU and not the sum of all hierarchy pressures.

Default-value audit (b4): The coefficient divides by ‖κ‖², so κ=0 would silently force that coefficient to zero. Parent, positive slab length and Launch exclude this. The envelope and phase primitives inherit the ℓ>0, 0<h≤1 requirements described for leading; with these guards the phase integrals are over smooth real functions and cannot vanish merely because they are undefined. The raw definition accepts bad data and gives no nonzero or regularity certificate itself. There is no real supremum or ENNReal.toReal conversion here.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.levelSource.text: This defines the source for $p\ge2$ using $Y_i=V_i+C_i$ and $Z_i=Y_i+B_i$; subtraction of natural-number indices is truncated at zero outside that range. The source $H_p$ contains $(\partial_t+M)C_p+\mathbf d\mathsf p_{p-1}$ and the two interaction sums of (5.26). At level two it subtracts the activation contribution of the curl correction, recovering (5.25). The correction $C_p$ is already known from $V_{p-1}$, so the source does not depend on the new transverse velocity.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.levelSource.summary: Collect lower-level terms before choosing the new mean

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.meanSource.text: At level $p$, the formal definition is $\overline f_p=-\langle H_p\rangle_s-\mathbf1_{p=2}R$, where $H_p$ is the source assembled before solving for the new mean and $R$ is the supplied parent residual. In the geometric application $R=R_U\circ X$ is independent of phase. The negative sign makes the mean correction cancel the averaged error, and level two is the only place where the previous parent's residual is inserted. This is the right side of the equation described in §1.3. The definition does not solve that equation or impose the endpoint conditions selecting its initial velocity.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.meanSource.summary: Only the first mean equation contains the parent residual

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.ops.text:
This abbreviation packages the actions ∂t+M, the label gradient 𝐝, the phase gradient κ∂s, label advection, phase advection and phase averaging. Its argument d is a ParentGeometry for the actual parent U,X,k; d carries smooth coefficient profiles and identifications with the inverse deformation, strain and covector. It acts on smooth lattice-twisted profiles. An equation using (ops d).material is therefore an equation in the profile space, including the inherited zero extension outside [0,T].

Default-value audit (b4): The operators contain derivatives within the positive-length slab and phase integrals. hT:0<T and smooth profile types ensure genuine derivatives on the slab; finite-dimensional vector/scalar values and smooth phase-periodic slices make the phase means integrable. Outside the slab the representative is intentionally zero and carries no physical claim. No inverse of a possibly singular matrix is selected here: d supplies the actual coefficient identities. No ENNReal.toReal is used in this alias.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.oscSource.text: For an arbitrary preliminary source $H_p$, phase averaging is the integral over one period; centering is an algebraic operation, not an existence statement. The forcing $f_p=-(H_p-\langle H_p\rangle_s)$ is the centered term in (5.27). Its sign cancels the oscillatory part of $H_p$ in the momentum equation. The additional forcing $f_p^S$ is formed only after the mean solve, and the transverse equation uses their sum; centering the preliminary source alone does not include that transport.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.oscSource.summary: Negate the oscillatory part of the preliminary source

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.radius.text: The formal radius is $\ell_*=(\mathsf D^a)^{-1}$, where $a$ is a nonnegative integer. In the parent regime $\mathsf D\ge2$, this is positive; choosing $a\ge3$ gives the paper’s $\ell_*\le\mathsf D^{-3}$. The later estimates first fix a sufficiently large threshold for $a$, then quantify over all larger integer exponents. The radius does not change with derivative order or expansion depth. The definition also accepts $\mathsf D=0$: since the reciprocal of zero is zero, it then gives zero for $a>0$ and one for $a=0$. Those values are excluded by the parent assumptions.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.radius.summary: Use one integer exponent to choose the spatial scale

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.remainder.text: The stored correction is indexed by its generating velocity, so the paper’s $C_{P+1}$ is the stored correction with index $P$. The expression is (5.30): the two final linear terms, label interactions with $i+j\ge P+1$, and phase interactions with $i+j\ge P+2$. Both indices run through $P+1$, where only the final correction remains. The activation error is separate. The expansion equations are needed to identify this expression with the uncanceled momentum residual.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.remainder.summary: Keep precisely the interactions beyond the canceled levels

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.strainField.text:
This is M(t,a)=(D_xU)(t,X(t,a)). Its value is a continuous linear map on Euclidean three-space, so subsequent norms are operator norms. X 0 t is the transition from time zero to t; the direction of these two time arguments matters.

Default-value audit (b4): fderiv ℝ (U t) can equal its default zero on a nonsmooth slice. Parent.velocity_smooth gives genuine spatial derivatives for every t∈[0,T], which is where the estimates use M. No regularity is claimed for values outside that slab. There is no division, integration, supremum, ENNReal.toReal or square root in this definition.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.strainField.summary: Parent velocity gradient along a trajectory

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.suppSource.text: The formal definition gives $f_p^S=-\sum_{i=2}^{p}(B_i\cdot\kappa)\partial_sY_{p+1-i}$, with $Y_j=V_j+C_j$ in paper notation. In particular, at $p=2$ it is $-(B_2\cdot\kappa)\partial_sV_1$ when $C_1=0$, the extra term in (1.12). The sum is empty below level two. At every included index $p+1-i\ge1$, so nonnegative-integer subtraction agrees with ordinary subtraction. For phase-independent $B_i,\kappa$ and differentiable periodic $Y_j$, its phase average vanishes. These properties are not imposed by the formula alone; they come from the geometric profiles and expansion equations.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.suppSource.summary: The newly solved mean transports the leading wave phase

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.totalDivergence.text:
This is 𝐝̃·W=(𝐝+κ∂s)·W, expressed as the sum of the label divergence determined by d.inverse and the phase derivative contracted with d.covector. The output is a smooth scalar profile. A zero output in Proposition 5.4 is the divergence cancellation needed before graph evaluation produces an Eulerian incompressible velocity.

Default-value audit (b4): The underlying derivatives are applied to smooth profile slices and along a slab with hT>0, so they do not use the zero derivative of a nonsmooth field on that domain. The type’s zero extension outside the slab is intentional and carries no assertion about Eulerian regularity there. The definition has no division, integration, supremum, ENNReal.toReal or square root.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.totalDivergence.summary: Divergence with label and phase derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.uNorm.text:
This measures all label and phase derivatives through order n on [0,T], with scales ℓ and h and multiplier one. It is the norm used for the mean corrections, which need not vanish before activation. Smoothness and both periodicity conditions are carried by the profile type. The norm contains no time derivatives.

Default-value audit (b4): For an arbitrary T<0 the time set is empty and the value is zero. At positive T, smooth lattice-twisted profiles have bounded spatial and phase jets on the compact quotient; hierarchyTwistedMixedWord_bddAbove_weighted supplies the requisite BddAbove statements. Thus the unbounded-supremum fallback is excluded in the stated theorems. The definition by itself does not require ℓ,h>0, so zero scales can suppress higher derivatives. Parent with radius/width supplies positive scales. No division, integral, ENNReal.toReal or square root occurs in this specialization.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.wNorm.text: For a smooth profile on $[0,T]$, this is the sum of suprema of $\ell_*^{|\alpha|}h^j\partial_a^\alpha\partial_s^j f/\gamma(t)$ on $[t_0,T]\times\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$, with $|\alpha|+j\le n$ and each multi-index once. No time derivative of $\gamma$ is taken. The profile is one-periodic in phase and satisfies the coupled label-translation law. The definition permits arbitrary $\gamma$ and interprets division by zero as zero; applications require continuous strictly positive $\gamma$, making it the ordinary weighted norm. Values outside $[0,T]$ are fixed to zero without asserting smoothness across the endpoints.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.wNorm.summary: Oscillatory corrections are measured against the central seed

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.waveVector.text: The formal vector is $\kappa(t,a)=D(X_{t,0})(X_{0,t}(a))^Tk_*$, with reference time zero. When $X$ is the smooth parent flow, the inverse derivative identity makes this $(D_aX(t,a))^{-T}k_*$, exactly the transported field in §5.1. The argument $a$ is a parent label, not the physical point. The formula alone does not require $k_*\ne0$ or guarantee invertibility: these enter through the parent and activation hypotheses. Likewise, nonvanishing and the frequency comparisons (5.3) are proved separately. Outside differentiability, the formal derivative expression is assigned its default value zero.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.waveVector.summary: Apply the transpose of the inverse deformation to the carrier

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.weight.text: Given a frequency $\lambda$ and central seed $\mathbf a(t,0)$, define $\gamma(t)=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|$. This is the weight used in the active-interval profile norms: $\|f\|_{[n],\gamma}$ measures spatial and phase derivatives of $f/\gamma$ on $[t_0,T]$. Because $\gamma$ depends only on time, those derivatives do not act on it. The definition itself proves neither positivity nor an upper bound. The parent frequency $\lambda\ge1$, nonzero central seed, and normalization imposed elsewhere give $0<\gamma\le1$. It does not impose the paper’s stronger equality $\max_{[t_0,T]}\gamma=1$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.weight.summary: Measure corrections relative to the amplitude of the central seed

TorusEuler.Paper.S5.width.text: The formal width is the real power $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$. Under the parent condition $\lambda\ge1$, this gives $0<h\le1$, as required for the chosen periodic profile $F_h$. In the finite profile norms, every phase derivative carries a factor $h$; converting to a physical derivative introduces $|k_*|h^{-1}$. With $|k_*|\le\mathsf D\lambda$ this is at most $\mathsf D\lambda^{3/2}$. The width definition does not assert these inequalities without their frequency assumptions. Combined with central amplitude scale $\lambda^{-3/4}$ and $\|F_h\|_\infty=O(h)$, it yields the leading velocity scale $\lambda^{-5/4}$.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5.width.summary: Set the narrow periodic profile scale from the frequency

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.Cd_reflFamily.text: Unfolding the completed-family component gives the divergence correction as the negated reflection of the original correction. This is a definitional identity, not a new estimate.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.CoefBounds.text:
Bounds `NG n`, `Nk n` for the norms (D.1) of the coefficients `(D_aX)⁻¹` and `κ` on every time set in `[0,T]`.

Default-value audit (b5): The predicate includes finite coefficient norms on every allowed time subset and their stated upper bounds. An empty subset is allowed but is not used to infer a nontrivial slab bound; the application supplies the actual slab and positive scales.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.CoefBounds.summary: Uniform bounds for the coframe and wave vector

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.EvenGeometry.text:
The parities of the coefficient profiles of an odd parent: `(D_aX)⁻¹`, `M`, `κ` are even.

Default-value audit (b5): A structure containing three parity equalities. It is not a new geometric construction and does not imply existence of an odd parent; evenGeometry proves it from the parent data.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.EvenGeometry.summary: Even coefficients for the reflected hierarchy

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.NormSetting.text:
The standing data of the norms: `T, ℓ, h > 0`, `0 ≤ t₀ ≤ T`, and the weight `γ` continuous, positive and at most one on `[t₀,T]`.

Default-value audit (b5): The structure explicitly excludes zero or negative scales and time length, requires 0 ≤ t₀ ≤ T, and imposes continuous positive weights at most one on the active interval. These conditions rule out degenerate reciprocal weights in subsequent norm comparisons.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.NormSetting.summary: Positive scales and weights on the time slab

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.NormSetting.active.text: The active interval lies in `[0, T]`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.NormSetting.active.summary: The active interval lies in the full slab

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.NormSetting.finP.summary: Finiteness of the active unweighted profile norms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.NormSetting.finU.summary: Finiteness of the full unweighted profile norms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.NormSetting.invBoun.text: The inverse bound of a norm setting.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.NormSetting.invBoun.summary: The reciprocal weight is bounded on the active interval

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.NormSetting.weight_.text: The weight of a norm setting is positive.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.OddExpansions.text:
This proposition asks for a threshold in a above which the physical perturbation of every permitted expansion is odd. It isolates the symmetry input needed by the quantitative approximation argument. oddExpansions_of establishes it from the parity of the construction and the uniqueness clause of Proposition 5.4.

Default-value audit (b5): A proposition over permitted expansions, not a choice of an expansion. It can be vacuous if there are no admissible expansions; later uses combine it with the existence clause of Proposition 5.4.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.OddExpansions.summary: Oddness of every sufficiently separated expansion

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.P_le_U.text: The plain seminorm is at most the `U` seminorm.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.P_le_U.summary: The full slab norm controls the active unweighted norm

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.P_le_W.text: The plain seminorm is at most the `W` seminorm.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.P_le_W.summary: The weighted norm controls the active unweighted norm

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.PhaseIndep.text:
A field is independent of the phase.

Default-value audit (b5): A universal equality predicate, meaningful for every field. It does not supply differentiability; the derivative consequences add smoothness hypotheses.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.PhaseIndep.eq_comp.text: A phase-independent field is its own composition with `(a, s) ↦ (a, 0)`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.PhaseIndep.eq_comp.summary: A phase independent field ignores the phase coordinate

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.PhaseIndep.fderiv_e.text: The derivative of a phase-independent smooth field only sees the label component of the increment.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.PhaseIndep.fderiv_e.summary: Only label increments affect phase independent fields

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.PhaseIndep.labelPar.text: Label derivatives of a phase-independent smooth field are phase independent.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.PhaseIndep.phasePar.text: The phase derivative of a phase-independent smooth field vanishes.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.PhaseIndep.phasePar.summary: Phase derivatives vanish for phase independent fields

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.S_eq_smul.text: `S = χ̃' V` (the activation term, the same for `χ̃'`).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.S_eq_smul.summary: Activation is the derivative of the switch

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.U_le_W.text: The `U` seminorm is at most the `W` seminorm for profiles vanishing before `t0`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.U_le_W.summary: The weighted norm controls an initially vanishing profile

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.U_mono.text: For derivative orders n ≤ m, the unweighted seminorm of order n is at most that of order m. The statement compares derivative orders of one profile and makes no monotonicity assertion in the hierarchy index.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.U_mono.summary: Unweighted norms increase with derivative order

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.Un.text:
The unweighted norm on `[0,T]` as a seminorm.

Default-value audit (b5): NormSetting supplies a positive time slab and smooth twisted profiles, which make the unweighted seminorm finite. It includes the whole slab; controlling it by an active weighted norm additionally requires vanishing before activation.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.V1_eq_smul.text: `V₁ = χ̃ V`: for a twisted profile `V` equal to `A₁` on `[t₀,T] × cell`, the first velocity `V₁ = χ̃A₁` (on the cell) is `χ̃ V` on the whole slab (lattice twist; before `t₀` both vanish).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.V1_eq_smul.summary: The first velocity is the switched leading wave

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.V1_transverse.text: `V₁ = χ̃A₁` is transverse: `κ·V₁ = 0` on the slab.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.V1_transverse.summary: The leading velocity is transverse to the wave vector

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.VanishBefore.text:
A profile vanishing for `t < t₀`.

Default-value audit (b5): A universal vanishing predicate restricted to [0,T] and t < t₀. At t₀ = 0 it is vacuous; equality at the activation time is obtained from the relevant smoothness or cutoff data when needed.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.VanishBefore.summary: A profile vanishes before the activation time

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.W_mono.text: For derivative orders n ≤ m, the weighted seminorm of order n is at most that of order m. The variables being compared are derivative orders, not hierarchy levels; this corrects the loose use of “level” in the source docstring.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.W_mono.summary: Weighted norms increase with derivative order

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.Wn.text:
The weighted norm as a seminorm.

Default-value audit (b5): NormSetting supplies continuous positive weights and a compact nonempty active interval, so the amplitude seminorm is finite. The weighted norm is meaningful at every permitted derivative order; controlling the whole slab additionally requires preactivation vanishing.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.Wn.summary: Weighted active profile norms as seminorms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.Yd_reflFamily.text: `Yd` commutes with the reflection of a family.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.Yd_reflFamily.summary: Reflection of the completed oscillatory velocity

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.Zd_reflFamily.text: `Zd` commutes with the reflection of a family.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.activation_average.text: The activation term has zero phase mean.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.activation_average.summary: The activation source has zero phase mean

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.activation_eval.text: The activation term on the slab: `S = χ̃' · (twisted extension of A₁)`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.activation_eval.summary: Activation is the differentiated time cutoff

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.activation_holder.text: Assumes an active-interval C^(1,1/2) bound Bγ(t) for the extended leading profile together with its divergence correction. At a fixed time, the activation source and its correction are χ̃′ times this pair, so homogeneity gives the bound B times χ.derivativeSize γ. Before activation both terms vanish. The estimates for B are supplied by the caller from Lemmas 5.3 and 5.5 and Lemma 5.7; this helper does not itself take those numbered hypotheses.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.activation_holder.summary: Bounding the activation error in physical space

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.approx_divergence.text: Let $U$ be the smooth periodic divergence-free parent with flow $X$ and its coefficient data. Suppose a smooth profile $W(t,a,s)$ has zero total profile divergence, $\widetilde{\mathbf d}\cdot W=0$, where $\widetilde{\mathbf d}=(D_aX)^{-T}(\nabla_a+k_*\partial_s)$. Then $V(t,x)=U(t,x)+W(t,X_{t,0}x,k_*\cdot X_{t,0}x)$ satisfies $\operatorname{div}V=0$ for all $t\in[0,T]$. The formal statement receives the full parent hypotheses of §5.1, including its quantitative bounds, although this implication uses the smooth flow and incompressibility. It is the divergence step in Lemma 5.8; zero label divergence alone would not remove the phase contribution.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.approx_divergence.summary: The full profile divergence becomes ordinary spatial divergence

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.approx_residual.text:
For the smooth periodic parent $U,p$ and its flow $X$, let smooth profiles $W,\mathsf P,R,F$ satisfy $(\partial_t+M)W+(W\cdot\widetilde{\mathbf d})W+\widetilde{\mathbf d}\mathsf P+R=F$. Require $R(t,a,s)=R_U(t,X_{0,t}(a))$, where $R_U=U_t+U\cdot
abla U+
abla p$. Then the momentum residual of $V=U+W^
atural$, $\Pi=p+\mathsf P^
atural$ is exactly $F^
atural$ on $[0,T]$, with evaluation through the inverse label and phase $k_*\cdot a$. This is the coordinate implication applied in Lemma 5.8 with $F=R_P+R_{\widetilde\chi}$. The formal statement assumes the profile momentum identity and the complete parent data; it does not derive the finite hierarchy equations.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.approx_residual.summary: Evaluate the profile equation and cancel the parent residual

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.approx_smooth.text:
Let $U,p$ be the smooth periodic parent fields on $[0,T]$, $T>0$, with flow $X$. For smooth velocity and pressure profiles satisfying phase periodicity and $f(t,a+n,s+k_*\cdot n)=f(t,a,s)$, the fields $U+W^
atural$ and $p+\mathsf P^
atural$ are smooth and periodic, where $f^
atural(t,x)=f(t,X_{t,0}x,k_*\cdot X_{t,0}x)$. The formal statement assumes the full quantitative parent conditions, but no hierarchy equation for the chosen profiles. It proves the regularity part of Lemma 5.8. It does not assert oddness, incompressibility or a particular momentum residual; those require symmetry and equations in addition to smoothness.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.approx_smooth.summary: Global profile translation laws give smooth periodic Eulerian fields

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_first.text: `⟨V₁⟩ = 0`: `V₁` agrees on the cell with the bridge profile of `χ̃A₁` (`Bridge.leadingVelocityProfile`), whose phase average vanishes.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_first.summary: The first oscillatory velocity has zero phase mean

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_le.text: (D.5) of Lemma D.1 (the phase average and the centered part).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_le.summary: Phase averaging and centering preserve derivative bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_material_ze.summary: Material evolution preserves a vanishing phase average

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_phaseGrad_z.text: `⟨κ∂_s q⟩ = 0` for every pressure profile (the phase derivative of a periodic function has mean zero, and `κ` does not depend on the phase).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_phaseGrad_z.summary: A periodic phase gradient has zero average

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_reflection.text: The phase average commutes with the reflection.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_sourceBefor.text: Averages the pre-mean source and rewrites the fast phase products by periodic integration by parts, using transversality and the divergence correction identity. The resulting formula contains averaged label products, a label divergence product and the mean–mean label product. This is the mechanism by which the mean source avoids paying a fast phase derivative.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_sourceBefor.summary: Integration by parts rewrites the mean source

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.average_vrefl.summary: Velocity reflection commutes with phase averaging

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.band_jets.text: Bernstein's inequality in operator norm (B.1): a real vector field on the torus with frequencies at most `4Λ` satisfies `‖∇^m g(x)‖ ≤ C_m Λ^m ‖g‖` (the coordinate sums of (B.1) are converted to operator norms by `exists_sortedWord` and `opNorm_le_coordinateSum`).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.band_jets.summary: Bernstein bounds for the parent residual jets

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.bilinear_abstract.text: The splitting argument for a bilinear map, over an abstract module with an involution `r`: if `r(B f g) = -σ(f)σ(g) B f g` whenever `r f = σ(f) f`, `r g = σ(g) g` with `σ = ±1`, then `r(B f g) = -B(r f)(r g)`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.bilinear_abstract.summary: Extending parity identities to all profile pairs

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.bilinear_neg_neg.text: A bilinear map is even under `(f,g) ↦ (-f,-g)`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.bilinear_neg_neg.summary: Two sign changes cancel in bilinear terms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.coefBounds_of_h5_1.text: The coefficient norms `‖(D_aX)⁻¹‖_{[n]} ≤ N_G(n)`, `‖κ‖_{[n]} ≤ N_κ(n)` on every time set in `[0,T]`, from (D.6) and (5.8) of Proposition 5.1 (`h5_1`), when `ℓ_* ≤ 𝖣^{-C}`; `N_G(n) = K_n 𝖣^C`, `N_κ(n) = K_n 𝖣^C λ`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.coefBounds_of_h5_1.summary: Parent geometry controls the advection coefficients

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.coefField.text:
The coefficient field `(t,a,s) ↦ c(t,a)`.

Default-value audit (b5): This is a total algebraic or continuous-linear construction with no division or noncanonical choice. Zero inputs have their literal algebraic values. Any geometric identification or differentiability property is supplied separately by the consuming theorem.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.coefField.summary: A label coefficient extended independently of phase

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.coefField_bounds.text: Norms of a phase-independent coefficient from bounds on its Fréchet jets (`ℓ^m |∇^m c(t,a)| ≤ B` for `m ≤ n`, uniformly bounded jets): the field `(t,a,s) ↦ c(t,a)` has a finite norm (D.1) of order `n`, at most `#W_n B` (the argument of `coef_bounds` without a functional).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.coefField_bounds.summary: Label jet bounds control coefficient profile norms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.coef_bounds.text: Norms of a phase-independent coefficient. For a smooth coframe `G` with uniformly bounded jets and `ℓ^m |∇^m G(t,a)| ≤ B` for `m ≤ n`, and a continuous linear functional `L`, the field `(t,a,s) ↦ L(G(t,a))` has a finite norm (D.1) of order `n`, at most `#W_n ‖L‖ B`.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.graph_from_words.text: (5.44), (5.45) at a fixed time from the word estimate. Let `A = X(t,·)⁻¹` be smooth with `G(A(x)) = D A(x)` for the coframe `G` at time `t`, and suppose the `d̃`-words of `f` satisfy `∑_{|w|=m} ‖d̃_w f‖_{[0],γ} ≤ P_m ‖f‖_{[m],γ}` with finite norms. Then the graph `F = f(t) ∘ (A, k·A)` satisfies `∑_{|w|=m} sup |∂_w F| ≤ γ(t) P_m ‖f‖_{[m],γ}` and `‖F‖_{C^{m,1/2}} ≤ 3(m+1) γ(t) (∑_{j≤m+1} P_j) ‖f‖_{[m+1],γ}` (the chain rule (3.1), `sup |g(t)| ≤ γ(t)‖g‖_{[0],γ}`, and the Hölder bound by one more derivative).

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.graph_norm_le_wNorm.text: Let a smooth profile $g(t,a,s)$ vanish for $t<t_0$ within $[0,T]$, and let $\gamma$ be positive continuous with $\gamma\le1$ on $[t_0,T]$. For any map $Y(t,x)$, $|g(t,Y(t,x),k_*\cdot Y(t,x))|\le\|g\|_{[0],\gamma}$ for all $t\in[0,T]$ and $x\in\mathbb R^3$. The order-zero weighted norm is the supremum of $|g|/\gamma$ over active times, labels and phases. No smoothness or invertibility of $Y$ is needed for this pointwise comparison. Lemma 5.8 uses $Y=X_{t,0}$ and $g=W_{\rm osc}$; the additional scale $\lambda^{-5/4}$ comes from the separate hierarchy estimate.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.lemma_5_8_of_odd.text:
Assume the localized seed, finite expansion, transverse inverse, hierarchy and physical evaluation results, together with oddness of all admissible expansions. For a depth-$P\ge2$ expansion over the smooth odd divergence-free periodic parent of §5.1, with stable positive central coupling, $0<\gamma\le1$ and $C_{m step}\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, the formal statement derives the full assertions of Lemma 5.8. These are smooth periodic $V=U+W^
atural$ and $\Pi=p+\mathsf P^
atural$, odd divergence-free $V$, the exact residual $R_P^
atural+R_{\widetilde\chi}^
atural$, and the velocity and residual estimates (5.47)–(5.48). The residual bound retains $\sup_{[t_0,T]}|\widetilde\chi\,{}^{\prime}|\gamma$ alongside $\lambda^{-2P/3}$. This is a conditional assembly theorem; the separate symmetry result supplies the assumed oddness from uniqueness of the expansion.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.lemma_5_8_of_odd.summary: Prove the physical bounds after reflection symmetry has been supplied

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.levelConstant_indep.text: Fix $P'\le P$ and the same numerical recurrence coefficient $K$ in both depths. The equality holds for every $q\le P'$. The numerical constant for a level is unchanged when the surrounding expansion is extended to a larger depth. The interaction pairs at the earlier levels are identical, so induction gives equality of their constants. This justifies the dependence $C_{n,p}$ in Theorem 5.6; it does not assert a bound uniform in $p$.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.master_recurrence.text: Assume a depth-$P$ expansion with smooth profiles, the parent band and deformation bounds, the residual and coercivity bounds, and a stable central seed with positive coupling and $0<\gamma\le1$. The parent, mean, transverse, and correction estimates give a recurrence for the actual profile norms and a direct estimate for the remainder. Phase integration replaces the fast derivative in the mean source by a label divergence. One parent exponent suffices independently of derivative order and depth, while the order and finite-depth constants retain their allowed dependence.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.oddExpansions_of.text: Assume Proposition 5.4, including uniqueness of the retained profiles. Over the smooth odd periodic parent of §5.1, take a seed with even dependence on the label and an admissible depth-$P\ge2$ expansion. Reflect $(a,s)$ to $(-a,-s)$, reverse the sign of velocity profiles and preserve the sign of pressure profiles. The reflected family satisfies the same defining equations and prescribed data. Uniqueness therefore makes the retained velocity expansion odd under this reflection. After composition with the odd inverse parent flow, its Eulerian perturbation is odd. This statement proves symmetry of the expansion; it does not derive its quantitative estimates or bound its residual.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.oddExpansions_of.summary: Reflect the finite expansion and use uniqueness of its retained levels

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tilde_step.text: One letter of `d̃`, by Lemma D.1. For a coframe `G` and a carrier `k`, whose coefficients `G_{ji}` and `k·G e_i` (fields independent of the phase) have finite norms (D.1) bounded by `Nc` and `Nk`, and a field `f` with `‖f‖_{[n+1],γ}` finite: `d̃_i f` has a finite weighted norm and `∑_i ‖d̃_i f‖_{[n],γ} ≤ c_n (3 Nc (3ℓ⁻¹ ‖f‖_{[n+1],γ}) + 3 Nk ‖∂_s f‖_{[n],γ})`. Uses `hD_1` (Lemma D.1): (D.4) for each of the four products of `d̃_i f` (`tildeWord_cons_eq`) and (D.3) for `∑_j ‖∂_{a_j} f‖_{[n],γ} ≤ 3ℓ⁻¹‖f‖_{[n+1],γ}`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tilde_step.summary: Bounding one physical derivative of a profile

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tilde_step_general.text: The one-step estimate for a general field : `∑_i ‖d̃_i f‖_{[n],γ} ≤ c_n (9 Nc ℓ⁻¹ + 3 Nk h⁻¹) ‖f‖_{[n+1],γ}`. Uses `hD_1` through `tilde_step` and the phase bound `‖∂_s f‖_{[n],γ} ≤ h⁻¹‖f‖_{[n+1],γ}` of (D.3).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tilde_step_general.summary: The full phase cost of one physical derivative

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tilde_step_phaseInd.text: The one-step estimate for a phase-independent field: `d̃_i f` is again phase independent, and `∑_i ‖d̃_i f‖_{[n],γ} ≤ 9 c_n Nc ℓ⁻¹ ‖f‖_{[n+1],γ}`, since `∂_s f = 0`. Uses `hD_1` through `tilde_step`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.tilde_step_phaseInd.summary: Phase independent fields avoid the fast derivative cost

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.transverseSolution_.text: (5.15) is preserved: if `(V, 𝗉)` solves the transverse equation from zero with source `f`, then `(ϱV, 𝗉 ∘ reflection)` solves it with source `ϱf`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.transverseSolution_.summary: Reflection preserves the transverse evolution equation

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.transverse_average_.text: A solution of the transverse equation (5.15) has a source of zero phase mean: `f = (∂_t+M)V + κ∂_s𝗉` with `⟨V⟩ = 0`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.transverse_average_.summary: The transverse equation forces zero source average

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.truncate.text:
The levels of `u` restricted to `1..P` (`C_i` for `i ≤ P`), zero elsewhere.

Default-value audit (b5): The natural-index condition sets V and B to zero outside 1 ≤ p ≤ P, and C to zero outside p ≤ P. It leaves both pressure families untouched. No estimate for these exterior pressures follows from the definition; later tail arguments use only the truncated velocity components.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.truncate.summary: Extending the finite velocity hierarchy by zero

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.twisted_jets.text: Jets of a twisted profile versus jets of a raw field at one time: every jet of one is a jet of the other or zero.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.twisted_jets.summary: Twisted extension preserves local derivative bounds

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.twisted_wNorm_le.text: Norm of a twisted profile versus the raw field: on `[t₀,T]`, `‖V₀‖_{[n],γ} ≤ ‖F‖_{[n],γ}` (the latter the norm (D.1) of the raw field on `[t₀,T] × ℝ³ × ℝ`).
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.twisted_wNorm_le.summary: Twisted extension preserves weighted leading norms

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.uNorm_average.summary: Phase averaging does not increase the unweighted norm

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.uNorm_divProduct.summary: An unweighted bound for the divergence product

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.uNorm_labelAdv.text: (5.39) for the label advection without weight, on `[0,T]`.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.uNorm_le_plain.text: For a field vanishing before `t₀`, the unweighted norm on `[0,T]` is the one on `[t₀,T]`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.uNorm_le_plain.summary: Vanishing before activation reduces the full slab norm

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.uNorm_le_wNorm.text: The profile is smooth and phase periodic, with the coupled label-translation law; the weight is continuous on the compact active interval. For a profile vanishing before $t_0$, its unweighted norm on $[0,T]$ is at most its weighted norm on $[t_0,T]$ when $0<\gamma\le1$. The vanishing assumption matters because the time intervals differ. The remainder proof applies this to terms containing oscillations; products of two means are estimated directly in the unweighted norm.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.uNorm_le_wNorm.summary: Preactivation vanishing extends control to the whole interval

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.uNorm_phaseAdv.text: (5.39), second line, in the unweighted norm on `[0,T]`: `‖(f·κ)∂_s g‖_{[n]} ≤ c_n (c_n N_κ ‖f‖_{[n]}) (h⁻¹ ‖g‖_{[n+1]})`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.uNorm_phaseAdv.summary: Unweighted control of the phase advection term

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.vrefl.text:
The symmetry of the construction on velocity profiles: `ϱf(t,a,s) = -f(t,-a,-s)`.

Default-value audit (b5): Reflection and negation are algebraic operations on already smooth twisted profiles. No reciprocal, partial inverse or arbitrary choice is introduced; pressures use ordinary reflection in reflFamily.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.vrefl.summary: Reflection of velocity profiles with a minus sign

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.vrefl_apply.text: Unfolding of the vector reflection `vrefl` (negated reflection).

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.vrefl_eval.summary: Evaluating velocity reflection at a label and phase

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.vrefl_vrefl.summary: Reflecting the velocity twice changes nothing

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wNorm_labelAdv_left.text: (5.39) for the label advection with the weight on the advecting field.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wNorm_labelAdv_left.summary: Weighted label advection of the first factor

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wNorm_labelAdv_righ.text: `‖(f·𝐝)g‖_{[n],γ} ≤ c_n (c_n N_G ‖f‖_{[n]}) (3ℓ⁻¹ ‖g‖_{[n+1],γ})`, (5.39) with the weight on the advected field.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wNorm_labelAdv_righ.summary: Weighted label advection of the second factor

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wNorm_phaseAdv_left.text: (5.39), second line, with the weight on the advecting field.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wNorm_phaseAdv_left.summary: Weighted phase advection of the first factor

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wNorm_phaseAdv_righ.summary: Weighted phase advection of the second factor

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wNorm_smul_time_le.text: A time multiplier of modulus at most one does not increase the weighted norm: if `F = c G` on `[t₀,T]` and `|c| ≤ 1` there, then `‖F‖_{[n],γ} ≤ ‖G‖_{[n],γ}`.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wNorm_smul_time_le.summary: A bounded time factor preserves the weighted estimate

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.waveC.text:
The wave vector `κ(t,a)` on a time set.

Default-value audit (b5): The wave vector is defined from the supplied flow derivative for every input. The parent-flow hypotheses are what identify it with the transported nonzero covector; the definition alone does not establish those geometric facts.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.waveC.summary: The transported wave vector as a coefficient field

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wavePotential_smul_.text: For any fixed wave vector K, scalar c and phase profile V, the wave potential of cV equals c times the wave potential of V. Linearity of the cross product and phase primitive proves the identity, even at K = 0 under the total reciprocal convention. The consuming completion estimate works at each fixed time.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wavePotential_smul_.summary: Time multiplication commutes with the wave potential

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wavePotential_zero.text: The wave potential of the zero profile vanishes.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.weighted_add.text: The time weight distributes over sums of fields.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.weighted_sum.text: The time weight distributes over finite sums of fields.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.weighted_zero.text: The time weight of the zero field is zero.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wordConst.text:
The one-step constant `κ₀_n = 12 c_n #W_n max(K_n, 0)` of the proof of Lemma 5.7, for the constants `K_n` of (5.8) in Proposition 5.1.

Default-value audit (b5): Finite sums, products and max are total. The max clips any supplied negative coefficient constant to zero; analytic use still requires that it bounds the coefficient jets. The order-zero word set is nonempty.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wordConst_nonneg.text: The word constant of Lemma 5.7 is nonnegative.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wordNorm_le_of_valu.text: A word norm is at most another one when every value of the first is dominated by a value of the second.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.wordNorm_le_of_valu.summary: Dominating every derivative value bounds the word norm

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.word_add.text: Derivative words are additive on smooth functions.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.word_comp_add.text: Words in constant directions commute with translations.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.word_comp_add.summary: Translations commute with constant directional derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.word_eventuallyEq.text: Words of functions that agree near a point agree near that point.

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.word_smul_const.text: A derivative word of a constant multiple.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.word_smul_const.summary: Constants pass through ordered derivative words

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.word_zero.text: Derivative words vanish on the zero function.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.word_zero.summary: Derivative words annihilate the zero field

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.words_general.text: Let $\ell_*,h>0$ and let the time weight $\gamma$ be positive. Suppose all finite norms of $f/\gamma$ exist, and the coefficients of label and phase differentiation have finite order-$j$ bounds $N_c(j)$ and $N_k(j)$. Assuming the finite-norm product estimate, the sum over all ordered sequences of $m$ physical coordinate derivatives is bounded by $\prod_{j=0}^{m-1}[C_j(9N_c(j)\ell_*^{-1}+3N_k(j)h^{-1})]\,\|f\|_{[m],\gamma}$. The formal conclusion also includes finiteness of these differentiated norms. With inverse-flow coefficients and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, this gives the derivative cost in Lemma 5.7. The product for $m=0$ is one; its order constants are those of the product estimate, not new assumptions on the parent.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.words_general.summary: Iterate the weighted chain rule with separate coefficient costs

TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.words_phaseIndep.text: Let $f$ be independent of phase, $\ell_*,h>0$, and $\gamma>0$. Assume finite weighted profile norms at every order and finite order-$j$ coefficient bounds $N_c(j),N_k(j)$ for the label and phase parts of the derivative operator. Given the finite-norm product estimate, the sum of the weighted norms after all ordered sequences of $m$ physical coordinate derivatives is at most $\prod_{j=0}^{m-1}[C_j9N_c(j)\ell_*^{-1}]\,\|f\|_{[m],\gamma}$. The phase-coefficient bounds remain formal premises, but no $N_k(j)h^{-1}$ factor appears in the conclusion because phase derivatives vanish. This is the improved mean estimate used in Lemma 5.7. The conclusion includes finiteness of all differentiated order-zero norms.
TorusEuler.Paper.S5b.words_phaseIndep.summary: Only inverse label coefficients remain for phase independent profiles

TorusEuler.Paper.Schedule.L.text: For a real-valued frequency sequence $\lambda_j$, the formal definition is $L_j=4\log\lambda_{j+1}$. This is the gain parameter in (1.14); in particular $L_{j+1}$ uses $\lambda_{j+2}$, which matters in Lemma 1.3. The formula is defined even without a positive-frequency hypothesis. The logarithm is assigned the value zero at zero and is extended to negative arguments using their absolute value. In the paper’s schedule all frequencies exceed one, so this convention is inactive and $L_j>0$. The formula alone provides neither that positivity nor any bound on the gain.
TorusEuler.Paper.Schedule.L.summary: The gain uses the next frequency in the sequence

TorusEuler.Paper.Schedule.ε.text: For the frequency sequence $\lambda_j$, put $L_j=4\log\lambda_{j+1}$. The formal definition assigns $\varepsilon_j=1/L_{j+1}^2$, agreeing with $\varepsilon_{j-1}=L_j^{-2}$ for $j\ge2$ in (1.14). Consequently $\varepsilon_j$ depends on $\lambda_{j+2}$, not $\lambda_{j+1}$. The formal formula also assigns a value at index zero, which this part of the paper does not use. Division by zero is assigned the value zero, so a zero gain would give a zero ratio, not an infinite one. The positive-frequency schedule supplies positive gains; separate estimates make these positive ratios small enough for amplification.
TorusEuler.Paper.Schedule.ε.summary: The ratio is the inverse square of the following gain

TorusEuler.Paper.Schedule.τ.text: For a positive frequency sequence $\lambda_j$, put $L_j=4\log\lambda_{j+1}$. At each wave index $j\ge1$, the formal definition is $\tau_j=\lambda_{j-1}^{-1/8}L_{j+1}^3$, the half-length used in $S_j=t_j+2\tau_j$. The formula uses a real exponent $-1/8$ and an integer cube. It is also assigned a value at index zero: subtraction of one from a nonnegative integer gives zero there, so it uses $\lambda_0$. The paper does not use that extra value. Positivity, decay of $\tau_j$, and the endpoint relation require separate assertions; this formula alone supplies none of them.
TorusEuler.Paper.Schedule.τ.summary: Defines the time available before each endpoint condition

TorusEuler.Paper.SmoothTerminalExtension.text: The formal condition asks for an open set containing $\{T\}\times(\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3)$ and a field $g$ smooth jointly on its union with $[0,T)\times(\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3)$. The field is periodic under every integer spatial translation and equals $u$ on that entire preterminal punctured slab. Thus it descends to a smooth extension through the terminal slice of the punctured torus. The field is defined everywhere, but smoothness is required only on the stated union; its other values are unconstrained. This condition neither asserts an Euler equation after $T$ nor extends a pressure. It specifies what an extension means and does not prove one exists.
TorusEuler.Paper.SmoothTerminalExtension.summary: One periodic field agrees with the preterminal velocity

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_5_13.text: Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$ and $\lambda\ge1$. Assume a smooth odd solenoidal unit-periodic parent $U$ and flow $X$, Fourier bands $2\mathsf D$ for $U$ and $4\mathsf D$ for the odd residual $R_U=U_t+U\cdot\nabla U+\nabla p_U$, bounds $\|DU\|,\|DX\|,\|DX^{-1}\|\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. The pressure may be any smooth periodic choice satisfying these conditions. Write $M=DU\circ X$, $K=DX^TDX$ and $\Omega=DX^T(M^T-M)DX$. For every prescribed exponent $C_A$ and $0<A\le\mathsf D^{C_A}$, a sufficiently large radius exponent gives $\ell_*^m(|K|_{m,1/2}+|\Omega|_{m,1/2})\le C_m\mathsf D^C\sqrt{\ell_*}\le C_m/A$ for $m\ge1$, with finite coefficient norms. The radius threshold may depend on $C_A$ but not the parent or derivative order. The displayed polynomial bound on $A$ is assumed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_5_13.summary: The radius suppresses positive-order Hölder coefficient norms

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_5_14.text: Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$ and $\lambda\ge1$. Assume a smooth odd solenoidal unit-periodic parent $U$ and flow $X$, Fourier bands $2\mathsf D$ for $U$ and $4\mathsf D$ for the odd residual $R_U=U_t+U\cdot\nabla U+\nabla p_U$, bounds $\|DU\|,\|DX\|,\|DX^{-1}\|\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. The pressure may be any smooth periodic choice satisfying these conditions. Let $B=DXv$, $v=z_t$, solve the mean equation with $z(0)=z(T)=0$ and $\operatorname{div}_a v=0$; set $g=DX^T\bar f$. For sufficiently small fixed $\ell_*$, finite scaled half-Hölder norm of $g$ at order $n$ implies finiteness for $v$ and $\|v\|_{[n],1/2}\le C_n\mathsf D^C\|g\|_{[n],1/2}$. Time runs over $[0,T]$. No derivative is lost here; the later supremum-norm estimate uses one more source derivative.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_5_14.summary: The endpoint inverse preserves the derivative order

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_5_59.text: For each integer $m\ge0$, the assertion asks for a nonnegative constant $C_m$ such that every continuous bilinear map $B:E\times F\to G$ between real normed spaces satisfies $\|B(f,g)\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le C_m\|B\|\|f\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\|g\|_{C^{m,1/2}}$ whenever $f:\mathbb R^3\to E$ and $g:\mathbb R^3\to F$ belong to $C^{m,1/2}$. The output’s Hölder regularity is also asserted. The constant is chosen before the spaces, fields and bilinear map. This states a generalization of (5.59); scalar multiplication and the tensor products used in §5.7 are particular cases. It does not require periodicity.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_5_59.summary: State the product estimate uniformly in the target spaces

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_D_2.text: Let $0<\ell_*\le1$ and let $c:I\times\mathbb R^3\to X$ be smooth in the label variable, where $X$ is any real normed space. Assume all derivatives through order $n+1$ are uniformly bounded in time and label. The formal statement proves $\|c\|_{[n]}\le\|c\|_{[n],1/2}\le4\ell_*^{-1/2}\|c\|_{[n+1]}$ and establishes finiteness of the Hölder quantities. At each order $m$ it also proves $\ell_*^m|c|_{m,1/2}\le4\ell_*^{-1/2}(\ell_*^m|c|_m+\ell_*^{m+1}|c|_{m+1})$. Each multi-index is counted once. The Hölder norm uses the maximum of supremum and seminorm; their sum is equivalent within a factor two. Thus the explicit constant four yields the paper's unspecified constant after the chosen norm convention is accounted for.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.eq_D_2.summary: Costs one derivative and half a power of the radius

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.section8.text: The formal statement asks for parameters, an inductive construction, a constant and a real time $T$ satisfying the conclusions of Theorem 7.1. These include smooth odd divergence-free periodic stage velocities, the residual and central-wave bounds, summable corrections, shrinking oscillation supports, and $0<T<S_j$ for every stage, with $t_j\to T$. Thus $T$ is the paper’s common accumulation time. This declaration specifies an existence assertion; the adjoining proof establishes it from Theorem 7.1. Its conclusion contains no limiting field and no uniform convergence on $[0,T]$. It represents only the initial choice in Section 8, not the whole opening paragraph.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.Text.section8.summary: Specify a common construction without yet asserting its limit

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.corollary_8_3.text: Given a common construction satisfying Theorem 7.1 and its smooth Euler limit $u,p$ from Proposition 8.1, assume bounded velocity, central vorticity blow-up, and fixed $c>0,C$ with $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\ge c\lambda_{j-1}^{1/8}-C\lambda_{j-1}^{1/32}-C$ throughout every sufficiently late $[t_j,t_{j+1})$. The formal statement concludes maximality at $T_\infty>0$, equality with the lifespan of every other maximal solution of finite lifespan from $u(0)$, and divergence of both integrals in (1.2). The quantitative bound is included in the formal Proposition 8.2, although not in its printed statement. This declaration specifies the implication; its proof uses crossing durations instead of a general continuation criterion. The integrals are nonnegative Lebesgue integrals over the half-open lifespan.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.corollary_8_3.summary: Assume the construction and quantitative terminal conclusions to obtain maximality

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_1_3.text: Let $b\ge1$ be an integer, $K(s)=320b(s+1)$, and $\mathcal B(s)>0$ satisfy $\log\mathcal B(s)\ge4K(s+1)^3$ for $s\ge1$. Suppose $\lambda_0\ge\mathcal B(1)$, $q_1=1$, $\lambda_j=\lambda_{j-1}^{K(q_j)}$, and $q_{j+1}=\max\{1\le s\le q_j+1:\mathcal B(s)\le\lambda_{j-1}\}$. Then $q_j\le q_{j+1}\le q_j+1$, $q_j\to\infty$, and $4\log\lambda_{j+2}\le(\log\lambda_{j-1})^2$ for $j\ge1$. Thus the last expression is exactly (1.15), since $L_{j+1}=4\log\lambda_{j+2}$.
