The formal statement omits threshold monotonicity and analytic-cost domination from §1.5; the arithmetic result therefore applies under fewer assumptions.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_1_3.summary: The schedule has slowly increasing unbounded derivative orders

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_1.text: Let $J$ be a time interval on which relative derivatives are uniquely determined. Suppose $D$ is differentiable, $\operatorname{tr}D=0$, $D'+D^2$ is symmetric, and $k'=-D^Tk$, $\mathbf a'=-D\mathbf a+p_{\rm w}k$, where $p_{\rm w}=2k\cdot D\mathbf a/|k|^2$. For differentiable $F$ and any $P$ with $P'=F$, transverse data give an Euler velocity $u=Dx+\mathbf aF(k\cdot x)$ on $\mathbb R^3$, with pressure $-x\cdot(D'+D^2)x/2-p_{\rm w}P(k\cdot x)$ and zero divergence. Nonzero perpendicular data at any $t_0\in J$ remain so throughout $J$, including earlier times. Unlike the paper, the formal statement requires neither a smooth odd periodic profile nor its normalization; the Euler identity also allows $k=0$, using zero for division by zero. The interval derivative includes one-sided endpoint derivatives.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_1.summary: The Euler identity needs weaker profile hypotheses than the paper assumes

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_2.text: Let nonzero perpendicular paths $k,\mathbf a\in\mathbb R^3$ satisfy $k'=-B^Tk$ and $\mathbf a'=-B\mathbf a+2(k\cdot B\mathbf a)k/|k|^2$ on a time set $J$, with $\operatorname{tr}B=0$. Put $E_1=k/|k|$, $E_2=\mathbf a/|\mathbf a|$, $E_3=E_1\times E_2$, $B_{ij}=E_i\cdot BE_j$ and $\sigma=|k||\mathbf a|$. The formal statement gives orthonormality and $E_1'=-B_{12}E_2-B_{13}E_3$, $E_2'=B_{12}E_1-B_{32}E_3$, $E_3'=B_{13}E_1+B_{32}E_2$, $(\log\sigma)'=B_{33}$. Derivatives are relative to $J$. These are (2.2), with no regularity assumption on $B$ beyond the supplied wave derivatives and no symmetry assumption on $B'+B^2$. All normalizations and the logarithm have nonzero positive denominators or arguments under the stated hypotheses.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_2.summary: Wave derivatives and zero trace suffice for the frame equations

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_3.text:
Let nonzero transverse preceding wave data solve the wave equations over continuous trace-free $B$, with positive activation strength $\sigma$ and couplings $
u,\eta$. Set $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$, $S=\sigma/r$, $\varepsilon=\eta/
u$, $	au=r(t-t_0)$. On $[0,T]$, $T\ge2$, require only $B_{12}=
u,B_{32}=\eta$ nonzero and $E_c=0$. Launch $k=\lambda E_3$, $\lambda>0$; write $k=\lambda(\zeta_1E_1+\zeta_2E_2/S+\zeta_3E_3)$ and $\mathbf a=\alpha_1E_1/S+\alpha_2E_2+\alpha_3E_3/S$. The formal statement gives $\sigma_p=\sigma$, $\zeta'=(-(1+1/(2S^2))\zeta_2,-\varepsilon\zeta_3,\varepsilon\zeta_2/(2S^2))$. Where $\zeta_3
e0$, it gives $\alpha_1'=-\alpha_2+\zeta_1\Pi$, $\alpha_2'=-(1-1/(2S^2))\alpha_1+\varepsilon(\zeta_1\alpha_1+\zeta_2\alpha_2)/(2S^2\zeta_3)+\zeta_2\Pi/S^2$, with $\Pi=(2\zeta_2\alpha_1+(\zeta_1+\varepsilon\zeta_3)\alpha_2)/(\zeta_1^2+\zeta_2^2/S^2+\zeta_3^2)$. As $S	o\infty$, $\zeta	o(\varepsilon	au^2/2,-\varepsilon	au,1)$ uniformly, and the amplitude matrix tends uniformly to $- igl( egin{smallmatrix}\varepsilon	au\sin2\varphi&\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon	an\varphi)\1&0\end{smallmatrix} igr)$, $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon	au^2/2)$. One threshold works for all model configurations and ensures $\zeta_3
e0$. The physical interval may lie inside a larger compact observation set. Compared with the paper, continuity of $B$ suffices. All derivatives are relative to the displayed interval. This states both finite-shear equations and their limit.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_3.summary: The exact model equations converge uniformly to the reference system

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_4.text:
Let a nonzero transverse preceding wave evolve over continuous trace-free $B$ with positive activation $\sigma,
u,\eta$ and continuous error $E_c$. Set $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$, $S=\sigma/r$, $\varepsilon=\eta/
u$, $	au=r(t-t_0)$, $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon	au^2/2)$ and $\delta=\|B_{12}/
u-1\|_\infty+\|B_{32}/\eta-1\|_\infty+\|B\|_\infty/r+\|E_c\|_\infty/
u$, on a compact set containing the physical interval. Assume $T\ge2$, sufficiently large integer $C_0$, $C_0\varepsilon\le1$, $C_0T^{C_0}\delta\le\varepsilon$, and $k'=-M^Tk$ launched at $\lambda E_3$, $\lambda>0$, $M=B+\mathbf a_p\otimes k_p+E_c$. The formal statement bounds both $\sup|\zeta-(	an\varphi,-\varepsilon	au,1)|$ and $\sup||k|^2\cos^2\varphi/\lambda^2-1|$ by $CT^p\delta\le1/2$, where $\zeta=(k\cdot E_1,Sk\cdot E_2,k\cdot E_3)/\lambda$. It gives $1/2\le\zeta_3\le3/2$, $|\zeta|\le3T^2$, and $|\sigma_p/\sigma-1|\le2T\delta$. Every transverse amplitude has $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)=(S\mathbf a\cdot E_1,\mathbf a\cdot E_2)$ satisfying $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)'=[- igl( egin{smallmatrix}\varepsilon	au\sin2\varphi&\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon	an\varphi)\1&0\end{smallmatrix} igr)+\mathcal E](\alpha_1,\alpha_2)$, with one continuous $\mathcal E$ and $\sup\|\mathcal E\|\le CT^p\delta$. Supremum conclusions concern $[0,T]$. The integer exponent $p$ and factor $C$ precede $C_0$ and all data. Vector norms are Euclidean; error-operator norms use the maximum norm on pairs. Continuity and the strength bound extend the printed lemma.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_4.summary: A common small error controls the wave vector and every transverse amplitude

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_5.text: For $0<\varepsilon\le1$, let $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)$ and consider $Y'=\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon\tan\varphi)-\varepsilon\tau\sin(2\varphi)Y-Y^2$, $Y(0)=1$, on $[0,\infty)$. There is a unique solution on that half-line, with $|Y|\le1$ and $Y=(1+e)\cos\varphi-\varepsilon\tau\sin(2\varphi)/4$ for one function $0\le e\le\varepsilon/8$. Its amplitude $a_{\rm ref}=\exp\int_0^\tau Y$ equals $\sqrt{\cos\varphi}\exp\int_0^\tau(1+e)\cos\varphi$. It has its global maximum at the unique zero $\tau_m$ of $Y$, with $2\le\varepsilon\tau_m\le3$, positive $Y$ before and negative $Y$ after, and $\log a_{\rm ref}(\tau_m)\ge\varepsilon^{-1/2}-1$. This declaration specifies the complete assertion of Lemma 2.5; a separate theorem proves it. The functions are defined on all real times, but the equation, bounds and uniqueness concern only $\tau\ge0$, with a right derivative at zero.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_5.summary: The assertion includes uniqueness on the nonnegative time axis

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_6.text:
Let $B,E_c$ be continuous on compact $I\supset[t_0,t_0+T/r]$, with $\operatorname{tr}B=0$ and nonzero perpendicular preceding wave data satisfying $k_p\prime=-B^Tk_p$, $\mathbf a_p\prime=-B\mathbf a_p+2(k_p\cdot B\mathbf a_p)k_p/|k_p|^2$. Set $E_1=\widehat{k_p}$, $E_2=\widehat{\mathbf a_p}$ and $E_3=E_1	imes E_2$; $B_{ij}=E_i\cdot BE_j$. Physical derivatives are relative to $I$; for interval $I$, endpoint derivatives are one-sided. Put $\sigma=|k_p(t_0)||\mathbf a_p(t_0)|$, $
u=B_{12}(t_0)>0$, $\eta=B_{32}(t_0)>0$, $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$, $S=\sigma/r$, $\varepsilon=\eta/
u$, and $\delta=\sup_I|B_{12}/
u-1|+\sup_I|B_{32}/\eta-1|+\sup_I\|B\|/r+\sup_I\|E_c\|/
u$. Assume $T\ge2$ and $C_0\varepsilon\le1$, $C_0T^{C_0}\delta\le\varepsilon$ for sufficiently large integer $C_0$. In physical time, the new wave solves $k'=-M^Tk$, $\mathbf a'=-M\mathbf a+2(k\cdot M\mathbf a)k/|k|^2$, $k\cdot\mathbf a=0$, with $M=B+\mathbf a_p\otimes k_p+E_c$, $k(t_0)=\lambda E_3(t_0)$, $\lambda>0$, and $\mathbf a(t_0)=-E_1(t_0)/S+E_2(t_0)$. Use $	au=r(t-t_0)$, $\alpha_1=S\mathbf a\cdot E_1$, $\alpha_2=\mathbf a\cdot E_2$, $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon	au^2/2)$, and $a_{m ref}=\exp\int_0^	au Y$ with $Y\prime=\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon	an\varphi)-\varepsilon	au\sin(2\varphi)Y-Y^2$, $Y(0)=1$, on $[0,\infty)$. On $[0,T]$, the assertion is $\alpha_2>0$, $|\alpha_1/\alpha_2+Y|\le CT^p\delta$, $\alpha_2\le|\mathbf a|\le(1+CT^p\delta)\alpha_2$, and $|\log(|\mathbf a|/a_{m ref})|\le\varepsilon$. It also asserts an invertible transverse propagator bounded by $252\exp(1)S|\mathbf a(	au_2)|/|\mathbf a(	au_1)|$ for $	au_1\le	au_2$. Absolute $C,p$ are chosen first, with integer $p$. This declaration states the result; the final theorem proves it.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_6.summary: The assertion includes positivity, logarithmic comparison and transverse propagation

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_7.text:
Let $B,E_c$ be continuous on compact $I\supset[t_0,t_0+T/r]$, with $\operatorname{tr}B=0$ and nonzero perpendicular preceding wave data satisfying $k_p\prime=-B^Tk_p$, $\mathbf a_p\prime=-B\mathbf a_p+2(k_p\cdot B\mathbf a_p)k_p/|k_p|^2$. Set $E_1=\widehat{k_p}$, $E_2=\widehat{\mathbf a_p}$ and $E_3=E_1	imes E_2$; $B_{ij}=E_i\cdot BE_j$. Physical derivatives are relative to $I$; for interval $I$, endpoint derivatives are one-sided. Put $\sigma=|k_p(t_0)||\mathbf a_p(t_0)|$, $
u=B_{12}(t_0)>0$, $\eta=B_{32}(t_0)>0$, $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$, $S=\sigma/r$, $\varepsilon=\eta/
u$, and $\delta=\sup_I|B_{12}/
u-1|+\sup_I|B_{32}/\eta-1|+\sup_I\|B\|/r+\sup_I\|E_c\|/
u$. Assume $T\ge2$ and $C_0\varepsilon\le1$, $C_0T^{C_0}\delta\le\varepsilon$ for sufficiently large integer $C_0$. In physical time, the new wave solves $k'=-M^Tk$, $\mathbf a'=-M\mathbf a+2(k\cdot M\mathbf a)k/|k|^2$, $k\cdot\mathbf a=0$, with $M=B+\mathbf a_p\otimes k_p+E_c$, $k(t_0)=\lambda E_3(t_0)$, $\lambda>0$, and $\mathbf a(t_0)=-E_1(t_0)/S+E_2(t_0)$. Use $	au=r(t-t_0)$, $\alpha_1=S\mathbf a\cdot E_1$, $\alpha_2=\mathbf a\cdot E_2$, $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon	au^2/2)$, and $a_{m ref}=\exp\int_0^	au Y$ with $Y\prime=\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon	an\varphi)-\varepsilon	au\sin(2\varphi)Y-Y^2$, $Y(0)=1$, on $[0,\infty)$. The assertion is $
u_+\ge\varepsilon
u/2$ on $[0,T]$. For $\sqrt2/\varepsilon\le	au\le T$, it adds $|
u_+/
u-1|\le\varepsilon$ and $|(\eta_+/
u_+)/\cos\varphi-1|\le1/2$, where $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon	au^2/2)$. The couplings are the $12$ and $32$ entries of $M$ in the new frame. This declaration specifies Lemma 2.7; the final theorem proves it.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_2_7.summary: The assertion separates uniform positivity from late-time comparison

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_3_1.text: The formal statement asks whether the constructed bump-based families $F_h,P_h$ have all properties of Lemma 3.1. For $0<h\le1$, these are smoothness and period one, oddness of $F_h$, $P_h'=F_h$, zero phase mean of $P_h$, $F_h'(0)=1$, $-Ch\le F_h'\le1$ and $|F_h|\le Ch$. One positive $C$ works for every width and phase. For each integer $j\ge2$, a separate positive width-independent $C_j$ gives $|\partial_s^jF_h|\le C_jh^{1-j}$. The exponent is integral and can be negative. This assertion fixes particular families, making it more specific than the paper's existence statement; its definition is distinct from the proof that follows.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_3_1.summary: The required properties are asserted for two specified families

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_4_1.text: Let $u$ be a smooth periodic divergence-free parent with flow $X$ on $[0,T]$, $0<T\le1$. Set $F=D_aX$, $M=(\nabla u)\circ X$, $H^\#=-(M_t+M^2)$, $K=F^TF$, and $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$. If $H^\#\le I$ as quadratic forms, then for each label and every $z\in H^1_0$, with $\xi=Fz$, $\int H^\#\xi\cdot\xi\le\frac12\int|\xi_t|^2$ and $\int(Kz_t\cdot z_t+\Omega z_t\cdot z)\ge\frac12\int|\xi_t|^2$. The formal statement represents $z$ by $Jv$ with $v\in L^2$ and $\int v=0$, so no test paths are lost. Symmetry of $H^\#$ is unnecessary. Here $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_4_1.summary: State the two displacement energy inequalities

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_10.text: Let $V=U+W^\natural$ arise from a depth-$P\ge2$ expansion over a smooth odd divergence-free periodic parent on $0<T\le1$, with deformation and gradient bounds $\mathsf D$, Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$ for $U,R_U$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p-\nabla R_U\le I$. Require $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\lambda\ge1$, a nonzero transverse seed satisfying (5.5), $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$, sufficiently small $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$, and $C_{\rm step}=\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b$ and $C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$. For every smooth periodic divergence-free $v$ with each spatial derivative through order two at most $\lambda^{-5/2}$, a flow of $V+v$ exists and every flow has forward and inverse derivative norms at most $C_{\rm step}\lambda^{1/4}$. The derivative bounds are separate, weaker premises than the paper’s summed $C^2$ bound. Constants precede the parent. The parent pressure need not be the normalized Poisson pressure.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_10.summary: State existence and deformation bounds for every small perturbation

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_3.text: Assume a smooth odd solenoidal parent and smooth periodic pressure on $0<T\le1$, bands $2\mathsf D$ for $U$ and $4\mathsf D$ for its odd residual $R_U$, bounds $\|DU\|,\|DX\|,\|DX^{-1}\|\le\mathsf D$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\|R_U\|\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. Let $0\le t_0<T$, $\lambda=|\kappa(t_0,0)|\ge1$, and a nonzero transverse central seed have relative growth at most $\mathsf D$, normalized coupling at least $\mathsf D^{-1}$ and $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$. For small fixed $\ell_*$ and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, nearby seeds obey $|\mathbf a(t,a)|\le2|\mathbf a(t,0)|$ and positive coupling. Supported transverse solutions obey $\|V\|_{[n],\gamma}\le C_n\mathsf D^C(\gamma(t_0)^{-1}\|V(t_0)\|_{[n]}+\|f\|_{[n],\gamma})$. Zero-initial centered forcing gives $\|V\|_{[n],\gamma}+\lambda\|\mathsf p\|_{[n],\gamma}\le C_n\mathsf D^C\|f\|_{[n],\gamma}$; the leading wave has bound $C_n\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/4}$. The first estimate requires full-interval profiles; the paper permits active-interval data. Pressure and amplitude assumptions are broader; the envelope is fixed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_3.summary: A common envelope supports all transverse estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_5.text: Assume a smooth odd unit-periodic solenoidal parent and smooth periodic pressure on $0<T\le1$, with bands $2\mathsf D$ for velocity and $4\mathsf D$ for its odd residual, gradient and both deformation bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, residual bound $\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. Put $M=DU\circ X$, $\kappa=DX^{-T}k_*$, $\lambda=|\kappa(t_0,0)|\ge1$ and $0\le t_0<T$. The nonzero central seed solves $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)M\mathbf a$, is transverse, has relative forward stability at most $\mathsf D$ and normalized coupling at least $\mathsf D^{-1}$, and satisfies $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$. For small fixed $\ell_*$ and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, transverse $V$ satisfies $\|C[V]\|_{[n],\gamma}\le C_n\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1}\|V\|_{[n+1],\gamma}$. If $V_t+MV+\kappa\mathsf p_s=f$, the same factor bounds $(\partial_t+M)C[V]+\mathbf d\mathsf p$ by the sum of the next-order norms of $V,f$. The profiles are smooth and $V,f$ have zero phase mean on all $[0,T]$; transversality, the equation and pressure normalization concern $[t_0,T]$. Smooth representatives of the homogeneous leading wave are also proved to exist. Thus full-interval assumptions accompany broader pressure and amplitude hypotheses.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_5.summary: Retain the frequency gain and specify the time intervals

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_7.text: For a smooth odd divergence-free periodic parent on $0<T\le1$ with deformation and gradient bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, velocity and residual Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$, residual size $\lambda^{-5/2}$ and coercivity $D^2p-\nabla R_U\le I$, impose the central seed conditions (5.5), $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda\ge1$ and $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$. Take $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$ sufficiently small and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$. A smooth profile with the combined lattice translation law, independent of phase outside the envelope, satisfies $\|D^mf^\natural\|\le C_m(\mathsf D^C\lambda^{3/2})^m\gamma(t)\|f\|_{[m],\gamma}$ and the $C^{m,1/2}$ bound using $m+1$. Here the derivative norm sums ordered coordinate sequences. The weighted estimates hold on $[t_0,T]$. Both estimates hold unweighted on $[0,T]$, and phase-independent fields omit $\lambda^{3/2}$. The target is any real normed space; constants precede the parent. The formal profile already incorporates continuation across cells.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_7.summary: State weighted and unweighted estimates for evaluated smooth profiles

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_8.text:
For a smooth odd divergence-free periodic parent on $0<T\le1$, require deformation and gradient bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$ for $U,R_U$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $D^2p-
abla R_U\le I$. Take $\lambda\ge1$, a nonzero transverse seed satisfying (5.5), $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$, and a depth-$P\ge2$ finite expansion with sufficiently small envelope. If $C_{m step}=\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b$ and $C_{m step}\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, then $V=U+W^
atural$ is smooth, odd and divergence free, $\Pi=p+\mathsf P^
atural$ is smooth, and their residual is $R_P^
atural+R_{\widetilde\chi}^
atural$. The bounds are $C_{0,P}\mathsf D^b\lambda^{-5/4}$ for the oscillatory supremum, $C_{m,P}\mathsf D^{b(m+2)}\lambda^{3(m+1)/2-5/4}$ and $C_{m,P}\mathsf D^{b(m+2)}\lambda^{-5/2}$ for oscillatory and mean Hölder norms, and $C_{m step}\lambda^2(\lambda^{-2P/3}+\|\widetilde\chi\,{}^{\prime}\gamma\|_\infty)$ for the residual. All hold on $[0,T]$. Constants precede the parent; the pressure class and peak normalization are broader than the paper’s.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_8.summary: State all physical estimates for every finite expansion

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_9.text: For a smooth odd divergence-free periodic parent on $0<T\le1$, require deformation and gradient bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$ for $U,R_U$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p-\nabla R_U\le I$. Take a nonzero transverse seed satisfying (5.5), $|\kappa(t_0,0)|=\lambda\ge1$, $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$, and a depth-$P\ge2$ finite expansion with sufficiently small envelope. Under $C_{\rm step}=\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b$ and $C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, the assertion gives $D_x^2\mathsf P^\natural\le C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-1/4}I$ on $[0,T]$ and $\|D V(t,0)-D U(t,0)-\widetilde\chi\mathbf a\otimes\kappa\|\le\lambda^{-1/3}$ on $[t_0,T]$. The first is a quadratic-form upper bound, the second an operator-norm bound. Constants precede the parent and expansion. Neither zero-mean Poisson normalization of $p$ nor attainment of $\max\gamma=1$ is required.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_5_9.summary: State an upper Hessian bound and an operator norm error

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_6_1.text: For $0<\rho\le1$, $\lambda\ge1$ and $T>0$, assume $T\|B_\rho\|\le1/8$, where $B_\rho=2\pi(e_1+\rho e_3)\otimes e_2$. The formal statement asserts existence of the first central wave: initial covector $\lambda e_1$, positive initial amplitude along $e_2$, nonzero transversality, the wave equations and attained peak $\lambda^{-3/4}$ on $[0,T]$. It also asserts that every such wave has initial strength in $[\lambda^{1/4}/2,\lambda^{1/4}]$, and, for every $\mathsf D\ge2$, obeys $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for transverse solutions and ordered times, with $\nu(t)\ge\mathsf D^{-1}$. Here $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a|$. The matrix norm is the operator norm. This declaration states the proposition; its proof is linked separately.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_6_1.summary: States existence and estimates for every admissible first wave

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_A_2.text: For $H=\mathbb R^3$ take $\mathcal R=\mathbb P$; for $H=L^2([0,1];\mathbb R^3)$ take $\mathcal R=\mathbb P\mathcal Q$, where $\mathcal Q$ removes the time average. Suppose $B:\mathbb T^3\to\mathcal L(H)$ is Lipschitz with constant $L\ge0$ and $\langle B(a)w,w\rangle\ge\mu\|w\|^2$, $\mu>0$, for all vectors in the first case and zero-time-mean paths in the second. Then $\mathcal RB$ is invertible on its projected half-Hölder space with bound $C(2+\mu^{-1}+\|B\|_\infty+L)^p$. The constants are chosen before $B$, with integer $p\ge0$. If $B\in C^{k,1/2}$, $k\ge1$, the same inverse preserves that class. The paper requires the stronger base hypothesis $B\in C^{1,1/2}$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_A_2.summary: State both projected inverse theorems with their regularity

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_B_1.text: On $\mathbb T^3=\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$, let $S_\Lambda$ have symbol $\psi(\xi/\Lambda)$, where $\psi$ is smooth, even, between zero and one, equal to one on the unit ball and zero outside the radius-two ball. For every $\Lambda>0$, the formal statement gives parity, frequency support, derivative commutation, the operator bounds, and (B.1)–(B.2), with constants chosen before the frequency, fields and target spaces. Spatial derivatives and norms are measured on periodic lifts. Bernstein's sum counts each multi-index once and permits any real normed target. The measurable-input $L^\infty$ clause is complex Banach-valued; the real-velocity branch assumes continuity. Spatial commutation covers all complex orders and one real coordinate derivative, with a separate first-time-derivative clause on smooth closed slabs. Higher real orders require iteration. The supplied description uses derivative-tensor Hölder sums; the underlying higher-order norm definition is absent and its normalization is not independently checked here. The paper assumes radiality and $\Lambda\ge1$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_B_1.summary: Collects commutation, support, boundedness, Bernstein and tail estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_1.text: Let $\ell_*,h>0$, let $\gamma(t)>0$ on a chosen time set, and let the fields be smooth in $(a,s)\in\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ with the required derivatives uniformly bounded. The formal statement proves (D.3) with label constant three, the weighted bilinear product estimate (D.4), and (D.5) with primitive constant two; it also proves that the output norms are finite. The norm sums one term per mixed multi-index, after division by $\gamma$. Products may be any continuous bilinear map, with its operator norm included in the constant. Phase averaging and inversion require period one and a real Banach target; inversion also requires zero phase average. Neither periodicity nor zero average is needed for differentiation or products. The phase-independent Hölder product estimate uses the maximum of supremum and seminorm; changing to their sum only alters the constant.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_1.summary: Controls differentiation, products, averaging and the periodic primitive

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_2.text: Assume $\mathsf D\ge1$ and smooth phase-independent coefficients with $|c|_m\le C_m\mathsf D^{q(m+1)}$. The formal statement uses nonnegative integer exponents. For inputs with exponents $q,r$, a bilinear product of norm at most one has exponent $2\max(q,r)$. In a complete real normed algebra, pointwise invertibility and $\|c^{-1}\|_\infty\le\mathsf D^e$ give exponent $3\max(q,e)$. Output constants are selected after the input constants and value spaces, but before $\mathsf D$, the time set and fields. Finally, $0<\ell_*\le\mathsf D^{-q}$ gives $\|c\|_{[n]}\le C'_n\mathsf D^q$ and $\ell_*^m|c|_m\le C'_m\mathsf D^{2q}\ell_*$ for $m\ge1$. Rounding the paper's fixed real exponent upward changes both this radius condition and its concluding powers; it does not reproduce that clause literally.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_2.summary: Preserves polynomial growth under products, inverses and weighting

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_3.text:
For $\mathcal Lv=\mathcal L_0v+\sum_
u T_
u(c_
u v)=f$, assume a zero-order estimate for every admissible unknown, derivative commutation for $\mathcal L_0$, the product rule for the coefficient actions, and commuting derivatives on coefficients and forcings. Suppose the actions obey the prescribed seminorm bounds and (D.7) holds for $1\le m\le n$. The formal statement proves $\|v\|_{[n]}\le C_n C_{m low}\|f\|_{[n]}$. Its finite norms sum one sorted derivative composition per multi-index in an arbitrary finite ordered family. Choosing the weighted label and phase derivatives gives (D.1). Solution constraints, quotient equations and prescribed data must be included in the spaces and derivative maps. The constant is selected before those spaces and maps, but may depend on the finite derivative family. This is an estimate for existing solutions; it asserts neither existence nor surjectivity of $\mathcal L$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.lemma_D_3.summary: Retains one zero-order inverse factor at higher orders

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_2.text:
Let $B,E_c$ be continuous on compact $I\supset[t_0,t_0+T/r]$, with $\operatorname{tr}B=0$ and nonzero perpendicular preceding wave data satisfying $k_p\prime=-B^Tk_p$, $\mathbf a_p\prime=-B\mathbf a_p+2(k_p\cdot B\mathbf a_p)k_p/|k_p|^2$. Set $E_1=\widehat{k_p}$, $E_2=\widehat{\mathbf a_p}$ and $E_3=E_1	imes E_2$; $B_{ij}=E_i\cdot BE_j$. Physical derivatives are relative to $I$; for interval $I$, endpoint derivatives are one-sided. Put $\sigma=|k_p(t_0)||\mathbf a_p(t_0)|$, $
u=B_{12}(t_0)>0$, $\eta=B_{32}(t_0)>0$, $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$, $S=\sigma/r$, $\varepsilon=\eta/
u$, and $\delta=\sup_I|B_{12}/
u-1|+\sup_I|B_{32}/\eta-1|+\sup_I\|B\|/r+\sup_I\|E_c\|/
u$. Assume $T\ge2$ and $C_0\varepsilon\le1$, $C_0T^{C_0}\delta\le\varepsilon$ for sufficiently large integer $C_0$. In physical time, the new wave solves $k'=-M^Tk$, $\mathbf a'=-M\mathbf a+2(k\cdot M\mathbf a)k/|k|^2$, $k\cdot\mathbf a=0$, with $M=B+\mathbf a_p\otimes k_p+E_c$, $k(t_0)=\lambda E_3(t_0)$, $\lambda>0$, and $\mathbf a(t_0)=-E_1(t_0)/S+E_2(t_0)$. Use $	au=r(t-t_0)$, $\alpha_1=S\mathbf a\cdot E_1$, $\alpha_2=\mathbf a\cdot E_2$, $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon	au^2/2)$, and $a_{m ref}=\exp\int_0^	au Y$ with $Y\prime=\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon	an\varphi)-\varepsilon	au\sin(2\varphi)Y-Y^2$, $Y(0)=1$, on $[0,\infty)$. Assume $0<\varepsilon_+\le\varepsilon/32$ and $H=2/\sqrt{\varepsilon\varepsilon_+}\le T$. The assertion gives $\eta_+/
u_+=\varepsilon_+$ at a crossing in $[	au_m,H]$, where $	au_m$ is the unique reference zero. For $A=\max_{[0,T]}|\mathbf a|$, all crossings there satisfy $\exp(-1)/(4\sqrt{\varepsilon\varepsilon_+})\le|\mathbf a||k|/(\lambda A)\le18\exp(3)/\sqrt{\varepsilon\varepsilon_+}$. On $[0,1]$, $|\mathbf a|\le\exp(3-\varepsilon^{-1/2})A$. Here $
u_+=\widehat k\cdot M\widehat a$ and $\eta_+=(\widehat k	imes\widehat a)\cdot M\widehat a$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_2.summary: The assertion uses one common maximum over the whole interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5.text: Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$ and $\lambda\ge1$. Assume a smooth odd solenoidal unit-periodic parent $U$ and flow $X$, Fourier bands $2\mathsf D$ for $U$ and $4\mathsf D$ for the odd residual $R_U=U_t+U\cdot\nabla U+\nabla p_U$, bounds $\|DU\|,\|DX\|,\|DX^{-1}\|\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. The pressure may be any smooth periodic choice satisfying these conditions. For $\kappa=DX^{-T}k_*$ normalized at $t_0$, the six coefficients $DX,DX^{-1},M,\kappa/\lambda,\lambda^2/|\kappa|^2,P_\kappa$ have order-$m$ bounds $C_m\mathsf D^{C(m+1)}$. A field with $\|D^mf\|\le C_m^{\prime}A_f\mathsf D^m$ satisfies $\|D_a^m(f\circ X)\|\le C_mA_f\mathsf D^{Cm}$. If $0<\ell_*\le\mathsf D^{-C}$, the scaled sums satisfy (5.8). One exponent works at every order; operator norms replace coordinate sums.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5.summary: A fixed parent power controls weighted derivatives

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5.text: Take a depth-$P\ge2$ expansion over a smooth odd divergence-free periodic parent on $0<T\le1$, with deformation and gradient bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$ for $U,R_U$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-\nabla R_U\le I$. Require (5.5), $\lambda\ge1$, $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$, small envelope and $C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, where $C_{\rm step}=\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b$. For smooth radial $0\le\psi\le1$, equal to one on $|\xi|\le1$ and zero on $|\xi|>2$, and every $\Lambda\ge1$, $u=S_\Lambda V$ and its zero-mean Poisson pressure exist. Both $u,R_u$ are odd and divergence free, with Fourier radii $2\Lambda,4\Lambda$. Put $\varepsilon=\Lambda^{2-P}(1+\|V\|_{C_tC^{P,1/2}})^2$ and $e=C\|R_V\|_{C_tC^{1,1/2}}+K_P\varepsilon$. Then $\|u-V\|_{C_tC^{2,1/2}}\le K_P\varepsilon$, the summed residual and pressure-Hessian errors are at most $e$, and $D^2(p-p_U)\le(C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-1/4}+e)I$. Constants precede the parent; $2-P$ is an integer exponent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5.summary: State the velocity, residual, and pressure estimates after truncation

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5.text: Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$ and $\lambda\ge1$. Assume a smooth odd solenoidal unit-periodic parent $U$ and flow $X$, Fourier bands $2\mathsf D$ for $U$ and $4\mathsf D$ for the odd residual $R_U=U_t+U\cdot\nabla U+\nabla p_U$, bounds $\|DU\|,\|DX\|,\|DX^{-1}\|\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. The pressure may be any smooth periodic choice satisfying these conditions. For a smooth periodic phase-independent solution $B_t+MB+\mathbf d\bar q=\bar f$, require $B=DXz_t$, $\operatorname{div}_az_t=0$ and $z(0)=z(T)=0$. At sufficiently small fixed $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$, $\|B\|_{[n]}\le C_n\mathsf D^C\|\bar f\|_{[n+1]}$ for every $n$. These are scaled label-derivative suprema on all of $[0,T]$. The exponent is chosen before the parent and order. This estimates existing solutions; it does not set $B(0)=0$.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5.summary: One extra source derivative controls the mean correction

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5.text: Assume a smooth odd unit-periodic solenoidal parent and smooth periodic pressure on $0<T\le1$, with bands $2\mathsf D$ for velocity and $4\mathsf D$ for its odd residual, gradient and both deformation bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, residual bound $\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. Put $M=DU\circ X$, $\kappa=DX^{-T}k_*$, $\lambda=|\kappa(t_0,0)|\ge1$ and $0\le t_0<T$. The nonzero central seed solves $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)M\mathbf a$, is transverse, has relative forward stability at most $\mathsf D$ and normalized coupling at least $\mathsf D^{-1}$, and satisfies $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$. For sufficiently small fixed $\ell_*$, the projected seed exists, and every depth $P\ge2$ admits a unique family of retained velocities and normalized pressures satisfying the mean and transverse recursions. For $W=\sum_{p=1}^P(V_p+C_{p+1}+B_p)$ and $\mathsf P=\sum_{p=1}^P(\mathsf p_p+\bar q_p)$, $\widetilde{\mathbf d}\cdot W=0$ and the momentum residual is $R_P+R_{\widetilde\chi}$. The oscillations and their sources vanish before activation and outside the envelope; there the remainder is phase independent. Means need not vanish before activation. Smoothness is on the closed slab; no continuation across its endpoints is asserted.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_5.summary: Specify existence, uniqueness, residual identity, and support

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_8.text: For every common construction satisfying Theorem 7.1, the formal statement asserts existence of smooth periodic velocity and mean-zero pressure solving Euler on $[0,T_\infty)$. The limiting datum $u(0)$ is smooth, odd and divergence free; $U_j(0)\to u(0)$ in every $C^{m,1/2}$. For each $S<T_\infty$, convergence to $u$ is uniform on $[0,S]$ in every such spatial norm, and $u$ remains odd. Any maximal solution with the same data and a finite lifespan must last at least to $T_\infty$ and agree there. Unlike the paper’s formulation, existence of a general maximal solution is not assumed or concluded. This declaration states the assertion; a separate theorem proves it. The precise numerical Hölder norm is defined in an omitted file.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_8.summary: The common approximate sequence has a smooth odd Euler limit

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_8.text: For a common construction satisfying Theorem 7.1 and its smooth Euler limit from Proposition 8.1, the formal statement asserts bounded velocity on $[0,T_\infty)$ and the full limit $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$ as $t\uparrow T_\infty$. It also asserts fixed real $c>0,C$ such that $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\ge c\lambda_{j-1}^{1/8}-C\lambda_{j-1}^{1/32}-C$ on every sufficiently late $[t_j,t_{j+1})$. Here the spatial domain is represented by period-one fields on $\mathbb R^3$, and the velocity norm is the essential supremum on one unit cell. The interval estimate is extra information beyond the printed Proposition 8.2. This declaration specifies the assertion; its proof and its application to integral divergence are separate.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_8.summary: The Euler limit satisfies two qualitative bounds and one quantitative bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_8.text: For a common construction satisfying Theorem 7.1 and its smooth periodic Euler limit from Proposition 8.1, the formal statement asserts both limits in Proposition 8.4. For every compact $K\subset\mathbb R^3\setminus\mathbb Z^3$ and integer $m\ge0$, $u(t)$ and its time derivative converge uniformly on $K$ with all spatial derivatives through order $m$, as $t\uparrow T_\infty$. Each limiting field is $C^m$ on a neighbourhood of $K$. The removed lattice is precisely the set of representatives of the torus origin. The time derivative is taken within $[0,T_\infty)$. This declaration states the implication; it does not itself prove it. No single jointly smooth extension through the terminal time is required by this conclusion.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.proposition_8.summary: The Euler limit has both local spatial limits at the terminal time

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.remark_1_2.text: There exist smooth odd divergence-free data $u_0$ on $\mathbb T^3$ and a smooth odd maximal Euler solution on $[0,T_*)$, with $0<T_*<\infty$, bounded velocity, $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$, and divergent time integrals of both gradient and vorticity norms. Velocity and its time derivative converge in every spatial $C^m$ norm on compact sets away from the origin. The velocity also extends smoothly in space and time through $T_*$ away from that point. Any maximal solution from $u_0$ has the same lifespan and velocity. The extension is periodic and need not solve Euler after $T_*$. This is the existential assertion of Remark 1.2, not an extension theorem for every singular solution.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.remark_1_2.summary: A singular Euler solution has a smooth local extension

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_1_1.text: There exist smooth odd divergence-free periodic data $u_0$ and a smooth odd maximal Euler solution $u,p$ on $[0,T_*)$, with finite $T_*>0$. Velocity remains uniformly bounded, $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$, and the time integrals of $\|\nabla u(t)\|_\infty$ and $\|\operatorname{curl}u(t)\|_\infty$ both diverge. For every compact set away from the torus origin and every $m\ge0$, velocity and its time derivative converge in $C^m$. The formal statement further spells out the classical uniqueness implicit in the paper: every maximal solution from $u_0$ has endpoint $T_*$ and agrees with $u$ before it. Fields are periodic functions on $\mathbb R^3$; pressure has zero spatial mean.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_1_1.summary: The maximal periodic Euler solution becomes singular

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_4_2.text: Let $0<T\le1$ and let $U$ be a smooth periodic divergence-free parent with flow $X$. Put $F=D_aX$, $M=(D_xU)\circ X$, $K=F^TF$, $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$ and assume $-(M_t+M^2)\le I$ as quadratic forms. For every $L\in C([0,T];C^{0,1/2})$, the formal statement gives unique $z,v=z_t,c,\nabla\phi$ satisfying $Kv-\int_0^t\Omega v+L=c+\nabla\phi$, $z(0)=z(T)=0$, with $z,v,c$ divergence free. Only the gradient of $\phi$ is unique. A polynomial in uniform bounds for $F^{-1},M,K,\Omega$ and the first label derivatives of $K,\Omega$ bounds $v$ and $(\mathbb PK(t))^{-1}\mathbb P$. Smooth force sources yield smooth $b=(Fv)\circ X^{-1}$ solving the linearized Euler equation and $b(0)=c$. The paper uses larger $C^{1,1/2}$ coefficient norms. The $C^{0,1/2}$ norm is the maximum of the supremum norm and Hölder seminorm.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_4_2.summary: Coercivity selects the initial correction and bounds both inverses

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_5_6.text: Assume a smooth odd unit-periodic solenoidal parent and smooth periodic pressure on $0<T\le1$, with bands $2\mathsf D$ for velocity and $4\mathsf D$ for its odd residual, gradient and both deformation bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, residual bound $\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. Put $M=DU\circ X$, $\kappa=DX^{-T}k_*$, $\lambda=|\kappa(t_0,0)|\ge1$ and $0\le t_0<T$. The nonzero central seed solves $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)M\mathbf a$, is transverse, has relative forward stability at most $\mathsf D$ and normalized coupling at least $\mathsf D^{-1}$, and satisfies $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$. Fix a sufficiently small radius $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$ and a depth-$P$ expansion, $P\ge2$. If $\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, then at every order the transverse velocity, forcing and $\lambda$ times pressure have size $C_{n,p}\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/4-2(p-1)/3}$; means and mean sources have size $C_{n,p}\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/2-2(p-2)/3}$; $C_{p+1}$ has size $C_{n,p}\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-9/4-2(p-1)/3}$. The finite sums satisfy (5.37), and $\|R_P\|_{[m]}\le C_{m,P}\lambda^{-5/4-2P/3}$. Means use the whole interval, oscillations the active weighted norm. The same exponent works for all orders, levels and depths.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_5_6.summary: Use one parent exponent at every level and order

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1.text: For every smooth radial Fourier cutoff and integer $a_0$, the formal statement chooses $b\ge1$, $a\ge a_0$ and fixed-order majorants before an admissible threshold $\mathcal B$. Every such threshold permits the construction for all sufficiently large $N$. It asserts smooth odd divergence-free periodic velocities on $[0,S_j]\times\mathbb R^3$, with $\|U_j\|_\infty,\|(D_aX_j)^{\pm1}\|_\infty\le\lambda_j$, $\|R_j\|_\infty\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-3}$ and $D^2\pi_j\le(\sum_{i<j}\lambda_i^{-1})I$. The central splitting has error $\le\lambda_j^{-1/4}$; at $t_{j+1}$, $\eta_j/\nu_j=\varepsilon_j$, $\pi\le\nu_j\le4\pi$ and $C^{-1}\lambda_j^{1/4}\le\sigma_j\le C\lambda_j^{1/4}L_{j+1}^2$, with $C=18e^3$. Localized increments satisfy $\|O_j\|_\infty,\|U_j-U_{j-1}-O_j\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le\lambda_j^{-1}$ for $m\le q_j$, and $t_j\to T_\infty\in(0,S_j)$. Each increment is identified with its finite expansion and Fourier truncation. The central amplitude is identified with the seed; the central covector is not identified with its transported counterpart, and first-wave directions and attained normalization are absent. The exponent quantifier is $\forall a_0\,\exists a\ge a_0$. Hölder estimates are stated at each time; their exact spatial norm definition is absent. This declaration states the assertion, not its proof.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_7_1.summary: States the common construction with explicit parameter dependence

TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_A_1.text:
On $[0,1]	imes\mathbb T^3$, let $K$ be symmetric and $\Omega$ skew-symmetric, continuous in time in $C^{0,1/2}$, spatially differentiable, with uniform value and first derivative bounds. Assume $K\ge\kappa I$, $\kappa>0$, and $\int(Kz_t\cdot z_t+\Omega z_t\cdot z)\ge\mu\int|z_t|^2$, $\mu>0$, for every $H^1_0$ path at each label. Every $L\in C_tC^{0,1/2}$ gives unique $z,v=z_t,c,
abla\phi$ solving $Kv-J(\Omega v)+L=c+
abla\phi$, with divergence-free $z,c$ and zero endpoints. Moreover $\|v\|_0\le CQ^p\|L\|_0$, where $Jv(t)=\int_0^tv$ and $Q=2+\kappa^{-1}+\mu^{-1}+K_0+K_1+\Omega_0+\Omega_1$; the subscripts give the uniform value and first derivative bounds. Smooth data give smooth $z,c,
abla\phi$. The paper's $C_tC^{1,1/2}$ assumption is stronger; scalar potentials remain undetermined up to time-dependent constants.
TorusEuler.Paper.Statement.theorem_A_1.summary: State existence, uniqueness and the polynomial velocity bound

TorusEuler.Paper.Text.eq_5_13.text: Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$ and $\lambda\ge1$. Assume a smooth odd solenoidal unit-periodic parent $U$ and flow $X$, Fourier bands $2\mathsf D$ for $U$ and $4\mathsf D$ for the odd residual $R_U=U_t+U\cdot\nabla U+\nabla p_U$, bounds $\|DU\|,\|DX\|,\|DX^{-1}\|\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. The pressure may be any smooth periodic choice satisfying these conditions. Write $M=DU\circ X$, $K=DX^TDX$ and $\Omega=DX^T(M^T-M)DX$. For every prescribed exponent $C_A$ and $0<A\le\mathsf D^{C_A}$, a sufficiently large radius exponent gives $\ell_*^m(|K|_{m,1/2}+|\Omega|_{m,1/2})\le C_m\mathsf D^C\sqrt{\ell_*}\le C_m/A$ for $m\ge1$, with finite coefficient norms. The radius threshold may depend on $C_A$ but not the parent or derivative order. The displayed polynomial bound on $A$ is assumed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Text.eq_5_13.summary: The proved estimate supplies the lifting condition

TorusEuler.Paper.Text.eq_5_14.text: Let $0<T\le1$, $\mathsf D\ge2$ and $\lambda\ge1$. Assume a smooth odd solenoidal unit-periodic parent $U$ and flow $X$, Fourier bands $2\mathsf D$ for $U$ and $4\mathsf D$ for the odd residual $R_U=U_t+U\cdot\nabla U+\nabla p_U$, bounds $\|DU\|,\|DX\|,\|DX^{-1}\|\le\mathsf D$, $\|R_U\|\le\lambda^{-5/2}$, and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. The pressure may be any smooth periodic choice satisfying these conditions. Let $B=DXv$, $v=z_t$, solve the mean equation with $z(0)=z(T)=0$ and $\operatorname{div}_a v=0$; set $g=DX^T\bar f$. For sufficiently small fixed $\ell_*$, finite scaled half-Hölder norm of $g$ at order $n$ implies finiteness for $v$ and $\|v\|_{[n],1/2}\le C_n\mathsf D^C\|g\|_{[n],1/2}$. Time runs over $[0,T]$. No derivative is lost here; the later supremum-norm estimate uses one more source derivative.
TorusEuler.Paper.Text.eq_5_14.summary: Endpoint control extends to every spatial derivative order

TorusEuler.Paper.Text.eq_5_59.text: For every integer $m\ge0$, there is a constant $C_m$ independent of the real normed spaces $E,F,G$ and the continuous bilinear map $B:E\times F\to G$, such that $f,g\in C^{m,1/2}(\mathbb R^3)$ imply $B(f,g)\in C^{m,1/2}$ and $\|B(f,g)\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le C_m\|B\|\|f\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\|g\|_{C^{m,1/2}}$. This theorem proves the formal assertion corresponding to (5.59), with all target-space and product choices included. The proof permits $C_m=3(m+1)2^m$. Scalar multiplication and the tensor products used in the cutoff residual are special cases; no periodicity assumption is needed.
TorusEuler.Paper.Text.eq_5_59.summary: The stated bilinear estimate is proved uniformly at every order

TorusEuler.Paper.Text.eq_D_2.text: Let $0<\ell_*\le1$ and let $c:I\times\mathbb R^3\to X$ be smooth in the label variable, where $X$ is any real normed space. Assume all derivatives through order $n+1$ are uniformly bounded in time and label. The formal statement proves $\|c\|_{[n]}\le\|c\|_{[n],1/2}\le4\ell_*^{-1/2}\|c\|_{[n+1]}$ and establishes finiteness of the Hölder quantities. At each order $m$ it also proves $\ell_*^m|c|_{m,1/2}\le4\ell_*^{-1/2}(\ell_*^m|c|_m+\ell_*^{m+1}|c|_{m+1})$. Each multi-index is counted once. The Hölder norm uses the maximum of supremum and seminorm; their sum is equivalent within a factor two. Thus the explicit constant four yields the paper's unspecified constant after the chosen norm convention is accounted for.
TorusEuler.Paper.Text.eq_D_2.summary: Costs one derivative and half a power of the radius

TorusEuler.Paper.Text.section8_setting.text: This theorem proves that there are admissible parameters, an inductive construction, a constant and a finite positive time $T_\infty$ satisfying Theorem 7.1. The same smooth periodic stage velocities have the stated residual, support, increment and central-wave bounds, and their activation times converge to $T_\infty$ while each stage lasts beyond it. This supplies the setting selected at the start of Section 8. The formal conclusion stops at that existence assertion: it does not introduce $w$ or assert uniform convergence on the closed interval. The continuous terminal velocity is established by a separate result using summability of the increments.
TorusEuler.Paper.Text.section8_setting.summary: Prove existence of a construction on one common positive interval

TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions.text: For smooth odd periodic velocities $U_j$ on $[0,S_j]\times\mathbb R^3$, their flows $X_j$, zero-mean pressures $\pi_j$ and residuals $R_j$, this condition requires frequency support $\le2\lambda_j^5$, $\|U_j\|_\infty,\|(D_aX_j)^{\pm1}\|_\infty\le\lambda_j$, $\|R_j\|_\infty\le\lambda_{j+1}^{-3}$ and $D^2\pi_j\le(\sum_{i<j}\lambda_i^{-1})I$. At the origin, the central splitting has error $\le\lambda_j^{-1/4}$; at $t_{j+1}$, $\eta_j/\nu_j=\varepsilon_j$, $\pi\le\nu_j\le4\pi$ and $C^{-1}\lambda_j^{1/4}\le\sigma_j\le C\lambda_j^{1/4}L_{j+1}^2$, with $C\ge2$. Times satisfy $0=t_1=t_2<t_3<\cdots\to T_\infty\in(0,S_j)$. At each time, oscillations are supported within distance $\lambda_{j-1}^{-1}$ of the integer lattice, with $\|O_j\|_\infty\le\lambda_j^{-1}$ and $\|U_j-U_{j-1}-O_j\|_{C^{m,1/2}}\le\lambda_j^{-1}$ for $m\le q_j$; $O_j=0$ before activation for $j\ge2$. These requirements neither construct the fields nor identify the oscillation with the finite expansion. Continuity in the time-dependent Hölder norm is not separately asserted; its exact spatial norm definition is absent.
TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Conclusions.summary: Records the estimates, activation times and localized increments

TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71StepData.text: For wave $j\ge1$, take parent $U_{j-1}$ on $[0,S_j]$, frequency $\lambda_j$, parent bound $\mathsf D=\lambda_{j-1}^9$, envelope radius $\mathsf D^{-a}$ and depth $P=6K_{j+1}$. The formal condition requires the parent and central estimates of §5.1, a transported phase, the projected seed at every label, and the finite expansion satisfying its equations. It identifies $V=U_{j-1}+W^\natural$, its approximate Euler equation, $U_j=S_{\lambda_j^5}V$, and $O_j=(W-\langle W\rangle)^\natural$ on $[0,S_j]$. Fields are periodic lifts to $\mathbb R^3$; physical evaluation uses the inverse parent flow. The seed at the origin is identified with $\mathbf a_j$ on $[t_j,S_j]$. No corresponding identification of $\kappa_j$ with $(D_aX_{j-1})^{-T}k_*$ is recorded. This declaration specifies requirements for given step data; it does not prove their existence.
TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71StepData.summary: Connects the parent, localized expansion and Fourier truncation

TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Steps.text: Fix a construction, a nonnegative integer envelope exponent $a$ and a Fourier cutoff symbol $\psi$. The formal condition asserts that, for every wave index $j\ge1$, there exist the phase, seed, time cutoff and finite expansion that realize step $j$ over $U_{j-1}$ on $[0,S_j]$. The expansion uses $\mathsf D=\lambda_{j-1}^9$, radius $\mathsf D^{-a}$ and depth $6K_{j+1}$; its physical evaluation produces $V$, $U_j=S_{\lambda_j^5}V$ and $O_j=W_{\rm osc}^\natural$. Thus one $a$ and one symbol serve all steps, while the profiles may vary with $j$. The central seed agrees with $\mathbf a_j$, but equality of the transported covector with $\kappa_j$ is not a required clause. The numbered theorem proves this condition for its constructed sequence.
TorusEuler.Paper.Theorem71Steps.summary: Requires a single cutoff and envelope exponent for all steps

TorusEuler.Paper.WaveOn.text: For paths $k,\mathbf a$ and a prescribed linear map $D(t)$ on a time set $J$, the formal condition is $k'=-D^Tk$ and $\mathbf a'=-D\mathbf a+2(k\cdot D\mathbf a)k/|k|^2$ at every time in $J$. Derivatives are taken relative to $J$, allowing one-sided endpoint derivatives. This includes the first three relations of (2.1), but not its final condition $k\cdot\mathbf a=0$. Nonvanishing, zero trace, pressure compatibility and regularity of $D$ are also separate assumptions. Division by zero is assigned zero, so the equations are defined even for $k=0$; the nonzero physical-wave interpretation requires additional data.
TorusEuler.Paper.WaveOn.summary: The two evolution equations do not include the transversality condition

TorusEuler.Paper.alpha.text: For the preceding wave’s orthonormal frame, set $\sigma=|k_p(t_0)||\mathbf a_p(t_0)|$, $\nu=B_{12}(t_0)>0$, $r=\sqrt{2\sigma\nu}$ and $S=\sigma/r$. At physical time $t=t_0+\tau/r$, the formal vector is $\alpha=(S E_1\cdot\mathbf a,E_2\cdot\mathbf a,S E_3\cdot\mathbf a)$. Thus $\mathbf a=\alpha_1E_1/S+\alpha_2E_2+\alpha_3E_3/S$, as in (2.3). Forming these coordinates does not impose the amplitude equation or transversality. The formula accepts every real $\tau$; the frame hypotheses and differential equations are guaranteed only where the physical time lies in the supplied compact set. Earlier intermediate formulas use the negative first component instead.
TorusEuler.Paper.alpha.summary: The three scaled projections are evaluated in normalized time

TorusEuler.Paper.corollary_8_3.text: Assume the common construction of Theorem 7.1, its smooth odd Euler limit from Proposition 8.1, and the formal Proposition 8.2 conclusions, including a uniform lower bound $c\lambda_{j-1}^{1/8}-C\lambda_{j-1}^{1/32}-C$ for central vorticity on every late activation interval. The theorem proves that $T_\infty>0$ is the maximal lifespan, that every maximal solution of finite lifespan from the same data has that time, and that both integrals in (1.2) diverge. The norms are essential suprema over a unit cell, with the operator norm for $\nabla u$. The conclusion agrees with Corollary 8.3. Its formal proof uses the quantitative vorticity and crossing-time estimates; it does not prove the periodic Beale–Kato–Majda continuation criterion cited by the paper.
TorusEuler.Paper.corollary_8_3.summary: The constructed solution has the terminal time and both infinite integrals

TorusEuler.Paper.exists_appendixB_cutoff.text: This glue theorem constructs an admissible S5 cutoff symbol from Mathlib’s smooth radial bump. Its radius is two, it equals one on the unit ball, and it vanishes outside the radius-two ball. The proof supplies radiality, smoothness, the range [0,1] and the two cutoff values. This is useful because Theorem 7.1 is quantified over every such symbol; it is not the proof of a numbered manuscript result.

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_1_3.text: Let $b\ge1$ be an integer, $K(s)=320b(s+1)$, and $\mathcal B(s)>0$ satisfy $\log\mathcal B(s)\ge4K(s+1)^3$ for $s\ge1$. Suppose $\lambda_0\ge\mathcal B(1)$, $q_1=1$, $\lambda_j=\lambda_{j-1}^{K(q_j)}$, and $q_{j+1}=\max\{1\le s\le q_j+1:\mathcal B(s)\le\lambda_{j-1}\}$. Then $q_j\le q_{j+1}\le q_j+1$, $q_j\to\infty$, and $4\log\lambda_{j+2}\le(\log\lambda_{j-1})^2$ for $j\ge1$. Thus the last expression is exactly (1.15), since $L_{j+1}=4\log\lambda_{j+2}$. The formal statement omits threshold monotonicity and analytic-cost domination from §1.5; the arithmetic result therefore applies under fewer assumptions.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_1_3.summary: All three arithmetic conclusions hold under fewer assumptions

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_1.text: Let $J$ be a time interval on which relative derivatives are uniquely determined. Suppose $D$ is differentiable, $\operatorname{tr}D=0$, $D'+D^2$ is symmetric, and $k'=-D^Tk$, $\mathbf a'=-D\mathbf a+p_{\rm w}k$, where $p_{\rm w}=2k\cdot D\mathbf a/|k|^2$. For differentiable $F$ and any $P$ with $P'=F$, transverse data give an Euler velocity $u=Dx+\mathbf aF(k\cdot x)$ on $\mathbb R^3$, with pressure $-x\cdot(D'+D^2)x/2-p_{\rm w}P(k\cdot x)$ and zero divergence. Nonzero perpendicular data at any $t_0\in J$ remain so throughout $J$, including earlier times. Unlike the paper, the formal statement requires neither a smooth odd periodic profile nor its normalization; the Euler identity also allows $k=0$, using zero for division by zero. The interval derivative includes one-sided endpoint derivatives.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_1.summary: The Euler identity holds for differentiable profiles and arbitrary primitives

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_2.text: Let nonzero perpendicular paths $k,\mathbf a\in\mathbb R^3$ satisfy $k'=-B^Tk$ and $\mathbf a'=-B\mathbf a+2(k\cdot B\mathbf a)k/|k|^2$ on a time set $J$, with $\operatorname{tr}B=0$. Put $E_1=k/|k|$, $E_2=\mathbf a/|\mathbf a|$, $E_3=E_1\times E_2$, $B_{ij}=E_i\cdot BE_j$ and $\sigma=|k||\mathbf a|$. The formal statement gives orthonormality and $E_1'=-B_{12}E_2-B_{13}E_3$, $E_2'=B_{12}E_1-B_{32}E_3$, $E_3'=B_{13}E_1+B_{32}E_2$, $(\log\sigma)'=B_{33}$. Derivatives are relative to $J$. These are (2.2), with no regularity assumption on $B$ beyond the supplied wave derivatives and no symmetry assumption on $B'+B^2$. All normalizations and the logarithm have nonzero positive denominators or arguments under the stated hypotheses.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_2.summary: The formal theorem proves the frame equations under the needed derivative hypotheses

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_3.text:
Let nonzero transverse preceding wave data solve the wave equations over continuous trace-free $B$, with positive activation strength $\sigma$ and couplings $
u,\eta$. Set $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$, $S=\sigma/r$, $\varepsilon=\eta/
u$, $	au=r(t-t_0)$. On $[0,T]$, $T\ge2$, require only $B_{12}=
u,B_{32}=\eta$ nonzero and $E_c=0$. Launch $k=\lambda E_3$, $\lambda>0$; write $k=\lambda(\zeta_1E_1+\zeta_2E_2/S+\zeta_3E_3)$ and $\mathbf a=\alpha_1E_1/S+\alpha_2E_2+\alpha_3E_3/S$. The formal statement gives $\sigma_p=\sigma$, $\zeta'=(-(1+1/(2S^2))\zeta_2,-\varepsilon\zeta_3,\varepsilon\zeta_2/(2S^2))$. Where $\zeta_3
e0$, it gives $\alpha_1'=-\alpha_2+\zeta_1\Pi$, $\alpha_2'=-(1-1/(2S^2))\alpha_1+\varepsilon(\zeta_1\alpha_1+\zeta_2\alpha_2)/(2S^2\zeta_3)+\zeta_2\Pi/S^2$, with $\Pi=(2\zeta_2\alpha_1+(\zeta_1+\varepsilon\zeta_3)\alpha_2)/(\zeta_1^2+\zeta_2^2/S^2+\zeta_3^2)$. As $S	o\infty$, $\zeta	o(\varepsilon	au^2/2,-\varepsilon	au,1)$ uniformly, and the amplitude matrix tends uniformly to $- igl( egin{smallmatrix}\varepsilon	au\sin2\varphi&\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon	an\varphi)\1&0\end{smallmatrix} igr)$, $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon	au^2/2)$. One threshold works for all model configurations and ensures $\zeta_3
e0$. The physical interval may lie inside a larger compact observation set. Compared with the paper, continuity of $B$ suffices. All derivatives are relative to the displayed interval. This states both finite-shear equations and their limit.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_3.summary: The exact model waves approach the same reference system uniformly

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_4.text:
Let a nonzero transverse preceding wave evolve over continuous trace-free $B$ with positive activation $\sigma,
u,\eta$ and continuous error $E_c$. Set $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$, $S=\sigma/r$, $\varepsilon=\eta/
u$, $	au=r(t-t_0)$, $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon	au^2/2)$ and $\delta=\|B_{12}/
u-1\|_\infty+\|B_{32}/\eta-1\|_\infty+\|B\|_\infty/r+\|E_c\|_\infty/
u$, on a compact set containing the physical interval. Assume $T\ge2$, sufficiently large integer $C_0$, $C_0\varepsilon\le1$, $C_0T^{C_0}\delta\le\varepsilon$, and $k'=-M^Tk$ launched at $\lambda E_3$, $\lambda>0$, $M=B+\mathbf a_p\otimes k_p+E_c$. The formal statement bounds both $\sup|\zeta-(	an\varphi,-\varepsilon	au,1)|$ and $\sup||k|^2\cos^2\varphi/\lambda^2-1|$ by $CT^p\delta\le1/2$, where $\zeta=(k\cdot E_1,Sk\cdot E_2,k\cdot E_3)/\lambda$. It gives $1/2\le\zeta_3\le3/2$, $|\zeta|\le3T^2$, and $|\sigma_p/\sigma-1|\le2T\delta$. Every transverse amplitude has $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)=(S\mathbf a\cdot E_1,\mathbf a\cdot E_2)$ satisfying $(\alpha_1,\alpha_2)'=[- igl( egin{smallmatrix}\varepsilon	au\sin2\varphi&\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon	an\varphi)\1&0\end{smallmatrix} igr)+\mathcal E](\alpha_1,\alpha_2)$, with one continuous $\mathcal E$ and $\sup\|\mathcal E\|\le CT^p\delta$. Supremum conclusions concern $[0,T]$. The integer exponent $p$ and factor $C$ precede $C_0$ and all data. Vector norms are Euclidean; error-operator norms use the maximum norm on pairs. Continuity and the strength bound extend the printed lemma.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_4.summary: Uniform bounds hold for the wave vector and a common amplitude error

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_5.text: For $0<\varepsilon\le1$, let $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)$ and consider $Y'=\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon\tan\varphi)-\varepsilon\tau\sin(2\varphi)Y-Y^2$, $Y(0)=1$, on $[0,\infty)$. There is a unique solution on that half-line, with $|Y|\le1$ and $Y=(1+e)\cos\varphi-\varepsilon\tau\sin(2\varphi)/4$ for one function $0\le e\le\varepsilon/8$. Its amplitude $a_{\rm ref}=\exp\int_0^\tau Y$ equals $\sqrt{\cos\varphi}\exp\int_0^\tau(1+e)\cos\varphi$. It has its global maximum at the unique zero $\tau_m$ of $Y$, with $2\le\varepsilon\tau_m\le3$, positive $Y$ before and negative $Y$ after, and $\log a_{\rm ref}(\tau_m)\ge\varepsilon^{-1/2}-1$. The formal theorem proves the whole assertion of Lemma 2.5, including uniqueness for all $\tau\ge0$. The functions have values at negative times as well, but neither the equation nor uniqueness constrains those values. At zero, the derivative is taken from within the half-line.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_5.summary: A unique logarithmic slope determines the reference amplitude

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_6.text:
Let $B,E_c$ be continuous on compact $I\supset[t_0,t_0+T/r]$, with $\operatorname{tr}B=0$ and nonzero perpendicular preceding wave data satisfying $k_p\prime=-B^Tk_p$, $\mathbf a_p\prime=-B\mathbf a_p+2(k_p\cdot B\mathbf a_p)k_p/|k_p|^2$. Set $E_1=\widehat{k_p}$, $E_2=\widehat{\mathbf a_p}$ and $E_3=E_1	imes E_2$; $B_{ij}=E_i\cdot BE_j$. Physical derivatives are relative to $I$; for interval $I$, endpoint derivatives are one-sided. Put $\sigma=|k_p(t_0)||\mathbf a_p(t_0)|$, $
u=B_{12}(t_0)>0$, $\eta=B_{32}(t_0)>0$, $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$, $S=\sigma/r$, $\varepsilon=\eta/
u$, and $\delta=\sup_I|B_{12}/
u-1|+\sup_I|B_{32}/\eta-1|+\sup_I\|B\|/r+\sup_I\|E_c\|/
u$. Assume $T\ge2$ and $C_0\varepsilon\le1$, $C_0T^{C_0}\delta\le\varepsilon$ for sufficiently large integer $C_0$. In physical time, the new wave solves $k'=-M^Tk$, $\mathbf a'=-M\mathbf a+2(k\cdot M\mathbf a)k/|k|^2$, $k\cdot\mathbf a=0$, with $M=B+\mathbf a_p\otimes k_p+E_c$, $k(t_0)=\lambda E_3(t_0)$, $\lambda>0$, and $\mathbf a(t_0)=-E_1(t_0)/S+E_2(t_0)$. Use $	au=r(t-t_0)$, $\alpha_1=S\mathbf a\cdot E_1$, $\alpha_2=\mathbf a\cdot E_2$, $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon	au^2/2)$, and $a_{m ref}=\exp\int_0^	au Y$ with $Y\prime=\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon	an\varphi)-\varepsilon	au\sin(2\varphi)Y-Y^2$, $Y(0)=1$, on $[0,\infty)$. The theorem proves $\alpha_2>0$, $|\alpha_1/\alpha_2+Y|\le CT^p\delta$, $\alpha_2\le|\mathbf a|\le(1+CT^p\delta)\alpha_2$ and $|\log(|\mathbf a|/a_{m ref})|\le\varepsilon$ on $[0,T]$. The invertible transverse propagator satisfies $\|\Phi(	au_2,	au_1)\|\le252\exp(1)S|\mathbf a(	au_2)|/|\mathbf a(	au_1)|$. Absolute $C$ and integer $p$ are uniform in the wave. The hypotheses allow continuous $B$ and a larger compact $I$ than the paper’s interval.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_6.summary: The physical amplitude follows the reference with controlled error

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_7.text:
Let $B,E_c$ be continuous on compact $I\supset[t_0,t_0+T/r]$, with $\operatorname{tr}B=0$ and nonzero perpendicular preceding wave data satisfying $k_p\prime=-B^Tk_p$, $\mathbf a_p\prime=-B\mathbf a_p+2(k_p\cdot B\mathbf a_p)k_p/|k_p|^2$. Set $E_1=\widehat{k_p}$, $E_2=\widehat{\mathbf a_p}$ and $E_3=E_1	imes E_2$; $B_{ij}=E_i\cdot BE_j$. Physical derivatives are relative to $I$; for interval $I$, endpoint derivatives are one-sided. Put $\sigma=|k_p(t_0)||\mathbf a_p(t_0)|$, $
u=B_{12}(t_0)>0$, $\eta=B_{32}(t_0)>0$, $r=\sqrt{2\sigma
u}$, $S=\sigma/r$, $\varepsilon=\eta/
u$, and $\delta=\sup_I|B_{12}/
u-1|+\sup_I|B_{32}/\eta-1|+\sup_I\|B\|/r+\sup_I\|E_c\|/
u$. Assume $T\ge2$ and $C_0\varepsilon\le1$, $C_0T^{C_0}\delta\le\varepsilon$ for sufficiently large integer $C_0$. In physical time, the new wave solves $k'=-M^Tk$, $\mathbf a'=-M\mathbf a+2(k\cdot M\mathbf a)k/|k|^2$, $k\cdot\mathbf a=0$, with $M=B+\mathbf a_p\otimes k_p+E_c$, $k(t_0)=\lambda E_3(t_0)$, $\lambda>0$, and $\mathbf a(t_0)=-E_1(t_0)/S+E_2(t_0)$. Use $	au=r(t-t_0)$, $\alpha_1=S\mathbf a\cdot E_1$, $\alpha_2=\mathbf a\cdot E_2$, $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon	au^2/2)$, and $a_{m ref}=\exp\int_0^	au Y$ with $Y\prime=\cos^2\varphi(1-\varepsilon	an\varphi)-\varepsilon	au\sin(2\varphi)Y-Y^2$, $Y(0)=1$, on $[0,\infty)$. Let $
u_+=\widehat k\cdot M\widehat a$ and $\eta_+=(\widehat k	imes\widehat a)\cdot M\widehat a$. Then $
u_+\ge\varepsilon
u/2$ on $[0,T]$. For $\sqrt2/\varepsilon\le	au\le T$, $|
u_+/
u-1|\le\varepsilon$ and $|(\eta_+/
u_+)/\cos\varphi-1|\le1/2$, with the reference angle $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon	au^2/2)$. This proves Lemma 2.7 under continuous-background hypotheses; it does not identify $\varphi$ with the perturbed wave’s angle.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_2_7.summary: The first coupling stays positive throughout amplification

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_3_1.text: For the selected bump construction and every $0<h\le1$, the formal theorem establishes smooth period-one functions $F_h,P_h$, with $F_h$ odd, $P_h'=F_h$ and $\int_0^1P_h=0$. A positive constant independent of width and phase gives $F_h'(0)=1$, $-Ch\le F_h'\le1$ and $|F_h|\le Ch$. For each integer $j\ge2$, a positive $C_j$ independent of $h,s$ gives $|\partial_s^jF_h|\le C_jh^{1-j}$. The power uses an integer exponent, including negative values. The paper asserts existence of some such family; this result asserts all those properties of the particular family subsequently used for the wave and its pressure.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_3_1.summary: The selected profiles realize the paper’s existence assertion

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_4_1.text: Let $u$ be a smooth periodic divergence-free parent with flow $X$ on $[0,T]$, $0<T\le1$. Set $F=D_aX$, $M=(\nabla u)\circ X$, $H^\#=-(M_t+M^2)$, $K=F^TF$, and $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$. If $H^\#\le I$ as quadratic forms, then for each label and every $z\in H^1_0$, with $\xi=Fz$, $\int H^\#\xi\cdot\xi\le\frac12\int|\xi_t|^2$ and $\int(Kz_t\cdot z_t+\Omega z_t\cdot z)\ge\frac12\int|\xi_t|^2$. The formal statement represents $z$ by $Jv$ with $v\in L^2$ and $\int v=0$, so no test paths are lost. Symmetry of $H^\#$ is unnecessary. Here $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_4_1.summary: Prove Lemma 4.1 for every Sobolev test path

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_10.text: For a depth-$P\ge2$ expansion over a smooth odd divergence-free periodic parent on $0<T\le1$, assume deformation and gradient bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$ for $U,R_U$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p-\nabla R_U\le I$. Take $\lambda\ge1$, a stable positively coupled nonzero transverse seed, $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$, sufficiently small envelope and $C_{\rm step}=\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b$ and $C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$. The theorem proves that every smooth periodic divergence-free $v$ with each derivative through order two bounded by $\lambda^{-5/2}$ admits a flow of $V+v$, and every such flow satisfies $\|D Y_{0,t}\|,\|D Y_{t,0}\|\le C_{\rm step}\lambda^{1/4}$. Constants are chosen before the parent and perturbation. This proves Lemma 5.10 under broader pressure and peak-normalization hypotheses, and with separate derivative bounds instead of the paper’s summed $C^2$ bound.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_10.summary: Every permitted perturbed flow has the same polynomial deformation bound

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_3.text: Assume a smooth odd solenoidal parent and smooth periodic pressure on $0<T\le1$, bands $2\mathsf D$ for $U$ and $4\mathsf D$ for its odd residual $R_U$, bounds $\|DU\|,\|DX\|,\|DX^{-1}\|\le\mathsf D$, $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\|R_U\|\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. Let $0\le t_0<T$, $\lambda=|\kappa(t_0,0)|\ge1$, and a nonzero transverse central seed have relative growth at most $\mathsf D$, normalized coupling at least $\mathsf D^{-1}$ and $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$. For small fixed $\ell_*$ and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, nearby seeds obey $|\mathbf a(t,a)|\le2|\mathbf a(t,0)|$ and positive coupling. Supported transverse solutions obey $\|V\|_{[n],\gamma}\le C_n\mathsf D^C(\gamma(t_0)^{-1}\|V(t_0)\|_{[n]}+\|f\|_{[n],\gamma})$. Zero-initial centered forcing gives $\|V\|_{[n],\gamma}+\lambda\|\mathsf p\|_{[n],\gamma}\le C_n\mathsf D^C\|f\|_{[n],\gamma}$; the leading wave has bound $C_n\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-5/4}$. The first estimate requires full-interval profiles; the paper permits active-interval data. Pressure and amplitude assumptions are broader; the envelope is fixed.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_3.summary: Seed localization and correction bounds hold together

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_3_of_ode.text: This supplies the local Leaves instance from Lemmas 3.1, D.1 and D.2 and the assumed weighted ODE derivative estimate, then invokes lemma_5_3_of_leaves. The separate theorem odeWordBound_of_D3 is what derives that ODE estimate from the cited D.3.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_3_of_ode.summary: Pass the supplied estimates to the transverse argument

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_5.text: Assume a smooth odd unit-periodic solenoidal parent and smooth periodic pressure on $0<T\le1$, with bands $2\mathsf D$ for velocity and $4\mathsf D$ for its odd residual, gradient and both deformation bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, residual bound $\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p_U-DR_U\le I$. Put $M=DU\circ X$, $\kappa=DX^{-T}k_*$, $\lambda=|\kappa(t_0,0)|\ge1$ and $0\le t_0<T$. The nonzero central seed solves $\mathbf a_t=-(I-2P_\kappa)M\mathbf a$, is transverse, has relative forward stability at most $\mathsf D$ and normalized coupling at least $\mathsf D^{-1}$, and satisfies $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$. For small fixed $\ell_*$ and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, transverse $V$ satisfies $\|C[V]\|_{[n],\gamma}\le C_n\mathsf D^C\lambda^{-1}\|V\|_{[n+1],\gamma}$. If $V_t+MV+\kappa\mathsf p_s=f$, the same factor bounds $(\partial_t+M)C[V]+\mathbf d\mathsf p$ by the sum of the next-order norms of $V,f$. The profiles are smooth and $V,f$ have zero phase mean on all $[0,T]$; transversality, the equation and pressure normalization concern $[t_0,T]$. Smooth representatives of the homogeneous leading wave are also proved to exist. Thus full-interval assumptions accompany broader pressure and amplitude hypotheses.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_5.summary: The curl correction gains one inverse frequency

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_7.text: Let a smooth odd divergence-free periodic parent on $0<T\le1$ have the gradient, deformation, Fourier, residual and coercivity bounds of §5.1, with $\mathsf D\ge2$, $\lambda\ge1$ and nonzero central seed satisfying (5.5) and $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$. For sufficiently small $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$ and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$, the theorem proves that evaluating a smooth globally continued profile through inverse labels costs $\mathsf D^C\lambda^{3/2}$ per physical derivative. The order-$m$ derivative sum is bounded by $C_m(\mathsf D^C\lambda^{3/2})^m\gamma(t)\|f\|_{[m],\gamma}$, and the $C^{m,1/2}$ bound uses $m+1$. The weighted bounds hold on $[t_0,T]$. Both hold unweighted on $[0,T]$; phase-independent fields omit the frequency factor. The derivative sum counts ordered coordinate sequences. Constants precede the parent and arbitrary real normed target. The paper’s cell continuation is encoded in the profile’s translation law.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_7.summary: The physical derivative estimates are proved for all derivative orders

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_8.text:
Let a smooth odd divergence-free periodic parent on $0<T\le1$ have gradient and deformation bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$ for $U,R_U$, $\|R_U\|_\infty\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p-
abla R_U\le I$. For $\lambda\ge1$, take a nonzero transverse seed satisfying (5.5), $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$, a sufficiently small envelope and a depth-$P\ge2$ expansion. Under $C_{m step}=\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b$ and $C_{m step}\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, this theorem proves smooth periodic $V=U+W^
atural$, $\Pi=p+\mathsf P^
atural$, odd divergence-free $V$, and residual $R_P^
atural+R_{\widetilde\chi}^
atural$. The oscillatory supremum is $O(\mathsf D^b\lambda^{-5/4})$; its $C^{m,1/2}$ bound has factor $\mathsf D^{b(m+2)}\lambda^{3(m+1)/2-5/4}$, while the mean has $\mathsf D^{b(m+2)}\lambda^{-5/2}$. The residual is bounded by $C_{m step}\lambda^2(\lambda^{-2P/3}+\|\widetilde\chi\,{}^{\prime}\gamma\|_\infty)$. Constants precede the parent; the cutoff supremum is over $[t_0,T]$.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_8.summary: Prove exact residual decomposition and all physical norm estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_9.text: For a depth-$P\ge2$ expansion over a smooth odd divergence-free periodic parent on $0<T\le1$, assume gradient and deformation bounds $\mathsf D\ge2$, velocity and residual Fourier radii $2\mathsf D,4\mathsf D$, residual size at most $\lambda^{-5/2}$ and $D^2p-\nabla R_U\le I$. Take $\lambda\ge1$, a stable positively coupled nonzero transverse seed, $0<\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|\le1$, sufficiently small envelope, and $C_{\rm step}=\Gamma_P\mathsf D^b$ and $C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$. This theorem proves $D_x^2\mathsf P^\natural\le C_{\rm step}\lambda^{-1/4}I$ on $[0,T]$ and $\|D V(t,0)-D U(t,0)-\widetilde\chi\mathbf a\otimes\kappa\|\le\lambda^{-1/3}$ on $[t_0,T]$. The former is only an upper quadratic-form bound. The latter uses operator norm. The parent pressure may be any smooth periodic pressure meeting the specified bounds; the paper’s Poisson choice and attained peak normalization are not required.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_5_9.summary: Prove the signed Hessian bound and central rank one approximation

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_6_1.text: For $0<\rho\le1$, $\lambda\ge1$, $T>0$ and $T\|2\pi(e_1+\rho e_3)\otimes e_2\|\le1/8$, the theorem proves existence of the first central wave with initial covector $\lambda e_1$, positive initial amplitude along $e_2$ and attained maximum $\lambda^{-3/4}$. Every wave with these properties satisfies $\lambda^{1/4}/2\le|\kappa(0)||\mathbf a(0)|\le\lambda^{1/4}$. For all $\mathsf D\ge2$ it also satisfies $\nu(t)\ge\mathsf D^{-1}$ and $|\mathbf b(t)|/\gamma(t)\le\mathsf D|\mathbf b(t')|/\gamma(t')$ for every transverse amplitude solution and $0\le t'\le t\le T$, where $\gamma=\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a|$. This is the proved numbered result, not merely a list of requirements. The operator norm is used for the central gradient.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_6_1.summary: Proves existence, propagation, coupling and the initial strength interval

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_A_2.text: For $H=\mathbb R^3$ take $\mathcal R=\mathbb P$; for $H=L^2([0,1];\mathbb R^3)$ take $\mathcal R=\mathbb P\mathcal Q$, where $\mathcal Q$ removes the time average. Suppose $B:\mathbb T^3\to\mathcal L(H)$ is Lipschitz with constant $L\ge0$ and $\langle B(a)w,w\rangle\ge\mu\|w\|^2$, $\mu>0$, for all vectors in the first case and zero-time-mean paths in the second. Then $\mathcal RB$ is invertible on its projected half-Hölder space with bound $C(2+\mu^{-1}+\|B\|_\infty+L)^p$. The constants are chosen before $B$, with integer $p\ge0$. If $B\in C^{k,1/2}$, $k\ge1$, the same inverse preserves that class. The paper requires the stronger base hypothesis $B\in C^{1,1/2}$.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_A_2.summary: Prove the base inverse and preservation of higher regularity

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_B_1.text: On $\mathbb T^3=\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$, let $S_\Lambda$ have symbol $\psi(\xi/\Lambda)$, where $\psi$ is smooth, even, between zero and one, equal to one on the unit ball and zero outside the radius-two ball. For every $\Lambda>0$, the formal statement gives parity, frequency support, derivative commutation, the operator bounds, and (B.1)–(B.2), with constants chosen before the frequency, fields and target spaces. Spatial derivatives and norms are measured on periodic lifts. Bernstein's sum counts each multi-index once and permits any real normed target. The measurable-input $L^\infty$ clause is complex Banach-valued; the real-velocity branch assumes continuity. Spatial commutation covers all complex orders and one real coordinate derivative, with a separate first-time-derivative clause on smooth closed slabs. Higher real orders require iteration. The supplied description uses derivative-tensor Hölder sums; the underlying higher-order norm definition is absent and its normalization is not independently checked here. The paper assumes radiality and $\Lambda\ge1$.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_B_1.summary: Collects commutation, support, boundedness, Bernstein and tail estimates

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_1.text: Let $\ell_*,h>0$, let $\gamma(t)>0$ on a chosen time set, and let the fields be smooth in $(a,s)\in\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ with the required derivatives uniformly bounded. The formal statement proves (D.3) with label constant three, the weighted bilinear product estimate (D.4), and (D.5) with primitive constant two; it also proves that the output norms are finite. The norm sums one term per mixed multi-index, after division by $\gamma$. Products may be any continuous bilinear map, with its operator norm included in the constant. Phase averaging and inversion require period one and a real Banach target; inversion also requires zero phase average. Neither periodicity nor zero average is needed for differentiation or products. The phase-independent Hölder product estimate uses the maximum of supremum and seminorm; changing to their sum only alters the constant.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_1.summary: Controls differentiation, products, averaging and the periodic primitive

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_2.text: Assume $\mathsf D\ge1$ and smooth phase-independent coefficients with $|c|_m\le C_m\mathsf D^{q(m+1)}$. The formal statement uses nonnegative integer exponents. For inputs with exponents $q,r$, a bilinear product of norm at most one has exponent $2\max(q,r)$. In a complete real normed algebra, pointwise invertibility and $\|c^{-1}\|_\infty\le\mathsf D^e$ give exponent $3\max(q,e)$. Output constants are selected after the input constants and value spaces, but before $\mathsf D$, the time set and fields. Finally, $0<\ell_*\le\mathsf D^{-q}$ gives $\|c\|_{[n]}\le C'_n\mathsf D^q$ and $\ell_*^m|c|_m\le C'_m\mathsf D^{2q}\ell_*$ for $m\ge1$. Rounding the paper's fixed real exponent upward changes both this radius condition and its concluding powers; it does not reproduce that clause literally.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_2.summary: Preserves polynomial growth under products, inverses and weighting

TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_3.text:
For $\mathcal Lv=\mathcal L_0v+\sum_
u T_
u(c_
u v)=f$, assume a zero-order estimate for every admissible unknown, derivative commutation for $\mathcal L_0$, the product rule for the coefficient actions, and commuting derivatives on coefficients and forcings. Suppose the actions obey the prescribed seminorm bounds and (D.7) holds for $1\le m\le n$. The formal statement proves $\|v\|_{[n]}\le C_n C_{m low}\|f\|_{[n]}$. Its finite norms sum one sorted derivative composition per multi-index in an arbitrary finite ordered family. Choosing the weighted label and phase derivatives gives (D.1). Solution constraints, quotient equations and prescribed data must be included in the spaces and derivative maps. The constant is selected before those spaces and maps, but may depend on the finite derivative family. This is an estimate for existing solutions; it asserts neither existence nor surjectivity of $\mathcal L$.
TorusEuler.Paper.lemma_D_3.summary: Retains one zero-order inverse factor at higher orders

TorusEuler.Paper.meanDeformation.text: For the two-time flow notation $X(s,t,a)$, this definition is $F(t,a)=D_aX(0,t,a)$, a linear map on Euclidean $\mathbb R^3$. It is the paper's deformation $D_aX(t,a)$ and sends label variations to spatial variations. No smoothness or flow equation is assumed by the definition itself. Where a spatial derivative does not exist, the formal derivative operation returns zero; under the smooth-parent hypotheses used in the paper it is the ordinary derivative. Invertibility follows from the reverse-flow identities, rather than from this formula alone.
TorusEuler.Paper.meanDeformation.summary: Differentiate particle position with respect to its initial label

TorusEuler.Paper.meanDeformationInv.text: The formal definition is $G(t,a)=D_xX(t,0,x)|_{x=X(0,t,a)}$. For the smooth parent flow, $X(t,0,\cdot)$ is the inverse of $X(0,t,\cdot)$, and differentiating their compositions gives $G=(D_aX)^{-1}$. This is the inverse deformation in §3.1 and the coefficient of the derivative $\mathbf d=G^T\nabla_a$. The displayed definition accepts arbitrary maps and does not itself prove the inverse identity. Derivatives are assigned zero at points where they do not exist; regularity and the trajectory uniqueness hypotheses rule out that case in the application.
TorusEuler.Paper.meanDeformationInv.summary: Differentiate the reverse flow at the current particle position

TorusEuler.Paper.meanGradient.text: For a velocity $U$ and two-time maps $X$, the formal definition is $M(t,a)=D_xU(t,X(0,t,a))$. The derivative is a linear map on Euclidean $\mathbb R^3$, with matrix entries $M_{ij}=\partial_jU_i$. For the smooth parent and its flow, this is the coefficient driving both $\kappa_t=-M^T\kappa$ and the Craik–Criminale seed equation in §3.1. The definition alone imposes no Euler equation, incompressibility or trajectory equation. At a spatial nondifferentiability point the formal derivative is assigned zero; the paper's smoothness assumptions ensure the usual gradient is used.
TorusEuler.Paper.meanGradient.summary: The parent gradient is evaluated at the particle’s current position

TorusEuler.Paper.meanGradientRate.text: For a parent velocity $u$ and particle flow $X$, set $M(t,a)=D_xu(t,X_{0,t}(a))$. This expression defines its time derivative with the label $a$ fixed, taken within $[0,T]$. At $t=0$ and $t=T$ it is the corresponding one-sided derivative. This is the $M_t$ in (4.1), not the derivative at fixed Eulerian position. If the derivative within the interval does not exist, the formal expression is assigned zero. This convention is irrelevant under the smooth-parent assumptions of §4 with $T>0$, which ensure the ordinary one-sided derivative at the endpoints and the usual derivative in the interior.
TorusEuler.Paper.meanGradientRate.summary: Differentiate the transported velocity gradient at fixed label

TorusEuler.Paper.meanHsharp.text: For $M(t,a)=D_xu(t,X_{0,t}(a))$, define $H^\#(t,a)=-(M_t(t,a)+M(t,a)^2)$, with time differentiation at fixed label within $[0,T]$. This is precisely the coefficient in (4.1). No symmetry is built into the definition. If $u$ solves Euler, (4.3) identifies it with the pressure Hessian along the flow; for a parent with residual $R$, the additional term is $-(\nabla R)\circ X$. The inverse requires the upper quadratic-form bound $H^\#\le I$, which is a separate assumption.
TorusEuler.Paper.meanHsharp.summary: Define the coefficient governing the displacement energy

TorusEuler.Paper.meanKinetic.text: For a differentiable particle map $a\mapsto X_{0,t}(a)$, write $F=D_aX_{0,t}(a)$. The coefficient is $K=F^TF$, so $Kw\cdot w=|Fw|^2$.
