TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.riccati_abs_.summary: Every global reference solution stays between minus one and one

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.riccati_devi.text: A supplied Riccati solution with $Y(0)=1$ determines a deviation in $[0,\varepsilon/8]$ throughout $[0,T]$, provided $\varepsilon>0$. The proof transforms the derivative and initial value, then applies the deviation barrier. This is a conditional estimate for an existing solution; global construction and uniqueness are separate declarations.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.riccati_devi.summary: The Riccati solution determines a bounded deviation

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.riccati_devi.text: For ε > 0, any solution of the specified Riccati initial value problem on the forward ray has deviation in [0,ε/8]. The hypotheses include Y(0)=1 and the derivative equation at every nonnegative time.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.riccati_devi.summary: The Riccati deviation stays between zero and ε/8

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.riccati_exis.text: The reference Riccati initial value problem has a solution on the entire forward ray with the prescribed bounded-deviation decomposition. The source uses the frozen manuscript's equation number; the arXiv proof map identifies it with the current reference equation.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.riccati_exis.summary: Global existence of the growing reference solution

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.riccati_gain.text: Let $0<\varepsilon\le1$ and $\tau_m\ge2/\varepsilon$. Suppose $Y$ is continuous on $[0,\infty)$, nonnegative on $[0,\tau_m]$, and has the form $Y=(1+e)\cos\varphi-\varepsilon\tau\sin(2\varphi)/4$, with $0\le e\le\varepsilon/8$ and $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)$. The formal statement gives $\int_0^{\tau_m}Y\ge1/\sqrt\varepsilon-1$. Since $a_{\rm ref}=\exp\int_0^\tau Y$, this is $\log a_{\rm ref}(\tau_m)\ge\varepsilon^{-1/2}-1$. The theorem assumes the sign and representation and does not require that $\tau_m$ be the unique zero. It records the final gain, rather than the intermediate inequalities in the paper’s proof.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.riccati_gain.summary: The bounded-deviation representation gives the required lower gain

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.riccati_refe.text: For $0<\varepsilon\le1$, this assembles a global Riccati solution, its deviation in $[0,\varepsilon/8]$, and a turning time in $[2/\varepsilon,3/\varepsilon]$. The rate is bounded by one in absolute value, positive before the zero and negative afterwards, and its integral to the zero is at least $1/\sqrt\varepsilon-1$. The integral is the logarithm of the separately defined reference amplitude.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.riccati_refe.summary: Global reference growth and its unique turning time

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.riccati_turn.text: Let $0<\varepsilon\le1$. Suppose $Y$ solves the Riccati equation on $[0,\infty)$ and $Y=(1+e)\cos\varphi-\varepsilon\tau\sin(2\varphi)/4$, where $\varphi=\arctan(\varepsilon\tau^2/2)$ and $0\le e\le\varepsilon/8$. The formal statement gives $\tau_m\in[2/\varepsilon,3/\varepsilon]$ with $Y(\tau_m)=0$, $Y>0$ on $[0,\tau_m)$, and $Y<0$ on $(\tau_m,\infty)$. These strict signs imply that there is no other nonnegative zero. The statement presupposes a global solution and its representation; it does not construct them or assert an amplitude estimate.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.riccati_turn.summary: The Riccati slope changes sign exactly once

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.riccati_uniq.text: Two solutions of the reference Riccati initial value problem agree on the nonnegative ray. This is uniqueness on the domain in the statement; it does not assert uniqueness of arbitrary extensions to negative time.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.riccati_uniq.summary: Uniqueness of the forward Riccati solution

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.s.text:
The scalar $s=(1+x^2)^{-1/2}$ used in the reference amplitude coefficients. Lean writes it as the reciprocal of `Real.sqrt (1 + x ε τ ^ 2)`. The quantity under the square root is positive for every real $\varepsilon,\tau$, so no sign assumption is needed for this definition. Later identities use $s^2(1+x^2)=1$.

Default-value audit (b5): The quantity under the square root is 1+x²>0, so the inverse is always of a positive number. No exceptional square-root or zero-inverse value enters this definition.

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.s_le_inv_x.text: Put $x=\varepsilon\tau^2/2$ and assume $x>0$. Then $(1+x^2)^{-1/2}\le1/x$. With $\varphi=\arctan x$, this is $\cos\varphi\le1/\tan\varphi$, used with the corresponding lower bound when locating a crossing. The formal statement needs only positivity of $x$, which excludes division by zero. It neither assumes a wave equation nor claims that this estimate is sharp near $x=0$; the crossing argument uses it in the late range $x\ge1$.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.s_le_inv_x.summary: The positive tangent bounds the cosine from above

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.s_le_one.text: The algebraic clock factor $s=(1+x^2)^{-1/2}$ is at most one for every real parameter and time. The proof uses $s^2(1+x^2)=1$ together with $s>0$. No choice of angle or sign of $\varepsilon$ is assumed, so this lemma also covers inputs outside the physical parameter range.

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.s_pos.text: The reciprocal square root s of 1+x² is positive for all real parameters and times. This justifies division by s in the normalized reference coordinates.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.s_pos.summary: The reference clock factor is strictly positive

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.s_ratio_boun.text: For $0<\varepsilon\le1$, $a\in[2/\varepsilon,3/\varepsilon]$, and $b\ge a$, the ratio $s(b)/s(a)$ lies between $1/(\varepsilon x(b))$ and $9/(\varepsilon x(b))$. This is a bound on the clock functions alone. It does not assume that $a$ is actually a zero of $Y$ or involve an amplitude solution.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.s_ratio_boun.summary: Comparing cosine factors after the turning-time window

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.s_sq_mul.text: The identity s²(1+x²)=1 is valid for all real parameters and times. It converts estimates involving the reciprocal square root into algebraic expressions.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.s_sq_mul.summary: The reference clock normalizes the squared length

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.s_zero.text: At τ = 0 the reference coordinate x vanishes, so the clock factor s equals one. This is the initial normalization of the reference system.

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.seven_sq_le_.text: If $0<\varepsilon\le1/16$, then $7\varepsilon^2\le7\varepsilon/16$. This elementary inequality turns the explicit quadratic error of the first reference coupling into a linear error. It has no time variable and contains no coupling or reference-solution hypothesis itself.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.seven_sq_le_.summary: Absorbing a quadratic error in the small parameter

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.sqrt_s_div_s.text: The square root of $s(b)/s(a)$ equals the exponential of half the difference of their logarithms. Since $s$ is positive for all real inputs, both the ratio and logarithms are nondegenerate without extra hypotheses. This identity combines the integrated damping correction with the reference amplitude's exponential formula.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.sqrt_s_div_s.summary: Writing the cosine prefactor as an exponential

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.x.text: The formal object is $x(\tau)=\varepsilon\tau^2/2$ for arbitrary real $\varepsilon,\tau$. It represents $\tan\varphi$ for the reference angle $\varphi=\arctan x$. For $\varepsilon\ge0$ and $\tau\ge0$, this is the limiting wave-vector turning law in (2.4). The definition does not use the actual perturbed wave vector, so it does not assert $x=(k\cdot E_1)/(k\cdot E_3)$ at finite shear. Estimates comparing the scaled wave coordinates with $(x,-\varepsilon\tau,1)$ establish the relation to the physical wave.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.x.summary: A quadratic function of normalized time determines the reference direction

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.x_bounds_of_.text: If $\varepsilon>0$ and $2/\varepsilon\le\tau_m\le3/\varepsilon$, then $2/\varepsilon\le\varepsilon\tau_m^2/2\le9/(2\varepsilon)$. Since the middle quantity is $\tan\varphi(\tau_m)$ for the reference angle, this places the peak-angle cosine at the scale of $\varepsilon$. The formal statement gives only the displayed tangent bounds, with the time interval as a hypothesis. It does not establish that $\tau_m$ is a zero of $Y$ or an amplitude maximum; those facts come from Lemma 2.5.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.x_bounds_of_.summary: The time bounds give explicit tangent bounds

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.x_mul_s_lt_o.text: For arbitrary real $\varepsilon,\tau$, put $x=\varepsilon\tau^2/2$ and $s=(1+x^2)^{-1/2}$. The formal statement proves $xs<1$. As $xs=\sin(\arctan x)$, this is the strict sine bound used to show positivity of the reference slope when $\varepsilon\tau\le2$. The inequality holds without a positive-parameter hypothesis; it is an algebraic fact about $x/\sqrt{1+x^2}$. It does not assert positivity of that expression when $\varepsilon$ is negative.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.x_mul_s_lt_o.summary: The rational expression has a strict upper bound for all inputs

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.x_mul_s_sq_l.text: Let $x=\varepsilon\tau^2/2$ and $s=(1+x^2)^{-1/2}$. For all real $\varepsilon,\tau$, the formal statement proves $xs^2\le1/2$. Since $xs^2=\sin\varphi\cos\varphi$ with $\varphi=\arctan x$, this is the bound used to make $e=\varepsilon/8$ an upper barrier for the deviation equation when $\varepsilon>0$. The statement is only the trigonometric inequality; the invariant interval and global existence for $e$ are proved separately.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.x_mul_s_sq_l.summary: The product of reference sine and cosine is at most one half

TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.x_nonneg.text: For ε ≥ 0, the polynomial coordinate x = ετ²/2 is nonnegative for every real τ. No forward-time assumption is needed for this elementary bound.
TorusEuler.ReferenceRiccati.x_nonneg.summary: The reference first coordinate is nonnegative

TorusEuler.RelayLabelJets.text: This proposition records smoothness of each label slice, a nonnegative constant `C`, and derivative bounds $\|D^jf\|\le CD^{16j+p}$ for all $j\le n$. The time index is an arbitrary type `X`; no time derivative is included. The fixed slope sixteen allows a common width condition to absorb every label order.
TorusEuler.RelayLabelJets.summary: Label derivatives with one fixed growth slope

TorusEuler.RelayLabelJets.add.text: Two smooth coefficient families with the same residual exponent `p` can be added, with the derivative constants replaced by $C+B$. The proof applies additivity of iterated derivatives and the triangle inequality at every order up to `n`. No new parent-power exponent or width condition is introduced.
TorusEuler.RelayLabelJets.add.summary: Adding coefficient profiles adds their allowances

TorusEuler.RelayLabelJets.bilinear.text: For two jet packages with residual exponents `p` and `q`, a bilinear map of norm at most one produces exponent $p+q$ and constant $2^nCB$. The hypothesis $D\ge1$ is retained. The finite Leibniz estimate distributes derivatives across the factors without changing the common slope sixteen.
TorusEuler.RelayLabelJets.bilinear.summary: A bilinear product adds the residual parent exponents

TorusEuler.RelayLabelJets.coefficients.text: If $\ell\ge0$, $D\ge1$, and $\ell D^{16}\le1$, a label-jet allowance $CD^{16j+p}$ yields a mixed-word coefficient bound $KD^p$ whenever $C\le K$. Every coefficient is phase independent. The proof absorbs $\ell^jD^{16j}$, leaving a residual power independent of the derivative order.
TorusEuler.RelayLabelJets.coefficients.summary: The envelope width removes derivative-dependent growth

TorusEuler.RelayLabelJets.const_smul.text: Multiplying a jet-controlled family by a real constant `s` preserves its residual parent exponent and multiplies its allowance by $|s|$. The proof packages scalar multiplication as a fixed continuous linear map and controls every iterated derivative. At `s = 0` the result correctly has zero allowance.
TorusEuler.RelayLabelJets.const_smul.summary: A scalar multiplies the jet allowance by its absolute value

TorusEuler.RelayLabelJets.map.text: If `hf` gives label jets for `f` and a fixed linear map `L` has norm at most one, the same allowance bounds `L ∘ f`. Smoothness follows by composition and each derivative is mapped linearly. Neither the residual parent exponent `p` nor the constant `C` is increased.
TorusEuler.RelayLabelJets.map.summary: A contractive linear map preserves the jet allowance

TorusEuler.RelayLabelJets.mono_power.text: For $D\ge1$ and `hpq : p ≤ q`, a jet bound with residual exponent `p` also holds with exponent `q` and the same constant. Only monotonicity of powers is used. This permits several coefficient expressions with different algebraic degrees to share one final exponent.
TorusEuler.RelayLabelJets.mono_power.summary: Enlarging a parent exponent preserves the derivative bound

TorusEuler.RelayLabelJets.sub.text: The difference of two coefficient families with the same residual parent exponent is bounded using the sum of their nonnegative constants. Iterated differentiation respects subtraction, followed by the norm triangle inequality. This handles the subtraction in the time derivative of the potential without relying on cancellation for its size estimate.
TorusEuler.RelayLabelJets.sub.summary: Subtracting coefficient profiles adds their allowances

TorusEuler.RelayTimeFamily.text: `RelayTimeFamily d f` means there is one nonnegative spatial cost sequence `K` such that every admissible input `s` yields a smooth coefficient field `f s` with mixed bound of amplitude `s.A ^ d` and spatial slope sixteen. The existential choice of `K` precedes the input `s`. This ordering expresses uniformity over stages, rather than permitting each stage to choose a new cost.
TorusEuler.RelayTimeFamily.summary: One cost sequence controls a family of relay coefficients

TorusEuler.RelayTimeFamily.add.text: Two relay coefficient families with the same amplitude power can be added while retaining that power and spatial slope. Their nonnegative cost sequences are added pointwise, and smoothness is preserved on every admissible slab. This is used after smaller powers have been enlarged to a common degree in the relay coefficient formulas.
TorusEuler.RelayTimeFamily.add.summary: Add relay families with the same amplitude exponent

TorusEuler.RelayTimeFamily.bilinear.text: Combining two relay families of amplitude powers `d` and `d′` through a fixed continuous bilinear map gives power `d + d′`. Their amplitudes multiply, and $A^dA^{d′}=A^{d+d′}$. The mixed product estimate supplies a single nonnegative output cost array. Spatial slope sixteen remains unchanged because Leibniz distributes the spatial order between the factors.
TorusEuler.RelayTimeFamily.bilinear.summary: Bilinear relay combinations add amplitude exponents

TorusEuler.RelayTimeFamily.congr.text: If two coefficient families agree pointwise for every admissible input, every time, and every spatial point, their `RelayTimeFamily` property transfers. The proof uses functional extensionality, so it changes only the expression of the field. It does not weaken the bound, alter the cost sequence, or create an estimate from equality alone.
TorusEuler.RelayTimeFamily.congr.summary: Replace a relay coefficient family by an equal formula

TorusEuler.RelayTimeFamily.map.text: A fixed continuous linear map applied to a relay coefficient family preserves its amplitude power `d` and spatial slope. The new uniform cost sequence is the old sequence multiplied by the map’s operator norm. Smoothness and mixed estimates are transported for each admissible input, while the cost is chosen once before that input.
TorusEuler.RelayTimeFamily.map.summary: Fixed linear maps preserve a relay family bound

TorusEuler.RelayTimeFamily.mono_power.text: If a relay family is controlled with amplitude exponent `d` and `d ≤ d′`, it is also controlled with exponent `d′`. The proof uses `s.A ≥ 1` from every admissible input. The cost array and smoothness are unchanged, allowing several coefficient formulas of different algebraic degrees to share one larger amplitude power.
TorusEuler.RelayTimeFamily.mono_power.summary: Increase the allowed amplitude power of a relay family

TorusEuler.RelayTimeFamily.smul.text: Multiplying a relay family by a fixed real scalar preserves its amplitude exponent and uniform-family property. The proof treats scalar multiplication as a continuous linear map, so its absolute size enters the cost array. This accounts for fixed factors such as minus one, two, and minus two in the normalized potential and pressure coefficients.
TorusEuler.RelayTimeFamily.smul.summary: Scale a relay coefficient family by a fixed scalar

TorusEuler.RelayTimeFamily.sub.text: The difference of two relay families with equal amplitude powers is again a family at that power. The proof applies the scalar-multiplication rule with minus one and then the addition rule. This retains one uniform cost sequence for the two terms of the time derivative of the normalized potential.
TorusEuler.RelayTimeFamily.sub.summary: Subtract relay families without changing the common exponent

TorusEuler.RelayTimeInput.text: This private structure collects a positive-length slab, scales `D,A ≥ 1`, smooth strain and covector fields, pointwise nonvanishing of the covector, and three mixed jet bounds through the fixed time order `q`. The bounds cover the strain, covector, and reciprocal squared covector norm, all with spatial slope sixteen. They are supplied fields of the structure, not conclusions obtained by constructing it.
TorusEuler.RelayTimeInput.summary: Admissible strain and covector data for relay coefficients

TorusEuler.RelayTimeInput.reciprocal.text: For a `RelayTimeInput s`, this is the scalar field $(\|s.k(t,x)\|^2)^{-1}$. It is one of the three primitive coefficient factors used in the relay polynomial estimates. The input record already carries its mixed jet bound, so the definition does not derive reciprocal estimates from a covector bound alone.
TorusEuler.RelayTimeInput.reciprocal.summary: The reciprocal squared norm of the relay covector

TorusEuler.RelayTimeInput.reciprocal_smo.text: The reciprocal squared covector norm of a `RelayTimeInput` is jointly smooth on its time-label slab. Smoothness of the squared norm follows from `k_smooth`, and `k_ne_zero` justifies inversion at every slab point. This regularity statement is separate from the already supplied `inv_bound`; neither one is inferred from the other.
TorusEuler.RelayTimeInput.reciprocal_smo.summary: The relay reciprocal is smooth on the valid slab

TorusEuler.ScalarTorusL2.text: This abbreviation names complex scalar L² over the torus Haar measure. It lets the proof use scalar Fourier density coordinate by coordinate before returning to complex vector fields. There is no zero-mean condition, smoothness condition, or prescribed Fourier support in the type itself.
TorusEuler.ScalarTorusL2.summary: Scalar square integrable Fourier fields on the torus

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerBase.text: Stores a first-wave selection, its scheduled physical stage, the dyadic cutoff identity and an initial pair of inductive stages. Equality fields identify the base velocity, pressure, stationary parent and oscillation with those of the selected approximation. This richer record lets later terminal estimates recover the actual construction behind the abstract base.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerBase.summary: The initial hierarchy and cutoff retain their exact field identities

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.text: Stores lifetime bounds, one radius exponent, one envelope constant, a scheduled base and a successor for every admissible inductive prefix. The successor is dependent on its actual tip and prefix. This record supports a single infinite construction while retaining the selected finite hierarchy and dyadic cutoff at every stage.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.summary: One schedule retains every selected physical step

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Ap.text: For the selected approximation at step `n`, this predicate requires all time jets `i ≤ q` to satisfy velocity half-Hölder bounds through the hierarchy depth and a first-order residual bound. The child-frequency exponents are `2*(m+1)+e` for velocity and `e` times the next-frequency factor `(-4)` for residual. It records the uniform pointwise-in-time inequalities, not their proof.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Ap.summary: The uncut velocity and residual bounds before truncation

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Me.text: At fixed time order `q` and spatial order `m`, the selected mean correction must belong to `SpatialHolderHalf m` at every slab time and have norm at most half the inverse child frequency. This predicate singles out the mean contribution. The other half of the increment budget is supplied later by the cutoff tail.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Me.summary: The mean contributes half the permitted mixed increment

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Po.text: For the actual selected step at index `n`, requires all time jets through `q` of the approximate velocity to satisfy the stated Hölder bounds at every spatial order up to the cutoff depth. The residual is measured at spatial order one. Both carry a common factor $\mu^B$, with explicit child-frequency powers and a next-frequency factor $\lambda_{j+1}^{-4}$ in the residual. This is a predicate on a fixed construction, not a proved estimate.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Po.summary: Approximation time bounds before absorbing the parent power

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Po.text: At a selected child step let $\mu=\lambda_{j-1}$, $\lambda=\lambda_j$, and $T=S_j$. For fixed nonnegative integers $q,m,B$, the formal condition requires $\partial_t^q\bar W^\natural(t)$ to have finite spatial Hölder measurement and norm at most $\mu^B\lambda^{-5/2}$ for every $t\in[0,T]$. Time derivatives fix the physical point and use the closed child interval. The exponent $B$ is an integer. This records the first kind of bound used in auxiliary equation (2.4); it does not prove that bound, include time continuity, or absorb $\mu^B$ to obtain $\tfrac12\lambda^{-1}$. The precise spatial-norm formula is not included among the supplied definitions.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Po.summary: A parent power multiplies the small mean correction

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Sc.text: For a selected depth-$P$ expansion on $[0,T]$, this condition prescribes factorially weighted time bounds through order $q$. With constants $K,L\ge1$, it bounds the amplitude-weighted oscillatory sum by a recurrence constant times $L^2\lambda^{-5/4}$ and the unweighted mean by a recurrence constant times $L^6\lambda^{-5/2}$. The unweighted remainder has factor $\lambda^{-5/4-2P/3}$. These three estimates require $m+3P\le H$. The activation correction is bounded by $2(KL)^2\lambda^{-5/4}$ when $m+1\le H$. Here $H$ is the available spatial-order allowance. This condition records estimates at a finite derivative range; it does not prove them at every order. Some spatial seminorm and recurrence-constant definitions are absent from the packet, so their exact normalization remains unverified.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Sc.summary: The means and oscillations keep different decay factors

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Sc.text: For a selected child, set $\mu=\lambda_{j-1}$, $\lambda=\lambda_j$ and $\mathsf D=\mu^9$. The condition bounds mixed derivatives of $D_aX$, its inverse, $M=(\nabla U)\circ X$, $\kappa/\lambda$ and $\lambda^2/|\kappa|^2$ through time order $q+1$, with spatial bound $C_m\mathsf D^{E+16m}$. The transported parent residual is bounded through time order $q$ by $C_m\mathsf D^{E+16m}\lambda^{-5/2}$. All bounds hold on the closed child slab and use full spatial derivatives. These are raw derivative estimates, not yet the weighted finite norms in (2.2); the label radius absorbs the spatial growth. The reciprocal expression is assigned zero at a zero covector. Nonvanishing belongs to the selected wave data, not to this list of inequalities alone.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Sc.summary: The transported residual uses one fewer time order

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Se.text: At reserve `depth+q+1`, this predicate asks for bounds on the actual selected mean, oscillation, remainder, and combined switch profiles. The mean and remainder use unweighted time norms; oscillation and switch use the central amplitude weight. All four share $\mu^E$, while their displayed child-frequency powers remain distinct. The predicate is an input interface, not an existence statement.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Se.summary: Four mixed profile bounds for the selected graph

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Te.text: This record asks for two conditional eventual statements on one scheduled construction. Parent stage bounds through `q` must imply uncut approximation bounds through `q+1` with some exponent `e`, and for each fixed `m` they must imply the half-size mean bound. The exponent is chosen before the eventual stage index; the mean threshold may depend on `q,m,A`.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.Te.summary: Two eventual graph estimates close the time induction

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.co.text: Projects a scheduled construction to the abstract `InductiveEulerConstruction` by keeping its lifetime bounds, certified base and each stored successor's step. It does not choose new stages. The auxiliary selected hierarchy data remain available in the original record and are reconnected to this abstract construction by the subsequent equality theorems.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.co.summary: Forgetting retained profiles gives the inductive construction

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ev.text: For any real constant `C`, the child frequency `P.frequency (n+2)` is eventually at least `C`. This is the divergence of the scheduled frequency sequence after a fixed index shift. It lets later cutoff arguments absorb fixed numerical constants while excluding only finitely many initial stages.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ev.summary: The child frequency eventually exceeds any fixed threshold

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ev.text: For any natural constant `C`, the exponent evaluated at `P.order (n+3)` is eventually at least `C`. The proof shifts the established divergence of adjacent frequency exponents. This supplies enough hierarchy depth for the cutoff tail and enough next-frequency decay to absorb the fixed residual-growth exponent.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ev.summary: The next frequency exponent eventually exceeds any fixed order

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ev.text: If a proposition holds for `n+1` at all sufficiently large natural indices, then it holds for all sufficiently large indices without that shift. The proof increases the threshold by one and writes each later index as a successor. No assertion is made about the finitely many excluded initial stages.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ev.summary: Remove one shift from an eventual stage statement

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.text: For fixed time order `q` and input exponent `B`, choose a natural exponent `E` before the scale `D` is supplied. For every `D ≥ 2`, the actual recursive flow-coefficient amplitude at input `D^B` is at most `D^E`. The additional inequality `(B+2)*q ≤ E` reserves enough power to cover the pulled-back residual amplitude as well.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.summary: The flow coefficient amplitude has a uniform polynomial power

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.text: Choose a function `L`, with `L N ≥ 1`, before the parameters and scheduled construction are supplied. If the radius exponent is at least seven, every selected stage satisfies scaled inverse-coframe derivative bounds through order `N`, with amplitude $\lambda_{n+1}^9$. The same function works for all stage indices, while its value may grow with the finite derivative reserve.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.summary: One coframe cost works for every selected stage

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.text: Choose the integer envelope exponent $a$ above a fixed threshold, independent of time order. Given parent coefficient bounds through time order $q+1$, with the residual through order $q$, the formal statement bounds the selected mean for every phase-independent source $f_{\rm m}$ by $\mathcal J_{q+1}(B)_{[m]}\le K_m\mathsf D^{r_0+a}\mathcal J_q(f_{\rm m})_{[m+1]}$. Here $\mathsf D=\mu^9$, $\lambda_0\ge e$, and the parent frequency satisfies $\mu\ge2$. The integer $r_0$ and constants $K_m$ are chosen from the time order and coefficient bounds before the construction and stage. Thus one label derivative is spent and one source time derivative is gained. The finite spatial seminorms used here are imported from files not supplied, so their exact normalization cannot be checked in this packet.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.summary: One extra label derivative controls the mean

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.text: Fix nonnegative integers $q,A$. Before choosing a construction or stage, the formal statement selects an integer $E$ and nonnegative constants $C_m$. If the parent frequency is $\mu\ge2$ and its velocity and residual obey $|\partial_t^iU|\le\mu^A$ and $|\partial_t^iR_U|\le\lambda^{-5/2}$ for $i\le q$, then the selected child coefficients satisfy mixed bounds $C_m(\mu^9)^{E+16m}$. These cover $D_aX$, its inverse, $M$, $\kappa/\lambda$ and its reciprocal squared length through time order $q+1$. The pullback $R_U\circ X$ is covered only through order $q$ and retains $\lambda^{-5/2}$. The bounds concern raw derivatives on the closed child interval. Turning them into the paper's weighted finite norms requires the label-radius estimates.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.summary: Parent estimates control all the selected coefficients

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.text: Fix integers $q,A\ge0$. There are an integer $B\ge A$ and constants $C_m\ge0$, chosen before the construction, such that the following holds. If $\mu=\lambda_{j-1}\ge2$ and the parent has time bounds $|\partial_t^iU|\le\mu^A$ and $|\partial_t^iR_U|\le\lambda_j^{-5/2}$ for $i\le q$, then on the closed child interval $[0,S_j]$ one has $\|D_x^m\partial_t^iU\|\le C_m\mu^{B+5m}$ for $i\le q+1$, and $\|D_x^m\partial_t^iR_U\|\le C_m\mu^{5m}\lambda_j^{-5/2}$ for $i\le q$. These are operator norms of full derivatives. Restriction to the shorter positive slab preserves the endpoint derivatives. This is the parent estimate in auxiliary (2.1), with its time order shifted by one.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.summary: The parent supplies one additional velocity time order

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.text: Fix a strength constant at least $2$. The formal statement chooses a radius-exponent threshold and an initial-frequency threshold before the time order. For each allowed envelope exponent $a$ and integers $q,A$, it then chooses an integer $e$ and nondecreasing constants $K_H\ge1$ before the construction. If the parent has time bounds through order $q$ with exponent $A$, and $(\mathsf D^e)^6\lambda^{-1/12}\le1$, the selected expansion has summed profile bounds through time order $q+1$, with loss $L=\mathsf D^e$ and spatial allowance $H$. Here $\mathsf D=\mu^9$. The conclusion concerns the aggregate oscillation, mean, remainder and activation correction. It does not separately state every profile, pressure and source estimate described in the paper's paragraph.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.summary: One fixed parent exponent controls the admitted orders

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.text: For fixed natural `e` and `q`, choose `E` uniformly for all `D ≥ 2` and nonnegative amplitudes `A ≤ D^e`. Then the reciprocal amplitude with initial value `D^4` is at most `D^E`. Induction follows its polynomial recurrence; the successor exponent can be taken as `e+2*E+1`. This theorem controls a scalar amplitude rather than a reciprocal field.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.summary: The reciprocal amplitude has a fixed parent-scale power

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.text: There is a fixed integer lower bound $a_0\ge30$ for the envelope exponent. Under the selected parent coefficient estimates, every retained transverse level $2\le p\le P$ has amplitude-weighted time norm through order $q+1$ bounded by its source norm times a fixed-order constant and $\mathsf D^{20+4E(q+2)}$, where $\mathsf D=\mu^9$. The constants are chosen before the construction and level; they may depend on the time order, spatial order and coefficient bounds. The mean source is measured only through order $q$ in the same collection of estimates. This is an inequality for the selected inverse, not a new existence theorem for arbitrary forcing, and it does not include the separate oscillatory pressure bound.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.summary: Each later oscillation is bounded by its source

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.text: For fixed `q`, `E`, and nonnegative `C`, choose one cost array before the construction and stage. A radius exponent at least sixteen and the scheduled parent coefficient record give raw mixed bounds for the amplitude operator and pressure row, plus four coefficient time-seminorm bounds. They all use time order `q+1`, spatial slope sixteen, and common amplitude $D^{4E}$.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.summary: Bound the actual transverse and normalized pressure coefficients

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.text: Fix `q`, `E`, and a nonnegative cost array before choosing the construction or stage. If its radius exponent is at least sixteen and its actual parent coefficient bounds hold, the exact relay coefficients satisfy time budgets through `q+1` with amplitude $D^{\max(6E,a+2E)}$. The cost array is chosen independently of the stage; the exponent records the inner coefficient degree and inverse label radius separately.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.summary: The selected relay coefficients share one parent exponent

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.text: For each selected step, there is a `TruncatedChildStage` using precisely the dyadic multiplier and cutoff scale `P.frequency (n+2)^5`, whose velocity and residual equal those of that step. The proof transports the existing cutoff along the schedule’s frequency identity and the stored symbol equality. It does not construct a second approximation or alter the cutoff.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.summary: Recover the dyadic cutoff used by the selected stage

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.text: There exists a cutoff-cost table, chosen before the schedule and construction, such that `TerminalCostBounds` for this table together with `TerminalGraphStep` yields the actual stages’ `TerminalTimeStep`. The Boolean row separates the stress-product cost from the ordinary cutoff tail. The proof uses the selected dyadic cutoff, absorbs fixed constants at sufficiently large stages, and combines the mean and tail halves of the mixed increment.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.ex.summary: Choose fixed cutoff costs and finish the stage induction

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.le.text: For `m ≤ N` and a nonnegative array `C`, the common parent cost through `N` is at least `C m`. The proof extracts the `m`th summand and then includes the added one. This lets every parent derivative required by the finite graph reserve use the same scalar coefficient.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.le.summary: The parent reserve cost dominates every included order

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.le.text: With nonnegative row costs and `m ≤ H`, the cost of row `m` is bounded by the finite majorant through `H`. The proof isolates that summand and includes the initial one. This turns the separate source, mean, transverse, seed, and relay estimates into a common coefficient `K H`.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.le.summary: Every included hierarchy row fits the majorant

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.me.text: For a phase-independent mean source, a word of length at most `m` and time order at most `q` is bounded by its order-`m+1` factorial time norm times $4q!D^{q+a}$. The hypotheses require $0<T\le1$, $0<\ell\le1$, `T⁻¹ ≤ D`, and `ell⁻¹ ≤ D^a`. The extra spatial order converts finite label norms to half-Hölder control; the factor $D^q$ pays for time extraction.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.me.summary: Read the mean source in half-Hölder word norms

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.mi.text: Given joint smoothness, a mixed coefficient bound, and compatible endpoint half-Hölder jets, the theorem bounds every time jet `i ≤ q` of a spatial word of length at most `n`. The scaled norm costs `terminalMeanWordConstant C n * D^(e+scale)`. It assumes positive slab and label width, `D ≥ 1`, and `ell * D^scale ≤ 1`, plus nonnegative arrays with `C' ≤ C`.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.mi.summary: Turn raw coefficient jets into half-Hölder word bounds

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.on.text: For `D ≥ 2` and a natural exponent `B`, the elementary estimate $1+D D^B\le D^{B+2}$ holds. First bound the added one by the existing positive term, then absorb the factor two into `D`. This is a scalar comparison used to replace nested coefficient amplitudes by one fixed power of the parent scale.

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.po.text: For a selected child let $\mu=\lambda_{j-1}$, $\lambda=\lambda_j$, $\lambda_+=\lambda_{j+1}$ and depth $P$. Assume the parent mixed bounds, inverse-flow derivative bounds, small activation amplitude $\gamma\le e^3\lambda_+^{-4}$, and profile estimates with spatial allowance $H\ge4P+q+1$ and $H\ge P+q+2$. Also require $\mathsf D^{\max(a,1)+1}\le\lambda^{1/2}$ and the fixed conversion cost to be at most $\mu$. The conclusion bounds $\partial_t^iV$ by $\mu^B\lambda^{2(m+1)+2q}$ for $i\le q,m\le P$, and $\partial_t^iR_V$ by $\mu^B\lambda^{2(q+2)}\lambda_+^{-4}$. The mean retains $\lambda^{-5/2}$ with a spatial-order-dependent parent power. These are bounds in the formal spatial Hölder norms. The exact formula selecting $B$ is imported from an omitted file; the later absorption into pure child powers is separate.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.po.summary: Physical differentiation leaves explicit parent-frequency losses

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.po.text: From the actual parent jets, coframe bounds, four profile estimates, switch-envelope smallness, and one full cost bounded by the parent frequency, obtain polynomial bounds for the uncut velocity, residual, and mean. The old-wave condition absorbs spatial oscillatory costs into child-frequency powers. The velocity/residual exponent is `terminalGraphReadoutPower q B E`; the mean exponent additionally contains `9*(a+1)*(m+1+q)` and may depend on fixed spatial order.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.po.summary: Convert the selected profile bounds to Eulerian estimates

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.sc.text: For the actual selected hierarchy, this theorem combines supplied coefficient rows, lower-time-order parent residual and mean estimates, leading-wave and switch bounds, transverse bounds, completion bounds, and relay bounds. It requires `K,L ≥ 1` and `L^6 * freq^(-1/12) ≤ 1`. The output is `ScheduledMixedProfileBounds` at the same `q` and reserve `H`; no new profiles or stage sequence are selected.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.sc.summary: Assemble the mixed estimates on one selected hierarchy

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.sc.text: This is the selected parent’s transported label wave vector divided by `P.frequency (n+2)`. The carrier comes from the exact selected child step, while the flow belongs to its parent. The index distinction matters: the parent scale is at `n+1`, but the carrier is normalized by the new child frequency. No new wave vector is chosen here.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.sc.summary: The transported covector normalized at the child frequency

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.sc.text: Assume the selected parent coefficient bounds with exponent $E$, nonnegative constants $C_m$, and envelope exponent $a\ge16$. Set $\mathsf D=\mu^9$, $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-a}$ and $h=\lambda^{-1/2}$. The formal statement bounds the factorial time norm of each row of $\ell_*^{-1}(D_aX)^{-1}$ through order $q+1$ by a fixed-order constant times $\mathsf D^{a+E}$. The coefficient $h^{-1}\kappa$ has bound of the same kind with $\mathsf D^E\lambda^{3/2}$. The transported residual uses time order $q$ and has factor $\mathsf D^E\lambda^{-5/2}$. These are the slow, fast and residual coefficients entering the hierarchy sources. The fixed-order constants and spatial seminorms are imported; their complete normalization is not included in the packet.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.sc.summary: The residual retains its small child-frequency factor

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se.text: Given `ScheduledMixedProfileBounds` with recurrence loss $(\mu^9)^e$, this theorem produces the four graph-input estimates with common factor $\mu^{54e}$. The reserve assumptions include `depth+q+1+3*depth ≤ H` and the switch’s extra derivative. The mean uses the sixth loss power exactly; oscillation and activation use only the second, and the tail needs no additional loss.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se.summary: Put all four profile bounds under one parent power

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se.text: Applies the stored successor function to the tip and certified prefix found in the actual construction trace at index `n`. The result retains the selected hierarchy for the next later stage, whose sequence index is `n + 2`. This avoids retrieving an unrelated successor that merely satisfies the same abstract estimates.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se.summary: The construction trace recovers its selected later hierarchy

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se.text:
At every selected later step, write $V=U_{j-1}+W^
atural$ for the approximate velocity before truncation, $O_j=W_{m osc}^
atural$, and $U_j=S_{\Lambda_j}V$. The formal statement proves the exact field identity $U_j-U_{j-1}-O_j= ar W^
atural+(S_{\Lambda_j}-\operatorname{Id})V$. It is an equality of the fields produced by that same step, not merely a decomposition into fields with similar bounds. The formal indexing here starts with $j=2$. Equality is stated for the globally defined functions; the analytic estimates and physical interpretation are used on $[0,S_j]$. The identity alone supplies neither summability nor a bound on either term.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se.summary: Both terms belong to the actual selected step

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se.text: For the oscillation of actual stage `n+2`, every fixed Eulerian time jet is continuous on that stage’s closed slab in the spatial half-Hölder norm of order `m`. The proof rewrites the stage oscillation as the selected approximation’s oscillation, then uses its smoothness and periodicity. It claims no uniform-in-stage bound or terminal limiting behavior by itself.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se.summary: The selected oscillation has continuous mixed spatial norms

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se.text: The residual of stage `n+2` equals the residual of the exact selected cutoff. This equality retains the pressure choice entering the momentum residual, through the scheduled construction’s stored identities. It prevents applying the auxiliary residual estimate to an unrelated truncated field with the same scale.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se.summary: The stage residual is the chosen cutoff residual

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se.text: For every selected later stage $j\ge2$ and integers $q,m\ge0$, the formal statement proves that $\partial_t^qU_j$ and $\partial_t^qR_j$ are continuous from $[0,S_j]$ into the spatial supremum norm. It also proves continuity of $\partial_t^q(U_j-U_{j-1}-O_j)$ in the formal spatial Hölder norm of order $m+1/2$. Continuity means that the norm of the difference tends to zero as time approaches any point from within the closed interval, including endpoints. The derivatives fix the physical spatial point. This supplies the continuity clauses in auxiliary Lemmas 1.2 and 1.3 at every selected later stage, but contains no numerical bounds. The precise Hölder-norm formula is not supplied.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se.summary: All selected time derivatives vary continuously in time

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se.text: For the fixed scheduled construction, the velocity at stage `n+2` is exactly the cutoff velocity attached to `selectedStep n`. This is a function equality, not merely a common estimate or agreement on the slab. It ensures later time-derivative bounds apply to the same stage sequence used in the terminal limit.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.se.summary: The stage velocity is the chosen cutoff velocity

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.st.text: At a later index `n + 2`, the oscillation stored in the abstract stage sequence is exactly the oscillation of the selected approximation. This equality is inherited from the scheduled step record. It allows support and derivative estimates for the concrete oscillation to pass to the common-sequence and terminal arguments.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.st.summary: The sequence keeps the selected oscillatory increment

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.st.text: Identifies the residual of sequence stage `n + 2` with the selected cutoff residual by rewriting both its velocity and pressure. The equality uses the actual momentum-residual definition. It ensures that later residual estimates concern the stage appearing in the convergence argument, rather than a separate field with a matching bound.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.st.summary: The sequence residual is the selected cutoff residual

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.st.text: At sequence index `n + 2`, the constructed stage velocity equals the cutoff velocity of the selected later hierarchy. This is a projection of the successor's stored equality field. It is used when estimates proved for the explicit finite hierarchy must be applied to the abstract stage sequence.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.st.summary: The sequence velocity is the selected cutoff velocity

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.text: For a selected step on $[0,T]$, the formal object is $\sum_{i=0}^q(T^i/i!)\|\partial_t^if\|_{[m],\gamma}$, with label radius $\ell_*$, phase width $h$, and the positive central amplitude $\gamma$. The time derivatives hold label and independent phase fixed. Each differentiated profile is then measured using the amplitude weight on the active interval; the derivative never acts on that weight. The selected data require positivity and continuity of $\gamma$, so division there uses an ordinary nonzero denominator. This is the intended oscillatory norm in the auxiliary note. Its underlying weighted spatial seminorm is defined in an omitted file, so the exact placement of its suprema cannot be checked from this packet alone.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.summary: Differentiate the profile before dividing by its amplitude

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.text: The parent cost is one plus the sum of `C j` through order `N`. With a nonnegative input array it is at least one and dominates every included derivative cost. This converts the parent’s order-dependent Bernstein estimates into one coefficient for a graph readout at a fixed finite reserve.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.summary: A common parent derivative cost through the reserve

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.text: If every entry of `C` is nonnegative, `terminalGraphParentCost C N` is at least one for every reserve `N`. The result follows by adding a nonnegative finite sum to one. It is used to keep the scalar graph-conversion factors nonnegative and to compare powers of those factors.

This scalar multiplies the number of retained levels `1,…,d` by the depth-`d` hierarchy level constant. It is the common fixed factor in the mean and oscillatory profile sums before their frequency powers are attached. The definition does not assert that any particular hierarchy satisfies those estimates.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.summary: The finite sum cost for retained profiles

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.text: If `K ≥ 0`, the finite profile-sum cost at any depth `d` is nonnegative. The number of levels is nonnegative, and the hierarchy level constant is at least one. This sign fact allows the common sixth-power loss to enlarge the oscillatory and mean bounds without reversing an inequality.

For nonnegative `K`, the explicit remainder factor is nonnegative at every depth. Its formula consists of `2*K`, a squared level constant, and nonnegative counts of omitted interaction pairs. The result justifies inserting an additional parent-frequency factor when placing the tail estimate under the same common loss as the other profile estimates.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.summary: The profile remainder cost is nonnegative

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.text: Assume that parent time bounds through order $q$ imply, eventually, physical approximation bounds through order $q+1$ with a fixed parent-frequency power. Assume separately that, for every fixed spatial order $m$, the corresponding mean correction is bounded by $\mu^B\lambda^{-5/2}$ for some fixed integer $B$. The formal statement turns these assumptions into the numerical estimates required before the cutoff step. In particular, frequency separation gives $\mu^B\le\tfrac12\lambda^{3/2}$ eventually, hence the mean is at most $\tfrac12\lambda^{-1}$. The velocity-residual loss is absorbed into a child exponent $2(q+1)+5$. All orders and exponents are fixed before the stage tends to infinity. The analytic approximation and mean estimates remain hypotheses of this implication.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.summary: The physical estimates close once their losses are fixed

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.text: The order majorant is one plus the sum of `rowCost m` through the finite reserve `H`. When the rows are nonnegative it is at least one, monotone in `H`, and dominates every included row. It collects the fixed analytic constants before the schedule compares them with the old frequency.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.summary: One majorant covers all finite derivative costs

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.text: If all row costs are nonnegative, their finite majorant is at least one at every reserve `H`. The proof only uses nonnegativity of the finite sum. This supplies the lower bound needed for hierarchy constants and powers of the common analytic cost; it gives no size bound relative to a frequency.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.summary: The hierarchy order majorant starts above one

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.text: For a nonnegative row-cost array, `terminalHierarchyOrderMajorant rowCost` is monotone in the reserve. Enlarging `H` adds only nonnegative terms to the finite sum. This permits one schedule threshold to cover nested sets of derivative orders without revising constants already included at a lower reserve.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.summary: Increasing the derivative reserve increases the cost majorant

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.text: This private scalar is six times the sum of `C j + C (j+1)` through order `m`. It gathers the two adjacent derivative orders needed to control half-Hölder norms of all label words of length at most `m`. The shift by one records the extra spatial derivative used in the Hölder comparison.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.summary: One coefficient cost for all shorter spatial words

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.text: If `C` is nonnegative and `C' j ≤ C j` pointwise, then every included adjacent-order cost `6*(C' m + C' (m+1))` is bounded by the majorant through `n`, provided `m ≤ n`. The array `C'` need not be nonnegative for this comparison. The proof uses a single summand of the larger finite sum.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.summary: The word majorant covers a smaller coefficient array

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.text: When every entry of `C` is nonnegative, the mean word constant is nonnegative at every reserve `m`. Each summand contains two nonnegative adjacent-order costs, and the overall factor is six. This elementary sign result supports all subsequent multiplication and monotonicity steps in the mean time-derivative bound.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.summary: The mean coefficient word cost is nonnegative

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.text: For a selected finite expansion and time order $q$, the formal object measures its mean fields with the unweighted factorial norm through order $q$, but their sources through order $\max(q-1,0)$. Oscillatory fields, pressures and sources use the amplitude-weighted time norms through order $q$. The same selected profiles, activation completion and transported parent residual enter these measurements. Thus for $q\ge1$ the mean inverse can use one fewer source time derivative, as auxiliary equation (2.3) permits. At $q=0$, natural-number subtraction makes the source order zero. This is a choice of measurements; it proves no inequality for those quantities.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.summary: The mean source is measured one order lower

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.text: The graph-conversion cost is evaluated at reserve `d+q+1`, using the parent Bernstein majorant, finite profile-sum constants, the remainder factor, and the switch factor `2*K^2`. This assembles the full scalar product that the enlarged threshold must dominate. It leaves the remaining parent-frequency exponent separate, so increasing depth changes the cost row rather than that exponent.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.summary: One threshold cost for the entire graph conversion

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.text: Using the hierarchy level constant `C`, this factor is `2*K*(C+1)^2` times one plus the relevant counts of omitted interaction pairs. It is the scalar coefficient in the unweighted remainder estimate at the next hierarchy level. Its parameters are depth and the fixed analytic cost; the child-frequency decay remains outside the definition.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.summary: The fixed scalar multiplying the finite-depth remainder

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.text: For a selected step on $[0,T]$, a spatial order $m$ and a time order $q$, the formal object is $\sum_{i=0}^q(T^i/i!)\|\partial_t^if\|_{[m]}$. The derivatives hold the Lagrangian label and independent phase fixed; the selected label radius and phase width enter the finite spatial measurement. There is no division by the central amplitude, as required for the mean terms in the auxiliary argument. The sum is a seminorm and contains only finitely many time derivatives. The packet supplies its time weighting explicitly but omits the underlying spatial-seminorm definition, so the exact derivative counting and suprema in that measurement remain unverified here.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.summary: Mean profiles carry no central-amplitude denominator

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.text: Assume eventual conditional estimates for each selected cutoff: parent time bounds through `q` imply child velocity/residual bounds through `q+1`, and the uncut mean plus cutoff tail satisfies the corresponding mixed increment bound. The theorem rewrites these estimates using the exact stage identities and shifts the index once. The result is a `TerminalTimeStep` for the fixed physical sequence.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerConstruction.te.summary: Transfer selected cutoff estimates to the common stage induction

TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerStep.text: Stores the selected later input over a given tip, its scheduled physical stage and a certified inductive successor. The cutoff symbol is dyadic. Equality fields connect the successor's velocity, pressure and wave oscillation to those of the stored hierarchy, so changing to the abstract recurrence does not lose their mathematical identity.
TorusEuler.ScheduledEulerStep.summary: A later hierarchy is attached to its exact preceding tip

TorusEuler.ScheduledLaterPhysicalWindowB.text: This proposition bundles a normalized window of length at least two, its exact clock endpoint and interval mapping, the two finite-comparison smallness inequalities, and a positive smaller target ratio. It also places the crossing search horizon within the first physical half and the full normalized interval. These are conditions for applying the crossing theorem.
TorusEuler.ScheduledLaterPhysicalWindowB.summary: The scheduled window carries all comparison and crossing conditions

TorusEuler.ScheduledPhysicalStage.text: For a fixed parent and the same physical approximation with its qualitative properties, this structure stores one Fourier symbol and truncation together with its cutoff bounds, physical wave bounds, pullback jets, and central derivative estimate. Its numerical fields relate these constants, radius, carrier, and exponent to the common schedule. It supplies evidence needed by stage closure; the record does not manufacture that evidence.
TorusEuler.ScheduledPhysicalStage.summary: One approximation and cutoff share every closing estimate

TorusEuler.ScheduledPhysicalStage.of_act.text: Fix a parent stage, its flow, a finite approximate solution and a Fourier-truncated child on $[0,T_{\rm child}]$. Assume the numerical scale inequalities and estimates for the cutoff tail, velocity, residual, localized oscillation, mean correction, pressure Hessian, spatial derivatives after composition with the parent flow, and central gradient error. The formal construction then produces the scheduled next-stage data for these same fields. Its cutoff frequency is $\lambda_{i+1}^5$, using $\lambda_{i+1}=\lambda_i^{K(q_{i+1})}$. This is a conditional conversion of already constructed analytic objects, not the frequency recurrence by itself or an existence proof for its assumptions. Several imported collections of bounds are named but not defined in the supplied files, so their full expansion cannot be recovered here.
TorusEuler.ScheduledPhysicalStage.of_act.summary: The actual approximation supplies the scheduled inductive data

TorusEuler.ScheduledPhysicalVelocityBoun.text: A proposition bundling the cutoff-depth velocity size, oscillation supremum bound, low-order mean Hölder bounds and central derivative-error bound for one physical approximation. The center estimate is restricted to the active slab; the other estimates hold on the full slab. The two scalar parameters are the already chosen step and mean costs.
TorusEuler.ScheduledPhysicalVelocityBoun.summary: The actual velocity carries four scheduled estimates

TorusEuler.SelectedPhysicalStageSeed.text: Records the central wave, carrier pullback, positive normalized weight, envelope inactivity, relay identities and leading-profile bounds for one actual physical approximation. Its active interval is $[t_0,T]$ with $0\le t_0<T$, sharing the parent's right endpoint and possibly starting at zero. These are the common inputs used to estimate first and later waves through the same measured levels.
TorusEuler.SelectedPhysicalStageSeed.summary: The same central wave measures every selected profile

TorusEuler.SelectedPhysicalStageSeed.exi.text: Constructs a `ScheduledPhysicalStage` with the dyadic symbol from one selected seed and its measured hierarchy levels. The hypotheses include coefficient bounds, a numerical budget, parent Bernstein estimates, a cutoff witness, the residual bound and a one-sided pressure increment bound. The proof derives velocity and flow estimates from those same levels and installs the same cutoff, preserving the identity of the physical fields.
TorusEuler.SelectedPhysicalStageSeed.exi.summary: Measured profiles and their estimates produce one scheduled stage

TorusEuler.SelectedPhysicalStageSeed.gam.text: Abbreviates the time weight $\lambda^{3/4}|\mathbf a(t,0)|$ of the central vector stored in a selected physical seed. The abbreviation preserves that exact function when passed to measured levels. Its positivity, continuity and upper bound belong to the seed record on the active slab, not to the abbreviation by itself.
TorusEuler.SelectedPhysicalStageSeed.gam.summary: The selected seed uses its normalized central amplitude

TorusEuler.SelectedPhysicalStageSeed.lab.text: Shows that the label covector at activation has norm equal to the child frequency. The proof identifies the transported label covector with the seed's central covector using its pullback identity and wave equation, then applies the normalization stored in the seed. The equality concerns activation, not every point or time.
TorusEuler.SelectedPhysicalStageSeed.lab.summary: The transported carrier has the prescribed activation length

TorusEuler.SelectedPhysicalStageSeed.mea.text: Forms the measured hierarchy levels from the approximation's operators, profiles, completion switch and parent residual, using the seed's own radius, phase width and time weight. The argument `hf` supplies nonnegative frequency. This abbreviation ensures recurrence estimates and physical readouts quantify over the same levels rather than independently chosen bounds.
TorusEuler.SelectedPhysicalStageSeed.mea.summary: The measured levels use the actual hierarchy fields

TorusEuler.Slab.text: This private abbreviation names the closed real interval $[0,T]$ used as the time domain for path-valued solutions. It is a set, which Lean may also coerce to the subtype of its members. The definition does not assume a positive duration; integration and ODE constructors impose the needed bound separately.

TorusEuler.SlabPath.text: This abbreviation denotes continuous maps from the closed-slab subtype to the target space. When the target is normed, compactness supplies the uniform path norm used in the ODE construction. Time values outside the interval are not part of a path's domain; extension to real time is a separate operation.

TorusEuler.SpatialHolderHalf.text:
Require C-to-order-m differentiability and bounded uniform and half-Holder increment ranges for every iterated derivative through order m. This is the lifted C-to-order-m-and-one-half regularity predicate, not an existence theorem for derivatives or inverse operators.

Default-value audit (b5): The predicate explicitly requires genuine differentiability and bounded supremum and increment ranges through the stated order. At order zero it is continuity plus bounded half-Holder behavior; it does not assert periodicity.
TorusEuler.SpatialHolderHalf.summary: The lifted spatial Holder regularity class

TorusEuler.SpatialJetTuple.text: This is the finite dependent tuple of bounded spatial jets of orders zero through `m`, indexed by `Fin (m + 1)`. It supplies a normed input space for bilinear momentum maps. The components are stored separately, so an arbitrary tuple need not satisfy the differential relations of one underlying function.
TorusEuler.SpatialJetTuple.summary: All spatial derivative orders through a fixed level

TorusEuler.SpatiallyPeriodic.text: A field on $\mathbb R^3$ is spatially periodic when $f(x+n)=f(x)$ for every $x\in\mathbb R^3$ and every $n\in\mathbb Z^3$. The formal condition allows any target space, so the same convention applies to velocity, pressure and other fields. It represents a field on $\mathbb T^3=\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$, with opposite faces of the centered cube identified. Periodicity alone imposes no continuity, differentiability, parity, incompressibility or mean-zero condition. These must be stated separately. In particular, a real wave vector in an unlocalized periodic profile does not automatically produce such a field.
TorusEuler.SpatiallyPeriodic.summary: Integer translations leave the spatial field unchanged

TorusEuler.SpatiallyPeriodic.existsUniqu.text: Every function on Euclidean labels that satisfies `SpatiallyPeriodic` factors uniquely through the quotient map to the unit three-torus. The codomain is an arbitrary type, so the statement asserts no continuity or integrability. Periodicity guarantees that choosing different representatives of a torus point produces the same value.
TorusEuler.SpatiallyPeriodic.existsUniqu.summary: A periodic lift descends uniquely to the torus

TorusEuler.SpatiallyPeriodic.exists_cont.text: A continuous spatially periodic lift descends to a continuous torus field.
TorusEuler.SpatiallyPeriodic.exists_cont.summary: A periodic continuous lift descends to the torus

TorusEuler.SpatiallyPeriodic.fderiv.text: If a field is spatially periodic and differentiable everywhere, its Fréchet derivative is periodic under the same lattice translations. The differentiability hypothesis `hf` ensures that `fderiv` is the genuine derivative throughout. This is used to extend convergence of periodic derivative fields from one centered cell to the entire lift.
TorusEuler.SpatiallyPeriodic.fderiv.summary: A differentiable periodic field has periodic spatial derivative

TorusEuler.SpatiallyPeriodic.gradient.text: For a spatially periodic scalar pressure, global differentiability makes the gradient spatially periodic as well. The proof converts the periodic Fréchet derivative to a gradient through the real inner-product duality. This supplies the period condition needed to pass from uniform gradient convergence on the centered cell to the whole space.
TorusEuler.SpatiallyPeriodic.gradient.summary: A differentiable periodic pressure has periodic gradient

TorusEuler.TerminalCostBounds.text: This predicate requires every listed cost to be at most `P.frequency i` in absolute value when its time order and depth are at most $S=7K(P.\mathrm{order}(i+2))$ and its spatial order is at most $S+\mathrm{reserve}(q,d)$. It quantifies over all stage indices and rows. The cost function and reserve are supplied arguments; this definition records their required estimates and does not construct a schedule satisfying them.
TorusEuler.TerminalCostBounds.summary: Fixed order costs bounded by the previous frequency

TorusEuler.TerminalGraphCostBounds.text: Requires graph costs with time order `q`, parent exponent `A`, and depth `d` to lie below the previous frequency when both `q` and `A` and the depth fit $S=7K(P.\mathrm{order}(i+2))$. The spatial order may additionally use `reserve (max q A) d`. This extends `TerminalCostBounds` by tracking the parent velocity exponent separately; it remains a proposition whose estimates must be supplied.
TorusEuler.TerminalGraphCostBounds.summary: Graph costs fit the common scheduled threshold

TorusEuler.TerminalGraphCostBounds.event.text: From `TerminalGraphCostBounds`, proves an eventual estimate uniformly over all rows and all spatial orders up to $\max(m_0,\mathrm{stepDepth}(i)+q+2)$. The time order `q`, parent exponent `A`, and baseline spatial order `m₀` are fixed before the stage index tends to infinity. The scheduled slow-order reserve ensures their depth and order demands eventually lie in the common threshold range.
TorusEuler.TerminalGraphCostBounds.event.summary: Every fixed graph order eventually fits the selected depth

TorusEuler.TerminalMeanParentInverseData.text: Packages fixed-time solenoidal inverses and the mixed recovery inverse for one supplied `rec`. The fields identify the operators being inverted, bound their inverse norms, record kinetic Lipschitz and supremum caps, and bound the combined recovery budget by $D^p$. The fixed-time inverse also has the direct bound $D^p$. This is data with obligations, not an existence theorem.
TorusEuler.TerminalMeanParentInverseData.summary: Two actual mean inverses with a common parent bound

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.text: Requires $\|D_x^n\partial_t^i f(t,x)\|\le C(n)A D^{pn}$ for every $i\le q$, every spatial order $n$, and all points on the closed time slab. The time derivative is `slabTimeJet`, so the spatial point is held fixed. The amplitude `A` and slope `p` are independent of `n`; `C n` may vary with spatial order. This proposition contains bounds only, with no smoothness or sign assumptions built in.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.summary: Mixed derivatives with a fixed spatial growth rate

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.add.text: Adds the mixed bounds for jointly smooth `f` and `g` on `a < b`. The inputs share time order, slope, scale, and amplitude, while their constants may differ. The sum has constant `C n + C' n`. Smoothness justifies the time and spatial derivative sum identities, after which the triangle inequality gives the estimate.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.add.summary: Add mixed bounds with a common amplitude and rate

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.apply_c.text: Applies a fixed continuous linear map `L` to a jointly smooth field with a mixed bound on `a < b`. The new bound keeps the same amplitude and spatial slope and replaces each constant by $\|L\|C(n)$. Time differentiation commutes with `L`, and its operator norm controls every spatial derivative of the output.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.apply_c.summary: A bounded linear readout preserves the mixed growth rate

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.bilinea.text: For jointly smooth `f` and `g` on `a < b`, combines their mixed bounds through time order `q` under the stated nonnegativity hypotheses. Applying the fixed bilinear map `B` multiplies amplitudes to $AA'$ and preserves the slope `p`; the constant becomes `terminalMixedProductCost`. Spatial derivative orders split across the factors, so their powers recombine as $D^{pn}$. The docstring says amplitudes are added, but the theorem's conclusion correctly multiplies them.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.bilinea.summary: Multiply amplitudes while retaining the spatial growth slope

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.congr.text: Transfers a mixed bound from `f` to `g` when `hEq` identifies their values for every time in the closed slab and every spatial point. Within-time derivatives agree on that slab, and the resulting spatial functions are equal. No equality outside the time interval and no separate regularity hypothesis are required for this congruence statement.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.congr.summary: Transfer mixed bounds across equality on the slab

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.const_s.text: Given a mixed jet bound and joint smoothness on a nondegenerate slab, multiplying the field by `r` replaces amplitude `A` by $\|r\|A$. The assumptions include nonnegative `D,A` and cost sequence. The proof passes through the continuous linear scalar map and bounds its norm, preserving the same derivative-order cost array and spatial slope.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.const_s.summary: A fixed scalar changes only the mixed-bound amplitude

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.materia.text: Given mixed bounds for `f` through `q+1` and `U` through `q`, bounds $\partial_t f+U\cdot\nabla f$ through `q`. Joint smoothness on `a < b` and all listed nonnegativity assumptions are required. The spatial slope remains `p`, while the amplitude becomes $A(1+D^pA_0)$. The new constant combines the pure time derivative with the spatially shifted bilinear advection term.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.materia.summary: One material derivative spends one time order

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.mono_am.text: Given an existing mixed bound, replaces its amplitude `A` by `A'` when `A ≤ A'`. The hypotheses `hD` and `hC` make the scale powers and order constants nonnegative, so multiplying preserves this comparison. No sign assumption on the old amplitude is stated separately. The spatial slope and the range of time derivatives remain unchanged.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.mono_am.summary: Enlarge the amplitude in every mixed derivative bound

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.mono_co.text: Replaces `C n` by the pointwise larger `C' n` in a mixed bound. The hypotheses `hD : 0 ≤ D` and `hA : 0 ≤ A` ensure that the shared multiplier is nonnegative. All time orders through `q` and the same spatial slope remain available. This theorem compares supplied bounds rather than estimating any new derivative.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.mono_co.summary: Enlarge the constants for each spatial order

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.mono_or.text: Restricts an existing mixed bound from time order `q` to `q'` under `hq : q' ≤ q`. The spatial slope, amplitude, constants, and closed slab stay fixed. It uses only the inclusion of the permitted time indices, so no positivity or smoothness assumption is added to those already present in the input predicate.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.mono_or.summary: Retain fewer time derivatives from a mixed bound

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.mono_sl.text: For `D ≥ 1`, a mixed bound with slope `p` also holds with any `p' ≥ p`. Nonnegativity of the amplitude and order constants permits comparison of $D^{pn}$ and $D^{p'n}$ at every spatial order. This is a deliberately coarser estimate, used to place different coefficient families under one common slope.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.mono_sl.summary: Increase the spatial growth slope of a mixed bound

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.of_pare.text: If each spatial derivative of a fixed time jet costs at most `C n * A * μ^(5*n)`, then for `μ ≥ 1` it also satisfies a mixed bound with scale `μ^9` and spatial slope one. Nonnegative amplitude and costs permit enlarging the power. This is a comparison of supplied bounds, not a new regularity theorem.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.of_pare.summary: Fit parent Bernstein bounds into the coefficient calculus

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.of_zero.text: Builds a mixed bound at time order zero from bounds on all spatial derivatives of `g` on the slab. The hypothesis named `h` supplies exactly these spatial inequalities. Since the only allowed time index is zero, `slabTimeJet_zero` reduces the conclusion to those inequalities. This is not a theorem asserting that the field itself vanishes.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.of_zero.summary: Spatial estimates supply the zeroth time order

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.restric.text: A mixed coefficient bound on `[a,b]` transfers to `[c,d]` when both intervals have positive length, the latter is contained in the former, and the underlying field is jointly smooth on the larger slab. The time jets defined with either closed interval agree on the smaller one, including its endpoints. The amplitude, spatial slope, and cost array remain unchanged.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.restric.summary: Restrict mixed jets to a smaller nondegenerate time slab

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.scaledA.text: Assume a smooth field has `TerminalMixedJetBound` with amplitude $D^e$ and spatial slope $p$. If `D ≥ 1`, $\ell\ge0$, and $\ell D^p\le1$, scaling labels by $\ell$ removes the spatial factor from active time derivatives. For $i\le q$, `PhaseJetBound` through $n$ is controlled by $(\sum_{m\le n}C(m))D^e$. Both the full and active intervals have positive length.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.scaledA.summary: The label radius absorbs the fixed derivative slope

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.slabTim.text: For a fixed continuous linear map `L` and a jointly smooth field `g` on `a < b`, taking any closed-slab time jet commutes with applying `L`. The conclusion is pointwise at `t ∈ Icc a b` and any spatial point. The map is independent of time, so this statement has no Leibniz terms involving derivatives of `L`.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.slabTim.summary: Time derivatives commute with a fixed bounded linear map

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.spaceDe.text: For a jointly smooth field on a nondegenerate slab `a < b`, a mixed bound for `f` gives one for its spatial Fréchet derivative. The spatial slope stays `p`, the amplitude becomes $AD^p$, and the constant at order `n` becomes `C (n+1)`. The proof commutes time and space derivatives; the regularity assumptions give those derivatives their classical meaning at the slab endpoints.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.spaceDe.summary: One spatial derivative multiplies the amplitude by its rate

TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.timeDer.text: An input bound through time order `q+1` gives a bound through `q` for the within-time derivative of the same field. The amplitude, spatial slope, and spatial constants do not change. The proof is the iteration identity for `slabTimeJet`; no extra smoothness is needed for this formal identity, although later applications use jointly smooth fields.
TorusEuler.TerminalMixedJetBound.timeDer.summary: Spend one time order without changing the spatial rate

TorusEuler.Theorem11.text: The formal assertion is the existence of smooth odd divergence-free periodic data $u_0$, a finite time $T_*>0$, and a smooth odd maximal Euler solution $u,p$ on $[0,T_*)$ with $u(0)=u_0$. It requires bounded velocity, central vorticity tending to infinity, divergence of the time integrals of the gradient and vorticity norms, and spatial $C^m$ limits of velocity and its time derivative on every compact set away from the torus origin. Pressure is normalized to have zero mean. The numbered version of Theorem 1.1 additionally states uniqueness of the maximal velocity and its lifespan. That comparison is not an explicit conjunct of this shorter assertion.
TorusEuler.Theorem11.summary: The shorter assertion collects the singularity conclusions

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.text: A truncated stage supplies continuous torus representatives of $V$ and $R_V$, a velocity $u=S_\Lambda V$, and a smooth periodic pressure $p$ of zero spatial mean on $[0,T]$. It requires $u$ smooth, odd and divergence free, with Fourier support $|\xi|\le2\Lambda$, and $\Delta p=-\operatorname{tr}((\nabla u)^2)$. Its actual momentum residual is identified both with $u_t+\mathbb P\operatorname{div}(u\otimes u)$ and with the cutoff expression in (5.58). These are conditions on the supplied objects, not an existence proof. A separate theorem constructs them from an approximate solution. No vanishing residual or quantitative cutoff error is part of this declaration.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.summary: Record the cutoff fields and their exact residual relation

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.CutoffBou.text: Bundles all spatial tail estimates through depth `P`, the order-two tail estimate, the order-one true residual estimate, and the order-zero pressure-Hessian difference estimate. All are pointwise in time on the child slab. A common pair of constants controls the residual and pressure; the error uses the spatial norm of that time slice.
TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.CutoffBou.summary: The cutoff tail residual and pressure estimates together

TorusEuler.TruncatedChildStage.PulledBac.text: Records joint smoothness of the parent-coframe pullback after adding the actual cutoff tail. The oscillatory part has a scaled jet bound through order two of size $B \cdot  D^p \cdot  \mathrm{freq}^{-5/4}$; the phase mean has a bound through order one of size $B \cdot  D^p \cdot  \mathrm{freq}^{-5/2}$. These measured hypotheses feed the child-flow estimate.
