It first obtains completeness from the closedness of endpointTorusSpace T, then uses the Hilbert-space projection instance. The subspace already contains both endpoint constraints. This declaration supplies the operator's existence in Lean, rather than a formula for its action or a regularity estimate.

TorusEuler.endpointJointSpatialProjectio.text: For $T>0$, consider square-integrable vector fields on $[0,T]\times\mathbb T^3$. Orthogonal projection onto spatially divergence-free fields commutes with $\mathcal Qv=v-T^{-1}\int_0^Tv(s)\,ds$. Thus their composition projects onto fields satisfying both constraints. This justifies $\mathcal R=\mathbb P\mathcal Q$ in Appendix A; the paper uses the special case $T=1$. The assertion is in the space-time $L^2$ space, where fields that agree almost everywhere represent the same field. Hölder-space versions require their separate compatibility results.
TorusEuler.endpointJointSpatialProjectio.summary: Interchange spatial projection and subtraction of the time mean

TorusEuler.endpointJointSpatialSolenoida.text: This submodule consists of joint $L^2$ fields annihilated by every bounded measurable time test η and smooth periodic scalar potential p. The kernels express weak spatial divergence zero. The definition imposes no zero time mean and no continuity in time. Its intersection-of-kernels form makes closedness available from continuity of each test functional.
TorusEuler.endpointJointSpatialSolenoida.summary: Joint fields with zero spatial divergence

TorusEuler.endpointJointSpatialSolenoida.text: This private instance gives the joint solenoidal submodule an orthogonal projection. Its closedness makes it complete as a subspace of joint $L^2$, after which the standard Hilbert-space instance applies. The declaration constructs typeclass evidence for every T; it neither adds an extra divergence assumption nor chooses a smooth representative.
TorusEuler.endpointJointSpatialSolenoida.summary: Orthogonal projection onto the solenoidal space

TorusEuler.endpointJointSubtractMean.text: On the joint $L^2$ space, this defines $Q=I-T^{-1}J^*J$, where J is time integration, not the primitive from zero to a variable time. Thus $J^*J$ lifts the time integral back as a constant path. The definition accepts hT : 0 ≤ T; later projection and range results impose strict positivity when cancelling the slab length.

TorusEuler.endpointJointSubtractMean_app.text: Applying the mean-removal operator to u expands to $u-T^{-1}J^*(Ju)$. This is an equality of joint $L^2$ elements, proved by unfolding the definition. The hypothesis is only hT : 0 ≤ T. Representative formulas and the conclusion that the result has zero integral are separate declarations, so this rewrite alone supplies neither.

Mean removal agrees almost everywhere with $u(t,a)-T^{-1}(Ju)(a)$. Here Ju is the spatial $L^2$ class obtained by integrating in time, and its chosen representative appears on the right. The theorem assumes $0\le T$, unlike the strict-positive projection theorem, because it only identifies two representatives of the same total operator.

TorusEuler.endpointJointSubtractMean_end.text: For a spatial half-Hölder family w of $L^2$ time paths, subtracting the mean after embedding into joint $L^2$ equals embedding after subtracting the mean at every label. The binder hT : 0 ≤ T is sufficient. The proof compares almost-everywhere slices and their integrals; it does not promote an $L^2$ path to continuity in time.
TorusEuler.endpointJointSubtractMean_end.summary: Mean removal respects the mixed embedding

TorusEuler.endpointJointSubtractMean_isS.text: For a positive slab, mean removal is idempotent and symmetric for the real $L^2$ inner product. The result packages those properties as LinearMap.IsSymmetricProjection; it does not yet identify the range. Idempotence uses the zero integral of the projected field, while symmetry follows from the adjoint expression $I-T^{-1}J^*J$.

TorusEuler.endpointJointSubtractMean_pre.text: Subtracting the time mean keeps a jointly solenoidal field inside the same submodule. The integral is spatially solenoidal, its adjoint lift is jointly solenoidal, and submodule closure handles the scaled subtraction. The statement allows hT : 0 ≤ T; it proves preservation even before the stricter hypothesis used to identify $Q$ as a projection.
TorusEuler.endpointJointSubtractMean_pre.summary: Mean removal preserves zero spatial divergence

TorusEuler.endpointJoint_eq_of_slices.text: Two joint L² fields are equal if their time slices agree almost everywhere at almost every spatial label. The proof uses measurability of the equality set and exchanges the order of the almost-everywhere quantifiers. This is the uniqueness principle that makes the subsequent chosen joint representative construction canonical as an L² class.
TorusEuler.endpointJoint_eq_of_slices.summary: Almost everywhere agreement of paths determines a joint field

TorusEuler.endpointJoint_eq_zero_of_four.text: If every real time-valued Fourier coefficient of `v` vanishes for all frequencies and complex phases, then `v = 0` in joint L². The proof uses only phases giving cosine and sine and a countable family of frequencies to obtain simultaneous almost-everywhere slice identities. Spatial Fourier uniqueness then applies at almost every time.
TorusEuler.endpointJoint_eq_zero_of_four.summary: Time valued Fourier coefficients determine a joint L² field

TorusEuler.endpointJoint_norm_sq_of_slic.text: Suppose `hf` identifies the time path `f a` with the joint field `v` almost everywhere in time for almost every label. Then the squared joint norm equals the Haar integral of the squared path norms. Fubini applies to the already square-integrable joint field; the conclusion does not assume arbitrary pointwise representatives are jointly measurable.
TorusEuler.endpointJoint_norm_sq_of_slic.summary: Joint energy is the integral of the path energies

TorusEuler.endpointJoint_sub_slices.text: Given slice representations `hv` and `hu` of two joint fields by path families `f` and `g`, the path difference represents their joint difference almost everywhere in both variables. The proof tracks the representative rules for subtraction in each L² space. This permits joint norm differences to be estimated through labelwise path differences.
TorusEuler.endpointJoint_sub_slices.summary: Subtraction agrees between joint fields and their path slices

TorusEuler.endpointL2Complexification.text: Assemble the real embedding and both projections into an `EndpointComplexification` for L² vector fields over `μ`. All required identities have been proved on equivalence classes, including squared-norm splitting. This permits the same operator-extension machinery to treat the finite-dimensional spatial case and the infinite-dimensional time-path case.
TorusEuler.endpointL2Complexification.summary: Entire vector valued L² spaces admit complexification

TorusEuler.endpointL2Energy.text: For $T\ge0$ and continuous operator fields $F,M$ on $[0,T]$, put $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$. For $v\in L^2([0,T];E)$, the defined energy is $\|Fv\|_{L^2}^2+\langle\Omega v,Jv\rangle_{L^2}$. With $F=D_aX$ and $z=Jv$, this is $\int(Kz_t\cdot z_t+\Omega z_t\cdot z)$ from §4.2. No zero-time-mean condition or positive lower bound is included in the definition. Such conditions enter the coercivity theorem, where $Jv$ becomes a displacement vanishing at both endpoints. Here $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$.
TorusEuler.endpointL2Energy.summary: Evaluate the energy on an arbitrary square-integrable path

TorusEuler.endpointL2Energy_coercive.text: On $0<T\le1$, suppose $F_t=MF$, $M_t$ is continuous, $GF=I$, $\|G\|\le D\ge1$, $\|M\|\le L$ with $L\ge0$, and $\langle-(M_t+M^2)w,w\rangle\le|w|^2$. For every $v\in L^2$ with $\int_0^Tv=0$, put $z=Jv$, $K=F^TF$ and $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$. Then $\int(Kv\cdot v+\Omega v\cdot z)\ge[2D^2(1+L)^2]^{-1}\|v\|_{L^2}^2$. This supplies the positive constant used in Theorem 4.2. The formal statement works in any complete real Hilbert space, with operator fields not necessarily arising from a flow. Here $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$.
TorusEuler.endpointL2Energy_coercive.summary: Control the label velocity by its displacement energy

TorusEuler.endpointL2Energy_eq_integral.text: If `g` agrees almost everywhere with the $L^2$ path `v`, the quadratic energy equals the integral of the label energy evaluated at `g` and its time primitive. The hypothesis `hT : 0 ≤ T` fixes the orientation of the interval integral. Multipliers and primitives are compared almost everywhere, so the statement is independent of the chosen representative.
TorusEuler.endpointL2Energy_eq_integral.summary: The Hilbert-space energy equals the label integral

TorusEuler.endpointL2Multiplier.text: Construct a continuous linear map from one $L^2$ space to another by multiplying by an almost-everywhere strongly measurable, essentially bounded operator field. The field is first bundled in $L^\infty$, then the Hölder bilinear map acts on it. The construction respects equivalence classes rather than assigning a canonical pointwise output everywhere.
TorusEuler.endpointL2Multiplier.summary: Pointwise coefficient multiplication on the L² quotient

TorusEuler.endpointL2Multiplier_apply_ae.text: For any $L^2$ input, a representative of the bundled multiplier output equals the coefficient applied to the input representative almost everywhere. This is the precise link between the quotient-space operator and the pointwise formula. It makes no claim about equality at every time, which would depend on chosen representatives.
TorusEuler.endpointL2Multiplier_apply_ae.summary: The quotient multiplier agrees almost everywhere with pointwise action

TorusEuler.endpointL2Multiplier_apply_to.text: For a representative `v` with proof `hv` of square integrability, applying the bundled coefficient multiplier to `hv.toLp v` equals bundling the pointwise product using its established integrability proof. The equality is in the $L^2$ quotient. It removes differences between two ways of constructing the same equivalence class.
TorusEuler.endpointL2Multiplier_apply_to.summary: Bundling before or after multiplication gives the same class

TorusEuler.endpointL2Operator.text: This is the fixed-label operator $B=K-J\Omega$ on $L^2$ time paths. Here $K=F^*F$, $\Omega=F^*(M^*-M)F$, and J is the forward time primitive. The assumptions cF and cM give continuity on the closed slab, making the multipliers bounded. The operator acts on all paths before restriction to zero time mean.

TorusEuler.endpointLabelEnergy.text: For arbitrary bounded operators `F` and `M`, form the label energy $\langle F^*Fv,v\rangle+\langle F^*(M^*-M)Fv,z\rangle$. In the application, `F` is the flow derivative and `v` is the label velocity. The definition itself assumes no flow equation or coercivity; those hypotheses belong to subsequent identities and estimates.
TorusEuler.endpointLabelEnergy.summary: The kinetic and vorticity terms in label coordinates

TorusEuler.endpointLabelEnergy_coercive.text: Let $0\le T\le1$, let $F_t=MF$, $M_t$ be continuous, and let $z_t=v$ with continuous $v$ and $z(0)=z(T)=0$. Assume $H^\#=-(M_t+M^2)\le I$ as a quadratic form. Put $\xi=Fz$, $K=F^TF$ and $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$. The formal statement proves $\int_0^T(Kv\cdot v+\Omega v\cdot z)\,dt\ge\frac12\int_0^T|M\xi+Fv|^2\,dt$. Here $M\xi+Fv=\xi_t$. It is a result for one label, valid also in a real Hilbert space. The displayed inequality (1.9) includes a further integration over labels, and the weak-path version requires its own extension from continuously differentiable paths.
TorusEuler.endpointLabelEnergy_coercive.summary: The label energy controls the derivative of the physical displacement

TorusEuler.endpointLabelEnergy_coercive_.text: Under the flow derivative equations, both endpoint conditions for `z`, $0\le T\le1$, `D ≥ 1`, and `L ≥ 0`, obtain the lower bound $[2D^2(1+L)^2]^{-1}\int\|v\|^2$. `hGF` is the explicit left-inverse relation; `hGbound`, `hMbound`, and `hupper` supply inverse, gradient, and Hessian bounds. This is a one-label C¹ estimate, before density gives the weak formulation.
TorusEuler.endpointLabelEnergy_coercive_.summary: The endpoint form controls the label velocity energy

TorusEuler.endpointLabelEnergy_eq.text: For operators $F,M,N$ and vectors $z,v$ in a real Hilbert space, set $\xi=Fz$, $\eta=M\xi+Fv$, $H=-(N+M^2)$, $K=F^TF$ and $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$. Then $Kv\cdot v+\Omega v\cdot z=|\eta|^2-H\xi\cdot\xi-(\eta\cdot M\xi+\xi\cdot N\xi+\xi\cdot M\eta)$. When $F_t=MF$, $z_t=v$, and $N=M_t$, the parenthesized expression is $\partial_t(\xi\cdot M\xi)$. This is the algebra behind (4.7); differentiability and vanishing endpoint values are not hypotheses of this algebraic identity.
TorusEuler.endpointLabelEnergy_eq.summary: Separate the kinetic term from the boundary derivative

TorusEuler.endpointMeanUnitIntegral.text: Packages integration of continuous vector functions on $[0,1]$ as a continuous linear map with operator norm at most one. The function is extended to the real line by clamping with `projIcc`; the integral only sees the original interval. This bounded map lets the joint primitive proof differentiate a curve of continuous functions.

TorusEuler.endpointMixedCoefficient.text: Turn a jointly indexed coefficient into a spatial half-Hölder field of bounded operators on time L². Time measurability at every label, uniform value and spatial increment bounds on the slab, and `hM : 0 ≤ M` are explicit inputs. The output acts on entire time paths by multiplication at each label.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedCoefficient.summary: Bundle the coefficients as a half Hölder operator field

TorusEuler.endpointMixedCoefficientMul_r.text: Suppose `hΩ` identifies a mixed operator field with multiplication by the joint coefficient `ω` on every time path, almost everywhere in labels. If `hw` represents the input joint field, then mixed multiplication represents the joint $L^2$ multiplier output. Both representation assumptions are retained explicitly; regularity of the operator field is not proved here.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedCoefficientMul_r.summary: Mixed multiplication represents the joint coefficient action

TorusEuler.endpointMixedCoefficientSolve.text: This specialization builds the mixed coefficients from `K` and `Ω`, using their time-slice measurability, nonnegative uniform bounds, and spatial half-Hölder bounds. With positive `T`, the combined Fourier law for `P` turns a projected mixed solution into the joint weak solution. The coefficient hypotheses are supplied here rather than inferred from arbitrary measurable fields.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedCoefficientSolve.summary: Concrete coefficient data produce the same weak solution

TorusEuler.endpointMixedCoefficient_appl.text: Evaluating the mixed coefficient at a label and applying it to a time path agrees almost everywhere with the original matrix field acting pointwise in time. This identifies the bundled path-operator field with `K`. It allows later mixed-space algebra to be compared directly with the original joint endpoint equation.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedCoefficient_appl.summary: The mixed coefficient still acts by timewise multiplication

TorusEuler.endpointMixedCoefficient_eval.text: A uniform pointwise bound `C` for `K` yields the same operator-norm bound for its temporal multiplier at each label. Other bounds `M` and `hKdif` are used only to construct the mixed half-Hölder coefficient. The independent parameter `C` permits a sharper supremum estimate than the combined construction budget.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedCoefficient_eval.summary: A pointwise coefficient bound controls each path operator

TorusEuler.endpointMixedCoefficient_hasS.text: If two coefficient curves form a spatial derivative pair at every slab time, their derivative curve has a uniform half-Hölder bound, and the mixed operators have the prescribed time actions at every label, the mixed coefficient fields form the same spatial derivative pair. The proof controls difference quotients in temporal operator norm, rather than relying only on pointwise convergence.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedCoefficient_hasS.summary: Pointwise coefficient jets become mixed operator jets

TorusEuler.endpointMixedCoefficient_slic.text: If every fixed-label time slice of a coefficient is continuous on $[0,T]$, each slice is almost-everywhere strongly measurable for the measure on $(0,T]$. Compactness and restriction to a measurable subinterval supply the result. This converts the coefficient regularity into the measurability required by the temporal $L^2$ construction.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedCoefficient_slic.summary: Continuous label slices define measurable path multipliers

TorusEuler.endpointMixedCorrection.text:
Sum coefficient-times-velocity products over all ordered derivative-word pairs in which at least one derivative acts on the coefficient. The coefficient-free highest velocity derivative is excluded from this correction.

Default-value audit (b5): The empty word has zero correction because its pair list is empty. The formula is a total finite sum for arbitrary word-indexed coefficient and field families; derivative meaning is supplied by later hypotheses.

TorusEuler.endpointMixedCorrectionPairs.text:
Enumerate pairs of ordered derivative words in which the coefficient word is nonempty. The recursion preserves repeated terms, so it retains the multiplicities needed by iterated product differentiation.

Default-value audit (b5): The empty word gives the empty list. Repeated derivative directions can yield repeated pairs, which are intentionally retained as product-rule multiplicities rather than removed.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedCorrectionPairs.summary: Ordered product rule terms with a coefficient derivative

TorusEuler.endpointMixedCorrectionPairs_.text: The correction list for a derivative word of length $n$ contains exactly $2^n-1$ entries, counted with multiplicity. The missing entry is the term with no derivative on the coefficient. This list count, rather than a count of distinct word pairs, controls the finite sum in the triangular derivative estimate.

Membership in `endpointMixedCorrectionPairs t` implies that the coefficient word is nonempty, the two word lengths add to `t.length`, and the unknown word is strictly shorter. This is the structural fact making the derivative recursion triangular. It identifies which terms may already be known when constructing the next derivative.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedCorrectionPairs_.summary: Every commutator term has a lower order unknown

TorusEuler.endpointMixedCorrectionPairs_.text: Both words in any correction pair are sublists of the original derivative word. Consequently a correction of a sorted word uses sorted subwords, with no new coordinate directions. This combinatorial fact allows the physical derivative recurrence to be restricted to canonical multi-indices while retaining the exact Leibniz multiplicities.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedCorrectionPairs_.summary: Correction words remain within the original multi-index

TorusEuler.endpointMixedCorrectionPairs_.text: Separate the first new coefficient derivative from the two ways to differentiate each existing correction term. This finite-sum identity supports induction on derivative-word length.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedCorrectionPairs_.summary: The next product rule correction from the previous one

TorusEuler.endpointMixedCorrection_congr.text: If the families `v` and `w` agree at every word shorter than `t`, their mixed correction at `t` is equal. The coefficient family `B` is unchanged. The proof uses the strict lower-order property of correction pairs, which ensures that the recursive construction never depends on an unknown derivative of the current order.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedCorrection_congr.summary: Lower order agreement determines the commutator

TorusEuler.endpointMixedCorrection_hasDe.text: Assume coefficient derivatives through word length `t.length` and unknown derivatives strictly below that length. Differentiating the mixed correction in direction `u i` gives the sum of the two product-rule terms for each correction pair. The two different length thresholds are explicit and are what allow induction on derivative order.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedCorrection_hasDe.summary: Differentiate all lower order correction products

TorusEuler.endpointMixedCorrection_hasSp.text: Differentiate every correction term by the product rule under the supplied coefficient and lower-velocity derivative hypotheses. Ordered word multiplicities are preserved rather than simplified combinatorially.

TorusEuler.endpointMixedCorrection_pathC.text: The Leibniz correction for the path coefficient K minus J Omega equals the K correction minus the time primitive of the Omega correction. This follows term by term from linearity of the finite sum and the primitive.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedCorrection_pathC.summary: Splitting the mixed spatial correction into two parts

TorusEuler.endpointMixedIntegration.text:
Define the mixed integration operator by applying the bounded temporal L2 primitive to each label value. It preserves the spatial half-Holder class by bounded linear functoriality.

Default-value audit (b5): The nonnegative duration is part of the input. The operator integrates L2 classes at each label and is zero on a zero-length interval; no continuity in time is asserted by the definition.

TorusEuler.endpointMixedJointValue.text: Select a joint L² realization of the half-Hölder path field using the proved existence theorem. The choice is noncomputable, but slice agreement determines the joint equivalence class uniquely. This intermediate value is later shown linear and bounded before it is packaged as the mixed-to-joint continuous linear map.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedJointValue.summary: Choose the joint realization of a mixed field

TorusEuler.endpointMixedJointValue_slice.text: The selected joint L² field agrees with the mixed field’s time paths almost everywhere in time at almost every label. This is the `choose_spec` property of the existence theorem. It is the only representative specification needed for the later norm, linearity, and embedding compatibility proofs.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedJointValue_slice.summary: The chosen joint field realizes the mixed time paths

TorusEuler.endpointMixedJoint_exists.text: Every spatial half-Hölder field with values in time L² admits a joint L² realization with the prescribed paths almost everywhere in labels and time. Continuity provides strong measurability and the half-Hölder norm bounds all path norms. The theorem supplies existence before the next definition selects a realization.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedJoint_exists.summary: A half Hölder family of paths has a joint realization

TorusEuler.endpointMixedPathCoefficient.text: At each spatial label, let $K$ and $\Omega$ be bounded operators on $L^2([0,T];\mathbb R^3)$, varying half-Hölder continuously with the label, and take $T\ge0$. Define $B=K-J\Omega$, where $J$ integrates a time path from zero. Thus $J$ acts after $\Omega$. When these operators are multiplication by the time-dependent matrices, this is $Bv=Kv-J(\Omega v)$ in Appendix A. The formula does not impose zero time mean, divergence freedom or coercivity; those are separate ingredients in the projected equation $\mathcal RBv=-\mathcal RL$.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedPathCoefficient.summary: Define the coefficient after integrating the vorticity term

TorusEuler.endpointMixedPathCoefficient_.text: Pointwise multiplication by the labelwise path coefficient K minus J Omega is exactly the mixed product operator. This identifies two representations of the same compressed equation.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedPathCoefficient_.summary: The mixed path coefficient gives the integrated operator

TorusEuler.endpointMixedPathCoefficient_.text: The mixed path coefficient has lower bound $[2D^2(1+L)^2]^{-1}\|v\|^2$ on every zero-time-mean path. Besides the coefficient action identities, the theorem assumes $0<T\le1$, deformation evolution, the inverse bound and the quadratic Hessian upper bound. No nonzero spatial-frequency restriction appears, so the estimate also applies to the spatial constant mode.

Evaluating the mixed coefficient at a fixed label gives the temporal operator $K(a)-J\circ\Omega(a)$. Here `J` is the bounded primitive on $L^2((0,T])$, not a scalar coefficient. The identity holds for every label and nonnegative duration, and exposes the operator to which spatial freezing will be applied.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedPathCoefficient_.summary: The path coefficient is multiplication minus integration

TorusEuler.endpointMixedPathCoefficient_.text: If `K` and `Ω` have torus directional derivatives `dK` and `dΩ`, then the path coefficient $K-J\Omega$ has derivative $dK-Jd\Omega$. The temporal primitive is a fixed bounded linear operator, so it commutes with this spatial differentiation. Nonnegative duration is the only time assumption needed here.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedPathCoefficient_.summary: Spatial differentiation passes through the primitive coefficient

TorusEuler.endpointMixedPathCoefficient_.text: For a temporal path with zero integral, pairing $K-J\Omega$ against that path equals the endpoint energy. The hypotheses `hK` and `hΩ` require the mixed operators to act as the physical kinetic and vorticity coefficients almost everywhere. The primitive adjoint identity changes the minus sign into the plus sign in the label energy.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedPathCoefficient_.summary: The path pairing recovers the positive label form

TorusEuler.endpointMixedPathCoefficient_.text: On $[0,1]$, let $v\in L^2$ have zero integral. Suppose the supplied operators on paths agree almost everywhere with multiplication by the matrices $K(t,a)$ and $\Omega(t,a)$ at a fixed label. Then $\langle(K-J\Omega)v,v\rangle_{L^2}=\int_0^1(Kv\cdot v+\Omega v\cdot Jv)\,dt$. This uses the adjoint identity for $J$ on a zero-mean second argument. It is the equality preceding Appendix A.1. The lower bound by $\mu\|v\|_{L^2}^2$ is not concluded here; it must come from the separate displacement energy hypothesis. Here $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedPathCoefficient_.summary: Identify the integrated operator with displacement energy

TorusEuler.endpointMixedPrimitive_apply_.text: Assume `hw` says the mixed half-Hölder field of time paths represents the joint field labelwise almost everywhere. At each specified time in the closed slab, evaluating the mixed primitive and embedding spatially agrees almost everywhere in labels with the primitive of the joint representative. Integration removes the input time-representative ambiguity.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedPrimitive_apply_.summary: Mixed and joint time primitives agree at each time

TorusEuler.endpointMixedPrimitive_contin.text: A representative obtained by applying a bounded operator to primitive evaluation is continuous on the closed interval and has the stated square-root-duration norm bound. This proves continuity of the Volterra term before the velocity is known to be continuous.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedPrimitive_contin.summary: Continuity and size of the mixed primitive

TorusEuler.endpointMixedPrimitive_eq_end.text: A continuous half-Holder curve agreeing with a mixed field almost everywhere has exactly the same Banach-valued primitive at every closed-interval time. This identifies recovered displacements independently of representative choices.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedPrimitive_eq_end.summary: The mixed and continuous primitives coincide

TorusEuler.endpointMixedPrimitive_eq_of_.text: A mixed time-path field and its continuous half-Hölder spatial representative have identical primitives at every time in the closed interval. The input comparison is only almost everywhere after embedding into spatial $L^2$. Integration and continuity upgrade that comparison to an equality of half-Hölder fields, including at the two time endpoints.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedPrimitive_eq_of_.summary: Both representatives give the same primitive at every time

TorusEuler.endpointMixedPrimitive_eq_spa.text: Under `hw`, the embedded mixed primitive at almost every time equals the spatial slice of the joint $L^2$ primitive. The theorem supplies a proof that each such time lies in the closed slab. This distinction matters: the mixed primitive is evaluated at a genuine time, while the joint slice is initially only almost-everywhere data.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedPrimitive_eq_spa.summary: Mixed integration agrees with joint spatial slices

TorusEuler.endpointMixedPrimitive_termin.text: With nonnegative `T` and the representation hypothesis `hw`, evaluating the mixed primitive at terminal time and embedding into spatial $L^2$ gives `endpointTorusTimeIntegral hT v`. This is the compatibility needed to recover the terminal displacement condition from zero time mean. The conclusion is equality of spatial equivalence classes.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedPrimitive_termin.summary: The terminal primitive equals the weak time integral

TorusEuler.endpointMixedProductOperator.text:
Define the operator K applied pointwise minus the time primitive of Omega applied pointwise on the mixed Holder space. This is the ambient operator before compression by the combined projection.

Default-value audit (b5): The nonnegative duration supplies the bounded primitive. The formula is valid for any mixed coefficients and is zero on the trivial duration-zero path space; coercivity and invertibility are not part of the definition.

TorusEuler.endpointMixedProjectedPrimiti.text: For almost every slab time, the weak projection of the joint primitive equals the embedded strong projection of the mixed primitive evaluation. The theorem supplies membership of that time in the closed interval.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedProjectedPrimiti.summary: The projected primitive agrees in both representations

TorusEuler.endpointMixedProjectedSolve_t.text: If `v` is fixed by `P` and `hr` says the projected residual $Bv+L$ vanishes, compatibility of both `P` and `B` with joint $L^2$ yields a constrained weak solution. The right side is $-L$, as retained in the conclusion. The theorem transports an existing solution; it does not assert a new inverse estimate.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedProjectedSolve_t.summary: A projected Hölder solution satisfies the joint weak equation

TorusEuler.endpointMixedProjection_commu.text: For positive `T`, suppose `hP` gives the combined angular-time symbol on all real-character moments of the bounded mixed operator `P`. Embedding `P w` into joint $L^2$ then gives the orthogonal joint constraint projection of the embedded field. The Fourier law is the evidence identifying the strong and weak projections.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedProjection_commu.summary: The mixed Fourier projection matches the joint constraint projection

TorusEuler.endpointMixedResidual_project.text: Averaging the joint L2 residual in time and applying the weak projection gives the embedding of its strong half-Holder projected mean. The identity also holds at duration zero by totalized normalization.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedResidual_project.summary: The mean residual agrees in strong and weak spaces

TorusEuler.endpointMixedSourceJetLp_norm.text: For nonnegative duration and bound `C`, a temporal path bounded almost everywhere by `C` has $L^2$ norm at most $\sqrt T\,C$. This local copy of the finite-measure estimate is used for source-jet difference quotients. It supplies the duration factor missing from a mere pointwise remainder estimate.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedSourceJetLp_norm.summary: A uniform source bound controls its temporal L² norm

TorusEuler.endpointMixedSource_hasSpatia.text: Compatible mixed source fields inherit the spatial derivative relation of their time-slice curves, provided the derivative curve has a uniform half-Hölder bound. The representation hypotheses hold at every label and almost everywhere in time. The proof bounds the temporal $L^2$ remainder by $\sqrt T$ times the pointwise bound, then identifies the derivative from its vanishing error.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedSource_hasSpatia.summary: Pointwise source jets become mixed path jets

TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint.text:
Construct a norm-nonincreasing linear embedding from half-Holder label fields of temporal L2 paths into joint time-label L2. Its slice identities ensure that the embedding does not depend on a pointwise choice of L2 representative.

Default-value audit (b5): The joint field is built through measurable L2 representatives, but the resulting L2 class and its labelwise almost-everywhere slice identities are fixed by the input. At nonpositive duration the time measure and target path spaces are trivial.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint.summary: Embedding mixed Holder fields into joint integral space

TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_apply_ae.text: For almost every label, the joint embedding's time path agrees almost everywhere with the mixed field evaluated at that label.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_apply_ae.summary: The joint embedding has the expected time slices

TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_coeffici.text: With the additional joint measurability hypothesis `hKjoint`, embedding the mixed coefficient product equals applying the joint L² multiplier to the embedded input. Slice representations identify both outputs almost everywhere. The theorem applies equally to the kinetic and vorticity coefficients, provided each meets the explicit uniform bounds.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_coeffici.summary: Coefficient multiplication commutes with the mixed embedding

TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_eq_proje.text: Suppose mixed fields `w` and `u` have real Fourier moments related by the combined symbol at every frequency and phase. For positive `T`, embedding `u` equals the joint orthogonal projection of embedded `w`. Fourier separation proves equality, so compatibility can be checked entirely through mode formulas rather than arbitrary representatives.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_eq_proje.summary: The mixed symbol formula identifies the weak projection

TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_injectiv.text: Equal joint L2 images imply equal mixed fields. Almost-everywhere equality of labelwise L2 paths becomes everywhere equality because those paths depend continuously on the torus label.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_injectiv.summary: The mixed to joint embedding is injective

TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_inner_eq.text: The inner product after passing from label-valued time paths to joint space-time $L^2$ equals the pairing after the Haar embedding into label $L^2$. Both expressions integrate the same pointwise inner products, with the integration order handled by the mixed-space isometry. This preserves the energy calculation across the two representations.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_inner_eq.summary: The two mixed Hilbert realizations have the same pairing

TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_integrat.text: For nonnegative duration, embedding the mixed primitive into joint L2 yields the joint primitive at fixed labels. The proof uses slice agreement and invariance of the integral under almost-everywhere equality.

TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_mul_of_a.text: The assumption `hCm` identifies the action of the mixed coefficient `Cmix` on time paths with the jointly measurable bounded coefficient `C` at almost every label. Under this compatibility, embedding `Cmix v` into joint $L^2$ equals the product multiplier applied after embedding. The explicit action hypothesis prevents identifying unrelated coefficient encodings.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_mul_of_a.summary: Coefficient multiplication agrees in both mixed representations

TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_norm_eq_.text: The joint space-time $L^2$ norm of a label-valued time-path field equals its norm under the Haar embedding. The two realizations differ only in how the product integration is represented. This equality transfers the weak contraction estimate for the mixed constraint projection into the form required by the spatial bootstrap.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_norm_eq_.summary: Both mixed representations have the same Hilbert norm

TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_norm_sq.text: For the bundled mixed-to-joint embedding, the squared joint norm is exactly the Haar integral of the squared norms of the labelwise time paths. This is an energy identity rather than equality with the full half-Hölder norm. Spatial Hölder variation is additional information not measured by the joint L² norm.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_norm_sq.summary: The mixed embedding preserves integrated path energy

TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_productO.text: For nonnegative `T`, bounded measurable coefficients `K` and `Ω`, and compatible mixed coefficient actions `hKm` and `hΩm`, the mixed operator $K-JΩ$ intertwines with the joint product operator. The proof combines multiplication compatibility with the primitive comparison. This establishes that the two endpoint equations describe the same integrated residual.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_productO.summary: The integrated operator agrees with its weak product form

TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_productO.text: If `Kmix` and `Ωmix` act as the physical coefficient multipliers on almost every label slice, their mixed product operator embeds into the joint $L^2$ flow operator. The equality is an equality of $L^2$ elements, established through almost-everywhere representatives. It connects the Hölder-in-label construction with the weak space-time equation used for uniqueness.

TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_terminal.text: At terminal time, spatially embedding the primitive of a mixed path field equals taking the joint field’s weak time integral. The theorem assumes `T ≥ 0` so terminal evaluation lies in the closed slab. This compatibility converts zero time mean of the weak velocity into the desired final-displacement condition.
TorusEuler.endpointMixedToJoint_terminal.summary: The terminal mixed primitive is the joint time integral

TorusEuler.endpointModeWeight.text: At a joint point, multiply the identity operator on real three-vectors by the value of a fixed continuous spatial character. The coefficient depends only on the label, not time. It is the bounded multiplication field used to insert a time path as a separated spatial Fourier mode.
TorusEuler.endpointModeWeight.summary: A spatial character acts as scalar multiplication

TorusEuler.endpointModeWeight_aestrongly.text: The scalar identity coefficient associated with a continuous spatial character is almost-everywhere strongly measurable for the joint measure. It is continuous as a function of the label coordinate and constant in time. This provides the measurability certificate required by the L² multiplier used in mode insertion.
TorusEuler.endpointModeWeight_aestrongly.summary: The character weight is measurable in time and space

TorusEuler.endpointOperatorEval.text: Bundle evaluation of a continuous linear operator on a vector as a continuous bilinear map. Its two arguments are the operator and the vector, in that order. This allows Mathlib's Hölder construction to multiply an essentially bounded operator field by an $L^2$ vector field and obtain an $L^2$ output.
TorusEuler.endpointOperatorEval.summary: Operator evaluation as a bounded bilinear map

TorusEuler.endpointParityPart.text: Defines half the sum of a field and its reflected field multiplied by `sign`. At sign minus one this is the odd component; at sign one it is the even component. The function is defined for any real sign, so the docstring’s word projection should be understood only for the two parity choices.
TorusEuler.endpointParityPart.summary: The odd or even component under spatial reflection

TorusEuler.endpointParityPart_const_smul.text: Shows that multiplying a field by a real constant before reflection averaging gives the same result as multiplying the averaged field afterward. The statement holds for every real sign and needs no regularity. It is used when moving time-dependent normalization constants through estimates one fixed time slice at a time.
TorusEuler.endpointParityPart_const_smul.summary: Reflection averaging commutes with constant rescaling

TorusEuler.endpointParity_contDiff_slice.text: Restricts joint smoothness on the closed time-space slab to a fixed time `t` satisfying `ht`. Since the spatial factor is all Euclidean space, the resulting slice is globally smooth in space. The membership hypothesis matters: the original slab certificate says nothing about slices outside its time interval.
TorusEuler.endpointParity_contDiff_slice.summary: A smooth slab field has smooth spatial slices

TorusEuler.endpointParity_integral_refle.text: For any real-valued function, the integral of its reflected version over the centered cell equals the original integral. Negation preserves volume and the cell itself. The statement uses the total Bochner integral convention, so it does not by itself certify integrability; the pressure-normalization application supplies continuity on the compact cell.
TorusEuler.endpointParity_integral_refle.summary: Reflection preserves the integral over the centered cell

TorusEuler.endpointParity_latticeVector_.text: Identifies the Euclidean lattice vector of the negated integer index with the negative of the original lattice vector. The proof is coordinatewise, using integer-cast negation. This allows the reflected field’s periodicity to use the original periodicity statement with the lattice index replaced by its negative.
TorusEuler.endpointParity_latticeVector_.summary: Integer lattice negation agrees with spatial negation

TorusEuler.endpointParity_neg_preimage_c.text: Shows that the inverse image of the centered fundamental cube under spatial negation is the same cube. Each coordinate interval is symmetric about zero. This geometric identity is used in the measure-preserving change of variables that keeps the pressure mean unchanged when selecting its even component.
TorusEuler.endpointParity_neg_preimage_c.summary: The centered fundamental cell is reflection invariant

TorusEuler.endpointPath_norm_sq.text: For a real vector time path, its squared L² norm equals the time integral of the squared pointwise norm over the restricted interval. This Hilbert-space identity is used to compare slice energies with joint energy. It holds for all real `T`, including the trivial space obtained from an empty interval.
TorusEuler.endpointPath_norm_sq.summary: Time path energy equals the squared L² norm

TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalCoefficientWo.text: For a derivative word $q$, this scalar cost is twice the closed-time norm of $K_q$ plus twice $T$ times that of $\Omega_q$. The vorticity factor carries the duration because it enters through a primitive. These are the coefficient factors multiplying the shorter velocity words in the physical derivative recurrence.
TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalCoefficientWo.summary: Combine kinetic and integrated vorticity coefficient costs

TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalCoefficientWo.text: For $0\le T\le1$, a weighted bound on the sum of the kinetic and vorticity coefficient time norms, together with $A_{\rm inv}D^9\sqrt\ell\le1$, implies the combined recurrence cost is at most $2H$. Nonnegative radius, inverse cap and coefficient constant are explicit. The factor $T$ can be discarded because the slab is at most unit length.
TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalCoefficientWo.summary: Weighted coefficient bounds pay for the inverse cap

TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalForcePrimitiv.text: For a matrix field $F(t,a)$ and a force $f_{\mathrm{lab}}(t,a)$ already written in labels, define $L(t,a)=-\int_0^tF(s,a)^Tf_{\mathrm{lab}}(s,a)\,ds$. The torus label is represented by its periodic lift to $\mathbb R^3$. In Theorem 4.2, $F=D_aX$ and $f_{\mathrm{lab}}=f\circ X$, giving the paper's source and $L(0)=0$. This expression neither performs the composition with $X$ nor imposes regularity. To treat it as a differentiable force primitive, one supplies the integrability and smoothness hypotheses used by the subsequent existence theorem.
TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalForcePrimitiv.summary: Define the negative primitive of the pulled-back force

TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalIntegratedRes.text: This defines the continuous periodic field $Kg-\int_0^t\Omega g+L-c$ after forgetting the half-Hölder norm. For a solution of the projected equation its solenoidal projection vanishes, which later yields a pressure potential. The definition itself imposes no equation, continuity in time, or differentiability on the supplied curves.
TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalIntegratedRes.summary: The integrated equation leaves a gradient residual

TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalInverseBudget.text:
Define the explicit recovery bound combining the instantaneous inverse, mixed inverse, projection norms, and kinetic and vorticity operator norms. Its time factors reflect the cancellation of the apparent inverse-duration cost in the recovered time average.

Default-value audit (b5): The expression is total for arbitrary real inverse caps, including negative caps. Its interpretation as an upper bound requires nonnegative valid inverse bounds and coefficient compatibility; the definition contains no inverse-time division.
TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalInverseBudget.summary: The common bound from both Holder inverses

TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalInverseBudget.text: Control the explicit recovery bound by the closed-time half-Holder norms of K and Omega and the supplied inverse and projection bounds. Almost-everywhere mixed-coefficient compatibility is sufficient.
TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalInverseBudget.summary: Bounding the inverse expression by time slice norms

TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalInverseBudget.text: The recovery budget is nonnegative when the slab duration and the two inverse caps `As` and `Am` are nonnegative. Every remaining factor is an operator norm or a nonnegative constant. This algebraic lemma permits multiplying the budget by upper bounds in the later physical derivative estimates.
TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalInverseBudget.summary: Nonnegative inverse caps give a nonnegative budget

TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalJetNormRecurr.text: Through order $N$, assume continuous coefficient, source and velocity words, compatible mixed representatives, projected differentiated equations, and the base spatial and mixed inverse bounds. Then each velocity time norm satisfies one recurrence using the same inverse budget and shorter velocity words. This theorem derives the recurrence from the physical equations; the subsequent lifting lemma performs the induction in derivative order.
TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalJetNormRecurr.summary: Every physical derivative uses the same base inverse

TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalLabelVelocity.text:
Evaluate the recovered solenoidal Holder curve on the torus covering map to obtain its physical label-space velocity lift. Time regularity and pointwise divergence statements are proved under additional hypotheses.

Default-value audit (b5): The torus covering map makes the lift periodic for every time. The solenoidal subspace is a weak divergence constraint; classical divergence and time smoothness require additional regularity, and no values are specially chosen outside the time interval.
TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalLabelVelocity.summary: The periodic lift of the recovered label velocity

TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalLabelVelocity.text: Evaluating a solenoidal half-Hölder field through the torus quotient gives a periodic function on the Euclidean lift. The curve `g` is arbitrary and no time regularity is assumed. Integer translation leaves `toUnitTorus x` unchanged, so periodicity holds for every real time, including times outside the interval used by the mean solver.

TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalMeanWordConst.text: Defines the scalar factor collecting the number of admissible spatial words, product-rule powers of two, coefficient bounds `C`, and the finite sum of derivative costs `H`. It depends on the requested order `N` and those two scalar families. Dependence on the parent deformation scale is kept outside this constant in the subsequent estimate.
TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalMeanWordConst.summary: The finite order constant in the mean estimate

TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalMeanWordConst.text: Assuming every entry of `C` and `H` is nonnegative, the finite order constant for the physical mean is nonnegative at each natural order `N`. The proof checks the finite sum and all scalar factors. This sign fact is needed when multiplying norm inequalities and absorbing deformation powers in the quantitative estimate.
TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalMeanWordConst.summary: Nonnegative budgets give a nonnegative mean constant

TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalMean_reflecti.text: For even deformation, inverse coframe and material coefficients and odd forcing, replaces a smooth periodic mean solution by odd label velocity, displacement and physical velocity, with even pressure. The same forced equation, divergence condition, zero-mean pressure and both displacement endpoint conditions remain valid. The positive slab and all original field equations are explicit hypotheses.
TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalMean_reflecti.summary: Select an odd mean while preserving its endpoint equation

TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalMixedSolution.text: A mixed solution fixed by the strong projection, with exact projected equation and coefficient actions representing the kinetic and vorticity forms, embeds into the constrained torus $L^2$ space. It satisfies the physical weak equation against every constrained test vector, with source equal to the negative embedded mixed forcing. No continuous time representative or pressure is constructed here.
TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalMixedSolution.summary: The projected mixed solve gives the physical weak equation

TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalMomentumResid.text: The field is $dK\,g+K\,dg-\Omega g+dL$, expressed as a continuous periodic vector field. It is the product-rule derivative of the integrated residual when the supplied derivative values are correct. The later pressure theorem makes its negative a gradient; the algebraic definition does not certify those derivative or projection conditions.

TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalPrimitive_eva.text: For a continuous solenoidal curve `g` and $t\in[0,T]$, evaluating its Banach-valued primitive at a torus label equals integrating the evaluated vector velocity. Continuity provides interval integrability, and the solenoidal subspace is complete because it is closed. This identity transfers the abstract zero endpoint primitives to the actual displacement field.
TorusEuler.endpointPhysicalPrimitive_eva.summary: Integrating before evaluating gives the same displacement

TorusEuler.endpointPotentialGradient.text:
Descend the smooth periodic Euclidean gradient to a continuous torus field. Existence is selected noncomputably, but uniqueness of descent makes the resulting gradient independent of the choice.

Default-value audit (b5): The noncomputable choice is from a unique torus descent of the smooth periodic gradient. Periodicity guarantees well-definedness, and there is no undefined or arbitrary gradient on a bad input because the structure requires smoothness.
TorusEuler.endpointPotentialGradient.summary: The gradient of a periodic potential on the torus

TorusEuler.endpointPotentialGradient_fou.text: The torus gradient of the real Fourier test equals the real scalar `L` applied to $2\pi i$ times the character, multiplied by the integer wave vector. This exact formula shows that these weak tests inspect longitudinal Fourier components. It holds for arbitrary real-linear `L`, including real and imaginary parts.
TorusEuler.endpointPotentialGradient_fou.summary: The gradient of a real Fourier test is longitudinal

TorusEuler.endpointPotentialGradient_toU.text: Evaluation of the torus potential gradient at the image of a Euclidean point is exactly the ordinary gradient of the periodic lift there.
TorusEuler.endpointPotentialGradient_toU.summary: The descended gradient agrees with the lift

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive.text: For a time-dependent vector field $v$, write $Jv(t)=\int_0^tv(s)\,ds$. This is the time primitive used in §4 and Appendix A. Its initial value is zero; if $v$ is integrable on $[0,T]$ and has zero integral, its terminal value is also zero. For square-integrable velocities in a complete real normed space it gives the absolutely continuous displacement, with derivative $v$ almost everywhere. The expression itself is defined without an integrability hypothesis, so derivative and endpoint interpretations must use the hypotheses of the accompanying theorems.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive.summary: Recover displacement by integrating the label velocity

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveEvaluation.text:
For a time in the closed interval, integration up to that time is a continuous linear map from temporal L2 to the target space, with norm at most the square root of that time.

Default-value audit (b5): The time is a subtype element of the closed interval, excluding out-of-window evaluation. At time zero the functional is zero. Integration makes it independent of the temporal L2 representative.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveEvaluation.summary: Evaluating a primitive at a prescribed time

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveEvaluation_a.text: Applying the bundled primitive-evaluation operator at a time belonging to the slab gives exactly `endpointPrimitive v t`. This is an equality in the target normed space, rather than an almost-everywhere equality of functions. Integration makes this value independent of null-set changes in the input $L^2$ representative.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveEvaluation_a.summary: The evaluation operator returns the anchored time integral

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveEvaluation_l.text: For an essentially bounded measurable coefficient field `Ω`, primitive evaluation of the bundled multiplier applied to an $L^2$ path equals the ordinary integral of $\Omega(r)v(r)$ from zero to the selected time. This removes the quotient-space packaging while preserving null-set independence. The coefficient's measurability and essential bound are explicit hypotheses.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveEvaluation_l.summary: Evaluating the primitive of a coefficient product gives its integral

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveLp.text:
Define the temporal L2 integration operator with operator norm bounded by the nonnegative duration. The resulting object is an L2 class, while pointwise representatives are treated by separate lemmas.

Default-value audit (b5): The interval duration is nonnegative. At zero duration the L2 space is trivial and the primitive operator is zero. A pointwise primitive of a chosen representative agrees only almost everywhere with the operator output.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveLp.summary: The bounded primitive on square integrable time paths

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveLpLinear.text: Bundle the primitive construction as a real linear map on $L^2$ velocities. The proof checks addition and scalar multiplication through almost-everywhere representatives and uses invariance of integrals under null-set changes. Continuity is supplied in the next construction from its quantitative norm bound, rather than assumed in this linear-map definition.

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveLpLinear_bou.text: For every $L^2$ input on a nonnegative interval, the linear primitive map has output norm at most `T` times the input norm. This follows by taking square roots of the integral estimate. It supplies a valid continuity constant even at `T=0`, when the quotient domain is trivial.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveLpLinear_bou.summary: The primitive operator grows at most linearly with duration

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveLpValue.text: Given an $L^2$ velocity on a nonnegative interval, form its anchored primitive and bundle that function into the same $L^2$ space using the established integrability proof. The construction selects the quotient class of the continuous primitive. Equality with a displayed representative is subsequently stated almost everywhere.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveLpValue.summary: The primitive represented as an L² equivalence class

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveLpValue_appl.text: A representative of the $L^2$ class constructed by `endpointPrimitiveLpValue` equals the anchored integral of the input representative almost everywhere on the time interval. The equality is measure-relative, as required by `toLp`. It does not select or promise a canonical pointwise representative at every time.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveLpValue_appl.summary: The bundled primitive agrees almost everywhere with its formula

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveLp_apply_ae.text: The temporal L2 primitive operator agrees almost everywhere on the interval with the ordinary interval primitive of an L2 representative.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveLp_apply_ae.summary: The bounded primitive agrees almost everywhere

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveLp_inner_add.text: For any two $L^2$ time paths on a nonnegative interval, the sum $\langle Ju,v\rangle+\langle u,Jv\rangle$ equals the inner product of their total time integrals. The proof uses absolutely continuous primitives and their almost-everywhere derivatives. If either terminal integral vanishes, the boundary term disappears, producing the skew-pairing identity used in endpoint coercivity.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveLp_inner_add.summary: Integration by parts leaves the terminal integral pairing

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveLp_inner_eq_.text: Let $T\ge0$ and let $u,v\in L^2([0,T];E)$ for a complete real Hilbert space. If $\int_0^Tv=0$, then $\langle Ju,v\rangle_{L^2}=-\langle u,Jv\rangle_{L^2}$. Only the second path needs zero mean. This is the pairing identity used in Appendix A to turn $\langle(K-J\Omega)v,v\rangle$ into the displacement energy. The conclusion is an identity of integrals, not the paper's pointwise formula for $J^*v$; its application to the energy requires no pointwise choice of an $L^2$ representative. Here $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveLp_inner_eq_.summary: Move the time integral across an inner product

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveLp_toLp_appl.text: If an explicit velocity function has $L^2$ membership proof `hv`, then the continuous primitive operator applied to its quotient class agrees almost everywhere with the function's anchored primitive. The result combines the operator's representative formula with invariance under the `toLp` representative choice. The conclusion is not an everywhere equality of representatives.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitiveLp_toLp_appl.summary: Bundling a velocity preserves its primitive formula

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive_congr_ae.text: If velocities agree almost everywhere on the full positive-oriented interval, their primitives agree at every time in its closed subinterval. No choice of L2 representative affects the displacement there.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive_congr_ae.summary: Almost everywhere equal velocities have equal primitives

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive_eq_neg_term.text: Assume $v$ is integrable on $[0,T]$ and $\int_0^Tv(s)\,ds=0$. For every $t\in[0,T]$, its primitive satisfies $Jv(t)=-\int_t^Tv(s)\,ds$. The conclusion identifies the displacement obtained from the initial endpoint with the same displacement recovered from the terminal endpoint. This is the equality used before Cauchy–Schwarz in §4.1. Continuity and differentiability of $v$ are unnecessary; in particular the statement applies to the square-integrable velocities representing $H^1_0$ displacements. Here $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive_eq_neg_term.summary: Express a zero-mean primitive as a terminal integral

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive_sub_eq_inte.text: For an interval-integrable velocity and two times `a,b` in the slab, the difference of primitive values equals the oriented integral from `a` to `b`. The theorem does not require `a≤b`; interval integration handles either orientation. This identifies the increment used in continuity and half-Hölder estimates.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive_sub_eq_inte.summary: Displacement increments are integrals over the intervening times

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive_sub_velocit.text: For two interval-integrable velocities on the whole slab, the primitive of their difference equals the difference of their primitives at every allowed time. The membership `ht` restricts integration to a subinterval where both integrability hypotheses still apply. This linearity is used to transfer $L^2$ stability estimates to displacement paths.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive_sub_velocit.summary: Primitives respect subtraction of integrable velocities

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive_terminal.text: If the integral of a velocity from zero to `T` vanishes, its anchored primitive is zero at `T`. The result simply unfolds the primitive definition and does not assume integrability or positivity of `T`. In analytic applications, those properties are supplied before this equality is used as an endpoint condition.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive_terminal.summary: Zero total time integral gives zero terminal displacement

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive_terminal_po.text: For $T\ge0$, let $v\in L^2([0,T];E)$ have zero time integral and put $z(t)=\int_0^tv(s)\,ds$. Then $\int_0^T\|z(t)\|^2\,dt\le(T^2/2)\int_0^T\|v(t)\|^2\,dt$. The formal statement allows a general real normed target space and does not require $T\le1$. For $E=\mathbb R^3$ it is exactly the second inequality in (4.5), with $z\in H^1_0$. The factor $1/2$ comes from integrating the terminal Cauchy–Schwarz estimate, rather than from a sharp Poincaré constant.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive_terminal_po.summary: Retain the exact factor in the displacement bound

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive_terminal_po.text: Let $v\in L^2([0,T];E)$ have zero integral, and let $t\in[0,T]$. For $z(t)=\int_0^tv(s)\,ds$, the formal statement gives $\|z(t)\|^2\le(T-t)\int_0^T\|v(s)\|^2\,ds$. It follows from the terminal representation $z(t)=-\int_t^Tv$ and Cauchy–Schwarz. This is the first bound in (4.5), with exactly the factor $T-t$. Neither a restriction $T\le1$ nor a three-dimensional target is needed; the paper's Sobolev displacement is a special case.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive_terminal_po.summary: Bound displacement by the remaining time and kinetic energy

TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive_zero.text: The time primitive at zero is zero for any integrand, because the integration interval has zero length. No regularity assumption is needed.
TorusEuler.endpointPrimitive_zero.summary: The displacement primitive starts at zero

TorusEuler.endpointProductOperator.text: Build $B=K-J\Omega$ on the joint $L^2$ space, first multiplying by each coefficient and then integrating the vorticity term in time. `hK`, `hΩ`, `bK`, and `bΩ` supply measurable, essentially bounded coefficients. The definition itself imposes neither ellipticity nor the endpoint constraint; these enter the inverse theorem.
TorusEuler.endpointProductOperator.summary: Multiplication minus integrated vorticity in the joint space

TorusEuler.endpointProductOperator_apply.text: Under the measurable bounded coefficient hypotheses, the operator representative equals $K(t,a)v(t,a)-\int_0^t\Omega(s,a)v(s,a)\,ds$ almost everywhere. The proof uses slice congruence to replace the representative of the intermediate multiplier inside the integral. It establishes the formula for arbitrary joint $L^2$ input, before projection.
TorusEuler.endpointProductOperator_apply.summary: The joint operator has the integrated equation formula

TorusEuler.endpointProductOperator_coerc.text: The hypothesis `hslice` supplies a lower bound for the explicit $K v-J(\Omega v)$ expression on almost every label slice. The theorem transfers it to the inner product of the bundled joint operator with `v`. Measurability and coefficient bounds remain explicit; no zero-mean or divergence condition is inferred automatically.
TorusEuler.endpointProductOperator_coerc.summary: Slice bounds give coercivity of the joint operator

TorusEuler.endpointProductPrimitive.text:
Define the bounded joint L2 time primitive, integrating at fixed label, with operator norm bounded by the nonnegative duration.

Default-value audit (b5): The construction takes a nonnegative duration and yields a bounded operator on joint L2 classes. It is zero for duration zero and does not choose classical time derivatives.
TorusEuler.endpointProductPrimitive.summary: The time primitive in the joint integral space

TorusEuler.endpointProductPrimitiveLinea.text: Construct time integration as a real linear map between joint $L^2$ spaces. Addition and scalar multiplication are checked by moving quotient equalities to almost-everywhere label slices and then into the integral. `hT : 0 ≤ T` supplies the square-integrable output; boundedness is established separately.
TorusEuler.endpointProductPrimitiveLinea.summary: Time integration is linear on the joint space

TorusEuler.endpointProductPrimitiveLinea.text: For `hT : 0 ≤ T`, the linear primitive satisfies $\|Jv\|_2\le T\|v\|_2$ on the joint space. Squaring reduces the estimate to the labelwise energy majorant; Fubini contributes the second factor of $T$. This bound certifies continuity of the subsequently bundled operator.
TorusEuler.endpointProductPrimitiveLinea.summary: Time integration costs at most the interval length

TorusEuler.endpointProductPrimitiveRep.text: At a pair `q`, integrate the chosen representative of `v` from zero to `q.1`, with label `q.2` fixed. The integration measure is already restricted to $(0,T]$. This representative is defined everywhere; later results identify it with the ordinary primitive only inside the time slab.
TorusEuler.endpointProductPrimitiveRep.summary: Integrate time while keeping the label fixed

TorusEuler.endpointProductPrimitiveRep_e.text: For `hq : q.1 ∈ Icc 0 T`, the extra restriction to $(0,T]$ does not change integration from zero to `q.1`. The chosen product representative therefore equals `endpointPrimitive` on that label slice. This equality is pointwise for the indicated representative, without asserting pointwise integrability of every slice.
TorusEuler.endpointProductPrimitiveRep_e.summary: The restricted integral is the usual primitive

TorusEuler.endpointProductPrimitiveRep_s.text: Assuming `hT : 0 ≤ T`, the squared norm of the primitive is at most $T$ times the full time-slice energy, almost everywhere in the product measure. The estimate combines the one-dimensional primitive bound with slice square integrability obtained from Fubini; exceptional labels are excluded by the conclusion.

TorusEuler.endpointProductPrimitiveValue.text: Package the primitive representative as a joint $L^2$ equivalence class, using the square-integrability theorem and `hT : 0 ≤ T`. The construction forgets changes on product null sets. Its chosen pointwise representative is identified with the original time integral only almost everywhere in the next theorem.
TorusEuler.endpointProductPrimitiveValue.summary: The primitive as a joint square integrable field

TorusEuler.endpointProductPrimitiveValue.text: The representative chosen by `toLp` for the joint primitive agrees almost everywhere with `endpointProductPrimitiveRep`. The nonnegative-time assumption is inherited from the construction. This theorem is the representative bridge used when proving linearity and bounds; it does not upgrade quotient equality to pointwise equality on exceptional product points.
TorusEuler.endpointProductPrimitiveValue.summary: The square integrable primitive has the expected representative

TorusEuler.endpointProductPrimitive_ae_t.text: For almost every label, the input has an $L^2$ time slice and the joint primitive agrees almost everywhere in time with `endpointPrimitiveLp` applied to that slice. The existential `hv` records the needed MemLp proof. The statement separates a label null set from the time null sets of representatives.
TorusEuler.endpointProductPrimitive_ae_t.summary: Joint integration agrees with the one label operator

TorusEuler.endpointProductPrimitive_appl.text: The chosen representative of the bundled joint primitive agrees almost everywhere with the ordinary time primitive of the input slice. The conclusion is a product-measure equality, not an identity for every representative and every label. Nonnegative `T` and almost-everywhere membership in the restricted interval justify the identification.
TorusEuler.endpointProductPrimitive_appl.summary: The joint operator integrates each label path

TorusEuler.endpointProduct_inner_lower_b.text: Assume `h` bounds the time-integrated inner product of `w` and `v` below by `c` times the time-slice energy for almost every label. Fubini yields $c\|v\|_2^2\le\langle w,v\rangle$ in the joint Hilbert space. This transfer does not require `c` to be positive; positivity is needed when inverting.
TorusEuler.endpointProduct_inner_lower_b.summary: Integrating slice coercivity preserves the constant

TorusEuler.endpointProjectedHilbertOpera.text: Let $V$ be a closed subspace of a real Hilbert space and $K$ a bounded operator. If $\langle Kv,v\rangle\ge\kappa\|v\|^2$ for every $v\in V$, with $\kappa>0$, then $v\mapsto P_VKv$ is injective on $V$, where $P_V$ is the orthogonal projection. In Appendix A.2, $V$ is the space of divergence-free spatial $L^2$ fields. This identifies two velocities solving the same fixed-time equation. The formal statement gives injectivity only; it does not assert surjectivity or a Hölder estimate.
TorusEuler.endpointProjectedHilbertOpera.summary: Use the energy inequality on a closed Hilbert subspace

TorusEuler.endpointProjectedMixedResidua.text: Rewrite a differentiated compressed equation with its forcing and Leibniz correction as a vanishing projected mixed residual. This is the form required by the time-recovery helper.
TorusEuler.endpointProjectedMixedResidua.summary: The differentiated equation has zero projected residual

TorusEuler.endpointProjectedWeak_eq_mean.text: If $w\in L^2([0,T];E)$ satisfies $w-T^{-1}\int_0^Tw=0$ in that space, then $w(t)=T^{-1}\int_0^Tw$ for almost every time. Appendix A.2 uses $T=1$ to recover the constant removed by $\mathcal Q$. This result alone supplies neither spatial Leray projection nor spatial Hölder regularity. The formal statement is meaningful even for zero interval length because the reciprocal at zero is assigned zero and the almost-everywhere assertion is then vacuous; the endpoint argument uses $T>0$.
TorusEuler.endpointProjectedWeak_eq_mean.summary: Identify a path whose time average has been removed

TorusEuler.endpointProjection_eq_zero_of.text: For positive `T` and `t ∈ [0,T]`, assume a continuous-field-valued path `G` has derivative `dG` within the slab and its weak spatial projection vanishes throughout. Then the projection of `dG` vanishes too. The bounded projection commutes with differentiation, and positive interval length supplies uniqueness of the derivative within the closed slab.
TorusEuler.endpointProjection_eq_zero_of.summary: Differentiation preserves a vanishing spatial projection

TorusEuler.endpointProjection_residual_e.text: If the weak projection of `F` equals the embedding of a solenoidal half-Hölder field `c`, subtracting `c` from `F` leaves a field with zero weak projection. This is the algebraic step preparing pressure reconstruction after the time-independent component has been recovered. The solenoidal membership of `c` is carried by its subtype.
TorusEuler.endpointProjection_residual_e.summary: Subtract the recovered solenoidal constant from the residual

TorusEuler.endpointRealFourierCharacter.text: For lattice frequency `k` and complex amplitude `c`, define the real continuous character $a\mapsto\operatorname{Re}(c e_k(a))$. Varying `c` includes cosine and sine tests. These real characters let the proof describe time-valued Fourier moments without first complexifying the entire joint time-space Hilbert space.
TorusEuler.endpointRealFourierCharacter.summary: Real Fourier characters include cosine and sine phases

TorusEuler.endpointRealFourierCharacter_.text: For each real Fourier character there is a smooth periodic potential whose gradient equals that character times the real frequency vector. The construction divides by $2\pi i$, with its nonzero proof supplied explicitly. At zero frequency the requested gradient is zero, so no division by the frequency itself is needed.
TorusEuler.endpointRealFourierCharacter_.summary: A character times its frequency is a smooth gradient

TorusEuler.endpointRealLeray_eq_coe_weak.text: For every real spatial $L^2$ field, the Fourier-defined real Leray projector equals the ambient vector underlying the weak solenoidal orthogonal projection. The latter initially has a subtype-valued codomain. This identification transfers a vanishing weak projection into modewise statements about the Fourier pressure correction.
TorusEuler.endpointRealLeray_eq_coe_weak.summary: The real Fourier projection is the weak spatial projection

TorusEuler.endpointRecoveredPrimitive_ha.text: Let $T\ge0$, and let an injective bounded linear map embed a Banach space $X$ into another Banach space $Y$. Suppose $v:[0,T]\to X$ is continuous, its image agrees almost everywhere with a $Y$-valued path $w$, and $\int_0^Tw=0$. Then $Jv(0)=Jv(T)=0$ and $(Jv)_t=v$ throughout the interval, with derivatives taken from within it. In Appendix A.2, the embedding passes from the strong spatial norm to the weak one. Injectivity makes the recovered zero mean valid in the stronger space as well. Here $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$.
TorusEuler.endpointRecoveredPrimitive_ha.summary: Integrate the recovered continuous representative without changing its mean

TorusEuler.endpointRecoveredPrimitive_of.text: A continuous half-Hölder solenoidal representative of a velocity in the endpoint subspace has primitive zero at both $0$ and `T`. Its primitive has within-interval derivative equal to the representative throughout the closed slab. The terminal zero comes from the weak zero-time-mean constraint and injectivity of the embedding into spatial $L^2$.
TorusEuler.endpointRecoveredPrimitive_of.summary: The recovered primitive vanishes at both endpoints

TorusEuler.endpointRecoveredSpatialHiera.text: A finite hierarchy of mixed spatial derivatives with continuous time representatives retains each spatial derivative relation at every time. Almost-everywhere representative agreement and continuity promote the identities to the closed slab.
TorusEuler.endpointRecoveredSpatialHiera.summary: Recovered spatial derivative hierarchies agree at every time

TorusEuler.endpointRecoveredTimeSlice_di.text: For a mixed field and its spatial derivative with continuous time representatives, every nonzero spatial difference quotient of the recovered field equals the segment average of the recovered derivative. This holds at every time in $[0,T]$, including endpoints. The proof first compares primitives, then differentiates within the closed interval using `hT : 0 < T`.
TorusEuler.endpointRecoveredTimeSlice_di.summary: Recovered difference quotients equal derivative averages

TorusEuler.endpointRecoveredTimeSlice_ha.text: Continuous time representatives of a mixed field and its torus directional derivative retain that derivative relation at every time in the closed slab. Both almost-everywhere slice comparisons and both continuity assumptions are needed. The argument passes through exact segment-average identities, avoiding any unsupported differentiation of chosen $L^2$ representatives.
TorusEuler.endpointRecoveredTimeSlice_ha.summary: Spatial derivatives persist through time recovery

TorusEuler.endpointRecoveryBudget_scalar.text: If the two inverse caps cost at most $C_sQ^{145}$ and $C_mQ^{145}$, projection norms have fixed bounds, and the remaining coefficient cost is at most $6Q$, the recovery expression is bounded by a fixed prefactor times $Q^{291}$. The hypotheses control signs needed for multiplication. This explicit degree is a sufficient bound, with no claim of sharpness.
TorusEuler.endpointRecoveryBudget_scalar.summary: Two inverse caps yield one fixed polynomial power

TorusEuler.endpointSimpleJoint.text: For a simple function `s` from labels to time L², form the joint representative $(t,a)\mapsto s(a)(t)$ and prove it square integrable using the uniform bound `hs`. Finite simple-function structure supplies joint measurability. This construction starts the approximation of continuous path-valued fields without assuming representatives vary measurably for arbitrary families.
TorusEuler.endpointSimpleJoint.summary: A bounded simple family of paths gives a joint field

TorusEuler.endpointSimpleJoint_slices.text: For almost every label, the time slice of `endpointSimpleJoint s hs` agrees almost everywhere with the path selected by `s`. This is the representative guarantee of the initial simple-function construction. It allows norm comparisons and Cauchy estimates to be made in terms of the original path-valued simple functions.
TorusEuler.endpointSimpleJoint_slices.summary: The joint simple field has the prescribed paths

TorusEuler.endpointSkew.text: Defines the operator $F^*(M^*-M)F$ on a complete real Hilbert space. In the flow application, `F` is the deformation and `M` the velocity gradient along trajectories, so this is the pulled-back vorticity coefficient. The definition itself requires neither a flow equation nor invertibility of `F`; those conditions enter later coercivity theorems.

TorusEuler.endpointSlabDirectionalWord.text: Defines a derivative word by recursively applying the within-slab Fréchet derivative in each prescribed constant space-time direction. The first letter is the outermost derivative, and the empty word is the original field. This definition accommodates both temporal and spatial directions; genuine derivative properties are proved later under smoothness and positive-duration assumptions.
TorusEuler.endpointSlabDirectionalWord.summary: Successive directional derivatives within the closed slab

TorusEuler.endpointSlabDirectionalWord_c.text: On a positive-duration closed slab, applying any finite word of constant space-time directional derivatives to a smooth field produces another smooth field there. Positive duration gives uniqueness of within-slab derivatives, including temporal endpoints. The statement is independent of periodicity and imposes no linear-independence condition on the chosen directions.
TorusEuler.endpointSlabDirectionalWord_c.summary: Every derivative word stays smooth on the slab

TorusEuler.endpointSlabDirectionalWord_e.text: For smooth data and a time inside a positive-duration slab, derivative words whose directions have zero time component agree with the existing `phaseOperatorWord` applied to the spatial slice. The proof identifies the within-slab derivative with the ordinary derivative of that slice. The result reconciles two encodings of the same spatial derivatives.
TorusEuler.endpointSlabDirectionalWord_e.summary: Pure spatial slab words agree with spatial operator words

TorusEuler.endpointSlabDirectionalWord_h.text: For a smooth field on a positive-duration slab, prefixing a purely spatial direction to a word gives the ordinary derivative of that word along the corresponding spatial line. The time is fixed anywhere in $[0,T]$, including endpoints. Spatial differentiation remains two-sided because the spatial domain is unrestricted.
TorusEuler.endpointSlabDirectionalWord_h.summary: A spatial letter gives a two-sided line derivative

TorusEuler.endpointSlabDirectionalWord_h.text: For a smooth field on a positive-duration slab, prefixing the direction $(1,0)$ yields the time derivative of a word at any fixed spatial point.
