The derivative is explicitly within $[0,T]$, so both endpoints are included. This does not claim smooth extension or an ordinary two-sided time derivative outside the slab.
TorusEuler.endpointSlabDirectionalWord_h.summary: A time letter gives the closed-interval derivative

TorusEuler.endpointSlabDirectionalWord_m.text: Applying a slab derivative word whose letters have been mapped by `d` is exactly the same as differentiating the original word with the direction family precomposed by `d`. The recursive identity carries no smoothness assumptions. It aligns the geometric jet-data indexing with the coordinate words used by the finite norms.
TorusEuler.endpointSlabDirectionalWord_m.summary: Relabelling directions relabels the derivative word

TorusEuler.endpointSlabDirectionalWord_p.text: If every time slice of a field is periodic on the slab, every constant space-time directional word remains periodic there, even when directions have time components. The proof uses translation invariance of the domain and congruence of the total within-derivative operator. This invariance statement alone does not assert differentiability; it carries no smoothness or positive-duration hypothesis.
TorusEuler.endpointSlabDirectionalWord_p.summary: Within-slab derivative words preserve spatial periodicity

TorusEuler.endpointSlabLiftDirections.text: Encodes one time direction $(1,0)$ and a family of purely spatial directions $(0,u_i)$ using `Sum Unit I`. This allows time and spatial letters to appear in the same derivative word without confusing their meaning. The spatial family is arbitrary and need not be a basis or contain nonzero vectors.
TorusEuler.endpointSlabLiftDirections.summary: Separating the time direction from spatial directions

TorusEuler.endpointSlabSpatialWord.text: Takes a list of spatial direction indices, tags every letter as spatial, and evaluates the corresponding within-slab derivative word. The empty list still denotes the original field. This is the common lifted expression represented by both strong half-Hölder coefficient curves and their mixed temporal realizations.
TorusEuler.endpointSlabSpatialWord.summary: Spatial words inside the common space-time encoding

TorusEuler.endpointSlabSpatialWord_eq_sp.text: On a smooth positive time slab, the coordinate words in the geometric jet structure equal the ordinary iterated spatial partial derivatives of each time slice.
TorusEuler.endpointSlabSpatialWord_eq_sp.summary: Spatial words are ordinary derivatives of the lift

TorusEuler.endpointSlab_slice_continuous.text: A coefficient continuous jointly on the closed time-label slab gives a continuous time curve when the label is fixed. The proof composes with the map $t\mapsto(t,a)$ and checks that it stays inside the slab. This supplies the temporal multiplier hypotheses for every label without an almost-everywhere restriction.

TorusEuler.endpointSlab_vadd_spatial.text: Translating the entire slab by a space-time vector with zero time component leaves the set unchanged. The spatial factor is all Euclidean space, so only the time coordinate constrains membership. This elementary set identity allows within-slab derivative congruence to respect lattice translations.
TorusEuler.endpointSlab_vadd_spatial.summary: Spatial translations leave the closed slab unchanged

TorusEuler.endpointSolenoidalEmbedding.text:
Restrict the Holder-to-L2 embedding to its divergence-free subspace, retaining the proof that the target lies in the weak solenoidal subspace.

Default-value audit (b5): This is a restriction of the same natural embedding to proven solenoidal subspaces. There is no coefficient inversion or exceptional branch.
TorusEuler.endpointSolenoidalEmbedding.summary: Embedding solenoidal Holder fields into the weak space

TorusEuler.endpointSolenoidalEmbedding_i.text: The embedding from solenoidal half-Hölder fields to solenoidal spatial $L^2$ fields is injective. Equality of embedded subtype elements reduces to equality in the full Hilbert space, then to equality of the original continuous representatives. Restricting to the divergence-free subspaces does not lose this uniqueness property.
TorusEuler.endpointSolenoidalEmbedding_i.summary: The constrained Hölder embedding remains injective

TorusEuler.endpointSourceCurve_eq_negPri.text: If a continuous force curve and source curve have lifts related by the negative time integral, then the source curve itself equals the negative Banach-valued force primitive throughout the interval. Evaluation commutes with the integral.
TorusEuler.endpointSourceCurve_eq_negPri.summary: A pointwise source formula determines its Holder primitive

TorusEuler.endpointSourceWords_eq_negPri.text: If a spatial derivative hierarchy has the base source equal to the negative force primitive, compatibility of its spatial derivatives and time regularity propagates that identity to every available word. The proof identifies derivatives and zero initial values on the closed interval.
TorusEuler.endpointSourceWords_eq_negPri.summary: Every source derivative is a negative force primitive

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialAllFiniteMixed.text: For a cutoff `N`, derivative families of the source and coefficient through the required orders yield a family `w` with `w [] = v`. Every word of length at most `N` satisfies the projected equation with its lower-order correction, and shorter words have the next directional derivative. The inverse, positive coercivity, weak bound, and translation compatibility remain explicit hypotheses.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialAllFiniteMixed.summary: Construct the full finite hierarchy of spatial derivatives

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialComplexificati.text: Instantiate the abstract complexification with real and complex Euclidean three-space. Coordinatewise embedding, real part, and imaginary part satisfy reconstruction, multiplication-by-$i$ identities, and squared-norm splitting. The object makes these concrete formulas available uniformly to the abstract extension machinery used by frozen spatial symbols.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialComplexificati.summary: Euclidean velocities have their standard complexification

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialDerivative.text: A compatible self-adjoint Hilbert operator supplies the weak bound and pairing for `P`. Together with positive coercivity, the compressed inverse, and actual directional derivatives of the coefficient and source, this gives the directional derivative of `v`. The conclusion records its projection constraint, commutator equation, and inverse norm estimate, rather than merely a formal differentiated identity.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialDerivative.summary: The compressed solution inherits one spatial derivative

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialDerivative_can.text: Given an actual equivalence `S` for the compressed coefficient and a projected source derivative `df`, this theorem constructs a projected candidate `w` solving the linearized coefficient equation. Its norm is bounded using the inverse norm and the coefficient product estimate. No derivative of `v` is asserted here; the limit argument establishes that identification later.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialDerivative_can.summary: Solve the equation that the spatial derivative must satisfy

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialDerivative_of_.text: This version identifies the derivative from difference-quotient bounds and limits when the strong projection intertwines with a bounded Hilbert operator `Q`. That compatibility supplies the weak norm bound; the projected pairing and coercivity are still explicit assumptions. The conclusion gives the actual line derivative of `v`, its projected equation, and its inverse-based norm estimate.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialDerivative_of_.summary: Obtain the derivative using a compatible Hilbert operator

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialDerivative_of_.text: Assume the compressed inverse, positive coercivity, translation commutation, a weak projection bound, and the specified difference-quotient bounds and supremum limits `hDfSup` and `hProdSup`. The theorem produces a projected `w` with the commutator equation and norm bound, and proves it is the line derivative of the periodic lift of `v`. The limits are hypotheses at this stage.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialDerivative_of_.summary: Identify the candidate derivative through weak error estimates

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialDerivative_of_.text: With a compressed inverse, positive coercivity, translation commutation, a projected pairing, and a weak Haar bound, directional derivative identities for `f` and `B` yield a derivative `w` of `v`. Its equation includes the coefficient commutator and its norm is bounded by the inverse norm. The theorem derives the required difference-quotient limits from the supplied actual derivative data.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialDerivative_of_.summary: Differentiate the compressed equation from actual data derivatives

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialDifference_equ.text: Assume `hτ` and `hτB` identify the same shift on fields and coefficients, `hComm` says projection commutes with it, and `hEq` gives the original projected equation. The difference quotient then solves the differentiated-form equation with a coefficient difference multiplying the translated unknown. This identity is exact for every `h`, before taking any limit.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialDifference_equ.summary: The difference quotient satisfies an exact commutator equation

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialDifference_fix.text: If `P` commutes with `τ` and fixes `v`, it also fixes the scaled difference $h^{-1}(τv-v)$. The statement is algebraic and permits every real `h`, including zero under Lean’s total inverse. It ensures that the coercive estimate may be applied to the finite differences before their limit is identified.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialDifference_fix.summary: Difference quotients remain in the projected subspace

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialDivergenceTest.text: This bounded functional pairs a spatial $L^2$ field with the gradient of a smooth periodic potential. It is the fixed-time counterpart of the joint endpoint divergence test. The velocity need not possess classical derivatives; vanishing of all such functionals is the weak solenoidal condition.

Evaluation of the spatial divergence functional is the torus integral of the real inner product of the potential gradient with the $L^2$ velocity. The proof replaces the continuous gradient’s $L^2$ representative almost everywhere. This formula connects the abstract kernel condition to the standard weak divergence definition.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialDivergenceTest.summary: The fixed time test is an integral gradient pairing

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialFixedIso.text: Identifies the fixed space of the strong spatial Leray projection with the canonical half-Hölder solenoidal subspace. The map is an isometric linear equivalence obtained from equality of the underlying submodules; it does not solve an equation. This changes the space used by the freezing inverse without changing the represented field or its norm.

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialFixedIso_apply.text: Applying the identification between the Leray fixed space and the half-Hölder solenoidal space leaves the underlying value unchanged. The argument `u` already lies in the fixed subspace, so the statement is a coercion identity, rather than a claim that an arbitrary field is divergence free. It permits equations for the original inverse to be rewritten on the recovery space.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialFixedIso_apply.summary: Changing solenoidal spaces preserves the field

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialFixedIso_symm_.text: The inverse identification also leaves the underlying half-Hölder field unchanged. Here `u` belongs to the canonical solenoidal subspace. The proof uses the forward value identity and the inverse law of the equivalence, allowing the norm and coefficient equation of the freezing inverse to survive conjugation between the two presentations.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialFixedIso_symm_.summary: Returning to the fixed space preserves values

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialSecondMixedDer.text: This version of the second derivative step uses compatibility with a self-adjoint Hilbert operator `Q` to obtain the weak estimate and pairing. The supplied first commutator equation and directional derivative data determine the new source `dg`. It returns a derivative of `w₁`; it does not independently assert that arbitrary mixed derivative orders commute.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialSecondMixedDer.summary: Obtain a second mixed derivative through the weak operator

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialSecondMixedDer.text: Given the equation for a first derivative `w₁`, the theorem constructs its derivative in the new direction `u`. The data include derivatives of `B`, `dB₁`, `df₁`, and the original field `v`, represented by `w₂`. The new source contains both product-rule terms, and the conclusion supplies the actual second derivative, projected equation, and norm bound.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialSecondMixedDer.summary: Differentiate the first commutator equation once more

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialSegmentAverage.text: Defines a continuous linear map that averages a half-Hölder vector field along the segment with lifted displacement $hu$, using the parameter interval $[0,1]$. The construction proves operator norm at most one. It averages the evaluation values themselves, so even a zero-length segment is meaningful and simply returns the value at its starting label.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialSegmentAverage.summary: Averaging a spatial field along a torus segment

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialSegmentAverage.text: Applying the segment-average continuous linear map to a field yields its explicit integral along the torus segment. This is a definitional equality for all labels, directions and real step lengths. It exposes the integral when proving that the recovered derivative agrees with difference quotients of the recovered field.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialSegmentAverage.summary: The segment operator evaluates to its defining integral

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialSlice.text:
Take the spatial L2 class of a joint field's slice when that slice is square integrable, and assign zero otherwise. The later almost-everywhere slice theorem proves the ordinary interpretation at almost every time; the definition alone gives no pointwise time representative.

Default-value audit (b5): The definition explicitly returns zero at a time whose chosen joint representative has a non-L2 slice. Fubini proves that branch is confined to a null set in the intended setting; this value cannot be used to claim pointwise time regularity before recovery.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialSlice.summary: Spatial slices with an exceptional time convention

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialSlice_apply_ae.text: For almost every time, the slice is square integrable and its L2 representative agrees almost everywhere in labels with the joint field. Fubini excludes the exceptional branch on a full-measure set.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialSlice_apply_ae.summary: Spatial slices agree almost everywhere with the joint field

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialSolenoidal.text: This submodule is the intersection of the kernels of spatial divergence tests over all smooth periodic potentials. It encodes distributional divergence freedom in the spatial $L^2$ space. It imposes no zero spatial mean: constant vector fields belong to the intended solenoidal space.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialSolenoidal.summary: The Hilbert subspace of weakly divergence free fields

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialWeakErrorEstim.text: Let $\mathcal R$ act on half-Hölder fields with values in a real Hilbert space, preserving the $L^2$ pairing against fields in its range. Assume $\langle B(a)v(a),v(a)\rangle\ge\mu\|v(a)\|^2$, $\mu>0$, for every projected field. Then each $u=\mathcal Ru$ satisfies $\|u\|_{L^2_a}\le\min(1,\mu)^{-1}\|\mathcal R(Bu)\|_{L^2_a}$, with normalized measure on the unit torus. This is the weak estimate used in the freezing argument. The paper retains $\mu^{-1}$; the formal constant is weaker when $\mu>1$ and agrees when $\mu\le1$.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialWeakErrorEstim.summary: Bound the weak norm by the projected residual

TorusEuler.endpointSpatialWordCoefficien.text: At a fixed time, this operator multiplies a solenoidal half-Hölder field by the half-Hölder coefficient $K(t)$. Its target is the full half-Hölder space, since multiplication need not preserve divergence. The definition composes ordinary coefficient multiplication with the subspace inclusion; projection is supplied elsewhere when solving the mean equation.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatialWordCoefficien.summary: Restrict coefficient multiplication to solenoidal fields

TorusEuler.endpointSpatial_realPart_embe.text: Take the real part of a complex half-Hölder vector field and embed it in real $L^2$. The result equals taking the real part after its complex torus $L^2$ embedding. This compatibility compares the two quotient-space constructions through their almost-everywhere values and supports the identification of the strong real Leray projection.
TorusEuler.endpointSpatial_realPart_embe.summary: Real parts commute with the spatial Hilbert embedding

TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray.text:
Define the path-valued Fourier multiplier imposing both spatial solenoidality and zero time mean. Its time-path Hilbert space is built over the specified interval; agreement with the joint L2 orthogonal projection is a later theorem.

Default-value audit (b5): For nonpositive T the restricted time measure on (0,T] is zero and the path space is degenerate. The concrete mixed projection remains defined, but the theorems identifying the endpoint constraint and proving idempotence in the intended setting assume T positive.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray.summary: The combined spatial and time mean projection

TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_agre.text: For positive duration, embedding the strong mixed projection into joint L2 equals the orthogonal projection onto the joint endpoint constraint space.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_agre.summary: The mixed projection agrees with its Hilbert version

TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_allS.text:
On $\mathbb T^3$ with values in $L^2([0,T];\mathbb R^3)$, $T>0$, let $\mathcal R=\mathbb P\mathcal Q$. Suppose $v=\mathcal Rv$, $\mathcal R(Bv)=f$, the base half-Hölder inverse exists, and $B$ is pointwise coercive on the projected fields with constant $\mu>0$. Supply actual half-Hölder directional derivatives of $B$ and $f$ through integer order $N$. Then all corresponding derivatives of $v$ exist, remain projected, and satisfy $\mathcal R(BD^
u v)=D^
u f-\mathcal R[D^
u,B]v$. Each norm is bounded by the inverse norm times its source and Leibniz terms involving lower solution derivatives. The statement does not independently construct the base inverse.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_allS.summary: Construct successive spatial derivatives of the mixed solution

TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_comp.text: With `X` the complexification of the $L^2$ time-path space, the Fourier coefficient of the strong mixed projection is obtained by extending `angularTimeLeray` complex-linearly. The coefficient statement applies for the supplied `T`. It identifies the combined constraint operator with the symbol used in the path-valued freezing construction.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_comp.summary: Complex Fourier modes carry the combined projection

TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_haar.text: For positive duration, the Haar L2 norm of the mixed field cannot increase under the combined projection. This weak norm control is used when passing difference quotients through the projection.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_haar.summary: The mixed projection contracts the spatial integral norm

TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_idem.text: For positive duration, the strong mixed projection is idempotent, by injectivity of the mixed-to-joint embedding and idempotence of the Hilbert-space projection.

TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_mem_.text: For positive duration, the joint L2 image of a strongly projected mixed field lies in the weak solenoidal zero-time-mean space.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_mem_.summary: The mixed projection satisfies the weak constraints

TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_neg_.text: The negative mixed Leray projection of a field has the projected negative derivative whenever the original field has a torus directional derivative. Positive duration supplies the Haar-space contraction estimate used by the derivative-preservation theorem. This validates the projected forcing derivative in the mixed spatial solve, rather than presuming formal commutation.

TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_pair.text: For positive `T` and a path-valued field `v` fixed by the mixed projection, projecting `w` does not change its Haar pairing with `v`. The proof uses the joint weak orthogonal projection and the equality of mixed inner products. This supplies the projected coercivity pairing for the time-dependent endpoint inverse.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_pair.summary: The mixed projection disappears against constrained fields

TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_real.text: Every real-character moment of a path-valued half-Hölder field is transformed by `angularTimeLeray` when the strong mixed projection is applied. The time-path space uses the restricted measure on $(0,T]$. The symbol combines spatial projection with removal of the time mean; no positivity assumption on `T` is needed for this algebraic coefficient identity.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_real.summary: The mixed projection acts by the time path symbol

TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_seco.text: For a positive time interval, a first mixed-projection derivative equation and the required directional derivative data yield its next spatial derivative. The explicit source `dg` contains both product-rule terms. The result remains fixed by the mixed projector and obeys the stated inverse norm estimate; time differentiability is addressed by separate recovery arguments.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_seco.summary: Take a second spatial derivative of the mixed solution

TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_spat.text: For positive `T`, the concrete mixed Leray projection supplies the abstract translation and weak estimates on time-path-valued half-Hölder fields. With coefficient and source derivative data, positive coercivity, and the compressed inverse, the theorem produces a spatial derivative of the mixed solution. It preserves both the spatial projection and zero-time-mean constraint encoded by the fixed space.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_spat.summary: Differentiate the path valued projected endpoint equation

TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_time.text: For positive `T`, the time integral of the projected path is zero at every torus label. The pointwise-in-label conclusion is stronger than an almost-everywhere representative statement because the result lies in a continuous half-Hölder space. The hypothesis `hT` makes the time-mean normalization legitimate.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_time.summary: The mixed projection has zero time mean at every label

TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_toru.text: The combined spatial and time-mean projection commutes with translations on the label torus. Its Fourier-symbol action makes this true for every interval parameter.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongMixedLeray_toru.summary: The mixed projection commutes with label translations

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray.text:
Define the concrete spatial Leray projection as a real homogeneous Fourier multiplier on half-Holder vector fields. Its fixed-space characterization and idempotence are separate theorems.

Default-value audit (b5): The Fourier multiplier is defined on all half-Holder fields. Its Leray symbol includes the zero spatial mode; mean vector fields are retained rather than silently removed. Fixed-space and projection properties are proved separately.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray.summary: The spatial Leray projection on Holder fields

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_ag.text: Embedding the strong spatial Leray projection of a real half-Hölder field in $L^2$ gives the real Hilbert-space Leray projection of the embedded field. This is an equality of operators on the shared inputs. It transfers orthogonality and the weak divergence constraint to the strong projection used in the freezing inverse.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_ag.summary: The Hölder and Hilbert Leray projections agree

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_al.text:
Let $v$ be a solenoidal half-Hölder vector field on $\mathbb T^3$ satisfying $\mathbb P(Bv)=f$. Assume this projected coefficient map already has a bounded inverse and $B$ is pointwise coercive on projected fields with a positive constant. Supply genuine half-Hölder directional derivatives of $B$ and $f$ through order $N$. Then the corresponding derivatives of $v$ exist, stay divergence free, and satisfy $\mathbb P(BD^
u v)=D^
u f-\mathbb P[D^
u,B]v$, with norm bounds using the inverse norm and lower derivatives. This supplies the differentiated equations in Lemma A.2, rather than proving the initial inverse theorem.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_al.summary: Construct successive derivatives from the base Hölder inverse

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_co.text: The complexified Fourier coefficient of the strong spatial projection equals the complex-linear extension of `angularLeray` acting on the original coefficient. This is the complex form of the already established real-character law. It is used when composing with the frozen inverse multipliers and when proving commutation with translations.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_co.summary: Spatial Leray has the complexified transverse symbol

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_fi.text: Identify the fixed space of the concrete strong Leray operator with the weakly divergence-free half-Holder subspace. This allows the freezing isomorphism to be used in the endpoint solver's space.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_fi.summary: The Leray fixed space is the solenoidal space

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_fi.text: A half-Holder field is fixed by the concrete Leray operator exactly when its L2 image is weakly divergence free. Agreement with the L2 orthogonal projection proves both directions.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_fi.summary: Leray fixed fields are exactly divergence free

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_ha.text: The Haar $L^2$ norm of a half-Hölder field cannot increase under the strong spatial Leray projection. Agreement with the orthogonal real $L^2$ Leray projector supplies the contraction. This gives the weak bound with constant one in the concrete spatial derivative argument; it is not a contraction claim for the Hölder norm.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_ha.summary: Spatial Leray contracts the embedded Hilbert norm

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_id.text: The strong spatial Leray projection is idempotent. The proof places its image in the solenoidal fixed space rather than relying on an unproved formal projection label.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_id.summary: Applying the spatial Leray projection twice

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_pa.text: For a field `v` fixed by the strong spatial Leray projection, the Haar pairing of `v` with the projection of `w` equals its pairing with `w`. The proof transfers the orthogonality of the $L^2$ projector through the embedding. This gives the exact energy pairing required by the abstract freezing theorem.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_pa.summary: Spatial Leray disappears against a projected field

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_pr.text: The actual periodic Leray projection commutes with each spatial direction.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_pr.summary: Spatial derivatives commute with the Leray projection

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_pr.text: If two half-Hölder fields form a torus directional derivative pair, applying the strong spatial Leray operator to both preserves that derivative relation at every label and line parameter. The proof uses translation invariance and agreement with the real $L^2$ projection. It supplies the hypothesis needed by the abstract first-order lift estimate.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_pr.summary: The actual Leray projection preserves line derivatives

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_re.text: At each integer Fourier mode, every real-character moment of the strong spatial projection is obtained by applying `angularLeray` to the original moment. The statement allows every complex character parameter `c`, encoding both real components of the coefficient. It includes the mean mode through the symbol value at zero.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_re.summary: Spatial Leray acts by the transverse real symbol

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_se.text: Starting from a projected first-derivative equation, the concrete spatial Leray theorem constructs its derivative in a further direction. The source includes the derivatives of both the coefficient and the existing product correction. It requires the listed derivative data and coercive inverse, and returns the second derivative with its equation and norm estimate.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_se.summary: Take a second derivative of the fixed time solution

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_sp.text: For the actual spatial Leray projection, positive coercivity, a supplied compressed equivalence, and directional derivatives `df` and `dB` yield a projected derivative `w` of `v`. The theorem records the commutator equation and inverse norm estimate. Translation commutation, the weak contraction, and the pairing identity are supplied by the concrete projector lemmas.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_sp.summary: Differentiate the concrete fixed time projected equation

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_to.text: The concrete strong spatial Leray projection commutes with every torus translation on real half-Hölder vector fields. Its previously established complex Fourier coefficient law supplies the proof. This verifies one of the abstract hypotheses needed to differentiate the compressed fixed-time equation, rather than assuming translation commutation as additional data.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialLeray_to.summary: The spatial Leray projection commutes with translations

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialProjecti.text:
Restrict the codomain of the strong Leray operator to the divergence-free half-Holder subspace. The underlying projected field is unchanged.

Default-value audit (b5): The codomain restriction uses the proved idempotence of the same concrete Leray map. It changes only the subspace type; zero fields and constant fields are handled by the ordinary projection, with no fallback branch.
TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialProjecti.summary: Leray projection with a solenoidal target

TorusEuler.endpointStrongSpatialProjecti.text: Embedding the strong spatial projection into L2 gives the same field as applying the weak L2 projection after embedding. This bridges the instantaneous equation between the two regularity spaces.

TorusEuler.endpointSubtractMean.text: For an $L^2$ path on $[0,T]$, the operator is $\mathcal Qv=v-T^{-1}\int_0^Tv(s)\,ds$, where the average is viewed as a constant path. When $T=1$ this is the projection used in Appendix A. For $T>0$ its range consists of zero-time-mean paths, whose primitives have both zero endpoint values. The formula is defined even at $T=0$ by assigning zero to the reciprocal there; that case is not an averaging operation on a positive interval. The definition alone does not assert orthogonality or compatibility with spatial projection.
TorusEuler.endpointSubtractMean.summary: Remove the constant path on an arbitrary interval

TorusEuler.endpointSubtractMean_apply.text: The mean-subtraction operator sends $v$ to $v$ minus the constant $L^2$ path with value $T^{-1}\int_0^T v$. This evaluation identity has no sign hypothesis on $T$. Its interpretation as a projection onto zero-integral paths is supplied separately under positive interval length.

TorusEuler.endpointSubtractMean_apply_ae.text: The path representative after mean subtraction equals $w(t)-T^{-1}\int_0^T w$ almost everywhere. The theorem is stated for every real `T`; positive time is needed for the intended average interpretation in application. At zero or negative `T`, the restricted time measure is empty, so the almost-everywhere assertion is vacuous.
TorusEuler.endpointSubtractMean_apply_ae.summary: Mean subtraction has its normalized time integral formula

TorusEuler.endpointSubtractMean_apply_ae.text: For an $L^2$ time path f, the fixed-label mean-removal operator agrees almost everywhere with $f(t)-T^{-1}\int f$. The theorem is valid for any real T, including an empty measured interval. It provides the representative formula used when comparing mean removal before and after embedding a spatial Hölder family of paths.

TorusEuler.endpointSubtractMean_isSymmet.text: For `hT : 0 < T`, the mean-subtraction map is symmetric and idempotent on the real vector-valued $L^2$ path space. Positive duration justifies the average factor $T^{-1}$. This strengthens the earlier norm-two estimate by identifying the map as an orthogonal projection, whose norm is at most one.
TorusEuler.endpointSubtractMean_isSymmet.summary: Time mean subtraction is an orthogonal projection

TorusEuler.endpointTemporalSpatialCorrec.text:
Sum the ordered product-rule terms in which at least one spatial derivative hits the coefficient. Only lower-order velocity words occur, which makes induction on word length possible.

Default-value audit (b5): The finite sum is zero for the empty derivative word. Every nonempty term has a positive coefficient order and lower velocity order; arbitrary input families remain allowed without any derivative compatibility until the later theorem assumes it.
TorusEuler.endpointTemporalSpatialCorrec.summary: The spatial product correction at a fixed time

TorusEuler.endpointTimeCoefficient.text: For a fixed label, form the bounded time L² multiplication operator associated with $t\mapsto K(t,a)$. The inputs `hK` and `hKsup` supply time measurability and a uniform slab bound. Spatial regularity is not needed to define this individual operator; it is needed later to bundle the family over labels.
TorusEuler.endpointTimeCoefficient.summary: A coefficient at one label multiplies time paths

TorusEuler.endpointTimeCoefficient_ae_bo.text: Fix a label `a`. The uniform coefficient bound `hKsup` on the closed slab implies $\|K(t,a)\|\le M$ for almost every time under the restricted measure. The statement uses only the slab bound, not spatial Hölder continuity. It supplies essential boundedness for the labelwise time L² multiplier.
TorusEuler.endpointTimeCoefficient_ae_bo.summary: A slab bound gives an almost everywhere path coefficient bound

TorusEuler.endpointTimeCoefficient_apply.text: Applying the time-path coefficient at label `a` agrees almost everywhere with $K(t,a)f(t)$. The theorem identifies the representative of the induced L² multiplier. It retains the explicit measurability and slab-bound inputs used in its construction, without assuming continuity in time.
TorusEuler.endpointTimeCoefficient_apply.summary: The path operator multiplies by the given time coefficient

TorusEuler.endpointTimeCoefficient_norm_.text: Assuming `hM : 0 ≤ M`, the time-path multiplier at each label has operator norm at most `M`. The bound is obtained from the pointwise coefficient bound on the closed slab. It is uniform in the label and involves no factor depending on the interval length.
TorusEuler.endpointTimeCoefficient_norm_.summary: The path multiplier inherits the slab coefficient bound

TorusEuler.endpointTimeCoefficient_norm_.text: Under `hKdif`, the difference of the time-path multipliers at labels `a` and `b` has operator norm at most $M\sqrt{d(a,b)}$. The proof compares their actions on an arbitrary L² path almost everywhere in time. Nonnegative `M` makes this a valid half-Hölder bound on the operator-valued family.
TorusEuler.endpointTimeCoefficient_norm_.summary: Spatial coefficient increments control path operator increments

TorusEuler.endpointTimeIntegral.text: Bundle the previously constructed linear partial time integral as a continuous linear map using the bound $\sqrt T$. The domain is joint time-label $L^2$ and the codomain is spatial $L^2$ for the s-finite measure `ν`. This operator defines the zero-time-integral constraint used in the endpoint subspace.
TorusEuler.endpointTimeIntegral.summary: Time integration as a bounded operator into spatial L²

TorusEuler.endpointTimeIntegralLinear.text: The partial integral becomes a real linear map from joint $L^2$ to spatial $L^2$. Addition and scalar multiplication are verified using Fubini to pass product almost-everywhere identities to almost every time path. This quotient-level argument prevents the definition from depending on arbitrary values along exceptional fibers.
TorusEuler.endpointTimeIntegralLinear.summary: Partial time integration is linear on product classes

TorusEuler.endpointTimeIntegralLinear_bo.text: For a joint $L^2$ field on a nonnegative time interval, the spatial $L^2$ norm of its partial time integral is at most $\sqrt T$ times the joint norm. Cauchy–Schwarz is applied along almost every label path and then integrated in labels. This proves continuity of the linear partial-integral map.
TorusEuler.endpointTimeIntegralLinear_bo.summary: Partial integration costs the square root of duration

TorusEuler.endpointTimeIntegralValue.text: Given a joint time-label $L^2$ class on a nonnegative interval, integrate its representative in time at each label and bundle the resulting label function into spatial $L^2$. The membership theorem justifies this construction. Subsequent identities are almost everywhere in labels, because representatives may differ on exceptional fibers.
TorusEuler.endpointTimeIntegralValue.summary: The time integral represented in spatial L²

TorusEuler.endpointTimeIntegralValue_app.text: A representative of the spatial $L^2$ value equals the time integral of the joint representative for almost every label. This is the exact `toLp` representative guarantee, with the exceptional set measured by `ν`. It does not assert that every individual label fiber has an integrable or canonical representative.
TorusEuler.endpointTimeIntegralValue_app.summary: The spatial quotient agrees with the partial time integral

TorusEuler.endpointTimeIntegral_apply_ae.text: For a joint $L^2$ class, the output of the continuous time-integral operator agrees almost everywhere in labels with integrating the selected representative over $(0,T]$. This formula connects the abstract operator to the time-mean constraint. Equality is intentionally limited to the measure-theoretic representative level.
TorusEuler.endpointTimeIntegral_apply_ae.summary: The bounded operator has the expected fiber integral

TorusEuler.endpointTimeIntegral_eq_zero_.text: The partial time-integral operator sends a joint $L^2$ class to zero exactly when its representative has zero time integral at almost every label. This identifies an algebraic kernel with the intended endpoint constraint. The conclusion remains almost everywhere in labels and does not impose a separate normalization by the interval length.
TorusEuler.endpointTimeIntegral_eq_zero_.summary: The operator kernel is the zero-integral path constraint

TorusEuler.endpointTimeIntegral_toLp_app.text: If a joint field has an $L^2$ membership proof, applying the time-integral operator to its `toLp` class gives the same label function almost everywhere as integrating the original field. The result uses Fubini to handle the representative change on time fibers. It does not strengthen product almost-everywhere equality to pointwise equality.
TorusEuler.endpointTimeIntegral_toLp_app.summary: Bundling explicit data preserves its time integral

TorusEuler.endpointTimeLp_norm_le.text: A temporal $L^2$ path bounded almost everywhere by `C` has norm at most $\sqrt T\,C$ when both `T` and `C` are nonnegative. The factor comes from the measure of $(0,T]$. This supplies the duration dependence when a continuous spatial source is represented as a Hölder field of time paths.
TorusEuler.endpointTimeLp_norm_le.summary: A bounded path gains a square-root time factor

TorusEuler.endpointTimeMultiplier.text:
Define multiplication by an operator curve continuous on the closed interval as a bounded operator on temporal L2. Compactness supplies its essential bound, and only values in the restricted time measure are relevant.

Default-value audit (b5): The chosen essential bound exists by continuity on a compact interval. It only constructs the same multiplication operator, not an arbitrary action. At nonpositive duration the restricted L2 space is trivial.
TorusEuler.endpointTimeMultiplier.summary: A continuous time coefficient on square integrable paths

TorusEuler.endpointTimeMultiplier_apply_.text: The bounded time multiplication operator agrees almost everywhere with application of the given coefficient to the L2 path representative.
TorusEuler.endpointTimeMultiplier_apply_.summary: The time multiplier acts pointwise almost everywhere

TorusEuler.endpointTimeParityPart.text: Applies the spatial reflection average independently to each time slice of a field. Time is neither reversed nor shifted. This makes it possible to select odd endpoint velocities and displacements and even pressure while retaining the same initial and terminal times in the forced mean equation.
TorusEuler.endpointTimeParityPart.summary: Select a spatial parity component at each time

TorusEuler.endpointTorusDivergenceTest.text: This continuous linear functional pairs a joint path with a bounded time test times the gradient of a smooth periodic scalar potential. Requiring every such pairing to vanish encodes weak spatial divergence freedom. No pointwise derivative of the $L^2$ velocity is needed or claimed in this definition.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusDivergenceTest.summary: Testing spatial divergence with separated time factors

TorusEuler.endpointTorusDivergenceTest_a.text: Evaluating the divergence test gives the joint integral of the bounded time factor times the inner product of the spatial potential gradient with the velocity. This is the standard weak divergence pairing. The time dependence of the testing factor remains arbitrary within bounded measurable functions.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusDivergenceTest_a.summary: The divergence test integrates a gradient pairing

TorusEuler.endpointTorusDivergenceTests_.text: For one fixed smooth potential `p`, all bounded time tests vanish exactly when its spatial gradient pairing with the velocity vanishes for almost every time. The potential is fixed outside the almost-everywhere assertion. A common full-measure set for every potential requires the later compatibility argument.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusDivergenceTests_.summary: A fixed potential has zero pairing at almost every time

TorusEuler.endpointTorusDivergenceTests_.text: Assume that at almost every time a joint L² velocity has a spatial representative with a C¹ divergence-free Euclidean lift. Then all its weak time-weighted gradient tests vanish. The slice representative may vary with time and need only agree almost everywhere in labels; no jointly smooth lift is required by the theorem.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusDivergenceTests_.summary: Classically solenoidal slices satisfy all weak tests

TorusEuler.endpointTorusDivergenceTests_.text: Given a square-integrable joint function `g`, suppose almost every time slice has a C¹ divergence-free lift. The quotient element `hg.toLp g` then passes every weak spatial gradient test. The proof tracks almost-everywhere agreement of the chosen L² representative with `g`, so quotient construction does not lose the solenoidal condition.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusDivergenceTests_.summary: A square integrable classical field enters the weak space

TorusEuler.endpointTorusFlowOperator.text: Builds the bounded operator $v\mapsto Kv-J(\Omega v)$ on joint time-label $L^2$, with $K=F^*F$ and $\Omega=F^*(M^*-M)F$. The duration is nonnegative and both coefficient fields are continuous on the slab. This ambient operator does not itself enforce solenoidality or zero time mean; those restrictions enter through the endpoint subspace.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusFlowOperator.summary: The endpoint operator on space-time velocities

TorusEuler.endpointTorusFlowOperator_app.text: For any joint $L^2$ velocity, the bounded endpoint operator agrees almost everywhere with the kinetic multiplier minus the time primitive of the pulled-back vorticity multiplier at each label. The equality is for representatives, not for every space-time point. Nonnegative duration and continuity of `F` and `M` are precisely the data used to build the operator.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusFlowOperator_app.summary: The weak operator has the expected pointwise formula

TorusEuler.endpointTorusGradientPairing_.text: Let `g` on the torus be represented by a C¹ Euclidean lift `v` through `hrep`. If `hdiv` makes its divergence vanish everywhere, its Haar pairing with every smooth potential gradient is zero. Periodicity of the lift is derived from the torus representation, then periodic integration by parts proves the weak condition.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusGradientPairing_.summary: A classical solenoidal lift annihilates torus gradients

TorusEuler.endpointTorusGradientPairing_.text: For a smooth periodic lift, vanishing pairing with every smooth periodic potential gradient is equivalent to pointwise zero divergence. The reverse implication uses integration by parts; the forward implication tests against the divergence and uses continuity after an L2 identity.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusGradientPairing_.summary: Weak gradient annihilation equals zero classical divergence

TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.text:
Specify a Holder field as the directional derivative of another by requiring the derivative identity along every translated torus line at every real line parameter. This is a predicate about an actual supplied derivative field.

Default-value audit (b5): The supplied derivative field must satisfy HasDerivAt along every line. In zero direction that identity forces the derivative field to be zero; no arbitrary derivative default is used.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.summary: A spatial directional derivative on torus lines

TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.text: If two half-Hölder fields have directional derivatives along the same fixed torus direction, their sum has the sum of those derivatives. The proof evaluates the fields along each translated torus line and uses the ordinary derivative sum rule. It supports the finite linear combinations arising from the differentiated mean forcing.

For a finite family of half-Hölder fields, if each indexed field has the stated derivative in one common torus direction, then their finite sum has the corresponding summed derivative. The empty finite set gives the usual derivative of zero. This rule keeps all terms when the mean forcing is assembled from finitely many product contributions.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.summary: Finite sums retain their torus derivatives

TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.text: Multiplication of a half-Hölder field by a natural number preserves its torus directional derivative, with the same natural multiple of the derivative field. The statement uses repeated addition, matching the integer multiplicities in the product rule. It does not itself state a rule for arbitrary real or time-dependent scalar multiplication.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.summary: Natural multiplicities pass through torus derivatives

TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.text: For two half-Hölder fields with derivatives in the same torus direction, the derivative of their difference is the difference of the derivatives. This follows pointwise along each torus line from the usual subtraction rule. It is needed for the signed coefficient corrections in the time-differentiated mean equation.

For time-smooth curves forming a spatial directional derivative pair on a positive closed interval, every available within-time derivative remains a spatial derivative pair. The endpoint derivative is taken within the interval.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.summary: Time derivatives preserve spatial derivative relations

TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.text: If `df` is the torus directional derivative of `f`, then `-df` is that derivative of `-f`. The assertion follows by negating the derivative identity along every torus line. It transfers the sign in the integrated source $L=-\int g$ to each spatial derivative word.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.summary: Negation preserves the torus derivative relation

TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.text: If `df` is the torus directional derivative of `f`, every nonzero-step difference quotient differs from `df` at the starting label by at most $\|df\|\sqrt{|h|\|u\|}$. The estimate holds in any complete real normed target. It upgrades a known derivative relation to a uniform quantitative remainder bound.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.summary: A half-Hölder derivative controls the spatial slope error

TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.text: If two half-Hölder-valued curves form a spatial derivative pair throughout $[0,T]$ and both have within-interval derivatives at `t`, their time derivatives form the same spatial derivative pair. Positive duration provides uniqueness of derivatives within the closed interval. The result includes endpoint times and requires no extension of the curves beyond the slab.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.summary: Time differentiation preserves the spatial derivative relation

TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.text: For half-Hölder curves in any real normed target, within-slab time differentiation preserves a spatial directional derivative relation when both curves have the required time derivatives. Positive duration ensures a nontrivial punctured within-slab filter at the evaluation time. The proof obtains uniform convergence along every torus line from the stronger half-Hölder norm, including at time endpoints.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.summary: Uniform line convergence preserves mixed derivatives

TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.text: If all nonzero directional difference quotients of a half-Hölder field equal segment averages of another half-Hölder field, that second field is its torus directional derivative. The average error tends to zero as the step tends to zero. The statement gives a genuine derivative at every label along every line, not merely an almost-everywhere derivative.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.summary: Segment averages determine the actual spatial derivative

TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.text: If every nonzero directional difference quotient differs from a candidate derivative by at most $C\sqrt{|h|\|u\|}$ at every label, that candidate is the actual torus line derivative. The error tends to zero with the step. No separate sign condition on `C` is needed, because the assumed nonnegative norm bound already controls the relevant remainder.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.summary: A square-root remainder proves spatial differentiability

TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.text: Two half-Hölder fields satisfying the same torus directional derivative relation for a common field and direction are equal. Evaluating the line-derivative identities at parameter zero gives pointwise uniqueness, and extensionality gives equality of fields. This identifies the differentiated source with the prescribed force derivative in the primitive argument.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusHasSpatialDeriva.summary: A torus directional derivative has unique values

TorusEuler.endpointTorusMeanTest.text: This continuous linear functional pairs an endpoint path with a bounded spatial scalar times one coordinate unit vector. Vanishing for all such tests imposes zero time integral componentwise at almost every label. The definition itself is a Hilbert pairing; the almost-everywhere characterization is proved later.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusMeanTest.summary: Testing each component of the time integral

TorusEuler.endpointTorusMeanTest_apply.text: Evaluating the coordinate mean test gives the joint integral of the spatial scalar test times that velocity component. This unfolds the Hilbert-space definition into a familiar scalar integral. It is the form used for Fubini and for detecting vanishing time integrals by all bounded spatial tests.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusMeanTest_apply.summary: The mean test integrates a weighted velocity component

TorusEuler.endpointTorusMeanTests_iff_ae.text: Vanishing of every coordinate mean test is equivalent to the vector-valued time integral being zero for almost every torus label. Fubini moves the time integral inside the spatial pairing, and bounded-test detection handles each coordinate. Finitely many coordinates can share one full-measure set.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusMeanTests_iff_ae.summary: The mean tests detect zero time integral at almost every label

TorusEuler.endpointTorusMeasure.text: This measure is Lebesgue measure restricted to $(0,T]$ multiplied by normalized Haar measure on the unit three-torus. It provides the joint space-time $L^2$ environment for the endpoint problem. The half-open time interval differs from the closed interval only at a null endpoint when duration is positive.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusMeasure.summary: Product measure for time paths on the spatial torus

TorusEuler.endpointTorusMeasure_finite.text: For every real `T`, the endpoint product measure is finite. The time factor is a bounded restricted interval and the spatial factor is a probability measure. This instance justifies the later inclusion of square-integrable paths into integrable paths and the bounded-test constructions.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusMeasure_finite.summary: The joint time and torus measure is finite

TorusEuler.endpointTorusSpace.text:
Define the joint endpoint-velocity space as the intersection of the kernels of all time-mean tests and all spatial divergence tests. Both constraints are weak and representative independent.

Default-value audit (b5): The constraint space is defined by intersections of kernels of continuous tests, including zero time mean and weak divergence. No pointwise representative or smoothness is chosen; at a zero time measure the space is trivial.

TorusEuler.endpointTorusSpace_eq_timeKer.text: For a nonnegative slab, the endpoint subspace is the intersection of the kernel of time integration and the joint weakly solenoidal submodule. This separates the final-displacement constraint from incompressibility. The equality is between submodules of the same joint $L^2$ space; it does not equate a time derivative with a classical function at every point.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusSpace_eq_timeKer.summary: Both endpoint constraints as an intersection

TorusEuler.endpointTorusSpace_starProjec.text: For hT : 0 < T, the orthogonal projection onto the endpoint space equals spatial solenoidal projection composed with time-mean removal. Multiplication of continuous linear maps denotes composition, so the rightmost operation acts first. The proof uses the intersection description, commutation, and the characterization of an orthogonal projection by membership and orthogonality. It concerns the joint Hilbert space, without asserting Hölder boundedness.

TorusEuler.endpointTorusTimeIntegral.text:
Define the bounded time integral of a joint time-label L2 field, with values in spatial L2. Nonnegative duration supplies the finite-interval construction.

Default-value audit (b5): The definition takes T nonnegative; T zero gives a zero-measure time interval and the zero integration map. It acts on L2 classes, so pointwise exceptional slices are not prescribed.

TorusEuler.endpointTorusTimeIntegral_adj.text: For hT : 0 ≤ T, the adjoint of time integration sends a spatial field v to its constant-in-time lift, almost everywhere on $(0,T]\times\mathbb T^3$. The proof tests against an arbitrary joint $L^2$ field and uses Fubini and the adjoint identity. This identifies the operator needed to subtract the temporal mean; it does not assert pointwise regularity of an $L^2$ representative.

Integrating the constant lift of a spatial field v gives $T v$ as an equality in spatial $L^2$. The binder hT : 0 ≤ T identifies the measure of $(0,T]$ with $T$. The adjoint supplies the constant lift, and almost-everywhere representative identities justify integrating it. The formula remains valid when $T=0$.

The constant-in-time adjoint lift of a solenoidal spatial field is jointly solenoidal. The proof identifies its almost-everywhere time slices with the original field and tests against gradients. The hypotheses are hT : 0 ≤ T and hw, the weak divergence constraint on the spatial input; no spatial regularity beyond $L^2$ is claimed.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusTimeIntegral_adj.summary: A constant lift preserves zero divergence

TorusEuler.endpointTorusTimeIntegral_app.text: For nonnegative duration, the torus partial-integral operator agrees almost everywhere in the torus variable with the ordinary interval integral from zero to `T`. This changes the restricted-set integral notation to the interval notation used in the paper. It preserves the quotient-space, almost-everywhere meaning of the output.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusTimeIntegral_app.summary: On the torus the operator equals the oriented time integral

TorusEuler.endpointTorusTimeIntegral_end.text: For hT : 0 < T, the time integral of $Qu$ is zero. The proof expands $Q$, uses $JJ^*v=Tv$, and cancels the nonzero scalar $T$. This is an equality in spatial $L^2$, hence encodes zero time mean at almost every label. It does not by itself select a continuous representative.

TorusEuler.endpointTorusTimeIntegral_eq_.text: For nonnegative duration, the joint time integral vanishes exactly when the time primitive at the terminal time vanishes for almost every label. This is the time-mean endpoint constraint in slice form.
TorusEuler.endpointTorusTimeIntegral_eq_.summary: Zero time integral in joint and labelwise form

TorusEuler.endpointTorusTimeIntegral_mem.text: With hT : 0 ≤ T, a joint weakly solenoidal field has a solenoidal time integral in spatial $L^2$. The proof uses the constant time test and rewrites the resulting joint pairing through the adjoint of integration. The input constraint hu is essential; integrating an arbitrary joint field does not supply divergence freedom.

TorusEuler.endpointTorus_inner_test_eq.text: For a test field with `hf : MemLp`, its bounded Hilbert functional on an endpoint path equals the integral of their real inner product. The proof replaces the chosen $L^2$ representative of the test by its original function almost everywhere. This validates the concrete formulas for both endpoint constraints.
TorusEuler.endpointTorus_inner_test_eq.summary: A Hilbert test equals its integral pairing

TorusEuler.endpointWeakCoefficient.text:
Turn a spatial half-Holder operator field into a bounded multiplication operator on spatial L2. Its essential measurability and bound follow from the Holder field; compatibility with strong multiplication is proved elsewhere.

Default-value audit (b5): The input is already a half-Holder coefficient, so boundedness and measurability are available. The operator acts on L2 equivalence classes; representative values on null sets have no mathematical role, and no ellipticity is asserted.
TorusEuler.endpointWeakCoefficient.summary: The spatial coefficient acting in square integral norm

TorusEuler.endpointWeakCoefficientEquiv.text: Positive `κ` and the pointwise lower bound `hK` produce a continuous linear equivalence on the weak solenoidal spatial subspace. Its forward map is multiplication by `K` followed by orthogonal projection. This is weak Hilbert-space invertibility; the definition does not itself provide a half-Hölder inverse estimate.
TorusEuler.endpointWeakCoefficientEquiv.summary: The projected weak kinetic coefficient is invertible

TorusEuler.endpointWeakCoefficientEquiv_.text: Applying the weak coefficient equivalence to a solenoidal vector gives the projected Hilbert operator associated with `endpointWeakCoefficient K`. This identifies the forward action of the abstract inverse construction. The same positive ellipticity hypotheses remain explicit, so the equivalence is tied to the intended projected equation.
TorusEuler.endpointWeakCoefficientEquiv_.summary: The equivalence acts as projected coefficient multiplication

TorusEuler.endpointWeakCoefficient_apply.text: For spatial $L^2$ input `v`, the representative of `endpointWeakCoefficient K v` equals $K(a)v(a)$ almost everywhere on the torus. The coefficient is half-Hölder and therefore measurable and bounded. The assertion identifies representatives of a quotient-space operator and does not claim equality on every exceptional point.
TorusEuler.endpointWeakCoefficient_apply.summary: Weak multiplication agrees with the pointwise coefficient action

TorusEuler.endpointWeakCoefficient_coerc.text: If `hK` bounds $\langle K(a)z,z\rangle$ below by $\kappa\|z\|^2$ at every label and vector, multiplication by `K` has the same lower bound in spatial $L^2$. Integration preserves the constant. Positivity of `κ` is not required for this inequality, but is required to construct an inverse.
TorusEuler.endpointWeakCoefficient_coerc.summary: Pointwise ellipticity gives the same weak quadratic bound

TorusEuler.endpointWeakInstant_of_subtra.text: Let a square-integrable path $w$ equal $\mathbb P(Kv-J(\Omega v)+L)$ almost everywhere and satisfy $\mathcal Qw=0$, where $\mathcal Q$ subtracts its time average. Then $\mathbb P(Kv)=c+\mathbb PJ(\Omega v)-\mathbb PL$ almost everywhere, with $c=T^{-1}\int_0^Tw$. This is (A.9) before recovery of a continuous representative. The formal statement allows arbitrary bounded linear maps and general normed spaces; it does not derive regularity of the right side. On the normalized interval of the paper, the average is simply the integral. Here $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$.
TorusEuler.endpointWeakInstant_of_subtra.summary: Restore the average removed by the time projection

TorusEuler.endpointWeakInstantaneous_of_.text: Assume positive `T`, measurable bounded coefficients `K` and `Ω`, and the joint weak identity `hweak` with source $-L$. The theorem extracts the spatially projected time average `c` and obtains the instantaneous projected equation for almost every time. This precedes the separate argument selecting a continuous representative; the assertion is not yet pointwise for every time.
TorusEuler.endpointWeakInstantaneous_of_.summary: Recover the instantaneous weak endpoint equation

TorusEuler.endpointWeakResidualProjected.text: If a joint residual is orthogonal to every solenoidal zero-time-mean test, its weak spatial projection equals the projection of its time average for almost every time. A countable reduction makes the equality simultaneous for all spatial test vectors.
TorusEuler.endpointWeakResidualProjected.summary: A weak residual equals its projected time average

TorusEuler.endpointWeakSpatialProjection.text:
Define the L2 orthogonal projection onto the closed weak solenoidal space, with its codomain restricted to that space. It is the Hilbert-space counterpart of the strong Holder projection.

Default-value audit (b5): The projection uses completeness of the closed weak solenoidal subspace. It is a globally defined orthogonal projection on spatial L2 and has no noninvertible-coefficient fallback.

TorusEuler.endpointWeightedPhysicalMeanE.text: Given the physical word recurrence, a common weighted source bound and inverse-weighted positive coefficient bounds, every derivative word satisfies $\ell^{|q|}\|g_q\|_{C_t}\le A_{\rm inv}M_f(1+2^NC)^{|q|}$. All scalar bounds and the duration are nonnegative. The theorem applies the abstract derivative induction to closed-time norms; it assumes the recurrence rather than constructing the physical solution.
TorusEuler.endpointWeightedPhysicalMeanE.summary: Lift the physical recurrence without repeated inverse losses

TorusEuler.endpointWeightedPhysicalMeanE.text: The physical lifting estimate needs forcing, coefficient and recurrence bounds only for sorted words through order $N$. Every correction pair remains a sublist of the original word, so the induction stays within that family. The proof extends the scalar data by zero on unsorted words internally; the conclusion is asserted only for sorted words, where the supplied data remain unchanged.
TorusEuler.endpointWeightedPhysicalMeanE.summary: Sorted multi-indices suffice for derivative lifting

TorusEuler.endpointWordLift.text: Packages a half-Hölder torus field as a bounded continuous function on Euclidean three-space by composing with the quotient map. The construction is continuous linear and retains the field’s periodic values. It provides a normed target in which time differentiation can be combined with spatial evaluation for the joint smoothness proof.
TorusEuler.endpointWordLift.summary: The bounded periodic lift of a spatial field

TorusEuler.endpointWordLift_apply.text: The bounded Euclidean lift of a half-Hölder field evaluates at `x` to that field’s value at `toUnitTorus x`. The statement is a definitional equality and holds with no smoothness assumptions. It lets the joint-derivative proof replace the bundled lift by the manuscript’s periodic spatial function.
TorusEuler.endpointWordLift_apply.summary: The lifted word is evaluation at the quotient label

TorusEuler.endpointWord_hasFDerivWithinA.text: A time derivative in the norm of bounded continuous functions, together with a spatial Fréchet derivative at the evaluation point, yields the joint derivative on the time-set product. Its linear map adds the time component and the spatial component. The uniform function norm controls the cross term, so separate pointwise differentiability alone would not supply this conclusion.
TorusEuler.endpointWord_hasFDerivWithinA.summary: Combining time and spatial derivatives of evaluation

TorusEuler.endpoint_integral_hasDerivWit.text: For a continuous `f` on $[0,T]$ and `t` in that interval, its primitive from zero has derivative `f t` within the same interval. The statement covers the endpoints using `HasDerivWithinAt`. It supplies the fundamental theorem of calculus step when differentiating the integrated label momentum equation.
TorusEuler.endpoint_integral_hasDerivWit.summary: Differentiate the time primitive within the closed interval

TorusEuler.envelopeCutoff.text: The scalar cutoff is $1-\mathrm{smoothTransition}(s-1)$. It equals one for $s\le1$ and zero for $s\ge2$, providing the radial envelope used after substituting $s=\|a\|/\ell$. This declaration defines the scalar function only; positivity of the spatial scale belongs to the radial-envelope lemmas.
TorusEuler.envelopeCutoff.summary: A smooth cutoff between radii one and two

TorusEuler.eqOn_iteratedFDeriv_gradient_.text: On an open target set separated from the far source, the lifted multiplier pressure and kernel pressure have equal gradient jets at every order. The representative hypothesis matches the cutoff tensor on the fundamental cell. Equality on an open neighborhood gives equality of derivatives even before any regularity is separately invoked.
TorusEuler.eqOn_iteratedFDeriv_gradient_.summary: Local pressure equality identifies all gradient jets

TorusEuler.eqOn_lift_farPressureTensorMu.text: A half Hölder torus tensor whose lift matches the far cutoff tensor on the fundamental cell has pressure equal to the corresponding separated kernel integral on `U`. The support lemma removes all cell points outside the far source set. Equality of representatives is required only on that cell; periodic separation is required for every target point.
TorusEuler.eqOn_lift_farPressureTensorMu.summary: The actual multiplier agrees with the far kernel on separated targets

TorusEuler.eqOn_pressureTensorDyadicLift.text: For a smooth periodic velocity and smooth periodic cutoff supported off the lattice, full dyadic pressure equals the sum of the near dyadic pressure and far kernel pressure on any target set separated from the far source. The identity descends both tensor pieces to half Hölder fields, applies multiplier linearity, then uses separated kernel agreement.
TorusEuler.eqOn_pressureTensorDyadicLift.summary: Full pressure splits into near multiplier and far kernel

TorusEuler.eq_L2_of_mFourierCoeff_eq.text: Two spatial L² fields in a complete complex normed target are equal if their Fourier coefficients agree at every lattice frequency. Apply the zero-coefficient theorem to their difference, with integrability justifying coefficient subtraction. The conclusion is equality of L² classes, not equality of arbitrary representatives at every label.
TorusEuler.eq_L2_of_mFourierCoeff_eq.summary: Fourier coefficients determine Banach valued L² fields

TorusEuler.eq_endpointPrimitive_of_close.text: On a positive closed interval, a smooth periodic solenoidal velocity whose projected residual is `R` equals its initial value plus the time primitive of residual minus projected tensor divergence. The proof first identifies the actual within derivative and then applies the fundamental theorem of calculus. No separate continuity hypothesis for `R` is needed.
TorusEuler.eq_endpointPrimitive_of_close.summary: The stage equation integrates from the initial slice

TorusEuler.eq_halfHolder_of_mFourierCoef.text: Two half-Hölder fields are equal if the Fourier coefficients of their underlying continuous fields agree at every frequency. Continuous Fourier uniqueness identifies their values, and extensionality identifies the bundled objects. The theorem does not require a Fourier series to converge in the half-Hölder norm.
TorusEuler.eq_halfHolder_of_mFourierCoef.summary: Fourier coefficients determine a half Hölder field

TorusEuler.eq_of_mFourierCoeff_eq.text: Two continuous fields valued in a complete complex normed space are equal when every Fourier coefficient agrees. If values differed at one point, Hahn–Banach would supply a scalar functional detecting the difference, contradicting scalar Fourier uniqueness. This separates functions without requiring a basis or finite-dimensional target.
TorusEuler.eq_of_mFourierCoeff_eq.summary: Continuous Banach valued fields are determined by Fourier coefficients

TorusEuler.eq_of_mFourierCoeff_eq_comple.text: Two complex continuous torus functions are equal if all their Fourier coefficients agree. The proof embeds them into scalar L² and uses injectivity of Fourier coordinates, then returns to continuous functions using full support of Haar measure. This provides pointwise function equality, not only an almost-everywhere identification.
TorusEuler.eq_of_mFourierCoeff_eq_comple.summary: Complex continuous torus functions are determined by coefficients

TorusEuler.eq_sum_evaluated_basis.text: Assumes every continuous real linear measurement of `g` belongs to one finite-dimensional scalar function space `W`. It then writes `g` in the fixed basis of `W` with coefficients in the original normed value space. Separation by continuous linear functionals proves equality. Completeness of that value space is not required by the statement.
TorusEuler.eq_sum_evaluated_basis.summary: Recovering a vector field from scalar coordinates

TorusEuler.eq_zero_L2_of_all_mFourierCoe.text: If every Fourier coefficient of a Banach-valued spatial L² field is zero, the field itself is zero. Scalar functionals reduce the claim to scalar Fourier uniqueness. The proof explicitly uses the essentially separable range of a strongly measurable representative, avoiding an unjustified common null set over an uncountable family of functionals.
TorusEuler.eq_zero_L2_of_all_mFourierCoe.summary: Vanishing Fourier coefficients force a Banach valued L² field to vanish

TorusEuler.eq_zero_of_integral_norm_sq_c.text: A continuous periodic vector field with zero cell integral of its squared norm vanishes at every point. The proof descends the field to the torus, obtains almost-everywhere vanishing from the nonnegative integral, and uses continuity to strengthen it to pointwise vanishing. This is the last step of the velocity uniqueness energy argument.
TorusEuler.eq_zero_of_integral_norm_sq_c.summary: Zero energy determines the zero periodic field

TorusEuler.eulerMomentum_of_prefix_dynam.text: Assuming the derivative on every closed prefix equals minus advection and the gradient of the same pressure, this proves the zero-residual momentum equation on the half-open solution interval. The result only assembles that identity; regularity, pressure normalization, periodicity and zero divergence remain separate requirements of `IsEulerSolution`.
TorusEuler.eulerMomentum_of_prefix_dynam.summary: The prefix identities give the Euler momentum equation

TorusEuler.eulerianMomentum_of_strongLab.text: At a specified time, suppose $F_t=MF$, $v_t$ exists, and $F$ has a bounded right inverse. If $F^TFv_t+F^Tq_x=F^Tf-2F^TMFv$, then $B=Fv$ has a time derivative and satisfies $B_t+MB+q_x=f$. Here $q_x$ denotes the pressure gradient expressed in physical coordinates along the trajectory. The conclusion is pointwise in a real Hilbert space. In Theorem 4.2 it is the momentum conversion after setting $F=D_aX$; the spatial change of variables and incompressibility still require separate flow identities.
TorusEuler.eulerianMomentum_of_strongLab.summary: Convert the label equation to the transported correction

TorusEuler.evalPeriodicMomentumJetZero.text: This bounded linear map extracts the zeroth component of a completed order zero tuple, evaluates it at `x`, and identifies the zero argument multilinear map with a vector. It lets convergence of completed momentum tuples imply convergence of the actual momentum at a fixed spatial point.
TorusEuler.evalPeriodicMomentumJetZero.summary: The zeroth completed jet evaluates to a vector

TorusEuler.evalPeriodicMomentumJetZero_a.text: Evaluating the extended order zero momentum tuple of two smooth inputs returns their actual signed projected momentum at `x`. The two inputs are taken through order two. The proof combines the agreement of the extension on smooth tuples with the canonical interpretation of the zeroth derivative.
TorusEuler.evalPeriodicMomentumJetZero_a.summary: Zeroth jet evaluation recovers the momentum value

TorusEuler.eval_endpointSourceDerivative.text: If evaluating the $C^1$ half-Hölder source curve gives minus the primitive of a continuous vector function, evaluating its within-interval derivative gives the negative of that function. The equality `hEval` is required at all slab times. Strict positivity of `T` identifies the two within derivatives, including at the endpoints.
TorusEuler.eval_endpointSourceDerivative.summary: The integrated force differentiates to its negative

TorusEuler.eval_halfHolderGradientProduc.text: Evaluation of the bundled Hölder product is exactly multiplication of the two evaluated operators in the stated order. The identity is definitional and introduces no smoothness or gradient hypothesis. It lets the source comparison pass between field algebra and matrix algebra at a spatial label.

TorusEuler.eval_halfHolderTorusDifferenc.text: Evaluation of the torus difference quotient at `a` equals $h^{-1}$ times the difference between the values at `a + toUnitTorus (h • u)` and `a`. The identity holds even at zero step because both sides use the same totalized inverse. Derivative statements later exclude the zero step when dividing increments.
TorusEuler.eval_halfHolderTorusDifferenc.summary: Evaluate the directional quotient as a difference of values

TorusEuler.eval_homogeneousHalfHolderMul.text: For a symbol smooth away from zero with `A 0 = 0`, a torus half Hölder input supported in a compact set separated from `x` has multiplier value equal to the corresponding periodic kernel integral. The support condition is imposed on the fundamental cell. The proof passes finite dyadic convolution identities to the limit with absolute integral bounds.
TorusEuler.eval_homogeneousHalfHolderMul.summary: The bounded multiplier agrees with its separated kernel integral

TorusEuler.eval_lift_recoveredSpatialWor.text: A smooth base field and a family of torus representatives are assumed to agree at the empty word and to satisfy the spatial derivative relation at every lower order. Induction then identifies each recovered representative with the corresponding ordinary spatial derivative word. Uniqueness of line derivatives makes this an identity for the same base field, not merely an existence assertion.
TorusEuler.eval_lift_recoveredSpatialWor.summary: Recovered derivative fields equal the actual lift derivatives

TorusEuler.eval_meanPressureGradientComp.text: Evaluation of the bundled gradient-composition field at a point gives the first operator composed with the second. This is a definitional equality that removes the Hölder wrapper before comparing the source to the physical Poisson equation. It clarifies the multiplication order appearing under the trace.
TorusEuler.eval_meanPressureGradientComp.summary: Evaluate the Hölder product as operator composition

TorusEuler.eval_pressureHessianMultiplie.text: An entry of the real multiplier output equals the real part of the corresponding entry of its complex continuous lift. The proof unfolds the real-operator extraction and identifies real and complex coordinate vectors. This connects the entrywise complex Fourier uniqueness result to equality of the real operator fields.
TorusEuler.eval_pressureHessianMultiplie.summary: The real Hessian entry is the real complex entry

TorusEuler.eval_pressureTensorMultiplier.text: For a half Hölder tensor supported in a compact cell source set separated from the observation point, the real Fourier pressure multiplier equals `periodicFarPressure`. The proof uses the complex multiplier agreement and proves integrability before moving real part through the integral. The support assumption is precisely the condition that all omitted cell sources vanish.
TorusEuler.eval_pressureTensorMultiplier.summary: The Fourier pressure multiplier equals the far integral on separated data

TorusEuler.eval_realifyHalfHolderMultipl.text: At any spatial point $a$, evaluation of the realified operator on $f$ equals the real part of the value of $L$ applied to the pointwise complex embedding of $f$. The formula unfolds the two Hölder mapping operations and makes subsequent estimates or identities possible at the level of actual point values.

TorusEuler.eval_sub_homogeneousHalfHolde.text: For two spatial labels, the difference of full multiplier outputs equals the difference of the dyadic outputs alone. The mean contribution is a constant field, so it cancels exactly. This identity allows off-support increment estimates to ignore the separately handled zero mode without dropping its contribution to the overall supremum norm.
TorusEuler.eval_sub_homogeneousHalfHolde.summary: The zero mode disappears from spatial increments

TorusEuler.eval_torusHalfHolderDirection.text: Evaluating the bundled directional field at a label equals applying the original operator field there to the chosen direction. This is a definitional identity.
