TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_fourierMode.summary: The Fourier character derivative is its value times phase

TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_frozenSymbol.text: As a function of the bounded operator $r$, the frozen symbol has Fréchet derivative `frozenSymbolDerivative r B`. The proof differentiates both occurrences of $r$ in $rBr$ and the subtraction in $I-r$. It applies on the whole operator space, without projection, positivity, or completeness assumptions.
TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_frozenSymbol.summary: Differentiating compression with the coefficient held fixed

TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_frozenSymbol_inve.text: At a symmetric projection with positive coercivity, the frozen inverse is Fréchet differentiable as the projection-variable operator varies. Its derivative sends an increment to minus the inverse, the direct-symbol derivative, and the inverse in that order. The theorem differentiates in the ambient operator space, not merely along projections.
TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_frozenSymbol_inve.summary: The derivative of the inverse has three operator factors

TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_inductionPrimaryW.text: Fix a time $t$, a differentiable label map $A(t,\cdot)$ with $A(t,0)=0$ and derivative $M$, and an amplitude differentiable at the origin. Use the supplied radial envelope with radius $\ell>0$, $2\ell<1/2$, and the normalized profile $F_h$ with $0<h\le1$. For any scalar multiplier $\chi(t)$, the formal theorem gives the central derivative of the periodically extended transported leading wave as $\chi(t)\mathbf a(t,0)\otimes(M^Tk)$. Here $k$ is the initial wave vector and $M^Tk=\kappa(t,0)$. The vanishing $F_h(0)=0$ and slope $F_h'(0)=1$ remove other product-rule terms. The statement allows general differentiable label maps; it does not require a full Euler flow.
TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_inductionPrimaryW.summary: Localization preserves the prescribed rank-one derivative at zero

TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_labelSlice.text: The hypothesis `hV` gives differentiability on the product of a closed time interval and all labels. At any allowed `ht`, fixing time yields an ordinary Fréchet derivative in the label variable. Its value is the within-domain derivative composed with the inclusion into the second factor, so no extension beyond the temporal endpoints is required.
TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_labelSlice.summary: Spatial differentiation of a slab-restricted function

TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_materialAccelerat.text: For a jointly $C^2$ velocity on `I × univ` and a trajectory satisfying its flow equation at `t`, the spatial derivative of material acceleration is the trajectory derivative of the velocity gradient plus its square. `I` must have unique derivatives and lie in the closure of its interior. These hypotheses permit the identity at closed-slab endpoints.
TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_materialAccelerat.summary: Material acceleration differentiates to the trajectory gradient equation

TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_of_continuous_lin.text: If a continuous linear-map field `D` gives the derivative of `f` along every affine line at every parameter, then `D x` is the Fréchet derivative at `x`. The proof estimates the remainder along the segment from `x` to a nearby point. Continuity is required in operator norm, not just separately in each direction.
TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_of_continuous_lin.summary: A continuous field of line derivatives gives the full derivative

TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_of_endpointCoordi.text: For a function on three-dimensional Euclidean space, line derivatives in all three coordinate directions determine its Fréchet derivative at `x` when the prescribed derivative columns are continuous there. The resulting linear map is the sum of coordinate projections multiplied by those columns. The line-derivative hypotheses hold at every base point and line parameter, a stronger input than derivatives only at `x`.
TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_of_endpointCoordi.summary: Continuous coordinate derivatives determine the full derivative

TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_of_uniform_spatia.text: On an open spatial set, uniform convergence of the approximating functions and their supplied differentials identifies the differential of the limit. The premise `hderiv` links each `DU j` to `U j`. The conclusion is local at `x ∈ s`; this theorem does not infer derivative convergence from convergence of values alone.
TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_of_uniform_spatia.summary: The uniform derivative limit is the actual derivative

TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_periodicFarMultip.text: When `x-y` lies off the lattice, differentiating the order `d` kernel action in the target gives the curried order `d+1` action. The source point and density vector are held fixed. The proof combines kernel smoothness with the derivative of translation and bounded linear output evaluation.
TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_periodicFarMultip.summary: Successive far kernel jets are actual derivatives

TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_phaseInterval.text: If the profile and its parameter derivative are jointly continuous and `hderiv` identifies that derivative pointwise, then a phase integral over fixed endpoints has derivative equal to the integral of `df`. The hypotheses justify this exchange. The parameter space is proper and the target complete, as specified by the surrounding section.
TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_phaseInterval.summary: Differentiating a phase integral under the integral sign

TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_planeWave.text: Fix $\mathbf a,k,x\in\mathbb R^3$, and assume $F$ has derivative $d$ at $k\cdot x$. The formal statement gives the spatial derivative of $y\mapsto F(k\cdot y)\mathbf a$ at $x$ as the linear map $v\mapsto d(k\cdot v)\mathbf a$, or $d\,\mathbf a\otimes k$. No time variable, nonvanishing or perpendicularity assumption is present. At $x=0$ and $F'(0)=1$, this becomes the central gradient $\mathbf a\otimes k$ used in §1.1. The formal identity therefore applies to any differentiable profile and any evaluated phase, not only the normalized periodic profile.
TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_planeWave.summary: The spatial derivative is a scalar multiple of the amplitude–wave-vector tensor

TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_profile_partials.text: If `hf` gives differentiability of the joint label-phase function at a point, its Fréchet derivative is the coproduct of the label derivative and the scalar-phase derivative. The coproduct acts on a pair by adding those two contributions. This decomposition supports the slow and fast terms in graph evaluation.
TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_profile_partials.summary: The joint profile derivative splits into label and phase parts

TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_selfAdvection.text: If `u` is differentiable and its derivative has derivative `D` symmetric in the two directions, then differentiating $(u\cdot\nabla)u$ gives $(Du)^2+D(u)$. Symmetry is supplied explicitly rather than inferred from a smoothness assumption. This is the spatial calculation used in the evolution of the velocity gradient along trajectories.
TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_selfAdvection.summary: Differentiating self-advection produces the squared velocity gradient

TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_slabSpaceSlice.text: For a function differentiable on the closed slab, fixing a time in the interval gives an ordinary spatial Fréchet derivative. It is the joint within-slab derivative composed with the inclusion $v\mapsto(0,v)$. This helper does not require `a < b`, because its conclusion stays entirely in the unrestricted spatial directions at a fixed allowed time.
TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_slabSpaceSlice.summary: A spatial slice inherits its joint derivative

TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_slabVelocityTimeD.text: For a jointly $C^2$ velocity on $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3$, spatial differentiation commutes with the derivative taken within the time interval. The hypotheses `hT` and `ht` include both endpoints while ensuring a nondegenerate slab. The proof uses symmetry of the second within derivative, so this is an endpoint statement as well as an interior one.
TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_slabVelocityTimeD.summary: Spatial differentiation commutes with the time derivative

TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_slice.text: For a function differentiable on a closed slab, fixing any time in the slab yields a Fréchet derivative in the spatial variable. The derivative is the within-slab derivative composed with the spatial inclusion. This permits higher spatial differentiation without requiring the time coordinate to lie in the interior.
TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_slice.summary: Fixing time leaves an ordinary spatial derivative

TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_spatialSlice.text: For a field differentiable on a closed time slab, its spatial slice at an admissible time has a Fréchet derivative obtained by composing the within-slab derivative with the spatial inclusion. Spatial points are unrestricted. This isolates spatial differentiation from the one-sided time behavior at the slab endpoints.
TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_spatialSlice.summary: A spatial slice inherits the slab derivative

TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_stationaryShear.text: The spatial derivative of the stationary shear at `x` is $\cos(2\pi x_2)$ times its fixed gradient at the origin. The formula holds for every shear parameter `s`. It is derived from the plane-wave derivative rule and the scalar derivative of the sine profile.
TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_stationaryShear.summary: The stationary shear derivative is a cosine times its central gradient

TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_stationaryShearFl.text: The spatial derivative of the shear flow is the identity plus $t\cos(2\pi a_2)$ times the central shear gradient. This is an exact formula for every label and real time. It supplies the deformation matrix whose inverse is obtained by negating its nilpotent rank-one correction.
TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_stationaryShearFl.summary: The shear deformation is identity plus a rank one term

TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_transportedProfil.text: Given a derivative `hA` of the inverse label map and the joint label-phase derivative `hf` of the profile, the transported profile derivative splits into the pulled-back label derivative and a rank-one phase term. The transported covector is `Ax.adjoint k`. This is a local fixed-time chain rule, without a global flow assumption.
TorusEuler.hasFDerivAt_transportedProfil.summary: The spatial chain rule separates labels from phase

TorusEuler.hasFDerivWithinAt_currySlab.text: On a convex parameter set, jointly continuous data and jointly continuous supplied parameter derivatives give the within-set derivative of the curried path map. The candidate derivative sends a direction to the path of pointwise derivatives. Convexity controls the remainder uniformly in time, upgrading pointwise differentiability to differentiability in the uniform path norm.
TorusEuler.hasFDerivWithinAt_currySlab.summary: A continuous derivative field differentiates the path-valued map

TorusEuler.hasFDerivWithinAt_eval_of_tim.text: For a time dependent bounded continuous function, a within time derivative in the uniform norm and a spatial derivative at `x` combine into a joint within derivative on `I ×ˢ univ`. The resulting linear map adds the time contribution and spatial contribution. Uniform control of the time remainder is what makes evaluation at varying spatial points legitimate.
TorusEuler.hasFDerivWithinAt_eval_of_tim.summary: Time and spatial derivatives combine under evaluation

TorusEuler.hasFDerivWithinAt_setIntegral.text: On a closed convex parameter set in a proper normed space, a jointly continuous integrand and supplied continuous parameter derivative over a compact integration set may be differentiated under the integral. The measure is locally finite and the target is complete. The conclusion is a within-set derivative, so it applies at boundary parameters as well.
TorusEuler.hasFDerivWithinAt_setIntegral.summary: Differentiate a compact integral with a continuous derivative

TorusEuler.hasFDerivWithinAt_setIntegral.text: For a smooth integrand on a closed convex parameter domain times the whole integration space, this identifies the derivative of its compact-set integral as the integral of the parameter component of its joint within-derivative. `UniqueDiffOn` fixes that derivative on the domain. The argument inherits properness and local finiteness from the surrounding section.
TorusEuler.hasFDerivWithinAt_setIntegral.summary: Smooth joint integrands supply the compact integral derivative

TorusEuler.hasFDerivWithinAt_spaceSlice.text: A within derivative on a time-space product restricts to the spatial slice at a time belonging to `I` by composition with the spatial inclusion. The result is a `HasFDerivWithinAt` statement on `O`. It separates the spatial component of the full derivative without assuming the product domain is open.
TorusEuler.hasFDerivWithinAt_spaceSlice.summary: Restricting a derivative to a spatial slice

TorusEuler.hasFDerivWithinAt_timeSlice.text: A within derivative on `I × O` restricts to the time slice at a fixed spatial point in `O` by composition with the time inclusion. The theorem states a `HasFDerivWithinAt` property and does not select a derivative using `fderivWithin`. No uniqueness or interval geometry is needed for this elementary chain rule.

TorusEuler.hasFDerivWithinAt_time_param.text: At a slab point, a jointly continuous time-derivative field and the specified parameter derivative combine into a joint within-slab Fréchet derivative. The time derivative is assumed along every parameter trajectory, while the parameter derivative is needed at the chosen time and point. The proof separates the time increment from the parameter increment without extending beyond the slab.
TorusEuler.hasFDerivWithinAt_time_param.summary: Combine the time derivative with the parameter derivative

TorusEuler.hasFDerivWithinAt_transported.text: Within the time slab, derivatives of the inverse label map and the full time-label-phase profile compose to give the derivative of graph evaluation. The conclusion retains `HasFDerivWithinAt`, so it applies at temporal boundary points. The nested products in the derivative track time, label, and phase separately.
TorusEuler.hasFDerivWithinAt_transported.summary: The profile graph has a joint derivative on the time slab

TorusEuler.hasGradientAt_activationWaveV.text: If the inverse label map `A t` has derivative `F.symm` at `x`, then the phase with initial covector $\mathrm{carrier}\,F^*E_3$ has Eulerian gradient $\mathrm{carrier}\,E_3$ there. `F` is already a continuous linear equivalence. No unit-length or nonzero assumption on `E₃` is required for this algebraic gradient identity.
TorusEuler.hasGradientAt_activationWaveV.summary: The chosen initial covector gives the activation gradient

TorusEuler.hasGradientAt_affineWavePress.text: Let $S$ be a symmetric linear map on Euclidean $\mathbb R^3$, let $p_{\rm w}\in\mathbb R$ and $k,x\in\mathbb R^3$, and assume $P'(k\cdot x)=F(k\cdot x)$. The formal statement proves that $p(y)=-y\cdot Sy/2-p_{\rm w}P(k\cdot y)$ has gradient $\nabla p(x)=-Sx-p_{\rm w}F(k\cdot x)k$. For Lemma 2.1, take $S=D'+D^2$. This is a fixed-time spatial calculation; it does not assume the wave equations or identify the acceleration. Smoothness or periodicity of $P$ away from the evaluated phase is unnecessary.
TorusEuler.hasGradientAt_affineWavePress.summary: Symmetry and the primitive relation give the pressure gradient

TorusEuler.hasGradientAt_endpointFiniteF.text: If `ha` says each included vector coefficient is the gradient mode of its pressure correction, the finite scalar pressure has gradient equal to the real part of the vector Fourier sum. The coefficient assumption is needed only for modes in `s`. The proof differentiates a finite sum, so no infinite-series differentiation is hidden here.
TorusEuler.hasGradientAt_endpointFiniteF.summary: Compatible finite coefficients reconstruct the desired gradient

TorusEuler.hasGradientAt_endpointPressur.text: If `X` has Fréchet derivative `F` at `a` and `q` has gradient `gradq` at `X a`, then the gradient of $q\circ X$ at `a` is $F^*\mathrm{gradq}$. This is the gradient chain rule. It does not require `X` to be invertible or volume preserving, although those properties appear elsewhere in the flow application.
TorusEuler.hasGradientAt_endpointPressur.summary: Pulling back pressure multiplies its gradient by the adjoint

TorusEuler.hasGradientAt_firstWaveTransp.text: The phase obtained by composing $x\mapsto\lambda e_1\cdot x$ with the inverse shear flow has the stated transported covector as its gradient at the moving particle. The equality is global in time and label. It uses the explicit inverse-flow derivative and does not require integer frequency, because the phase is read on the Euclidean lift.
TorusEuler.hasGradientAt_firstWaveTransp.summary: The inverse shear transports the phase gradient

TorusEuler.hasGradientAt_transportedOsci.text: A supplied label-and-phase derivative of the oscillatory pressure gives its Eulerian gradient after transport. The slow label gradient is acted on by the inverse-flow adjoint; the phase part becomes the rank-one projection of $\mathrm{src}-2MV$. The derivative identity `hp` is an input. No nonzero-covector assumption appears because the equality remains algebraically valid with totalized inversion.
TorusEuler.hasGradientAt_transportedOsci.summary: The pressure gradient separates slow and transverse parts

TorusEuler.hasGradientAt_transportedPhas.text: Let the inverse label map $A(t,\cdot)$ be differentiable at $x$, with derivative $G$. For any $k_*\in\mathbb R^3$, the formal statement proves $\nabla_x(k_*\cdot A(t,x))=G^Tk_*$. When $A=X(t,\cdot)^{-1}$, this is $\kappa=(D_aX)^{-T}k_*$ at the particle with label $a=A(t,x)$. This is a local spatial chain rule, valid even for $k_*=0$. It requires no time evolution or incompressibility and does not make the phase periodic. The lattice restriction or the localized extension is a separate issue in §3.1.
TorusEuler.hasGradientAt_transportedPhas.summary: Transpose the inverse-flow derivative against the initial wave vector

TorusEuler.hasGradientAt_transportedPres.text: The pressure profile evaluated at the inverse label and transported phase has gradient $A_x^*p_a+p_sA_x^*k$. The hypotheses supply the derivative of the label map and the two partial derivatives of the pressure profile at the graph point. This is a pointwise chain rule, with no pressure equation assumed.
TorusEuler.hasGradientAt_transportedPres.summary: The transported pressure has slow and fast gradient parts

TorusEuler.hasGradientAt_wavePressurePro.text: For $0<h\le1$, differentiates the pressure $-c(x)P_h(\phi(x))$ at a point with specified coefficient and phase gradients. The result separates the fast term $-cF_h\kappa$ from the slow term $-P_h\nabla c$. It assumes only those pointwise gradient witnesses; the full Hessian calculation later requires $C^2$ regularity.

TorusEuler.hasOffOriginLimits_advection_.text: A velocity with smooth spatial slices and `HasOffOriginLimits` has the same property for its self-advection field. The construction requests one additional derivative from the velocity limit, differentiates it, and applies the local bilinear convergence theorem. The resulting limit is the self advection of a local limiting velocity on the chosen neighborhood.
TorusEuler.hasOffOriginLimits_advection_.summary: Velocity terminal limits give advection terminal limits

TorusEuler.hasOffOriginLimits_neg_sub.text: For two fields with smooth preterminal spatial slices and off origin limits, their negative sum has off origin limits as well. The proof intersects the two limiting neighborhoods so both local representatives are defined together. Actual derivative rules for negation and subtraction transfer the uniform jet convergence to that common region.
TorusEuler.hasOffOriginLimits_neg_sub.summary: Linear combinations preserve local terminal spatial limits

TorusEuler.hasOffOriginLimits_normalized.text: Assume smooth periodic velocity slices, normalized $C^2$ periodic complex pressure slices satisfying the tensor Poisson equation, a continuous periodic terminal velocity smooth off the lattice, global uniform velocity convergence and local convergence of every spatial jet. Then the real pressure gradient has `HasOffOriginLimits T`. The proof extends velocities by zero outside `Ico 0 T` only to apply a filter-indexed theorem; eventual agreement removes that extension.
TorusEuler.hasOffOriginLimits_normalized.summary: Normalized Euler pressures inherit all off-origin terminal limits

TorusEuler.hasOffOriginLimits_of_inducti.text: If oscillations have periodically repeated supports of radii tending to zero, every compact punctured region eventually avoids them. The hypothesis `hjets` supplies smooth terminal slices and continuous jets wherever this eventual vanishing holds. These data imply `HasOffOriginLimits T w`, with the actual value `w T` as the local limit.
TorusEuler.hasOffOriginLimits_of_inducti.summary: Shrinking supports give the velocity terminal trace

TorusEuler.hasOffOriginLimits_of_uniform.text: Uniform convergence of smooth approximants and all their spatial jets on compact punctured regions yields `HasOffOriginLimits T f`. The velocity limit `w` must agree with `f` before the terminal time through `hmatch`. A compact neighborhood is enlarged first, allowing the limiting jets to be identified as actual derivatives of the terminal trace.
TorusEuler.hasOffOriginLimits_of_uniform.summary: Local jet convergence supplies the terminal spatial limits

TorusEuler.hasOffOriginLimits_timeDeriva.text: If within interval dynamics identifies the time derivative of `u` with a field `g` on the punctured lift, terminal spatial limits for `g` also hold for `timeDerivative T u`. The proof uses uniqueness of within derivatives on `Ico 0 T`. It does not construct `g` or prove the required limiting behavior.
TorusEuler.hasOffOriginLimits_timeDeriva.summary: The equation transfers terminal limits to the time derivative

TorusEuler.hasOffOriginLimits_timeDeriva.text: It suffices to know the dynamics on every closed interval $[0,S]$ with $S<T$. Around each preterminal time, one chooses a larger such prefix and restricts its within derivative to `Ico 0 T`. Once the right hand side `g` has off origin limits, the same limits hold for the actual time derivative.
TorusEuler.hasOffOriginLimits_timeDeriva.summary: Closed prefix equations identify the preterminal time derivative

TorusEuler.hasSpatialHolderWords_iff_spa.text: For an integer $n\ge0$ and a half-Hölder field on $\mathbb T^3$, having successive ordered coordinate derivatives through order $n$, each represented by a half-Hölder field with the actual differentiation identities, is equivalent to the periodic lift belonging to $C^{n,1/2}(\mathbb R^3)$. This identifies the regularity used in the differentiated equations of Lemma A.2 with the paper's function class. It is an equivalence of membership, not a numerical norm estimate; the comparison of coordinate bounds with Fréchet-derivative norms is supplied separately.
TorusEuler.hasSpatialHolderWords_iff_spa.summary: Identify coordinate derivatives with the full Hölder class

TorusEuler.hasSum_annularPartition.text: For a frequency of norm at least one, the dyadically rescaled cutoff differences have sum one. The unit inner region and zero outer region make the sum telescope and eventually stop changing. This theorem provides an actual `HasSum` witness, so the later use of its `tsum` does not rely on totalized summation.
TorusEuler.hasSum_annularPartition.summary: The annular cutoff differences sum to one away from zero

TorusEuler.hessianSub.text: If both scalar pressure fields are $C^2$, the Hessian of their difference is the difference of their Hessians at every spatial point. The proof first subtracts gradients and then differentiates that identity. The regularity assumptions ensure this is the classical subtraction rule used in the physical cutoff argument.

TorusEuler.hessian_const_smul.text: The Hessian of a constant scalar multiple of a scalar spatial field equals that scalar times its Hessian. The statement has no differentiability hypotheses: it uses the total Fréchet derivative’s constant-scalar rule over the field. Later analytic applications separately establish pressure smoothness before interpreting these Hessians as classical derivatives.
TorusEuler.hessian_const_smul.summary: A constant scalar factors out of the Hessian

TorusEuler.hierarchyAdmissibleWords.text:
The canonical sorted derivative words of total order at most `n`. For `Fin 4`, the first three letters specify the label multi-index and the last specifies the phase order in (D.1).

Default-value audit (b5): Order zero includes the empty derivative word. The sorted-word convention removes permutations but retains each mixed multi-index once; equivalence with arbitrary word order uses commutation theorems.
TorusEuler.hierarchyAdmissibleWords.summary: One sorted word for each mixed multi-index

TorusEuler.hierarchyAdmissibleWords_mono.text: The finite set of admissible derivative words increases with the order bound. Its elements are sorted lists of coordinate indices of length at most that bound, so increasing the bound preserves membership. Sorted words represent one choice for each mixed multi-index in the finite norm.
TorusEuler.hierarchyAdmissibleWords_mono.summary: Higher derivative orders retain all earlier multi-indices

TorusEuler.hierarchyAdvectionAtLevel.text:
The level-`p` contribution of a quadratic term.

Default-value audit (b5): Finite sums and index sets are defined at zero order or empty ranges as well. The paper use supplies the intended order and level restrictions.
TorusEuler.hierarchyAdvectionAtLevel.summary: Quadratic interactions at a specified level

TorusEuler.hierarchyAdvectionLevel.text: The two indices and the shift are nonnegative integers, so subtraction is truncated at zero. Positive interaction indices make this agree with ordinary subtraction in the paper’s uses. Label advection of levels $i$ and $j$ is assigned level $i+j$, while phase advection is assigned level $i+j-1$. This is the counting convention before (5.26). It determines which terms are canceled at the current level and which survive in the remainder; numerical estimates for these terms are proved later.
TorusEuler.hierarchyAdvectionLevel.summary: A fast derivative lowers the combined level by one

TorusEuler.hierarchyAdvectionLevel_at_le.text: Membership in `hierarchyAdvectionPairs P shift` forces the first index to be at least `shift + 1` and the second at least one. Therefore their interaction level $i+j-\mathrm{shift}$ is at least two. This also justifies natural-number subtraction in the filtration; arbitrary index pairs would not satisfy the conclusion.
TorusEuler.hierarchyAdvectionLevel_at_le.summary: Allowed interactions start at the second level

TorusEuler.hierarchyAdvectionPairs.text:
The positive index pairs at depth `P`. Phase advection uses `shift=1` and omits the zero first inputs `C₀` and `B₁`. Label advection uses `shift=0`.

Default-value audit (b5): These are finite intervals of natural indices. Small P can produce empty sets; the level constraints in the expansion select the intended interactions.
TorusEuler.hierarchyAdvectionPairs.summary: The pairs retained in quadratic advection

TorusEuler.hierarchyCompletionExponent.text: The index is a nonnegative integer, but it is converted to a real number before forming $p-1$; this subtraction is not truncated at zero. The exponent for $C_{p+1}$ is the exponent for $V_p$ minus one, namely $-9/4-2(p-1)/3$. This records the frequency gain in (5.36) and explains why the correction belongs to the next level. Lemma 5.5 supplies the corresponding analytic estimate under the zero-mean, transversality, and parent coefficient hypotheses.
TorusEuler.hierarchyCompletionExponent.summary: The correction gains one power of inverse frequency

TorusEuler.hierarchyFastAdvection_le.text: Assume nonzero phase width, smooth fields, bounded finite jet sets, and `hκN` bounding the scaled phase coefficient by $L\,\mathrm{freq}^{3/2}$. The fast-advection norm is bounded by that coefficient size times the advector's order-$n$ norm and the advected field's next-order norm. The theorem uses, rather than derives, the frequency-dependent coefficient estimate.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFastAdvection_le.summary: Fast advection uses the supplied phase coefficient bound

TorusEuler.hierarchyFastAdvection_timeWe.text: With nonzero phase scale `h`, smooth slices and bounded derivative-word sets, the normalized fast-advection norm is bounded by a quadratic combinatorial constant times $L\mathrm{freq}^{3/2}$ and the two profile norms. The second profile needs one more derivative. `hκN` supplies the scaled wave-vector bound; no positivity of the time weight is asserted by this algebraic estimate.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFastAdvection_timeWe.summary: The weighted fast product costs three half powers

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteLabelNorm_endp.text: Sums the contraction estimate over all admissible label words through order `n`. Every original word measurement set is assumed bounded, and the sign has absolute value at most one. The result applies with or without the optional Hölder measurements and therefore also to fields already normalized by a time-dependent weight.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteLabelNorm_endp.summary: The finite weighted label norm keeps its original constant

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteMixedWordNorm_.text: The time index set and real normed target are arbitrary; smoothness is required only in the spatial variables, uniformly bounded norms being a separate issue. For a smooth field independent of phase, the mixed finite norm equals the label norm exactly. Every derivative involving the phase vanishes, while the remaining terms have the same radius weights. This identifies the general norm (D.1) with the coefficient norm used for the mean equation in §5.3.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteMixedWordNorm_.summary: Only label derivatives contribute to the mean norm

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm.text: This expression sums derivative suprema through order $n$ using nondecreasing derivative indices, so each coordinate multi-index occurs once. The time parameter indexes a supremum and is never differentiated. With half-Hölder regularity included, each summand is the maximum of its supremum norm and half-Hölder seminorm; the quotient at identical points is assigned zero. This differs from their sum by at most a factor two. Each supremum is real valued; using it as a norm requires bounded derivative values, a condition proved or assumed in applications. The definition alone does not establish such boundedness.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm.summary: The finite norm sums derivatives through a chosen order

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_advec.text: For constant weighted directions, the finite norm of $a(z)D_i g$ is bounded by the coefficient norm, advector norm, and the order-$n+1$ norm of $g$, with the square of the product constant. Smoothness and bounded jet sets are explicit. The extra derivative falls on the advected field, not the undifferentiated advector.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_advec.summary: An advective component costs one extra derivative

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_bilin.text: For smooth factors with bounded jet sets, the product's finite word norm is bounded by the product of the two input norms, $\|B\|$, and an explicit constant counting admissible words and Leibniz terms. The Boolean-style proposition `holder` selects either suprema alone or suprema together with half-Hölder quotients. Boundedness is an explicit hypothesis for both inputs.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_bilin.summary: The finite weighted norm satisfies a product estimate

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_clm_a.text: This specializes the bilinear estimate to $c(t,x)g(t,x)$ for an operator-valued coefficient. Smoothness and bounded jet sets are assumed separately for `c` and `g`. The evaluation bilinear map has norm at most one, so only the combinatorial product constant and the two finite norms remain in the bound.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_clm_a.summary: Apply an operator coefficient in the finite norm

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_const.text: If all jet sets through order $n+1$ are bounded, differentiating once in a fixed constant weighted direction yields bounded sets through order $n$ and a norm no larger than the original next-order norm. The insertion map is injective, so no count of admissible words appears. The field must be smooth at each time.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_const.summary: One more order controls a weighted coordinate derivative

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_false.text: Uniform Fréchet derivative bounds $C_m A D^{6m}$ through order $n$ yield bounded supremum jet sets and a finite label norm bounded by $A\sum_w C_{|w|}$. The sum is over admissible sorted words. The radius condition $\ell D^6\le1$ absorbs each derivative cost, and only spatial smoothness at each time is assumed.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_false.summary: Pointwise jet bounds give a finite label norm

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_holde.text: For $0<\ell\le1$, smooth fields and bounded supremum jet sets through order $n+1$, the half-Hölder word norm at order $n$ is at most four times the next-order supremum norm divided by $\sqrt\ell$. The explicit factor four reflects the value term and three label directions under the max convention for Hölder norms.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_holde.summary: One derivative controls the half-Hölder finite norm

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_holde.text: Suppose smooth time slices have jets $C_m A D^{6m}$, with $D\ge1$, $\ell>0$, and $\ell D^6\le1$. The order-$n$ half-Hölder finite norm is bounded by $4A/\sqrt\ell$ times a sum of constants through order $n+1$. This combines the weighted supremum estimate with the one-derivative Hölder comparison.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_holde.summary: Power bounds give the half-Hölder norm at every order

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_le_of.text: Suppose continuous torus words through order $N$ lift to the actual spatial derivatives of a smooth velocity, and each weighted time norm is at most $B$. The finite half-Hölder label norm of that velocity is at most the number of admissible words times $B$. The lift identities are essential: arbitrary bounded auxiliary fields would not control these derivatives.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_le_of.summary: Recovered torus words bound the label norm

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_linea.text: An all-order bound for the normalized linear relay assembled from the actual curl, its commutator, and the inverse-coframe gradient. Each row has its own coefficient budget and every primitive profile is used at order `n + 1`. The single inverse frequency is common to them.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_linea.summary: All-order derivative bounds for the linear relay

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_mono_.text: Adding higher orders can only increase the finite mixed norm.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_mono_.summary: Increasing the derivative order increases the finite norm

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_nonne.text: The finite word norm is nonnegative when all its jet-value sets are bounded above. Each such set contains zero, so its real supremum is nonnegative, and summing preserves that inequality. The explicit boundedness condition prevents treating an arbitrary conditional supremum as an automatically valid analytic norm.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_nonne.summary: Bounded jet ranges give a nonnegative finite norm

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_phase.text: For smooth profiles with one-periodic, zero-mean phase slices and bounded admissible derivative words, the normalized phase primitive has finite word norm at most twice that of the input. Every constant weighted direction is retained. This is the supremum version selected by `False`, not the Hölder extension of the finite norm.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_phase.summary: Phase integration costs at most a factor of two

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_physi.text: A smooth operator field multiplying a smooth recovered label velocity has a finite supremum-word bound controlled by the operator's half-Hölder norm and the common weighted bound on actual recovered derivative representatives. The hypotheses explicitly identify those representatives with derivatives of `v`. The variable `coframe` is generic here; its role as $D_aX$ in the physical mean is supplied by the application.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_physi.summary: The deformation converts the recovered bound to physical velocity

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_pulle.text: A pulled-back curl costs one weighted label derivative and one coframe coefficient. The inverse frequency commutes with all spatial and phase derivatives.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_pulle.summary: A slow curl costs one weighted label derivative

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_restr.text: Composing the time index with any map `incl : S → T` cannot increase the finite-word norm, provided the original measurement sets are bounded above. Every sample in the restricted family is already a sample in the original family. The map need not be injective or represent an interval inclusion.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_restr.summary: Restricting the time parameter cannot enlarge the measurement

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_sup_l.text: A common bound on the pointwise mixed jets controls their exact sum with only the number of admissible multi-indices as a factor.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_sup_l.summary: A common derivative bound controls the finite sum

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_unitL.text: At label radius one, smooth fields whose jets through order two satisfy $C_mD^{pm+q}$ have order-one half-Hölder norm bounded by an explicit sum of constants times $D^{2p+q}$. Only the first three derivative orders are assumed. This is used to bound the coefficient norm entering the low-order mean inverse.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_unitL.summary: Two derivatives bound the low-order coefficient input

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_waveC.text: The divergence correction built from the wave potential is bounded in the finite supremum word norm by an explicit constant times `freq⁻¹`. The hypotheses supply smooth periodic zero-mean velocity, coefficient budgets for the normalized potential and inverse-coframe rows, a nonzero label scale, and positive frequency. The velocity budget is needed at order `n + 1`.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_waveC.summary: The actual curl correction gains inverse frequency at finite order

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_waveL.text: The actual four-term relay formed from potential, potential-time profile, and phase pressure has finite word norm bounded by an explicit order constant times $K^2\lambda^{-1}(V_0+F_0)$. The theorem assumes smooth periodic zero-mean profiles, their order-`n + 1` bounds, and all named normalized coefficient budgets. It estimates a spatial expression; identifying it with the actual time derivative requires the separate derivative lemmas.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordNorm_waveL.summary: The full linear relay retains one inverse-frequency factor

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordSeminorm.text: A linear slice map with smooth values and bounded measurement sets gives a seminorm by summing the actual real suprema over admissible words. The `hBounded` argument is required for every input and relevant word. This establishes triangle inequality and absolute homogeneity, rather than merely naming an arbitrary real-valued expression a norm.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordSeminorm.summary: The finite derivative measurements form a genuine seminorm

TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordSeminorm_a.text: Evaluating the constructed finite-word seminorm gives exactly `hierarchyFiniteWordNorm` of the linear slice map’s output. The equality is definitional. Its smoothness and boundedness arguments certify that the underlying real suprema have the intended analytic meaning, while the formula itself is unchanged by the seminorm packaging.
TorusEuler.hierarchyFiniteWordSeminorm_a.summary: The seminorm evaluates to the actual sum of suprema

TorusEuler.hierarchyGraphPoint.text: For any label map $A(t,x)$ and carrier $k_*\in\mathbb R^3$, the graph point associated with $(t,x)$ is $(t,A(t,x),k_*\cdot A(t,x))$. In §5.6, $A(t,x)=X_{t,0}(x)$ is the inverse parent flow, so a profile evaluated here becomes its Eulerian field $f^\natural$. This formula imposes no regularity, periodicity or flow equation on $A$ and makes no approximation. Smoothness and chain-rule conclusions require the later hypotheses on the chosen parent flow. The phase is a real number; its periodic dependence belongs to the profile rather than to this graph-point definition.
TorusEuler.hierarchyGraphPoint.summary: Specify the label and phase at which the profile is evaluated

TorusEuler.hierarchyHigherPressureGradie.text: The proposed gradient profile is the coframe adjoint applied to the slow label gradient plus the longitudinal projection of `force - 2 • M(V)`. It rewrites the expensive phase derivative using the transverse pressure equation. This is a definition for arbitrary inputs; the subsequent transport theorem proves it equals a physical gradient under the required identities.
TorusEuler.hierarchyHigherPressureGradie.summary: Use the transverse equation for the fast pressure gradient

TorusEuler.hierarchyInactiveRegion.text: The underlying domain is $[0,T]\times\mathbb R^3\times\mathbb R$ and the label set is denoted $S$. For closed $S$, the condition is open relative to this time slab. The inactive region consists of points in the time interval with $t<t_0$ or label outside the envelope support. It is independent of phase and describes the vanishing asserted in Proposition 5.4. The strict time inequality matches the proof; vanishing at the activation time itself follows from continuity where that endpoint is approached from below.
TorusEuler.hierarchyInactiveRegion.summary: Separate times and labels where oscillations must vanish

TorusEuler.hierarchyInactiveThroughActiv.text: Defines the points in the closed profile slab whose time is at most `τ` or whose label lies outside `S`. This differs from `hierarchyInactiveRegion`, which uses strict preactivation time. Extending a vanishing statement to the activation slice requires continuity and positive activation; the definition alone asserts no such vanishing.
TorusEuler.hierarchyInactiveThroughActiv.summary: The inactive region includes the activation slice

TorusEuler.hierarchyInductiveMeanExponen.text: Explicitly the exponent is $-7/4-2(p-1)/3$, with real subtraction after converting the integer level. This is a definition of a power, not a norm estimate. The induction measures the mean with the oscillatory exponent minus $1/2$, corresponding to $\lambda^{1/2}\|B_p\|_{[n]}$ in (5.40). This allows a factor $\lambda^{1/12}$ compared with the sharper mean estimate (5.35). The smallness assumption uses that allowance to remove the parent power before estimating the next supplementary transverse source.
TorusEuler.hierarchyInductiveMeanExponen.summary: Remove the parent loss by weakening the mean decay slightly

TorusEuler.hierarchyJetValues.text:
Quantities measured by the supremum at each word. The half-Hölder choice also includes all half-power difference quotients at fixed time, with the max convention of `HalfHolder`.

Default-value audit (b5): The set explicitly contains zero, so it is nonempty. At coincident points the difference quotient is 0/0 and takes the totalized value zero. Boundedness of this set is a separate hypothesis whenever its real supremum is used to control values.
TorusEuler.hierarchyJetValues.summary: Values sampled by each derivative supremum

TorusEuler.hierarchyJetValues_bdd_biline.text: Smooth factors with bounded admissible jet sets have bounded jet sets after applying a continuous bilinear map. This establishes the analytic boundedness needed to interpret the product norm's real suprema. The bound is obtained from the wordwise Leibniz estimate and works for either the supremum or the half-Hölder choice.
TorusEuler.hierarchyJetValues_bdd_biline.summary: Products retain bounded derivative and Hölder ranges

TorusEuler.hierarchyJetValues_constDeriv.text: For smooth time-indexed fields and constant directions, the jet-value set of a word applied to one extra directional derivative equals the original field's jet-value set at the sorted extended word. The equality covers both sup values and optional Hölder quotients. It depends on permutation invariance of smooth constant-direction derivatives.
TorusEuler.hierarchyJetValues_constDeriv.summary: Differentiation shifts the canonical word range

TorusEuler.hierarchyJetValues_le_of_reco.text: A recovered half-Holder curve representing an actual spatial derivative word controls the corresponding weighted lift supremum and half-Holder increments. The scale may be zero here; the theorem only multiplies by its nonnegative power.
TorusEuler.hierarchyJetValues_le_of_reco.summary: Converting recovered Holder words to weighted label bounds

TorusEuler.hierarchyJetValues_nonempty.text: The set of quantities used to measure a word derivative is nonempty because its definition includes zero. This holds for either choice of the Hölder flag and without regularity or boundedness assumptions on the field. Nonemptiness alone does not justify using its real supremum as a bound; later lemmas also require `BddAbove`.

TorusEuler.hierarchyJetValues_sup_le_fin.text: If every admissible word has a bounded jet-value set, the supremum for any one admissible word lies below the sum defining the finite norm. Zero belongs to each set, making all summands nonnegative. The boundedness hypothesis is essential for the conditional real supremum to behave as the intended norm.
TorusEuler.hierarchyJetValues_sup_le_fin.summary: One word supremum lies below the finite norm

TorusEuler.hierarchyJetValues_true_label.text: Uniform bounds $A,B$ on adjacent jets give both boundedness of the weighted word's half-Hölder jet set and a supremum bound $\ell^m(A+\sqrt{2AB})$. This includes the empty word, unlike the radius-gain lemmas. Nonnegative radius and constants and smooth time slices ensure all values and difference quotients are covered.
TorusEuler.hierarchyJetValues_true_label.summary: Adjacent jets bound the entire Hölder range

TorusEuler.hierarchyJetValues_true_label.text: For a nonempty word and adjacent power bounds, the entire half-Hölder jet range is bounded by $(C_m+\sqrt{2C_mC_{m+1}})D^{p+q}\sqrt\ell$. The radius restriction implies $\ell\le1$, allowing the value bound's factor $\ell$ to be replaced by $\sqrt\ell$. The theorem returns boundedness as well as the supremum inequality.
TorusEuler.hierarchyJetValues_true_label.summary: The full positive-word norm gains a radius factor

TorusEuler.hierarchyLabelDirection.text: This defines constant vector fields on $\mathbb R^3$ for any real $\ell_*$. At $\ell_*=0$, every positive-order scaled directional derivative is zero. The three label derivative directions are $\ell_*\partial_{a_i}$. Consequently, an order-$m$ derivative carries the factor $\ell_*^m$ used in the coefficient norm of Appendix D. These directions are used for phase-independent fields, particularly the parent coefficients and mean correction. The positive radius allows their estimates to be compared with ordinary label derivatives.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLabelDirection.summary: Each label derivative carries the envelope radius

TorusEuler.hierarchyLabelJetValues_endpo.text: For each time slice smooth in space, proves boundedness and a nonincreasing supremum of the selected label-word measurements. The `holder` parameter determines whether half-Hölder quotients are included. The original measurement set must be bounded above; its built-in zero supplies nonemptiness and nonnegativity even when the time type has no points.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLabelJetValues_endpo.summary: The weighted jet supremum cannot grow under parity selection

TorusEuler.hierarchyLabelWord_endpointPa.text: Extends the coordinate-word reflection identity to the hierarchy’s label directions scaled by `ell`. Each derivative contributes one minus sign under reflection, while the scalar factor `ell` commutes with averaging. Smoothness is explicit; the equality holds for arbitrary real `ell` and does not assume a positive envelope scale.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLabelWord_endpointPa.summary: Weighted label derivatives have the same parity rule

TorusEuler.hierarchyLatticeShift.text: The joint translation associated with an integer lattice vector leaves time fixed, translates the label, and changes the phase by its inner product with the carrier `k`. This is the compatibility shift satisfied by transported periodic profiles. It is distinct from an ordinary label translation at fixed phase.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLatticeShift.summary: A lattice translation carries its phase shift

TorusEuler.hierarchyLatticeShift_vadd_sl.text: Translation by any carrier-dependent lattice shift maps the whole profile slab to itself. The result is stated as equality of translated sets and holds for every real $T$. It lets the domain appearing in a within-slab derivative be replaced after translating both label and phase.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLatticeShift_vadd_sl.summary: The slab is invariant under the twisted translation

TorusEuler.hierarchyLeibnizSplits.text:
Assign each derivative in an ordered word to one of the two factors. The list retains multiplicity when equal coordinate directions recur.

Default-value audit (b5): Repeated derivative letters retain combinatorial multiplicity. The empty word has one split into two empty words, so the zeroth product rule is not lost.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLeibnizSplits.summary: All assignments of a derivative word to two factors

TorusEuler.hierarchyLeibnizSplits_append.text: The full Leibniz list equals the list of splits with nonempty first word followed by the unique pair `([], w)`. This is an equality of ordered lists, preserving multiplicities. It isolates the highest solution derivative before the remaining terms are estimated as coefficient commutators.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLeibnizSplits_append.summary: Separate the term with an undifferentiated coefficient

TorusEuler.hierarchyLeibnizSplits_order_.text: A Leibniz split assigns the original word's derivatives to two factors. If its first word is nonempty, the second word has strictly smaller length than the original. The membership hypothesis records an actual split, including repeated directions. This strict decrease is what makes differentiated coefficient equations amenable to induction.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLeibnizSplits_order_.summary: Differentiating the coefficient lowers the solution order

TorusEuler.hierarchyLeibnizSplits_spec.text: Every split produced by the ordered Leibniz list consists of two subwords whose lengths add to the original word length. Repeated letters retain their multiplicity in the list; this is the combinatorial bookkeeping behind the product rule.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLeibnizSplits_spec.summary: Leibniz subwords preserve the total derivative order

TorusEuler.hierarchyLevelConstant.text:
Constants for the full finite hierarchy. Their only quantitative inputs are the derivative-order constant bound, the depth and the level.

Default-value audit (b5): The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLevelConstant.summary: Constants accumulated through the finite depth

TorusEuler.hierarchyLevelConstant_monoto.text: For nonnegative `K`, the sequence `hierarchyLevelConstant P K` is monotone in its level index. Each new step cap retains the previous constant and adds nonnegative terms. This allows all lower levels to be bounded by one coefficient during the strong induction; it does not give uniformity in depth.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLevelConstant_monoto.summary: The chosen constants can grow with the hierarchy level

TorusEuler.hierarchyLevelConstant_one_le.text: The recursively defined level constant is at least one when its input bound K is nonnegative. This permits later estimates to absorb unit factors without changing the level or frequency exponents.

TorusEuler.hierarchyLevelPairs.text:
The quadratic pairs contributing to the retained source at level `p`.

Default-value audit (b5): Finite sums and index sets are defined at zero order or empty ranges as well. The paper use supplies the intended order and level restrictions.

TorusEuler.hierarchyLevelPairs_eq_of_ret.text: If the target level `p` is at most `Q`, and `Q ≤ P`, the quadratic interaction pairs for that level are identical at depths `P` and `Q` when the shift is at most one. The index constraints already keep every retained interaction within the smaller depth. This is exact independence, not an inequality between truncated sums.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLevelPairs_eq_of_ret.summary: Retained interactions do not depend on the final depth

TorusEuler.hierarchyLevelPairs_spec.text: A pair in `hierarchyLevelPairs P shift p` has first index at least `shift + 1`, second index at least one, and total index `p + shift`. The lemma unpacks the finite-set filter. These facts identify earlier levels and justify exponent identities in the quantitative hierarchy induction.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLevelPairs_spec.summary: Identify the positive indices in a measured source

TorusEuler.hierarchyLevelPairs_two_fast.text: For retained depth at least two, the fast pairs at level two consist only of $(2,1)$. This identifies the interaction of $C_2$ with the phase derivative of the first oscillation. The conclusion is an equality of finite sets, not a bound on that interaction.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLevelPairs_two_fast.summary: The first fast product uses the first completion

TorusEuler.hierarchyLevelPairs_two_slow.text: If `2 ≤ P`, the slow pairs at level two form exactly the singleton $(1,1)$. Thus the first slow source contains only the interaction of the leading profile with itself. The lower bound on retained depth ensures that this pair is present in the truncated index set.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLevelPairs_two_slow.summary: The first slow product uses two leading waves

TorusEuler.hierarchyLinearRelayAt.text:
The exact four slow terms after commuting the time derivative through the pulled-back curl. `Qt` is the potential-time profile computed from (5.33), and `p` is the oscillatory phase pressure.

Default-value audit (b5): The raw fields are arbitrary functions and the label derivatives are totalized. The analytic relay identity and bounds assume smoothness and the momentum relation separately.

TorusEuler.hierarchyLinearRelayAt_eq_coo.text: The four terms in `hierarchyLinearRelayAt` can be regrouped into three coordinate sums: the potential-time curl, the material curl commutator, and the pressure gradient. A nonzero label scale cancels its reciprocal in the coefficient rows. This exact rewrite prepares the relay for uniform finite-word estimates.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLinearRelayAt_eq_coo.summary: The linear relay splits into curl and pressure coordinate terms

TorusEuler.hierarchyLinearRelayAt_freque.text: Scaling the covector by a positive frequency scales the entire four-term linear relay by its reciprocal. The statement assumes differentiability of the primitive and pressure profiles needed by the slow derivatives.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLinearRelayAt_freque.summary: Every linear relay term gains one inverse frequency

TorusEuler.hierarchyLinearRelayAt_input_.text: Scaling both input slices by `r` scales the complete linear relay, including the curl commutator and pressure gradient. The proof first scales the three primitive profiles and then each label derivative. No regularity in time is required for `r`, because it is a scalar on the fixed label–phase slice.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLinearRelayAt_input_.summary: A fixed-time weight passes through the entire relay

TorusEuler.hierarchyLinearRelayAt_smul.text: At a point where the potential, its prescribed time profile, and the pressure are differentiable, multiplying all three by one real scalar multiplies the entire relay by that scalar. The coframe and strain remain fixed. This justifies pulling a frequency factor or a fixed-time amplitude weight outside the spatial relay expression.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLinearRelayAt_smul.summary: A common scalar scales the entire linear relay

TorusEuler.hierarchyLinearRelayAt_sub_tr.text: For a transverse force `F`, subtracting the pulled-back curl of its potential from the forced relay gives the zero-forcing relay. Continuity and the two stated differentiability assumptions justify splitting label derivatives. The pressure contribution of `F` is zero, so its only remaining contribution is precisely the subtracted curl completion.
TorusEuler.hierarchyLinearRelayAt_sub_tr.summary: Removing the force completion leaves the homogeneous relay

TorusEuler.hierarchyLongitudinalProjecti.text:
The longitudinal projection used in the transverse pressure equation.

Default-value audit (b5): At κ=0 the totalized inverse squared norm makes the operator zero, rather than a rank-one projection. The analytic uses supply a nonzero covector.

TorusEuler.hierarchyMeanCap.text: The scalar cap is `K * slow * (3 * (A*A)) + K`. It counts the three quadratic types contributing to each slow pair and adds the residual coefficient. This is a bookkeeping constant only; the corresponding source estimate still requires the recurrence, previous bounds, and parent-loss assumptions.
TorusEuler.hierarchyMeanCap.summary: Count the three products in the mean source

TorusEuler.hierarchyMeanExponent.text: The definition accepts every nonnegative integer $p$, converting it to a real number before subtracting $2$; the mean estimates themselves use only $p\ge2$. The mean and its source have frequency exponent $-5/2-2(p-2)/3$ for $p\ge2$, as in (5.35). This is stronger by $\lambda^{-1/12}$ than the mean bound propagated without parent powers in (5.40). Keeping both estimates is what permits the next source to be controlled without accumulating parent losses.
TorusEuler.hierarchyMeanExponent.summary: Record the sharper frequency scale for each mean level

TorusEuler.hierarchyMixedDirection.text: The definition permits arbitrary real scales, although the physical estimates take $\ell_*>0$ and $h>0$. Derivative indices are ordered only to represent each multi-index once. The derivative directions are the three operators $\ell_*\partial_{a_i}$ and the phase operator $h\partial_s$. Thus mixed derivatives acquire exactly the weights $\ell_*^m h^j$ in (D.1). This is the scaling convention behind the finite expansion estimates; it specifies how derivatives are measured and is not itself a bound on a field.
TorusEuler.hierarchyMixedDirection.summary: Spatial localization and phase width set derivative weights

TorusEuler.hierarchyOscExponent.text: For a nonnegative integer level $p$, the formal definition assigns the real exponent $-5/4-2(p-1)/3$ to the oscillation and its transverse source. The subtraction is performed after $p$ is read as a real number, so the expression also has its usual arithmetic meaning at $p=0$. At $p=1$ it is $-5/4$; at the first omitted level $P+1$ it is $-5/4-2P/3$. Thus the later estimates have the depth gain $\lambda^{-2P/3}$ described in §1.3. This assignment of exponents is not itself a bound on any profile or remainder.
TorusEuler.hierarchyOscExponent.summary: Each additional level gains two thirds of a frequency power

TorusEuler.hierarchyOscExponent_antitone.text: The exponent $-5/4-2(p-1)/3$ decreases as the natural-number level increases. `Antitone` means $i\le j$ implies the exponent at $j$ is at most the exponent at $i$. A separate lower bound on the frequency is needed to turn this comparison of exponents into decay of powers.
TorusEuler.hierarchyOscExponent_antitone.summary: Oscillatory powers decrease with the hierarchy level

TorusEuler.hierarchyOscSourceCap.text: This cap adds the relay contribution, the slow-pair contribution, and two fast-pair contributions, using the supplied bound `B` for a mean factor. It is independent of frequency and parent scale as an expression. The induction supplies nonnegative inputs and proves that it bounds the measured transverse source.
TorusEuler.hierarchyOscSourceCap.summary: Count relay and quadratic costs in the transverse source

TorusEuler.hierarchyParentResidualConsta.text: The parent-residual coefficient is `K` when the optional loss is absent and `K * loss` when it is present. This isolates the residual’s possible extra parent factor from the primitive solver constants. The generalized recurrence theorem later requires this coefficient to be bounded by `K * L^5`.
TorusEuler.hierarchyParentResidualConsta.summary: Allow a separate loss in the level-two residual

TorusEuler.hierarchyPeriodicProfileSubmo.text:
The smooth slab profiles that are periodic under one phase translation.

Default-value audit (b5): The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.hierarchyPeriodicProfileSubmo.summary: Smooth profiles periodic in the phase variable

TorusEuler.hierarchyPhasePeriod.text:
One period in the phase direction of the joint profile domain.

Default-value audit (b5): The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.

TorusEuler.hierarchyPhasePeriod_vadd_sla.text: Translating the entire slab by one phase period yields the same set. This set-level equality complements the pointwise membership lemma. It is used when the domain of a derivative within the slab is translated, including derivatives at either time endpoint.
TorusEuler.hierarchyPhasePeriod_vadd_sla.summary: The slab is invariant under phase translation

TorusEuler.hierarchyPressureLabelGradien.text: This function takes the Fréchet derivative of the uncurried pressure at `(a,s)` and retains only its label component. The output is a vector in three-dimensional space. The definition itself accepts any pressure function; later gradient identities and derivative estimates impose the smoothness needed for its calculus interpretation.
TorusEuler.hierarchyPressureLabelGradien.summary: The pressure gradient with phase held fixed

TorusEuler.hierarchyPressureLabelRestric.text: This continuous linear map restricts a scalar differential on label-phase space to the label directions and then identifies that covector with a vector using the Euclidean inner product. It is the representation of the slow pressure gradient before a profile is read on the physical phase graph.
TorusEuler.hierarchyPressureLabelRestric.summary: Extract the label part of a pressure differential

TorusEuler.hierarchyPressureLabelRestric.text: The label restriction of a differential is the inverse Euclidean dual map applied after composing with the inclusion of label directions. This definitional identity makes the vector representation explicit. It introduces neither a differentiability hypothesis nor an additional estimate; those belong to applications where the argument is a pressure derivative.
TorusEuler.hierarchyPressureLabelRestric.summary: Read the label restriction through the Euclidean dual

TorusEuler.hierarchyProfileReflection.text:
The joint reflection fixes time and reverses both label and phase.

Default-value audit (b5): The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.hierarchyProfileReflection.summary: Reversing label and phase while fixing time

TorusEuler.hierarchyProfileReflectionPar.text: Multiplying a profile by any real function of time preserves its simultaneous label-phase reflection sign. The reflection does not change time, so only commutation of scalar multiplication is needed. No smoothness or support assumption on the multiplier is required for this algebraic statement, which applies in particular to cutoff derivatives.
TorusEuler.hierarchyProfileReflectionPar.summary: A time-only multiplier leaves the reflection sign unchanged

TorusEuler.hierarchyProfileReflection_ap.text: Profile reflection maps (t,a,s) to (t,−a,−s). Time is unchanged, so reflecting a profile preserves the same physical time slab.
TorusEuler.hierarchyProfileReflection_ap.summary: The coordinate formula for profile reflection

TorusEuler.hierarchyProfileReflection_me.text: The joint reflection fixes time while negating label and phase, so it preserves the slab condition in both directions. This membership equivalence lets reflection identities be checked on the slab and extended through zero representatives. It also preserves the domain of derivative calculations at boundary times.
TorusEuler.hierarchyProfileReflection_me.summary: Reflection preserves membership in the time slab

TorusEuler.hierarchyProfileSlab.text:
The time, label and phase domain of the finite expansion.

Default-value audit (b5): If T<0 the slab is empty; if T=0 it has only one time. The analytic constructors requiring unique within-slab derivatives explicitly assume T>0.

TorusEuler.hierarchyQuadraticConstant.text: The product constant is twice the number of admissible sorted words times $2^n$. It depends only on the derivative order and the finite ordered index type. It accounts for the word count, the choices in Leibniz's rule, and the two-factor difference estimate when a bilinear map has norm at most one.
TorusEuler.hierarchyQuadraticConstant.summary: An explicit constant counts the product terms

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayCurlRow.text:
The coefficient of one weighted derivative of the pulled-back curl.

Default-value audit (b5): The row contains ℓ⁻¹, which is zero when ℓ=0 under totalized field inversion. All uses that undo the radius weighting require a positive radius.

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayCurlRow_eq_scal.text: The geometric curl row at width `ell` equals `ell⁻¹` times the unit-width continuous linear row applied to `G`. No positivity or nonzero-width hypothesis is needed for this algebraic equality. Its use as an estimate of an actual rescaled derivative requires the positive label scale supplied by the construction.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayCurlRow_eq_scal.summary: Extract the inverse label width from the curl row

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayGeometricCoeffi.text: With $D\ge1$, $\ell D^{16}\le1$, and the stated label-jet bounds for `G` and `M`, all curl, material-commutator, and pressure rows satisfy one mixed-derivative budget. The strain and coframe powers are absorbed by the label width, leaving the explicit $|\ell^{-1}|D^2$ factor. The theorem proves coefficient bounds, not the relay estimate itself.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayGeometricCoeffi.summary: Parent bounds control all geometric relay coefficients

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayGeometricRowBud.text: Writing $A=\sum_{j\le n}C_j$, this definition takes $(n+1)(A+2\,2^nA^2)|\ell^{-1}|D^2$. The linear terms control curl and pressure rows, while the quadratic term allows the strain–coframe commutator. It is an explicit finite-order allowance rather than a universal numerical constant.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayGeometricRowBud.summary: A common allowance for the three geometric row types

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayLabelJet.text:
Compose the Fréchet derivative of a label–phase function with the inclusion of label directions. The resulting continuous linear map differentiates only the three label coordinates at fixed phase.

Default-value audit (b5): The Fréchet derivative is a total function and becomes zero at nondifferentiability points. The relay estimates supply differentiability or smoothness before using this as a classical label derivative.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayLabelJet.summary: The label component of a profile derivative

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayMaterialRow.text:
This row is M composed with the curl row minus the curl row formed with GM. It records the commutator contribution to the material derivative of the divergence correction.

Default-value audit (b5): This combines the two curl rows algebraically and inherits their inverse-radius convention. Radius positivity is part of the analytic use, not of this raw row definition.

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayMaterialRow_eq_.text: The material relay row at width `ell` is `ell⁻¹` times its fixed unit-width bilinear expression in `G` and `M`. This identity holds for every real width, including zero under totalized inversion. It separates a fixed scalar cost from the two parent coefficients before mixed derivative bounds are applied.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayMaterialRow_eq_.summary: Extract the inverse label width from the material row

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayPotentialCoeffi.text:
The coefficient of the potential after normalizing the covector by the central frequency.

Default-value audit (b5): The raw inverse squared norm is total and gives zero at k=0. The wave-potential interpretation in the construction requires k≠0.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayPotentialCoeffi.summary: The vector-potential coefficient after normalizing frequency

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayPotentialCoeffi.text: Scaling a covector by a positive frequency multiplies its potential coefficient by the reciprocal frequency. The squared norm contributes two inverse factors, while the cross-product operator contributes one positive factor. The equality is valid even for the zero covector because the total coefficient definition is used; positivity is required only for the scaling parameter.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayPotentialCoeffi.summary: Potential coefficients gain one inverse frequency

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayPressureAmplitu.text:
The scalar row sends v to −2⟨k,Mv⟩/‖k‖². It is the amplitude contribution to the transverse pressure slope, before taking the mean-zero phase primitive.

Default-value audit (b5): At k=0 totalized inversion makes this scalar row zero. Pressure recovery uses a nonzero transported covector and the solution equation.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayPressureAmplitu.summary: The amplitude contribution to the pressure slope

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayPressureRow.text:
This scalar-to-vector map is multiplication by the coframe-transformed coordinate vector, with a factor ℓ⁻¹. It restores the unweighted slow derivative from the radius-weighted derivative norm.

Default-value audit (b5): The inverse label radius is total at zero. Applications use ℓ>0; the raw definition alone is not an invertible rescaling.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayPressureRow.summary: The pressure-gradient row with inverse radius

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayPressureRow_eq_.text: The geometric pressure-gradient row is `ell⁻¹` times the unit-width continuous linear row of the inverse coframe. This equality separates the label normalization from the field dependence. It is valid even at zero width as a total algebraic identity, and does not claim that a degenerate width represents a meaningful spatial rescaling.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayPressureRow_eq_.summary: Extract the inverse label width from the pressure row

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayPressureSourceC.text:
The scalar row sends f to ⟨k,f⟩/‖k‖². The complementary amplitude row supplies the other term in the transverse pressure slope.

Default-value audit (b5): At k=0 this row is zero under the totalized formula. The transverse pressure construction requires nonzero covectors before interpreting the row as division by squared length.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayPressureSourceC.summary: The forcing contribution to the pressure slope

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayTimeAmplitudeCo.text:
This continuous linear operator collects the terms involving M, the covector and the amplitude in the time derivative of the normalized vector potential. Its inverse powers of the covector norm require nonvanishing when it is used analytically.

Default-value audit (b5): The formula contains inverse powers of ‖k‖². Nonzero covectors are supplied by the parent geometry in the relay estimates; the raw expression at k=0 is not a time derivative of a physical wave potential.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayTimeAmplitudeCo.summary: The amplitude coefficient in the potential time derivative

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayWordBound_label.text: A smooth operator-valued coefficient bounded through order `n`, applied to one weighted label derivative of a profile bounded through order `n + 1`, has budget $2^nAC$. The label index is `Fin 3`; the phase coordinate is excluded. Reciprocal label scale is accounted for in the supplied coefficient rather than differentiated separately.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayWordBound_label.summary: A coefficient times a label derivative loses one order

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayWordBound_linea.text: Smooth phase-independent operator coefficients acting on smooth periodic zero-mean velocity and forcing profiles produce a smooth normalized primitive with an explicit word bound. The constant combines the two coefficient budgets and the factor from phase integration. Time is only an arbitrary index, so no time regularity of coefficients or forcing is assumed.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayWordBound_linea.summary: A linear combination of profiles has a bounded phase primitive

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayWordBound_of_fi.text: If every sampled derivative set is bounded above, the finite mixed norm bounds each word of order at most n. Boundedness is explicit because the norm is a finite sum of real suprema.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayWordBound_of_fi.summary: The finite norm bounds all normalized words

TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayWordBound_of_ph.text: A normalized label-jet bound gives the same mixed-word bound for the phase-independent lift of the coefficient.
TorusEuler.hierarchyRelayWordBound_of_ph.summary: Label bounds also control phase-independent mixed words

TorusEuler.hierarchyScaledCoframeRow.text: This definition composes one coordinate projection with the operator field `A` and multiplies it by $\ell^{-1}$. Applied to an advector, it is the chosen component of $Az$ divided by the label radius. It pairs with a radius-weighted coordinate derivative in the slow-advection estimate.
TorusEuler.hierarchyScaledCoframeRow.summary: A coframe row carries the reciprocal label radius

TorusEuler.hierarchyScaledPhaseCoefficie.text: The coefficient is the linear form $z\mapsto h^{-1}\langle\kappa,z\rangle$. Factoring this reciprocal width out of the weighted phase derivative recovers the physical fast-advection term. The definition permits arbitrary real `h`; the later identity cancelling the width assumes `hh : h ≠ 0`.
TorusEuler.hierarchyScaledPhaseCoefficie.summary: The phase coefficient carries the reciprocal width

TorusEuler.hierarchySeminorm_remainder_l.text: The exact algebraic remainder is bounded in an arbitrary seminorm from separate estimates for its linear, slow-product, completion-phase, and mean-phase terms. The assumptions include $\lambda\ge1$, nonnegative constants, and `loss * freq^(-1/12) ≤ 1`. The conclusion counts the retained tail pairs explicitly; the analytic product estimates are hypotheses here.
TorusEuler.hierarchySeminorm_remainder_l.summary: Component estimates control the exact finite remainder

TorusEuler.hierarchySeminorm_sum_le.text: For any real seminorm `N`, the seminorm of a finite sum is bounded by the sum of the individual seminorms. The ambient object needs only an additive group and real module structure. This permits the hierarchy estimates to be assembled before choosing concrete weighted or unweighted function norms.
TorusEuler.hierarchySeminorm_sum_le.summary: A seminorm of a finite sum obeys the triangle inequality

TorusEuler.hierarchySeminorm_velocity_su.text: Given all measured level bounds through depth `P ≥ 1`, this theorem bounds the total oscillation at $\lambda^{-5/4}$, its part beyond the first velocity at $\lambda^{-23/12}$, and the total mean at $\lambda^{-5/2}$. Constants retain the number of levels and explicit powers of `loss`. The norms are arbitrary seminorm families satisfying the supplied nonnegativity conditions.
TorusEuler.hierarchySeminorm_velocity_su.summary: Summing levels separates the leading oscillation from corrections

TorusEuler.hierarchySlowAdvectionCompone.text: With nonzero label radius, this bounds the component $(Az)_i\partial_{a_i}g$ using the scaled coframe-row norm, the advector norm, and one extra order of the advected field. Smoothness and bounded jet sets are required for each input. The coefficient bound `hAN` is assumed; this statement does not establish the deformation estimates itself.
TorusEuler.hierarchySlowAdvectionCompone.summary: Slow advection uses one coframe row and derivative

TorusEuler.hierarchySmoothProfileSubmodu.text:
A smooth slab profile is represented by its zero extension. Values of this representative outside the slab do not enter any derivative or equation.

Default-value audit (b5): The representative is deliberately zero outside the slab. Smoothness is required within the slab, and no smooth zero extension across the time endpoints is claimed. If the slab is empty the stored function must be zero everywhere.
TorusEuler.hierarchySmoothProfileSubmodu.summary: Smooth slab profiles stored by zero extension

TorusEuler.hierarchyStepCap.text:
The order-dependent constants grow with depth through finitely many terms, independently of the frequency and parent loss.

Default-value audit (b5): The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.

TorusEuler.hierarchyStepCap_ge.text: When `K` and `A` are nonnegative, the explicit step cap is at least `A`. Every additional term in its definition is nonnegative, including the finite interaction counts. This supplies monotonicity of the recursively chosen constants without claiming they are minimal or sharply estimated.
TorusEuler.hierarchyStepCap_ge.summary: The next finite constant dominates the previous one

TorusEuler.hierarchyTailPairs.text: This is a finite index set, not an estimate. Both indices are positive and at most $P+1$; phase-advection indexing starts the first index at two. After cancellation through depth $P$, label interactions remain when $i+j\ge P+1$, and phase interactions remain when $i+j\ge P+2$. These are the ranges in (5.30), with positive indices up to the last correction level. The formal sum omits initial phase factors that are identically zero under the expansion conventions.
TorusEuler.hierarchyTailPairs.summary: Select the quadratic terms above the retained depth

TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedMixedWord.text: This recursively defines linear differentiation by a word in four coordinate directions. The first three directions carry the label scale and the last carries the phase scale; the empty word leaves the profile unchanged. Each step differentiates the previously obtained profile while preserving smoothness and both periodicity conditions.
TorusEuler.hierarchyTwistedMixedWord.summary: Apply a sequence of scaled label and phase derivatives
