No smallness condition is imposed; later estimates make the exponential harmless.
TorusEuler.linearODE_perturbation_bounds.summary: Growth and error under an integrated matrix perturbation

TorusEuler.linearODE_unique_of_mem.text: Two solutions of a continuous linear ODE on an interval agree everywhere if they agree at any time in the interval.
TorusEuler.linearODE_unique_of_mem.summary: A continuous linear equation has unique trajectories

TorusEuler.linearODE_variation_of_consta.text: In a real Banach space, let $A$ and $f$ be continuous on $[a,b]$. Suppose bounded linear maps $\Phi,\Psi$ satisfy $\Phi(a)=\Psi(a)=I$, $\Phi\prime=A\Phi$ and $\Psi\prime=-\Psi A$, and let $z\prime=Az+f$ on the interval. Then $z(t)=\Phi(t)z(a)+\int_a^t\Phi(t)\Psi(r)f(r)\,dr$ for every $t\in[a,b]$. Derivatives at the endpoints are taken within the interval. The paper applies this general identity with the unperturbed triangular flow and forcing equal to the coefficient error applied to the perturbed solution. The statement assumes the two fundamental evolutions; it supplies neither their existence nor a propagator bound.
TorusEuler.linearODE_variation_of_consta.summary: A fundamental solution and its inverse give the integral identity

TorusEuler.linearODE_weightedHierarchyWo.text: Specializes the localized weighted word estimate to $x(l)=0$. Under the same closed-support, smoothness, positive-weight, stability, and commutator-cap assumptions, the resulting constant is the order factor times $K\cdot (r-l)\cdot H$. The proof verifies a zero initial word bound and invokes the general theorem, so support propagation remains part of the argument.
TorusEuler.linearODE_weightedHierarchyWo.summary: Zero initial data removes the initial-value contribution

TorusEuler.linearODE_weightedHierarchyWo.text: On $[l,r]$, initial data and forcing vanish outside a closed set `S`, while weighted homogeneous stability and positive-order coefficient estimates are required only on `S`. Smoothness, a strictly positive time weight, and a cap on $K\cdot (r-l)\cdot C$ yield a global finite-word bound for the weighted solution. Outside `S`, uniqueness gives zero solution and closedness gives zero derivatives.
TorusEuler.linearODE_weightedHierarchyWo.summary: Localized initial data and forcing give a global word bound

TorusEuler.linearODE_wordBounds.text: On a positive slab $[0,T]$, assumes smooth coefficients, forcing, and solution, a strictly positive differentiable weight, weighted homogeneous stability on `S`, and initial, forcing, and positive-order coefficient bounds through order `N`. Every solution word through that order is bounded by $\mathrm{linearODEWordFactor}(KTC,N)\,K(B+TH)$. Independence from other parameters requires a separate uniform bound on $K\cdot T\cdot C$.
TorusEuler.linearODE_wordBounds.summary: Control all parameter words through a prescribed order

TorusEuler.linearODE_wordBounds_Icc.text: For $l < r$, gives the same all-word estimate on $[l,r]$, replacing time length `T` by $r-l$ and initial data at zero by data at `l`. All smoothness, positive-weight, homogeneous-stability, and coefficient hypotheses are stated on that interval. The proof translates the problem to a zero-start slab and translates solutions back.
TorusEuler.linearODE_wordBounds_Icc.summary: The weighted word estimate allows any launch time

TorusEuler.lipschitzOnWith_halfHolder_of.text: If every label evaluation has the stated within-interval time derivative and the derivative fields have half-Hölder norm at most `B ≥ 0`, the entire field curve is `B`-Lipschitz in the half-Hölder norm. The proof controls values and spatial increments separately. A pointwise value bound on derivatives alone would not establish this norm-level conclusion.
TorusEuler.lipschitzOnWith_halfHolder_of.summary: Uniform derivative control gives a Lipschitz Hölder-space curve

TorusEuler.lipschitzWith_toUnitTorus.text: The map from Euclidean space to the unit torus is Lipschitz with constant one. It packages the preceding distance comparison as a `LipschitzWith` statement, supplying continuity and quantitative control for translated curves. This concerns the quotient map, not a discontinuous choice of real representatives of torus points.

TorusEuler.listSum_le_card_mul.text: If every entry of a real-valued list is at most $M$, its sum is at most the list length times $M$. Nonnegativity is not assumed for this elementary addition inequality. The finite-word product estimates apply it after finding a common bound for all Leibniz terms.

TorusEuler.listSum_sub.text: The difference of two sums over the same list is the sum of the termwise differences. This is an additive identity requiring no analytic hypotheses. It aligns corresponding Leibniz terms at two spatial points before applying the bilinear difference estimate used for the half-Hölder seminorm.

TorusEuler.list_eq_castSucc_map_of_not_m.text: Any word in `Fin 4` that omits the last letter can be written as a word in `Fin 3` mapped through `Fin.castSucc`. This finite combinatorial fact separates genuine label words from words containing the phase direction. It supplies the indexing correspondence for equality of the two finite derivative norms.
TorusEuler.list_eq_castSucc_map_of_not_m.summary: A word without phase letters is a label word

TorusEuler.localizedCoefficient_holderHa.text: Suppose $r>0$, $0\le\chi\le1$, $\chi$ vanishes beyond distance $2r$ from $a_0$, and $|\chi(a)-\chi(b)|\le(C/r)d(a,b)$ with $C\ge0$. If $B$ has Lipschitz constant $L\ge0$, then $E(a)=\chi(a)(B(a_0)-B(a))$ satisfies $\|E\|_\infty\le2rL$, Lipschitz bound $(1+2C)L$, and half-Hölder seminorm at most $\max(4,1+2C)L\sqrt r$. These are the quantitative estimates used near the freezing point. For a full half-Hölder norm bound one must combine the supremum and increment estimates, using the small radius chosen in the proof.
TorusEuler.localizedCoefficient_holderHa.summary: Obtain small Hölder increments from a Lipschitz coefficient

TorusEuler.localizedCompletedWave_proper.text: Fix a time. Let the smooth inverse label map commute with integer translations, and let a transverse profile vanish for all phases in a collar of the centered label-cell boundary. Assume its phase potential is jointly smooth in label and phase; inside the cell the covector must be nonzero and equal to $(D_xA)^Tk_*$. The formal statement constructs $W$ as the curl of the periodically extended evaluated potential. It proves that $W$ is smooth, spatially periodic and divergence free everywhere, and equals $V^\natural+C[V]^\natural$ where the label lies inside the cell. Arbitrary real $k_*$ are permitted. This is a spatial assertion at a fixed time; joint time regularity requires separate hypotheses.
TorusEuler.localizedCompletedWave_proper.summary: Periodizing the potential produces a globally divergence-free velocity

TorusEuler.localizedCurl_properties.text: Assume the inverse label is smooth and lattice-equivariant, the evaluated potential is smooth, and it vanishes in a collar of width $0<\delta\le1/2$. Its localized curl is smooth, periodic, and divergence free. Where inverse labels lie in the cell interior, it agrees exactly with the curl of the unperiodized transported potential.
TorusEuler.localizedCurl_properties.summary: A collar supported potential gives a smooth periodic solenoidal wave

TorusEuler.localizedTransportedProfile.text: For an arbitrary real wave vector $k_*$, first evaluate the profile as $a\mapsto f(t,a,k_*\cdot a)$ on the centered label cell. The formal definition extends that field periodically and composes it with the inverse label map $A(t,x)$. This is the localized interpretation of $f^\natural$ in §3.1. It is a formula defined without smoothness or support assumptions. Vanishing near the cell boundary is needed for a smooth extension, and integer-translation equivariance of $A$ is needed for spatial periodicity after composition. The phase itself need not be periodic, and $k_*$ need not lie in $\mathbb Z^3$.
TorusEuler.localizedTransportedProfile.summary: Evaluate on one label cell, periodize, then return to physical space

TorusEuler.localizedTransportedProfile_e.text: Assume the forward flow `X` is a left inverse of the label map, is lattice-equivariant, fixes zero and is `L`-Lipschitz. If the profile vanishes outside the centered label radius `r`, then its transported value vanishes at any point farther than `L*r` from every lattice point. This is the support statement before applying the Fourier cutoff.
TorusEuler.localizedTransportedProfile_e.summary: Transported support stays near lattice translates of the origin

TorusEuler.localizedTransportedProfile_e.text: Assume the inverse label is continuous at `x`, its value lies in the interior centered cell, and the profile vanishes in the stated positive-width collar. Then localized periodized graph evaluation agrees with ordinary transported evaluation near `x`. This local equality transfers derivatives without differentiating the discontinuous representative globally.
TorusEuler.localizedTransportedProfile_e.summary: The localized and ordinary profiles agree near interior labels

TorusEuler.localizedTransportedProfile_r.text: Assume an odd spatial label map `A t` and a profile whose simultaneous label-phase reflection is given by a continuous linear map `L`. With a positive radial envelope contained within the cell, its localized transported realization obeys the same output reflection at $-x$. Both the label and the graph phase change sign under oddness of `A t`.
TorusEuler.localizedTransportedProfile_r.summary: Odd inverse labels carry reflection to physical space

TorusEuler.localized_couplingDifference_.text: Bounds the change in $\langle k,Ma\rangle$ when the covector and amplitude have relative error at most `δ`, while the gradient has absolute operator error at most `δ`. With $D\ge1$, $0\le\delta\le1$ and $\|M\|\le D$, the error is at most $4D\delta\|k_0\|\|a_0\|$. The three-term expansion separates the covector, amplitude and gradient contributions.
TorusEuler.localized_couplingDifference_.summary: The coupling changes linearly with relative errors

TorusEuler.localized_coupling_positive.text: Assume nonzero reference covector and amplitude, central raw coupling at least $D^{-1}\|k_0\|\|a_0\|$, and the stated relative and gradient errors with $0\le\delta\le(8D^2)^{-1}$. Both perturbed norms remain within factors one half and two. The raw coupling stays strictly positive and above $(2D)^{-1}$ times the reference norm product, while its normalized value is at least $(8D)^{-1}$.
TorusEuler.localized_coupling_positive.summary: Positive central coupling survives a small spatial perturbation

TorusEuler.localized_norm_bounds.text: A perturbation satisfying $\|x-x_0\|\le\delta\|x_0\|$ with $\delta\le1/2$ has norm between half and twice the reference norm. The proof uses only the triangle inequality in a normed additive group. A separate assumption that `δ` is nonnegative is unnecessary for this conditional statement; the later seed application supplies it through its nonnegative error budget.
TorusEuler.localized_norm_bounds.summary: Relative closeness preserves the vector size

TorusEuler.localized_normalized_coupling.text: Identifies the contraction of the normalized covector and normalized amplitude with $\langle k,Ma\rangle/(\|k\|\|a\|)$. This algebraic identity holds for arbitrary vectors, including zero vectors under Lean’s totalized normalization and division. It does not assert positivity or a meaningful direction at zero; those facts enter through the nonvanishing hypotheses of the coupling theorem.
TorusEuler.localized_normalized_coupling.summary: Normalized coupling is the raw contraction quotient

TorusEuler.locallyFinite_latticeTranslat.text: The supports of all lattice translates of a fixed smooth compactly supported bump form a locally finite family. Near any spatial point, only lattice vectors within a bounded radius can contribute, and there are finitely many of them. This permits smooth summation of the translated extensions without requiring convergence of an infinite derivative series.
TorusEuler.locallyFinite_latticeTranslat.summary: Translated bump supports are locally finite

TorusEuler.logNormDerivOfScaled.text: Let $v$ be a path in a real inner-product space and assume $v\ne0$ at a time where its relative derivative is $v'=|v|w$. The formal statement proves $(\log|v|)'=(v/|v|)\cdot w$. Substitution of $w=v'/|v|$ gives the logarithmic-norm identity displayed in the proof of Lemma 2.2. It applies to any such path, rather than only to the wave vector or amplitude. The norm is positive under the hypothesis, so the logarithm and division have their ordinary mathematical meanings. The wave equations must be substituted separately to obtain $-B_{11}$ and $-B_{22}$.
TorusEuler.logNormDerivOfScaled.summary: The radial component gives the logarithmic derivative of a nonzero norm

TorusEuler.longitudinalMode.text: This private coefficient is the integer frequency embedded in complex Euclidean space. It spans the longitudinal direction for that mode and is inserted into spatial $L^2$ to generate gradient directions. At frequency zero it is the zero vector, leaving constant velocity coefficients unconstrained.
TorusEuler.longitudinalMode.summary: The frequency vector as a longitudinal coefficient

TorusEuler.lp_two_norm_sq_eq_intervalInt.text: For an $L^2$ equivalence class on the restricted time measure and nonnegative `T`, its norm squared equals the interval integral of the squared norm of its chosen representative. The value is independent of that representative up to null sets. This identity converts integral energy bounds into operator-norm estimates.
TorusEuler.lp_two_norm_sq_eq_intervalInt.summary: The L² norm equals its squared time integral

TorusEuler.lp_two_sq_eq_integral.text: For an $E$-valued element of `Lp E 2 μ`, its squared norm equals the integral of the squared norm of its chosen representative. The real inner-product-space structure supplies the identity through the L² inner product. The theorem is generic in the underlying measured space and is not a new PDE estimate.
TorusEuler.lp_two_sq_eq_integral.summary: The Hilbert norm equals the integrated square

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_add_continuous.text: The Fourier coefficient of the sum of two continuous torus fields is the sum of their Fourier coefficients. Completeness of the complex target and compactness of the torus ensure that the integrands are integrable before additivity is applied. This supports the real cutoff’s linearity and the momentum rearrangement.
TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_add_continuous.summary: Fourier coefficients add for continuous fields

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_advection_eq_ze.text: If the continuous torus velocity `g` is supported in the $2\Lambda$ band and `A` agrees with its self advection after lifting, every coefficient of `A` outside the $4\Lambda$ band is zero. Spatial differentiation preserves frequencies; multiplying the differentiated field by `g` adds two frequencies. The equality assumption `hA` identifies the supplied representative.
TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_advection_eq_ze.summary: Self advection doubles the parent frequency band

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_comp_clm.text: A continuous complex-linear scalar functional applied to a continuous torus field commutes with taking its Fourier coefficient. The proof moves the functional through the Bochner integral and uses complex linearity for the character factor. This reduces vector-valued Fourier uniqueness to scalar Fourier uniqueness.
TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_comp_clm.summary: Scalar linear functionals commute with Fourier coefficients

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_comp_complexCLM.text: For a continuous torus field with values in a complete complex normed space, applying a continuous complex linear map commutes with taking a Fourier coefficient. Continuity on the compact torus supplies Bochner integrability. This is the integral identity behind the cutoff formulas for vector components and tensor columns.
TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_comp_complexCLM.summary: Fourier coefficients commute with bounded complex maps

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_compactDyadicBl.text: The coefficient of the `j`th compact-symbol block at lattice frequency `k` is the symbol evaluated at $2^{-j}k$ applied to the input coefficient. The Fourier transform of the dilated kernel gives the formula. This identifies the actual convolution block before its size and increment bounds are established.
TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_compactDyadicBl.summary: A dyadic block samples the symbol at the scaled frequency

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_compactSymbolDy.text: The blocks inside `compactSymbolDyadicBlocks` act on each input Fourier coefficient by evaluating the compact symbol at the scaled lattice frequency. Packing the blocks with decay certificates does not change their convolution action. This formula is used when summing annular pieces to recover the desired nonzero-frequency multiplier.
TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_compactSymbolDy.summary: The certified blocks keep the original sampled symbol formula

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_complexHessianE.text: The Fourier coefficient of a chosen matrix entry of a continuous operator field equals that entry of the operator-valued Fourier coefficient. Compactness of the torus supplies integrability, and the continuous complex-linear coordinate map commutes with the integral. This justifies proving the operator equality entry by entry.
TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_complexHessianE.summary: Extracting an entry commutes with Fourier integration

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_complexPressure.text: For real source data, each entry of the constructed complex multiplier has the Fourier coefficient prescribed by two coordinate derivative factors and the inverse Laplacian symbol. The proof combines entrywise integration with the exact multiplier symbol. This establishes the formula for all integer frequencies before any candidate potential is introduced.
TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_complexPressure.summary: Each constructed Hessian entry has the correct coefficient

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_complexPressure.text: For every integer frequency, the Fourier coefficient of the complex multiplier output is the pressure symbol applied to the input coefficient. Positive homogeneity supplies the hypothesis of the general multiplier theorem. This identifies the constructed operator mode by mode, including frequency zero, rather than merely asserting an operator-norm bound.
TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_complexPressure.summary: The multiplier has the prescribed Fourier coefficients

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_complexPressure.text: The Fourier coefficient of the complex pressure multiplier equals negative inverse Laplacian mode times the double derivative contraction of the tensor coefficient. Homogeneity of the symbol validates the dyadic Fourier law. The identity also holds at zero, where the output coefficient is zero by normalization.
TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_complexPressure.summary: Every pressure coefficient has the exact Poisson multiplier

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_conj.text: The coefficient at $k$ of the complex-conjugated field is the conjugate of the original coefficient at $-k$. The sign reversal comes from conjugating the Fourier character. This identity supports the proof that a real, even multiplier preserves real-valued fields despite using complex Fourier notation.

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_coordinateDeriv.text: For a continuously differentiable lifted torus vector field, a continuous field representing its coordinate derivative has Fourier coefficient equal to $2\pi i k_i$ times the original coefficient. The actual derivative representation `hd` is required. The result uses the unit-torus frequency normalization and includes the zero mode, whose derivative coefficient vanishes.
TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_coordinateDeriv.summary: Fourier coefficients identify a vector coordinate derivative

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_coordinate_hess.text: For continuous torus representatives `g` and `h` of a periodic $C^2$ complex field and one of its Hessian entries, the Fourier coefficient of `h` is the coefficient of `g` times the two coordinate derivative symbols. The hypotheses `hg` and `hh` are exact representation equalities, not automatically supplied by their types.
TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_coordinate_hess.summary: Transfer the Hessian formula to torus representatives

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_cutoff_comp_coo.text: For a continuous torus field in a complete complex normed space, taking any continuous complex-linear scalar coordinate commutes with its Fourier coefficient. The proof moves the linear map through the Bochner integral after proving integrability on the compact torus. This reduces vector Fourier identities to their scalar coordinate versions.
TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_cutoff_comp_coo.summary: Linear coordinates commute with Fourier coefficients

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_finiteFourierSu.text: In a complete complex normed space, the coefficient of a finite Fourier sum at $k$ is the assigned value when $k$ belongs to the synthesis set, and zero otherwise. Character orthogonality proves the result. This identifies a polynomial exactly, rather than approximately, through its finite coefficient list.
TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_finiteFourierSu.summary: A finite synthesis has exactly its assigned coefficients

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_finsetSum_conti.text: For finitely many continuous fields with values in a complete complex normed space, the Fourier coefficient of their sum equals the sum of the coefficients. Continuity is required only for indices belonging to `s`. The proof establishes integrability of each character weighted term before interchanging the finite sum and integral.
TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_finsetSum_conti.summary: Fourier coefficients distribute over finite sums

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_halfHolderConst.text: The Fourier coefficient of the constant field with value `a` is `a` at zero frequency and zero at every other frequency. The proof realizes the constant as a one-term finite Fourier synthesis. This makes the separate mean contribution disjoint from all annular nonzero-frequency blocks.
TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_halfHolderConst.summary: A constant field has only its zero Fourier coefficient

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_halfHolderDyadi.text: The Fourier coefficient of the multiplier output is the sum of the Fourier coefficients of its dyadic blocks. The blocks are summable in the continuous-function supremum norm, and coefficient extraction is continuous in that norm. No claim about summability in the full half-Hölder norm is needed for this interchange.
TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_halfHolderDyadi.summary: Fourier coefficients pass through the uniformly convergent block sum

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_halfHolderTorus.text: The Fourier coefficient of the embedded half-Hölder field equals that of its underlying continuous field. The proof compares the representatives inside the coefficient integral. This compatibility allows the same symbol formula to be used on the continuous/Hölder side and on the weak L² side of the construction.
TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_halfHolderTorus.summary: Embedding into L² preserves every Fourier coefficient

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_homogeneousHalf.text: Assume `hhom` makes `A` invariant under positive scaling away from zero. Then every Fourier coefficient of the constructed multiplier output is `A(k)` applied to the corresponding input coefficient. At nonzero frequencies the annular partition telescopes; at zero the separate constant term gives the prescribed value. This is where symbol identification is actually proved.
TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_homogeneousHalf.summary: With homogeneity the constructed operator has the prescribed symbol

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_inner_latticeVe.text: If `hv` places a real spatial $L^2$ field in the weak solenoidal subspace, the Fourier coefficient of its contraction with a frequency vector vanishes at that frequency. The proof uses real and imaginary Fourier potentials as smooth tests. This establishes a consequence of weak divergence freedom without differentiating the velocity.
TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_inner_latticeVe.summary: Weak solenoidality annihilates longitudinal Fourier coefficients

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_neg_of_parity.text: If a torus field satisfies `hg : g (-z) = c • g z` for a real scalar `c`, its Fourier coefficients satisfy the corresponding relation at opposite frequencies. The proof changes variables by the measure-preserving negation map. This statement does not require a finite Fourier expansion.

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_operatorTorusCo.text: For a continuous integrable operator kernel and continuous input, the Fourier coefficient of the convolution equals the Euclidean Fourier transform of the kernel at the lattice frequency applied to the input coefficient. Completeness of both value spaces and joint integrability justify Fubini and operator interchange. The kernel need not be scalar.
TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_operatorTorusCo.summary: An operator convolution applies its sampled symbol to each coefficient

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_realInput.text: The Fourier coefficient of the bundled complexification of a real half-Hölder field equals the coefficient obtained by complexifying its values directly. This follows by pointwise evaluation of `HalfHolder.map`. It aligns two encodings of the same scalar source before comparing the constructed multiplier with the actual pressure.
TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_realInput.summary: Identify the Fourier coefficients of complexified source data

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_realVectorFouri.text: For an even symbol, each Fourier coefficient of the complexified real cutoff is the input coefficient multiplied by $\psi(\Lambda^{-1}k)$ inside the closed band of radius $2\Lambda$, and zero outside it. The conditional band test is part of the finite-synthesis definition. The identity holds without a positivity assumption on `Λ`; physical cutoff estimates impose one separately.
TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_realVectorFouri.summary: The real cutoff has the prescribed finite Fourier coefficients

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_real_coordinate.text: For a periodic real $C^2$ field and exact continuous torus representatives of it and a mixed derivative, complexified Fourier coefficients differ by the two coordinate derivative factors. The assumptions `hg` and `hh` tie the representatives to the actual field. This is a Fourier identity, with no Hölder-norm estimate yet.
TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_real_coordinate.summary: The real Hessian has the complex Fourier derivative formula

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_real_hessian_eq.text: For a periodic $C^2$ potential and exact representatives of its Hessian entry and Laplacian, the Hessian coefficient equals two derivative factors times `inverseLaplacianMode` times the source coefficient. The zero mode is handled separately; inversion occurs only when `k ≠ 0`. No zero-mean normalization of the potential is required, since its Hessian ignores constants.
TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_real_hessian_eq.summary: Recover Hessian coefficients from the Laplacian source

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_real_laplacian.text: For a periodic real $C^2$ field, the coefficient of its represented Laplacian equals `laplacianMode k` times its represented scalar coefficient after complexification. Exact lift identities are required for both torus functions. This provides the equation used to eliminate the potential’s coefficient in favour of its Laplacian source.
TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_real_laplacian.summary: The real Laplacian obeys the Fourier symbol identity

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_single_mode_eq_.text: The Fourier coefficient at `k` of one character at frequency `a` times a vector `e` vanishes when `hk : k ≠ a`. The proof integrates the product of the two characters and uses their orthogonality. This is the local calculation behind the finite frequency support argument.

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_smoothFourierCu.text: For positive `hΛ` and a symbol vanishing when its argument has norm greater than two, the cutoff coefficient at $k$ is $\psi(\Lambda^{-1}k)\widehat g(k)$. Completeness of the target space is assumed. The support hypothesis ensures that frequencies omitted by finite synthesis would also have zero multiplier.
TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_smoothFourierCu.summary: The cutoff multiplies Fourier coefficients by the scaled symbol

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_smoothFourierCu.text: If `hk` places the frequency strictly beyond radius $2\Lambda$, its Fourier coefficient in the cutoff output is zero. The result uses only the finite synthesis band, so no smoothness or support assumption on `ψ` is required. Completeness is needed for the coefficient-recovery theorem used in the proof.
TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_smoothFourierCu.summary: Frequencies beyond the cutoff band vanish

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_smul_finiteFour.text: For the product of a scalar finite Fourier sum and a vector finite Fourier sum, the coefficient at `k` vanishes if `k` is unequal to every sum `j + l` from their supports. Expanding the product gives the convolution rule directly. The hypothesis concerns membership in the finite supports, without imposing a radius or symmetry.
TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_smul_finiteFour.summary: Products cannot create unrelated Fourier frequencies

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_timeDerivative_.text: A jointly smooth family supported in one fixed finite band has its supplied time derivative supported in that same band throughout $[a,b]$. The strict inequality `hab` makes within derivatives unique at the endpoints. The proof differentiates the finite Fourier representation; `hd` identifies the continuous torus field `d` with the actual derivative.
TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_timeDerivative_.summary: Time differentiation preserves a fixed Fourier band

TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_torusLiftConvol.text: For a Schwartz kernel and continuous torus field, the Fourier coefficient after convolution is the input coefficient multiplied by the Euclidean Fourier transform of the kernel at the lattice frequency. Joint integrability justifies swapping the Euclidean and torus integrals. Haar translation invariance and the character law then separate the coefficient.
TorusEuler.mFourierCoeff_torusLiftConvol.summary: A convolution coefficient is multiplied by the sampled transform

TorusEuler.mFourier_add_arg.text: For each lattice frequency, evaluating the torus character at `z + w` gives the product of its values at `z` and `w`. This character law is used when translating the Haar integration variable in the convolution coefficient calculation. It is an exact algebraic identity valid at every torus point.
TorusEuler.mFourier_add_arg.summary: Fourier characters turn spatial addition into multiplication

TorusEuler.mFourier_neg_arg.text: Evaluating the torus character at the negative spatial point is the same as evaluating the character with negative frequency at the original point. This group-character identity applies directly on the quotient torus. It supplies the change of variables in the coefficient and polynomial parity arguments.

TorusEuler.materialAcceleration.text:
The Eulerian material acceleration on a time slab.

Default-value audit (b5): Both time and spatial derivatives are totalized. The PDE interpretation requires time regularity within the specified slab and spatial differentiability; an empty time set must not be used as a classical evolution domain.

TorusEuler.materialAcceleration_restrict.text: For a jointly continuously differentiable velocity, identifies material acceleration computed within a smaller closed interval with that computed within the enclosing interval. The smaller interval must have positive length, and the evaluation time must lie inside it. Unique within derivatives justify the equality even at the smaller interval’s endpoints.
TorusEuler.materialAcceleration_restrict.summary: Material acceleration agrees on a positive smaller slab

TorusEuler.matrix_det_hasDerivWithinAt.text: If every matrix entry has within-set derivative given by the corresponding entry of $Af(t)$, then the determinant has derivative $\operatorname{tr}(A)\det f(t)$. This three-dimensional identity does not assume the matrix is invertible. It therefore establishes the volume evolution before a determinant-one conclusion is available.

TorusEuler.max_initialCoefficientCosts_g.text: If every entry of the coefficient-cost table is at least one, then one plus its sum through order `n` is at least one. Only nonnegativity of the summands is needed in the proof. This elementary estimate supplies an admissible enlarged constant for the coefficient calculus.
TorusEuler.max_initialCoefficientCosts_g.summary: A finite coefficient budget is at least one

TorusEuler.meanCoefficient_radius_condit.text: If $D,B\ge1$, $A\le BD^a$, and $\ell\le(BD^{a+9})^{-2}$, then $\ell D^6\le1$ and $AD^9\sqrt\ell\le1$. The displayed theorem does not assume a positive radius or nonnegative $A$; negative radii satisfy these algebraic conclusions under Lean's square-root convention. Applications needing a geometric radius must supply positivity separately.
TorusEuler.meanCoefficient_radius_condit.summary: One radius restriction satisfies both smallness conditions

TorusEuler.meanDerivativeLifting.text: Assume a wordwise inverse recurrence, nonnegative solution sizes, weighted forcing bounded by $M$, and positive-order coefficient costs satisfying $A\ell^{|s|}B_s\le C$. Then every word through order $N$ obeys $\ell^{|s|}V_s\le AM(1+2^NC)^{|s|}$. The induction uses strictly shorter solution words; the inverse factor $A$ is retained only once outside the order-dependent constant.
TorusEuler.meanDerivativeLifting.summary: Keep a single low-order inverse cost through differentiation

TorusEuler.meanPressureGradientComp.text: This construction packages the pointwise operator product of two half-Hölder fields as another half-Hölder field, using the preceding value and increment estimates. It records composition in the order `U` after `V`. The name refers to their role as gradients; the inputs need not themselves come from differentiable vector fields.
TorusEuler.meanPressureGradientComp.summary: Compose two gradient fields in the Hölder space

TorusEuler.meanPressureGradientProduct_b.text: For two half-Hölder operator fields, their pointwise product is bounded in value and in square-root-distance increments by twice the product of their norms. The second inequality uses the difference-of-products decomposition. These bounds construct the operator-composition field before taking its trace in the Poisson source.
TorusEuler.meanPressureGradientProduct_b.summary: The product of two Hölder gradients is Hölder controlled

TorusEuler.meanPressureHessian_closedSla.text: The actual mean pressure Hessian on the closed slab has its uniform spatial Hölder bound and its supremum bound from the linearized momentum.
TorusEuler.meanPressureHessian_closedSla.summary: The mean pressure Hessian has a uniform bound

TorusEuler.meanPressureHessian_halfHolde.text: Assume a smooth periodic pressure satisfies the stated Poisson equation with periodic half-Hölder coefficient fields. Its Hessian then belongs to the order-zero half-Hölder space, with norm bounded by $48\lVert\mathrm{pressureHessianMultiplier}\rVert$ times the forcing-gradient norm plus the product of the velocity-gradient norms. This is a two-sided norm estimate for the mean component, unlike the signed leading-pressure estimate.
TorusEuler.meanPressureHessian_halfHolde.summary: The periodic Poisson multiplier controls the mean Hessian

TorusEuler.meanPressureHessian_rate_abso.text: The mean velocity and source estimates give the same frequency decay for the mean pressure Hessian after a polynomial parent loss is absorbed into the parameter threshold. This is an estimate for the selected mean correction, not the full pressure.
TorusEuler.meanPressureHessian_rate_abso.summary: Absorbing the parent factor in the mean pressure bound

TorusEuler.meanPressurePoissonSource.text: Given half-Hölder fields representing the two velocity gradients and the forcing gradient, this defines the scalar field obtained by tracing the forcing gradient and subtracting twice the trace of the gradient composition. The construction is made inside the half-Hölder space. Its identification with a physical pressure Laplacian requires the later representation and momentum hypotheses.
TorusEuler.meanPressurePoissonSource.summary: The forcing divergence minus twice the mixed gradient trace

TorusEuler.meanPressurePoissonSource_eva.text: At any point, the bundled Poisson source is the trace of `Df` minus twice the trace of `DU.comp DV`. The theorem unfolds the linear trace and Hölder composition definitions. It is an exact formula for the defined field and does not assume that the three operators are actual gradients.
TorusEuler.meanPressurePoissonSource_eva.summary: Evaluate the scalar Poisson source pointwise

TorusEuler.meanPressurePoissonSource_lif.text: Assume the three torus half-Hölder fields lift to the actual derivatives of `U`, `V` and `f`. Then the lift of the defined source equals forcing divergence minus twice the trace of the two velocity gradients. This connects the torus functional-space construction to the Euclidean formula used by the Poisson identity.
TorusEuler.meanPressurePoissonSource_lif.summary: The torus source lifts to the physical divergence formula

TorusEuler.meanPressureTraceCLM.text: This definition sums the three diagonal coordinate evaluations of a continuous linear endomorphism of Euclidean space. The result is a continuous linear map to the reals, suitable for mapping half-Hölder fields. The following identity checks that this coordinate expression agrees with the basis-independent linear-map trace.
TorusEuler.meanPressureTraceCLM.summary: The matrix trace as a continuous linear map

TorusEuler.meanPressureTraceCLM_apply.text: Applying the bundled trace map to a gradient operator gives its `LinearMap.trace`. This identity validates the coordinate construction used in the Hölder-space source formula. It holds for any continuous linear operator, independently of whether it is realized as the gradient of a divergence-free field.
TorusEuler.meanPressureTraceCLM_apply.summary: The coordinate sum is the ordinary matrix trace

TorusEuler.meanPressure_poisson_closedSl.text: For twice jointly differentiable divergence-free parent and mean velocities, assume the linearized momentum equation uses `derivWithin` on the positive closed slab. Then the mean-pressure Poisson identity holds at every slab time, including both endpoints. The proof obtains zero divergence of that within-time derivative from the joint regularity and divergence constraint.
TorusEuler.meanPressure_poisson_closedSl.summary: The Poisson identity also holds at temporal endpoints

TorusEuler.meanScalarBudget_le_power.text: Assume $\mathsf D\ge1$, nonnegative inverse, coefficient and source bounds, and $A_{\rm inv}\le C\mathsf D^a$. The estimate yields exponent $a+2b+2s$, deliberately enlarging the square-root costs. With $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-s}$, the inverse estimate, two deformation factors and the Hölder comparison costs can be bounded by a single power of $\mathsf D$. The exponent may depend on the fixed radius exponent $s$. It does not depend on the derivative order, which is the essential requirement in Proposition 5.2.
TorusEuler.meanScalarBudget_le_power.summary: The inverse and Hölder costs form one parent power

TorusEuler.meanScalarRadius_absorbs_inve.text: The exponents $a,s$ are nonnegative integers and $\mathsf D\ge1$, so $\ell_*>0$ and its square root has the usual positive meaning. If the inverse constant satisfies $A\le\mathsf D^a$ and $\ell_*=\mathsf D^{-s}$ with $s\ge2(a+9)$, then $A\mathsf D^9\sqrt{\ell_*}\le1$. This is the scalar smallness condition behind (5.13). The radius is chosen once from the inverse bound, rather than decreased separately at each derivative order.
TorusEuler.meanScalarRadius_absorbs_inve.summary: One radius makes the coefficient perturbation small

TorusEuler.mean_factor_absorb.text: The smallness condition `L^6 * freq^(-1/12) ≤ 1` absorbs all six parent factors in the mean estimate. It replaces the stronger mean exponent by `hierarchyInductiveMeanExponent p`, with the same nonnegative constant `a`. This produces the parent-factor-free mean bound used in the next transverse source.
TorusEuler.mean_factor_absorb.summary: Convert the strong mean bound into the propagated bound

TorusEuler.memLp_endpointDivergenceTest.text: A bounded measurable time factor multiplied by the torus gradient of a smooth periodic potential belongs to joint $L^2$. The gradient is bounded because it is continuous on a compact torus. This makes its Hilbert inner product with any endpoint path a well-defined bounded linear divergence test.
TorusEuler.memLp_endpointDivergenceTest.summary: Separated divergence tests are square integrable

TorusEuler.memLp_endpointL2Mul.text: An almost-everywhere strongly measurable operator field with an almost-everywhere uniform bound sends an $L^2$ representative to another $L^2$ representative by pointwise application. The bound `hbound` is measure-dependent and need not hold on an exceptional null set. This is the integrability result behind the bundled endpoint multiplier.
TorusEuler.memLp_endpointL2Mul.summary: Bounded measurable coefficients preserve square integrability

TorusEuler.memLp_endpointMeanTest.text: A bounded measurable spatial scalar test multiplied by a coordinate unit vector belongs to the joint $L^2$ endpoint space. Its value is independent of time. Finite product measure and the supplied bound on the test justify this assertion, enabling continuous linear tests for the coordinate time mean.
TorusEuler.memLp_endpointMeanTest.summary: Bounded spatial tests define square integrable joint fields

TorusEuler.memLp_endpointPrimitive.text: An interval-integrable velocity has a square-integrable primitive on a nonnegative finite interval. Continuity of the primitive on the compact slab supplies the bound needed for its $L^2$ membership. This allows time integration to be bundled as an operator between quotient spaces, even when the original velocity is only integrable.

TorusEuler.memLp_endpointProductPrimitiv.text: For nonnegative `T`, the chosen primitive representative belongs to joint $L^2$. Strong measurability and the integrable slice-energy majorant establish the claim. This is the proof needed before turning an everywhere-defined Bochner integral into an element of the quotient space `Lp E 2` over time and labels.
TorusEuler.memLp_endpointProductPrimitiv.summary: Time integration preserves joint square integrability

TorusEuler.memLp_endpointSeparatedTest.text: An essentially bounded scalar time function `η`, certified by `hη`, may multiply an arbitrary spatial $L^2$ field `y` to give a joint space-time $L^2$ field. The product measure and separated variables are essential here. This builds admissible probes without requiring pointwise regularity of either factor.
TorusEuler.memLp_endpointSeparatedTest.summary: Separate a bounded time test from a spatial field

TorusEuler.memLp_endpointTimeIntegral.text: For nonnegative `T`, integrating a joint $L^2$ field over $(0,T]$ in time gives an $L^2$ function of the label. Fubini and the finite time interval provide the required bound. The statement establishes integrability of the resulting label function before it is bundled into its quotient space.
TorusEuler.memLp_endpointTimeIntegral.summary: Partial time integration gives a square-integrable label field

TorusEuler.memLp_realBanachFourierCutoff.text: If `g` belongs to `MemLp` at exponent infinity on the finite torus measure, so does its real convolution cutoff. Essential boundedness provides integrability, then continuity and compactness bound the output. This declaration establishes membership only; the dimension-independent norm inequality is a later result.

TorusEuler.memLp_realVectorFourierCutoff.text: Every output of `realVectorFourierCutoffOfFunction` belongs to `MemLp` at exponent infinity on the torus. The argument uses continuity of the finite reconstruction and compactness of the torus. This proves boundedness and measurability of the output, not a norm estimate in terms of an arbitrary input.
TorusEuler.memLp_realVectorFourierCutoff.summary: The finite vector cutoff is essentially bounded

TorusEuler.mem_endpointCenteredSeparated.text: The product of an essentially bounded time function with a weakly solenoidal spatial field belongs to `endpointTorusSpace T` when `hzero` says its time integral vanishes. The proof checks zero time mean and the spatial gradient pairing separately. These tests isolate the time-independent part of an orthogonal residual.
TorusEuler.mem_endpointCenteredSeparated.summary: A centered separated test satisfies both constraints

TorusEuler.mem_endpointHalfHolderSolenoi.text: A half-Holder field is solenoidal exactly when its continuous representative has zero integral pairing with every smooth periodic gradient.
TorusEuler.mem_endpointHalfHolderSolenoi.summary: The Holder divergence condition through gradient tests

TorusEuler.mem_endpointJointSpatialSolen.text: Membership in the joint solenoidal submodule is equivalent to the vanishing of endpointTorusDivergenceTest T η p u for every pair of tests. The theorem unfolds the intersection of kernels and has no time-length hypothesis. It is a criterion in weak form; it does not assert that a classical divergence exists for u.

A joint field is weakly solenoidal exactly when, for each smooth potential p, its spatial pairing with the gradient of p is zero for almost every time. Read the quantifiers literally: the statement is ∀ p, followed by an almost-everywhere equality in time. It does not itself produce one exceptional null set valid simultaneously for every potential.

TorusEuler.mem_endpointSpatialSolenoidal.text: A spatial L2 field belongs to the weak solenoidal subspace exactly when it annihilates every smooth periodic potential gradient under integration.
TorusEuler.mem_endpointSpatialSolenoidal.summary: The weak solenoidal space through gradient tests

TorusEuler.mem_endpointTorusSpace.text: A joint $L^2$ path belongs to the endpoint subspace exactly when all coordinate mean-test integrals and all separated divergence-test integrals vanish. This expands the intersection-of-kernels definition. It does not by itself upgrade the path to a continuous velocity or assert pointwise endpoint values.
TorusEuler.mem_endpointTorusSpace.summary: Membership means that both families of tests vanish

TorusEuler.mem_endpointTorusSpace_iff_fo.text: For positive `T`, joint membership in the weak endpoint space is equivalent to zero time mean and transversality of every real Fourier coefficient. The converse compares `v` with its orthogonal projection and uses Fourier separation to show their difference vanishes. This is a full characterization, not merely a necessary condition on modes.
TorusEuler.mem_endpointTorusSpace_iff_fo.summary: Endpoint constraints are equivalent to constraints on every Fourier path

TorusEuler.mem_endpointTorusSpace_iff_sl.text: Membership in the joint constraint space is equivalent to zero time integral at almost every label and vanishing gradient pairing at almost every time for each smooth periodic potential. A common exceptional set for all tests is obtained separately.
TorusEuler.mem_endpointTorusSpace_iff_sl.summary: The endpoint constraints expressed through slices

TorusEuler.mem_freezingFixedSpace.text: A vector belongs to the fixed subspace exactly when the operator leaves it unchanged. This converts the kernel definition into the equation used by compressed inverses.

TorusEuler.mem_freezingFixedSpace_iff_we.text: Suppose the fixed vectors of `Q` are exactly a Hilbert submodule `V`, and `P` intertwines with `Q`. A half-Hölder field is fixed by `P` exactly when its Haar embedding lies in `V`. This turns the abstract projected-space condition into the weak divergence and, where applicable, time-mean constraints.
TorusEuler.mem_freezingFixedSpace_iff_we.summary: Recognize projected fields by the weak constraint

TorusEuler.mem_frequencyBand.text: An integer frequency belongs to the band of radius R exactly when the Euclidean norm of its lattice vector is at most R. This is the defining spectral cutoff condition.
TorusEuler.mem_frequencyBand.summary: A Fourier-band index has bounded lattice length

TorusEuler.mem_frequencyBand_neg.text: A frequency belongs to the closed finite ball of radius `R` exactly when its negative does. The radius is any real number, including negative values where both membership assertions fail. This symmetry permits reindexing finite Fourier sums by frequency negation when proving parity and reality.
TorusEuler.mem_frequencyBand_neg.summary: Frequency balls are invariant under sign reversal

TorusEuler.mem_hierarchyAdmissibleWords.text: A word belongs to the canonical finite list exactly when its length is at most n and its letters are nondecreasing. This avoids counting permutations as separate mixed multi-indices.
TorusEuler.mem_hierarchyAdmissibleWords.summary: Admissible words are sorted and have bounded length

TorusEuler.mem_hierarchyLevelPairs_iff.text: Membership in `hierarchyLevelPairs P d p` is equivalent to explicit lower and upper bounds on both positive indices and the equation $i+j=p+d$. The first index starts at $d+1$, which excludes a nonexistent preceding completion in the fast sum. This finite-set description supports the change of index between fast and slow products.
TorusEuler.mem_hierarchyLevelPairs_iff.summary: Which pairs contribute to a hierarchy level

TorusEuler.mem_periodicComplexSolenoidal.text: A complex $L^2$ field belongs to the Fourier solenoidal subspace exactly when its inner product with every inserted longitudinal mode vanishes. It suffices to test generators because the pairing is linear on their span. This characterization includes the harmless zero-frequency test.
TorusEuler.mem_periodicComplexSolenoidal.summary: Solenoidality can be tested against individual longitudinal modes

TorusEuler.mem_periodicComplexSolenoidal.text: A complex spatial $L^2$ field belongs to the Fourier solenoidal subspace precisely when every Fourier coefficient lies in its transverse mode space. This translates the longitudinal testing definition into a coefficientwise condition. It includes zero frequency, where the transverse space is the whole coefficient space.
TorusEuler.mem_periodicComplexSolenoidal.summary: A Hilbert field is solenoidal exactly when its coefficients are

TorusEuler.mem_transverseModeSpace_iff.text: A complex coefficient, placed in the Euclidean wrapper, belongs to the transverse mode space exactly when its frequency contraction vanishes. The statement includes zero frequency, where all coefficients qualify. It translates algebraic divergence-free conditions into the closed subspace language used for Hilbert-space projection.
TorusEuler.mem_transverseModeSpace_iff.summary: Orthogonality is exactly zero frequency contraction

TorusEuler.mem_transversePlane.text: A vector belongs to `transversePlane k` exactly when its inner product with `k` is zero. This unfolds the kernel of the continuous linear functional defined by `k`. The statement holds in any real inner-product space; when $k=0$ the kernel is the whole space, not a two-dimensional plane.
TorusEuler.mem_transversePlane.summary: Membership in the transverse space means orthogonality

TorusEuler.mixedApprox_approximates_join.text: A strongly measurable family of L² time paths, uniformly bounded by nonnegative `M`, has a joint L² field realizing its slices almost everywhere. The proof constructs a Cauchy sequence from bounded simple approximations, takes its joint L² limit, and compares subsequences in measure. It does not assert a pointwise representative identity at every label.
TorusEuler.mixedApprox_approximates_join.summary: A bounded measurable family admits a joint L² realization

TorusEuler.mixedApprox_tendsto_integral.text: For a strongly measurable family `f` bounded by nonnegative `M`, its specified `approxBounded` simple approximations have integrated squared path error tending to zero. The equality hypothesis `hs` identifies the exact approximation sequence. Dominated convergence uses their shared bound, rather than assuming uniform convergence in the label variable.
TorusEuler.mixedApprox_tendsto_integral.summary: Bounded simple approximations converge in integrated path energy

TorusEuler.mixedPhaseJet.text: First differentiate the profile `j` times in phase, then take its `k`th Fréchet derivative in the parameter at fixed phase. The value is a continuous `k`-multilinear map, written `P [×k]→L[ℝ] E`. In applications the parameter is the label and time is fixed, so this represents one mixed derivative from the finite profile norm.
TorusEuler.mixedPhaseJet.summary: Phase derivatives followed by parameter derivatives

TorusEuler.momentumResidual.text: For a time set $I$, velocity $U$ and pressure $p$, the formal definition is $R_U=\partial_tU+(U\cdot\nabla)U+\nabla p$, with the time derivative taken within $I$. For a smooth parent on $[0,T]$, this is the ordinary material acceleration plus the pressure gradient, with one-sided derivatives at the endpoints. It is not an independent force chosen to fit an estimate. The definition does not impose $\operatorname{div}U=0$ or $R_U=0$, and derivative values outside their regularity hypotheses carry no Euler interpretation. In §1.3, the mean correction cancels this parent's defect together with the averaged wave error.
TorusEuler.momentumResidual.summary: The residual is the actual defect in the momentum equation

TorusEuler.momentumResidual_restrict_Icc.text: Extends the material-acceleration restriction identity to the momentum residual for the same pressure. The smaller closed slab is positive and contained in the original one, and the velocity is jointly continuously differentiable there. The pressure term is identical in both expressions, so no extra pressure differentiability is needed for this equality.
TorusEuler.momentumResidual_restrict_Icc.summary: The physical residual is unchanged by valid slab restriction

TorusEuler.momentumResidual_transportedH.text: Adding a transported velocity and pressure profile to a parent gives the parent residual plus profile time evolution, parent strain, self-advection, and the transported pressure gradient. The inverse-label transport identity cancels the parent material derivative. All derivatives and geometric identities are supplied at the point; unique within-set time differentiation covers closed-slab endpoints.
TorusEuler.momentumResidual_transportedH.summary: The physical residual splits into parent and profile contributions

TorusEuler.momentumTensor.text:
The rank-one momentum tensor with column `i` equal to `v i • u`.

Default-value audit (b5): The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.momentumTensor.summary: The rank-one tensor formed from two velocities

TorusEuler.momentumTensorColumn.text:
Select one column of a continuous torus tensor field and bundle it as a continuous vector field. The column map is used to apply the vector Fourier cutoff to a tensor.

Default-value audit (b5): The source builds this object by the explicit algebraic operations or certified restrictions shown in the body. There is no exceptional-input fallback in this declaration; any analytic interpretation still requires the hypotheses of the theorem using it.
TorusEuler.momentumTensorColumn.summary: One continuous column of the momentum tensor

TorusEuler.momentumTensorComplexify.text: Defines a continuous real-linear map that complexifies every column of a real momentum tensor. It preserves the column indexing used by tensor divergence and supplies complex-valued data for Fourier synthesis. The map does not alter the tensor-product convention or require the tensor to arise from a velocity.
TorusEuler.momentumTensorComplexify.summary: Complexifying the momentum tensor column by column

TorusEuler.momentumTensorDivergence.text:
Tensor divergence adds the derivative of the `i`th column in coordinate `i`.

Default-value audit (b5): Finite sums and index sets are defined at zero order or empty ranges as well. The paper use supplies the intended order and level restrictions.
TorusEuler.momentumTensorDivergence.summary: Divergence of a tensor by differentiating its columns

TorusEuler.momentumTensorDivergence_appl.text: Tensor divergence is the sum over i of the derivative in coordinate direction i of column i. This fixes the convention used when converting self-advection into a tensor divergence.
TorusEuler.momentumTensorDivergence_appl.summary: The coordinate formula for tensor divergence

TorusEuler.momentumTensorDivergence_self.text: For a divergence-free velocity, tensor divergence is the Euler advection term.
TorusEuler.momentumTensorDivergence_self.summary: Tensor divergence equals advection for incompressible velocity

TorusEuler.momentumTensorFourierCutoff.text:
The real tensor cutoff operates on the columns of a physical momentum tensor.

Default-value audit (b5): The tensor cutoff is built from explicit complexification and real-part maps. Approximation and derivative bounds use the symbol conditions and positive scale of the cutoff lemmas.
TorusEuler.momentumTensorFourierCutoff.summary: Fourier truncation of each momentum-tensor column

TorusEuler.momentumTensorFourierCutoff_a.text: The i-th column of the tensor Fourier cutoff is the vector Fourier cutoff of the i-th original column. This identity lets the proof commute truncation with tensor divergence by a finite sum.

TorusEuler.momentumTensorRealPart.text: Defines a continuous real-linear map from complex momentum tensors to real tensors by taking each column’s coordinatewise real part. The map is used after complex Fourier synthesis. It is a projection onto real data and need not be injective on arbitrary complex tensors.
TorusEuler.momentumTensorRealPart.summary: Taking real parts of momentum-tensor columns

TorusEuler.momentumTensorRealPart_comple.text: Taking real parts after complexifying a momentum tensor returns that tensor exactly. This follows column by column from the real-vector identity. It supplies the retraction hypothesis of the abstract tensor tail estimate, ensuring that the cutoff error there refers to the original real momentum tensor.
TorusEuler.momentumTensorRealPart_comple.summary: Real momentum tensors survive the complex detour

TorusEuler.momentumTensor_apply.text: The `i`th column of `momentumTensor u v` is the scalar component `v i` multiplied by the vector `u`. This fixes the tensor convention used by the residual expansion. For $u=v$, taking the column divergence gives the usual Euler momentum transport once incompressibility is supplied separately.
TorusEuler.momentumTensor_apply.summary: The momentum tensor stores velocity-product columns

TorusEuler.momentum_realFourierCutoff_eq.text: Given continuous representatives of velocity, its proposed time term, tensor divergence, pressure term, and residual, an exact input momentum identity yields the tensor formula for the truncated residual. The cutoff velocity must be divergence free. The field `u_t` is only assumed to equal the cutoff time representative here; actual time differentiation and the gradient character of the pressure term are established elsewhere.
TorusEuler.momentum_realFourierCutoff_eq.summary: Rearrange truncated momentum into the residual tensor

TorusEuler.mono_exponent.text: With `freq ≥ 1` and nonnegative coefficient and parent scale, replacing a frequency exponent by a larger exponent increases the resulting bound. This monotonicity is applied after exact exponent identities. It lets smaller terms fit the exponent used for their hierarchy level.
TorusEuler.mono_exponent.summary: Weaken an estimate by increasing its frequency exponent

TorusEuler.mono_factor.text: For nonnegative frequency, parent scale at least one, and ordered constants and natural exponents, increasing the coefficient and parent power weakens the upper bound. The frequency power remains fixed. The theorem is scalar bookkeeping used to place differently shaped estimates under one common parent-loss budget.
TorusEuler.mono_factor.summary: Enlarge a coefficient and its parent power

TorusEuler.mul_endpointClosedTimeNorm_le.text: For positive label scale, a bounded weighted derivative-word value set controls the closed-time norm of its actual half-Holder representative up to a factor square root two. Positivity is needed when dividing by the scale power.
TorusEuler.mul_endpointClosedTimeNorm_le.summary: Weighted lift bounds control recovered Holder norms

TorusEuler.mul_le_of_meanCoefficientThre.text: If $B\le C D^9\sqrt\ell$ and $A D^9\sqrt\ell\le1$, then $AB\le C$, provided $A,C\ge0$. This is the scalar absorption used after the low-order inverse norm multiplies a differentiated coefficient bound. The theorem assumes the two quantitative bounds and does not derive the coefficient estimate or choose the radius.
TorusEuler.mul_le_of_meanCoefficientThre.summary: The low-order inverse absorbs a coefficient derivative

TorusEuler.mul_norm_halfHolder_le_of_hie.text: If a torus half-Hölder field represents the unweighted spatial derivative word, its norm multiplied by $\ell^{|w|}$ is bounded by $\sqrt2$ times the weighted word supremum. Nonnegative radius and spatial smoothness justify moving the weight into the field. This supplies coefficient estimates in the torus Banach space from label-side bounds.
TorusEuler.mul_norm_halfHolder_le_of_hie.summary: Transfer an unweighted torus derivative with its radius

TorusEuler.mul_sum_list_map.text: Multiplying a real-valued list sum by $c$ equals summing the products by $c$. This requires no positivity assumptions and is proved by induction on the list. It is used to move the radius and inverse-cost factors inside the sum of correction terms in the derivative-lifting recurrence.
TorusEuler.mul_sum_list_map.summary: Distribute a scalar through a finite list sum

TorusEuler.multilinear_diagonal_eq_sum.text: A continuous `j`-linear map evaluated on `j` copies of `y` equals the sum over all coordinate selections of the corresponding monomial times its basis evaluation. This is a finite algebraic identity with no differentiability requirement. It converts directional Taylor terms into coordinate moments whose cancellation is already available.
TorusEuler.multilinear_diagonal_eq_sum.summary: Expand a diagonal multilinear term into coordinate monomials

TorusEuler.multiplierDerivativeMass.text: Sum twelve integrals: derivative orders zero through five, each with frequency weight either one or $\|\xi\|$. This scalar quantity controls five integrations by parts and up to one derivative of the inverse-transform kernel. The definition is available for any symbol; smooth compact support later ensures these are genuine finite derivative masses.
TorusEuler.multiplierDerivativeMass.summary: Weighted derivative integrals controlling the multiplier kernel

TorusEuler.multiplierDerivativeMass_le_o.text: If the symbol's support lies in the radius-`R` ball and every derivative through order five is uniformly bounded by `M`, the weighted derivative mass is bounded by $12\max(1,R)M$ times that ball's volume. The factor twelve counts the two weights and six derivative orders; no separate smoothness assumption is stated here.
TorusEuler.multiplierDerivativeMass_le_o.summary: A fixed support ball controls all derivative masses

TorusEuler.multiplierDerivativeMass_nonn.text: Every term in `multiplierDerivativeMass` integrates a product of nonnegative norms and powers, so the full finite sum is nonnegative. The theorem is unconditional for the total integral definition. It supplies positivity when the mass is used as a constant in subsequent kernel and convolution estimates.
TorusEuler.multiplierDerivativeMass_nonn.summary: The weighted derivative mass is nonnegative

TorusEuler.multiplierDerivativeMass_sum_.text: For weight exponent `d≤1` and derivative order `n≤5`, the corresponding rectangular partial sum of weighted derivative integrals is at most the full multiplier mass. Every summand is nonnegative. This helper lets each integration-by-parts estimate use the same single constant, independently of the selected derivative and weight orders.
TorusEuler.multiplierDerivativeMass_sum_.summary: Partial derivative sums fit inside the full mass

TorusEuler.multiplierJetDecayConstant.text: The explicit coefficient multiplies the weighted symbol derivative mass by $2^p$, $(2\pi)^d$, and $(2d+2)^p$. It is designed to control an order `d` inverse Fourier kernel derivative with polynomial decay order `p`. Its numerical value depends on the supplied symbol and the two finite orders.
TorusEuler.multiplierJetDecayConstant.summary: Fourier integration by parts fixes the decay coefficient

TorusEuler.multiplierJetDecayConstant_no.text: The kernel decay coefficient is nonnegative at every pair of natural orders. The proof combines the nonnegative symbol mass with the nonnegative powers and positive Fourier normalization factors. This is used to multiply and compare decay bounds without reversing inequalities.
TorusEuler.multiplierJetDecayConstant_no.summary: The chosen kernel decay coefficient is nonnegative

TorusEuler.multiplierJetMass.text: This finite sum collects integrals of weighted norms of symbol derivatives, with moment order through `d` and derivative order through `p`. These quantities control inverse Fourier kernel decay. The definition is available for arbitrary symbols, while the later decay estimates use Schwartz symbols to guarantee genuine derivatives and integrable moments.
TorusEuler.multiplierJetMass.summary: Weighted symbol derivatives determine the kernel constants

TorusEuler.multiplierJetMass_nonneg.text: The weighted derivative mass is nonnegative because each integrand is a product of nonnegative norms and powers, and the outer sum is finite. This sign statement holds even for arbitrary symbols. It does not establish integrability of those moments or justify a decay estimate without the later Schwartz hypotheses.
TorusEuler.multiplierJetMass_nonneg.summary: The sum of symbol derivative masses is nonnegative

TorusEuler.multiplierKernelCell.text: The kernel construction integrates over the canonical half open fundamental domain of the coordinate lattice. This differs from using its closed parallelepiped at boundary points, which would double count adjacent cells. Compact closure and measurability are proved immediately afterward, providing the bounded source region needed for integral and series exchanges.
TorusEuler.multiplierKernelCell.summary: A half open cell avoids double counting periodized sources

TorusEuler.multiplierKernelCell_measurab.text: The chosen half open coordinate fundamental domain is measurable. This private fact is used when restricting Lebesgue measure and changing integral domains in the periodization argument. It ensures those operations refer to an ordinary measurable source cell, including the convention on its boundary.

TorusEuler.multiplierKernelCell_measure_.text: The fundamental cell has finite Lebesgue measure because it lies in the compact coordinate parallelepiped. This private estimate supports integration of bounded fields on the cell and domination of integral norms by a summable series. An exact numerical value for the volume is unnecessary for those arguments.

TorusEuler.nearPressureCutoffTensor.text: This private field multiplies the quadratic complex velocity tensor by the scalar cutoff $\chi$. The intended cutoff is one near the target and vanishes near the singular lattice. Its support allows a velocity smooth only off the lattice to produce a globally smooth tensor field for the near pressure multiplier.

TorusEuler.nextOrder.text: This private function returns `order + 1` if its threshold $B(\mathrm{order}+1)$ does not exceed the current frequency, and otherwise keeps the current order. It is an explicit two-case implementation of the schedule’s constrained maximum once the current order is known to be positive and admissible.
TorusEuler.nextOrder.summary: Advance the derivative order only when its threshold is met

TorusEuler.nextOrder_isGreatest.text: If the current order is at least one and already satisfies its frequency threshold, `nextOrder` is the greatest positive order at most one higher whose threshold is met. No monotonicity of $B$ is required: either the highest allowed order qualifies, or every other allowed natural order is at most the admissible current one.
TorusEuler.nextOrder_isGreatest.summary: The two-case choice realizes the admissible maximum

TorusEuler.nextSlab_le_of_halfLength.text: If activation occurs in the old first half and the new half length is at most one quarter of the old one, the new full endpoint precedes the old endpoint strictly. Positivity of the old half length supplies strictness. This scalar inequality is used when nesting the smooth stage slabs.
TorusEuler.nextSlab_le_of_halfLength.summary: The new endpoint lies strictly before the old endpoint

TorusEuler.nonempty_laterPrimaryCosts.text: Combines the independently established later-wave pressure and activation estimates into a `LaterPrimaryCosts` witness. The radius floor is the maximum of their floors, and the pressure power is explicitly $2a+74$. No external certificate is introduced: the two estimate theorems provide the required proof fields, though this review has not recompiled them.
TorusEuler.nonempty_laterPrimaryCosts.summary: The later pressure and activation costs can be chosen

TorusEuler.nonempty_truncatedChildStage.text:
Let $T>0$ and let $V,R_V$ be smooth periodic fields on $[0,T]	imes\mathbb R^3$, with $V$ odd and divergence free. Suppose a smooth periodic spatial pressure $\Pi(t)$ satisfies $V_t+V\cdot
abla V+
abla\Pi=R_V$ at every time, using time derivatives within the interval. For an even cutoff symbol, the formal construction produces the finite Fourier cutoff $u=S_\Lambda V$, a jointly smooth periodic zero-mean pressure with $\Delta p=-\operatorname{tr}((
abla u)^2)$, and the exact projected residual identity (5.58). The resulting velocity is smooth, odd, divergence free and supported in $|\xi|\le2\Lambda$. The construction does not require the symbol’s smooth tail estimates; those are additional inputs for the quantitative error bounds in Proposition 5.11.
TorusEuler.nonempty_truncatedChildStage.summary: Construct the cutoff velocity and its normalized pressure from an approximation

TorusEuler.nonneg_appendixFiniteDerivati.text: The finite derivative quantity obtained by summing a seminorm over admissible ordered words is nonnegative. Each summand is nonnegative by the seminorm axioms. No derivative commutation or analytic regularity is needed for this algebraic fact; those assumptions enter when relating arbitrary words to the chosen ordered representatives.
TorusEuler.nonneg_appendixFiniteDerivati.summary: Nonnegativity of the finite derivative sum

TorusEuler.nonneg_periodicMomentumJetBou.text: The explicit coefficient used for the momentum jet estimate is nonnegative at every natural order. This follows from nonnegativity of operator norms, the square root, and positive numerical factors. It supplies the sign assumptions needed to package the subsequent bilinear map as a bounded operator.
TorusEuler.nonneg_periodicMomentumJetBou.summary: The chosen momentum constant is nonnegative

TorusEuler.nonneg_spatialHolderHalfNorm.text: The finite spatial half-Hölder norm is nonnegative on its domain.
TorusEuler.nonneg_spatialHolderHalfNorm.summary: The finite Hölder norm is nonnegative on its domain

TorusEuler.normDerivOfScaled.text: If $v\prime(t)=\|v(t)\|w$ within the set `s` and `hzero` makes $v(t)$ nonzero, computes the length derivative as $\|v(t)\|\langle\widehat v(t),w\rangle$. The vector $w$ is the normalized instantaneous derivative, not a path. The proof differentiates the squared norm and its square root; it is valid in any real inner-product space.
TorusEuler.normDerivOfScaled.summary: Differentiate the length of a nonzero vector

TorusEuler.norm_add_latticeVector_eq_dis.text: The norm of `x + latticeVector k` equals the distance from `x` to the lattice point indexed by `-k`. This private identity aligns the translation convention in the kernel series with the geometric separation convention for `offOrigin`. It is an algebraic rewrite, with no lower bound asserted.
TorusEuler.norm_add_latticeVector_eq_dis.summary: Translated lengths are distances from the singular lattice

TorusEuler.norm_adjoint_coordinate_le.text: The norm of $A^*e_i$ is bounded by $\|A\|$. The proof uses preservation of the operator norm by the adjoint and the unit norm of `coordinateDirection i`. This coordinate estimate introduces no factor depending on the derivative order or on the selected coordinate.
TorusEuler.norm_adjoint_coordinate_le.summary: A coframe row is bounded by the operator norm

TorusEuler.norm_adjoint_sub_self_differe.text: Bounds the difference between $M^*-M$ and $N^*-N$ by $2\|M-N\|$. The proof rewrites that difference as the skew part of $M-N$ and applies the preceding norm estimate. It transfers a spatial modulus for the velocity gradient to its skew part.
TorusEuler.norm_adjoint_sub_self_differe.summary: Differences of skew parts have the same factor two

TorusEuler.norm_adjoint_sub_self_le.text: Bounds the norm of $M^*-M$ by $2\|M\|$ on a complete real Hilbert space. This follows from the triangle inequality and the isometry of adjoint. It controls the unpulled vorticity coefficient before multiplying on both sides by the deformation.
TorusEuler.norm_adjoint_sub_self_le.summary: The skew part is bounded by twice the gradient

TorusEuler.norm_advectionHalfHolder_le.text: For a $C^2$ velocity with nonnegative uniform bounds $M$, $B$, and $H$ on its value, first derivative, and second derivative, the supplied advection field has half Hölder norm at most $2(BM+B^2+HM)$. The representative equality `hA` is essential. The proof combines a Lipschitz estimate at short distances with a supremum estimate at long distances.
TorusEuler.norm_advectionHalfHolder_le.summary: Velocity and two derivatives bound half Hölder advection

TorusEuler.norm_angularLeray_le.text: The continuous linear operator norm of the angular Leray symbol is at most one at every real frequency. This follows from its symmetric-projection property. The estimate includes zero frequency and gives the order-zero bound used when higher angular derivatives are assembled into a common family of estimates.
TorusEuler.norm_angularLeray_le.summary: The real Leray symbol has norm at most one

TorusEuler.norm_appendixCutoffKernel_int.text: Assuming a smooth symbol vanishes outside the radius-two ball and $\Lambda>0$, bounds the torus integral of the cutoff kernel’s norm by the Euclidean inverse-Fourier kernel’s $L^1$ norm. The latter depends on the symbol alone. This is the analytic input for the cutoff operator bound, rather than a bound derived solely from finite summation.
TorusEuler.norm_appendixCutoffKernel_int.summary: A scale independent bound for the kernel integral

TorusEuler.norm_applyField_bilinear_le.text: The bilinear map $(A,x)\mapsto A(x)$ has operator norm at most one for the given normed spaces. The proof applies the defining operator-norm inequality twice. This is the precise bound required to instantiate the generic product estimate with the amplitude generator acting on the amplitude field.
TorusEuler.norm_applyField_bilinear_le.summary: Applying an operator has bilinear norm at most one

TorusEuler.norm_apply_le_spatialHolderHa.text: The spatial order-zero half-Hölder norm controls pointwise values.
TorusEuler.norm_apply_le_spatialHolderHa.summary: The zeroth Hölder norm controls pointwise size

TorusEuler.norm_apply_mixedPhaseJet_phas.text: For fixed derivative directions and any real weight `w`, a uniform phase bound on the weighted mixed derivative gives the average and oscillation bounds with constants one and two. The normalized primitive has the same factor-two bound when all label slices have zero mean. The weight may include a time factor because time is fixed throughout this statement.
TorusEuler.norm_apply_mixedPhaseJet_phas.summary: Weighted derivative evaluations obey the phase-operation estimates

TorusEuler.norm_axis.text: The chosen Euclidean coordinate vector has norm one for every index in `Fin 3`. The statement concerns the Hilbert-space norm on `Vec3`, not a componentwise bound. It provides the nonzero initial directions and the exact normalization used to compute the first wave’s initial strength and frame.
TorusEuler.norm_axis.summary: Every coordinate direction has unit length

TorusEuler.norm_bilinear_apply_le.text: The norm of $B(a,b)$ is at most $\|B\|\|a\|\|b\|$ for a continuous bilinear map represented as a nested continuous linear map. Applying the operator norm bound twice supplies each individual term in the finite-order product estimate. No differentiability hypotheses are involved in this inequality.

TorusEuler.norm_bilinear_sub_le.text: The difference $B(a,b)-B(a',b')$ is bounded by $\|B\|\|a-a'\|\|b\|+\|B\|\|a'\|\|b-b'\|$. The proof adds and subtracts the mixed value through bilinearity. This elementary estimate controls changes in either factor when proving the Hölder version of the product rule.
TorusEuler.norm_bilinear_sub_le.summary: Split a bilinear difference between its factors

TorusEuler.norm_center_fderiv_sub_le_of_.text: For `hj : 1 ≤ j`, `hinit : 2 ≤ freq 0` and `hfreq : ∀ n, freq n ^ 2 ≤ freq (n+1)`, the reciprocal-frequency tail is at most $2/\mathrm{freq}(j+1)$. With monotone activation, a current activation interval inside $[0,T)$, and all stage slabs containing $[0,T]$, vanishing late oscillations and the order-one correction bounds transfer this bound to the central derivative difference. Stage differentiability and prefix derivative convergence identify the derivatives and limit. The docstring mentions curl, but the conclusion concerns the full Fréchet derivative; applying curl costs its operator norm.
TorusEuler.norm_center_fderiv_sub_le_of_.summary: The central derivative differs from the stage by a small tail

TorusEuler.norm_clm_apply_sub_le.text: The difference $Av-Bw$ is bounded by $\|A-B\|\|v\|+\|B\|\|v-w\|$. The estimate holds for arbitrary bounded linear maps and vectors. It separates convergence of a velocity gradient from convergence of the velocity itself when passing to the nonlinear advection term.
TorusEuler.norm_clm_apply_sub_le.summary: Separate operator and vector errors in a product

TorusEuler.norm_coefficientMul_sub_sup_l.text: The supremum difference between `C w` and `D v` is bounded by the norm of `C` times the supremum difference `w-v`, plus the supremum difference `C-D` times the norm of `v`. This elementary product splitting keeps convergence in the value component separate from the full Hölder bounds used to control factors.
TorusEuler.norm_coefficientMul_sub_sup_l.summary: Separate the two errors in a coefficient product

TorusEuler.norm_compactDyadicBlock_le.text: If `hzero : σ 0 = 0`, the continuous supremum norm of the `j`th block is bounded by the kernel’s half-moment times $\|f\|2^{-j/2}$.
