Removing the nonnegative zeroth level gives the norm inequality used before contracting a tensor derivative.
TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_fderiv.summary: A spatial derivative costs one Hölder order

TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_fderiv_zero.text: If a vector field has one order of spatial half-Hölder regularity, its Fréchet derivative has order-zero half-Hölder regularity and norm bounded by the original order-one norm. This supplies the gradient fields needed by the pressure Poisson multiplier from estimates on the mean velocity and forcing.
TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_fderiv_zero.summary: One Hölder derivative controls the derivative field

TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_halfHolderP.text: A bounded torus operator commuting with actual line derivatives preserves every finite lifted half-Hölder order. The norm factor remains $2\sqrt{2}\|P\|$, independent of the order `m`. The input must be periodic and satisfy `SpatialHolderHalf m`; induction uses the derivative operator’s norm bound and the exact splitting of the higher norm.
TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_halfHolderP.summary: Bound every Hölder order of the projected lift

TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_mono.text: An order-`m` half-Hölder field has order `n` whenever `n ≤ m`, and its order-`n` norm is no larger. The definition sums all levels through the specified order, so the proof restricts regularity and removes nonnegative summands. This lets high-order tail information supply the first and second orders used in the residual.
TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_mono.summary: Lowering derivative order cannot increase this Hölder norm

TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_neg.text: Negating a half-Hölder field preserves its regularity and leaves the full finite-order norm unchanged. The proof uses negation of iterated derivatives and invariance of norms of both values and increments. This permits the cutoff tail estimate for $V-u$ to be used with the paper’s velocity error $u-V$.
TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_neg.summary: Changing the sign preserves the Hölder norm

TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_of_bounded_.text: Uniform adjacent spatial jet bounds control the lift half-Hölder norm.
TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_of_bounded_.summary: Adjacent derivative bounds control the half-Hölder norm

TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_of_contDiff.text: A smooth periodic lift has finite spatial half-Hölder norm at every order.
TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_of_contDiff.summary: A smooth periodic lift has finite Hölder regularity

TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_of_level_bo.text: If a $C^m$ field has all derivative norms bounded by `A` and all corresponding increments bounded by $B\sqrt{\|v\|}$, with `B ≥ 0`, it has order-`m` half-Hölder regularity and norm at most $(m+1)(A+B)$. The result proves boundedness of the quotient ranges explicitly before summing the levels.
TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_of_level_bo.summary: Uniform level bounds assemble a Hölder norm

TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_one_halfHol.text: If `P` preserves all torus line-derivative relations, its guarded lift maps periodic order-one half-Hölder fields to the same class. The norm bound is $2\sqrt2\|P\|$ times the input norm. The proof separately controls the field and reconstructed derivative columns; the periodicity and regularity hypotheses select the meaningful branch of the lifted definition.
TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_one_halfHol.summary: A derivative-preserving operator is bounded on first-order lifts

TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_one_iff.text: A field has first-order half-Hölder regularity exactly when it is $C^1$ and both the field and its Fréchet derivative have order-zero half-Hölder regularity. The explicit $C^1$ condition prevents a totalized derivative value from being mistaken for genuine differentiability. This decomposition is used to establish the projected field’s regularity.
TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_one_iff.summary: First-order regularity is regularity of value and derivative

TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_periodicLer.text: The actual periodic Leray projection preserves every spatial half-Hölder order.
TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_periodicLer.summary: The Leray projection preserves every spatial Hölder order

TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_realVectorC.text: At positive scale, the real cutoff of an order-`m` half-Hölder field retains that regularity and has norm bounded by $2(m+1)(1+C_m)$ times the input norm. The proof writes the cutoff as the original field minus its zero-loss tail. The bound is uniform in the cutoff scale, with dependence only on the fixed symbol and order.
TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_realVectorC.summary: The real cutoff is bounded at each Hölder order

TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_sub_le_of_u.text: If smooth fields differ by at most a nonnegative $\delta$ in every derivative through order `m+1`, their difference belongs to $C^{m,1/2}$ and its norm is at most $3(m+1)\delta$. The extra derivative controls the half Hölder quotient. The theorem supplies the regularity predicate as well as the numerical norm bound.
TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_sub_le_of_u.summary: Uniform derivative errors control the full Hölder difference

TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_succ_iff.text: Order $m+1$ half-Hölder regularity is equivalent to differentiability of `f`, order-zero regularity of `f`, and order-$m$ regularity of its Fréchet derivative. The order-zero clause retains control of the original function as well as its derivatives. This equivalence includes bounded derivative norms and Hölder quotients, not merely a formal derivative identity.
TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_succ_iff.summary: Separate the first derivative from higher regularity

TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_to_words.text: Ordinary lifted order-`n` half-Hölder regularity supplies a family of torus fields representing all coordinate derivative words through that order. This private implication discards the quantitative bound furnished by `exists_halfHolderWords_norm_le` and keeps the derivative relations. It is one direction of the equivalence used to restate the higher freezing inverse.
TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_to_words.summary: Convert Hölder regularity into derivative words

TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_zero_iff.text: Order-zero half-Hölder regularity is equivalent to continuity of the field, boundedness of its norm range and boundedness of its increment-quotient range. The theorem makes the finiteness requirements explicit. It is the entry criterion for descending a periodic Euclidean field into the bundled quotient half-Hölder space.
TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_zero_iff.summary: Order zero means continuity and two finite bounds

TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_zero_of_con.text: A continuously differentiable periodic lift belongs to the spatial half-Hölder domain.
TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_zero_of_con.summary: A differentiable periodic field has zeroth Hölder regularity

TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_zero_of_hal.text: Pulling back a bundled half-Hölder torus field gives order-zero half-Hölder regularity on Euclidean space and lift norm at most twice the bundled norm. The factor two comes from adding the separate supremum and seminorm contributions. This is a norm comparison, not equality or an isometric identification of the two spaces.
TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_zero_of_hal.summary: A quotient Hölder field has a controlled lift norm

TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_zero_of_uni.text: If $f$ is differentiable everywhere and its value and Fréchet derivative have uniform bounds $A$ and $B$, then $f$ has spatial half Hölder regularity and norm at most $3A+B$. Small displacements use the derivative estimate; large displacements use the value estimate. The hypotheses themselves imply $A,B\ge0$, and zero displacement is handled separately.
TorusEuler.spatialHolderHalf_zero_of_uni.summary: Supremum and gradient bounds imply half Hölder control

TorusEuler.spatialHolderWords_to_holder.text: A family satisfying `HasSpatialHolderWords n` yields order-`n` half-Hölder regularity of the Euclidean lift. The successor step reconstructs a Fréchet derivative from the three continuous coordinate derivatives and then applies induction to their remaining words. The hypothesis uses actual torus-line derivatives, which prevents arbitrary named fields from being treated as a derivative hierarchy.
TorusEuler.spatialHolderWords_to_holder.summary: Recover Hölder regularity from actual derivative words

TorusEuler.spatialJet_derivative_time_co.text: Given a tower smooth in the uniform time norm and compatible under spatial differentiation, the time differentiated tower remains spatially compatible. The hypothesis `hx` supplies the original derivative relation. Difference quotients converge uniformly as bounded continuous functions, allowing the derivative relation to pass to the limit even at closed slab endpoints.
TorusEuler.spatialJet_derivative_time_co.summary: Spatial differentiation commutes with bounded jet time derivatives

TorusEuler.spatialJet_inc_le.text: Every derivative through order `m` has increments bounded by the full order-`m` norm times $\sqrt{\|v\|}$. The theorem first uses the corresponding derivative seminorm, then compares that seminorm with the whole norm. It supplies the difference estimate for the product-rule argument, alongside the separate pointwise derivative bound.
TorusEuler.spatialJet_inc_le.summary: Derivative increments are controlled by the full norm

TorusEuler.spatialJet_le.text: For `j ≤ m`, the pointwise norm of the `j`th iterated derivative is bounded by the full order-`m` half-Hölder norm. The regularity hypothesis ensures the relevant supremum is a genuine upper bound. This is the basic estimate used to control each Leibniz term in products and residual tensors.
TorusEuler.spatialJet_le.summary: Every spatial derivative is bounded by the full norm

TorusEuler.spatialJets_timePrimitive_has.text: If the tower `U` is continuous in time and successive entries are spatial derivatives, its time primitives satisfy the same derivative relation. The derivative of the order `m` primitive is the curried order `m+1` primitive. Bounded evaluation and currying commute with integration, allowing the previous integral differentiation result to apply.
TorusEuler.spatialJets_timePrimitive_has.summary: Time integration preserves compatibility of spatial jets

TorusEuler.spatialLevel_le_norm.text: For a field with order-`m` half-Hölder regularity, any level `j ≤ m` contributes at most the full norm. Each other summand is nonnegative under the boundedness hypotheses supplied by that regularity. The lemma turns order-specific supremum and increment bounds into estimates using a single input budget.
TorusEuler.spatialLevel_le_norm.summary: One derivative level is bounded by the full Hölder norm

TorusEuler.spatialLevel_nonneg.text: For an order-`m` half-Hölder field, the sum of the supremum and seminorm at any derivative level `j ≤ m` is nonnegative. The regularity predicate supplies boundedness of both real-supremum ranges. This permits derivative levels to be discarded or added when comparing the various finite-order norms.
TorusEuler.spatialLevel_nonneg.summary: Every bounded derivative level contributes a nonnegative amount

TorusEuler.spatialLp_eq_zero_of_realMode.text: A real spatial L² field is zero if all its cosine and sine Fourier moments vanish. The proof tests each real coordinate, combines both moment families into complex Fourier coefficients, and uses L² Fourier expansion uniqueness. Both `hre` and `him` are required; one family alone does not separate arbitrary fields.
TorusEuler.spatialLp_eq_zero_of_realMode.summary: Cosine and sine moments determine a real L² field

TorusEuler.spatialPartial.text: Takes the joint within-slab derivative of $f$ and restricts it to the spatial directions. The result is a function valued in continuous linear maps from $E$ to the target. This operation defines notation for the mixed derivative proof; it does not, by itself, show that a spatial slice is differentiable.
TorusEuler.spatialPartial.summary: Extract the spatial partial from the joint derivative

TorusEuler.spatialPartial_smooth.text: The spatial component of the joint within-slab derivative is jointly smooth when `0 < T` and the original function is smooth. Restriction to spatial directions is a fixed continuous linear operation, so it preserves the smoothness of the derivative map. This permits the induction to switch between spatial and temporal differentiation.
TorusEuler.spatialPartial_smooth.summary: The extracted spatial partial is jointly smooth

TorusEuler.spatialPartial_timePartial_co.text: For a smooth function on $[0,T]\times E$ with `0 < T`, extracting a time partial after a spatial partial equals extracting them in the reverse order at each slab point. The proof uses the symmetry of the second derivative within a set that is the closure of its interior. It therefore covers the time endpoints.
TorusEuler.spatialPartial_timePartial_co.summary: The extracted time and spatial partials commute

TorusEuler.spatialRestrict.text: Defines a continuous linear map that sends a joint derivative $L$ to $v\mapsto L(0,v)$. This separates the spatial component without changing the target space. The operation itself is purely linear algebra; later theorems identify its value on an actual joint derivative with the ordinary Fréchet derivative of the fixed-time spatial slice.
TorusEuler.spatialRestrict.summary: Restrict a joint derivative to spatial directions

TorusEuler.spatialSlice_smooth.text: Any jointly smooth field on the closed slab has an infinitely smooth spatial slice at a slab time. Composition with the fixed-time inclusion proves the assertion. This local helper is used when taking the ordinary spatial gradient and Hessian of the generic pressure, independently of the within-time derivative convention.
TorusEuler.spatialSlice_smooth.summary: Smooth spatial pressure slices on the slab

TorusEuler.spatialSupNorm.text:
Define the real supremum of the pointwise norm over all Euclidean labels. It acts as the intended uniform norm only when the range is bounded above; the definition itself imposes no boundedness.

Default-value audit (b5): This is a real iSup, not an extended-real supremum; unbounded norm ranges can take Lean's default zero. Only bounded-above ranges support the intended pointwise norm comparison.

TorusEuler.spatialSupNorm_nonneg.text: For a field with bounded norm range, its real supremum norm is nonnegative. The proof compares the supremum with the norm at the origin. The boundedness hypothesis is kept explicit because the definition uses a conditional real supremum, not an extended-real supremum that automatically records infinity.
TorusEuler.spatialSupNorm_nonneg.summary: A bounded spatial supremum is nonnegative

TorusEuler.spatialTimeLift.text: This bounded real linear map takes a bounded operator on three-vectors to its pointwise action on $L^2$ time paths over $(0,T]$. The result is an operator on equivalence classes of paths. Its almost-everywhere evaluation lemma supplies the precise connection with the informal pointwise description.
TorusEuler.spatialTimeLift.summary: A spatial operator acts at every time along a path

TorusEuler.spatialTimeLift_apply_ae.text: The path obtained by applying the lifted operator agrees almost everywhere with $t\mapsto A(v(t))$. Equality is deliberately almost everywhere because $L^2$ paths are equivalence classes. This evaluation identity is used to prove symmetry, idempotence, and commutation with time integration.
TorusEuler.spatialTimeLift_apply_ae.summary: The lifted spatial action is pointwise almost everywhere

TorusEuler.spatialTimeLift_commutes_endp.text: Any fixed bounded spatial operator, lifted to time paths, commutes with the mean-subtraction map. The identity follows because the operator preserves constant paths and commutes with integration. There is no positivity hypothesis on `T` in this algebraic statement; orthogonality of mean subtraction is established separately.
TorusEuler.spatialTimeLift_commutes_endp.summary: Spatial action commutes with subtracting the time average

TorusEuler.spatialTimeLift_const.text: Applying the lifted spatial operator to a constant $L^2$ path gives the constant path with the transformed value. This is equality of path-space elements, proved from their almost-everywhere representatives. It supports the algebraic commutation between spatial action and subtraction of the time average.
TorusEuler.spatialTimeLift_const.summary: Constant paths remain constant under spatial operators

TorusEuler.spatialTimeLift_integral.text: Time integrating the path after applying a fixed bounded spatial operator gives the operator applied to the original time integral. The path belongs to $L^2$ on a finite measure interval, hence is integrable. This identity is the key reason the spatial action preserves the zero-time-mean condition.
TorusEuler.spatialTimeLift_integral.summary: Spatial operators commute with path integration

TorusEuler.spatialTimeLift_isSymmetricPr.text: If `hA` makes the spatial operator a symmetric projection, its lifted action is a symmetric projection on the real $L^2$ path space. Idempotence holds almost everywhere and symmetry is integrated through the path inner product. No positive-duration assumption is needed for this lifting statement.
TorusEuler.spatialTimeLift_isSymmetricPr.summary: A symmetric spatial projection remains one on paths

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_centeredLab.text: The coordinatewise centered-label representative is unchanged when an integer lattice vector is added. This follows from periodicity of the fractional-part operation. The result is a statement about values only: the representative jumps at cell boundaries, so it is not by itself a smooth map.
TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_centeredLab.summary: The centered representative is invariant under lattice translation

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_closedSlab_.text: Smooth periodic slices of velocity and pressure give a periodic momentum residual at each slab time, with velocity periodicity assumed over the full time interval to handle the time derivative.
TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_closedSlab_.summary: The momentum residual remains spatially periodic

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_curl.text: The curl of a spatially periodic vector function is also spatially periodic. The statement itself has no differentiability assumption because Lean’s total derivative respects translation identities even outside the differentiable case. Classical smoothness and the divergence-of-curl identity are established separately before physical applications.
TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_curl.summary: Curl respects the periodic translation identity

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_divergence.text: For a differentiable periodic vector field, divergence is periodic with the same lattice. The proof differentiates the equality between a lattice translate and the original field, then compares traces. Differentiability is explicit because equality of functions alone does not provide the derivative formula used here.
TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_divergence.summary: Divergence inherits periodicity from a differentiable field

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_dyadicPerio.text: The double dyadic and lattice kernel expression is spatially periodic by reindexing the lattice translates. No separate convergence argument is part of this theorem. Its analytic use together with smoothness requires the later off origin summable-majorant estimates.
TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_dyadicPerio.summary: The full kernel respects the unit periods

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_endpointFin.text: The real pressure formed from the finite Fourier sum is spatially periodic for every frequency set and coefficient family. Its argument passes through the unit torus, so integer lattice translations do not change the value. This is a periodicity assertion independent of whether its gradient reconstructs a chosen vector field.
TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_endpointFin.summary: Finite Fourier pressures have the prescribed periods

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_endpointPar.text: If a field is invariant under integer lattice shifts, its reflection average has the same periodicity for any real sign. Reflection sends a lattice shift to the opposite shift, which is still available in the periodicity hypothesis. This result does not require the sign to be a genuine parity value.

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_firstWaveCo.text: The cosine factor $\cos(2\pi a_1)$ is unchanged by any integer lattice translation of the label. Lean indexes coordinates from zero, so `a 1` is the second component. This scalar periodicity is the starting point for periodicity of the shear sweep and the explicit first-wave seed.
TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_firstWaveCo.summary: The initial shear repeats across the lattice

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_firstWaveCo.text: The transported covector is spatially periodic at every time. The inverse-deformation matrix repeats on the label lattice, and its adjoint is applied to the same constant launch covector. This provides ordinary coefficient periodicity before the oscillatory velocity is placed in the carrier-twisted space.
TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_firstWaveCo.summary: The transported first-wave covector is label periodic

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_firstWaveIn.text: At each fixed time, the explicit inverse deformation is spatially periodic in the label. The identity term is constant and the material-gradient term is periodic. This property concerns the derivative matrix; the shear flow itself is lattice equivariant rather than a spatially periodic map.
TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_firstWaveIn.summary: The inverse deformation repeats with the label lattice

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_firstWaveLo.text: The constructed first-wave velocity is periodic for every real choice of its scalar parameters and every time. Centered periodization gives periodicity of the potential, and the inverse shear map respects lattice translations. This algebraic periodicity statement is weaker than the separate smoothness theorem and does not require its collar hypotheses.
TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_firstWaveLo.summary: The completed first velocity is spatially periodic

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_firstWaveMa.text: The material gradient is spatially periodic for every shear parameter. Translating the second label coordinate by an integer changes the cosine angle by an integer multiple of $2\pi$, leaving the matrix unchanged. This periodicity permits the coefficient to be embedded into any carrier-twisted profile space.
TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_firstWaveMa.summary: The material shear coefficient repeats on the lattice

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_firstWaveSm.text: For every shear ratio `s`, amplitude scale `c`, and time `t`, the vector seed is spatially periodic. Its label dependence enters through the periodic sweep. The result concerns the unlocalized seed; localization and the twisted periodization used for the physical oscillation are separate constructions.
TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_firstWaveSm.summary: The explicit seed is periodic in its label

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_firstWaveSw.text: At each fixed time `t`, the scalar `firstWaveSweep t` is spatially periodic. Multiplication of the periodic cosine by its time-dependent scalar preserves every integer translation. This statement places no restriction on time and does not assert periodicity in time; it supplies the spatial hypothesis for later uniform derivative bounds.
TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_firstWaveSw.summary: The shear sweep repeats across the lattice

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_fourierMode.text: For every integer frequency, the lifted Fourier mode is invariant under translation by an integer lattice vector. The proof uses equality in the torus quotient. This connects the library character with the periodicity predicate used throughout the Euler formalization on Euclidean space.
TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_fourierMode.summary: Integer Fourier characters are spatially periodic

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_halfHolderP.text: For any input function and any bounded torus operator, `halfHolderProjectionLift` is spatially periodic. On its admissible branch it is evaluation through the torus quotient; otherwise the definition returns zero. This unconditional periodicity theorem therefore does not certify that the input had a valid half-Hölder descent or that the output is its mathematical projection.

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_iteratedFDe.text: The iterated Fréchet derivatives of a spatially periodic function are spatially periodic at every order. Translation commutes with the totalized derivative operator, so no smoothness hypothesis is needed for this identity. Smoothness is supplied separately when these derivatives are used to define the actual periodic jet spaces.

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_latticeDete.text: Adding any integer lattice vector leaves the detector unchanged. Although sine itself may change sign under a unit shift, its square is periodic with period one. The proof uses the double-angle cosine identity to avoid tracking coordinate-dependent signs. Periodicity is later inherited by the cutoff built from this detector.
TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_latticeDete.summary: Integer translations preserve the cutoff detector

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_liftConvolu.text: If the input field is invariant under all lattice translations, its convolution has the same periodicity for any kernel. The proof compares the integrands pointwise after a lattice shift. No convergence assumption is needed for this identity of total integral expressions; the analytic existence of convolution is established separately.

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_lift_realVe.text: The real vector Fourier cutoff, composed with the quotient map, is a spatially periodic field. Periodicity follows from being a function on the torus, regardless of approximation estimates.
TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_lift_realVe.summary: The truncated torus field lifts periodically

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_lift_smooth.text: The Fourier cutoff composed with the quotient map is invariant under integer lattice translations. This periodicity holds for arbitrary symbol, scale, and input because the output is defined on the quotient torus. Separate hypotheses establish norm estimates or agreement with a prescribed smooth multiplier.

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_localizedTr.text: Fix a time and suppose $A(x+n)=A(x)+n$ for all $n\in\mathbb Z^3$. For arbitrary $k_*\in\mathbb R^3$ and any profile $f$, the formal statement proves spatial periodicity of the field obtained by evaluating $f(t,a,k_*\cdot a)$ in the centered cell, extending it periodically and composing with $A$. The result needs no smoothness, transversality or support assumptions and applies to arbitrary values of the profile. It is the periodicity part of the construction in §3.1. Vanishing near the boundary is still needed for smoothness; integer coordinates of $k_*$ are unnecessary for this extended field.
TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_localizedTr.summary: Integer-translation equivariance of the inverse map suffices

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_modOne_line.text: For an arbitrary $k_*\in\mathbb R^3$, the formal theorem proves that the circle-valued phase $a\mapsto k_*\cdot a\pmod1$ is invariant under every integer translation exactly when $k_*\in\mathbb Z^3$. The phase takes values in $\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$, rather than being a real-valued periodic function. This is the precise lattice restriction discussed in §3.1. It is a statement about the phase itself; a particular scalar profile could have additional symmetries. The localized construction avoids requiring a global periodic linear phase by cutting the field off inside one label cell and extending that field periodically.
TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_modOne_line.summary: A phase modulo one is periodic exactly at lattice frequencies

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_nearPressur.text: If both cutoff and velocity are spatially periodic, the cutoff quadratic tensor is spatially periodic. The statement follows by replacing each translated input with its unshifted value. It is independent of the support and smoothness conditions needed to use this source in the pressure convergence argument.
TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_nearPressur.summary: Periodic cutoff and velocity give a periodic near source

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_normalizedF.text: At every real time, the normalized pressure coefficient is spatially periodic. The proof combines periodicity of the sweep with periodicity of the cosine in the numerator. This concerns the scalar coefficient before multiplication by the envelope and the phase primitive, rather than the complete physical pressure.
TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_normalizedF.summary: The normalized pressure repeats across the lattice

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_operatorLif.text: A spatially periodic input field remains periodic after convolution with any operator-valued kernel. The identity follows from periodicity of the integrand under lattice translation of the output point. It is valid as an equality of total integral expressions; convergence and norm estimates are separate assertions.
TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_operatorLif.summary: Operator convolution preserves the lattice period

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_periodicLer.text: Specializes the unconditional periodicity property of the general projection lift to the spatial Leray operator. It remains true for inadmissible inputs because the underlying definition then returns zero. The theorem should be read as a property of the total extension; meaningful projection and regularity claims require the hypotheses supplied by the neighbouring estimates.
TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_periodicLer.summary: The Leray lift is periodic for every input

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_periodizeCe.text: Extending a function by evaluating it at the centered representative produces a spatially periodic function. This statement alone does not assert continuity at cell walls.
TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_periodizeCe.summary: The centered extension is spatially periodic

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_pressureVel.text: Integer periodicity of velocity gives integer periodicity of its pressure tensor pointwise. Both factors are evaluated at the same translated point, so the equality follows directly from the input periodicity. No differentiability, incompressibility or Fourier expansion is needed for this property.
TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_pressureVel.summary: The quadratic pressure source is spatially periodic

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_pullback.text: Composing any function on torus labels with `toUnitTorus` produces a lattice-periodic Euclidean field. The codomain is arbitrary, and no regularity is asserted or required. This supplies the periodicity needed to descend coordinate derivatives and compare the Fourier cutoff with physical differential operators.

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_stationaryS.text: The stationary shear is spatially periodic for every real parameter. Translating the second coordinate by an integer changes its sine phase by an integer multiple of $2\pi$, leaving the velocity unchanged. This verifies the periodicity requirement for the initial parent on the torus.
TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_stationaryS.summary: The sinusoidal shear is periodic under integer translations

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_transported.text: Affine lattice equivariance of the inverse-label map and the corresponding joint label-phase shift law for the profile imply spatial periodicity after graph evaluation. This statement works for any target type and needs no smoothness or integrality of the carrier vector. Compatibility of the profile absorbs the carrier’s phase shift.
TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_transported.summary: A compatible phase twist produces a periodic physical field

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_truncatedPa.text: Shows that the slice pressure is invariant under every integer spatial translation, for every radius and input. Each Fourier mode is periodic, so the finite synthesis has the same property. This supplies the periodicity needed to package the potential for the Leray and pressure-recovery arguments.
TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_truncatedPa.summary: The finite pressure respects lattice translations

TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_tsum_lattic.text: The double sum over dyadic grades and all integer translations is spatially periodic for any family `K`. Translating the observation point simply reindexes the lattice by a bijection. This identity holds for Lean’s totalized infinite sum without a summability premise; later estimates are needed to interpret it as a convergent kernel.
TorusEuler.spatiallyPeriodic_tsum_lattic.summary: Summing all lattice translates gives a periodic expression

TorusEuler.sq_intervalIntegral_le.text: For `a ≤ b`, a continuous real function `g` that is nonnegative everywhere satisfies $(\int_a^b g)^2\le(b-a)\int_a^b g^2$. The proof uses Hölder with exponents two and two on the restricted interval. The global nonnegativity hypothesis is stronger than what integration on this interval alone would require.
TorusEuler.sq_intervalIntegral_le.summary: Cauchy Schwarz bounds a squared time integral

TorusEuler.sqrt_two_geom_prefix.text: The sum of $(\sqrt2)^j$ for indices below `n` is at most three times $(\sqrt2)^n$. This finite geometric estimate controls the low-frequency part of a difference after applying the Lipschitz bound to each block. The same splitting index is used for the complementary decaying tail.
TorusEuler.sqrt_two_geom_prefix.summary: The low-frequency prefix costs one final scale

TorusEuler.sqrt_two_inv_geom.text: The sequence of powers of $1/\sqrt2$ is summable. This is the scalar convergence input for the uniform majorant of the Banach-valued dyadic blocks. It ensures that the infinite sum used later is a genuine convergent series rather than merely Lean's totalized `tsum` expression.

TorusEuler.sqrt_two_inv_geom_sum.text: The sum of all powers of $1/\sqrt2$ is at most four. Together with each block's geometric supremum bound, this yields the uniform size bound for the reconstructed function. Summability is established separately before the infinite-series formula is evaluated in this estimate.
TorusEuler.sqrt_two_inv_geom_sum.summary: The decreasing half-scale series is bounded by four

TorusEuler.sqrt_two_pow_sq.text: For every natural index `j`, the square of $(\sqrt2)^j$ is $2^j$. This exact identity converts between half-order scales and the original dyadic frequency. It is used in the estimates choosing the splitting index for a spatial increment and involves no real-power ambiguity.
TorusEuler.sqrt_two_pow_sq.summary: Squaring the half-scale recovers the dyadic scale

TorusEuler.stage_spatial_jets_of_joint_s.text: A jointly smooth velocity on a nondegenerate closed time slab has smooth spatial slices and jointly continuous spatial derivatives of every order, including at the time endpoints. The proof restricts the joint within derivative to spatial directions. This supplies the continuity assumptions required before passing stage jets to a uniform limit.
TorusEuler.stage_spatial_jets_of_joint_s.summary: Closed slab smoothness controls all spatial jets

TorusEuler.stationaryInductiveEulerStage.text: Builds the full stage-zero record using the sine shear tilted by the scheduled gain ratio, zero pressure and the explicit two-time shear flow. It assumes that the ratio has absolute value at most one and that the initial frequency is at least $1+4\pi$. These hypotheses justify the velocity, Fourier, deformation and residual bounds.
TorusEuler.stationaryInductiveEulerStage.summary: The scheduled stationary shear supplies the zero stage

TorusEuler.stationaryInductiveEulerStage.text: Computes the velocity field of the constructed zero stage as the explicit stationary shear with the scheduled ratio. The equality holds pointwise for every real time and spatial point because that stage is time independent. The same parameter hypotheses required by the constructor remain arguments of this identity.
TorusEuler.stationaryInductiveEulerStage.summary: The base-stage velocity is the prescribed tilted shear

TorusEuler.stationaryPrimaryPressure_pro.text: For a nonnegative coefficient at the point, two derivatives of the coefficient of size $K\lambda^{-7/4}$, and phase derivatives bounded by $B\lambda$, proves an upper quadratic-form bound of order $K\lambda^{-1/4}$. The leading rank-one tensor uses the lower bound for the profile slope. This is one-sided control; it does not bound the absolute Hessian norm by the same rate.
TorusEuler.stationaryPrimaryPressure_pro.summary: The signed pressure product has a small upper Hessian

TorusEuler.stationaryShear.text: The formal velocity is $U_0(x)=\sin(2\pi x_2)(e_1+\rho e_3)$ for a real parameter $\rho$. Its values lie in the plane spanned by $e_1,e_3$ and depend only on the transverse coordinate $x_2$. This formula defines a field on all of $\mathbb R^3$ that is invariant under integer translations and odd under $x\mapsto-x$. It is the initial shear of §1.1 and (6.1). The definition permits any real tilt, whereas the amplification construction chooses $\rho>0$ small. The assertion that this field solves Euler with zero pressure is supplied separately.
TorusEuler.stationaryShear.summary: A one-dimensional sine shear initializes the construction

TorusEuler.stationaryShearComplexTorus.text: This torus field is the finite Fourier sum over the positive and negative second-coordinate unit frequencies with the prescribed sine coefficients. It is a complex Euclidean-valued representation of the stationary parent. The lift theorem proves that its values are exactly the complexification of the real sinusoidal shear.
TorusEuler.stationaryShearComplexTorus.summary: Synthesizing the stationary parent from its two Fourier modes

TorusEuler.stationaryShearComplexTorus_l.text: The complex torus field evaluated on a Euclidean label equals coordinatewise complexification of the stationary sinusoidal shear at that label. The proof expands both distinct frequencies and uses the sine identity. Thus later Fourier support statements refer to the actual parent velocity, not an unrelated model field.
TorusEuler.stationaryShearComplexTorus_l.summary: The two mode field is the actual stationary shear

TorusEuler.stationaryShearDeformation_in.text: For every real scalar `c`, the operators $I+cD$ and $I-cD$ are two-sided inverses when $D$ is the stationary shear gradient. The proof uses $D^2=0$. No smallness of `c` or bound on the shear parameter is required for these exact algebraic inverse identities.
TorusEuler.stationaryShearDeformation_in.summary: The shear deformation inverse reverses its nilpotent correction

TorusEuler.stationaryShearFlow.text: For $U_0(a)=\sin(2\pi a_2)(e_1+\rho e_3)$, the formal flow formula is $X_0(t,a)=a+tU_0(a)$, for all real $t$ and $\rho$. The second coordinate remains $a_2$, so $U_0(X_0(t,a))=U_0(a)$ and the formula describes trajectories of the stationary shear. Its displacement is periodic under integer translations of the label $a$. This is the explicit flow used in the first-wave construction. The displayed definition gives particle positions; its inverse, derivatives and volume-preserving properties are proved separately and should not be read as additional conclusions of the formula itself.
TorusEuler.stationaryShearFlow.summary: Particles keep their second coordinate while moving along the shear

TorusEuler.stationaryShearFlow_inverse.text: Composing the explicit shear flow for time `t` with the same flow for time `-t` returns the initial label. Velocity is constant along each trajectory, so the two increments cancel exactly. This establishes a concrete inverse without invoking a general inverse-function construction or restricting the time size.

TorusEuler.stationaryShearFlow_jacobian_.text: Let $U_0(x)=\sin(2\pi x_2)(e_1+\rho e_3)$ with $|\rho|\le1$, and let $X_0(t,a)=a+tU_0(a)$. For every $t\in[0,1]$ and label $a\in\mathbb R^3$, the formal statement bounds both $\|D_aX_0(t,a)\|$ and $\|D_xX_0(-t,X_0(t,a))\|$ by $1+4\pi$. These are Euclidean operator norms. The second derivative is evaluated at the transported point and is the inverse of the first. Thus the result supplies the deformation and inverse-deformation bounds for the base interval $S_0=1$. It permits a larger tilt range than the construction's positive $\rho$.
TorusEuler.stationaryShearFlow_jacobian_.summary: The flow derivative and its inverse have a common bound

TorusEuler.stationaryShearFlow_jacobians.text: For any real $\rho,t$ and label $a\in\mathbb R^3$, take $X_0(t,a)=a+t\sin(2\pi a_2)(e_1+\rho e_3)$ and $B_\rho=2\pi(e_1+\rho e_3)\otimes e_2$. The formal theorem proves $D_aX_0(t,a)=I+t\cos(2\pi a_2)B_\rho$ and $D_xX_0(-t,X_0(t,a))=I-t\cos(2\pi a_2)B_\rho$. The inverse derivative is taken at the image of the original label, not at an unrelated point. These are the deformation formulas in (6.2); the flow itself is a separate definition. No small-time or tilt restriction is needed, because $B_\rho^2=0$.
TorusEuler.stationaryShearFlow_jacobians.summary: Computes both derivatives at corresponding particle positions

TorusEuler.stationaryShearFlow_jacobians.text: The spatial derivative of the forward shear flow and the derivative of its inverse evaluated at the corresponding particle are two-sided inverse operators. The proof inserts their explicit identity-plus-or-minus-nilpotent formulas. This is a statement about the actual Jacobians, not arbitrary matrices chosen to satisfy inverse identities.
TorusEuler.stationaryShearFlow_jacobians.summary: The actual forward and inverse shear Jacobians cancel

TorusEuler.stationaryShearFlow_lattice_e.text: Translating a starting label by an integer lattice vector translates its evolved position by the same vector. The stationary shear velocity is periodic, so the velocity increment is unchanged. This verifies that the explicit lifted flow descends to the torus while retaining its concrete Euclidean formula.
TorusEuler.stationaryShearFlow_lattice_e.summary: The shear flow respects integer lattice translates

TorusEuler.stationaryShearFlow_origin.text: For the shear flow $X_0(t,a)=a+t\sin(2\pi a_2)(e_1+\rho e_3)$, the formal statement proves $X_0(t,0)=0$ for every pair of real numbers $\rho,t$. This is an exact identity for the flow lifted to $\mathbb R^3$, and therefore also fixes the origin of $\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$. It follows from the zero value of the sine at the origin. No smallness, positivity or frequency condition is required. The assertion concerns this explicit stationary shear, not every particle of the flow or every later velocity in the induction.
TorusEuler.stationaryShearFlow_origin.summary: The shear flow fixes the origin for every time

TorusEuler.stationaryShearFlow_second.text: For every real $\rho,t$ and label $a\in\mathbb R^3$, let $X_0(t,a)=a+t\sin(2\pi a_2)(e_1+\rho e_3)$. The formal theorem states $(X_0(t,a))_2=a_2$. It is an equality for the lifted trajectories in Euclidean space, so it is stronger than equality only modulo integers on the torus. The formal coordinates are numbered starting at zero; its coordinate numbered one is the paper's second coordinate. The statement imposes no restriction on $t$ or $\rho$ and makes no assertion that the first and third coordinates are conserved.
TorusEuler.stationaryShearFlow_second.summary: Each shear trajectory keeps its second spatial coordinate

TorusEuler.stationaryShearFourierCoeff.text: This coefficient function is $1/(2i)$ times the complex shear direction at the positive second-coordinate unit frequency, its negative at the opposite frequency, and zero elsewhere. It is an explicitly finite spectral description. A later coefficient theorem proves that it is the Fourier transform of the actual shear.
TorusEuler.stationaryShearFourierCoeff.summary: The stationary shear has two opposite sine coefficients

TorusEuler.stationaryShearGradient.text: The formal definition is the linear map $B_\rho v=2\pi v_2(e_1+\rho e_3)$ on $\mathbb R^3$, for every real $\rho$. Equivalently, $B_\rho=2\pi(e_1+\rho e_3)\otimes e_2$, with $(a\otimes b)v=(b\cdot v)a$. This is the gradient at the origin of $U_0(x)=\sin(2\pi x_2)(e_1+\rho e_3)$, rather than its spatially constant gradient everywhere: at a general point the gradient is $\cos(2\pi x_2)B_\rho$. Coordinates follow the paper's ordering after shifting the formal indices by one. This definition alone states no bound on $\|B_\rho\|$.
TorusEuler.stationaryShearGradient.summary: Defines the constant gradient at the central particle

TorusEuler.stationaryShearGradient_adjoi.text: The adjoint shear matrix sends $ce_1$ to $2\pi c e_2$, independently of the third-direction shear parameter. The proof compares inner products against an arbitrary vector. This identity simplifies inverse-transpose transport of the first wave vector into a formula involving only the first two coordinate directions.
TorusEuler.stationaryShearGradient_adjoi.summary: The adjoint sends the first direction into the second

TorusEuler.stationaryShearGradient_apply.text: Applying the central stationary-shear gradient to `v` gives $2\pi v_2(e_1+se_3)$. This is the explicit rank-one action of the matrix in the manuscript. The identity holds for arbitrary shear parameter and vector, and makes the first-wave amplitude equation an elementary component calculation.
TorusEuler.stationaryShearGradient_apply.summary: The shear matrix reads the second component

TorusEuler.stationaryShearGradient_coupl.text: For any real $\rho$, let $D_0=2\pi(e_1+\rho e_3)\otimes e_2$, the central gradient of the initial sine shear. The formal theorem proves $e_1\cdot D_0e_2=2\pi$ and $e_3\cdot D_0e_2=2\pi\rho$. Thus the coordinate-frame couplings in §1.1 are $\nu=2\pi$ and $\eta=2\pi\rho$, with ratio $\eta/\nu=\rho$. Positivity of $\eta$ follows only after requiring $\rho>0$; no smallness assumption is needed for these identities. The theorem states the two entries of the linear map. Its identification with the derivative of the actual periodic shear is a separate derivative identity.
TorusEuler.stationaryShearGradient_coupl.summary: The coordinate-frame entries are two pi and two pi times tilt

TorusEuler.stationaryShearGradient_origi.text: For $U_0(x)=\sin(2\pi x_2)(e_1+\rho e_3)$ and any real $\rho$, the formal theorem proves $D_xU_0(0)=2\pi(e_1+\rho e_3)\otimes e_2$. The derivative is a linear map on Euclidean three-space; on a vector $v$ it acts as $2\pi v_2(e_1+\rho e_3)$. This specifies the paper’s convention $(\nabla U_0)_{ij}=\partial_j(U_0)_i$ and identifies the actual periodic velocity with the linear background used at the center. Positivity or smallness of $\rho$ is unnecessary for this derivative identity, although used later to select the amplification regime.
TorusEuler.stationaryShearGradient_origi.summary: Differentiating the sine shear yields the initial linear map

TorusEuler.stationaryShearGradient_sq.text: For $B_\rho=2\pi(e_1+\rho e_3)\otimes e_2$, the formal statement proves $B_\rho\circ B_\rho=0$ as a linear map on $\mathbb R^3$, for every real $\rho$. The reason is the perpendicularity $e_2\cdot(e_1+\rho e_3)=0$. Consequently the candidate deformation maps $I+cB_\rho$ and $I-cB_\rho$ are inverse for every real scalar $c$. That consequence explains the inverse formula in (6.2), although this declaration itself concludes only the square-zero identity. No frequency, time or tilt bound is required.
TorusEuler.stationaryShearGradient_sq.summary: The rank-one central gradient has square zero

TorusEuler.stationaryShearMode.text: This integer frequency has value one in the second coordinate and zero in the other two. Together with its negative it supports the sinusoidal stationary parent. Naming this explicit frequency lets the formalization prove exact Fourier support and compare it with the initial truncation band.
TorusEuler.stationaryShearMode.summary: The unit frequency in the second coordinate

TorusEuler.stationaryShearMode_ne_neg.text: The positive unit frequency in the second coordinate is not equal to its negative. The proof reads the second component, where the equality would say one equals negative one. This guarantees that finite synthesis over the two signed modes contains two distinct terms.

TorusEuler.stationaryShearTorus.text: Forms the real part of the two-mode complex Fourier representation of the stationary shear and packages it as a continuous torus map. The continuity proof uses finiteness of the Fourier sum. The next theorem identifies its Euclidean lift with the explicit sine shear used to begin the physical induction.
TorusEuler.stationaryShearTorus.summary: The stationary shear as a continuous torus field

TorusEuler.stationaryShearTorus_lift.text: Shows that evaluating the torus map at the quotient image of a Euclidean point gives the explicit stationary shear. This holds for every real parameter and spatial point. It transfers known differential and symmetry properties of the sine formula to the continuous torus representation required by stage records.
TorusEuler.stationaryShearTorus_lift.summary: The torus representation equals the explicit sine shear

TorusEuler.stationaryShear_advection.text: For $U_0(x)=\sin(2\pi x_2)(e_1+\rho e_3)$, the formal theorem proves $D U_0(x)[U_0(x)]=0$ for every real $\rho$ and every $x\in\mathbb R^3$. This is the paper's $(U_0\cdot\nabla)U_0=0$: the field depends only on its second coordinate and has zero component in that direction. The derivative is the full spatial linear map evaluated on the velocity. The result requires no parameter or time restriction. Choosing zero pressure then gives the stationary Euler equation, but the pressure and residual are not themselves part of this theorem's conclusion.
TorusEuler.stationaryShear_advection.summary: The stationary shear has zero nonlinear transport term

TorusEuler.stationaryShear_base_T1.text: Let $\lambda_0\ge1$ and let $\rho$ be any real number. The velocity $U_0(t,x)=\sin(2\pi x_2)(e_1+\rho e_3)$ is jointly smooth on $[0,1]\times\mathbb R^3$, periodic under integer translations, odd, and divergence free. Its Fourier coefficients vanish outside the band of radius $2\lambda_0^5$. These are the formal conclusions needed for (T1) at the base stage. Periodic fields are represented by functions on $\mathbb R^3$ descending to $\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$. This statement gives support in the prescribed larger band, not the sharper claim that the only nonzero modes are exactly $\pm e_2$. No bound on $|\rho|$ is needed for these regularity properties.
TorusEuler.stationaryShear_base_T1.summary: The shear supplies the base regularity and Fourier support

TorusEuler.stationaryShear_base_T2.text: Assume `hs : |s| ≤ 1` and `hfreq₀ : 1 + 4π ≤ freq₀`. The velocity and both actual flow Jacobians on $[0,1]$ are bounded by the base frequency. The residual norm is at most the displayed successor-frequency budget because it is exactly zero; no positivity assumption on `freq₁` is needed for that last inequality.
TorusEuler.stationaryShear_base_T2.summary: The initial parent satisfies velocity deformation and residual budgets

TorusEuler.stationaryShear_base_T3.text: The derivative of the gradient of the zero pressure is the zero operator at every point. This supplies the index-zero Hessian condition, where the accumulated pressure budget is empty. The theorem concerns the explicit constant pressure and does not assert a corresponding fact for arbitrary stationary parents.

TorusEuler.stationaryShear_closedSlabLer.text: Proves that the Leray-projected momentum expression of the time-independent shear is identically zero, for every real parameter and time. The time derivative is zero and the shear advects itself trivially. This supplies the base stage’s residual identity; no forcing term is introduced by the chosen closed-slab derivative convention.
TorusEuler.stationaryShear_closedSlabLer.summary: The stationary shear has zero projected momentum

TorusEuler.stationaryShear_closed_residu.text: The sum of its within-interval time derivative, self-advection, and the gradient of zero pressure vanishes. The theorem is stated for every real evaluation time, since the velocity is time-independent and its self-advection is zero. It provides the residual identity also at the closed slab endpoints.
TorusEuler.stationaryShear_closed_residu.summary: The stationary parent has zero momentum residual on the slab

TorusEuler.stationaryShear_gradient_squa.text: At every spatial point, composing the shear velocity gradient with itself gives the zero operator. The gradient is a cosine scalar times the same square-zero central rank-one map. This makes the quadratic trace source in the parent pressure Poisson equation vanish identically.
TorusEuler.stationaryShear_gradient_squa.summary: The stationary velocity gradient squares to zero everywhere

TorusEuler.stationaryShear_isLabelFlowOn.text: The transition from start time `r` to time `t` is the explicit shear flow evaluated at duration $t-r$. It satisfies the initial identity and within-set trajectory equation on any time set `J`. The underlying flow formula is globally defined, so this particular parent needs no local existence argument.
TorusEuler.stationaryShear_isLabelFlowOn.summary: The explicit shear gives a two time flow on any set

TorusEuler.stationaryShear_mFourierCoeff.text: The Fourier coefficient of the complex torus stationary parent at every integer frequency equals the explicitly defined coefficient function. Finite synthesis gives exact coefficient recovery, and the outside-band cases reduce to zero. This certifies the two-mode representation used for the initial truncation condition.
TorusEuler.stationaryShear_mFourierCoeff.summary: The parent Fourier coefficients are the prescribed pair

TorusEuler.stationaryShear_mFourierCoeff.text: For any real $\rho$, regard $U_0(x)=\sin(2\pi x_2)(e_1+\rho e_3)$ as a field on $\mathbb R^3/\mathbb Z^3$ and allow its Fourier coefficients to have complex vector components. The formal statement proves that the coefficient at an integer frequency $k$ is nonzero if and only if $k=e_2$ or $k=-e_2$. Thus it establishes exact support, not merely containment in these modes. Neither coefficient can vanish because the first component of $e_1+\rho e_3$ is one. Complexifying the coefficients is the usual Fourier representation of a real field; it does not change the underlying velocity.
TorusEuler.stationaryShear_mFourierCoeff.summary: The Fourier support is exactly the second coordinate pair

TorusEuler.stationaryShear_normalized_pr.text: The constant zero pressure has zero centered-cell mean and its Laplacian equals minus the trace of the square of the stationary velocity gradient. The square vanishes everywhere by the preceding lemma. This verifies the normalized pressure equation for the actual parent rather than only asserting that zero is an admissible value.
TorusEuler.stationaryShear_normalized_pr.summary: Zero pressure satisfies the parent Poisson normalization

TorusEuler.stationaryShear_on_flow.text: Evaluating the stationary shear along its explicit trajectory gives the original shear at the starting label. The second coordinate remains fixed, and that is the only coordinate on which the velocity depends. The identity holds for all real times, enabling the simple affine-in-time flow formula.
TorusEuler.stationaryShear_on_flow.summary: The shear velocity stays constant along its trajectories

TorusEuler.stationaryShear_second.text: For $U_0(x)=\sin(2\pi x_2)(e_1+\rho e_3)$ and every real $\rho$, the formal theorem proves $(U_0(x))_2=0$ at every $x\in\mathbb R^3$. Its coordinate numbered one is the paper's second coordinate, since the formal indexing starts at zero. The field may depend on $x_2$ even though its second velocity component vanishes. This is the pointwise observation used to show that the nonlinear advection is zero and that the second coordinate is conserved along its flow; those conclusions require separate identities.
TorusEuler.stationaryShear_second.summary: The stationary shear has no velocity in the second direction

TorusEuler.stationaryShear_stage_deforma.text: For a shear parameter of absolute value at most one and `C ≥ 1 + 4π`, certifies the actual two-time stationary shear flow on the unit time slab. Explicit inverse-flow and Jacobian formulas establish the derivative bounds. The hypotheses are quantitative; the theorem does not cover arbitrary large shear parameters with the same constant.
TorusEuler.stationaryShear_stage_deforma.summary: The stationary flow satisfies the stage deformation bound

TorusEuler.strongLabelMomentum_of_integr.text: On $[0,T]$, $T>0$, suppose $F_t=MF$, $v_t$ exists, $\Omega v$ and $g$ are continuous, and $Kv-J(\Omega v)-Jg=c+P$, where $K=F^TF$ and $\Omega=F^T(M^T-M)F$. If the pressure term has derivative $P_t=-Q$, then $Kv_t+Q=g-2F^TMFv$. This is the differentiation giving (4.11), including endpoint derivatives taken within the interval. The formal statement assumes the derivative relation for the pressure term; it does not prove time differentiability of an arbitrary scalar potential or construct its normalization. Here $Jw(t)=\int_0^tw(s)\,ds$.
TorusEuler.strongLabelMomentum_of_integr.summary: Obtain strong label momentum under a pressure derivative hypothesis

TorusEuler.stronglyMeasurable_endpointPr.text: The labelwise time integral is strongly measurable as a function of the pair of time and label. The proof inserts the indicator of $0<s\le t$ before integrating in $s$. It applies to the measurable representative supplied by `Lp`, including exceptional slices where the integral is totalized.
TorusEuler.stronglyMeasurable_endpointPr.summary: The primitive has a measurable joint representative

TorusEuler.sub_latticeVector_mem_offOrig.text: If a point belongs to `offOrigin`, subtracting any lattice vector leaves it in `offOrigin`. Here the punctured torus lift excludes all points representing the torus origin, not merely the zero vector in Euclidean space. This invariance ensures translated local extensions are evaluated within their smooth domain.
TorusEuler.sub_latticeVector_mem_offOrig.summary: Lattice translation preserves the punctured lift

TorusEuler.sum_Icc_previous.text: The sum of $f(p-1)$ over $2\le p\le P+1$ equals the sum of $f(p)$ over $1\le p\le P$. Only an additive commutative monoid is required. The explicit bijection handles $P=0$ as an empty sum and later aligns each oscillation with its divergence correction.
TorusEuler.sum_Icc_previous.summary: Shift the completion indices in a finite sum

TorusEuler.sum_Icc_split_first.text: For `hP : 1 ≤ P`, this splits a sum over $1\le p\le P$ into its first term and the sum over $2\le p\le P$. The hypothesis prevents an invalid first term when the interval is empty. It separates the prescribed wave from the recursively solved levels.
TorusEuler.sum_Icc_split_first.summary: Separate the leading term from the corrections

TorusEuler.sum_choose_mul_real.text: For any real constant `A`, summing $\binom qi A$ over $0\le i\le q$ gives $2^qA$. The private helper factors out `A` and uses the finite binomial sum. It needs no sign hypothesis because the conclusion is an equality; nonnegativity enters only when later estimates replace individual terms by a common bound.
TorusEuler.sum_choose_mul_real.summary: Binomial coefficients sum to a power of two

TorusEuler.sum_coordinateDirection.text: Summing each spatial coordinate times its corresponding standard direction reconstructs the original vector in three-dimensional Euclidean space. This identity supplies the coordinate expansion required by the multilinear operator-norm comparison. It involves only finite sums and is independent of smoothness, periodicity, or the flow.
TorusEuler.sum_coordinateDirection.summary: Coordinate directions reconstruct each spatial vector

TorusEuler.sum_insertCoordinateL2.text: Extract each of the three scalar coordinates of `u`, insert it back into its coordinate position, and sum: the resulting L² class is `u`. The proof combines representative identities with the finite Euclidean basis expansion. This avoids assuming vector-valued Fourier density as an independent library fact.
TorusEuler.sum_insertCoordinateL2.summary: Summing the coordinate fields reconstructs the vector field

TorusEuler.sum_list_map_const.text: Summing a constant real value over a list gives that value times the real coercion of the list length. The proof preserves list multiplicity rather than replacing the list by a set. This evaluates the common upper bound on all correction terms after the derivative induction has bounded them individually.
TorusEuler.sum_list_map_const.summary: Evaluate a constant list sum by its length

TorusEuler.sum_mul_bound.text: If every term of a finite sum is at most `M`, the sum is at most the cardinality of the index set times `M`. No sign condition is needed for this additive comparison. The lemma isolates pair-counting constants from the parent and frequency powers.
TorusEuler.sum_mul_bound.summary: Count the finitely many terms in a source

TorusEuler.sum_partSize.text: For an ordered partition of `n` derivative slots, summing the sizes of all blocks gives exactly `n`. The covering and disjointness fields of the partition supply this identity. It is the exponent-counting input that turns a product of lower-order deformation estimates into the required bound at order `n`.
TorusEuler.sum_partSize.summary: Partition block sizes exhaust the derivative order

TorusEuler.sum_phaseCoordinateDirection.text: A label-phase pair is the sum of its four coordinate values times the corresponding label-phase basis directions. The three spatial terms and one phase term are indexed by `Fin 3 ⊕ Unit`. This finite expansion supports the dimension factor in the mixed-derivative operator-norm estimate.
TorusEuler.sum_phaseCoordinateDirection.summary: Four coordinates reconstruct a label-phase pair

TorusEuler.sum_physical_coefficient_cost.text: The kinetic correction sum plus $T$ times the vorticity correction sum equals a single list sum using `endpointPhysicalCoefficientWordNorm`. This is an exact algebraic rearrangement, with no continuity or positivity assumptions. It puts the two analytic estimates into the form required by the common derivative recurrence.
TorusEuler.sum_physical_coefficient_cost.summary: Combine the two correction sums into one cost

TorusEuler.sum_spatialDerivativeWord_sup.text: A smooth field with jet bound `M` through order `m` has the sum of supremum norms over all ordered coordinate words of length `m` bounded by $3^mM$. Each coordinate direction has unit norm. This ordered-word sum includes multiplicities that are absent from an unordered multi-index notation, and therefore supplies an explicit overcounting constant.
TorusEuler.sum_spatialDerivativeWord_sup.summary: A Fréchet jet controls the sum of coordinate derivatives

TorusEuler.sum_weighted_labelJets_le_of_.text: Suppose $v_j\le C_j A D^{pj}$ for $j\le n$, with nonnegative amplitude, radius and constants, and `hscale : ℓ * D ^ p ≤ 1`. Then the weighted sum $\sum_{j\le n}\ell^j v_j$ is at most $A\sum_{j\le n}C_j$. The factor $(\ell D^p)^j$ pays for each successive derivative.
TorusEuler.sum_weighted_labelJets_le_of_.summary: Small radius absorbs the derivative powers

TorusEuler.summable_inv_one_add_latticeV.text: The sequence $(1+\|n\|)^{-p}$ over the three-dimensional integer lattice is summable for `p > 3`. Away from the origin it is dominated by the reciprocal norm power from the preceding lemma. The added one keeps the expression finite and positive at the origin, without changing the summability threshold.
TorusEuler.summable_inv_one_add_latticeV.summary: A nonsingular lattice majorant is summable

TorusEuler.summable_latticeVector_norm_p.text: The sum over integer triples of the reciprocal Euclidean norm to power `p` converges when `p > 3`. The origin contributes the totalized inverse value zero. The proof identifies the integer triples with a rank-three lattice and applies the lattice summability theorem; the single zero term does not affect convergence.
TorusEuler.summable_latticeVector_norm_p.summary: Inverse lattice powers are summable above dimension three

TorusEuler.summable_pressureNearBlockMas.text: The block mass equals the fixed Schwartz half moment multiplied by $(\sqrt2)^{-j}$. The scaling formula for weighted kernel integrals gives this equality, and the ratio is strictly between zero and one. Thus cancellation supplies an absolutely summable majorant for pressure blocks at every derivative order.
TorusEuler.summable_pressureNearBlockMas.summary: Dyadic half moments form a summable geometric sequence

TorusEuler.summable_pressureNearBlock_ap.text: For a smooth periodic tensor field, the complex values of its pressure blocks are summable at every spatial point. Compact periodicity supplies the input bounds at orders zero and one; the order-zero block estimate dominates the terms by a summable half-moment sequence. This is used to identify the dyadic sum by uniqueness of limits.
TorusEuler.summable_pressureNearBlock_ap.summary: Smooth periodic data have a convergent pressure block series

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_bilinear_d.text: For a bounded bilinear map `B`, uniform convergence of `U j` to a continuous limit on the compact interval implies uniform convergence of `B (U j) (U j)`. Compactness supplies a uniform bound for the limiting curve. The proof controls the two factors separately, rather than treating a quadratic map as globally uniformly continuous.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_bilinear_d.summary: Uniform convergence passes through a bounded quadratic expression

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_clm_apply_.text: Suppose the operator fields `A` and vector fields `v` converge uniformly on `s` to `B` and `w`. Uniform nonnegative bounds `C` and `M` for the two limits ensure that their applications converge uniformly too. The bounds are explicit hypotheses; uniform convergence alone on an unbounded domain would not supply them.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_clm_apply_.summary: Uniformly converging factors give a uniformly converging product

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_cutoff_smu.text: For a compact cell `C`, a fixed smooth cutoff supported off the lattice, and fields $C^m$ there, convergence of their jets through order $m$ on `C ∩ tsupport χ` implies convergence of the cutoff-product jets on all of `C`. A finite Leibniz sum is bounded on the compact cell; outside the support both products vanish locally.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_cutoff_smu.summary: Local convergence on cutoff support becomes global cell convergence

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_dyadicPeri.text: On a compact punctured set, finite sums of periodic dyadic block derivatives converge uniformly to the corresponding derivative of the full kernel. Absolute summability over the product index justifies regrouping scales and lattice translates. This uniform derivative convergence is used when identifying the far integral with the bounded Fourier multiplier.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_dyadicPeri.summary: Finite dyadic sums converge with every derivative off the lattice

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_eulerAdvec.text: On a compact space-time set `K`, assume uniform convergence of the velocities and their displayed spatial `fderiv` fields, together with continuity of the limiting fields. Then the corresponding advection expressions converge uniformly. The theorem uses these derivative expressions as supplied; it does not derive differentiability or the derivative convergence from velocity convergence alone.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_eulerAdvec.summary: Pass to the limit in the advection expression

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_farKernelI.text: A common kernel norm bound over the observation set turns convergence to zero of the integral density error into uniform convergence of far-kernel outputs. Every density and the limit must be integrable, and each kernel action must be measurable. The result is uniform in the observation point because its bound does not depend on that point.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_farKernelI.summary: Integral source convergence gives uniform far-field convergence

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_farKernelI.text: Uniform convergence of continuous velocities on a compact source set gives uniform convergence of a bounded measurable far-kernel integral of their tensors. The limit velocity is continuous too, so all tensor densities are integrable. The kernel bound is uniform over the target, and the source measure is locally finite.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_farKernelI.summary: Continuous velocity limits control the far pressure field

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_farKernel_.text: For an open target region and compact source set, uniform convergence of continuous velocities passes to the actual derivatives of the far contribution through every prescribed finite order. The kernel jet tower must be measurable, uniformly bounded, and compatible under differentiation. The theorem also proves regularity of the limiting far field; the near pressure contribution is handled separately.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_farKernel_.summary: Global velocity convergence controls every separated pressure derivative

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_iteratedFD.text: On a compact set inside an open neighborhood, uniform convergence of both input jet towers through order `d` gives convergence of the order `d` derivative after a fixed bounded bilinear map. The approximants need only eventually be $C^d$ on the neighborhood. The proof preserves the order of the two arguments in the bilinear error decomposition.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_iteratedFD.summary: Local derivative convergence passes through bilinear products

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_iteratedFD.text: For a localized profile transported by an origin-fixing Lipschitz lattice-equivariant flow, assumes `S` stays a common positive distance beyond the transported support radius. Then every fixed directional derivative of its cutoff converges uniformly to zero on `S` as the cutoff scale grows. The continuous torus representative is supplied explicitly, and the conclusion concerns a fixed time and profile.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_iteratedFD.summary: Localized cutoff tails vanish beyond the transported support

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_iteratedFD.text: Uniform convergence of order `d+1` derivatives implies convergence of order `d` derivatives of the Fréchet derivative map. The proof uses the canonical currying isometry for multilinear maps. This is a representation identity for totalized derivative operators and needs no extra smoothness hypothesis of its own.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_iteratedFD.summary: A higher jet identifies the corresponding gradient jet

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_iteratedFD.text: Uniform convergence of scalar derivatives of order `d+1` implies uniform convergence of gradient derivatives of order `d` on the same set. Currying and the Riesz identification are continuous linear maps. The result is a representation statement and does not independently assume or prove smoothness of the scalar fields.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_iteratedFD.summary: One additional scalar derivative controls gradient convergence

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_iteratedFD.text: For a fixed bounded periodic field that vanishes in balls of a common radius around every point of `S`, each fixed directional derivative of its cutoff converges uniformly to zero on `S` as the scale tends to infinity. The proof chooses moment order `m+1`, leaving a reciprocal-scale bound. No compactness of `S` is required once the common gap is given.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_iteratedFD.summary: Cutoff derivatives vanish uniformly beyond a common support gap

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_iteratedFD.text: On a compact set off the lattice, uniform convergence of every velocity jet to those of a locally smooth limit implies uniform convergence of each quadratic tensor jet. Both approximants and limit are smooth off the lattice. Compactness bounds the limit jets, and the difference is split into two bilinear terms each containing a small velocity-jet error.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_iteratedFD.summary: Velocity jet convergence passes to the quadratic tensor

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_lift_farPr.text: Under the same continuous cutoff, separation and uniform velocity hypotheses, far pressure multipliers represented by half Hölder tensors converge in each gradient jet on the compact target. The torus representatives need match the cutoff tensors only eventually along the filter. Their limit is expressed by the actual kernel integral of the terminal tensor, without requiring a half Hölder representative of that limit.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_lift_farPr.summary: The far Fourier pressure inherits the kernel jet limit

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_nearPressu.text: For a fixed smooth cutoff supported off the lattice, convergence of every velocity jet on every compact off-origin set yields convergence of all near tensor jets on the centered cell. The proof first forms tensor jets on the compact intersection with the cutoff support, then extends convergence across the cell using cutoff multiplication.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_nearPressu.summary: Compact local velocity limits give near tensor limits on the cell

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_periodicFa.text: For continuous velocities converging uniformly on a compact source set separated from the compact target, integration against the actual periodic kernel gives convergence of every prescribed far-field derivative on an open target neighborhood. The theorem also proves regularity of the limiting field. A bounded bilinear tensor map and output action are retained as explicit inputs.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_periodicFa.summary: The constructed periodic kernel carries velocity limits to far jets

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_periodicFa.text: Continuous velocities converging uniformly on a compact source set give uniform convergence of the actual far pressure gradient derivatives through order `m` on an open neighborhood of a separated compact target. The scalar kernel theorem is applied at order `m+1`, then the gradient representation removes one stored scalar derivative.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_periodicFa.summary: Uniform velocity convergence gives all far pressure gradient limits

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_periodicPr.text: Uniform convergence of completed velocity tuples through order two, together with continuity of the limiting tuple, gives uniform time convergence of signed projected momentum at a fixed spatial point. The argument uses the bounded quadratic map and zeroth evaluation. The conclusion is pointwise in space, although the jet hypotheses use spatial uniform norms.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_periodicPr.summary: Two orders of jet convergence pass through projected momentum

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_periodicVe.text: Uniform convergence of actual derivatives through order `m` for smooth periodic inputs gives uniform convergence of their completed compatible jet tuples. The proof applies the finite component comparison and the inherited subtype metric. It does not require convergence of derivatives above the finite order being stored.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_periodicVe.summary: Actual derivative convergence passes to the completed jet norm

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_spatialHol.text: Uniform convergence of derivatives through order `m+1` on the time set and the entire lift implies uniform convergence to zero of the order `m` half Hölder norm of the difference. Smooth spatial slices are assumed for both approximants and limit. A finite simultaneous error estimate feeds the previous quantitative comparison.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_spatialHol.summary: Convergence of one extra derivative gives Hölder convergence

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_spatialJet.text: If every evaluated component of a finite bounded jet tuple converges uniformly over time and all spatial points, the tuples converge uniformly in their product norm. Finiteness allows the componentwise eventual estimates to hold simultaneously. The statement is a norm comparison and does not require the tuple entries to be compatible derivatives.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_spatialJet.summary: Uniform component convergence gives convergence of finite tuples

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_spatial_fd.text: Uniform convergence of the first iterated spatial derivatives implies uniform convergence of the ordinary Fréchet derivatives on the same time and space set. The proof applies the canonical isometry between one argument continuous multilinear maps and continuous linear maps. This changes only the representation of the derivative, with no added regularity hypothesis.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_spatial_fd.summary: The first multilinear jet gives derivative convergence

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_terminal_o.text: A jointly continuous field on $[0,T]\times K$, with $K$ compact and $T\ge0$, converges uniformly on $K$ to its value at $T$ along the preterminal filter. Compactness turns continuity into uniform continuity. At $T=0$ that filter has no preterminal points, so the conclusion is vacuous rather than an existence assertion.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformlyOn_terminal_o.summary: A continuous closed slab has a uniform terminal trace

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformly_lift_smoothF.text: A smooth cutoff symbol `ψ` supported in the radius-two ball and satisfying `ψ 0 = 1` gives uniform convergence of its cutoffs at scales `n+1` to any continuous torus field lifted to Euclidean space. The proof uses its integrable Schwartz kernel and mass-one normalization. It does not assume absolute convergence of the original Fourier series.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformly_lift_smoothF.summary: Smooth spectral cutoffs converge uniformly on the periodic lift

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformly_of_spatially.text: If every approximating field and the limiting field are periodic, uniform convergence on `centeredCell` implies uniform convergence on all of `Vec3`. Every point can be translated into that cell without changing any of the values being compared. The period hypothesis for the limit is required explicitly.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformly_of_spatially.summary: Convergence on one cell controls the entire periodic lift

TorusEuler.tendstoUniformly_pressureTens.text: Smooth periodic tensors whose every spatial jet converges uniformly on the centered cell to those of a smooth periodic limit have globally uniformly convergent pressure jets. For output order $d$, only input orders $d$ and $d+1$ determine the eventual error. Periodicity propagates their small cell errors globally, and pressure linearity allows estimating the difference.
TorusEuler.tendstoUniformly_pressureTens.summary: Convergent tensor jets give globally convergent pressure jets

TorusEuler.tendsto_atTop_of_activationBo.text: If activation times converge to `T` from below and a sequence of lower bounds tends to infinity, eventual uniform lower bounds throughout each half-open successive interval force `f` to tend to infinity from the left at `T`. Monotonicity of the times is not assumed: the proof finds the first later crossing of each nearby time.
TorusEuler.tendsto_atTop_of_activationBo.summary: Bounds on successive intervals give a full terminal limit

TorusEuler.tendsto_halfHolder_torusTrans.text: As nonzero `h` tends to zero, translation by the torus image of `h • u` converges to the original field in the value supremum norm.
