The half-Hölder increment estimate gives this directly. The theorem does not claim convergence in the complete half-Hölder norm, whose difference-quotient component need not vanish under translation.
TorusEuler.tendsto_halfHolder_torusTrans.summary: Small directional translations converge uniformly to the field

TorusEuler.tendsto_intervalIntegral_of_u.text: Continuous curves converging uniformly on $[0,T]$ have integrals from zero to any slab time converging to the integral of the continuous limit. The proof bounds the integral of the difference by the interval length times the uniform error. This helper needs no derivative convergence and is used for the nonlinear term and vanishing residual separately.
TorusEuler.tendsto_intervalIntegral_of_u.summary: Uniform convergence passes through a time integral

TorusEuler.tendsto_l1_farPressureCutoffT.text: On a compact source set, uniformly convergent continuous velocities with continuous limit give convergence to zero of the integral norm of the far tensor difference, provided $0\le\chi\le1$. This isolated lemma imposes no measurability on $\chi$, so its conclusion concerns the totalized integral expression. The later pressure application assumes a continuous cutoff and proves genuine integrability.
TorusEuler.tendsto_l1_farPressureCutoffT.summary: Uniform velocity convergence controls the cutoff norm integral

TorusEuler.tendsto_l1_tensor_of_uniform_.text: Uniform convergence on a compact set of finite measure, with continuous limit, makes the integral of the tensor difference norm tend to zero. The tensor map is bounded bilinear. The theorem does not itself assume measurable approximants; genuine integrability is supplied by continuity in its subsequent far-kernel application, avoiding reliance on the totalized integral.
TorusEuler.tendsto_l1_tensor_of_uniform_.summary: Uniform velocity convergence makes the tensor error integral vanish

TorusEuler.tendsto_nearPressure_of_bound.text: Given a bounded bilinear tensor map and bounded linear cutoff, divergence and Leray maps, convergence of velocities in `V` implies convergence of the signed near nonlinearity in `E`. The maps are explicit inputs; the theorem does not establish their boundedness for a particular norm. It applies continuity of the diagonal tensor map followed by those linear maps.
TorusEuler.tendsto_nearPressure_of_bound.summary: Bounded nonlinear and linear maps preserve the near limit

TorusEuler.tendsto_operatorLiftConvoluti.text: At each Euclidean point, partial sums of the scaled-kernel lift convolutions tend to the value of the certified dyadic multiplier at the corresponding torus point. The proof evaluates convergence of the continuous-function series. Its conclusion is pointwise convergence of these partial sums, with uniform convergence available from the earlier summability result.
TorusEuler.tendsto_operatorLiftConvoluti.summary: Finite sums of lifted convolutions converge to the multiplier value

TorusEuler.tendsto_sup_norm_zero_of_tend.text: For an arbitrary filtered family, eventual boundedness of the full half-Hölder norm and convergence of its Haar $L^2$ norm to zero imply convergence of the value supremum norm to zero. Local averaging supplies the interpolation estimate. The conclusion deliberately concerns `val.1`; it does not claim convergence of the Hölder seminorm itself.
TorusEuler.tendsto_sup_norm_zero_of_tend.summary: Uniform Hölder control upgrades L2 convergence to uniform convergence

TorusEuler.tendsto_torusDifference_coeff.text: Assume the difference quotients of `B` are eventually bounded in half-Hölder norm by `‖dB‖` and converge to `dB` in supremum norm. Multiplying them by the translated fixed field `v` then converges uniformly to `dB v`. This validates the coefficient-error limit without requiring the difference quotients to converge in full Hölder norm.
TorusEuler.tendsto_torusDifference_coeff.summary: The differentiated coefficient product converges uniformly

TorusEuler.tensorDivergenceMode.text: The tensor divergence at frequency `k` is the vector whose component `i` sums the derivative symbol in coordinate `j` times tensor entry `(i,j)`. It is the single-divergence part of the pressure and Leray mode comparison. The formula is finite and keeps the two coordinate roles explicit.
TorusEuler.tensorDivergenceMode.summary: A Fourier derivative contracts one tensor index

TorusEuler.terminalBorelAtom.text: Defines the atom $\varepsilon^n b_n(t/\varepsilon)$ from the fixed cutoff monomial. For positive scale it retains the normalized polynomial near zero while shrinking support and controlling lower derivatives. The raw definition is total at every real scale; positivity is a hypothesis of the subsequent jet and scaling theorems.
TorusEuler.terminalBorelAtom.summary: Shrinking the support of a prescribed time jet

TorusEuler.terminalBorelAtom_eventuallyE.text: For $\varepsilon>0$, the rescaled atom and $t^n/n!$ agree eventually in the neighborhood filter of zero. Positivity ensures the rescaled argument remains inside the bump’s unit region near zero and permits cancellation of powers of the scale. The equality is local, not an identity on the whole time axis.
TorusEuler.terminalBorelAtom_eventuallyE.summary: The atom agrees with its polynomial near zero

TorusEuler.terminalBorelBase.text: Multiplies $t^n/n!$ by the fixed bump. Near zero it agrees with the normalized monomial, while away from zero its support is compact. The degree `n` is any natural number, including zero. Its normalization makes the derivative of order `n` at zero equal to one.
TorusEuler.terminalBorelBase.summary: A normalized time monomial with compact support

TorusEuler.terminalBorelBump.text: Chooses the scalar smooth bump with center zero, inner radius one and outer radius two. It equals one near the endpoint and vanishes outside its support radius. This fixed bump is the building block for normalized time monomials; the shrinking radii used in the Borel series are chosen later.
TorusEuler.terminalBorelBump.summary: A fixed smooth cutoff near the time origin

TorusEuler.terminalBoundaryTimeJet.text: Evaluates the ambient iterated within derivative at `(T,y)` repeatedly in the pure time direction `(1,0)`. It packages the boundary data as a spatial function for each order. No regularity is assumed by the definition; the following theorem proves these spatial functions smooth from smoothness on a nondegenerate closed slab.
TorusEuler.terminalBoundaryTimeJet.summary: The normal Taylor data on a terminal slice

TorusEuler.terminalCurl_tendsto_atTop_of.text: Assume $t_j\to T$, every $t_j<T$, lower bounds $b_j\to\infty$ and errors $e_j\to0$. For every sufficiently large $j$ and every $r\in[t_j,t_{j+1})$, suppose $|\operatorname{curl}U_j(r,0)|\ge b_j$ and $\|\nabla u(r,0)-\nabla U_j(r,0)\|\le e_j$. Then $|\operatorname{curl}u(r,0)|\to\infty$ as $r\uparrow T$ within $[0,T)$. The loss is at most $Ce_j$, where $C$ is the norm of the fixed matrix-to-curl map. Monotonicity of the activation sequence is not an explicit hypothesis. The bounds must hold throughout each sufficiently late interval, not merely at its endpoints. The result does not establish integral divergence or any Euler equation. At a spatial point without a derivative, the derivative expression is assigned zero; this convention does not assert differentiability.
TorusEuler.terminalCurl_tendsto_atTop_of.summary: Interval bounds pass to the limit when derivative errors vanish

TorusEuler.terminalCutoffStress.text: The stress is the tensor product of the two cutoff velocities minus the cutoff of their original tensor product: $Sg\otimes Sh-S(g\otimes h)$. It is unprojected and contains no divergence. This grouping makes time differentiation a bilinear Leibniz sum, whose terms can be estimated independently before applying divergence and the Leray projection.
TorusEuler.terminalCutoffStress.summary: The bilinear difference between cutoff tensor products

TorusEuler.terminalCutoffStress_differen.text: The stress built from two continuous torus inputs is differentiable as a field on $\mathbb R^3$. No positivity of the cutoff radius or regularity of the multiplier is needed for this algebraic statement: the implemented cutoff is a finite Fourier synthesis. Approximation estimates later add the multiplier and radius hypotheses that make it a genuine cutoff.
TorusEuler.terminalCutoffStress_differen.summary: The cutoff stress is spatially differentiable

TorusEuler.terminalCutoffStress_div_sum.text: Spatial differentiation followed by `momentumTensorDivergence` commutes with the finite binomial sum of cutoff stresses. The factors `U j` and `U (q - j)` are independent continuous torus inputs. Their Fourier cutoffs are smooth, so differentiating the sum is legitimate; the divergence contraction is a continuous linear map. No time regularity is claimed by this algebraic identity.
TorusEuler.terminalCutoffStress_div_sum.summary: Divergence distributes over the differentiated stress sum

TorusEuler.terminalCutoffStress_periodic.text: For arbitrary multiplier `ψ`, radius `Λ`, and continuous torus fields `g` and `h`, the lifted cutoff stress is spatially periodic. Every term depends on the point through its image in the unit torus. This provides the periodicity required when applying the Leray estimate to the divergence of the differentiated stress.

TorusEuler.terminalCutoffStress_smooth.text: If `g` represents a jointly smooth velocity on a positive-length slab, the self-stress formed from `g t` is jointly smooth in time and space there. Both the tensor of cutoff velocities and the cutoff momentum tensor are shown smooth. Their difference can therefore be differentiated repeatedly in the residual identity without relying on default derivatives.
TorusEuler.terminalCutoffStress_smooth.summary: The quadratic cutoff stress is jointly smooth

TorusEuler.terminalCutoffTailCost.text: This selects the order-`depth` uniform Hölder tail constant of the Schwartz kernel belonging to the fixed dyadic multiplier. It depends on the derivative depth and the chosen cutoff, not on a stage, a solution, or its frequency radius. Later scheduling estimates must dominate this cost; the definition itself contains no such domination.

TorusEuler.terminalCutoffTailCost_nonneg.text: Every natural cutoff depth has a nonnegative `terminalCutoffTailCost`. Unfolding the fixed-kernel absolute-moment formula proves the sign. This permits multiplication of a depth-norm bound by the tail cost when estimating the true child-minus-parent increment. It does not claim the cost is small or uniformly bounded as depth increases.
TorusEuler.terminalCutoffTailCost_nonneg.summary: The chosen dyadic tail cost is nonnegative

TorusEuler.terminalCutoffVector.text: This field evaluates the real vector Fourier cutoff at the image of `x` in the unit torus. It is the spatial operator used on each time jet of an approximate velocity or residual. The definition allows arbitrary `ψ` and `Λ`; it alone does not say the operation approximates the identity or preserves a particular frequency band.
TorusEuler.terminalCutoffVector.summary: Lift the vector Fourier cutoff to Euclidean space

TorusEuler.terminalCutoffVector_holder.text: For a smooth multiplier equal to one on the unit ball and zero beyond radius two, a positive cutoff radius, and a $C^{m,1/2}$ torus lift, the cutoff remains $C^{m,1/2}$. Its norm is bounded by one plus the order-`m` tail constant times the input norm. The argument adds the controlled cutoff difference back to the original field.
TorusEuler.terminalCutoffVector_holder.summary: The Fourier cutoff preserves the spatial Hölder estimate

TorusEuler.terminalCutoffVector_nsmul.text: For a natural number `n`, cutting off `n • g` equals `n` times the cutoff of `g` at every torus point. This is proved by viewing the multiple as a finite sum of equal inputs. The identity moves binomial coefficients through the cutoff in the differentiated momentum tensor calculation.
TorusEuler.terminalCutoffVector_nsmul.summary: The Fourier cutoff respects natural scalar multiples

TorusEuler.terminalFlowTimeAmplitude.text: Defines a common amplitude using $g=AD(1+DA)^q$ and $c=Dg^q$, then taking $g+c+Dc$. These terms accommodate the material gradient, the deformation matrices, and the normalized transported covector. The expression depends on the fixed time order and parent scale and amplitude, while the spatial order is left to a separate constant.
TorusEuler.terminalFlowTimeAmplitude.summary: A common polynomial amplitude for the flow coefficients

TorusEuler.terminalGraphCostEnvelope.text: For a fixed row and spatial order and depth, sums the absolute graph costs over every time order `q ≤ s` and every parent velocity exponent `A ≤ s`. This converts a cost table with two order parameters into the single threshold parameter needed for scheduling. The finite envelope is chosen from the cost table; it does not depend on the later initial frequency.
TorusEuler.terminalGraphCostEnvelope.summary: One finite envelope includes the parent time exponent

TorusEuler.terminalGraphReadoutCost.text: This scalar collects the finite dimension factor, the repeated advection factor, the parent cost, and all four profile conversion costs. It includes `q.factorial` for extracting time derivatives and `exp 3` for the switch envelope. Keeping their complete product in one threshold entry is what allows a single remaining parent-frequency power after absorption.
TorusEuler.terminalGraphReadoutCost.summary: The full fixed-order scalar in the graph estimate

TorusEuler.terminalGraphReadoutPower.text: The remaining natural-number exponent is `1 + parentPower*q + max parentPower (q+profilePower)`. The first one pays for the whole fixed scalar cost, the product accounts for repeated advection, and the maximum covers the parent and extracted profile amplitudes. Neither the spatial reserve nor hierarchy depth appears among its arguments.
TorusEuler.terminalGraphReadoutPower.summary: The parent exponent left after graph-cost absorption

TorusEuler.terminalGraphReadoutScalars_l.text: Assume `μ ≥ 1`, a positive slab with `T⁻¹ ≤ μ`, `freq ≥ 1`, nonnegative profile coefficients, and the full graph cost at most `μ`. For `i ≤ q`, `m ≤ N`, `depth = 6*exponent`, and `next = freq^exponent`, the theorem bounds the mean, velocity, and residual scalar factors by one parent power. The mean retains `freq^(-5/2)` and the residual retains `next^(-4)`.
TorusEuler.terminalGraphReadoutScalars_l.summary: Absorb all graph scalars into one parent power

TorusEuler.terminalIteratedDerivWithin_c.text: On any set `s` with `UniqueDiffOn ℝ s`, a fixed continuous linear map $A$ commutes with every iterated within-set derivative of a smooth curve. The conclusion is `EqOn`, so it concerns points of `s` only. Applying this to evaluation, projection, or coordinate maps transfers actual time derivatives between the spaces used for the mean equation.
TorusEuler.terminalIteratedDerivWithin_c.summary: A fixed linear map commutes with time differentiation

TorusEuler.terminalIteratedDerivWithin_c.text: For smooth operator and vector curves on a set with unique derivatives, the $n$th derivative of $C(t)u(t)$ is the binomial sum of $C^{(i)}(t)u^{(n-i)}(t)$. The hypothesis `ht : t ∈ s` restricts evaluation to that set. Both factors must be smooth; the proof inducts using the first-order product rule and Pascal’s identity.
TorusEuler.terminalIteratedDerivWithin_c.summary: Time differentiation distributes over an operator applied to a curve

TorusEuler.terminalLabelTimeSeminormCost.text: Defines $(q+1)$ times the number of admissible label and phase derivative words through order `n`, multiplied by $\sum_{j=0}^n C(j)$. This is the finite coefficient used when raw mixed derivative bounds are transferred to the factorial time seminorm. The label-length condition absorbs the spatial power before this summation is applied.
TorusEuler.terminalLabelTimeSeminormCost.summary: Finite constants for the coefficient time norm

TorusEuler.terminalLabelTimeSeminormCost.text: Assuming every `C j` is nonnegative, proves the finite coefficient `terminalLabelTimeSeminormCost C q n` is nonnegative for all orders. It uses only positivity of the natural counts and the finite sum. No smoothness, scale separation, or actual profile bound is part of this arithmetic statement.
TorusEuler.terminalLabelTimeSeminormCost.summary: The coefficient time norm constant is nonnegative

TorusEuler.terminalLinearODECost.text: Defines constants recursively for the equation $g_t=B(f,g)$. At time order zero the spatial constant is `C₀`; the next order adds the old constant and the bilinear differentiation cost formed from the coefficient constants `C` and the preceding solution constants. The recursion depends on orders and the fixed bilinear map, not on the particular solution or frequency.
TorusEuler.terminalLinearODECost.summary: Constants for repeated differentiation of a linear equation

TorusEuler.terminalLinearODECost_nonneg.text: If both input spatial constant functions are nonnegative, every recursively defined linear-equation constant is nonnegative at every time and spatial order. The proof follows the recursion and the nonnegativity of the bilinear product cost. It does not require a differential equation, a solution, or a frequency parameter.

TorusEuler.terminalLogScale_tendsto_atTo.text: If a real frequency sequence tends to positive infinity, the shifted gain $4\log(\mathrm{freq}(j+1))$ also tends to positive infinity. There is no requirement that all earlier frequencies be positive; divergence gives eventual positivity. The index shift is retained explicitly because the induction reads gains from later frequencies.
TorusEuler.terminalLogScale_tendsto_atTo.summary: Diverging frequencies give diverging logarithmic gains

TorusEuler.terminalMaterialIterate.text: Applies the same operator `terminalMaterialStep a b U` exactly $q$ times to $f$. The parent velocity remains fixed as a function throughout this iteration, so differentiating products still differentiates its values. At order zero the result is $f$. Regularity and agreement with derivatives along trajectories are separate theorems.

TorusEuler.terminalMaterialIterate_succ.text: Rewrites order $q+1$ as one application of `terminalMaterialStep a b U` to the order-$q$ field. This is a function-iteration identity for arbitrary inputs, not an assertion of differentiability. It allows the proof along a label trajectory to use the chain rule at each successive order with the same parent velocity.
TorusEuler.terminalMaterialIterate_succ.summary: The next material derivative repeats the same operator

TorusEuler.terminalMaterialIterate_zero.text: The zeroth iterate of material differentiation is exactly the original field, as an equality of functions. There are no interval or regularity assumptions: this follows from zero iterations of an operator. It supplies the base case for the later smoothness induction and for the identity between material derivatives and trajectory derivatives.
TorusEuler.terminalMaterialIterate_zero.summary: Zero material derivatives leave the field unchanged

TorusEuler.terminalMaterialStep.text: Defines $D_t f=\partial_t f+D_xf(U)$ using `derivWithin` on $[a,b]$ and the spatial Fréchet derivative. The time derivative holds the Eulerian point fixed; the second term evaluates the spatial derivative on the parent velocity. This definition alone assumes neither smoothness nor a nondegenerate interval. Those hypotheses enter the pullback identities.
TorusEuler.terminalMaterialStep.summary: Material differentiation on the closed time interval

TorusEuler.terminalMeanChoosePositiveSum.text: The sum of $\binom{n+1}{i+1}$ over $0\le i\le n$ is at most $2^{n+1}$. This omits the zeroth-index term from the full binomial sum. It bounds the kinetic-coefficient derivatives on the right side of the higher mean equation, where the highest velocity derivative has already been moved to the left.
TorusEuler.terminalMeanChoosePositiveSum.summary: Positive-index binomial terms fit the same total bound

TorusEuler.terminalMeanChooseSum.text: The sum of the real casts of $\binom ni$ for $0\le i\le n$ is exactly $2^n$. Lean obtains this from the natural-number binomial identity. The equality bounds the number and weights of terms produced when differentiating a product in time, keeping that combinatorial cost dependent only on the chosen time order.
TorusEuler.terminalMeanChooseSum.summary: All binomial coefficients sum to a power of two

TorusEuler.terminalMeanCoefficientMul_je.text: For a smooth curve of half Hölder matrix coefficients on a positive-length interval, the $i$th time derivative of its multiplication operator is multiplication by the $i$th derivative of the coefficient. Evaluation is at `t ∈ Icc 0 T`. The reason is that `coefficientMulL` is a fixed continuous linear map between the corresponding Banach spaces.
TorusEuler.terminalMeanCoefficientMul_je.summary: Coefficient multiplication commutes with time derivatives

TorusEuler.terminalMeanGainPolynomial_le.text: Given polynomial bounds for $A,B,G,C$ in a scale `D ≥ 1`, this bounds $C(1+A(1+B))^{q+1}G$ by an explicit coefficient times $D^{(p+a)(q+1)+2a+e}Z$. The time order $q$ is fixed. The listed input caps are nonnegative, while $C$ itself needs only its supplied upper bound. This is scalar bookkeeping for the mean recurrence, not an estimate for a new solution.
TorusEuler.terminalMeanGainPolynomial_le.summary: The triangular mean estimate remains a parent polynomial

TorusEuler.terminalMeanProductWords_time.text: Suppose smooth word families $K,f,g$ have exact strong spatial derivative relations and `hEq` identifies the base field $g$ with $Kf$. If scaled time derivatives of $K,f$ through $q$ and word lengths through $N$ have bounds $A,B$, then the corresponding words of $g$ are bounded by $2^{N+1+q}AB$. The hypotheses require nonnegative scaling and caps; no extra spatial order is consumed.
TorusEuler.terminalMeanProductWords_time.summary: Mixed Leibniz words retain the available spatial order

TorusEuler.terminalMeanSpatialInverse_cl.text: Assumes the projected equation, coercivity, derivative families and inverse cap uniformly on $[0,T]$, with $T\ge0$. Continuous coefficient and source curves make their closed-time suprema valid pointwise bounds. For positive radius, their weighted norm hypotheses yield the same one-inverse-factor bound for the velocity's closed-time norm. No continuity assumption on the supplied velocity words is needed for this final supremum estimate.
TorusEuler.terminalMeanSpatialInverse_cl.summary: The mean inverse estimate is uniform on the closed slab

TorusEuler.terminalMeanSpatialInverse_ra.text: If the weighted coefficient is bounded by $H D^b\sqrt\ell$ and $A_{\rm inv}D^b\sqrt\ell\le1$, proves its projected contribution costs at most $2\|P\|H$ after multiplication by the inverse cap. The only sign hypotheses are $A_{\rm inv},H\ge0$. Although intended for positive-order coefficient words, this arithmetic theorem does not assume that the natural order is positive or that $\ell>0$.
TorusEuler.terminalMeanSpatialInverse_ra.summary: A radius threshold absorbs the coefficient inverse loss

TorusEuler.terminalMeanSpatialInverse_wo.text: Under the fixed-time inverse and derivative hypotheses, assumes all weighted source words through order $N$ are bounded by $B$ and every positive-order coefficient word, including its inverse factor, costs at most $C$. For $\ell\ge0$, the velocity word bound is $A_{\rm inv}\|P\|B(1+2^NC)^{|q|}$. Only one leading inverse factor remains, because the smaller-radius coefficient hypothesis has absorbed the others.
TorusEuler.terminalMeanSpatialInverse_wo.summary: The spatial hierarchy keeps one leading inverse factor

TorusEuler.terminalMeanSpatialInverse_wo.text: Given a coercive kinetic coefficient, a supplied continuous linear inverse equivalence with norm cap, the projected base equation and genuine coefficient, source and velocity derivative families through order $N$, bounds every velocity word by its source plus lower velocity words multiplied by positive-order coefficient words. The ordered product rule retains its multiplicities. The theorem uses the supplied inverse; it does not construct an inverse from coercivity alone.
TorusEuler.terminalMeanSpatialInverse_wo.summary: Each mean derivative obeys a triangular inverse estimate

TorusEuler.terminalMeanTimeBound.text: This scalar induction works for any bound predicate `V i C` monotone in $C$. If order zero holds at $AG$ and each next order is bounded by $A(G+BC)$ from all lower orders, then order $i\le q$ holds at $(1+A(1+B))^{i+1}G$. Nonnegativity of $A,B,G$ is explicit. No differential equation or inverse is constructed here.
TorusEuler.terminalMeanTimeBound.summary: A triangular time recurrence gives a geometric bound

TorusEuler.terminalMeanWeightedSum_norm_.text: If every summand has scaled norm $a\|f_i\|\le B$ with $a\ge0$, then the scaled norm of the finite natural-weighted sum is at most $B$ times the sum of its weights. No positivity assumption on $B$ is separately needed. This converts time Leibniz sums into scalar binomial totals in the mean bounds.
TorusEuler.terminalMeanWeightedSum_norm_.summary: Bound a natural-weighted sum in half Hölder norm

TorusEuler.terminalMeanWordDeriv_add_sub.text: Given three strong derivative relations in the same direction, the derivative relation for $a+b-c$ has value $a\prime+b\prime-c\prime$. This follows from linearity in the half Hölder space. The auxiliary mean recurrence uses it to combine the differentiated vorticity product, the forcing term, and the kinetic commutator terms.
TorusEuler.terminalMeanWordDeriv_add_sub.summary: Strong spatial derivatives preserve addition and subtraction

TorusEuler.terminalMeanWordDeriv_sum.text: If each pair of half Hölder fields satisfies the strong spatial derivative relation in direction $u$, the same relation holds for their finite sums weighted by natural numbers `k i`. The proof combines linearity with repeated addition. These weights represent the binomial coefficients appearing after time differentiation of the mean equation.
TorusEuler.terminalMeanWordDeriv_sum.summary: Strong spatial derivatives pass through weighted finite sums

TorusEuler.terminalMeanWordProduct.text: Defines the complete word product as the undifferentiated coefficient acting on the velocity word, plus every ordered product-rule term with positive coefficient order. Keeping the correction list preserves multiplicities of repeated derivative choices. For arbitrary coefficient and velocity families this is just an algebraic field; genuine derivative interpretation requires the subsequent coherence hypotheses.
TorusEuler.terminalMeanWordProduct.summary: The full ordered product includes the undifferentiated coefficient

TorusEuler.terminalMeanWordProduct_close.text: For $T\ge0$ and positive radius, continuous coefficient and velocity word curves with uniform weighted closed-time bounds $K,V$ give the same product bound $2^{|w|+1}KV$ in the closed-time norm. Continuity supplies bounded source suprema, and the nonempty interval lets the pointwise estimate pass to its supremum. Positive radius is used when dividing by its target-order power.
TorusEuler.terminalMeanWordProduct_close.summary: The weighted product bound holds uniformly in time

TorusEuler.terminalMeanWordProduct_nil.text: At the empty derivative word, the full product reduces to the undifferentiated coefficient multiplying the undifferentiated velocity. The positive-coefficient correction list is empty, so its sum is zero. This establishes the base value for identifying the recursively generated products with genuine spatial derivatives.
TorusEuler.terminalMeanWordProduct_nil.summary: The empty word is the original coefficient product

TorusEuler.terminalMeanWordProduct_norm_.text: For nonnegative radius and bounds $K,V$ on all weighted coefficient and velocity words through the target length, proves the weighted product norm is at most $2^{|w|+1}KV$. One factor of two comes from half-Hölder multiplication, while $2^{|w|}$ counts all binary placements of derivative letters. The bound is algebraic and does not require the families to be actual derivatives.
TorusEuler.terminalMeanWordProduct_norm_.summary: Every binary derivative choice contributes to the product bound

TorusEuler.terminalMeanWordProduct_spati.text: If the coefficient and velocity word families have the prescribed torus derivatives through order $N$, differentiating the product at a word of length below $N$ gives the product at the word with that direction prepended. The proof differentiates the coefficient action and every correction term, preserving the original ordered multiplicities. No commutation or deduplication of derivative words is assumed.
TorusEuler.terminalMeanWordProduct_spati.summary: The ordered products are genuine spatial derivatives

TorusEuler.terminalMeanWords_timeJet_bou.text: Assume smooth coefficient, forcing, and solenoidal velocity word families, their spatial derivative relations, the higher projected equations `hEq`, a genuine bounded fixed-time inverse, coercivity, and the stated coefficient and zeroth-order caps. The source bound `hGcap` uses only $i<q$; the conclusion controls velocity time orders $i\le q$ without enlarging the word length $N$. Its explicit bound is $(1+A(1+B))^{i+1}G$, with $A,B$ defined from those caps.
TorusEuler.terminalMeanWords_timeJet_bou.summary: The mean gains one time order from its source

TorusEuler.terminalMixedJetBound_inv_nor.text: For a smooth nowhere-zero covector `κ` on `a < b`, mixed bounds for `κ` and spatial bounds for $(\|\kappa\|^2)^{-1}$ at time order zero produce the corresponding reciprocal bounds through `q`. The inner product first controls the squared length with amplitude `A*A`; the scalar reciprocal theorem then applies. All scale, amplitude, and cost sign assumptions are explicit.
TorusEuler.terminalMixedJetBound_inv_nor.summary: Control the reciprocal squared length of the normalized covector

TorusEuler.terminalMixedJetBound_of_line.text: For smooth fields on `a < b` satisfying `hODE : g_t = B(f,g)`, combines a zeroth-time bound for `g` with a coefficient bound for `f` through order `q`. With `D ≥ 0`, `A ≥ 1`, and nonnegative remaining data, it obtains amplitude $A_0A^q$ and constants `terminalLinearODECost`. This uses the differentiated equation and the existing solution; it is neither an existence theorem nor a replacement for the initial spatial bound.
TorusEuler.terminalMixedJetBound_of_line.summary: Differentiate a linear equation using lower time orders

TorusEuler.terminalMixedJetBound_of_reci.text: On `a < b`, assume the coefficient is jointly smooth and nowhere zero, its mixed jets are bounded through `q`, and its reciprocal already has the stated spatial bound at time order zero. The reciprocal then has mixed bounds through `q` with the explicit recursive amplitude and cost. Nonnegative scales and costs are hypotheses. The proof uses $g_t=-f_tg^2$ and does not assume an unknown higher reciprocal jet.
TorusEuler.terminalMixedJetBound_of_reci.summary: Reciprocal time derivatives retain the same spatial slope

TorusEuler.terminalMixedProductCost.text: Defines the spatial binomial convolution $2^q\|B\|\sum_{j=0}^n\binom nj C(j)C'(n-j)$ for a fixed bounded bilinear map `B`. The factor $2^q$ bounds the sum of time-binomial coefficients through order `q`. This constant records derivative distribution only; amplitudes and powers of the spatial scale are supplied separately in the product estimate.
TorusEuler.terminalMixedProductCost.summary: Constants for the mixed derivative product rule

TorusEuler.terminalMixedProductCost_nonn.text: For nonnegative spatial constant functions `C` and `C'`, proves the mixed product constant is nonnegative at every time and spatial order. The operator norm, binomial coefficients, and $2^q$ are already nonnegative. This is the sign fact used when comparing amplitudes in the bilinear and material-derivative estimates.
TorusEuler.terminalMixedProductCost_nonn.summary: The mixed product constant is nonnegative

TorusEuler.terminalPiecewise.text: Defines the piecewise field to equal `f` when time is nonpositive and `g` when time is positive. In particular its value at zero comes from `f`. Continuity or differentiability across that boundary is not built into the expression; matching values and derivatives must be proved before using the smooth gluing result.
TorusEuler.terminalPiecewise.summary: Choosing the left field at the time boundary

TorusEuler.terminalPiecewise_contDiffOn_.text: Under `a < 0`, an open spatial domain, smoothness on both closed half-slabs and matching time jets of every order, proves the piecewise field is $C^k$ on the combined slab. The proof inducts on `k`, upgrading the matching data to derivative-valued jets. The hypotheses are all-order even when the requested conclusion is one finite order.
TorusEuler.terminalPiecewise_contDiffOn_.summary: Smooth gluing at each finite derivative order

TorusEuler.terminalPiecewise_hasFDerivWi.text: Given smooth fields on the two half-slabs with equal values and full within derivatives on their common boundary, the piecewise field has the piecewise derivative on the combined slab. This is a derivative-existence statement, not yet all-order smoothness. It handles the boundary by combining the one-sided derivative estimates and handles interior points by local equality.
TorusEuler.terminalPiecewise_hasFDerivWi.summary: Matching first derivatives differentiates the glued field

TorusEuler.terminalProjectedHigherTimeDe.text: Let $P:Y\to X$ be bounded linear, with $X$ real normed and $Y$ real Banach. For smooth operator curves $K,\Omega:X\to Y$ and smooth curves $v,g$ on $[0,T]$, $T>0$, assume $P(Kv)=c+P\int_0^t(\Omega v+g)$. The formal statement isolates $P(Kv^{(n+1)})$ as $P[\sum_{i=0}^n\binom ni\Omega^{(i)}v^{(n-i)}+g^{(n)}-\sum_{i=0}^n\binom{n+1}{i+1}K^{(i+1)}v^{(n-i)}]$. Derivatives are taken within the closed interval. Only source derivatives through order $n$ occur. To obtain the auxiliary note's formula one must identify $P$ with the Leray projection and use $\Omega=K_t-\mathcal D$, then regroup the sums. These geometric identifications are not assumptions of this general identity.
TorusEuler.terminalProjectedHigherTimeDe.summary: The highest velocity derivative remains under the projection

TorusEuler.terminalProjectedTimeDerivati.text: Assume the integrated identity `hEq` for $P(K(t)v(t))$, with smooth $K,v$, continuous $\Omega,g$, and `0 < T`. Differentiating within $[0,T]$ gives $P\,\partial_t(Kv)=P(\Omega v+g)$. The source is needed only continuously at this stage. The constant initial trace $c$ disappears under differentiation; it is not replaced by a zero initial condition.
TorusEuler.terminalProjectedTimeDerivati.summary: Differentiate the integrated projected mean equation

TorusEuler.terminalRealAdjoint.text: Packages the real adjoint operation on linear maps of $\mathbb R^3$ as a continuous linear map. This permits the mixed-derivative bound machinery to treat transposition as a fixed linear operation with its operator norm as a cost. The real scalar field matters: over complex scalars, taking adjoints is conjugate linear.
TorusEuler.terminalRealAdjoint.summary: Take adjoints as a bounded linear operation

TorusEuler.terminalReciprocalTimeAmplitu.text: Starting from `B`, the amplitude at the next time order is `W + A * (W * W)`, where `W` is the previous amplitude. This mirrors the reciprocal identity $g_t=-f_t g^2$ while retaining the already bounded lower orders. It is a scalar cost function; it contains neither a reciprocal field nor a proof that one satisfies the bound.
TorusEuler.terminalReciprocalTimeAmplitu.summary: A polynomial amplitude for reciprocal time derivatives

TorusEuler.terminalReciprocalTimeAmplitu.text: If `A` and `B` are nonnegative, every value of the reciprocal amplitude recurrence is nonnegative. The induction uses only sums and products of nonnegative numbers. This numerical result is needed when enlarging amplitudes in mixed-jet estimates, but it supplies no nonvanishing or smoothness information about a reciprocal field.
TorusEuler.terminalReciprocalTimeAmplitu.summary: Nonnegative inputs give a nonnegative reciprocal amplitude

TorusEuler.terminalReciprocalTimeCost.text: At time order zero the spatial cost is `C₀`. Each successor adds the previous cost to the bilinear cost for multiplying the derivative of the original coefficient by two copies of its reciprocal. The same spatial slope is retained, while factorial product constants are collected in a new function of spatial order.
TorusEuler.terminalReciprocalTimeCost.summary: Spatial costs through successive reciprocal time orders

TorusEuler.terminalReciprocalTimeCost_no.text: When both input spatial cost arrays are nonnegative, the reciprocal cost is nonnegative for every time and spatial order. The proof follows the recursive construction and uses nonnegativity of the mixed bilinear product cost. It is a property of the cost arrays alone and does not construct reciprocal estimates.
TorusEuler.terminalReciprocalTimeCost_no.summary: Nonnegative reciprocal costs remain nonnegative at every order

TorusEuler.terminalSpatialDerivative_ite.text: For two half Hölder curves that are $C^n$ on $[0,T]$, the supplied strong spatial derivative relation survives all within-time derivatives of order $m\le n$. The strict positivity of $T$ handles uniqueness at the endpoints. This theorem assumes the spatial relation and the time regularity of both curves; it does not infer them from pointwise bounds.
TorusEuler.terminalSpatialDerivative_ite.summary: Every available time derivative preserves the spatial relation

TorusEuler.terminalSpatialDerivative_of_.text: Assume `hSpatial` identifies $df(r)$ as the strong derivative of $f(r)$ in direction $u$ at every time. If both curves have genuine within-time derivatives `ft` and `dft` at $t\in[0,T]$, with `0 < T`, then `dft` is the strong spatial derivative of `ft`. The proof differentiates a difference-quotient integral identity in the half Hölder space.
TorusEuler.terminalSpatialDerivative_of_.summary: Time differentiation preserves a strong spatial derivative

TorusEuler.terminalTimeAntidiagonal_le.text: For nonnegative sequences `u` and `v`, summing $u_i v_j$ over $i+j\le q$ is at most the product of the two partial sums through `q`. The private proof embeds the triangular index set into the square of all pairs. No analytic convergence is involved: every sum is finite, and nonnegativity justifies adding the omitted pairs.
TorusEuler.terminalTimeAntidiagonal_le.summary: The triangular convolution is bounded by the full product

TorusEuler.terminalTimeConvolution_le.text: Let $T>0$, let $q$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $u_i,v_i\ge0$. Write $w_i=T^i/i!$. The formal statement proves $\sum_{n=0}^q w_n\sum_{i=0}^n\binom ni u_iv_{n-i}\le(\sum_{i=0}^q w_iu_i)(\sum_{j=0}^q w_jv_j)$. The factorial identity changes each weighted binomial coefficient into $w_iw_{n-i}$. The left sum then uses only pairs whose total order is at most $q$, whereas the product includes every pair with both orders at most $q$. Nonnegativity permits the enlargement. This is the scalar estimate behind the auxiliary product bound; applying it to profiles additionally requires the appropriate spatial product inequality.
TorusEuler.terminalTimeConvolution_le.summary: Factorial weights bound the full Leibniz sum

TorusEuler.terminalTimeJet.text: Abbreviates the $n$th iterated derivative of a Banach-valued curve within $[0,T]$. Unlike `slabTimeJet`, this takes a curve without a separate spatial argument, so it also describes time derivatives in a space of half Hölder fields. The abbreviation carries no regularity hypothesis; the surrounding product and projected-equation theorems provide one.
TorusEuler.terminalTimeJet.summary: Time derivatives on the endpoint interval

TorusEuler.terminalTimeJetWeight.text: The scalar coefficient of time order `i` is $T^i/i!$. Factorials compensate for binomial coefficients when the product rule is summed over all derivative orders up to `q`. The definition is available for every real `T`; positivity, which is needed to make the resulting weighted sum a seminorm, is established under `T > 0`.
TorusEuler.terminalTimeJetWeight.summary: Factorial weights for the time derivative norm

TorusEuler.terminalTimeJetWeight_mul_cho.text: For any real $T$ and integers $0\le i\le n$, the formal statement proves $(T^n/n!)\binom ni=(T^i/i!)(T^{n-i}/(n-i)!)$. The condition $i\le n$ ensures that natural-number subtraction agrees with the ordinary difference. Factorials are positive, so no zero denominator occurs. Unlike the later estimate for sums of norms, this algebraic identity does not require $T>0$ and is valid also at $T=0$. It explains the choice of factorial weights in the auxiliary time norms; it contains neither a product estimate for fields nor assumptions about the Euler construction.
TorusEuler.terminalTimeJetWeight_mul_cho.summary: The time weights cancel the binomial coefficient

TorusEuler.terminalTimeJetWeight_pos.text: If `hT : 0 < T`, then $T^i/i!$ is strictly positive for every natural `i`. The proof combines positivity of powers with positivity of natural factorials after casting to the reals. Strict positivity is used to extract an individual derivative from the time norm; nonnegativity alone is enough for summing inequalities.
TorusEuler.terminalTimeJetWeight_pos.summary: Positive slab duration makes every time weight positive

TorusEuler.terminalTimeJetWeight_zero.text: The weight for time order zero is exactly one for every real slab parameter `T`, since $T^0=1$ and $0!=1$. Consequently the time norm always includes the original spatial seminorm without scaling. This identity supplies the base case of the transverse time induction and the order-zero norm simplification.

TorusEuler.terminalTimeJet_coefficientMu.text: For smooth curves `K` and `v` in the coefficient and vector half-Hölder spaces on $[0,T]$, expands the `n`th time jet of their coefficient product as $\sum_{i=0}^n\binom ni K^{(i)}v^{(n-i)}$. The positive slab length and `ht` include endpoint derivatives. The equality is proved as an identity of Hölder fields, not just a numerical norm estimate.
TorusEuler.terminalTimeJet_coefficientMu.summary: Hölder coefficient products obey the time Leibniz rule

TorusEuler.terminalTimeJet_coefficientMu.text: For a smooth half-Hölder coefficient curve `K`, the time jet of its operator-valued multiplication curve equals multiplication by the same time jet of `K`. The theorem assumes `T > 0` and a time in the closed slab. It uses linearity and boundedness of `coefficientMulL`, so no additional product terms occur until the operator is applied to a time-dependent vector field.
TorusEuler.terminalTimeJet_coefficientMu.summary: Differentiate the coefficient before forming its multiplication operator

TorusEuler.terminalTimeJet_halfHolder_ev.text: For a smooth time curve valued in `HalfHolder` and `T > 0`, evaluates its closed-slab time jet at a torus label by first evaluating the curve and then differentiating. Point evaluation is a bounded linear map on the Hölder space, which supplies the commutation. The statement includes `t = 0` and `t = T` through the within-time derivative.
TorusEuler.terminalTimeJet_halfHolder_ev.summary: Point evaluation commutes with Hölder valued time derivatives

TorusEuler.terminalTime_cutoff_depth_eve.text: For an `InductiveEulerParameters` schedule with `hInit : 1 < P.frequency 0`, any fixed spatial order `m` and real exponent eventually satisfy both cutoff depth inequalities. The threshold may depend on these fixed inputs. The proof uses growth of the frequencies to make the selected orders unbounded; it does not assert one starting index works simultaneously for all derivative orders.
TorusEuler.terminalTime_cutoff_depth_eve.summary: The prescribed depths eventually absorb fixed derivative costs

TorusEuler.terminalTime_cutoff_residual_.text: Assume `freq ≥ 2`, a nonnegative `exponent`, `next = freq ^ k`, `k ≥ 16 + 2 * exponent`, and both scalar costs at most `freq`. At cutoff radius $\mathrm{freq}^5$ and depth $6k$, the projected residual term and quadratic tail together are at most $\mathrm{next}^{-5/2}$. The proof bounds each by $\mathrm{next}^{-3}$ and absorbs their sum using `next ≥ 4`.
TorusEuler.terminalTime_cutoff_residual_.summary: Absorb both terms of the new residual bound

TorusEuler.terminalTime_cutoff_tail_rate.text: Let $\lambda\ge2$, let $C,\psi$ be real numbers with $C\le\lambda$, and let $m,P$ be nonnegative integers satisfying $5m+5+\psi\le3P$. The formal statement proves $C(\lambda^5)^{m-P}\lambda^{2(P+1)+\psi}\le\tfrac12\lambda^{-1}$. Here $m-P$ is an ordinary integer exponent, so a negative value denotes a reciprocal power. The declaration does not require $m\le P$ or $C\ge0$; those conditions enter the analytic tail application separately. This is the numerical step in the auxiliary truncation argument. It gives an explicit sufficient depth inequality at one stage, rather than itself proving that the inequality holds eventually along the schedule.
TorusEuler.terminalTime_cutoff_tail_rate.summary: A fixed depth inequality gives the half-size bound

TorusEuler.terminalTime_cutoff_velocity_.text: If `freq ≥ 2` and `C ≤ freq`, multiplication of $\mathrm{freq}^{2+\mathrm{exponent}}$ by `C` is bounded by $\mathrm{freq}^{\mathrm{exponent}+3}$. No lower bound on `C` or on the exponent is required for this scalar inequality. Its application uses a nonnegative cutoff cost already controlled by the schedule.
TorusEuler.terminalTime_cutoff_velocity_.summary: The cutoff velocity costs one further frequency power

TorusEuler.terminalTime_neBot.text: For T>0, the neighborhood filter 𝓝[Ico 0 T] T is not the bottom filter. Thus a terminal Tendsto statement is a genuine left-hand limit from physical times, rather than a limit along an empty approach. The proof uses that T lies in the closure of [0,T). It is a topology lemma supporting the interpretation of the paper’s t↑T limits.
TorusEuler.terminalTime_neBot.summary: Approaching the terminal time is nonvacuous

TorusEuler.terminalVelocityBound_of_exte.text: Let $w$ be continuous on $[0,T]\times[-1/2,1/2]^3$, and suppose $u(t,x)=w(t,x)$ there for $0\le t<T$. Then one finite constant bounds the essential supremum of $|u(t,x)|$ over that cube at every time before $T$. This follows from compactness of the closed time interval and spatial cell. Periodicity and the Euler equations are not hypotheses of this elementary assertion; they give its interpretation as a velocity bound on $\mathbb T^3$ in Proposition 8.2. Continuity and agreement with $w$ are assumed here, rather than established by this theorem.
TorusEuler.terminalVelocityBound_of_exte.summary: A continuous extension over one closed period bounds the velocity

TorusEuler.terminal_contDiffOn_materialI.text: For a nondegenerate closed interval and jointly smooth $U$ and $f$, every finite material iterate is jointly smooth on the same slab. Induction uses the previous preservation theorem and the zeroth-iterate identity. No quantitative norm bound or frequency information is concluded; these regularity facts make the subsequent chain-rule and product estimates applicable.
TorusEuler.terminal_contDiffOn_materialI.summary: All material derivatives remain jointly smooth

TorusEuler.terminal_contDiffOn_materialS.text: If `hab : a < b` and both $U$ and $f$ are jointly smooth on $[a,b]\times\mathbb R^3$, one material derivative of $f$ is jointly smooth there. The proof adds the smooth within-time derivative to the smooth spatial derivative applied to $U$. The strict interval hypothesis supplies uniqueness of derivatives at both endpoints.

TorusEuler.terminal_contDiffOn_spaceDeri.text: If `hab : a < b` and $f$ is jointly smooth, then $(t,x)\mapsto D_xf(t,x)$ is jointly smooth on the same closed slab. Lean first differentiates jointly within the slab and then restricts the resulting linear map to spatial directions. Nondegeneracy ensures uniqueness of the joint derivative used in that construction.
TorusEuler.terminal_contDiffOn_spaceDeri.summary: Spatial differentiation preserves joint smoothness on the slab

TorusEuler.terminal_contDiffOn_timeSlice.text: Joint smoothness on the slab gives within-interval smoothness of $t\mapsto f(t,x)$ for each fixed $x$. The proof composes with $t\mapsto(t,x)$. This is regularity relative to the closed time interval, not the choice of an extension across its endpoints; derivative identities at those endpoints are established by separate lemmas.
TorusEuler.terminal_contDiffOn_timeSlice.summary: Every fixed-point time curve is smooth within the interval

TorusEuler.terminal_contDiff_slice.text: A jointly smooth field on a closed slab has a smooth ordinary spatial slice at each time belonging to the interval. The proof is composition with the fixed-time inclusion and does not require positive interval length. This local helper is used when treating stage velocity and residual as continuous functions on the spatial torus.
TorusEuler.terminal_contDiff_slice.summary: Fixed-time slices preserve the stage field regularity

TorusEuler.terminal_contDiff_spaceSlice.text: A jointly smooth field on $[a,b]\times\mathbb R^3$ is smooth as a function of space at any `t ∈ Icc a b`. This follows by composition with $x\mapsto(t,x)$, whose image remains in the slab. No time derivative or quantitative bound is asserted, and the interval need not be nondegenerate for this spatial conclusion.
TorusEuler.terminal_contDiff_spaceSlice.summary: Every spatial slice of a smooth field is smooth

TorusEuler.terminal_derivWithin_fderiv_c.text: For a jointly smooth field and `a < b`, the within-time derivative of $D_xf$ equals the spatial derivative of the within-time derivative of $f$, at every time in $[a,b]$. The proof uses symmetry of the second Fréchet derivative and that the closed slab is the closure of its interior. Thus it includes both temporal endpoints.
TorusEuler.terminal_derivWithin_fderiv_c.summary: One time derivative commutes with spatial differentiation

TorusEuler.terminal_iteratedDerivWithin_.text: On a nondegenerate closed slab, a spatial Fréchet derivative commutes with the order-$q$ `slabTimeJet` of a jointly smooth field. The theorem is pointwise at `t ∈ Icc a b` and any spatial point. Induction uses joint smoothness of each time derivative and the one-step commutation theorem, so endpoint behavior is retained at every order.
TorusEuler.terminal_iteratedDerivWithin_.summary: All time derivatives commute with a spatial derivative

TorusEuler.terminal_poincare_integral.text: A path with continuous derivative on $[0,T]$ and `hterminal : f T = 0` satisfies $\int_0^T\|f\|^2\le(T^2/2)\int_0^T\|f'\|^2$. The theorem requires `0 ≤ T`, but neither initial vanishing nor `T ≤ 1`. It proves the classical-path estimate used before the paper extends the argument by density.
TorusEuler.terminal_poincare_integral.summary: Terminal vanishing controls the integrated displacement

TorusEuler.terminal_poincare_pointwise.text: Let $f$ be a path in a real Banach space on $[0,T]$, with $T\ge0$, a continuous derivative on that interval, and $f(T)=0$. For every $t\in[0,T]$, the formal theorem proves $|f(t)|^2\le(T-t)\int_0^T|f'(s)|^2\,ds$. The pointwise estimate displayed before (1.9) instead integrates from $t$ to $T$ and is therefore sharper. The proof obtains that sharper bound before enlarging the interval, but the exported conclusion is the weaker one stated here. Applying it to $f(t)=\xi(t,a)$ and then integrating in time and labels still requires the corresponding regularity and integrability hypotheses; those space-time steps are not this theorem’s conclusion.
TorusEuler.terminal_poincare_pointwise.summary: A vanishing endpoint controls the path by its derivative

TorusEuler.terminal_spatialHolderHalf_ns.text: If `hf` gives spatial $C^{m,1/2}$ regularity, multiplying the field by the natural number `n` preserves that regularity and bounds its norm by $n$ times the original norm. The proof uses the exact triangle estimate inductively. The natural scalar form matches the binomial coefficients in the differentiated cutoff stress.
TorusEuler.terminal_spatialHolderHalf_ns.summary: Natural multiples scale the spatial Hölder bound

TorusEuler.terminal_spatialHolderHalf_su.text: If each field indexed by the finite set `s` is spatially $C^{m,1/2}$, their sum has that regularity and norm at most the sum of the individual norms. Both regularity and the numerical estimate are concluded. Empty sums use the zero-field lemma, so no nonempty-set assumption is hidden in the aggregation.
TorusEuler.terminal_spatialHolderHalf_su.summary: Finite sums preserve the spatial Hölder bound

TorusEuler.terminal_spatialHolderHalf_ze.text: The zero vector field has spatial $C^{m,1/2}$ regularity and exactly zero spatial Hölder norm for every natural order `m`. The proof establishes the regularity predicate before simplifying the supremum-based formula. This supplies the empty-sum case when the cutoff residual estimate combines finitely many differentiated stress terms.

TorusEuler.terminal_waveRelayGeometry_co.text: If the inverse coframe `G` and strain `M` are jointly smooth on the slab, then their curl, material, and pressure-gradient relay rows are jointly smooth there for every fixed real `ell`. The proof uses their unit-width linear or bilinear formulas followed by fixed scalar multiplication. No nondegenerate-slab or positive-width assumption is needed merely to preserve smoothness.
TorusEuler.terminal_waveRelayGeometry_co.summary: The three geometric relay rows are jointly smooth

TorusEuler.theorem11.text: The formal assertion is the existence of smooth odd divergence-free periodic data $u_0$, a finite time $T_*>0$, and a smooth odd maximal Euler solution $u,p$ on $[0,T_*)$ with $u(0)=u_0$. It requires bounded velocity, central vorticity tending to infinity, divergence of the time integrals of the gradient and vorticity norms, and spatial $C^m$ limits of velocity and its time derivative on every compact set away from the torus origin. Pressure is normalized to have zero mean. The numbered version of Theorem 1.1 additionally states uniqueness of the maximal velocity and its lifespan. That comparison is not an explicit conjunct of this shorter assertion.
TorusEuler.theorem11.summary: The shorter theorem gives all stated singularity properties

TorusEuler.theorem11Witness_of_solution_.text: Packages a specified Euler solution and its assumed terminal behavior into an `EulerSingularityWitness` for its actual initial velocity. Oddness, bounded velocity, central curl blow-up, both off-origin limit statements and divergence of the curl integral are inputs. Maximality follows from central blow-up, and the gradient integral follows from the curl bound. This assembly does not construct those analytic hypotheses.
TorusEuler.theorem11Witness_of_solution_.summary: The terminal bounds certify the constructed solution

TorusEuler.theorem11_library.text: Proves `Theorem11` by choosing the established later-primary cost record and passing it through the uniform-stage construction and limit argument. This is the retained proof following the frozen manuscript of 18 November 2026. The current `TorusEuler.theorem11` instead projects the latest spine theorem; this declaration does not claim to follow that newer conditional-proof route or export its uniqueness clause.
TorusEuler.theorem11_library.summary: The retained direct proof gives the existence theorem

TorusEuler.theorem11_of_continuation_and.text: Let $u,p$ solve smooth periodic Euler on $[0,T)$, $T>0$, with mean-zero pressure and odd velocity. Assume uniformly bounded velocity, $|\operatorname{curl}u(t,0)|\to\infty$, and local $C^m$ terminal limits for both $u$ and $\partial_tu$ on every compact set avoiding the torus origin. Assume additionally that a finite vorticity integral would yield a smooth Euler continuation agreeing with $u$ to some $S>T$. The formal statement then gives the existence conclusion of Theorem 1.1, including both infinite integrals and maximality. The continuation criterion is an input, not a theorem proved here. The main Section 8 proof follows a different route, using quantitative vorticity estimates and crossing durations. This link therefore cannot certify the general periodic Beale–Kato–Majda criterion.
TorusEuler.theorem11_of_continuation_and.summary: A continuation criterion is an explicit hypothesis of this implication

TorusEuler.theorem11_of_inductiveEulerLo.text: Above a universal base-frequency threshold, lifetime bounds, a certified initial pair and a local compatible successor imply `Theorem11`. The proof first forms a common infinite family and then applies the terminal assembly. This is a conditional reduction of the headline theorem, not a standalone proof that the required local constructions exist.
TorusEuler.theorem11_of_inductiveEulerLo.summary: The local construction suffices for the headline theorem

TorusEuler.theorem11_of_inductiveEulerSt.text: Projects the singularity witness into `Theorem11`, once a compatible stage family, its central waves and a sufficiently large initial frequency have been supplied. The threshold is existential and uniform in the family. This conditional assembly belongs to the frozen library route and is distinct from the current unconditional paper-spine entry point.
TorusEuler.theorem11_of_inductiveEulerSt.summary: The stage construction implies the headline existence statement

TorusEuler.theorem11_of_laterPrimaryCost.text: A supplied later-primary cost record yields the frozen existence proposition `Theorem11` by first proving uniform physical estimates and then applying the schedule-and-limit theorem. This short theorem exposes the last hypothesis of the retained direct route. Its unconditional closure is `theorem11_library`, which supplies the cost record using the two analytic existence results.
TorusEuler.theorem11_of_laterPrimaryCost.summary: The later primary estimates complete the direct existence route

TorusEuler.theorem11_of_quantitative_act.text: An odd Euler solution with a continuous extension on the closed time-cell slab and off-origin limits for velocity and its time derivative satisfies `Theorem11` once monotone activation times converge from below and the stated frequency, gain, rate, delay, and curl-error bounds hold. Compactness bounds velocity, interval coverage gives central vorticity blowup, and interval mass gives integral divergence. The solution and extension are explicit hypotheses.
TorusEuler.theorem11_of_quantitative_act.summary: A supplied Euler solution inherits all terminal conclusions

TorusEuler.theorem11_of_solution_and_ter.text: Existentially packages the given solution, its lifespan and its initial velocity to prove the library statement `Theorem11`. All analytic conclusions needed for the witness are supplied in the hypotheses or derived by the preceding assembly. This declaration is conditional and does not assert uniqueness; the unconditional headline theorem and the paper’s uniqueness statement are separate declarations.
TorusEuler.theorem11_of_solution_and_ter.summary: The same terminal bounds imply the existence statement

TorusEuler.theorem11_of_uniformPhysicalE.text: Assumes the uniform physical stage estimates for a finite index type and concludes the existence proposition `Theorem11`. It chooses a numerical schedule large enough for the independent stage-to-limit theorem, constructs the corresponding stages and central waves, then applies that theorem. The uniform estimates remain a genuine hypothesis here; their construction occurs in the next module.
TorusEuler.theorem11_of_uniformPhysicalE.summary: Uniform physical estimates imply the frozen existence theorem

TorusEuler.thirdAxisSimp.text: Lists the three components of the third coordinate vector as $(0,0,1)$. The statement supplies the component simplifications for the arctangent term of the explicit seed. This direction carries the shear parameter in the first-wave amplitude, while the transported covector has no component in it.
TorusEuler.thirdAxisSimp.summary: Components of the third coordinate direction

TorusEuler.threeHundredTwenty_le_frequen.text: For `b ≥ 1`, every scheduled exponent $K(q)$ is at least $320$. The natural-number formula already contains the positive factor `q+1`, so no additional lower bound on `q` is needed. This estimate supplies generous numerical margins in the parent and residual frequency budgets.

TorusEuler.timeDerivative.text: For a velocity $u(t,x)$ and a real $T$, the formal definition differentiates $t\mapsto u(t,x)$ at fixed spatial point within the set $[0,T)$. When $T>0$ and $u$ is smooth on that slab, this is the usual time derivative for $0<t<T$ and the right derivative at $t=0$. The expression is defined even without differentiability, assigning zero when no derivative exists. It also has values at times outside the slab, which do not describe an Euler evolution there. Theorem 1.1 uses only its values before $T_*$ when asserting the off-origin spatial limit as $t\uparrow T_*$, not a derivative through the singular time.
TorusEuler.timeDerivative.summary: The time derivative is taken within the solution interval

TorusEuler.timeDerivative_eq_neg_momentu.text: At a time `t ∈ Ico 0 T`, the Euler equation in `h : IsEulerSolution T u p` gives $u_t=-Du\,u-\nabla p$ pointwise. The theorem only rearranges the existing momentum identity. It is used when subtracting the two Euler equations in the classical uniqueness energy estimate.
TorusEuler.timeDerivative_eq_neg_momentu.summary: The time derivative equals the negative Euler momentum

TorusEuler.timeDerivative_eq_of_prefix_d.text: If an evolution derivative identity holds on every earlier closed prefix, then `timeDerivative T u` equals its prescribed derivative throughout $[0,T)$. For each time the proof chooses a strictly later prefix endpoint still below $T$. That prefix is a within-neighborhood of the time, which justifies changing the derivative's domain.
TorusEuler.timeDerivative_eq_of_prefix_d.summary: Closed-prefix dynamics determine the half-open derivative

TorusEuler.timeEval.text: Defines the continuous linear map that evaluates a joint derivative on $(1,0)$. Its input is a linear map from time and space to the target, and its output is the corresponding time-direction vector. It performs no differentiation itself; it is used to extract time partials from the joint within-slab derivative.
TorusEuler.timeEval.summary: Read the time component of a joint derivative

TorusEuler.timeJet.text: Defines the order-$q$ time derivative of $r\mapsto f(r,p.2)$ within $[0,T]$, evaluated at `p.1`. The pair $p$ retains the fixed spatial coordinate during differentiation. This private operator belongs to the mixed-to-joint proof; it is distinct from the same-named profile operator, which acts on bundled twisted profiles.
TorusEuler.timeJet.summary: Time derivatives at a fixed point in product coordinates

TorusEuler.timeJet_eq_partialIterate.text: On a positive-length slab, the private fixed-spatial-point `timeJet` of a jointly smooth function agrees with repeated application of `timePartial`. The conclusion is equality only on the slab. Induction uses congruence of within-interval derivatives and the time-slice identification, allowing the norm proof to work with linear coordinate extraction.
TorusEuler.timeJet_eq_partialIterate.summary: Slice time derivatives equal iterated extracted partials

TorusEuler.timeJet_spatialPartial.text: For a jointly smooth function with `0 < T`, the order-$q$ fixed-point time derivative of its extracted spatial partial equals the spatial derivative of its order-$q$ time derivative. The equality is between spatial functions at a time in the interval. The proof combines commutation of extracted partials with their identification as actual slice derivatives.
TorusEuler.timeJet_spatialPartial.summary: Slice time derivatives commute with the extracted spatial partial

TorusEuler.timeJet_timePartial.text: At an allowed time on a positive-length slab, taking $q$ slice time derivatives of `timePartial T f` is the same as taking $q+1$ slice time derivatives of $f$. Joint smoothness is assumed. The proof identifies both sides with function iterates of the same extracted time-partial operator and uses the iteration law.
TorusEuler.timeJet_timePartial.summary: One extracted time partial raises the slice time order

TorusEuler.timeL2_norm_sq_eq_integral.text: For an $L^2$ time path on a nonnegative interval, its norm squared is the interval integral of the squared norm of its representative. The restriction measure ignores endpoint null sets. This identity is used to express Cauchy–Schwarz bounds directly in the Hilbert norm of a time path.
TorusEuler.timeL2_norm_sq_eq_integral.summary: The time-path norm is its integral energy

TorusEuler.timeLerayLift.text: This bounded linear map sends a spatial operator to its lifted action composed with the time mean projection. It isolates all time-path structure from the frequency-dependent angular symbol. Consequently angular differentiation can be transferred by postcomposition with one fixed bounded linear map.
TorusEuler.timeLerayLift.summary: Lifting a spatial operator together with time mean subtraction

TorusEuler.timeMeasure_real_univ.text: Under `hT : 0 ≤ T`, the real-valued measure of the whole restricted time space is $T$. The measure is Lebesgue measure restricted to $(0,T]$. This normalization turns the abstract finite-measure integration estimate into the familiar factor $\sqrt T$ in the endpoint path bounds.

TorusEuler.timeMeasure_real_univ_product.text: When `T` is nonnegative, the real-valued mass of the whole space for Lebesgue measure restricted to $(0,T]$ equals $T$. This elementary normalization is used after Fubini to obtain the joint primitive bound. At `T = 0`, both sides vanish and the identity remains valid.
TorusEuler.timeMeasure_real_univ_product.summary: The time measure has mass equal to its length

TorusEuler.timeMeasure_real_univ_weak.text: For `hT : 0 ≤ T`, the real mass of Lebesgue measure restricted to $(0,T]$ is exactly $T$. The nonnegative-length condition includes the zero interval. This normalization justifies the time average in the weak endpoint argument; division by $T$ is used later only with a strictly positive length.

TorusEuler.timePartial.text: Takes the joint within-slab derivative of $f$ on $[0,T]\times E$ and evaluates it on $(1,0)$. This is an encoding of the time partial on the closed slab. The definition makes sense for arbitrary $T$ and $f$; identification with the derivative of a time slice requires the later smoothness and positive-length hypotheses.
TorusEuler.timePartial.summary: Extract the time partial from the joint derivative

TorusEuler.timePartial_eqOn_congr.text: If two functions agree throughout the closed slab, their extracted within-slab time partials also agree there. This is a congruence statement for the selected derivative and needs no smoothness or positive-length assumption. It allows local equalities to be substituted under repeated within-slab differentiation without asserting anything outside the domain.
TorusEuler.timePartial_eqOn_congr.summary: Agreement on the slab preserves the extracted time partial

TorusEuler.timePartial_iterate_smooth.text: If the original function is jointly smooth on a positive-length closed slab, iterating the extracted time-partial operator any finite number of times preserves that smoothness. The proof is induction using `timePartial_smooth`. This concerns the within-slab operator; its equality with repeated one-variable derivatives is a separate theorem.
TorusEuler.timePartial_iterate_smooth.summary: Repeated extracted time partials remain smooth

TorusEuler.timePartial_smooth.text: For `0 < T` and a jointly smooth function on $[0,T]\times E$, the extracted `timePartial` is jointly smooth there. The proof differentiates within a set with unique derivatives and then applies the fixed linear map `timeEval`. This supplies the regularity needed to repeat time differentiation without assuming it anew.
TorusEuler.timePartial_smooth.summary: The extracted time partial is jointly smooth

TorusEuler.toUnitTorus.text:
The quotient of the periodic Euclidean lift by the integer lattice.

Default-value audit (b5): This is the quotient map identifying lattice translates, not a choice of a representative. No inverse is claimed; surjectivity and the exact lattice equivalence are proved separately.
TorusEuler.toUnitTorus.summary: Passing from a periodic lift to the unit torus

TorusEuler.toUnitTorus_add.text: The quotient map from `Vec3` to the product of three unit circles sends a vector sum to the sum of the corresponding labels. This identity translates Euclidean increments into torus translations. It supports directional difference quotients of periodic lifts without choosing a fundamental-domain representative for each point.

TorusEuler.toUnitTorus_eq_iff.text: Two lifted positions have the same torus image exactly when their difference is an integer lattice vector. This identifies the quotient relation used by periodic functions.
TorusEuler.toUnitTorus_eq_iff.summary: Equal torus points differ by an integer translation

TorusEuler.toUnitTorus_neg_cutoff.text: The quotient map takes a negated Euclidean vector to the negation of its torus label. This coordinatewise additive identity lets oddness of a lifted field be expressed as oddness on the torus. It is the geometric substitution used in the even-symbol parity argument for the real cutoff.
TorusEuler.toUnitTorus_neg_cutoff.summary: Spatial reflection descends to torus reflection

TorusEuler.toUnitTorus_sub.text: Taking the torus image of `x − y` equals subtracting their torus images. The coordinate quotient homomorphisms supply the equality. This identifies a Euclidean convolution evaluated on periodic lifts with torus translation by the image of its integration variable, without choosing special representatives of torus points.
TorusEuler.toUnitTorus_sub.summary: The quotient map preserves subtraction of spatial points

TorusEuler.toUnitTorus_surjective.text: The quotient map from Euclidean space onto the unit torus is surjective. This permits pointwise statements on torus fields to be checked on their lifts.
TorusEuler.toUnitTorus_surjective.summary: Every torus point has a Euclidean representative

TorusEuler.toUnitTorus_zero.text: The Euclidean zero vector maps to zero in the unit torus. This normalization is used when comparing directional derivatives at zero line parameter.

TorusEuler.torusCharacter_add.text: For a fixed lattice frequency, the character evaluated at the sum of two labels equals the product of its two values. This group-character identity permits Haar translation in the operator-convolution coefficient calculation. It is valid pointwise and requires no integrability or regularity hypothesis on any input field.
TorusEuler.torusCharacter_add.summary: A torus character converts addition into multiplication

TorusEuler.torusDist_le_lift.text: The distance between the torus images of two Euclidean points is at most the norm of their difference. Coordinate quotient norms can only decrease, and the product torus norm is controlled by the Euclidean norm. This transfers a half-Hölder estimate on torus labels to the periodic Euclidean lift.
TorusEuler.torusDist_le_lift.summary: Torus distance is bounded by Euclidean lift distance

TorusEuler.torusEuclideanDistance.text: Defines a geodesic Euclidean distance on the three-torus by taking the square root of the sum of the three squared circle distances. This auxiliary distance matches the length of a shortest Euclidean lift. It is distinguished from the default product distance used by the formal half-Hölder space, and comparison lemmas connect the two.
TorusEuler.torusEuclideanDistance.summary: Euclidean distance from coordinate circle distances

TorusEuler.torusEuclideanDistance_le_lif.text: For arbitrary Euclidean representatives $x,a$, the torus Euclidean distance between their images is at most $\|x-a\|$. Each circle distance is bounded by the corresponding real-coordinate separation. This transfers vanishing of a torus source on a Euclidean torus ball to vanishing of its periodic lift on an ordinary Euclidean ball.
TorusEuler.torusEuclideanDistance_le_lif.summary: Every lift bounds torus Euclidean distance

TorusEuler.torusEuclideanDistance_le_two.text: Bounds the auxiliary Euclidean torus distance by twice the default product distance. The proof bounds all three squared coordinate distances by the squared product distance and uses $3\le4$. The convenient factor two converts the off-support estimate to the chosen Hölder metric; it is a sufficient comparison constant, not an optimality assertion.
TorusEuler.torusEuclideanDistance_le_two.summary: Euclidean distance is bounded by twice product distance

TorusEuler.torusEuclideanDistance_lifts.text: For Euclidean representatives $x,a$, expresses the auxiliary torus distance as the norm built from the coordinate differences $x_i-a_i$ after subtracting their nearest integers. This uses the circle-distance formula and makes the shortest-lift construction explicit. Ties in rounding do not affect the squared distances, so the identity needs no uniqueness assertion.
TorusEuler.torusEuclideanDistance_lifts.summary: Coordinate rounding computes torus lift distance

TorusEuler.torusHalfHolderDerivativeOper.text: Extends a bounded operator `P` on vector-valued half-Hölder fields to fields valued in continuous linear maps. It evaluates the derivative in each coordinate direction, applies `P`, then reconstructs the linear map using coordinate functionals. This is a finite linear construction. Commutation with differentiation is a separate property of `P`, not a consequence of this definition.

Identifies the bundled continuous linear operator on derivative fields with the earlier pointwise construction `torusHalfHolderProjectedDerivative`. The result holds for every bounded `P` and every half-Hölder linear-map field `H`. It is an equality of constructions, with no assumption that `H` actually differentiates another field.

TorusEuler.torusHalfHolderDirection.text: Applies a fixed vector `v` to each continuous linear map in a half-Hölder operator field, producing a half-Hölder vector field. This packages a candidate directional derivative while preserving the quotient-space representation. The definition itself does not establish that the operator field is the derivative of any function.
TorusEuler.torusHalfHolderDirection.summary: Evaluating a derivative field in one direction

TorusEuler.torusHalfHolderProjectedDeriv.text: Forms an operator-valued half-Hölder field by applying `P` to each coordinate column of `H` and reconstructing the linear map with coordinate projections. The construction uses the three standard Euclidean directions. It is meaningful for any continuous linear operator `P` on fields; no commutation with differentiation is built into the definition.
TorusEuler.torusHalfHolderProjectedDeriv.summary: Applying a spatial operator to derivative columns

TorusEuler.torusIntegral_eq_centeredCell.text: The standard torus probability integral is the lift's integral over the centered unit cube.
TorusEuler.torusIntegral_eq_centeredCell.summary: The torus integral equals the fundamental-cube integral

TorusEuler.torusLInf.text: The formal quantity is the essential supremum of $|f(x)|$ over $[-1/2,1/2]^3$ with respect to Lebesgue measure, taking values in $[0,\infty]$. For a continuous periodic field it equals the ordinary spatial supremum. Vector values use the Euclidean norm; when $f=D_xu$, the pointwise norm is the induced operator norm. Theorem 1.1 integrates these nonnegative extended-valued quantities over $[0,T_*)$, allowing the result to be infinity. The definition itself neither imposes periodicity nor asserts finiteness or divergence. Integrating over the closed cube does not duplicate boundary mass because its faces have measure zero.
TorusEuler.torusLInf.summary: The norm may take the value positive infinity

TorusEuler.torusLInf_curl_le.text: For a spatial field $v$, the formal inequality is $\|\operatorname{curl}v\|_\infty\le C\|\nabla v\|_\infty$, with $C$ the operator norm of the fixed linear map taking a derivative matrix to its coordinate curl. Both spatial norms are essential suprema over $[-1/2,1/2]^3$, and the gradient is measured in operator norm. No Euler equation, periodicity or separate differentiability assumption occurs in the formal inequality. In its application to Corollary 8.3, $v=u(t)$ is smooth and periodic, so these expressions are the usual torus norms of the genuine derivatives. The constant is independent of $v$ and time, allowing integration to transfer divergence from vorticity to gradient. At a spatial point without a derivative, the derivative expression is assigned zero; this convention does not assert differentiability.
TorusEuler.torusLInf_curl_le.summary: A fixed linear map controls the essential supremum of vorticity

TorusEuler.torusLInf_stationaryShear_le_.text: If `hs : |s| ≤ 1`, the torus essential-supremum norm of the stationary shear is at most two, expressed through `ENNReal.ofReal`. The bound follows from the pointwise velocity estimate. No representative or exceptional null set is needed because the estimate already holds everywhere.
TorusEuler.torusLInf_stationaryShear_le_.summary: The parent velocity has essential supremum at most two

TorusEuler.torusLiftConvolution.text: For integrable scalar kernel `K` and continuous torus field `g`, define the continuous field obtained by integrating $K(y)g(z-[y])$. Compactness bounds `g`, and the L¹ kernel provides an integrable dominating function. The complete complex target ensures the Bochner integral has its usual value.
TorusEuler.torusLiftConvolution.summary: Convolve a torus field using a Euclidean kernel

TorusEuler.torusLiftConvolution_toUnitTo.text: Evaluating the torus convolution at the image of `x` equals the Euclidean lift convolution applied to $z\mapsto g([z])$ at `x`. The equality follows from the quotient subtraction identity. It connects the torus operator to the real-space kernel estimates without changing the actual integrand.
TorusEuler.torusLiftConvolution_toUnitTo.summary: Torus convolution agrees with convolution of the periodic lift

TorusEuler.torusLip_of_fourierBand.text: A continuous torus field with frequencies below $4\Lambda$ has increments bounded by $8\Lambda$ times the first kernel-derivative L¹ norm, its supremum norm, and torus distance. Positive scale and the normalized smooth cutoff are explicit. Bernstein bounds the Euclidean derivative, and close lifts contribute the extra factor two.
TorusEuler.torusLip_of_fourierBand.summary: A Fourier band bound gives a torus Lipschitz estimate

TorusEuler.torusQuotient_continuous.text: The coordinatewise quotient map from Euclidean three-space to torus labels is continuous. This local helper supplies continuity of lifted and translated fields inside operator-valued convolution. It uses the additive-circle quotient topology and does not require a global continuous choice of Euclidean representatives for torus points.
TorusEuler.torusQuotient_continuous.summary: Passing from Euclidean points to torus labels is continuous

TorusEuler.torusQuotient_neg.text: The image of `-x` under the torus quotient equals the negative of the image of `x`. The proof is coordinatewise on the additive circle.
